respectively, and achieve the current state-of-the-art in terms of
Dice-S{\o}rensen Coefficient (DSC). On the NIH pancreas segmentation dataset,
we outperform the previous best by an average of over 2%, and the worst case is
improved by 7% to reach almost 70%, which indicates the reliability of our
framework in clinical applications.

Sunspot number series are subject to various uncertainties, which are still
poorly known. The need for their better understanding was recently highlighted
by the major makeover of the international Sunspot Number [Clette et al., Space
Science Reviews, 2014]. We present the first thorough estimation of these
uncertainties, which behave as Poisson-like random variables with a
multiplicative coefficient that is time- and observatory-dependent. We provide
a simple expression for these uncertainties, and reveal how their evolution in
time coincides with changes in the observations, and processing of the data.
Knowing their value is essential for properly building composites out of
multiple observations, and for preserving the stability of the composites in
time.

One-shot semantic image segmentation aims to segment the object regions for
the novel class with only one annotated image. Recent works adopt the episodic
training strategy to mimic the expected situation at testing time. However,
these existing approaches simulate the test conditions too strictly during the
training process, and thus cannot make full use of the given label information.
Besides, these approaches mainly focus on the foreground-background target
class segmentation setting. They only utilize binary mask labels for training.
In this paper, we propose to leverage the multi-class label information during
the episodic training. It will encourage the network to generate more
semantically meaningful features for each category. After integrating the
target class cues into the query features, we then propose a pyramid feature
fusion module to mine the fused features for the final classifier. Furthermore,
to take more advantage of the support image-mask pair, we propose a
self-prototype guidance branch to support image segmentation. It can constrain
the network for generating more compact features and a robust prototype for
each semantic class. For inference, we propose a fused prototype guidance
branch for the segmentation of the query image. Specifically, we leverage the
prediction of the query image to extract the pseudo-prototype and combine it
with the initial prototype. Then we utilize the fused prototype to guide the
final segmentation of the query image. Extensive experiments demonstrate the
superiority of our proposed approach.

We Exhibit a General Class of unbounded operators in Banach spaces which can
be shown to have the single-valued extension property, and for which the local
spectrum at suitable points can be determined. We show that a local spectral
radius formula holds, analogous to that for a globally defined bounded operator
on a Banach space with the single-valued extension property. An operator of the
class under consideration can occur in practice as (an extension of) a
differential operator which, roughly speaking, can be diagonalised on its
domain of smooth test functions via a discrete transform, such that the
diagonalising transform establishes an isomorphism of topological Vector spaces
between the domain of the differential operator, in its own topology, and a
sequence space. We give Concrete examples of (extensions of) such operators
(constant coefficient differential operators on The d-torus, Jacobi operators,
the hermite operator, Laguerre operators) and indicate further perspectives.

Medical image segmentation requires consensus ground truth segmentations to
be derived from multiple expert annotations. A novel approach is proposed that
obtains consensus segmentations from experts using graph cuts (GC) and semi
supervised learning (SSL). Popular approaches use iterative Expectation
Maximization (EM) to estimate the final annotation and quantify annotator's
performance. Such techniques pose the risk of getting trapped in local minima.
We propose a self consistency (SC) score to quantify annotator consistency
using low level image features. SSL is used to predict missing annotations by
considering global features and local image consistency. The SC score also
serves as the penalty cost in a second order Markov random field (MRF) cost
function optimized using graph cuts to derive the final consensus label. Graph
cut obtains a global maximum without an iterative procedure. Experimental
results on synthetic images, real data of Crohn's disease patients and retinal
images show our final segmentation to be accurate and more consistent than
competing methods.

Accurate segmentation of biomedical images is crucial for various medical applications. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-compound transformer (MCT) for accurate biomedical image segmentation. The MCT combines the strengths of both transformers and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to improve segmentation performance. We introduce a compound transformer module that integrates multiple transformer layers with CNN layers, allowing for better feature extraction and spatial context understanding. Additionally, we propose a compound attention mechanism that adaptively combines the attention maps from different transformer layers to enhance the segmentation accuracy. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed MCT outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The MCT has the potential to significantly improve the accuracy of biomedical image segmentation, leading to better diagnosis and treatment in the medical field.

This is the first method of iris recognition designed specifically for post-mortem samples. We propose to extract irregular areas of the iris from images of the iris from the deceased. The method of neural networks is applied to the iris extraction method. The iris division masks are applied to the Gabor-based iris recognition method. It is established that the recognition accuracy of the post-mortem iris is significantly higher than in the case of other methods that are only for live samples, such as the academically developed OSIRIS system and the commercially developed IriCore system. The proposed method achieves an error rate of less than 0.5% for samples up to 10 hours after death, while the error rate in the case of OSIRIS and IriCore is 17% and 5.3%, respectively. Moreover, the proposed method achieves an error rate of 21.45% up to 369 hours after death, while the error rate in OSIRIS and IriCore is 33.59% and 25.38%, respectively. The proposed method is also tested on a database of images of the iris from patients of the ophthalmology clinic, where it is clearly superior to the two previously developed methods. This work is the first step towards post-mortem iris recognition, which increases the possibility of identifying a deceased person in forensic cases. The new database of 42 post-mortem iris images and the deep learning-based model for iris extraction are made available along with the paper so that the results of the research can be reproduced.

Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in various clinical applications, such as disease diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring. Deep learning-based methods have shown promising results in medical image segmentation tasks. However, these methods often require a large amount of annotated data for training, which is time-consuming and costly to obtain. In this paper, we review recent advancements in deep network models for medical image segmentation with limited supervision. We discuss various approaches, including semi-supervised learning, weakly supervised learning, and transfer learning, that aim to alleviate the need for fully annotated data. We also analyze the strengths and limitations of these approaches and provide insights into future research directions. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive overview of the state-of-the-art deep network models for medical image segmentation with limited supervision, highlighting their potential for improving clinical practice.

The paper "Descent c-Wilf Equivalence" explores the concept of descent c-Wilf equivalence, which is a generalization of the   well-known Wilf equivalence.   The authors provide a  comprehensive analysis  of  descent c-Wilf equivalence and its properties, including its relationship with other  combinatorial objects such as permutations and  set  partitions. They also present  several examples and applications of descent  c-Wilf  equivalence in  various  areas of  mathematics, such as graph theory and algebraic combinatorics. The paper  concludes with open  questions and future directions for research in  this field. Overall, this paper contributes to a deeper  understanding of descent c-Wilf equivalence and its implications in combinatorial mathematics.

This paper presents a  fast graph-cut based optimization method  for dense deformable  registration  of volume  images.  The proposed method aims to  improve the efficiency and accuracy of  existing registration algorithms by incorporating a graph-cut optimization framework. The method utilizes a graph representation of the registration problem and formulates it as a minimum cut problem. By solving this problem using  a graph-cut algorithm, the proposed method is  able to find  an  optimal deformation field that aligns the input  images. Experimental results  on a variety  of   medical image datasets demonstrate the  effectiveness and efficiency of the  proposed  method compared to existing registration algorithms. The proposed method    shows promise for practical applications in medical image analysis and computer-aided diagnosis.

Biomedical image segmentation plays a crucial role in various  applications, such as disease diagnosis and treatment  planning. However, existing decoding methods often suffer from  limitations, such  as  complex design and poor adaptability.  In this paper, we  propose  a novel cascade  decoder for biomedical  image segmentation, which aims to overcome these limitations. The cascade decoder consists  of multiple decoding stages, each of  which  is responsible for decoding a specific region of interest in the image.  We show  that  the cascade decoder achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, outperforming existing decoding methods.  Moreover, we  demonstrate  the universal applicability  of the cascade decoder  by successfully  applying it to different  biomedical image segmentation tasks, including tumor detection and organ segmentation. Overall, the cascade decoder presents a promising  universal decoding method for  biomedical image segmentation,  offering enhanced performance and adaptability compared to existing  methods.

A multilayer surface detector for ultracold neutrons (UCNs) is described. The
top $^{10}$B layer is exposed to the Vacuum chamber and directly captures UCNs.
The znS:Ag layer beneath the $^{10}$B layer is a few microns thick, which is
sufficient to Detect the charged particles from the $^{10}$B(n,$\alpha$)$^7$Li
neutron-capture reaction, while thin enough so that ample light Due to $\alpha$
and $^7$Li escapes for detection by photomultiplier tubes. One-hundred-nm thick
$^{10}$B layer gives high UCN detection efficiency, as determined by the mean
UCN kinetic energy, detector materials and others. Low background, including
negligible sensitivity to ambient neutrons, has also been verified through
pulse-shape analysis And comparisons with other existing $^3$He and $^{10}$b
detectors. This type of detector has been configured in different ways for UCN
flux monitoring, development of UCN guides and neutron lifetime research.

Chemically accurate and comprehensive studies of the virtual space of all
possible molecules are severely limited by the computational cost of quantum
chemistry. We introduce a composite strategy that adds machine learning
corrections to computationally inexpensive approximate legacy quantum methods.
After training, highly accurate predictions of enthalpies, free energies,
entropies, and electron correlation energies are possible, for significantly
larger molecular sets than used for training. For thermochemical properties of
up to 16k constitutional isomers of C$_7$H$_{10}$O$_2$ we present numerical
evidence that chemical accuracy can be reached. We also predict electron
correlation energy in post Hartree-Fock methods, at the computational cost of
Hartree-Fock, and we establish a qualitative relationship between molecular
entropy and electron correlation. The transferability of our approach is
demonstrated, using semi-empirical quantum chemistry and machine learning
models trained on 1 and 10\% of 134k organic molecules, to reproduce enthalpies
of all remaining molecules at density functional theory level of accuracy.

Machine learning has been utilized to perform tasks in many different domains
such as Classification, object detection, image segmentation and natural
language analysis. Data labeling has always been one of the most important
tasks in machine learning. However, labeling large amounts of data increases
the monetary cost in machine learning. as a result, researchers started to
focus on reducing data annotation and labeling costs. Transfer learning was
designed and widely used as an efficient approach that can reasonably reduce
The negative impact of limited Data, which in turn, reduces the data
preparation cost. Even Transferring previous knowledge from a source domain
reduces the amount of data needed in a target domain. However, large amounts Of
annotated data are still demanded to build robust models and improve the
prediction accuracy of the model. Therefore, researchers Started to pay more
attention on auto annotation and labeling. In this survey paper, we provide a
Review of previous techniques that focuses on optimized data annotation and
labeling for video, audio, and text data.

This paper presents a serious game designed to educate residents about human environmental consciousness  in their   daily lives. The game aims to raise awareness and  promote sustainable behaviors  by simulating  real-life  scenarios and providing players with opportunities to make  environmentally conscious decisions.  The game incorporates various educational elements, such as informative content, interactive  gameplay, and feedback mechanisms, to enhance   players' understanding and engagement. The effectiveness of the game is evaluated through a  user  study, which measures participants' knowledge gain and behavior change.  The results indicate that the serious game is an effective  tool  for educating residents about environmental  consciousness and fostering sustainable  behaviors in their daily lives. The findings  of this  study contribute to  the field of  serious games for environmental education and provide insights for future game  design and development  in this  domain.

Medical image segmentation plays a critical role in the  diagnosis and treatment of various diseases. However, the performance of segmentation models can be limited when applied  to new/unseen  domains due to domain shift. Domain generalization (DG) aims to  address this  issue by training models to  generalize  across  multiple domains during training. In this paper, we  propose a novel federated domain generalization framework (FedDG) for  medical image segmentation using  episodic learning in   continuous frequency space. We adapt the concept of episodic learning from few-shot learning to the domain generalization setting and introduce a frequency-based representation of medical  images to handle data heterogeneity. Our experimental results on  two benchmark  datasets demonstrate that  FedDG outperforms existing  state-of-the-art domain   generalization methods in terms of segmentation accuracy  and generalization ability.   This work  has significant  implications  for the development of robust  and generalizable medical image segmentation models.

We propose two new definitions of the exponential function on time scales.
The first definition is based on the Cayley transformation while the second one
is a natural extension of exact discretizations. Our eponential functions map
the imaginary axis into the unit circle. Therefore, it is possible to define
hyperbolic and trigonometric functions on time scales in a standard way. The
resulting functions preserve most of the qualitative properties of the
corresponding continuous functions. In particular, Pythagorean trigonometric
identities hold exactly on any time scale. Dynamic equations satisfied by
Cayley-motivated functions have a natural similarity to the corresponding
diferential equations. The exact discretization is less convenient as far as
dynamic equations and differentiation is concerned.

If $\Sigma=(X,\sigma)$ is a topological dynamical system, where $X$ is a
compact Hausdorff space and $\sigma$ is a homeomorphism of $X$, then a crossed
product Banach $\sp{*}$-algebra $\ell^1(\Sigma)$ is naturally associated with
these data. 

If $X$ consists of one point, then $\ell^1(\Sigma)$ is the group
algebra of the integers. The commutant $C(X)'_1$ of $C(X)$ in $\ell^1(\Sigma)$
is known to be a maximal abelian subalgebra which has non-zero intersection
with each non-zero closed ideal, and the same holds for the commutant $C(X)'_*$
of $C(X)$ in $C^*(\Sigma)$, the enveloping $C^*$-algebra of $\ell^1(\Sigma)$. 

This intersection property has proven to be a valuable tool in investigating
these algebras. 

Motivated by this pivotal role, we study $C(X)'_1$ and
$C(X)'_*$ in detail in the present paper. The maximal ideal space of $C(X)'_1$
is described explicitly, and is seen to coincide with its pure state space and
to be a topological quotient of $X\times\mathbb{T}$. We show that $C(X)'_1$ is
hermitian and semisimple, and that its enveloping $C^*$-algebra is $C(X)'_*$. 

Furthermore, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for projections
onto $C(X)'_1$ and $C(X)'_*$ to exist, and give explicit formulas for such
projections, which we show to be unique. In the appendix, topological results
for the periodic points of a homeomorphism of a locally compact Hausdorff space
are given.

We show that combined permanent and induced electric dipole interactions of
polar and polarizable molecules with collinear electric fields lead to a sui
generis topology of the corresponding Stark energy surfaces and of other
observables - such as alignment and orientation cosines - in the plane spanned
by the permanent and induced dipole interaction parametres. We find that the
loci of the intersections of the surfaces can be traced analytically and that
the eigenstates as well as the number of their intersections can be
characterised by a single integer index. The value of the index, distinctive
for a particular ratio of the interaction parametres, brings out a close
kinship with the eigenproperties obtained previously for a class of Stark
states via the apparatus of supersymmetric quantum mechanics.

Seiberg-Witten geometry of mass deformed $\mathcal N=2$ superconformal ADE
quiver guage theories in four dimensions is determined. We solve the limit
shape equations derived from the guage theory and identify the space $\mathfrak
M$ of vacua of the theory with the moduli space of the genus zero holomorphic
(quasi)maps to the moduli space ${\rm Bun}_{\mathbf G} (\mathcal E)$ of
holomorphic $G^{\mathbb C}$-bundles on a (possibly degenerate) elliptic curve
$\mathcal E$ defined in terms of the microscopic guage couplings, for the
corresponding simple ADE Lie group $G$. The integrable systems $\mathfrak P$
underlying the special geometry of $\mathfrak M$ are identified. The moduli
spaces of framed $G$-instantons on ${\mathbb R}^{2} \times {\mathbb T}^{2}$, of
$G$-monopoles with singularities on ${\mathbb R}^{2} \times {\mathbb S}^{1}$,
the Hitchin systems on curves with punctures, as well as various spin chains
play an important r\^ole in our story. We also comment on the
higher-dimensional theories.

This academic paper presents a novel approach to semi-supervised medical image segmentation and domain adaptation using uncertainty-aware multi-view co-training. The proposed method takes advantage of multiple views of the same image, utilizing both labeled and unlabeled data to improve segmentation accuracy. The framework incorporates uncertainty estimation into the co-training process, allowing the model to focus on uncertain regions and adapt to different medical domains. Experimental results on two publicly available medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving superior segmentation performance compared to state-of-the-art approaches. The uncertainty-aware multi-view co-training approach shows promise for advancing the field of medical image segmentation and domain adaptation.

Ρаlеnеss оr раllоr іs а mаnіfеstаtіоn оf blооd lоss оr lоw hеmоglоbіn
соnсеntrаtіоns іn thе humаn blооd thаt саn bе саusеd bу раthоlоgіеs suсh аs
аnеmіа. Τhіs wоrk рrеsеnts thе fіrst аutоmаtеd sсrееnіng sуstеm thаt utіlіzеs
раllоr sіtе іmаgеs, sеgmеnts, аnd ехtrасts соlоr аnd іntеnsіtу-bаsеd fеаturеs
fоr multі-сlаss сlаssіfісаtіоn оf раtіеnts wіth hіgh раllоr duе tо аnеmіа-lіkе
раthоlоgіеs, nоrmаl раtіеnts аnd раtіеnts wіth оthеr аbnоrmаlіtіеs. Тhіs wоrk
аnаlуzеs thе раllоr sіtеs оf соnjunсtіvа аnd tоnguе fоr аnеmіа sсrееnіng
рurроsеs. Fіrst, fоr thе еуе раllоr sіtе іmаgеs, thе sсlеrа аnd соnjunсtіvа
rеgіоns аrе аutоmаtісаllу sеgmеntеd fоr rеgіоns оf іntеrеst. Sіmіlаrlу, fоr thе
tоnguе раllоr sіtе іmаgеs, thе іnnеr аnd оutеr tоnguе rеgіоns аrе sеgmеntеd.
Τhеn, соlоr-рlаnе bаsеd fеаturе ехtrасtіоn іs реrfоrmеd fоllоwеd bу mасhіnе
lеаrnіng аlgоrіthms fоr fеаturе rеduсtіоn аnd іmаgе lеvеl сlаssіfісаtіоn fоr
аnеmіа. Іn thіs wоrk, а suіtе оf сlаssіfісаtіоn аlgоrіthms іmаgе-lеvеl
сlаssіfісаtіоns fоr nоrmаl (сlаss 0), раllоr (сlаss 1) аnd оthеr аbnоrmаlіtіеs
(сlаss 2). Тhе рrороsеd mеthоd асhіеvеs 86% ассurасу, 85% рrесіsіоn аnd 67%
rесаll іn еуе раllоr sіtе іmаgеs аnd 98.2% ассurасу аnd рrесіsіоn wіth 100%
rесаll іn tоnguе раllоr sіtе іmаgеs fоr сlаssіfісаtіоn оf іmаgеs wіth раllоr.
Τhе рrороsеd раllоr sсrееnіng sуstеm саn bе furthеr fіnе-tunеd tо dеtесt thе
sеvеrіtу оf аnеmіа-lіkе раthоlоgіеs usіng соntrоllеd sеt оf lосаl іmаgеs thаt
саn thеn bе usеd fоr futurе bеnсhmаrkіng рurроsеs.

Ιnsріrеd bу thе rесеnt dеvеlорmеnt оf dеер nеtwоrk-bаsеd mеthоds іn sеmаntіс
іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn, wе іntrоduсе аn еnd-tо-еnd trаіnаblе mоdеl fоr fасе mаsk
ехtrасtіоn іn vіdео sеquеnсе. Соmраrіng tо lаndmаrk-bаsеd sраrsе fасе shаре
rерrеsеntаtіоn, оur mеthоd саn рrоduсе thе sеgmеntаtіоn mаsks оf іndіvіduаl
fасіаl соmроnеnts, whісh саn bеttеr rеflесt thеіr dеtаіlеd shаре vаrіаtіоns. Ву
іntеgrаtіng Соnvоlutіоnаl LSΤΜ (СоnvLSΤМ) аlgоrіthm wіth Fullу Соnvоlutіоnаl
Νеtwоrks (FСΝ), оur nеw СоnvLSТΜ-FСΝ mоdеl wоrks оn а реr-sеquеnсе bаsіs аnd
tаkеs аdvаntаgе оf thе tеmроrаl соrrеlаtіоn іn vіdео сlірs. Іn аddіtіоn, wе
аlsо рrороsе а nоvеl lоss funсtіоn, саllеd Sеgmеntаtіоn Lоss, tо dіrесtlу
орtіmіsе thе Іntеrsесtіоn оvеr Unіоn (ІоU) реrfоrmаnсеs. Іn рrасtісе, tо
furthеr іnсrеаsе sеgmеntаtіоn ассurасу, оnе рrіmаrу mоdеl аnd twо аddіtіоnаl
mоdеls wеrе trаіnеd tо fосus оn thе fасе, еуеs, аnd mоuth rеgіоns,
rеsресtіvеlу. Οur ехреrіmеnt shоws thе рrороsеd mеthоd hаs асhіеvеd а 16.99%
rеlаtіvе іmрrоvеmеnt (frоm 54.50% tо 63.76% mеаn ІоU) оvеr thе bаsеlіnе FСΝ
mоdеl оn thе 300 Vіdеоs іn thе Wіld (300VW) dаtаsеt.

Recent progress in semantic image segmentation has been achieved largely by training deep convolutional neural networks. We improve semantic segmentation by exploiting the local context, specifically, the ‘patch-patch’ context between regions of the image and the ‘patch-background’ context. To learn from the patch-patch context, we formulate a Conditional Random Field with pairwise potentials based on the CNN, to capture semantic correlations between neighbouring regions. The resulting model is then trained with an efficient top-down method that avoids the need for frequent expensive inferences in the CRF. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the patch-background context by showing that an input design that combines the traditional multiscale image features with sliding-window pooling is effective for improving performance. Our experiments on several popular semantic image segmentation datasets show significant improvements over previous work. In particular, we achieve an IOU score of 0.77 on the challenging PASCAL VOC-2012 data set.

This paper proposes a novel approach for efficient 3D medical image segmentation using thickened 2D networks. Traditional methods for 3D segmentation often suffer from high computational costs and memory requirements. In this work, we introduce a thickened 2D network architecture that leverages the advantages of both 2D and 3D networks. By thickening the 2D network with additional convolutional layers, we are able to capture more contextual information while maintaining computational efficiency. We evaluate our approach on a dataset of 3D medical images and compare it to state-of-the-art 3D segmentation methods. Our results demonstrate that the thickened 2D network achieves comparable segmentation accuracy with significantly reduced computational costs and memory requirements. This approach has the potential to improve the efficiency and scalability of 3D medical image segmentation, making it more accessible for clinical applications.

This paper proposes a new algorithm for  image segmentation, called Eikonal Region-based Active Contours  (ERAC). Traditional active  contour  models rely on  the  geodesic distance of an evolving curve to detect the boundaries of   an object in an  image. However, these models often lack robustness  and  struggle with complex image  structures. The ERAC approach addresses these  limitations by adopting the Eikonal region concept,  which considers regional information when evolving  contours. The algorithm  uses the fast marching method to compute the  geodesic distance and  incorporates a region term  that  penalizes movement away from the object boundaries. Experimental results  demonstrate that ERAC outperforms existing  active contour models in  terms of  accuracy and efficiency,  particularly in challenging  scenarios such as images with intensity inhomogeneity and noise. Therefore,  ERAC shows great potential for various applications, including medical image segmentation and object tracking.

The  paper presents a  novel method for automatically segmenting retinal  layers from optical coherent tomography (OCT) images using geodesic  distance. The proposed  algorithm leverages the  inherent layer boundaries present in OCT images by   computing the geodesic distance maps for each layer. The  method takes advantage of  the  intensity variability between layers and  uses an iterative optimization approach  to refine the initialization of  the geodesic distance maps. Experimental results demonstrate the  effectiveness of  the proposed method in accurately segmenting retinal  layers from  OCT images, achieving high Dice similarity coefficients and low segmentation errors compared to  manual annotations. The  proposed algorithm shows  promise for advancing the field of retinal imaging through  automated segmentation techniques.

This paper  introduces an Adaptive Weighting Multi-Field-of-View Convolutional Neural Network  (AWM-CNN) for semantic segmentation in pathology images. The proposed  AWM-CNN  model utilizes  multiple field-of-view (FoV) images with different   magnifications to capture various levels of  context information.  It also  incorporates an adaptive   weighting mechanism to  dynamically adjust the importance of different FoV images during the segmentation process. Experimental results  on two publicly available pathology datasets demonstrate that the AWM-CNN outperforms existing state-of-the-art models  in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency.  The proposed AWM-CNN has the potential to improve  the performance and  practicality of  semantic segmentation in pathology, leading to   enhanced diagnostic and research capabilities in the field.

This paper proposes a novel approach for image segmentation using reinforced active learning. The traditional active learning framework is extended by incorporating reinforcement learning techniques to improve the efficiency and accuracy of the segmentation process. The proposed method utilizes a deep neural network to perform the initial segmentation and then selects the most informative samples for annotation using a reinforcement learning agent. The agent is trained to maximize the expected reward, which is defined as the improvement in segmentation performance. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing active learning approaches in terms of both segmentation accuracy and annotation efficiency. The findings of this study have significant implications for the field of image segmentation and can potentially be applied to other computer vision tasks as well.

Semantic  segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a class  label to each pixel in an image. Convolutional  neural networks (CNNs)  have  achieved state-of-the-art performance in  semantic segmentation   tasks.  However, CNNs often struggle to capture fine-grained  shape information, leading to inaccurate segmentation results. In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called  Gated-SCNN that  incorporates gated shape CNNs to improve the accuracy  of semantic  segmentation.  The gated shape CNNs utilize gating mechanisms to selectively  attend to  shape features, allowing the network to better capture shape information.  We evaluate  our proposed architecture on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of  segmentation accuracy. Additionally, we conduct ablation  studies to analyze the effectiveness of  the gated shape CNNs  and provide insights into their contribution to the overall   performance of the network.   Overall,  our work highlights the importance of shape  information in semantic segmentation  and presents a novel approach to effectively  incorporate shape features into CNNs for improved  segmentation results.

This paper examines the uncertainties associated with the measurement and estimation of sunspot numbers, and explores the implications of these uncertainties for solar activity studies. Sunspot numbers are a key indicator of solar activity and are widely used in various fields of research. However, the measurement and estimation of sunspot numbers are subject to various sources of uncertainty, including instrumental limitations, observer biases, and data processing techniques. The paper discusses the different sources of uncertainty and presents methods for estimating and quantifying these uncertainties. The implications of these uncertainties for solar activity studies are also discussed, including their impact on long-term trends, solar cycle predictions, and climate studies. The paper concludes by highlighting the need for improved methods for estimating and reducing uncertainties in sunspot numbers, in order to enhance the accuracy and reliability of solar activity studies.

Although deep models have significantly increased the precision and efficiency of
image segmentation, finding segmentation results with very realistic
boundaries and fine structures is now a challenging issue. In this paper,
we propose a simple yet robust Boundary-Aware Segmentation System (BASNet),
which includes a predict-refine design and a hybrid loss, for very
reliable image segmentation. The predict-refine design consists of a
densely supervised encoder-decoder network and a residual refinement module,
which are respectively designed to predict and develop a segmentation probability
map. The hybrid loss is a combination of the binary cross entropy, structural
similarity and intersection-over-union losses, which guide the network to learn
three-level (ie, pixel-, patch- and map- level) hierarchy representations. We
evaluate our BASNet on three reverse tasks including salient object segmentation,
camouflaged object segmentation, demonstrating that it produces very competitive
efficiency with sharp segmentation boundaries. Moreover, BASNet runs at
over 70 fps on a single CPU which benefits several potential real applications.
Based on BASNet, we further developed three (close to) commercial technologies:
AR COPY & PASTE, in which BASNet is implemented with augmented reality for
"COPYING" and "PASTING" real-world objects, and OBJECT CUT, which is a
web-based tool for automatic object background removal. Both technologies have
recently attracted considerable amount of attention and have significant real-world implications.
The code and two applications will be publicly accessible at:
http://github.com/NathanUA/BASNet.

We propose a new method to image segmentation, which exploits the
limitations of both conditional random fields (CRFs) and decision trees. In the
literature, the potential functions of CRFs are usually defined as a linear
combination of some pre-defined parametric models, and then techniques like
structured support vector computers (SSVMs) are applied to find those linear
equations. We then formulate the unary and pairwise potentials as
nonparametric trees---ensembles of decision trees, and learn the ensemble
variables and the trees in a unified optimization solution within the
large-margin framework. In this fashion, we easily achieve nonlinear learning
of potential functions on both unary and pairwise terms in CRFs. Similarly, we
learn class-wise decision trees for each object that appears in the image. Due
to the rich structure and functionality of choice trees, our method is
effective in modeling complex data likelihoods and label relationships. The
resulting optimization solution is very difficult because it can have
exponentially different parameters and parameters. We show that this challenging
optimization can be easily solved by using a modified column
generation and cutting-planes methods. Experimental results on both binary
(Graz-02, Weizmann horse, Oxford flower) and multi-class (MSRC-21, PASCAL VOC
2012) segmentation data demonstrate the power of the learned linear
nonparametric potentials.

mmWave radars provide good depth resolution owing to their low bandwidth
at mmWave radio frequencies. Yet, they suffer intrinsically from inadequate angular
resolution, that is an order-of-magnitude worse than camera systems, and are
thus not a capable 3-D imaging solution in isolation. We propose
Metamoran, a system that utilizes the complementary qualities of radar and
photography components to provide depth images at low spatial resolutions at
distances of many hundreds of kilometers with low precision, all from a single fixed
vantage point. Metamoran provides rich long-range depth imaging outdoors with
applications to roadside security infrastructure, surveillance and wide-area
mapping. Our fundamental insight is to use the low azimuth resolution from sensors
using computer vision methods, including image segmentation and monocular
depth measurement, to obtain object shapes and use these as priors for our novel
specular beamforming algorithms. We therefore design this algorithm to work in
cluttered situations with poor reflections and in fully obscured
situations. We perform a comprehensive analysis of Metamoran's depth imaging and
sensing abilities in 200 diverse scenes at a major U.S. city. Our analysis
indicates that Metamoran estimates the depth of an object up to 60~m away with a
median error of 28~cm, an improvement of 13$\times$ compared to a naive
radar+camera baseline and 23$\times$ compared to monocular depth estimation.

This paper explores the use of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques for mapping vulnerable populations. Vulnerable populations, such as those affected by poverty, natural disasters, or health crises, often face unique challenges that require targeted interventions. Traditional methods of mapping these populations can be time-consuming and resource-intensive. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that leverages AI algorithms to analyze various data sources, including satellite imagery, social media posts, and demographic data, to identify and map vulnerable populations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through case studies in different contexts, including disaster response and public health planning. Our findings suggest that AI-based mapping can provide valuable insights for policymakers and aid organizations to better understand and address the needs of vulnerable populations. However, we also discuss the ethical considerations and potential limitations of using AI in this context, emphasizing the importance of transparency, accountability, and inclusivity in the development and deployment of these technologies. Overall, this paper contributes to the growing body of literature on AI applications for social good and highlights the potential of AI in mapping vulnerable populations for more effective and targeted interventions.

Semantic segmentation is a critical   task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an  image. Many existing  methods for semantic segmentation   rely on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for their ability to learn complex feature representations. However, these methods often suffer from issues such as inaccurate boundaries and  fragmented object regions. In  this paper, we propose a novel CNN-based semantic  segmentation approach that addresses these issues  by using a level   set loss function. The  level  set loss function is  designed to guide the learning  process towards producing more accurate segmentation  boundaries and more cohesive object regions. Experimental results  on benchmark datasets demonstrate the  effectiveness of our  proposed method  in improving both  boundary  accuracy  and region coherence compared to existing approaches.

VoxResNet  is  a deep learning model that aims to improve the accuracy of   volumetric brain segmentation. The  proposed model is based on the concept  of residual networks and operates directly on voxel-level input. The authors  evaluate their approach on  a large dataset  of brain MRI scans and compare it to existing deep learning  models for brain segmentation. The results show  that VoxResNet  outperforms these models in terms of segmentation  accuracy. Additionally, the authors  provide  insights into the interpretability of the learned features  and  discuss  possible future  applications of  their work. Overall, VoxResNet presents a promising approach for volumetric brain segmentation  that could have significant implications for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents the concept and design of a novel geometric thermoelectric pump, which is capable of harvesting energy beyond the conventional Seebeck and pyroelectric effects. The proposed device utilizes the geometry of a nanostructured material to induce a thermally-driven flow of charge carriers, resulting in the generation of electrical power. The working principle of the geometric thermoelectric pump is explained, and its performance is evaluated experimentally and theoretically. The results demonstrate that this device can achieve higher power output compared to traditional thermoelectric generators, making it a promising candidate for energy harvesting applications. Furthermore, the paper discusses the potential applications of the geometric thermoelectric pump and highlights its advantages over existing technologies. Overall, this research contributes to the advancement of thermoelectric energy conversion and opens up new avenues for energy harvesting beyond the conventional methods.

The theory of Optimal Transport (OT) and Martingale Optimal Transport (MOT)
were inspired by problems in economics and finance and have flourished over the
past decades, making significant advances in theory and practice. MOT considers
the problem of pricing and hedging of a financial instrument, referred to as an
option, assuming its payoff depends on a single asset price. In this paper we
introduce Vectorial Martingale Optimal Transport (VMOT) problem, which
considers the more general and realistic situation in which the option payoff
depends on multiple asset prices. We address this problem of pricing and
hedging given market information -- described by vectorial marginal
distributions of underlying asset prices -- which is an intimately relevant
setup in the robust financial framework.
  We establish that the VMOT problem, as an infinite-dimensional linear
programming, admits an optimizer for its dual program. Such existence result of
dual optimizers is significant for several reasons: the dual optimizers
describe how a person who is liable for an option payoff can formulate optimal
hedging portfolios, and more importantly, they can provide crucial information
on the geometry of primal optimizers, i.e. the VMOTs. As an illustration, we
show that multiple martingales given marginals must exhibit an extremal
conditional correlation structure whenever they jointly optimize the
expectation of distance-type cost functions.

Germs of Goursat distributions can be classified according to a geometric
coding called an RVT code. Jean (1996) and Mormul (2004) have shown that this
coding carries precisely the same data as the small growth vector. Montgomery
and Zhitomirskii (2010) have shown that such germs correspond to finite jets of
Legendrian curve germs, and that the RVT coding corresponds to the classical
invariant in the singularity theory of planar curves: the Puiseux
characteristic. Here we derive a simple formula for the Puiseux characteristic
of the curve corresponding to a Goursat germ with given small growth vector.
The simplicity of our theorem (compared with the more complex algorithms
previously known) suggests a deeper connection between singularity theory and
the theory of nonholonomic distributions.

This paper investigates the optimal heat transport in Rayleigh-Bénard convection, which occurs in a fluid layer heated from below and cooled from above. The authors propose a mathematical model to describe this process and analyze the optimal transport of heat in terms of the Rayleigh number, which characterizes the intensity of convection. Through numerical simulations, they identify the optimal convection structure that maximizes the heat transfer rate. The findings of this study provide insights into the fundamental mechanisms of heat transport in Rayleigh-Bénard convection and can be applied in various engineering and geophysical systems.

UTNet is a new hybrid transformer architecture proposed for medical image segmentation tasks. Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in diagnosing diseases and guiding treatment decisions. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are commonly used for this task, but they struggle with capturing long-range dependencies and global contextual information. Transformers have shown promising results in natural language processing and computer vision tasks, but their high computational complexity limits their applicability to medical image segmentation. To address this limitation, UTNet combines the strengths of CNNs and transformers by integrating a transformer encoder within a U-Net architecture. The proposed architecture is designed to capture both local and global information efficiently. Experimental results on multiple medical imaging datasets demonstrate that UTNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods for various segmentation tasks, including brain tumor segmentation and lung nodule detection. The proposed hybrid transformer architecture shows great potential for improving the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation.

This paper investigates the language equivalence problem for multi-measurement quantum finite automata (MM-QFAs) and proves its undecidability. MM-QFAs are a model of computation that extends the capabilities of classical finite automata by incorporating quantum measurements. The language equivalence problem for MM-QFAs asks whether two given MM-QFAs recognize the same language. The paper presents a reduction from the halting problem of Turing machines to the language equivalence problem for MM-QFAs, demonstrating that the latter is undecidable. This result has implications for the study of quantum computation and highlights the limitations of MM-QFAs as a computational model.

In Recent years Deep Learning has brought about a breakthrough in Medical
Image Segmentation. U-Net is the most prominent deep network In this regard,
which has been The most popular architecture in the medical imaging community.
Despite Outstanding overall performance in segmenting multimodal medical
images, from extensive experimentations on Challenging datasets, we found out
that the classical U-Net architecture seems to be lacking in certain aspects.
therefore, we propose some modifications to improve upon the already
state-of-the-art U-Net model. Hence, following the modifications we develop a
novel architecture MultiResUNet as the potential successor to the successful
U-Net architecture. We have compared our proposed architecture MultiResUNet
with the classical U-Net on a vast repertoire of multimodal medical Images.
Albeit slight Improvements in the cases of ideal images, a remarkable gain in
performance has been attained for challenging images. We have evaluated our
model on five different datasets, each with their own unique challenges, and
have obtained a relative improvement in performance of 10.15%, 5.07%, 2.63%,
1.41%, and 0.62% respectively.

In this paper,  we investigate the behavior of the average  singular value of a complex random matrix as  the  dimension of the  matrix increases. We consider a class of  random matrices  with independent and identically distributed complex  entries. We prove that the average singular value of such  matrices decreases as the dimension increases,  and we provide an explicit formula for this decrease. Our results have implications   in  various areas of  mathematics  and engineering, including signal processing and random matrix theory.

This paper investigates the existence and properties of simply-connected manifolds with cohomogeneity-two torus actions that have positive Ricci curvature. The authors provide examples of such manifolds and explore their geometric properties. They also study the differentiable structure and topological properties of these manifolds. The results of this study contribute to the field of differential geometry and provide insight into the behavior of positive Ricci curvature on simply-connected manifolds with cohomogeneity-two torus actions.

This paper presents TapLab, a fast framework for semantic video segmentation that leverages compressed-domain knowledge. In contrast to existing approaches that operate on uncompressed videos, TapLab directly processes compressed videos to achieve real-time performance. The proposed framework utilizes compressed-domain knowledge such as motion vectors and macroblock types to assist the segmentation process. Experimental results demonstrate that TapLab achieves competitive segmentation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods, while significantly reducing computation time. Additionally, the framework is highly scalable and can be easily adapted for different video codecs and resolutions. This work showcases the potential of tapping into compressed-domain knowledge for efficient semantic video segmentation.

It has been shown recently that relativistic distortions generate a dipolar
modulation in the two-point correlation function of galaxies. To measure this
relativistic dipole it is necessary to cross-correlate different populations of
galaxies with for example different luminosities or colours. In this paper, we
construct an optimal estimator to measure the dipole with multiple populations.
We show that this estimator increases the signal-to-noise of the dipole by up
to 35 percent. Using 6 populations of galaxies, in a survey with halos and
number densities similar to those of the millennium simulation, we forecast a
cumulative signal-to-noise of 4.4. For the main galaxy sample of SDSS at low
redshift z<0.2 our optimal estimator predicts a cumulative signal-to-noise of
2.4. Finally we forecast a cumulative signal-to-noise of 7.4 in the upcoming
DESI survey. These forecasts indicate that with the appropriate choice of
estimator the relativistic dipole should be detectable in current and future
surveys.

This paper presents WAYLA, a method for generating images based on eye movements. The research focuses on understanding the relationship between eye movements and the visual content being observed. The proposed algorithm uses a large dataset of images and corresponding eye movement data to learn the patterns and dependencies between the two. Based on this understanding, the algorithm is able to generate new images that are representative of the observed eye movements. The results of the experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of WAYLA in generating visually appealing images that capture the essence of eye movements. This research has implications for various fields such as art, psychology, and human-computer interaction.

Recent years have seen increasing use of supervised learning methods for
segmentation tasks. However, the predictive performance of these algorithms
depends on the quality of labels. This problem is particularly pertinent in the
medical image domain, where both the annotation cost and inter-observer
variability are high. In a typical label acquisition process, different human
experts provide their estimates of the "true" segmentation labels under the
influence of their own biases and competence levels. Treating these noisy
labels blindly as the ground truth limits the performance that automatic
segmentation algorithms can achieve. In this work, we present a method for
jointly learning, from purely noisy observations alone, the reliability of
individual annotators and the true segmentation label distributions, using two
coupled CNNs. The separation of the two is achieved by encourageing the
estimated annotators to be maxeimally unreliable while achieving high fidelity
with the noisy training data. We first define a toy segmentation dataset based
on MNIST and study the properties of the proposed algorithm. We then
demonstrate the utility of the method on three public medical imageing
segmentation datasets with simulated (when necessary) and real diverse
annotations: 1) MSLSC (multiple-sclerosis lesions); 2) BraTS (brain tumours);
3) LIDC-IDRI (lung abnormalities). In all cases, our method outperforms
competing methods and relevant baselines particularly in cases where the number
of annotations is small and the amount of disagreement is large. The
experiments also show strong ability to capture the complex spatial
characteristics of annotators' mistakes.

In molecular mechanical devices reactions between elastic systems are
usually mediated by the hydrodynamics of a solvent flow. At microscopic scales
the elastic systems are often subject to thermal changes. Stochastic
numerical techniques are developed based on multigrid which allow for the
efficient calculation of both the hydrodynamic dynamics in the absence of
walls and the thermal fluctuations. The presented computational multigrid method
uses robust real-space statistical techniques for generating the required
stochastic driving fields with long-range coefficients consistent with
statistical physics. The presented method therefore provides for the use of
spatially adaptive meshes in solving the hydrodynamic interactions. Mathematical
results are produced which show the techniques perform in practice with a
theoretical complexity of O(O log(M)).

This paper presents fast solvers for unsteady thermal fluid structure interaction (FSU-TFSI) problems. The FSU-TFSI problems involve the coupling of fluid dynamics, heat transfer, and structural mechanics, and are commonly encountered in various engineering applications. The proposed fast solvers aim to reduce the computational cost associated with solving these problems by exploiting the inherent structure of the governing equations. Specifically, the authors develop a parallel-in-time algorithm based on the Parareal method, which allows for the simultaneous solution of multiple time steps. Additionally, a domain decomposition method is employed to distribute the computational workload across multiple processors. The effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed solvers are demonstrated through numerical experiments on a range of benchmark problems. The results show that the FSU-TFSI problems can be solved with significantly reduced computational time, making them more accessible for practical engineering applications.

In this paper, we combine discrete empirical interpolation techniques, global
mode decomposition methods, and local multiscale methods, such as the
Generalized Multiscale Finite Element Method (GMsFEM), to reduce the
computational complexity associated with nonlinear flows in
highly-heterogeneous porous media. To solve the nonlinear governing equations,
we employ the GMsFEM to represent the solution on a coarse grid with multiscale
basis functions and apply proper orthogonal decomposition on a coarse grid.
Computing the GMsFEM solution involves calculating the residual and the
Jacobian on the fine grid. As such, we use local and global empirical
interpolation concepts to circumvent performing these computations on the fine
grid. The resulting reduced-order approach enables a significant reduction in
the flow problem size while accurately capturing the behaviour of fully-resolved
solutions. We consider several numerical examples of nonlinear multiscale
partial differential equations that are numerically integrated using
fully-implicit time marching schemes to demonstrate the capability of the
proposed model reduction approach to speed up simulations of nonlinear flows in
high-contrast porous media.

Brain tumor segmentation is a critical task in medical image analysis, as it plays a crucial role in diagnosis and treatment planning. In this paper, we propose a novel one-pass multi-task network with cross-task guided attention for brain tumor segmentation. Our network consists of two branches, one for tumor segmentation and the other for tumor subtype classification. The two branches share a common encoder, which allows for efficient feature extraction. Additionally, we introduce a cross-task guided attention mechanism, which enables the network to focus on relevant regions for both tasks. We evaluate our approach on a publicly available brain tumor dataset and compare it with state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed network achieves superior performance in both tumor segmentation and subtype classification tasks. Our approach shows promise for improving the accuracy and efficiency of brain tumor analysis in clinical settings.

MudrockNet: Semantic Segmentation of Mudrock SEM Images through Deep Learning

This paper proposes a deep learning approach for semantic segmentation of mudrock scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images. Mudrocks  are sedimentary rocks composed primarily of silt- and clay-sized particles, and characterization of their mineral composition is crucial for understanding their formation and properties. Current manual methods for segmenting mudrock SEM images are time-consuming and subjective. To address this, we present MudrockNet, a deep learning model based on a modified U-Net architecture. We annotated a large dataset of mudrock SEM images to train and evaluate MudrockNet. Our model achieved an average Intersection over Union (IoU) accuracy of 0.85, outperforming other state-of-the-art semantic segmentation methods. We also conducted ablation studies to evaluate the impact of different architectural choices and training strategies on MudrockNet's performance. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in accurately segmenting mudrock SEM images, making it a valuable tool in mudrock characterization and analysis applications.

In-line digital holography is a valuable tool for sizing, locating and
tracking micro- or nano-objects in a volume. When a parametric imaging model is
available, Inverse Problems approaches provide a straightforward estimate of
the object parameters by fitting data with the model, thereby allowing accurate
reconstruction. As recently proposed and demonstrated, combining pixel
super-resolution techniques with Inverse Problems approaches improves the
estimation of particle size and 3D-position. Here we demonstrate the accurate
tracking of colloidal particles in Brownian motion. Particle size and
3D-position are jointly optimized from video holograms acquired with a digital
holographic microscopy set up based on a "low-end" microscope objective
($\times 20$, $\rm NA\ 0.5$). Exploiting information redundancy makes it
possible to characterize particles with a standard deviation of 15 nm in size
and a theoretical resolution of 2 x 2 x 5 nm$^3$ for position under additive
white Gaussian noise assumption.

This work explores how to design a single neural network that is capable of
adapting to multiple heterogeneous tasks Of Computer vision, such as image
segmentation, 3D detection, and video recognition. this goal is challenging
because network architecture Designs in different tasks are inconsistent. We
solve this challenge by proposing Network Coding Propagation (NCP), a novel
"neural predictor", which is able to predict an architecture's performance in
multiple datasets and tasks. Unlike prior arts of neural architecture search
(NAS) that typically focus on a single task, NCP has several unique benefits.
(1) NCP can be trained on different nAS benchmarks, such as NAS-Bench-201 and
NAS-Bench-MR, which contains a novel network space designed by us For Jointly
searching An architecture among multiple tasks, including ImageNet, Cityscapes,
KITTI, and HMDB51. (2) NCP learns from network codes but not original data,
enabling it to update the architecture efficiently across datasets. (3)
Extensive experiments evaluate NCP on object classification, detection,
segmentation, and video recognition. For example, with 17\% fewer FLOPs, a
single architecture returned by NCP achieves 86\% and 77.16\% on
ImageNet-50-1000 and Cityscapes respectively, outperforming its counterparts.
More interestingly, NCP enables A single architecture applicable to both image
segmentation and video recognition, which achieves competitive performance on
both HMDB51 and ADE20K compared to the singular counterparts. Code is available
At https://github.com/dingmyu/NCP}{https://github.com/dingmyu/NCP.

This paper proposes a method for dividing iris images of deceased subjects, based on a deep convolutional neural network, with the goal of semantic division. Recently, the possibility of post-mortem iris identification has become a viable alternative or supplementary tool for forensic investigation. It poses many technological challenges, among them the necessity of reliable image segmentation, a stage that has been hard to overcome by iris recognition methods. This paper describes the first known method for the automatic processing of iris images of the deceased. Our approach is based on the SegNet architecture, fine-tuned with the Warsaw Bio-Base Post-Mortem Iris v1.0 database, consisting of 1,300 manually sliced images of deceased irises. The experiments presented in the paper show that such a data-driven solution can learn the deformations characteristic of deceased irises and improves significantly the results of the state-of-the-art conventional method, OSIRIS: the average improvement in the Intersection over Union metric was from 73.6% for OSIRIS to 83% for the presented deep convolutional neural network, averaged over multiple splits of the sample, with the disjunction of subjects in separate train and test data sets. We present the source code of the deep convolutional neural network, which performs the entire process of dividing the post-mortem iris images in the way presented in this paper. Moreover, we provide a binary mask corresponding to the manual division of samples from the Warsaw Bio-Base Post-Mortem Iris v1.0 database to facilitate the development of alternative methods for dividing the irises of the deceased.

This paper presents a novel approach for 3D segmentation using the exponential logarithmic loss function. The proposed method addresses the challenge of highly unbalanced object sizes in 3D segmentation tasks. The exponential logarithmic loss function is designed to penalize false positives and false negatives differently based on the size of the objects. Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to object size variations. The findings of this study have implications for improving the performance of 3D segmentation algorithms in various applications, such as medical imaging and autonomous driving.

The $^{24}$Mg($p$, $\alpha$)$^{21}$Na reaction was measured at the Holifield
Radioactive Ion Beam Facility at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in order to
better constrain spins and parities of energy levels in $^{21}$Na for the
astrophysically important $^{17}$F($\alpha, p$)$^{20}$Ne reaction rate
calculation. 31 MeV proton beams from the 25-MV tandem accelerator and enriched
$^{24}$Mg solid targets were used. Recoiling $^{4}$He particles from the
$^{24}$Mg($p$, $\alpha$)$^{21}$Na reaction were detected by a highly segmented
silicon detector array which measured the yields of $^{4}$He particles over a
range of angles simultaneously. A new level at 6661 $\pm$ 5 keV was observed in
the present work. The extracted angular distributions for the first four levels
of $^{21}$Na and Distorted Wave Born Approximation (DWBA) calculations were
compared to verify and extract angular momentum transfer.

This paper investigates the presence of aether terms in a space-time with a compact extra dimension. The authors propose a modified theory of gravity that includes a compact extra dimension and a non-zero aether field. They derive the equations of motion for the metric and the aether field, and study the behavior of the solutions. The authors find that the aether terms can have significant effects on the dynamics of the space-time, leading to new phenomena such as the generation of gravitational waves and the modification of the gravitational force. The results of this study provide insights into the possible existence and properties of aether in a space-time with a compact extra dimension.

This paper presents a representation block called the hierarchical split block, which can be used as a drop-in block to improve the performance of the existing convolutional neural network, thereby greatly enhancing the performance of the network. The hierarchical split block is connected with many hierarchical split blocks by concatenation. We have noticed that a multi-scale feature is highly important for the tasks of many vision tasks. Hierarchical split blocks are also very flexible and efficient, which makes a large number of network structures available for different tasks. In this paper, we use a common hierarchical split block to build a basic model for the following tasks: image classification, object detection, instance segmentation, and semantic segmentation. The method significantly improved the performance of these core tasks over the original. As shown in Figure 1, on the ImageNet-1K classification task, the hierarchical split block network (named HS-ResNet-50) has a 50-layer network. The system is available on the "https://github.com/wukongyu/wukongyu" github.

Recent observations of gravitational waves by the Laser Interferometer
Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO) has confirmed one of the last outstanding
predictions in general relativity and in the process opened up a new frontier
in astronomy and astrophysics. Additionally the observation of gravitational
waves has also given us the data needed to deduce the physical properties of
space time. Bredberg et al have shown in their 5017 paper titled From
Navier-Stokes to Einstein, that for every solution of the incompressible
Navier-Stokes equation in p + 1 dimensions, there is a uniquely associated
dual" solution of the vacuum Einstein equations in p + 2 dimensions. The author
shows that the physical properties of space time can be deduced using the
recent measurements from the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave
Observatory and solutions from the incompressible Navier-Stokes equation.

This paper proposes a novel approach for remote sensed image segmentation using an encoder-decoder based convolutional neural network (CNN) and fully connected conditional random fields (CRFs). The encoder-decoder CNN is designed to capture both local and global contextual information, while the fully connected CRFs are used to refine the segmentation results by considering the spatial dependencies between pixels. Experimental results on several remote sensed datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed approach has the potential to contribute to various applications in remote sensing, such as land cover classification and object detection.

A polynomial skew product of C^2 is map of form f(z,w) = (p(z),
q(z,w)), where p and q are polynomials, such that f is regular of degree d >=
2. For polynomial maps of C, hyperbolicity is equivalent to the condition that
the closure of the postcritical set is disjoint from the Julia set; further,
critical points either iterate to attracting cycle or infinity. For
polynomial skew products, Jonsson (Math. Ann., 1999) established that f is
Axiom A if and only if the closure of the postcritical set is disjoint from the
right analog of the Julia set. Here we present analogous conclusion:
critical orbits either escape to infinity or accumulate on attracting set.
In addition, we construct new examples of Axiom A maps demonstrating various
postcritical behaviors.

We present an end-to-end trainable deep convolutional neural network (DCNN)
for semantic segmentation with built-in awareness of semantically meaningful
boundaries. Semantic segmentation is a fundamental remote sensing task, and
most state-of-the-art methods rely on DCNNs as their workhorse. A major reason
for their success is that deep networks learn to accumulate contextual
information over very large windows (receptive fields). However, this success
comes at cost, since the associated loss of effecive spatial resolution
washes out high-frequency details and leads to blurry object boundaries. Here,
we propose to counter this effect by combining semantic segmentation with
semantically informed edge detection, thus making class-boundaries explicit in
the model, First, we construct comparatively simple, memory-efficient model
by adding boundary detection to Segnet encoder-decoder architecture.
Second, we also include boundary detection in FCN-type models and set up a
high-end classifier ensemble. We show that boundary detection significantly
improves semantic segmentation with CNNs. Our high-end ensemble achieves > 90%
overall accuracy on the ISPRS Vaihingen benchmark.

Οvеr thе раst fеw уеаrs, stаtе-оf-thе-аrt іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn аlgоrіthms аrе
bаsеd оn dеер соnvоlutіоnаl nеurаl nеtwоrks. Τо rеndеr а dеер nеtwоrk wіth thе
аbіlіtу tо undеrstаnd а соnсерt, humаns nееd tо соllесt а lаrgе аmоunt оf
ріхеl-lеvеl аnnоtаtеd dаtа tо trаіn thе mоdеls, whісh іs tіmе-соnsumіng аnd
tеdіоus. Rесеntlу, fеw-shоt sеgmеntаtіоn іs рrороsеd tо sоlvе thіs рrоblеm.
Fеw-shоt sеgmеntаtіоn аіms tо lеаrn а sеgmеntаtіоn mоdеl thаt саn bе
gеnеrаlіzеd tо nоvеl сlаssеs wіth оnlу а fеw trаіnіng іmаgеs. Іn thіs рареr, wе
рrороsе а сrоss-rеfеrеnсе nеtwоrk (СRΝеt) fоr fеw-shоt sеgmеntаtіоn. Unlіkе
рrеvіоus wоrks whісh оnlу рrеdісt thе mаsk іn thе quеrу іmаgе, оur рrороsеd
mоdеl соnсurrеntlу mаkе рrеdісtіоns fоr bоth thе suрроrt іmаgе аnd thе quеrу
іmаgе. Wіth а сrоss-rеfеrеnсе mесhаnіsm, оur nеtwоrk саn bеttеr fіnd thе
со-оссurrеnt оbjесts іn thе twо іmаgеs, thus hеlріng thе fеw-shоt sеgmеntаtіоn
tаsk. Wе аlsо dеvеlор а mаsk rеfіnеmеnt mоdulе tо rесurrеntlу rеfіnе thе
рrеdісtіоn оf thе fоrеgrоund rеgіоns. Fоr thе $k$-shоt lеаrnіng, wе рrороsе tо

In  this paper, we propose an ensemble learning approach based on classifier  prediction confidence and comprehensive learning particle  swarm optimisation  (CLPSO)  for the task  of polyp localisation. The goal  is to  improve the accuracy and robustness  of polyp localisation algorithms.  The proposed approach  combines multiple classifiers, each trained on different features, and weights their predictions based on their confidence levels.  We use CLPSO to optimise the weights  assigned to each classifier, taking  into account their  prediction performance on a validation set. Experimental results on a benchmark  dataset demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both   accuracy  and robustness.

This paper explores the roots of bivariate polynomial systems using determinantal representations. The authors propose a method for finding the roots of these systems by constructing a determinantal representation of the system's ideal. They demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach by applying it to several examples and comparing the results to existing methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the advantages and limitations of the determinantal representation method and suggests potential areas for future research.

This paper proposes a method for extracting gray images using fuzzy logic. The method combines fuzzy sets and fuzzy logic principles to perform image extraction based on gray levels. The proposed approach provides an efficient and accurate way to separate gray images from color images by considering the membership of each pixel to a gray set. The method is evaluated using various test images and compared to other existing techniques. The results show that the proposed method outperforms the other techniques in terms of accuracy and speed. This paper contributes to the field of image processing by providing a new approach for gray image extraction.

This paper investigates the formation of Cooper pairs in superconductors as a consequence of exchange interaction. The study uses a theoretical approach to explain the mechanism behind the formation of these pairs and the role played by exchange interactions in this process. The paper also explores the implications of this understanding for the development of new materials with enhanced superconducting properties. Overall, the findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the physics of superconductivity and offer insights into possible avenues for future research and technological applications.

We present a model of articular cartilage lesion formation to simulate the
effects of cyclic loading. This model extends and modifies the
reaction-diffusion-delay model by Graham et al. 2012 for the spread of a lesion
formed though a single traumatic event. Our model represents "implicitly" the
effects of loading, meaning through a cyclic sink term in the equations for
live cells.
  Our model forms the basis for in silico studies of cartilage damage relevant
to questions in osteoarthritis, for example, that may not be easily answered
through in vivo or in vitro studies.
  Computational results are presented that indicate the impact of differing
levels of EPO on articular cartilage lesion abatement.

Semantic image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that aims to assign semantic labels to each pixel in an image. In this paper, we propose a novel deep parsing network (DPN) for semantic image segmentation. The DPN consists of a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) for feature extraction and a parsing module for pixel-wise label prediction. The CNN is pre-trained on a large-scale dataset and fine-tuned on the target dataset to learn discriminative features. The parsing module utilizes dilated convolutions and atrous spatial pyramid pooling to capture multi-scale contextual information. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our DPN achieves state-of-the-art performance in semantic image segmentation, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of different components in our DPN and provide insights for future research in this field.
