This paper explores the concept of observation and its relationship to quantum objectivity. It argues that the act of observation in quantum mechanics is not a passive process, but rather an active and participatory one. The paper examines various interpretations of quantum mechanics, including the Copenhagen interpretation and the many-worlds interpretation, and discusses how they approach the issue of observation. It also considers the role of consciousness in the process of observation and how it may affect the objectivity of quantum measurements. The paper concludes by suggesting that a deeper understanding of the nature of observation is necessary for a more comprehensive understanding of quantum mechanics and its implications.

In this paper, a new validity index is proposed for fuzzy-possibilistic C-means (FCM) clustering. The validity index aims to evaluate the quality of clustering results by considering factors such as the fuzziness and overlapping of clusters. The index is based on the fuzzy Pareto dominance concept, which allows for a more comprehensive evaluation of clustering solutions. The proposed index is compared with existing validity indices using several benchmark datasets, and experimental results show that it provides a more accurate assessment of clustering performance. Overall, the new validity index is a valuable tool for evaluating fuzzy-possibilistic C-means clustering algorithms and can help researchers and practitioners in choosing the most appropriate clustering solution.

The total electronic Raman scattering spectrum, including the nonresonant,
mixed and resonant components, is determined for the charge-density-wave (CDW)
phase of the spinless Falicov-Kimball model at half filling within dynamical
mean-field theory. Its frequency dependence is investigated for different
values of the energy of the incident photons. The spectra reflect the different
structures in the density of states and how they are modified by screening and
resonance effects. The calculations are performed for the $B_{\rm 1g}$, $B_{\rm
2g}$ and $A_{\rm 5g}$ symmetries (which are typically examined in experiment).
Our results for the resonance effects of the Raman spectra, found by tuning the
energy of the incident photons, give information about the many-body charge
dynamics of the CDW-ordered phase.

LECs are widely used in various perception-based tasks like image segmentation, object detection, self-driving. These LECs are trained with large image datasets in which multimodal factors such as weather conditions, time of day, traffic density, etc., are included. The LECs learn from these factors during the training. During the test, if one of these factors varies, the components become confused, resulting in low confidence predictions. These images with factors not encountered during the training are called “Out-of-Distribution (OOD) images”. To perform safe driving, it is necessary to detect these OOD images so that a suitable mitigation strategy can be performed. Detecting the OOD images in such datasets is difficult because of the multiple factors associated with each image. We propose a solution to this problem by using the latent space of a VAE with a suitable learning rate. This low-dimensional latent space encodes the multi-factor information in a few latent factors, enabling fast detection. We evaluate our approach on the nuScenes dataset. Our results show that the latent space of the VAE is sensitive to the value of the generative factors.

The double-slit experiment is a fundamental demonstration of quantum mechanics that illustrates the wave-particle duality of matter. In this experiment, a beam of particles or waves is passed through two parallel slits, creating an interference pattern on a screen. However, the traditional setup of the experiment does not allow for the modification of the optical path, limiting the types of measurements that can be made. In this paper, we propose a method for modifying the optical path in a nonlinear double-slit experiment by utilizing an adjustable phase plate. By introducing phase shifts to the interfering waves, we are able to manipulate the resulting interference pattern. We demonstrate the feasibility of this approach through simulations and provide experimental results confirming the effectiveness of the phase plate in modifying the optical path. This modification opens up new possibilities for studying the behavior of particles and waves in the double-slit experiment, enabling more precise measurements and deeper insights into the underlying physics.

This  paper presents a novel approach for  segmenting  microscopy data to identify nuclei in divergent images. The proposed method  utilizes a combination of image processing techniques and machine learning algorithms to  accurately detect and segment nuclei in various types  of microscopy images. The  approach  involves pre-processing the images to enhance contrast  and remove noise, followed by feature  extraction and  selection.  A support vector machine classifier is then  trained on a labeled dataset to  classify pixels as  either nucleus or non-nucleus. The segmented nuclei are further refined using morphological operations  and post-processing  techniques. The proposed method  is evaluated  on  a  diverse set of microscopy images and compared with existing segmentation techniques. The  results demonstrate  the effectiveness  and robustness  of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting nuclei in divergent microscopy images.

This paper investigates the phenomenon of Anderson localization in a partially random Bragg grating. The authors propose a conserved area theorem to explain the localization of light in this system. They use numerical simulations to demonstrate the validity of their theorem and compare their results with experimental data. The findings of this study provide insights into the behavior of light in disordered photonic structures and contribute to the understanding of Anderson localization in complex systems.

This paper proposes a novel approach to improve image co-segmentation using deep metric learning. Image co-segmentation is the task of simultaneously segmenting common objects from a set of images. Existing methods often suffer from limitations such as high computational complexity and low accuracy. To address these issues, the authors propose a deep metric learning framework that leverages the power of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to learn discriminative features for image co-segmentation. The proposed framework consists of two main components: a feature extraction network and a metric learning network. The feature extraction network is responsible for extracting high-level features from input images, while the metric learning network learns a similarity metric to measure the similarity between image patches. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. The findings of this study have implications for various computer vision applications, such as object recognition and image retrieval.

The isothermal entropy change and the adiabatic temperature change for the
exactly solved spin-5/2 Fisher's super-exchange antiferromagnet are rigorously
calculated in order to examine magnetocaloric properties of the model in a
vicinity of the second-order phase transition. It is shown that the large
inverse magnetocaloric effect occurs around the temperature interval
$T_c(h\neq0) < T < T_c(h=5)$ for any magnetic-field change $\Delta h: 0 \to h$.
The most pronounced inverse magnetocaloric effect can be found for the
magnetic-field change, which coincides with the critical field of a
zero-temperature phase transition from the antiferromagnetically ordered ground
state to the paramagnetic one.

A Software-defined Constrained Optimal Routing (SCOR) platform is introduced
as a Northbound interface in SDN architecture. It  is based on  constraint
programming techniques and is implemented in  MiniZinc modelling language. Using
constraint programming  techniques in this Northbound interface has created an
efficient tool for implementing complex Quality of Service routing applications
in a few lines of code. The  code  includes  only the problem  statement and the
solution  is found by  a general solver program. A  routing framework is
introduced based on  SDN's architecture model which uses  SCOR as its Northbound
interface and an upper layer  of applications implemented  in SCOR. Performance
of  a  few implemented routing applications  are evaluated in different network
topologies, network  sizes and various   number of concurrent flows.

In this academic paper, the authors propose a novel cost-effective region-based active learning framework for semantic segmentation, called CEREALS. The framework aims to reduce the annotation cost by selecting informative regions for annotation instead of annotating the entire image. To achieve this, the authors propose a region selection strategy that considers both uncertainty and representativeness of the regions. They evaluate the proposed framework on various benchmark datasets and compare it with existing active learning methods. The results demonstrate that CEREALS outperforms existing approaches in terms of annotation cost reduction without sacrificing segmentation accuracy. This paper provides valuable insights into cost-effective active learning techniques for semantic segmentation tasks.

Scaling properties of time series are often studied in terms of the scaling
laws of empirical moments, which are the time average estimates of moments of
the dynamic variable. Nonlinearities in the scale function of empirical
moments are also considered as a sign of multifractality in the data. We
show that, unlike for the Brownian motion, this method attempts to disclose the
exact monofractal nature of self-similar L\'evy systems. We prove that for
this class of systems it provides apparent multifractality characterised by a
piecewise-linear scaling function with three distinct regimes, which match at
the stability index of the considered process. This result is motivated by
previous theoretical evidence. It is derived by developing an appropriate
mathematical normalisation which is able to cure empirical moments, without
hiding their dependence on time, when moments they aim at estimating do not
exist.

In biomedical image segmentation, the availability of large annotated  datasets is  often limited, posing challenges for training  accurate   deep learning  models. This paper  introduces SPDA,  a novel data augmentation technique that leverages the properties  of  superpixels to generate  high-quality synthetic training samples. SPDA utilizes  superpixels to group pixels with similar  characteristics and applies various geometric and color transformations  to generate new images. Experimental results on several challenging biomedical image datasets demonstrate that the  proposed  SPDA approach improves the segmentation performance of  deep  learning models, outperforming traditional data augmentation methods. The proposed technique provides a promising solution to overcome the limited  annotated data problem  in  biomedical image segmentation tasks.

Semantic image segmentation is a fundamental problem in computer vision that involves assigning a semantic label to each pixel in an image. Recent research has shown that deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are highly effective for this task. However, these CNNs often suffer from high computational costs and memory requirements. In this paper, we propose a novel framework called progressively diffused networks (PDN) that addresses these limitations. PDNs rely on a two-step approach, where the image is first segmented using a lightweight CNN, and then progressively refined using a more powerful CNN. This allows for a trade-off between computational efficiency and segmentation accuracy. We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and compare it to state-of-the-art methods. The results show that PDNs achieve competitive performance while being significantly faster and more memory-efficient than existing approaches. Overall, our work highlights the potential of progressively diffused networks as a promising solution for semantic image segmentation.

This paper provides an alternate characterization of Leavitt path algebras using the concept of Baer and Baer *-rings. Leavitt path algebras are important algebraic structures that arise from the study of graph $C^*$-algebras, and they have applications in areas such as symbolic dynamics and noncommutative geometry. The authors show that every Leavitt path algebra can be realized as a Baer *-ring, and conversely, every Baer *-ring can be realized as a Leavitt path algebra. The paper also investigates the relationship between the two characterizations and provides a number of examples illustrating the connections between Baer *-rings and Leavitt path algebras. This alternate characterization enhances our understanding of Leavitt path algebras and provides new insights into their algebraic properties.

Maximum flow (and minimum cut) algorithms have had a strong impact on
computer vision. In particular, graph cuts algorithms provide mechanism for
the discrete optimization of an energy functional which has been used in a
variety of applications such as image segmentation, stereo, image stitching and
texture synthesis. Algorithms based on classical formulation of max-flow
defined on graph are known to exhibit metrication artefacts in the solution.
Therefore, a recent trend has been to instead employ spatially continuous
maximum flow (or the dual min-cut problem) in these same applications to
produce solutions with no metrication errors. However, known fast continuous
max-flow algorithms have no stopping criteria or have not been proved to
converge. In this work, we revisit continuous max-flow problem and show
that the analogous discrete formulation is different from classical
max-flow problem. We then apply an appropriate combinatorial optimization
technique to this combinatorial continuous max-flow CCMF problem to find a
null-divergence solution that exhibits no metrication artefacts and may be
solved exactly by fast, efficient algorithm with provable convergence.
Finally, by exhibiting dual problem of our CCMF formulation, we clarify the
fact, already proved by Nozawa in the continuous setting, that the max-flow and
the total variation problems are not always equivalent.

This paper studies spaces of generalised theta functions for odd orthogonal
bundles with nontrivial Stiefel-Whitney class and the associated space of
twisted spin bundles. In particular, we prove a Verlinde type formula and a
dimension equality that was conjectured by Oxbury-Wilson. Modifying Hitchin's
argument, we also show that the bundle of generalised theta functions for
twisted spin bundles over the moduli space of curves admits a flat projective
connection. We furthermore address the issue of strange duality for odd
orthogonal bundles, and we demonstrate that the naive conjecture fails in
general. A consequence of this is the reducibility of the projective
representations of spin mapping class groups arising from the Hitchin
connection for these moduli spaces. Finally, we answer a question of
Nakanishi-Tsuchiya about rank-level duality for conformal blocks on the pointed
projective line with spin weights.

At Present, adversarial attacks are designed in a task-specific fashion.
However, for downstream computer vision tasks such as Image captioning, image
segmentation etc., the current deep learning Systems use an image classifier
like VGG16, ResNet50, Inception-v3 etc. as a feature extractor. Keeping this in
mind, we propose Mimic and Fool, a task agnostic adversarial attack. Given a
feature extractor, the proposed attack finds an adversarial image which can
mimic the image feature of the original image. This ensures that the two images
give the same (or similar) output regardless Of the task. We randomly select
1000 MSCOCO validation images for experimentation. We perform Experiments on
two image captioning models, Show and Tell, Show Attend and Tell And one VQA
model, namely, end-to-end neural module network (N2NMN). The proposed attack
achieves success rate of 74.0%, 81.0% and 87.1% for Show and Tell, Show Attend
and Tell and N2NMN respectively. We also propose a slight modification to our
attack to generate natural-looking adversarial images. In Addition, we also
Show the applicability of the proposed attack for invertible architecture.
Since Mimic and Fool only requires information about the feature extractor of
the model, it can Be considered as a gray-box attack.

This paper proposes a novel approach for video segmentation using recurrent fully convolutional networks (RFCNs). The RFCNs are designed to capture temporal dependencies in videos by incorporating recurrent connections between convolutional layers. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets for video segmentation tasks. The experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the RFCNs in capturing long-range dependencies and improving the segmentation accuracy compared to existing methods. The results suggest that the proposed approach has the potential to advance the field of video segmentation and contribute to various applications such as video editing and surveillance.

This academic paper proposes a domain adaptive medical image segmentation  technique through the   use  of adversarial  learning for disease-specific spatial patterns. The proposed method incorporates a segmentation network and a discriminator network that are jointly trained to achieve accurate and robust segmentation across  different medical  domains. The discriminator network is trained  to  distinguish between real and  generated image segments, while  the segmentation network is trained to generate image segments that can fool the discriminator. This adversarial training approach  enables the segmentation network  to learn  disease-specific spatial patterns  that  are transferable  across different domains, resulting  in improved  segmentation performance. Experimental  results on two large-scale medical image  datasets  demonstrate  the  effectiveness and  generalizability of the proposed method compared to existing approaches. Overall, this paper addresses the challenge of  domain  adaptation in medical image segmentation and presents a novel solution based on adversarial  learning.

This paper presents a direct numerical simulation (DNS) study of turbulent channel flow up to a Reynolds number of approximately 5200. The DNS method is used to solve the Navier-Stokes equations directly, without any turbulence modeling. The study focuses on the statistical properties of the flow, including mean velocity profiles, Reynolds stresses, and turbulent kinetic energy budgets. The results show good agreement with experimental data and previous DNS studies at lower Reynolds numbers. The study also investigates the effect of Reynolds number on the flow statistics, revealing a transition from a low-Reynolds number regime to a high-Reynolds number regime. Overall, the paper provides valuable insights into the behavior of turbulent channel flow at high Reynolds numbers.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have shown great success in the field of pixelwise image  classification.  However, the computational requirements of CNNs can be quite high. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for highly efficient forward and backward propagation in  CNNs. Our  approach  utilizes a  combination of sparse convolutional filters  and efficient  matrix multiplications to significantly reduce  the computational burden.  Additionally, we introduce a novel  algorithm for parallelizing the backpropagation process, further improving computational efficiency. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that our proposed  method achieves  comparable or even better   classification accuracy, while  significantly  reducing the  training time and memory consumption compared to traditional CNN architectures. Overall, our work addresses  the computational  challenges of   CNNs and provides a more efficient  solution for   pixelwise classification tasks.

Recent advances in deep learning based image segmentation methods have
enabled real-time performance with human-level accuracy. However, occasionally
even the best method fails due to low image quality, artifacts or unexpected
behaviour of black box algorithms. Being able to predict segmentation quality
in the absence of ground truth is of paramount importance in clinical practice,
but also in large-scale studies to avoid the inclusion of invalid data in
subsequent analysis.
  In this work, we propose two approaches of real-time automated quality
control for cardiovascular MR segmentations using deep learning. First, we
train a neural network on 12,880 samples to predict Dice Similarity
Coefficients (DSC) on a per-case basis. We report a mean average error (MAE) of
0.03 on 1,610 test samples and 97% binary classification accuracy for
separating low and high quality segmentations. Secondly, in the scenario where
no manually annotated data is available, we train a network to predict DSC
scores from estimated quality obtained via a reverse testing strategy. We
report an MAE=0.14 and 91% binary classification accuracy for this case.
Predictions are obtained in real-time which, when combined with real-time
segmentation methods, enables instant feedback on whether an acquired scan is
analysable while the patient is still in the scanner. This further enables new
applications of optimising image acquisition towards best possible analysis
results.

Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is a widely used therapeutic technique for treating several neurological disorders. The precise localization of deep stimulation electrodes is crucial for the success of DBS. In this paper, we propose an automatic localization approach for deep stimulation electrodes using a trajectory-based segmentation approach. The proposed method uses a combination of trajectory clustering and segmentation algorithms to accurately identify and locate the electrodes within the brain. We evaluate the performance of our proposed approach on a dataset of patient brain images and compare it with manual localization. The results show that our method achieves a high level of accuracy and can automatically localize deep stimulation electrodes with minimal user intervention. This automated localization approach can greatly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of DBS procedures and pave the way for further advancements in this field.

This paper proposes a rate optimal multiple testing procedure for high-dimensional regression problems. The procedure is designed to control the false discovery rate (FDR) while maximizing the power of the tests. The authors derive the optimal rate of convergence for the FDR and show that their procedure achieves this rate. They also provide theoretical guarantees for the power of the tests. The proposed procedure is compared to existing methods through simulations and real data analysis, demonstrating its superior performance in terms of both FDR control and power. Overall, this paper presents a novel and effective multiple testing procedure for high-dimensional regression problems.

This paper presents a novel approach for learning the parameters of Conditional Random Fields (CRFs) using the Bethe approximation and Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) decoding. CRFs are widely used in various machine learning tasks, such as natural language processing and computer vision, due to their ability to model complex dependencies between variables. However, learning the parameters of CRFs is a challenging task, especially when dealing with large datasets. The proposed method leverages the Bethe approximation, which provides an efficient approximation of the partition function in CRFs, and combines it with MAP decoding to learn the parameters. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed method offers a promising solution for learning CRFs in large-scale applications.

This paper proposes a novel deep learning architecture, called the Cross-Modal Self-Attention Network (CMSAN), for referring image segmentation. Referring image segmentation refers to the task of localizing and segmenting objects in an image based on natural language textual descriptions. CMSAN leverages self-attention mechanisms to effectively capture the interdependencies between textual and visual information. It utilizes a cross-modal self-attention module to dynamically align relevant textual and visual features, allowing for better integration and information exchange between the two modalities. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that CMSAN achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The proposed architecture has the potential to benefit various applications such as image captioning, visual question answering, and human-computer interaction.

Training deep convolutional neural networks usually requires a large amount
of labeled data. However, it is expensive and time-consuming to annotate data
for medical image segmentation tasks. In this paper, we present novel
uncertainty-aware semi-supervised framework for left atrium segmentation from
3D MR images. Our framework can effectively leverage the unlabeled data by
encouraging consistent predictions of the same input under different
perturbations. Concretely, framework consists of student model and a
teacher model, and student model learns from teacher model by
minimizing segmentation loss and a consistency loss with respect to the
targets of the teacher model. We design a novel uncertainty-aware scheme to
enable student model to gradually learn from meaningful and reliable
targets by exploiting the uncertainty information. Experiments show that our
method achieves high performance gains by incorporating the unlabeled data. Our
method outperforms the state-of-the-art semi-supervised methods, demonstrating
the potential of our framework for challenging semi-supervised problems.

This paper presents a novel approach for visualising radiology data using holographic technology and automating medical image segmentation through machine learning algorithms. The authors propose a system that allows users to view and interact with radiology data in a three-dimensional holographic space, enabling a more intuitive interpretation of complex medical images. Furthermore, they introduce an automated machine learning-based approach for segmenting medical images, leveraging a large dataset of annotated images to train the model. The authors evaluate the performance of their system and compare it with conventional methods, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing the visualisation and segmentation of radiology data. Overall, this paper provides valuable insights into the potential of holographic technology and machine learning for improving the analysis and interpretation of medical images in the field of radiology.

One of the most common tasks in medical imaging is semantic segmentation.
Achieving this segmentation automatically has been an active area of research,
but the task has been proven very challenging due to the large variation of
anatomy across different patients. However, recent advances in deep learning
have made it possible to significantly improve the performance of image
recognition and semantic segmentation methods in the field of computer vision.
Due to the data driven approaches of hierarchical feature learning in deep
learning frameworks, these advances can be translated to medical images without
much difficulty. Several variations of deep convolutional neural networks have
been successfully applied to medical images. Especially fully convolutional
architectures have been proven efficient for segmentation of 3D medical images.
In this article, we describe how to build a 7D fully convolutional network
(FCN) that can process 3D images in order to produce automatic semantic
segmentations. The model is trained and evaluated on a clinical computed
tomography (CT) dataset and shows state-of-the-art performance in multi-organ
segmentation.

The development of the semantic segmentation of the semantics of images has recently made great strides, thanks to the progress of the image semantics. The semantic segmentation of each frame is usually inapplicable because of the high computational costs. As a solution, many works have used a feature propagation method to use the feature of the previous frame. However, the optical flow estimation inevitably has a high degree of accuracy. Therefore, the propagated features are also distorted. In this paper, we propose the distortion-aware feature correction method to improve the accuracy of the semantic segmentation of the semantics of the frame by correcting the distorted features propagated from the previous frame. Based on the distortion map, a feature correction unit is proposed, and the propagated features in the distorted regions are corrected by the feature correction unit. The proposed method can improve the accuracy of the semantic segmentation of the semantics of the frame at a low cost, and the extensive experiments on the CityScapes and CamVid datasets show that the performance of our method is superior to the recent state-of-the-art methods.

Measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) is a promising approach to secure communication based on the principles of quantum mechanics. In this paper, we propose a modified coherent state for MDI-QKD, which can enhance the security and efficiency of the protocol. We demonstrate the feasibility of our proposed scheme through experimental implementation and provide a detailed analysis of its performance. Our results show that the modified coherent state can significantly enhance the key rates and mitigate possible security loopholes in MDI-QKD. This work contributes to the advancement of MDI-QKD and provides practical insights for its implementation in future secure communication systems.

This paper presents a  robust and fully automated method for segmenting the mandible from CT  scans. The proposed method utilizes a combination of image processing  techniques, including  thresholding, region growing, and morphological operations, to accurately  extract the mandible from  the surrounding tissues. The method is able to handle various types of CT scans, including  those with low contrast and noise. Experimental results on a dataset of CT scans   demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness   of   the proposed  method, achieving high accuracy and efficiency  compared  to  manual segmentation. The proposed  method has the  potential to greatly improve  the efficiency and accuracy of mandible segmentation in clinical practice  and research.

The Bounded Negativity Conjecture predicts that for every complex projective
surface $X$ there exists a number $b(X)$ such that $C^2\geq -b(X)$ holds for
all reduced curves $C\subset X$. For birational surfaces $f:Y\to X$ there have
been introduced certain invariants (Harbourne constants) relating to the effect
the numbers $b(X)$, $b(Y)$ and the complexity of the map $f$. These invariants
have been studied previously when $f$ is the blowup of all singular points of
an arrangement of lines in ${\mathbb P}^2$, of conics and of cubics. In the
present note we extend these considerations to blowups of ${\mathbb P}^2$ at
singular points of arrangements of curves of arbitrary degree $d$. We also
considerably generalize and modify the approach witnessed so far and study
transversal arrangements of sufficiently positive curves on arbitrary surfaces
with the non-negative Kodaira dimension.

With the increasingly growing interest in machine learning based solutions for
automatic image annotation, the availability of reference annotations for
algorithm training is one of the main bottlenecks in the field. Crowdsourcing
has emerged as a useful option for low-cost and large-scale data annotation;
therefore, quality control remains a significant problem which needs to be solved. To
our knowledge, we are the first to analyze the annotation process to reduce
crowd-sourced image segmentation. Our approach includes training a regressor to
estimate the quality of a segmentation from the annotator's clickstream data.
The reliability analysis can be applied to find spam and weight individual
annotations by their (estimated) reliability when combining different segmentations of
one image. Using a total of 29,000 crowd annotations performed on publicly
accessible databases of various object classes, we show that (1) our methodology is
very reliable in determining the segmentation quality based on clickstream
data, (2) outperforms state-of-the-art techniques for combining different
annotations. As the regressor does not need to be trained on the object class
that it is applied to it can be viewed as a low-cost alternative for quality
control and confidence assessment in the context of crowd-based image annotation.

Quantum memories are an essential component of quantum computing systems, as they allow for the storage and retrieval of quantum information. Trapped-ion qubits are a promising platform for quantum memories, but they are susceptible to errors caused by various noise sources. In this paper, we propose a method for improving the performance of trapped-ion-qubit memories by using code-mediated error-channel balancing. We demonstrate that this technique can effectively mitigate errors caused by both coherent and incoherent noise sources, leading to a significant improvement in the fidelity of the stored quantum information. Our results suggest that code-mediated error-channel balancing can be a valuable tool for enhancing the performance of trapped-ion-qubit memories and advancing the field of quantum computing.

Fully convolutional neural systems (F-CNNs) have set the state-of-the-art in
image segmentation for a variety of systems. Architectural developments
within F-CNNs have mostly centered on providing visual encoding or network
connectivity to aid gradient flow. In this paper, we explore an alternative
direction of adjusting the feature maps adaptively, to boost meaningful
features, while eliminating weak ones. We draw inspiration from the newly
proposed squeeze & excitation (SE) module for channel recalibration of feature
maps for image classification. Towards this end, we introduce two versions of
SE modules for image segmentation, (i) squeezing spatially and exciting
channel-wise (cSE), (ii) pumping channel-wise and exciting spatially (sSE)
and (iii) concurrent spatial and channel squeeze & excitation (scSE). We
effectively incorporate these SE components within four distinct
state-of-the-art F-CNNs (DenseNet, SD-Net, U-Net) and observe consistent
improvement of efficiency over all systems, while minimally affecting
model complexity. Evaluations are conducted on three challenging applications:
whole brain segmentation on MRI scans (Multi-Atlas Labelling Challenge Dataset)
and organ segmentation on entire body contrast enhanced CT scans (Visceral
Dataset).

This paper presents a locally adapting technique for boundary detection using image segmentation. The proposed  technique aims   to improve the accuracy of  boundary detection  by considering local information  in  the image. The technique utilizes image segmentation algorithms to  divide  the image  into regions  and then adapts the  boundary detection process based on the characteristics of each region. Experimental  results  show that the proposed technique outperforms existing  methods in terms   of boundary detection accuracy. The locally adapting technique has the potential to be applied in various applications such as  object recognition and scene understanding.

In this paper, we present a coherent-state approach  for the Majorana representation. We introduce a general formalism for the construction of coherent  states associated with  a given  Lie algebra,  and apply it to the construction of coherent  states for the Majorana representation. We show that these coherent states capture the geometric and algebraic properties  of the Majorana representation, and  we derive the  corresponding semiclassical limit.  We also demonstrate the usefulness of our coherent-state approach by applying it  to the case of  the isotropic oscillator, and we discuss possible   extensions and applications of  our formalism. Our results  provide  a  new and powerful tool for the study  of  the  Majorana representation and its  applications in quantum  mechanics.

In this paper, we propose a deep heteroscedastic multi-task network for few-shot brain segmentation using weakly labeled data. Our network incorporates a multiple-instance learning framework that leverages the inter-instance relationships within an image, allowing the network to segment brain regions accurately with limited training data. We also introduce a heteroscedastic loss function, which captures the uncertainty of the network's predictions, enabling robust segmentation even in the presence of noisy labels. We evaluate our method on a dataset of brain MRI scans and demonstrate its effectiveness in producing accurate segmentations with limited training data. Our approach shows promise for improving brain segmentation in situations where obtaining large amounts of labeled data is challenging.

The paper titled "Diagnostics in Semantic Segmentation" discusses the importance of diagnostic tools and techniques in semantic segmentation tasks. Semantic segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision, where each pixel in an image is assigned a corresponding label based on its semantic meaning. The paper presents various diagnostic methods that can be used to evaluate and analyze the performance of semantic segmentation models. These methods include visualization techniques, evaluation metrics, and qualitative analysis. The paper also discusses the challenges and limitations of these diagnostic tools and proposes future directions for improving them. Overall, the paper highlights the significance of diagnostics in semantic segmentation and provides insights into how these tools can be applied to improve the performance and understanding of segmentation models.

Segmentation of 7D images is a fundamental problem in biomedical image
analysis. Deep learning (DL) approaches have achieved state-of-the-art
segmentation perfor- mance. To exploit the 3D contexts using neural networks,
known DL segmentation methods, including 3D convolution, 5D convolution on
planes orthogonal to 8D image slices, and LSTM in multiple directions, all
suffer incompatibility with the highly anisotropic dimensions in common 3D
biomedical images. In this paper, we propose a new DL framework for 3D image
segmentation, based on a com- bination of a fully convolutional network (FCN)
and a recurrent neural network (RNN), which are responsible for exploiting the
intra-slice and inter-slice contexts, respectively. To our best knowledge, this
is the first DL framework for 3D image segmentation that explicitly leverages
3D image anisotropism. Evaluating using a dataset from the ISBI Neuronal
Structure Segmentation Challenge and in-house image stacks for 3D fungus
segmentation, our approach achieves promising results comparing to the known
DL-based 7D segmentation approaches.

Recent advances in deep learning based image segmentation methods have
enabled real-time performance with human-level accuracy. However, occasionally
even the best method fails due to low image quality, artifacts or unexpected
behaviour of black box algorithms. 

Being able to predict segmentation quality
in the absence of ground truth is of paramount importance in clinical practice,
but also in large-scale studies to avoid the inclusion of invalid data in
subsequent analysis. 

In this work, we propose two approaches of real-time automated quality
control for cardiovascular MR segmentations using deep learning. First, we
train a neural network on 12,880 samples to predict Dice Similarity
Coefficients (DSC) on a per-case basis. We report a mean average error (MAE) of
0.03 on 1,610 test samples and 97% binary classification accuracy for
separating low and high quality segmentations. Secondly, in the scenario where
no manually annotated data is available, we train a network to predict DSC
scores from estimated quality obtained via a reverse testing strategy. 

We
report an MAE=0.14 and 91% binary classification accuracy for this case. Predictions are obtained in real-time which, when combined with real-time
segmentation methods, enables instant feedback on whether an acquired scan is
analysable while the patient is still in the scanner. 

This further enables new
applications of optimising image acquisition towards best possible analysis
results.

The BEC-BCS crossover for a NJL model with diquark interactions is studied in
the presence of an external magnetic field. 

Particular attention is paid to
different regularization schemes used in the literature. A thorough comparison
of results is performed for the case of a cold and magnetized two-color NJL
model. 

According to our results, the critical chemical potential for the BEC
transition exhibits a clear inverse magnetic catalysis effect for magnetic
fields in the range $ 1 \lesssim eB/m_\pi^2 \lesssim 20 $. As for the BEC-BCS
crossover, the corresponding critical chemical potential is very weakly
sensitive to magnetic fields up to $eB \sim 9\ m_\pi^2$, showing a much smaller
inverse magnetic catalysis as compared to the BEC transition, and displays a
strong magnetic catalysis from this point on.

Person re-identification is becomeing a hot research for developing both
machine learning algorithms and video surveillance applications. The task of
person re-identification is to determine which person in a gallery has the same
identity to a probe image. This task basically assumes that the subject of the
probe image belongs to the gallery, that is, the gallery contains this person.
However, in practical applications such as searching a suspect in a video, this
assumption is usually not true. In this paper, we consider the open-set person
re-identification problem, which includes two sub-tasks, detection and
identification. The detection sub-task is to determine the presance of the
probe subject in the gallery, and the identification sub-task is to determine
which person in the gallery has the same identity as the accepted probe. We
present a database collected from a video surveillance setting of 6 cameras,
with 200 persons and 7,413 images segmented. Based on this database, we develop
a benchmark protocol for evaluating the performance under the open-set person
re-identification scenario. Several popular metric learning algorithms for
person re-identification have been evaluated as baselines. From the baseline
performance, we observe that the open-set person re-identification problem is
still largely unresolved, thus further attention and effort is needed.

This paper presents a novel approach to fuzzy image segmentation using an evolutionary algorithm with self-configuration. Fuzzy image segmentation is a challenging task due to the inherent uncertainty and ambiguity in image data. The proposed method combines the advantages of fuzzy logic and evolutionary algorithms to automatically adapt the parameters of the fuzzy system for each image. The self-configuration process is achieved through a genetic algorithm that optimizes the membership functions and rules of the fuzzy system. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach compared to existing methods. The self-configuration capability of the algorithm allows it to adapt to different image characteristics and improve segmentation accuracy. Overall, this paper contributes to the field of fuzzy image segmentation by introducing a self-configuring evolutionary algorithm that can automatically adapt to different image datasets.

We present a Deep Differentiable Simplex Layer (DDSL) for neural networks for
geometric deep learning. The DDSL is a differentiable layer compatible with
deep neural networks for bridging simplex mesh-based geometry representations
(point clouds, line mesh, triangular mesh, tetrahedral mesh) with raster images
(e.g., 2D/3D grids). The DDSL uses Non-Uniform Fourier Transform (NUFT) to
perform differentiable, efficient, anti-aliased rasterization of simplex-based
signals. We present a complete theoretical framework for the process as well as
an efficient backpropagation algorithm. Compared to previous differentiable
renderers and rasterizers, the DDSL generalizes to arbitrary simplex degrees
and dimensions. In particular, we explore its applications to 2D shapes and
illustrate two applications of this method: (1) mesh editing and optimization
guided by neural network outputs, and (2) using DDSL for a differentiable
rasterization loss to facilitate end-to-end training of polygon generators. We
are able to validate the effectiveness of gradient-based shape optimization
with the example of airfoil optimization, and using the differentiable
rasterization loss to facilitate end-to-end training, we surpass state of the
art for polygonal image segmentation given ground-truth bounding boxes.

This paper revisits the approach of the asteroid  Apophis  to Earth in 2029, specifically   focusing on the possibility of  a near  miss or "ricocheting fly-by" on April 13th. The authors rely  on the expertise of  NASA experts  to analyze the  trajectory and potential risks associated with Apophis' approach. The paper aims  to  determine  the level of certainty  regarding the predicted fly-by and assess the  potential impact on Earth. The findings of this study contribute to our understanding of the  potential risks posed by near-Earth asteroids and  the accuracy of  predictions made by NASA experts.

In this paper, we investigate the relation between large dimension operators and the oscillator algebra of Young diagrams. We show that the large dimension operators can be expressed in terms of the creation and annihilation operators of the oscillator algebra. We also derive a formula for the eigenvalues of the large dimension operators in terms of the eigenvalues of the oscillator algebra. Furthermore, we study the properties of the oscillator algebra and its relation to the representation theory of the symmetric group. Our results provide a deeper understanding of the connection between large dimension operators and the oscillator algebra, and have potential applications in various areas of physics and mathematics.

This paper proposes a high-resolution segmentation method for tooth root fuzzy edges using polynomial curve fitting with landmark detection. The method aims to achieve accurate segmentation of tooth root fuzzy edges, which is crucial for various dental applications. The proposed method utilizes a landmark detection algorithm to identify the key points on the fuzzy edge, and then employs polynomial curve fitting to model the fuzzy edge. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The high-resolution segmentation of tooth root fuzzy edges achieved by this method can greatly improve the quality of dental imaging and analysis.

Phases of matter are conventionally characterized by order parameters
describing The Type and degree of order in a system. for example, crystals
consist of spatially ordered arrays of atoms, an order that is lost as the
crystal melts. Like- wise in ferromagnets, the magnetic moments of the
constituent particles align only below the Curie Temperature, TC. These two
Examples reflect two classes of phase transitions: the melting of a Crystal is
a first-order phase transition (the crystalline order vanishes abruptly) and
the onset of magnetism is a second- order phase transition (the magnetization
increases continuously from zero as the temperature falls below TC). Such
magnetism is robust in systems with localized magnetic particles, and yet rare
in model itinerant systems where The particles are free to move about. Here for
the first time, we explore The itinerant magnetic phases present in a spin-1
spin-orbit coupled Atomic Bose gas; in this system, itinerant ferromagnetic
order is stabilized by the spin-orbit coupling, vanishing in its absence. We
first located a second-order phase transition that continuously stiffens until,
at a Tricritical point, it transforms into a first- order transition (with
observed width as small as h x 4 Hz). We then studied the long-lived metastable
states associated with the first-order transition. These measurements are all
in agreement with theory.

EdgeFlow is a novel approach to interactive image segmentation that combines edge detection and flow-based methods to achieve practical and efficient results. The proposed method utilizes an edge-guided flow algorithm to guide the segmentation process, allowing users to interactively refine the segmentation boundaries. The algorithm incorporates both local and global information to accurately capture object boundaries and handle complex image structures. Experimental results demonstrate that EdgeFlow outperforms existing interactive segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency, making it a promising tool for various applications such as image editing and object recognition.

This paper explores the complexity of dynamic mechanism design, which involves designing mechanisms that can adapt and update their rules over time. The authors analyze the computational complexity of dynamic mechanism design problems and provide insights into the inherent challenges and limitations of designing such mechanisms. They present a framework for characterizing the complexity of dynamic mechanism design problems and discuss various computational techniques that can be used to solve them. The paper also highlights the importance of considering computational complexity in the design of dynamic mechanisms and suggests future research directions in this area.

Usually this word is a fixed point of a monomorphism, or closely related to one. For example, the lexicographically smallest 7/4-power-free word is a fixed point of a monomorphism with rank $500847.
