This paper presents a new approach for the design and implementation of generalized coupled-line all-pass phasers. The proposed method leverages the advantages of coupled-line structures to achieve a compact and efficient design with improved performance. The design methodology includes the derivation of the characteristic equations and the design parameters of the all-pass phasers. The proposed phasers are capable of producing phase shifts with arbitrary discrete values. The performance of the proposed phasers is evaluated through simulations, and the results demonstrate their superior performance in terms of phase shift accuracy, insertion loss, and return loss. Furthermore, a practical design example is presented to illustrate the application of the proposed phasers in microwave systems. Overall, this paper provides a novel and practical solution for the design and implementation of generalized coupled-line all-pass phasers.

Recent state-of-the-art image segmentation algorithms are mostly based on
deep neural networks, thanks to their high performance and fast computation
time. However, these methods are usually trained in supervised manner, which
requires large number of high quality ground-truth segmentation masks. On the
other hand, classical image segmentation approaches such as level-set methods
are formulated in self-supervised manner by minimizing energy functions such
as Mumford-Shah functional, so they are still useful to help generation of
segmentation masks without labels. Unfortunately, these algorithms are usually
computationally expensive and often have limitation in semantic segmentation.
In this paper, we propose a novel loss function based on Mumford-Shah
functional that can be used in deep-learning based image segmentation without
or with small labeled data. This loss function is based on the observation that
the softmax layer of deep neural networks has striking similarity to the
characteristic function in Mumford-Shah functional. We show that the new
loss function enables semi-supervised and unsupervised segmentation. In
addition, our loss function can be also used as a regularized function to
enhance supervised semantic segmentation algorithms. Experimental results on
multiple datasets demonstrate effectiveness of the proposed method.

We discuss the compatibility of quantum gravity with dynamical matter degrees
of freedom. Specifically, we present bounds we obtained in [1] on the allowed
number and type of matter fields within asymptotically safe quantum gravity. As
a novel result, we show bounds on the allowed number of spin-3/2
(Rarita-Schwinger) fields, e.g., gravitino. These bounds, obtained within
truncated Renormalization Group flows, indicate compatibility of asymptotic
safety with matter fields of standard model. Further, they suggest that
extensions of the matter content of the standard model are severely restricted
in asymptotic safety. This means that searches for new particles at colliders
could provide experimental tests for this particular approach to quantum
gravity.

A revised collection of the number of sunspot groups is presented. This collection is based on the work of Hoyt and Schatten (Sol. Phys. 179, 189, 1998). There are mainly two main changes: the elimination of many observations from the Maunder minimum (MM) and the addition of a few long series. Several minor corrections are also given. In addition, we have recalculated the percentage of active days during the MM on the basis of this new collection as a reliable indicator of solar activity. In this way, the level of solar activity obtained in this work is higher than that obtained from the original Hoyt and Schatten data. However, it remains compatible with a solar grand minimum. The new collection is also available in digital form.

This  paper presents a novel approach for segmenting 3D  medical images using the live-wire technique. The live-wire technique  is  a popular  method  for segmenting 2D  images, but its application to 3D images has been limited due to  the computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a modified live-wire  algorithm that takes advantage of   parallel processing and GPU  acceleration to overcome the  computational challenges.  We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a  dataset of 3D medical images,  achieving high segmentation accuracy  and efficiency. Our method has  the  potential to improve the segmentation process in medical imaging applications, leading  to more  accurate diagnoses and treatment planning.

This paper explores the concept of longest gapped repeats and palindromes in DNA sequences. Longest gapped repeats are defined as repeated sequences with a certain number of gaps between them, while palindromes are sequences that read the same forwards and backwards. The authors present algorithms for efficiently identifying and counting these patterns in DNA sequences. They also discuss the biological significance of longest gapped repeats and palindromes, including their potential role in gene regulation and evolution. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions in this area.

This paper proposes a method for segmenting overlapping wear particles in microscopic images with limited labelled data and imbalanced samples. The proposed method utilizes a deep learning framework and incorporates a novel data augmentation technique to address the scarcity of labelled data. Additionally, a weighted loss function is introduced to handle the imbalanced nature of the dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness, even with limited labelled data and imbalanced samples. This research contributes to the field of wear particle analysis and provides a practical solution for segmenting overlapping wear particles in microscopic images.

This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the criteria necessary for determining the efficiency and reliability of measures of quantum correlations in physical systems. We discuss the importance of both theoretical and experimental considerations in the design and evaluation of these measures, highlighting the various challenges faced in this field. Specifically, we explore the properties that must be satisfied by a good measure of quantum correlations, such as the ability to capture both entanglement and other nonclassical correlations, as well as the ability to account for the structure and dynamics of the underlying system. Furthermore, we provide a systematic framework for determining the reliability of different measures, including the use of logical consistency, computational efficiency, and experimental feasibility as criteria for evaluation. Finally, we highlight some recent advancements in the field, including the development of new measures and the application of machine learning techniques to improve the accuracy and efficiency of quantum correlation measurements. Overall, this paper provides a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners in the field of quantum information science, offering insights into the criteria that should guide the selection and evaluation of measures of quantum correlations.

Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have become increasingly popular for
solving a variety of computer vision tasks, ranging from image classification
to image segmentation. Recently, autonneomous vehicles have created a demand for
depth information, which is often obtained using hardware sensors such as Light
detection and ranging (LIDAR). Although it can provide precise distance
measurements, most LIDARs are still far too expensive to sell in mass-produced
consumer vehicles, which has motivated methods to generate depth information
from commodity automotive sensors like cameras.
  In this paper, we propose an approach called Deep Sensor Cloning (DSC). The
idea is to use Convolutional Neural Networks in conjunction with inexpensive
sensors to replicate the 3D point-clouds that are created by expensive LIDARs.
To accomplish this, we develop a new dataset (DSDepth) and a new family of CNN
architectures (DSCnets). While previous tasks such as KITTI depth prediction
use an interpolated RGB-D images as ground-truth for training, we instead use
DSCnets to directly predict LIDAR point-clouds. When we compare the output of
our models to a $75,000 LIDAR, we find that our most accurate DSCnet achieves a
relative error of 5.77% using a single camera and 4.69% using stereo cameras.

This paper proposes a novel approach to improve multi-modal learning by leveraging uni-modal teachers. Multi-modal learning, which involves learning from multiple sources of information, has shown promising results in various domains. However, it often requires a large amount of labeled data for each modality, which can be expensive and time-consuming to obtain. In this paper, we introduce the concept of uni-modal teachers, which are pre-trained models that specialize in a single modality. We then propose a framework that combines the predictions of these uni-modal teachers to improve the performance of a multi-modal model. Our experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Furthermore, we show that our framework can effectively handle missing modalities and adapt to new modalities without retraining the entire model. Overall, our findings suggest that leveraging uni-modal teachers can significantly enhance multi-modal learning and make it more accessible in real-world applications.

In this paper, we present the Medusa algorithm, a novel approach for constructing polynomial matings. Polynomial matings have been widely used in computational mathematics for generating fractal images and exploring various mathematical properties. However, existing algorithms have limitations in terms of efficiency and flexibility. The Medusa algorithm overcomes these limitations by employing a recursive construction procedure that adapts to the structure of the polynomials being mated. We provide a detailed description of the algorithm and demonstrate its efficiency and effectiveness through various experimental results. Our findings indicate that the Medusa algorithm consistently outperforms existing methods in terms of both speed and quality of the generated fractal images. Furthermore, the algorithm offers enhanced flexibility in terms of the types of matings that can be generated, allowing for the exploration of new mathematical possibilities. Overall, the Medusa algorithm represents a significant advancement in the field of computational mathematics and has the potential to greatly enhance the study and application of polynomial matings.

This paper presents a survey on machine learning techniques for auto labeling of video, audio, and  text data. Auto labeling is the process of automatically assigning labels or tags to data without human intervention. The paper provides an  overview of the different machine learning algorithms  and approaches that have been used for auto labeling in  the context  of  video,  audio,  and  text data. It  discusses the challenges and limitations of these techniques  and provides insights into the current state of the  field. The  survey also highlights the  potential applications  and future  directions for research in this area. Overall, this paper serves as a comprehensive resource for researchers and  practitioners interested  in auto  labeling of video,  audio,  and text data  using machine  learning  techniques.

Collecting training data from the Physical world Is usually time-consuming
and even dangerous for Fragile robots, And thus, recent advances in robot
learning advocate the use of simulators as the training platform.
Unfortunately, the reality gap between synthetic and real visual data prohibits
direct migration of the models trained in virtual worlds to the real world.
This paper proposes a modular architecture for tackling the virtual-to-real
problem. The proposed architecture separates the learning model into a
perception module and a control policy module, and uses semantic image
Segmentation as the meta Representation for relating these two modules. The
perception module translates the perceived RGB image to semantic image
segmentation. The Control policy module is implemented as a deep reinforcement
learning agent, which performs actions based on the translated image
segmentation. Our Architecture is evaluated in an obstacle avoidance task and a
target following task. Experimental results show that our architecture
significantly outperforms all of the baseline methods in both virtual and real
environments, and demonstrates a faster learning curve than them. We also
Present a detailed analysis for a variety of variant configurations, and
validate the transferability of our modular architecture.

This paper presents a comprehensive survey of data mining techniques for social media analysis. Social media platforms have become a rich source of user-generated content, providing valuable insights into various aspects of human behavior and societal trends. However, the sheer volume and complexity of social media data pose significant challenges for effective analysis. In this survey, we review and categorize the existing data mining techniques that have been applied to social media analysis. We discuss the different types of social media data, such as text, images, and networks, and the specific challenges associated with each type. We then provide an overview of the various data mining techniques, including text mining, image analysis, sentiment analysis, and social network analysis, and discuss their applications in social media analysis. Finally, we highlight the current trends and future directions in this field, including the integration of multiple data mining techniques and the development of novel algorithms to handle the unique characteristics of social media data. This survey serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners interested in leveraging data mining techniques for social media analysis.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have shown to be powerful medical image
segmentation models. In this study, we address some of the main unresolved
issues regarding these models. Specifically, training of these models on small
medical image datasets Is still challenging, with Many studies promoting
techniques Such as transfer learning. Moreover, these models are infamous for
producing over-confident predictions and for failing silently when presented
with out-of-distribution (OOD) data at test time. In this paper, we advocate
for multi-task learning, i.e., training a single model on several different
datasets, spanning several different Organs Of interest and different imaging
modalities. We show that not only a single CNN learns to automatically
recognize The context and accurately segment the Organ of Interest in each
context, but Also that such a joint model often has more accurate and
better-calibrated predictions than dedicated models trained separately on each
dataset. Our experiments show that multi-task learning can outperform transfer
learning in medical image segmentation Tasks. for detecting OOD data, we
propose a method based on spectral analysis of CNN feature maps. We show that
different datasets, representing different imaging modalities and/or different
organs of interest, have distinct spectral signatures, which can be used to
identify whether or not a test image is similar to the images used to train a
model. We show that This approach is far more accurate than OOD detection based
on prediction uncertainty. The methods proposed in this paper contribute
significantly to improving the accuracy and reliability of CNN-based medical
image segmentation models.

What is aging? Mechanistic answers to this question remain elusive despite
decades of  research. Here, we  propose a mathematical model of cellular aging
based on a model gene interaction  network. Our network model is made   of only
non-aging components - the  biological functions  of gene  interactions decrease
with a constant mortality rate. Death of   a cell occurs in the model when an
essential gene loses all of its interactions  to  other genes, equivalent  to the
deletion of an  essential  gene. Gene interactions  are stochastic based on  a
binomial distribution. We show that the defining characteristic of biological
aging, the exponential   increase  of mortality rate over time, can arise from
this gene  network  model during the early stage of aging. Hence, we demonstrate
that cellular aging is an emergent property of  this  model network. Our model
predicts that the rate   of aging,  defined by  the Gompertz coefficient,  is
approximately proportional to the average number of active interactions per
gene and that the stochastic heterogeneity of  gene interactions is an important
factor in the   dynamics of the  aging process.  This theoretic framework offers a
mechanistic foundation for  the pleiotropic nature of aging  and can provide
insights on cellular aging.

This paper introduces a novel  approach for modelling spatially correlated aleatoric uncertainty in stochastic segmentation networks. The proposed method  leverages  the inherent spatial correlation present  in many  segmentation tasks to  improve uncertainty estimation. The authors demonstrate the  effectiveness  of their approach on  several  benchmark  datasets, achieving state-of-the-art   performance in terms of uncertainty estimation. The results  suggest that incorporating spatial correlation in aleatoric uncertainty modelling can lead to more  accurate and reliable segmentation predictions.  The proposed method has the  potential to enhance the performance  of various computer vision applications that rely on segmentation networks.

Conventional deformable registration methods aim at solving an optimization
model carefully designed on image pairs and their computational costs are
exceptionally high. In contrast, recent deep learning based approaches can
provide fast deformation estimation. These heuristic network architectures are
fully data-driven and thus lack explicit geometric constraints, e.g.,
topology-preserving, which are indispensable to generate plausible
deformations. We design new deep learning based framework to optimize a
diffeomorphic model via multi-scale propagation in order to integrate
advantages and avoid limitations of these two categories of approaches.
Specifically, we introduce a generic optimization model to formulate
diffeomorphic registration and develop series of learnable architectures to
obtain propagative updating in coarse-to-fine feature space. Moreover, we
propose a novel bilevel self-tuned training strategy, allowing efficient search
of task-specific hyper-parameters. This training strategy increases the
flexibility to various types of data while reduces computational and human
burdens. We conduct two groups of image registration experiments on 3D volume
datasets including image-to-atlas registration on brain MRI data and
image-to-image registration on liver CT data. Extensive results demonstrate the
state-of-the-art performance of the proposed method with diffeomorphic
guarantee and extreme efficiency. We also apply our framework to challenging
multi-modal image registration, and investigate how our registration to support
the down-streaming tasks for medical image analysis including multi-modal
fusion and image segmentation.

3D convolution neural networks (CNN) have been proved very successful in
parsing organs or tumours in 3D medical images, but it remains sophisticated
and time-consuming to choose or design proper 3D networks given different task
contexts. Recently, Neural Architecture Search (NAS) is proposed to solve this
problem by searching for the best network architecture automatically. 

However,
the inconsistency between search stage and deployment stage often exists in NAS
algorithms due to memory constraints and large search space, which could become
more serious when applying NAS to some memory and time consuming tasks, such as
3D medical image segmentation. In this paper, we propose coarse-to-fine neural
architecture search (C2FNAS) to automatically search a 3D segmentation network
from scratch without inconsistency on network size or input size. Specifically,
we divide the search procedure into two stages: 1) the coarse stage, where we
search the macro-level topology of the network, i.e. 

how each convolution
module is connected to other modules; 2) the fine stage, where we search at
micro-level for operations in each cell based on previous searched macro-level
topology. 

The coarse-to-fine manner divides the search procedure into two
consecutive stages and meanwhile resolves the inconsistency. We evaluate our
method on 10 public datasets from Medical Segmentation Decalthon (MSD)
challenge, and achieve state-of-the-art performance with the network searched
using one dataset, which demonstrates the effectiveness and generalization of
our searched models.

This paper proposes a method for enforcing mutual consistency of hard regions in semi-supervised medical image segmentation. The authors argue that existing methods often struggle with accurately segmenting hard regions in medical images due to limited labeled data. To address this issue, they propose a novel framework that leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to enforce mutual consistency between the predictions of hard regions. The proposed method consists of two steps: initial segmentation using a deep neural network and refinement using a consistency regularization term. Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy for hard regions. The authors conclude that their method can effectively improve the performance of semi-supervised medical image segmentation by enforcing mutual consistency of hard regions.

S-folds are generalizations of orientifolds in type IIB string theory, such
that the geometric identifications are accompanied by non-trivial S-duality
transformations. They were recently used by Garcia-Etxebarria and Regalado to
provide the first construction of four dimensional N=3 superconformal theories. In this note, we classify the different variants of these N=3 preserving
S-folds, distinguished by an analog of discrete torsion, using both a direct
analysis of the different torsion classes and the compactification of the
S-folds to three dimensional M-theory backgrounds. 

Upon adding D3-branes, these
variants lead to different classes of N=3 superconformal field theories. 

We
also analyze the holographic duals of these theories, and in particular clarify
the role of discrete gauge and global symmetries in holography. 

In the main part of the paper, certain properties of cohomology groups
associated to the S-folds were conjectured and used. This arXiv version
includes an appendix written by Kiyonori Gomi in 2023 providing the proofs of
the required properties using the technique of Borel equivariant cohomology,
whose brief review is also provided.

We present an information-theoretic approach to lower bound the oracle
complexity of nonsmooth black box convex optimisation, unifying previous lower
bounding techniques by identifying a combinatorial problem, namely string
guessing, as a single source of hardness. As a measure of complexity we use
distributional oracle complexity, which subsumes randomised oracle complexity
as well as worst-case oracle complexity. We obtain strong lower bounds on
distributional oracle complexity for the box $[-1,1]^n$, as well as for the
$L^p$-ball for $p \geq 1$ (for both low-scale and large-scale regimes),
matching worst-case upper bounds, and hence we close the gap between
distributional complexity, and in particular, randomised complexity, and
worst-case complexity. Furthermore, the bounds remain essentially the same for
high-probability and bounded-error oracle complexity, and even for combination
of the two, i.e., bounded-error high-probability oracle complexity. This
considerably extends the applicability of known bounds.

Although deep models have greatly improved the accuracy and robustness of
image segmentation, obtaining segmentation results with highly accurate
boundaries and fine structures is still a challenging problem. In this paper,
we propose a simple yet powerful Boundary-Aware Segmentation Network (BASNet),
which comprises a predict-refine architecture and a hybrid loss, for highly
accurate image segmentation. The predict-refine architecture consists of a
densely Supervised encoder-decoder network and a residual refinement module,
which are respectively used to predict and Refine a segmentation Probability
map. the hybrid loss is A Combination of the binary cross entropy, structural
similarity and intersection-over-union losses, Which guide the network to learn
three-level (ie, pixel-, patch- and map- Level) hierarchy representations. We
evaluate our BASNet on two reverse tasks including salient object segmentation,
camouflaged object segmentation, showing that it achieves very competitive
performance with sharp segmentation boundaries. Importantly, BASNet runs at
over 70 fps on a single GPU which benefits many potential real applications.
Based on BASNet, we further developed two (close to) commercial applications:
AR COPY & PASTE, in which BASNet is Integrated with augmented reality for
"COPYING" and "PASTING" real-world objects, and OBJECT CUT, which is a
web-based tool for automatic object background removal. Both applications have
already drawn Huge amount of Attention and have important real-world impacts.
The code and two applications will be publicly available at:
https://github.com/NathanUA/BASNet.

This paper presents a study on noise reduction and hyperfine level coherence in spontaneous noise spectroscopy of atomic vapor. The authors investigate the effects of various noise reduction techniques, such as lock-in amplification and phase-sensitive detection, on the coherence of hyperfine levels in atomic vapor. The results show that these techniques can significantly improve the signal-to-noise ratio and enhance the coherence of the hyperfine levels. The findings have important implications for applications in quantum information processing and precision measurements.

nnDetection: A Self-configuring Method for Medical Object Detection

Abstract: 

Medical object detection plays a crucial role in various clinical applications such as disease diagnosis, treatment planning, and surgical assistance. However, manual configuration of object detection models for specific medical tasks can be time-consuming and error-prone. In this paper, we propose nnDetection, a self-configuring method for medical object detection, which automatically adapts the model architecture and hyperparameters to the given medical task and dataset. Our method incorporates an adaptive neural network architecture search algorithm to dynamically select and optimize the architecture based on the specific features and characteristics of the medical images. Additionally, we employ a hyperparameter optimization strategy that finds the optimal set of hyperparameters for the object detection model. Experimental results on a benchmark medical image dataset demonstrate that nnDetection outperforms manually configured object detection models in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. The self-configuring nature of nnDetection makes it a valuable tool for medical professionals, as it eliminates the need for extensive manual tuning and allows for more reliable and accurate medical object detection.

This paper presents a robust principal component analysis (PCA) algorithm that incorporates partial subspace knowledge. Traditional PCA methods assume that the data lies entirely in a low-dimensional subspace, which may not be accurate in real-world scenarios. The proposed algorithm leverages partial subspace knowledge to improve the accuracy of PCA. The algorithm is based on a convex optimization framework and utilizes a nuclear norm penalty to encourage low-rank solutions. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in accurately recovering the underlying subspace structure even when only partial knowledge is available. The algorithm also outperforms existing robust PCA methods in terms of robustness and computational efficiency. Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of robust PCA and offers a practical solution for scenarios where only partial subspace knowledge is available.

Segmentation is a fundamental task for extracting semantically meaningful
regions from an image. The goal of segmentation algorithms is to accurately
assign object labels to each image location. However, image-noise, shortcomings
of algorithms, and image ambiguities cause uncertainty in label assignment.
Estimating the uncertainty in label assignment is important in multiple
application domains, such as segmenting tumors from medical images for
radiation treatment planning. One way to estimate these uncertainties is
through the computation of posteriors of Bayesian models, which is
computationally prohibitive for many practical applications. On the other hand,
most computationally efficient methods fail to estimate label uncertainty. We
therefore propose in this paper the Active Mean Fields (AMF) approach, a
technique based on Bayesian modeling that uses a mean-field approximation to
efficiently compute a segmentation and its corresponding uncertainty. Based on
a variational formulation, the resulting convex model combines any
label-likelihood measure with a prior on the length of the segmentation
boundary. A specific implementation of that model is the Chan-Vese segmentation
model (CV), in which the binary segmentation task is defined by a Gaussian
likelihood and a prior regularizing the length of the segmentation boundary.
Furthermore, the Euler-Lagrange equations derived from the AMF model are
equivalent to those of the popular Rudin-Osher-Fatemi (ROF) model for image
denoising. Solutions to the AMF model can thus be implemented by directly
utilizing highly-efficient ROF solvers on log-likelihood ratio fields. We
qualitatively assess the approach on synthetic data as well as on real natural
and medical images. For a quantitative evaluation, we apply our approach to the
icgbench dataset.

The paper "On the Convex Pfaff-Darboux Theorem of Ekeland and Nirenberg" explores the convex Pfaff-Darboux theorem, which is a fundamental result in convex analysis. The authors provide a detailed proof of this theorem and discuss its implications in various areas of mathematics, including differential geometry and optimization theory. The paper also presents several examples and applications of the convex Pfaff-Darboux theorem, highlighting its importance in understanding the behavior of convex functions and their level sets. Overall, this paper contributes to the existing literature on convex analysis and provides a comprehensive understanding of the convex Pfaff-Darboux theorem.

Semantic image segmentation is a crucial task in computer  vision, particularly in  the context of  traffic conditions  analysis. However,  the performance of semantic image segmentation models heavily relies on the quality of ground  truth   annotations.  In this paper,  we investigate the impact of ground   truth annotation quality  on the performance of semantic image segmentation  models for traffic  conditions analysis. We  propose a novel  metric  to quantify the quality of ground truth  annotations and  conduct experiments on a large dataset of traffic  images. Our  results demonstrate that the quality of ground  truth  annotations significantly affects the performance of semantic image segmentation models, with higher quality annotations leading  to improved segmentation accuracy. We also analyze the factors that contribute to the quality of ground truth annotations and provide insights for  improving  the annotation process. Overall, our findings  highlight the importance of high-quality ground truth annotations in achieving accurate semantic  image segmentation  for traffic conditions analysis.

We introduce a novel Deep Learning framework, which quantitatively estimates
image segmentation quality without the need for human inspection or labeling.
We refer to this method as a Quality Assurance Network -- QANet. Specifically,
given an image and a `proposed' corresponding segmentation, obtained by any
method including manual annotation, the QANet solves a regression problem in
order to estimate a predefined quality measure with respect to the unknown
ground truth. The QANet is by no means yet another segmentation method.
Instead, it performs a multi-level, multi-feature comparsion of an
image-segmentation pair based on a unique network architecture, called the
RibCage.
  To demonstrate the strength of the QANet, we addressed the evaluation of
instance segmentation using two different datasets from different domains,
namely, high throughput live cell microscopy images from the Cell Segmentation
Benchmark and natural images of plants from the Leaf Segmentation Challenge.
While synthesized segmentations were used to train the QANet, it was tested on
segmentations obtained by publically available methods that participated in the
different challenges. We show that the QANet accurately estimates the scores of
the evaluated segmentations with respect to the hidden ground truth, as
published by the challenges' organizers.
  The code is available at: TBD.
