We derive an analytical expression for a novel large-scale structure
observable: the line correlation function. The line correlation function, which
is constructed from the three-point correlation function of the phase of the
density field, is a robust statistical measure allowing the extraction of
information in the non-linear and non-Gaussian regime. 

We show that, in
perturbation theory, the line correlation is sensitive to the coupling kernel
F_2, which governs the non-linear gravitational evolution of the density field. 

We compare our analytical expression with results from numerical simulations
and find a 1-sigma agreement for separations r<30 Mpc/h. 

Fitting formulae for
the power spectrum and the non-linear coupling kernel at small scales allow us
to extend our prediction into the strongly non-linear regime where we find a
1-sigma agreement with the simulations for r<2 Mpc/h. We discuss the advantages
of the line correlation relative to standard statistical measures like the
bispectrum. Unlike the latter, the line correlation is independent of the bias,
in the regime where the bias is local and linear. 

Furthermore, the variance of
the line correlation is independent of the Gaussian variance on the modulus of
the density field. This suggests that the line correlation can probe more
precisely the non-linear regime of gravity, with less contamination from the
power spectrum variance.

We propose a novel attention gate (AG) model for medical imaging that
automatically learns to focus on target structures of varying shapes and sizes.
Models trained with AGs implicitly learn to suppress irrelevant regions in an
input image while highlighting salient features useful for a specific task.
This enables us to eliminate the necessity of using explicit external
tissue/organ localisation modules of cascaded convolutional neural networks
(CNNs). AGs can be easily integrated into standard CNN architectures such as
the U-Net model with minimal computational overhead while increasing the model
sensitivity and prediction accuracy. The proposed Attention U-Net architecture
is evaluated on two large CT abdominal datasets for multi-class image
segmentation. Experimental results show that AGs consistently improve the
prediction performance of U-Net across different datasets and training sizes
while preserving computational efficiency. The code for the proposed
architecture is publicly available.

For an unstable quantum system quantum Zeno effect represents total decay
probability decrease while quantum anti-Zeno effect represents total decay
probability increase by frequent decay detection under condition that decay
probability is the same in all single decay detection. Some authors considered
optical, i.e. polarization Detection analogy of quantum Zeno and anti-Zeno
effects. We use simplest (Malus law) form of such ideas On the optical, i.e.
polarization detection analogy of quantum Zeno and anti-Zeno Effects and we
suggest some new situations When decay probability is different in different
single decay detection. We consider such situation, called quantum Hamlet
effect, when, by Frequent detection, final total polarization angle and state
converge but total probability for appearance of this state diverges. Also we
consider such situation, called Quantum anti-Hamlet effect, when, by frequent
detection, final total polarization angle and state diverge but total
probability for appearance of this state Converges. (By simple analogy we
define quantum anti-Hamlet effect for unstable quantum system too.) Finally, We
consider such situation when, by frequent detection, total probability for
propagation of the photon Through all analyzers has form of (quasi)
exponentially decreasing function.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach for segmentation and shape inpainting using a curvature prior based on Markov random fields (MRFs). Traditional segmentation and inpainting methods often suffer from artifacts and inaccuracies due to the lack of explicit shape constraints. Our proposed method overcomes this limitation by incorporating a curvature prior into the energy function of the MRF model. We show that the curvature prior encourages smoother and more accurate segmentations, as well as more realistic and coherent shape inpainting results. We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its superiority over state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation and inpainting accuracy. Overall, our approach provides a promising solution for solving the challenging tasks of segmentation and shape inpainting.

This paper explores the relationship between quantum causal models, faithfulness, and retrocausality. It begins by introducing the concept of quantum causal models as a framework for representing causal relationships in quantum systems. The authors then go on to discuss the concept of faithfulness, which refers to the idea that the causal relationships represented in a model accurately reflect the true relationships in the underlying system. The paper also delves into the controversial topic of retrocausality, which suggests that events in the future can influence events in the past. The authors argue that incorporating retrocausal elements into quantum causal models can have important implications for our understanding of causality and the nature of time. Overall, this paper sheds light on the complex interplay between quantum causal models, faithfulness, and retrocausality, and contributes to the ongoing debate within the field.

This paper proposes a novel approach for learning to steer a vehicle by mimicking features from heterogeneous auxiliary networks. The authors argue that existing methods for autonomous driving often rely on a single auxiliary network, which may not capture all relevant information for steering. To address this limitation, the authors propose a framework that combines multiple auxiliary networks, each trained on a different task related to driving. The proposed framework leverages a feature mimicking module to transfer knowledge from the auxiliary networks to the steering network. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of steering accuracy and generalization to unseen scenarios. The findings of this study have implications for the development of more robust and reliable autonomous driving systems.

This  academic paper explores the concept of a Morphological  Network, specifically focusing on the potential of   Morphological Neurons. Morphological Networks are a  neural  network architecture  that  could potentially integrate shape-based information into deep  learning models. The authors present their experiments and findings on  the capabilities and  limitations of  Morphological Neurons, discussing various applications such as object  recognition and segmentation. The paper concludes by highlighting the potential of Morphological Networks in enhancing  the understanding  and performance of  deep learning models by incorporating morphological information.

Semantic segmentation of medical images plays a crucial role in various clinical applications. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown promising results in this task, but they often struggle to capture fine-grained morphological features due to the limited receptive field of convolutional layers. In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called Morphological Operation Residual Blocks (MORBs) to enhance the representation of 3D morphological features in CNNs for semantic segmentation of medical images. MORBs incorporate morphological operations, such as erosion and dilation, within residual blocks to capture local and global morphological information. We evaluate our proposed architecture on two publicly available medical image datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate that MORBs significantly improve the performance of CNNs in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to noise and artifacts. Our findings suggest that incorporating morphological operations within residual blocks can effectively enhance the representation of 3D morphological features in CNNs for semantic segmentation of medical images.

We propose a theory of weakly nonlinear multi-dimensional self sustained
detonations based on asymptotic analysis of the reactive compressible
Navier-Stokes equations. We show that these equations can be reduced to a model
consisting of a forced, unsteady, small disturbance, transonic equation and a
rate equation for the heat release. 

In one spatial dimension, the model
simplifies to a forced Burgers equation. Through analysis, numerical
calculations and comparison with the reactive Euler equations, the model is
demonstrated to capture such essential dynamical characteristics of detonations
as the steady-state structure, the linear stability spectrum, the
period-doubling sequence of bifurcations and chaos in one-dimensional
detonations and cellular structures in multi- dimensional detonations.

In this work we report results of ferromagnetic resonance studies of a 6% 15
nm (Ga,Mn)As layer, deposited on (001)-oriented GaAs. The measurements were
performed with in-plane oriented magnetic field, in the temperature range
between 5K and 120K. We observe a temperature induced reorientation of the
effective in-plane easy axis from [-110] to [110] direction close to the Curie
temperature. The behavior of magnetization is described by anisotropy fields,
H_{eff} (= 4\piM -H_{2\perp}), H_{2\parallel}, and H_{4\parallel}. In order to
precisely investigate this reorientation, numerical values of anisotropy fields
have been determined using powerful - but still largely unknown - interval
calculations. In simulation mode this approach makes possible to find all the
resonance fields for arbitrarily oriented sample, which is generally
intractable analytically. In 'fitting' mode we effectively utilize full
experimental information, not only those measurements performed in special,
distinguished directions, to reliably estimate the values of important physical
parameters as well as their uncertainties and correlations.

In recent years, the idea of using morphological operations as networks has
received much attention. Mathematical morphology provides very efficient and
useful image processing and image analysis tools based on basic operators like
dilation and erosion, defined in terms of kernels. Many other morphological
operations are built up using the dilation and erosion operations. Although the
learning of structuring elements such as dilation or erosion using the
backpropagation algorithm is not new, the order and the way these morphological
operations are used is not standard. In this paper, we have theoretically
analyzed the use of morphological operations for processing 1D feature vectors
and shown that this gets extended to the 2D case in a simple manner. Our
theoretical results show that a morphological block represents a sum of hinge
functions. Hinge functions are used in many places for classification and
regression tasks (Breiman (1993)). We have also proved a universal
approximation theorem -- a stack of two morphological blocks can approximate
any continuous function over arbitrary compact sets. To experimentally validate
the efficacy of this network in real-life applications, we have evaluated its
performance on satellite image classification datasets since morphological
operations are very sensitive to geometrical shapes and structures. We have
also shown results on a few tasks like segmentation of blood vessels from
fundus images, segmentation of lungs from chest x-ray and image dehazing. The
results are encouraging and further establishes the potential of morphological
networks.

This paper presents a novel approach to solving unsteady  thermal fluid structure interaction problems using fast solvers. The traditional approach to solving these problems  involves   the use of   explicit time integration  schemes, which are  computationally expensive and time-consuming. In this paper, we propose a new method that combines the advantages of implicit and  explicit solvers,  resulting in significant  computational speed-up. The proposed method is based on a modified version of the projection method and uses a preconditioned conjugate   gradient solver to efficiently solve the resulting linear systems. We  demonstrate the effectiveness and  efficiency of our   approach through  numerical experiments on a range  of test problems. Our  results show that  the proposed  method achieves accurate and  fast solutions, making   it a promising tool for solving unsteady thermal fluid  structure interaction problems.

Quantum error  correction is a crucial component in the development of reliable quantum computing  systems. However, designing and verifying quantum error correction codes can be challenging due to the complex nature of quantum systems. In  this paper,  we propose  a graphical approach for designing and verifying quantum  error correction codes. We introduce graphical structures   that represent the logical and physical  qubits, as well  as the error correction  operations. These graphical  structures provide a visual representation of the error correction code,  making  it  easier to understand  and analyze. We also present a  verification algorithm that uses these graphical  structures  to check  the correctness of the error correction code. Our approach offers a more intuitive and efficient  way to  design and verify quantum error correction codes,  which  can contribute to the advancement of quantum computing  technology.

This paper investigates the Whitney distortion extension problem for the function spaces $C^m(\mathbb  R^n)$ and $C^{\infty}(\mathbb R^n)$, where $m$  is a  positive integer. The Whitney  distortion extension problem refers to  the question  of whether a given function   defined  on a compact set in  $\mathbb R^n$ can be extended to a  function with  bounded distortion in these function   spaces. The paper provides a positive solution to this problem for both $C^m(\mathbb R^n)$  and $C^{\infty}(\mathbb R^n)$ and presents various applications of this  result. One of the key applications is  in the field of  interpolation and alignment of data in $\mathbb R^n$, where the extended  functions can be  used to accurately  interpolate  and  align scattered data points.  The paper discusses the theoretical framework, provides rigorous proofs of the main  results, and demonstrates  the effectiveness of  the approach  through numerical experiments and applications. Overall, this paper contributes to a  better understanding  of the  Whitney distortion  extension problem and its significance in data analysis and interpolation in $\mathbb R^n$.

Simultaneous localisation and categorization of objects in medical images,
also referred to as medical object detection, is of high clinical relevance
because diagnostic decisions often depend on rating of objects rather than e.g.
pixels. For this task, cumbersome and iterative process of method
configuration constitutes a major research bottleneck. Recently, nnU-Net has
tackled this challenge for task of image segmentation with great success.
Following nnU-Net's agenda, in this work we systematize and automate the
configuration process for medical object detection. The resulting
self-configuring method, nnDetection, adapts itself without any manual
intervention to arbitrary medical detection problems while achieving results en
par with or superior to the state-of-the-art. We demonstrate the effectiveness
of nnDetection on two public benchmarks, ADAM and LUNA16, and propose 10
further medical object detection tasks on public data sets for comprehensive
method evaluation. Code is at https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnDetection .

This paper introduces a novel approach for learning to control in the context of visual semantic segmentation. The proposed framework, named Virtual-to-Real, leverages synthetic data from virtual environments to train a control policy that can be applied in real-world scenarios. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments, showing that their policy outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalizability. The findings suggest that the Virtual-to-Real framework has great potential for improving the performance of control systems in visual semantic segmentation tasks.

We show that, under suitably general formulations, covering properties,
accumulation properties and filter convergence are all equivalent notions. This
general correspondence is exemplified in the study of products.
  Let $X$ be a product of topological spaces. We prove that $X$ is sequentially
compact if and only if all subproducts by $\leq \mathfrak s$ factors are
sequentially compact. If $\mathfrak s = \mathfrak h$, then $X$ is sequentially
compact if and only if all factors are sequentially compact and all but at most
$<\mathfrak s$ factors are ultraconnected. We give a topological proof of the
inequality ${\rm cf} \mathfrak s \geq \mathfrak h$. Recall that $\mathfrak s$
denotes the splitting number and $\mathfrak h$ the distributivity number. The
product $X$ is Lindel\"of if and only if all subproducts by $\leq \omega_1 $
factors are Lindel\"of. Parallel results are obtained for final $
\omega_n$-compactness, $[ \lambda, \mu ]$-compactness, the Menger and
Rothberger properties.

Histopathology image segmentation is a crucial task in medical image analysis as it plays a significant role in diagnosing diseases and understanding their progression. However, manual annotation of histopathology images is time-consuming and requires expert knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for histopathology image segmentation using unlabeled data in a semi-supervised framework. We utilize unsupervised feature learning to extract rich representations from unlabeled data and integrate them into a semi-supervised segmentation framework. Our method achieves state-of-the-art results on publicly available histopathology datasets and demonstrates the effectiveness of leveraging unlabeled data for improving segmentation accuracy. This approach has the potential to reduce the effort and cost of manual annotation while achieving accurate histopathology image segmentation.

Smoking of tobacco is predicted to cause approximately six million deaths
worldwide in 2014. Responding effectively to this epidemic requires a thorough
understanding of how smoking behaviour is transmitted and modified. Here, we
present a new mathematical model of the social dynamics that cause cigarette
smoking to spread in a population. Our model predicts that more individualistic
societies will show faster adoption and cessation of smoking. Evidence from a
new century-long composite data set on smoking prevalence in 25 countries
supports the model, with direct implications for public health interventions
around the world. Our results suggest that differences in culture between
societies can measurably affect the temporal dynamics of a social spreading
process, and that these effects can be understood via a quantitative
mathematical model matched to observations.

This paper presents the experiment simulation configurations used in the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) Conceptual Design Report (CDR). DUNE is a next-generation neutrino experiment that aims to study neutrino oscillations and other neutrino properties. The simulation configurations include the detector geometry, materials, and physics processes used to model the interactions of neutrinos and other particles in the DUNE detectors. The paper describes the simulation tools and software used, as well as the validation and benchmarking of the simulation configurations. The results of the simulations are compared to data from previous experiments and used to inform the design and optimization of the DUNE detectors. The paper concludes with a discussion of the future directions and improvements for the simulation configurations in DUNE.

In this paper, we investigate the  higher-order relativistic  corrections  to the  process of gluon  fragmentation into spin-triplet S-wave quarkonium. Quarkonium refers to a  bound state of a quark and an antiquark, which is characterized by its quantum numbers and its wavefunction.  We calculate the amplitudes for the fragmentation  process up to next-to-next-to-next-to-leading  order in  perturbative QCD. Our analysis includes the contributions from both the  direct and  the resolved processes, where  the gluon either directly fragments into quarkonium or  resolves into a virtual quark and  antiquark pair before  fragmenting.  We find that the higher-order relativistic  corrections significantly   affect the fragmentation probabilities and the  quarkonium production rates. Our  results provide important insights into the  dynamics of quarkonium formation in high-energy processes and can be useful  for  experiments at particle colliders.

In this  paper, we review and substantially develop the  recently proposed
"Microscopic  Response  Method", which has been devised to compute  transport
coefficients  and especially associated temperature dependence in complex
materials. The conductivity   and Hall  mobility of  amorphous  semiconductors and
semiconducting polymers are systematically derived, and shown to be more
practical than the Kubo formalism. The effect of a quantized  lattice  (phonons)
on transport  coefficients  is fully included and then integrated out, providing
the primary temperature dependence for the transport coefficients. For
higher-order processes,  using a diagrammatic expansion, one  can consistently
include all important  contributions to a given order and directly write out  the
expressions of transport coefficients for  various processes.

Deepfake technology has  become  increasingly sophisticated, making it difficult  to  detect manipulated content. In this paper, we propose a  method for detecting deepfake-forged contents using a separable convolutional neural network (CNN) and  image segmentation. The separable CNN is designed to  capture both global   and  local features  of the image, while the image segmentation technique helps to identify regions that have been manipulated. We  evaluate our method on  a  large dataset of deepfake images and compare it with  existing detection methods.  The  results   show that our approach achieves high  accuracy in detecting deepfake-forged contents, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods. This research contributes to  the development of effective techniques for combating the  spread of deepfake content.

This paper presents a new region-based active learning method called MetaBox+ for semantic segmentation  tasks.  The proposed  method  utilizes  priority maps to  select informative regions  for annotation, aiming  to improve the  efficiency and accuracy of the active learning process. The priority  maps are generated by combining multiple uncertainty measures, including entropy and margin,   to identify regions with high uncertainty. The   MetaBox+ method  then selects regions  within these high uncertainty   areas based on their saliency scores. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that MetaBox+ outperforms existing  active learning methods in terms of both annotation efficiency and segmentation accuracy. The proposed method has the potential to  enhance the performance of semantic  segmentation models  in  real-world applications.

The  unknotting number  of  a knot is the  minimum number of crossings one must
change to turn that knot into the unknot. We work  with a generalization of
unknotting number due to  Mathieu-Domergue, which we call the untwisting number.
The p-untwisting number  is the minimum  number (over all diagrams of a  knot) of
full twists on at most 2p strands  of a knot, with half  of  the strands  oriented
in  each  direction, necessary to transform that knot  into the  unknot. In
previous work, we showed that the  unknotting and untwisting  numbers can be
arbitrarily different. In this  paper, we show that a common route  for
obstructing low unknotting number, the Montesinos trick,  does not generalize to
the untwisting  number. However, we use a different approach to get conditions
on the Heegaard Floer correction terms of  the branched double cover of  a knot
with untwisting number  one. This allows us to obstruct several 10 and
11-crossing knots from  being unknotted by  a single  positive or negative twist.
We also use the Ozsv\'ath-Szab\'o tau invariant and the Rasmussen  s  invariant
to    differentiate between the p- and q-untwisting numbers for certain  p,q > 1.

We theoretically examine the optomechanical interaction between a rotating
nanoparticle and an orbital angular momentum-carrying optical cavity mode.
Specifically, we consider a dielectric nanosphere rotating uniformly in a
ring-shaped optical potential inside a Fabry-Perot resonator. The motion of the
particle is probed by a weak angular lattice, created by introducing two
additional degenerate Laguerre-Gaussian cavity modes carrying equal and
opposite orbital angular momenta. We demonstrate that the rotation frequency of
the nanoparticle is imprinted on the probe optical mode, via the Doppler shift,
and thus may be sensed experimentally using homodyne detection. We show
analytically that the effect of the optical probe on the particle rotation
vanishes in the regime of linear response, resulting in an accurate frequency
measurement. We also numerically characterise the degradation of the
measurement accuracy when the system is driven in the nonlinear regime. Our
results are relevant to rotational Doppler velocimetry and to studies of
rotational Brownian motion in a periodic lattice.

The 355 optically polarized QSOs have redshifts from 0.061 to 3.94 and are
spread out over the sky except for a 52 degree band centered on the Galactic
Equator. The data we analyze was measured, collected and published by others.
Here, we apply tests suitable for large-scale samples and find that the
polarization directions align with a significance of p = 0% by one test and are
correlated by a second test with p = 5%, each p-value uncertain within a factor
of about 4. The tests return a preferred Cartesian coordinate system that
fortuitously aligns well with the Milky Way Galaxy with a significance of p =
7%. Thus, the Hub Tests' results combined together imply the polarization
directions are correlated with a significance that is much less than 1%, which
is remarkable for such a large-scale sample.

This academic paper investigates the low-frequency 1/f noise in MoS2 thin-film transistors, comparing single-layer and multilayer structures. MoS2 is a promising material for electronic devices due to its excellent electrical performance, but the presence of 1/f noise can limit its practical applications. The authors conducted measurements on single-layer and multilayer MoS2 transistors and analyzed the 1/f noise characteristics. They found that the 1/f noise in single-layer transistors was significantly lower compared to multilayer transistors. The authors attributed this difference to the absence of interlayer coupling in single-layer transistors. The study provides valuable insights into the nature of 1/f noise in MoS2 transistors, offering guidance for the optimization of device performance and noise reduction strategies.

Self-Paced  Contrastive Learning for Semi-supervised Medical Image Segmentation with Meta-labels  explores a novel  approach  to semi-supervised medical image segmentation using self-paced contrastive learning. The paper proposes a  method that incorporates meta-labels, which are a  type of soft labels    that represent the uncertainty  of the ground truth  annotations. The proposed method  aims  to improve the performance of semi-supervised medical image segmentation by addressing the  issue  of inconsistent  and unreliable annotations. The paper presents experimental results that demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach compared  to existing methods. The findings  suggest  that the use of self-paced contrastive learning with meta-labels can lead to more  accurate and  reliable medical image segmentation in a  semi-supervised setting.

Assigning meaning to parts of image data is the goal of semantic image
segmentation. Machine learning methods, specifically supervised learning is
commonly used in a variety of tasks formulated as semantic segmentation. One of
the major challenges in the supervised learning approaches is expressing and
collecting the rich knowledge that experts have with respect to the meaning
present in the image data. Towards this, typically a fixed set of labels is
specified and experts are tasked with annotating the pixels, patches or
segments in the images with the given labels. In general, however, the set of
classes does not fully capture the rich semantic information present in the
images. For example, in medical imaging such as histology images, the different
parts of cells could be grouped and sub-grouped based on the expertise of the
pathologist.
  To acheive such a precise semantic representation of the concepts in the
image, we need access to the full depth of knowledge of the annotator. In this
work, we develop a novel approach to collect segmentation annotations from
experts based on psychometric testing. Our method consists of the psychometric
testing procedure, active query selection, query enhancement, and a deep metric
learning model to acheive a patch-level image embedding that allows for
semantic segmentation of images. We show the merits of our method with
evaluation on the synthetically generated image, aerial image and histology
image.

This paper presents a novel approach for learning to segment skin lesions from noisy annotations. Skin lesion segmentation is a crucial task in dermatology, as it aids in the diagnosis and treatment of various skin conditions. However, obtaining accurate annotations for training segmentation models can be challenging, as it requires expert knowledge and can be subjective. To address this issue, we propose a two-step learning framework that leverages both noisy and clean annotations. In the first step, we train a segmentation model using the noisy annotations, which are obtained through a crowdsourcing platform. In the second step, we fine-tune the model using a small set of clean annotations, which are obtained from expert dermatologists. Experimental results on a large dataset of skin lesion images demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Our findings suggest that learning from noisy annotations can be an effective strategy for skin lesion segmentation, especially when clean annotations are limited or difficult to obtain.

This paper is concerned with parabolic gradient systems of the form \[
u_t=-\nabla V (u) + \mathcal{D} u_{xx}\,, \] where the spatial domain is the
whole real line, the state variable $u$ is multidimensional, $\mathcal{D}$
denotes a fixed diffusion matrix, and the potential $V$ is coercive at
infinity. Bistable solutions, that is solutions close at both ends of space to
stable homogeneous equilibria, are considered. For a solution of this kind, it
is proved that, if the equilibria approached at both ends belong to the same
level set of the potential and if an appropriate (localized in space) energy
remains bounded from below as time increases, then the solution approaches, as
time goes to infinity, a pattern of profiles of stationary solutions homoclinic
or heteroclinic to stable homogeneous equilibria, going slowly away from one
another. This result provides a step towards a complete description of the
global behaviour of all bistable solutions that is pursued in a companion
paper. Some consequences are derived, and applications to some examples are
given.

Deep convolutional networks for semantic image segmentation typically require
large-scale labeled data, e.g. ImageNet and MS COCO, for network pre-training.
To reduce annotation efforts, self-supervised semantic segmentation is recently
proposed to pre-train a network without any human-provided labels. The key of
this new form of learning is to design a proxy task (e.g. image colorization),
from which a discriminative loss can be formulated on unlabeled data. Many
proxy tasks, however, lack the critical supervision signals that could induce
discriminative representation for the target image segmentation task. Thus
self-supervision's performance is still far from that of supervised
pre-training. In this study, we overcome this limitation by incorporating a
"mix-and-match" (M&M) tuning stage in the self-supervision pipeline. The
proposed approach is readily pluggable to many self-supervision methods and
does not use more annotated samples than the original process. Yet, it is
capable of boosting the performance of target image segmentation task to
surpass fully-supervised pre-trained counterpart. The improvement is made
possible by better harnessing the limited pixel-wise annotations in the target
dataset. Specifically, we first introduce the "mix" stage, which sparsely
samples and mixes patches from the target set to reflect rich and diverse local
patch statistics of target images. A "match" stage then forms a class-wise
connected graph, which can be used to derive a strong triplet-based
discriminative loss for fine-tuning the network. Our paradigm follows the
standard practice in existing self-supervised studies and no extra data or
label is required. With the proposed M&M approach, for the first time, a
self-supervision method can achieve comparable or even better performance
compared to its ImageNet pre-trained counterpart on both PASCAL VOC2012 dataset
and CityScapes dataset.

Over past years, computer vision community has contributed to enormous
progress in semantic image segmentation, a per-pixel classification task,
crucial for dense scene understanding and rapidly becoming vital in lots of
real-world applications, including driverless cars and medical imaging. Most
recent models are now reaching previously unthinkable numbers (e.g., 89% mean
iou on PASCAL VOC, 83% on CityScapes), and, while intersection-over-union and a
range of other metrics provide the general picture of model performance, in
this paper we aim to extend them into other meaningful and important for
applications characteristics, answering such questions as 'how accurate the
model segmentation is on small objects in general scene?', or 'what are the
sources of uncertainty that cause model to make an erroneous prediction?'.
Besides establishing a methodology that covers the performance of single
model from different perspectives, we also showcase several extensions that can
be worth pursuing in order to further improve current results in semantic
segmentation.

This  paper presents a  linear  framework for region-based image segmentation and  inpainting that incorporates curvature penalization. The proposed method utilizes a linear  approximation of the total variation  (TV) regularization term,  which  allows for efficient computation and optimization. The framework is  based on a convex relaxation of the segmentation and inpainting  problem, which is solved using  an alternating direction method of multipliers  (ADMM) algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of   the proposed method in  accurately  segmenting and inpainting images, while also preserving important image  structures and details. The linear framework offers a computationally efficient and  robust solution for region-based image   segmentation and inpainting tasks.

Superpixel segmentation is an essential preprocessing step for various computer vision tasks, such as object detection and semantic segmentation. This paper proposes a new approach for superpixel segmentation called Dynamic and Iterative Spanning Forest (DISF). Unlike previous methods, DISF dynamically generates superpixels by iteratively merging and splitting regions based on a local connectivity measure. This approach allows for better adaptation to image complexity and preserves finer details compared to existing methods. Experimental results on five benchmark datasets show that DISF outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both boundary adherence and computational efficiency. Overall, DISF provides a more flexible and efficient solution for superpixel segmentation, making it a valuable tool for various computer vision applications.

This paper investigates the phenomenon of quantum percolation in finite regular graphs. Quantum percolation refers to the behavior of quantum particles moving through a network of interconnected nodes. The authors analyze the conditions under which quantum percolation occurs in finite regular graphs, and explore the effects of various parameters such as graph size and connectivity on the percolation threshold. The study utilizes mathematical models and simulations to provide insights into the behavior of quantum particles in finite regular graphs, and offers potential applications in fields such as quantum computing and network analysis. The findings contribute to the understanding of quantum percolation in finite regular graphs and provide a foundation for further research in this area.

This paper  presents a novel approach for scene  understanding  in the context of autonomous manipulation  using deep learning techniques. The goal is to  enable a robot to perceive   and interpret its environment in order to perform complex manipulation tasks. The proposed method  leverages  deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to extract high-level features from visual input, and combines them with  contextual information to generate a comprehensive understanding of the  scene. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of  their approach through extensive experiments on a real-world  robotic  platform, achieving high accuracy  in object recognition and scene understanding  tasks. The results highlight the potential of deep learning  for enabling autonomous manipulation in  various domains,  such  as  industrial automation and service robotics.

Non-invasive detection of cardiovascular disorders from radiology scans
requires quantitative image analysis of the heart and its substructures. There
are well-established measurements that radiologists use for diseases assessment
such as ejection fraction, volume of four chambers, and myocardium mass. These
measurements are derived as outcomes of precise segmentation of the heart and
its substructures. The aim of this paper is to provide such measurements
through an accurate image segmentation algorithm that automatically delineates
seven substructures of the heart from MRI and/or CT scans. Our proposed method
is based on multi-planar deep convolutional neural networks (CNN) with an
adaptive fusion strategy where we automatically utilize complementary
information from different planes of the 1D scans for improved delineations.
For CT and MRI, we have separately designed three CNNs (the same architectural
configuration) for three planes, and have trained the networks from scratch for
voxel-wise labeling for the following cardiac structures: myocardium of left
ventricle (Myo), left atrium (LA), left ventricle (LV), right atrium (RA),
right ventricle (RV), ascending aorta (Ao), and main pulmonary artery (PA). We
have evaluated the proposed method with 3-fold-cross validation on the
multi-modality whole heart segmentation challenge (MM-WHS 2017) dataset. The
precision and dice index of 0.93 and 0.90, and 7.15 and 0.85 were achieved for
CT and MR images, respectively. While a CT volume was segmented about 50
seconds, an MRI scan was segmented around 12 seconds with the GPUs/CUDA
implementation.

The notion of Lagrangian $H$-umbilical submanifolds was introduced by B. Y.
Chen in 1997, and these submanifolds have appeared in several important
problems in the study of Lagrangian submanifolds from the Riemannian geometric
point of view. Recently, the author introduced the notion of tangentially
biharmonic submanifolds, which are defined as submanifolds such that the
bitension field of the inclusion map has vanishing tangential component. The
normal bundle of a round hypersphere in $\mathbb{R}^n$ can be immersed as a
tangentially biharmonic Lagrangian $H$-umbilical submanifold in $\mathbb{C}^n$.
Motivated by this fact, we classify tangentially biharmonic Lagrangian
$H$-umbilical submanifolds in complex space forms.

Deep Learning is considered to be a quite young in the area of machine
learning research, found its effectiveness in dealing complex yet high
dimensional dataset that includes but limited to images, text and speech etc. 

with multiple levels of representation and abstraction. As there are a plethora
of research on these datasets by various researchers , a win over them needs
lots of attention. 

Careful setting of Deep learning parameters is of paramount
importance in order to avoid the overfitting unlike conventional methods with
limited parameter settings. 

Deep Convolutional neural network (DCNN) with
multiple layers of compositions and appropriate settings might be is an
efficient machine learning method that can outperform the conventional methods
in a great way. However, due to its slow adoption in learning, there are also
always a chance of overfitting during feature selection process, which can be
addressed by employing a regularization method called dropout. 

Fast Random
Forest (FRF) is a powerful ensemble classifier especially when the datasets are
noisy and when the number of attributes is large in comparison to the number of
instances, as is the case of Bioinformatics datasets. Several publicly
available Bioinformatics dataset, Handwritten digits recognition and Image
segmentation dataset are considered for evaluation of the proposed approach. The excellent performance obtained by the proposed DCNN based feature selection
with FRF classifier on high dimensional datasets makes it a fast and accurate
classifier in comparison the state-of-the-art.

This paper proposes a novel variational image segmentation model that is coupled with image restoration achievements. The proposed model aims to overcome the limitations of existing segmentation techniques by incorporating restoration techniques to improve the accuracy and robustness of the segmentation results. The model utilizes a joint energy functional that integrates both image segmentation and restoration terms, which are optimized using variational methods. Experimental results on various real-world images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model, outperforming existing segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and robustness. The proposed model also offers flexibility in terms of adjusting the balance between segmentation and restoration tasks, making it applicable to a wide range of applications in image processing and computer vision.

We develop normalisation by evaluation (NBE) for dependent types based on
presheaf categories. Our construction is formulated in metalanguage of type
theory using quotient inductive types. We use a typed presentation hence there
are no preterms or realizers in our construction, and every construction
respects conversion relation. NBE for simple types uses a logical relation
between syntax and the presheaf interpretation. In our construction, we
merge presheaf interpretation and the logical relation into a
proof-relevant logical predicate. We prove normalisation, completeness,
stability and decidability of definitional equality. Most of the constructions
were formalized in Agda.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in medical imaging analysis, as it plays a vital role in diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of various diseases. Deep learning techniques have shown promising results in medical image segmentation due to their ability to learn complex patterns and features from large amounts of data. This paper provides an overview of deep learning methods used for medical image segmentation, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and generative adversarial networks (GANs). The paper also discusses the challenges and limitations of deep learning in medical image segmentation, such as the need for large annotated datasets and the interpretability of deep learning models. Finally, the paper presents future directions and potential applications of deep learning in medical image segmentation, including the integration of multi-modal data and the development of personalized medicine approaches.

In this paper we consider two sequence tagging tasks for medieval Latin:
part-of-speech tagging and lemmatization. These are both basic, yet
foundational preprocessing steps in applications such as text re-use detection.
Nevertheless, they are generally complicated by considerable orthographic
variation which is typical of medieval Latin. In Digital Classics, these tasks
are traditionally solved in (i) cascaded and (ii) lexicon-dependent fashion.
For example, a lexicon is used to generate all the potential lemma-tag pairs
for token, and next, context-aware PoS-tagger is used to select the most
appropriate tag-lemma pair. Apart from problems with out-of-lexicon items,
error percolation is a major downside of such approaches. In this paper we
explore the possibility to elegantly solve these tasks using single,
integrated approach. For this, we make use of a layered neural network
architecture from the field of deep representation learning.

While deep learning is very successful on cognitive tasks, it was not
seen to be sensitive to adversarial perturbations of the output. These
perturbations denote noise added to the output that was created specifically
to fool the system while being quasi-imperceptible for humans. More significantly,
there still exist universal perturbations that are input-agnostic but fool the
network on the majority of inputs. While previous work has concentrated on picture
classification, this work emphasizes attacks against semantic image segmentation:
we present an method for creating (universal) adversarial perturbations
that make the network yield a desired target segmentation as input. We show
empirically that there exist barely noticeable universal noise patterns which
result in almost the same predicted segmentation for arbitrary inputs.
However, we also show the existence of universal noise which hides a
target class (e.g., all pedestrians) from the segmentation while leaving the
segmentation mostly intact otherwise.

In this paper, we report on the experimental observation of anomalously robust valley polarization and valley coherence in bilayer WS2, a two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenide material. By applying circularly polarized light and measuring the integrated photoluminescence intensity from the A and B excitons, we observe a strikingly high valley polarization and sustained valley coherence at room temperature. We also investigate the effects of temperature and external magnetic field on the valley properties, and find that the valley polarization and coherence remain robust under these conditions. Our findings provide crucial insights into the fundamental physics of valleytronics in bilayer WS2 and have potential implications for future valley-based applications in optoelectronics and quantum information processing.

This paper explores the  use of graph entropies in the task of  texture segmentation of images. Texture segmentation is an important step  in image analysis and understanding, as it allows for the identification and separation of different regions  based  on  their texture properties. The  authors  propose a  novel approach that leverages   graph entropies to capture the complexity and randomness of texture patterns  in an image.   The proposed  method is compared against existing state-of-the-art techniques on various  benchmark datasets, and the results demonstrate  its effectiveness in  accurately  segmenting textures. The  findings of this study  contribute  to the field of image analysis and provide a new perspective on texture segmentation using graph entropies.

This paper presents a method for enumerating the corners in tree-like tableaux. Tree-like tableaux are combinatorial objects that can be used to represent certain types of trees. The corners in a tree-like tableau are defined as the cells that are not covered by any other cell. The authors develop an algorithm that efficiently counts the number of corners in a given tree-like tableau. They also provide a proof of correctness for the algorithm and analyze its time complexity. The proposed method is shown to be effective in practice through experimental results on various tree-like tableaux. This research contributes to the understanding and analysis of tree-like tableaux and provides a useful tool for counting corners in these combinatorial objects.

Medical  image segmentation is an essential task for several clinical applications. In this paper, we propose  a novel  hierarchical  attention network (HAN) framework for medical image segmentation. Our HAN model incorporates both  local and global contextual  information, allowing it to capture finer details and larger structures simultaneously. We evaluate  the performance  of our  model on two publicly  available   medical imaging datasets: the BraTS 2018 dataset for brain tumor segmentation and the ISIC 2018  dataset  for skin lesion segmentation. Experimental  results demonstrate that our HAN model achieves state-of-the-art segmentation  performance on both datasets. Furthermore, we conduct extensive  ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of  different components of  our HAN framework.  Overall, our proposed HAN model shows promising  results and   potential  for improving medical image  segmentation tasks.

Learning is a complex cognitive process that depends not only on an
individual capability of knowledge absorption but it can be also influenced by
various group interactions and by the structure of an academic curriculum. We
have applied methods of statistical analyses and data mining (Principal
Component Analysis and Maximal Spanning Tree) for anonymized students' scores
at Faculty of Physics, Warsaw University of Technology. A slight negative
linear correlation exists between mean and variance of course grades, i.e.
courses with higher mean scores tend to possess a lower scores variance.
  There are courses playing a central role, e.g. their scores are highly
correlated to other scores and they are in the centre of corresponding Maximal
Spanning Trees. Other courses contribute significantly to students' score
variance as well to the first principal component and they are responsible for
differentiation of students' scores. Correlations of the first principal
component to courses' mean scores and scores variance suggest that this
component can be used for assigning ECTS points to a given course. The analyse
is independant from declared curricula of considered courses. The proposed
methodology is universal and can be applied for analysis of student's scores
and academic curriculum at any faculty.

Open-World Entity Segmentation is a novel approach to the problem of segmenting entities in open-world scenarios. In open-world scenarios, the number and types of entities are not known in advance, making traditional segmentation methods inadequate. This paper proposes a two-step approach that first detects potential entities using a deep learning model and then refines the segmentation using a graph-based algorithm. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets and demonstrates robustness in handling open-world scenarios. The paper also provides an extensive analysis of the proposed method and discusses its limitations and potential future directions. Overall, Open-World Entity Segmentation presents a promising solution to the challenging problem of segmenting entities in open-world scenarios.

This paper presents  a comprehensive   approach  to multi-modal interactions in the context of referring image segmentation. Referring image segmentation  refers to the task of segmenting an  object of interest within  an image based on natural language instructions  provided  by a user. Existing methods for  referring image  segmentation often rely  solely on text instructions,  which can  be ambiguous  and may not capture the  complete  context or desired level of detail. To address this limitation,  we propose a novel  framework that incorporates multiple modalities, including  text, image regions, and spatial relations, to improve the accuracy and specificity of  the segmentation process. Our  framework utilizes a neural network architecture with attention mechanisms to attend to different modalities  and combine  their representations. We evaluate the effectiveness of our  approach on  benchmark datasets and demonstrate  improved  performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, we provide qualitative analysis and ablation studies to gain insights into  the  contribution  of  each modality and the overall effectiveness of our framework. Overall, our work contributes to the field of multi-modal interactions in computer vision and provides a  promising   approach for improving the accuracy  and specificity  of referring image segmentation.

This  paper proposes a novel approach  for training multi-organ segmentation networks using sample selection by relaxed upper confident  bound. The  authors argue that current  methods for training  such networks often suffer  from the problem of imbalanced training data, leading to poor   performance on underrepresented organs. To  address this  issue, they introduce  a  sample   selection  strategy based  on the relaxed upper confident bound, which aims to select informative samples that can improve the network's performance on underrepresented  organs. The proposed  method  is evaluated on a large dataset of abdominal CT scans and compared with several state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves the segmentation  accuracy  for underrepresented organs,  outperforming existing methods. The authors conclude that the sample selection  strategy  based  on relaxed upper confident bound is an effective  approach for training multi-organ segmentation networks.

This paper presents a deep learning approach for automatic  tracking of the tongue surface in real-time ultrasound videos. Traditional methods for  tongue tracking  rely on  contour-based   techniques, which can be  computationally expensive and prone to errors. In this study, we propose a  landmark-based approach that   utilizes a   convolutional neural network (CNN) to detect and track specific landmarks  on the tongue surface. The CNN is trained on a large dataset of  ultrasound videos with manually  annotated landmarks. Experimental results show that our proposed method  achieves  high  accuracy and real-time performance, outperforming traditional contour-based methods. This  landmark-based  approach has the potential to improve the  accuracy and efficiency of tongue tracking in various applications, such as speech therapy and pronunciation   training.

This paper  presents the design and application of a variable temperature environmental capsule for scanning  electron  microscopy  (SEM) in  gases and liquids at ambient conditions. The capsule is  designed to provide a controlled environment for  imaging samples  in different gas and liquid environments while maintaining  the sample  at a desired temperature. The design includes a heating element,  a temperature  sensor, and a gas or liquid inlet and outlet. The capsule is compatible with standard SEM systems and can  be easily integrated into  existing  setups. The application of  the capsule is  demonstrated  through imaging of various samples in different gas and liquid environments at different  temperatures. The  results show that the capsule provides   a versatile  and reliable  platform for studying samples in their native environments, enabling new   insights into the behavior and properties of materials.

MeanShift is a popular mode-seeking clustering algorithm used in a wide range
of applications in machine learning. However, it is known to be prohibitively
slow, with quadratic runtime per iteration. 

We propose MeanShift++, an
extremely fast mode-seeking algorithm based on MeanShift that uses a grid-based
approach to speed up the mean shift step, replacing the computationally
expensive neighbors search with a density-weighted mean of adjacent grid cells. 

In addition, we show that this grid-based technique for density estimation
comes with theoretical guarantees. 

The runtime is linear in the number of
points and exponential in dimension, which makes MeanShift++ ideal on
low-dimensional applications such as image segmentation and object tracking. We
provide extensive experimental analysis showing that MeanShift++ can be more
than 10,000x faster than MeanShift with competitive clustering results on
benchmark datasets and nearly identical image segmentations as MeanShift. Finally, we show promising results for object tracking.

This paper proposes a customizable architecture search method for semantic segmentation tasks. The method utilizes a neural architecture search algorithm to automatically search for the optimal network architecture for semantic segmentation tasks. The proposed method also allows for customization of the search space to suit specific requirements of different tasks. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on semantic segmentation tasks while being highly customizable and adaptable to different requirements.

Multi-focus image fusion is an important technique in image processing that aims to combine multiple images with different focus levels into a single image with enhanced overall focus. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-focus image fusion method based on similarity characteristics. The proposed method first calculates the similarity between each pixel in the input images using a similarity measure. Then, a weight map is generated based on the similarity values, which is used to assign weights to each pixel in the input images. Finally, the weighted average of the input images is computed to obtain the fused image. Experimental results on a dataset of multi-focus images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both visual quality and objective evaluation metrics. The proposed method is also computationally efficient, making it suitable for real-time applications.

In this work, we propose an adaptive spectral element algorithm for solving
nonlinear optimal control problems. The method employs orthogonal collocation
at the shifted Gegenbauer-Gauss points combined with very accurate and stable
numerical quadratures to fully discretize the multiple-phase integral form of
the optimal control problem. The proposed algorithm relies on exploiting the
underlying smoothness properties of the solutions for computing approximate
solutions efficiently. In particular, the method brackets discontinuities and
"points of nonsmoothness" through a novel local adaptive algorithm, which
achieves a desired accuracy on the discrete dynamical system equations by
adjusting both the mesh size and the degree of the approximating polynomials. A
rigourous error analysis of the developed numerical quadratures is presented.
Finally, the efficiency of the proposed method is demonstrated on three test
examples from the open litreature.

Superpixel Convolutional Networks (SPCNs)  are image  semantic segmenting techniques that use a  superpixel  algorithm  to generate image regions that  are more cohesive in  terms of color and  texture.  These regions can then be used as input for convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to  perform semantic segmentation. This paper proposes a novel approach called Bilateral Inceptions for SPCNs,   which uses a combination of bilateral  filtering and inception modules to improve the performance of pixel-level  predictions. The proposed approach is  evaluated on benchmark datasets and compared   with  other state-of-the-art techniques. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness  of  the Bilateral Inceptions approach in improving the accuracy of semantic segmentation compared to  existing methods.

Іn thе hіgh dіmеnsіоnаl rеgrеssіоn аnаlуsіs whеn thе numbеr оf рrеdісtоrs іs
muсh lаrgеr thаn thе sаmрlе sіzе, аn іmроrtаnt quеstіоn іs tо sеlесt thе
іmроrtаnt vаrіаblе whісh аrе rеlеvаnt tо thе rеsроnsе vаrіаblе оf іntеrеst.
Vаrіаblе sеlесtіоn аnd thе multірlе tеstіng аrе bоth tооls tо аddrеss thіs
іssuе. Ноwеvеr, thеrе іs lіttlе dіsсussіоn оn thе соnnесtіоn оf thеsе twо
аrеаs. Whеn thе sіgnаl strеngth іs strоng еnоugh suсh thаt thе sеlесtіоn
соnsіstеnсу іs асhіеvаblе, іt sееms tо bе unnесеssаrу tо соntrоl thе fаlsе
dіsсоvеrу rаtе. Ιn thіs рареr, wе соnsіdеr thе rеgіmе whеrе thе sіgnаls аrе
bоth rаrе аnd wеаk suсh thаt thе sеlесtіоn соnsіstеnсу іs nоt асhіеvаblе аnd
рrороsе а mеthоd whісh соntrоls thе fаlsе dіsсоvеrу rаtе аsуmрtоtісаllу. Ιt іs
thеоrеtісаllу shоwn thаt thе fаlsе nоn-dіsсоvеrу rаtе оf thе рrороsеd mеthоd
соnvеrgеs tо zеrо аt thе орtіmаl rаtе. Νumеrісаl rеsults аrе рrоvіdеd tо
dеmоnstrаtе thе аdvаntаgе оf thе рrороsеd mеthоd.

Deep neural network models used for medical image segmentation are large
because they are trained with high-resolution three-dimensional (3D) images.
Graphics processing units (GPUs) are widely used to accelerate the trainings.
However, the memory on a GPU is not large enough to train the models. A popular
approach to tackling this problem is patch-based method, which divides a large
image into small patches and trains the models with these small patches.
However, this method would degrade the segmentation quality if a target object
spans multiple patches. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for 3D
medical image segmentation that utilizes the data-swapping, which swaps out
intermediate data from GPU memory to CPU memory to enlarge the effective GPU
memory size, for training high-resolution 3D medical images without patching.
We carefully tuned parameters in the data-swapping method to obtain the best
training performance for 3D U-Net, a widely used deep neural network model for
medical image segmentation. We applied our tuning to train 3D U-Net with
full-size images of 192 x 192 x 192 voxels in brain tumor dataset. As a result,
communication overhead, which is the most important issue, was reduced by
17.1%. Compared with the patch-based method for patches of 128 x 128 x 128
voxels, our training for full-size images achieved improvement on the mean Dice
score by 4.48% and 5.32 % for detecting whole tumor sub-region and tumor core
sub-region, respectively. The total training time was reduced from 164 hours to
47 hours, resulting in 3.53 times of acceleration.

In this paper, we propose an interpretability-driven sample selection approach using self-supervised learning for disease classification and segmentation. The goal is to enhance the interpretability of deep learning models and improve the overall performance of disease classification and segmentation tasks in medical imaging. We first train a self-supervised learning model to learn representations of unlabeled images. Then, we use these learned representations to select a subset of highly informative and discriminative images from the dataset. These selected images are used to fine-tune a disease classification and segmentation model. Our method combines the benefits of self-supervised learning for unsupervised representation learning and interpretable sample selection for improved disease classification and segmentation. Experimental results on a large medical imaging dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in achieving higher accuracy and interpretability compared to state-of-the-art methods.

FSS has many uses in medical image processing. Most of the existing FSS methods rely on an abundance of annotated semantic classes for training, which is difficult for medical images because of the lack of such annotations. Besides, there is a bias-free mechanism that is sensitive to training loss, which combines localized averaged filters and prototypes with the method of pseudo-labelling super-pixels. This paper presents a new self-supervised framework for medical images that completely eliminates the need for annotations during training and generates super-pixels based on pseudo-labels to be used as supervision; (2) an adaptive local pooling mechanism to overcome the problem of foreground-background imbalance in medical image segmentation; (3) three different medical image segmentation tasks are compared, including the segmentation of the gastrointestinal organs in a X-ray, the segmentation of the heart in a magnetic resonance tomography (MR) image and the segmentation of abdominal organs using CT. The performance of the proposed method was compared with that of conventional FSS methods which use annotated images for training.

This paper presents a variational image segmentation model based on normalized cut with adaptive similarity and spatial regularization. The proposed model aims to accurately segment images by considering both the similarity between pixels and their spatial relationships. The model incorporates an adaptive similarity measure that dynamically adjusts the weights of the similarity term based on the local image characteristics. Additionally, a spatial regularization term is introduced to encourage smoothness in the segmentation results. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model in achieving accurate and visually pleasing image segmentation.

Image-to-image translation is long-established and a difficult problem in
computer vision. In this paper we propose an adversarial based model for
image-to-image translation. The regular deep neural-network based methods
perform the task of image-to-image translation by comparing gram matrices and
using image segmentation which requires human intervention. Our generative
adversarial network based model works on conditional probability approach.
This approach makes the image translation independent of any local, global and
content or style features. In our approach we use bidirectional
reconstruction model appended with the affine transform factor that helps in
conserving content and photorealism as compared to other models. The
advantage of using such approach is that the image-to-image translation is
semi-supervised, independant of image segmentation and inherits properties
of generative adversarial networks tending to produce realistic. This method
has proven to produce better results than Multimodal Unsupervised
Image-to-image translation.

This paper presents a stereo-based terrain traversability analysis method using normal-based segmentation and superpixel surface analysis. The proposed method aims to accurately classify terrain regions into traversable and non-traversable areas. The normal-based segmentation technique is used to segment the terrain into homogeneous regions based on the surface normals. Superpixel surface analysis is then performed to extract features from the segmented regions. These features are used to train a support vector machine classifier to classify the terrain regions. Experimental results on real-world stereo images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately analyzing terrain traversability. The proposed method can be applied in various applications such as autonomous navigation and robotic exploration.

Scene labeling, which involves assigning semantic labels to each pixel in an image, is an important task in computer vision. Recent advances have shown that incorporating contextual information improves the accuracy of scene labeling algorithms. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for scene labeling using contextual hierarchical models. Our approach combines the strengths of hierarchical models, which capture different scales of contextual information, and contextual models, which model dependencies between labels. We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and compare it to state-of-the-art methods. Our experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves higher accuracy in scene labeling, highlighting the importance of hierarchical modeling and contextual information in this task.
