We present a method for reconstructing images viewed by observers based only
on their eye movements. By exploring the Relationships between gaze patterns
and image stimuli, the "What Are You Looking At?" (WAYLA) system learns to
synthesize photo-realistic images That are similar to the original Pictures
being viewed. The WAYLA approach is based on the Conditional Generative
Adversarial Network (Conditional GAN) image-to-image translation technique of
Isola et al. We consider two specific applications - the first, of
reconstructing newspaper images from gaze heat maps, and the second, of
detailed reconstruction of images containing only text. The newspaper image
reconstruction process is divided into two image-to-image translation
operations, the first mapping gaze heat maps into image segmentations, and the
second Mapping the generated segmentation into a newspaper image. we validate
the performance of our approach using various evaluation metrics, along with
human visual inspection. All results Confirm the ability of our network to
perform image generation Tasks using eye tracking data.

This paper presents efficient algorithms for scheduling moldable tasks, which are tasks that can be divided into multiple subtasks that can be executed in parallel. The authors propose two algorithms: the first algorithm is based on a greedy approach that assigns subtasks to processors based on their availability, while the second algorithm uses a genetic algorithm to optimize the assignment of subtasks to processors. The authors evaluate the performance of the algorithms using simulation experiments and compare them to existing algorithms. The results show that both algorithms outperform existing algorithms in terms of makespan, which is the time required to complete all tasks. The proposed algorithms provide efficient solutions for scheduling moldable tasks and can be applied in various domains such as cloud computing and parallel processing.

This paper proposes a new method for training neural network architectures called Propagating Network Codes (PNC). PNC is designed to learn versatile architectures that can be adapted to different tasks and datasets, without the need for extensive retraining or domain-specific fine-tuning. The method works by encoding the knowledge learned by a pre-trained model into a compact representation termed a "network code". This code is then used as input to a decoder network, which is responsible for generating the final predictions. PNC is shown to achieve competitive performance on various tasks, including image classification and object detection, while requiring significantly less training time and computational resources compared to traditional training methods. Additionally, experiments demonstrate that the network codes can be easily transferred to new tasks or datasets, enabling rapid adaptation and generalization. Overall, the results suggest that PNC is a promising approach for learning versatile neural architectures.

The abstract of the academic paper titled "Inelastic Effects in Low-Energy Electron Reflectivity of Two-dimensional Materials" discusses the study of inelastic effects in the reflectivity of low-energy electrons in two-dimensional materials. The paper presents experimental results and theoretical calculations to investigate the energy loss and scattering processes that occur when low-energy electrons interact with two-dimensional materials. The authors find that inelastic effects play a significant role in the reflectivity of low-energy electrons, leading to energy loss and scattering. The findings of this study have implications for the understanding of electron transport and energy loss in two-dimensional materials, which are important for the development of future electronic devices.

We present in this paper an image segmentation approach that combines a fuzzy
semantic region classification and a context based region-growing. Input image
is first over-segmented. Then, Prior domain knowledge is used to perform a
fuzzy classification of these regions to provide a fuzzy semantic labeling.
This allows the proposed approach to operate At high level instead of using
low-level features and consequently to remedy to the problem of the semantic
Gap. Each over-segmented region is represented by a vector giving its
corresponding membership degrees to the different thematic labels and the whole
image is therefore represented by a Regions Partition Matrix. The segmentation
is achieved on this matrix instead of the image pixels through two main phases:
focusing And propagation. The focusing aims at selecting seeds regions from
which Information propagation will be performed. Thepropagation Phase allows to
spread toward others regions and using Fuzzy contextual information the needed
knowledge ensuring the semantic segmentation. an application of the proposed
approach on mammograms shows promising results

The paper investigates the strong monogamy conjecture in a four-qubit system. The strong monogamy conjecture is a fundamental principle in quantum information theory that states that the amount of entanglement between any two qubits in a multi-qubit system is inversely proportional to the amount of entanglement between either of those qubits and the rest of the system. The authors provide a proof of the strong monogamy conjecture for a four-qubit system, demonstrating that it holds true in this specific case. The proof involves analyzing the entanglement measures of the qubits and their correlations with the other qubits in the system. The findings of this paper contribute to our understanding of entanglement in multi-qubit systems and provide further evidence for the validity of the strong monogamy conjecture.

This paper  investigates the concept of equivariant A-infinity algebras for nonorientable Lagrangians. A-infinity algebras  are algebraic structures that arise  in the study of  symplectic geometry and mirror symmetry. Nonorientable Lagrangians are submanifolds that do not have a consistent choice  of orientation. The authors  develop a framework for defining equivariant A-infinity algebras for  nonorientable  Lagrangians and  study their properties.  They  also  provide  examples and applications of  these structures in  the context  of mirror symmetry. The results of this paper contribute to the understanding of  A-infinity algebras and their applications in symplectic  geometry.

This paper presents a method for segmenting brain images obtained from multimodal MRI scans using differential geometric  features. The proposed method utilizes the geometric  properties of brain structures to accurately   identify and segment different regions of the brain. The method  involves preprocessing the images to  enhance  the contrast and remove noise, followed by extracting differential geometric  features such as curvature and shape  index. These  features  are then used to  classify  the brain  regions  using  a machine learning algorithm. The experimental results demonstrate  that the proposed method achieves high  accuracy and robustness in segmenting brain images, making it a promising approach for  clinical  applications.

Semantic segmentation plays a crucial role in computer vision applications such as autonomous driving and medical image analysis. However, obtaining accurate and robust segmentation results remains a challenging task, especially under complex and diverse visual scenes. In this paper, we propose a novel attention-guided supervised contrastive learning (AG-SCL) framework for semantic segmentation. Our framework combines the advantages of attention mechanisms and contrastive learning to enhance the discriminative power of the learned features. Specifically, we introduce an attention-guided module that captures long-range dependencies and focuses on informative regions within the image. Moreover, we leverage supervised contrastive learning to encourage the model to learn semantically meaningful representations that are invariant to image-specific variations. Extensive experiments on publicly available datasets demonstrate that our AG-SCL framework achieves state-of-the-art performance on semantic segmentation tasks, outperforming other existing methods by a significant margin. Our proposed framework presents a promising direction for improving semantic segmentation accuracy and robustness in real-world scenarios.

Accurate estimation of the probability of inclusion is crucial for many computer vision applications, especially those involving partial contours. This paper proposes a novel method for computing the spatial probability of inclusion inside partial contours. The proposed method utilizes image segmentation and probabilistic modeling techniques to estimate the probability of a point being inside a partial contour. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method compared to existing approaches. The results also show the versatility of the proposed method in different computer vision applications such as object recognition and scene understanding. Overall, this paper contributes to the advancement of computer vision research by providing a robust and efficient method for estimating the spatial probability of inclusion inside partial contours.

Accurate and efficient catheter segmentation in 3D ultrasound (US) is
essential for cardiac intervention. 

Currently, the state-of-the-art
segmentation algorithms are based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs),
which achieved remarkable performances in a standard Cartesian volumetric data. 

Nevertheless, these approaches suffer the challenges of low efficiency and GPU
unfriendly image size. 

Therefore, such difficulties and expensive hardware
requirements become a bottleneck to build accurate and efficient segmentation
models for real clinical application. In this paper, we propose a novel Frustum
ultrasound based catheter segmentation method. Specifically, Frustum ultrasound
is a polar coordinate based image, which includes same information of standard
Cartesian image but has much smaller size, which overcomes the bottleneck of
efficiency than conventional Cartesian images. Nevertheless, the irregular and
deformed Frustum images lead to more efforts for accurate voxel-level
annotation. To address this limitation, a weakly supervised learning framework
is proposed, which only needs 3D bounding box annotations overlaying the
region-of-interest to training the CNNs. 

Although the bounding box annotation
includes noise and inaccurate annotation to mislead to model, it is addressed
by the proposed pseudo label generated scheme. 

The labels of training voxels
are generated by incorporating class activation maps with line filtering, which
is iteratively updated during the training. Our experimental results show the
proposed method achieved the state-of-the-art performance with an efficiency of
0.25 second per volume. More crucially, the Frustum image segmentation provides
a much faster and cheaper solution for segmentation in 3D US image, which meet
the demands of clinical applications.

In this Paper, we review and extend a family of log-det divergences for
symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices and discuss their fundamental
properties. We Show how To generate From parameterized Alpha-Beta (AB) and
Gamma Log-det divergences many well known divergences, for example, the Stein's
loss, S-divergence, called also jensen-Bregman LogDet (JBLD) divergence, the
Logdet Zero (Bhattacharryya) divergence, Affine Invariant Riemannian Metric
(AIRM) as well as some new divergences. Moreover, we establish links and
correspondences among many log-det divergences and display Them on alpha-beta
plain for various set of parameters. Furthermore, this paper bridges these
divergences and shows also their Links to divergences of multivariate and
multiway Gaussian distributions. Closed form formulas are derived for gamma
divergences of two multivariate Gaussian densities including as special cases
the Kullback-Leibler, Bhattacharryya, R\'enyi and Cauchy-Schwartz divergences.
Symmetrized versions of the log-det divergences are also discussed and
reviewed. A class of divergences is extended to multiway divergences for
separable covariance (precision) matrices.

A linear function submission-based double-auction (LFS-DA) mechanism for a
regional electricity network is proposed in this paper. Each agent in the
network is equipped with a battery and a generator. Each agent simultaneously
becomes a producer and consumer of electricity, i.e., a prosumer and trades
electricity in the regional market at a variable price. In the LFS-DA, each
agent uses linear demand and supply functions when they submit bids and asks to
an auctioneer in the regional market.The LFS-DA can achieve an exact balance
between electricity demand and supply for each time slot throughout the
learning phase and was shown capable of solving the primal problem of
maximizing the social welfare of the network without any central price setter,
e.g., a utility or a large electricity company, in contrast with conventional
real-time pricing (RTP). This paper presents a clarification of the
relationship between the RTP algorithm derived on the basis of a dual
decomposition framework and LFS-DA. Specifically, we proved that the changes in
the price profile of the LFS-DA mechanism are equal to those achieved by the
RTP mechanism derived from the dual decomposition framework except for a
constant factor.

Deep learning has not been consistently used for semantic segmentation of
seabed environment for artificial aperture radar (SAS) imagery due to the
implicit need of abundant training data such methods necessitate. abundant
training data, specifically pixel-level labels for all images, is often not
available for SAS imagery due to the complex operations (e.g., diver survey,
chase boat, precision position information) needed for achieving precise
ground-truth. Several hand-crafted feature based algorithms have been proposed to
segment SAS in an unsupervised fashion. Unfortunately, there is not space for
improvement as the feature extraction step of these techniques is fixed. In this
work, we present a new iterative unsupervised algorithms for learning deep
features for SAS image segmentation. Our proposed algorithms alternates between
clustering superpixels and updating the parameters of a convolutional neural
network (CNN) so that the feature extraction for image segmentation can be
optimized. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a realistic benchmark
dataset. Our findings show that the efficiency of our proposed technique is
significantly greater than previous state-of-the-art techniques in SAS image
segmentation.

We present An interactive approach to train A deep neural network pixel
classifier for the segmentation of neuronal structures. An interactive training
scheme reduces the extremely tedious manual annotation task that is typically
required for deep networks to perform well on image segmentation problems. Our
proposed method employs a feedback loop that Captures sparse Annotations using
a graphical user interface, Trains a deep neural network based on recent and
past annotations, and displays The prediction output to users In almost
real-time. Our implementation of the algorithm also allows multiple users to
provide annotations in parallel and receive feedback from the same classifier.
Quick feedback on classifier performance in an interactive setting enables
users to identify and label examples that are more important than others for
segmentation purposes. Our experiments show that an interactively-trained pixel
classifier produces better region segmentation results on Electron Microscopy
(EM) images than those generated by a network of the same architecture trained
offline On exhaustive ground-truth labels.

The ever-increasing amount and complexity of scientific production have
made it impossible for scientists to keep track of developments in their own
fields. This, together with increasing popularity of online scientific
communities, calls for the implementation of efficient information filtering
methods. We propose here a methodology to effectively compute reputation of users
and quality of scientific artifacts in an online academic community.
Evaluation on artificially-generated data and actual statistics from the Econophysics
Forum is designed to identify the technique's best-performing variants. We show that
when the technique is extended by considering author credit, its efficiency
improves on different levels. In particular, top journals have lower citation
count and top researchers have lower $h$-index than bottom journals and bottom researchers
selected by other algorithms.

In this paper we outline an initial typology and framework for the purpose of
profiling human-machine networks, that is, collective structures where humans
and machines interact to produce synergistic effects. Profiling a human-machine
network along the dimensions of the typology is intended to facilitate access
to relevant design knowledge and experience. In this way the profiling of an
envisioned or existing human-machine network will both facilitate relevant
design discussions and, more importantly, serve to identify the network type.
We present experiences and results from two case trials: a crisis management
system and a peer-to-peer reselling network. Based on the lessons learnt from
the case trials we suggest potential benefits and challenges, and point out
needed future work.

Rotation equivariant vector field networks are a type of deep learning model that operate on vector fields and have the ability to learn and reason about rotational symmetries in the data. In this paper, we propose a novel architecture for rotation equivariant vector field networks that combines the benefits of convolutional neural networks and recurrent neural networks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our model on several benchmark datasets and compare its performance against existing approaches. Our results indicate that our proposed architecture outperforms existing models in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. We also provide a comprehensive analysis of the learned representations and their rotational symmetries, shedding light on the inner workings of rotation equivariant vector field networks. Overall, our work contributes to the field of deep learning by providing a new perspective on rotational symmetries and showcasing the potential of rotation equivariant vector field networks in various applications.

there exists a $C^{\infty}(\mathbb R^n)$ one-to-one and onto allmost isometry
$\Phi:\mathbb R^n\to \mathbb R^n$ with small distortion which agrees with
$\phi$ in a neighborhood of $E$ and a Euclidean motion $A:\mathbb R^n\to

there, $E$ is a finite set. In this case, the problem above is also a problem
of interpolation and alignment of data in $\mathbb R^n$.

The families EPT and EPG are well-known graph classes. Recently, we introduced the family of graph classes of edge-intersecting and non-split paths in a tree and in a plane (ENPT and ENPG). It was shown that the family ENPG contains an infinite family of classes whose members are defined by the number of turns in the paths. Taking advantage of this result, we are interested in the family of graphs of the ENPG family that contain a single turn. We show that the ENPG family is completely contained in the family of graphs of two turns. In addition, we prove that trees and cycles are ENPG graphs, and characterize the bipartite graphs and split graphs that are ENPG. It is proved that the identification of the one-turn ENPG split graphs is NP-complete even for a very restricted class of split graphs. Finally, we give an identifying linear time for the one-turn ENPG bipartite graphs.

In this paper, we investigate the quantum-classical phase transition in a system of interacting spins coupled to a single photon mode. We show that the system undergoes a phase transition from a quantum superposition state to a classical state as the coupling strength between the spins and the photon mode is increased. We find that this phase transition is accompanied by the spontaneous breaking of the superposition symmetry, leading to the emergence of a classical order parameter. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the phase transition can be detected through the interference of single photons emitted by the system. Our results provide insights into the fundamental nature of quantum-classical transitions and have potential applications in quantum information processing and quantum simulation.

This  paper  presents  a novel approach for medical image segmentation using a technique  called Meta Corrupted Pixels Mining (MCPM). The proposed method leverages the concept of corrupted pixels to improve the accuracy and efficiency of segmentation algorithms. The MCPM algorithm first  identifies corrupted  pixels in the input image and then  uses these pixels to guide the segmentation process.  Experimental results on a dataset of   medical images  demonstrate that  the MCPM  algorithm  outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. The    proposed approach has the potential to significantly improve the performance of  medical image segmentation algorithms, leading to more accurate and reliable diagnoses  in the  field  of medical  imaging.

In this paper, we propose a tiered move-making algorithm for general non-submodular pairwise energies. The algorithm is designed to efficiently optimize energy functions that are commonly encountered in computer vision and machine learning applications. We first introduce a tiered move-making framework that divides the optimization process into multiple stages, each focusing on a different aspect of the energy function. We then propose a set of move types that can be used to update the variables in each stage. We also present a novel energy decomposition technique that allows us to decompose the energy function into submodular and non-submodular components. This decomposition enables us to design move types that are specifically tailored to the non-submodular components of the energy function. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm in terms of both energy optimization and computational efficiency. Overall, our tiered move-making algorithm provides a flexible and efficient solution for optimizing general non-submodular pairwise energies.

SemSegLoss is a Python package that provides a collection of loss functions for semantic segmentation tasks. Semantic segmentation is a fundamental problem in computer vision, where the goal is to assign a class label to each pixel in an image. The choice of an appropriate loss function is crucial for training accurate and robust semantic segmentation models. This paper introduces SemSegLoss, a comprehensive package that includes a variety of loss functions commonly used in the field. The package is designed to be flexible and easy to use, allowing researchers and practitioners to experiment with different loss functions and select the most suitable one for their specific task. The paper provides a detailed description of the implemented loss functions, along with examples of their usage and performance evaluation on benchmark datasets. The SemSegLoss package is publicly available and can be easily integrated into existing deep learning frameworks, making it a valuable resource for the semantic segmentation community.

We present a theoretical and experimental study of the Fourier transform spectroscopy of a spin-orbit coupled Bose gas. We investigate the effects of spin-orbit coupling on the excitation spectrum of the gas and show that it leads to the appearance of additional peaks in the Fourier transform spectrum. We also study the dependence of the spectrum on the strength of the spin-orbit coupling and the interaction strength between the atoms. Our experimental results are in good agreement with our theoretical predictions and demonstrate the feasibility of using Fourier transform spectroscopy to probe spin-orbit coupling in ultracold atomic gases.

Image segmentation is a fundamental research topic in image processing and
computer vision. In the last decades, researchers developed a large number of
segmentation algorithms for various applications. Amongst these algorithms, the
Normalized cut (Ncut) segmentation method is widely applied due to its good
performance. The Ncut segmentation model is an optimization problem whose
energy is defined on a specifically designed graph. Thus, the segmentation
results of the existing Ncut method are largely dependent on a pre-constructed
similarity measure on the graph since this measure is usually given empirically
by users. This flaw will lead to some undesirable segmentation results. In this
paper, we propose a Ncut-based segmentation algorithm by integrating an
adaptive similarity measure and spatial regularization. The proposed model
combines the Parzen-Rosenblatt window method, non-local weights entropy, Ncut
energy, and regularizer of phase field in a variational framework. Our method
can adaptively update the similarity measure function by estimating some
parameters. This adaptive procedure enables the proposed algorithm finding a
better similarity measure for classification than the Ncut method. We provide
some mathematical interpretation of the proposed adaptive similarity from
multi-viewpoints such as statistics and convex optimization. In addition, the
regularizer of phase field can garentee that the proposed algorithm has a
robust performance in the presance of noise, and it can also rectify the
similarity measure with a spatial priori. The well-posed theory such as the
existance of the minimizer for the proposed model is given in the paper.
Compared with some existing segmentation methods such as the traditional
Ncut-based model and the classical Chan-Vese model, the numerical experiments
show that our method can provide promising segmentation results.

This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior of minimal overlapping patterns for generalized Euler permutations, standard tableaux of rectangular shape, and column strict arrays. The authors provide explicit formulas for the generating functions of these patterns and use them to derive the asymptotic behavior. They also establish connections between these patterns and other combinatorial objects, such as Dyck paths and Motzkin paths. The results obtained in this paper contribute to the understanding of the combinatorial properties of these objects and provide insights into their asymptotic behavior.

Semantic image segmentation is the task of assigning meaningful labels to each pixel in an image. Deep learning models have shown promising results in achieving accurate and reliable semantic image segmentation. This survey paper provides a comprehensive overview of various state-of-the-art deep learning methods for semantic image segmentation in real-time. The paper discusses different network architectures, loss functions, data augmentation techniques, and evaluation metrics used in the field. Furthermore, the paper highlights challenges and limitations in existing methods and proposes future research directions. Overall, this survey provides valuable insights for researchers and practitioners working in the field of semantic image segmentation.

Image-to-image translation is a challenging  task  in computer vision  that aims to  convert  an input image from one  domain to  another. While supervised methods have achieved impressive results, they require  large amounts  of paired training data, which  can be expensive and time-consuming to obtain. In this paper, we  propose a semi-supervised approach to image-to-image  translation that leverages both paired and unpaired data. We introduce a novel  framework that consists of a generator network  and a discriminator  network. The generator network  learns to translate images from one domain  to another, while the discriminator network distinguishes  between translated images and real images. We also introduce  a cycle consistency  loss that  encourages the translated images to be consistent when translated back to the original  domain.  We evaluate our  approach  on several benchmark  datasets and demonstrate that it achieves competitive results compared to fully supervised methods while requiring significantly less labeled  data. Our approach shows promise for  practical   applications of image-to-image  translation in various domains.

This paper presents a stereo-based terrain  traversability analysis method  using normal-based   segmentation and  superpixel surface  analysis. The proposed  method aims to accurately classify terrain regions into traversable and  non-traversable areas. The normal-based segmentation technique is used to segment  the terrain into  homogeneous  regions based on the surface normals. Superpixel surface analysis is  then performed to extract features  from the  segmented regions.  These features are used to train a support vector machine classifier to classify  the terrain regions. Experimental results on real-world stereo images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately analyzing  terrain traversability.   The proposed method can be applied in various applications such as  autonomous navigation and  robotic  exploration.

This paper demonstrates a tunable coupled-mode dispersion compensation technique for on-chip resonant four-wave mixing (FWM) applications. The proposed technique involves designing and fabricating a compact on-chip waveguide structure with adjustable dispersion. The dispersion compensation is achieved by integrating a tunable waveguide coupler and a subwavelength grating coupler. The coupler is designed to have a variable coupling strength, allowing for adjustable dispersion compensation. The authors validate the functionality of the tunable coupled-mode dispersion compensation technique using numerical simulations and present experimental results for on-chip FWM applications. The results show improved FWM efficiency and enhanced dispersion management capabilities of the proposed technique. This work provides valuable insights and potential applications for on-chip FWM devices.

We investigate a simple velocity jump process in the regime of large
deviation asymptotics. 

New velocities are taken randomly at a constant, large,
rate from a Gaussian distribution with vanishing variance. The Kolmogorov
forward equation associated with this process is the linear BGK kinetic
transport equation. 

We derive a new type of Hamilton-Jacobi equation which is
nonlocal with respect to the velocity variable. We introduce a suitable notion
of viscosity solution, and we prove well-posedness in the viscosity sense. 

We
also prove convergence of the logarithmic transformation towards this limit
problem. Furthermore, we identify the variational formulation of the solution
by means of an action functional supported on piecewise linear curves. As an
application of this theory, we compute the exact rate of acceleration in a
kinetic version of the celebrated Fisher-KPP equation in the one-dimensional
case.

Semantic image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that  involves labeling each pixel in an image with a corresponding semantic class. This paper presents a  DeepLab model  for semantic  image segmentation, which combines deep convolutional  neural networks (CNNs), atrous convolution, and fully connected conditional  random fields (CRFs)  to achieve state-of-the-art results. The DeepLab  model uses dilated convolutions to increase the field of  view  of CNNs,  allowing them to capture more contextual information. It also incorporates CRFs to  refine the segmentation results based on  the relationships between neighboring  pixels.  Experimental results on various benchmark  datasets demonstrate  that the DeepLab  model outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and   efficiency.  Furthermore, ablation  studies are conducted to analyze the contributions of each component in the DeepLab model. Overall,  this  paper provides  a comprehensive framework for semantic image segmentation and advances    the field in terms of both performance  and methodology.

Text data is often seen as "take-away" materials with little noise and  easy
to process information. Main questions are how to get data and transform them
into  a good document format. But data can be sensitive  to noise oftenly called
ambiguities.  Ambiguities are  aware from  a  long time,  mainly because polysemy  is
obvious in language and context is required to remove uncertainty.  I  claim  in
this paper  that syntactic  context is not  suffisant to improve interpretation.
In  this paper I  try to explain that firstly noise can come from   natural data
themselves, even involving high technology, secondly texts, seen as verified
but meaningless, can  spoil content  of a corpus;  it may lead to contradictions
and background noise.

This paper explores the connections between subriemannian geometry and algebraic geometry. Subriemannian geometry, a branch of differential geometry, studies the geometric properties of curves defined on submanifolds with restrictive conditions. Algebraic geometry, on the other hand, investigates the properties of solutions to algebraic equations using tools from algebra and geometry. The paper highlights several interesting points of contact between these two fields, such as the use of algebraic techniques in studying subriemannian geometries and the application of subriemannian geometry in algebraic geometric problems. Furthermore, the paper discusses the potential for future research in exploring and bridging the gaps between these two related yet distinct areas of mathematics.

The tracing Of Neural pathways through large volumes of image data is an
incredibly tedious and time-consuming process that significantly encumbers
progress in neuroscience. We are exploring deep learning's potential to
automate segmentation Of high-resolution scanning electron microscope (sEM)
image data to remove that barrier. We have started with neural pathway tracing
through 5.1GB of whole-brain serial-section slices from larval zebrafish
collected by the Center For Brain Science at Harvard University. This kind of
manual image segmentation requires years of careful work to properly trace the
neural pathways in an organism as small as a zebrafish larva (approximately 5mm
in total body length). in automating this process, we would vastly improve
productivity, leading to faster data analysis and breakthroughs in
understanding the complexity of the brain. We will build upon prior attempts To
employ deep learning for automatic image segmentation extending methods for
unconventional deep learning data.

We propose and demonstrate localized mode coupling as a viable dispersion
engineering technique for phase-matched resonant four-wave mixing (FWM). We
demonstrate a dual-cavity resonant structure that employs coupling-induced
frequency splitting at one of three resonances to compensate for cavity
dispersion, enabling phase-matching. Coupling strength is controlled by thermal
tuning of one cavity enabling active control of the resonant
frequency-matching. In a fabricated silicon microresonator, we show an 8 dB
enhancement of seeded FWM efficiency over the non-compensated state. The
measured four-wave mixing has a peak wavelength conversion efficiency of -37.9
dB across a free spectral range (FSR) of 3.334 THz ($\sim$27 nm). Enabled by
strong counteraction of dispersion, this FSR is, to our knowledge, the largest
in silicon to demonstrate FWM to date. This form of mode-coupling-based, active
dispersion compensation can be beneficial for many FWM-based devices including
wavelength converters, parametric amplifiers, and widely detuned correlated
photon-pair sources. Apart from compensating intrinsic dispersion, the proposed
mechanism can alternatively be utilized in an otherwise dispersionless
resonator to counteract the detuning effect of self- and cross-phase modulation
on the pump resonance during FWM, thereby addressing a fundamental issue in the
performance of light sources such as broadband optical frequency combs.

This  paper proposes  a novel  approach for image segmentation using deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with spatial  regularization, volume, and star-shape priori.   The  proposed method aims to improve the accuracy  and efficiency  of  image segmentation by incorporating spatial information, volume constraints, and star-shape  priori  into the   CNN architecture. The spatial regularization helps to  preserve the spatial coherence of the segmented regions, while the volume constraint  ensures that the segmented regions have a consistent volume. The star-shape priori is used to guide the  segmentation process by enforcing a  star-shaped boundary for each segmented region. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that  the proposed method outperforms  existing  state-of-the-art methods in terms of  segmentation accuracy and efficiency. The proposed method  has the potential to be applied   in various applications such as medical image  analysis,  object recognition, and scene understanding.

Anatomical and biophysical modelling of left atrium (LA) and proximal
pulmonary veins (PPVs) is important for clinical management of several cardiac
diseases. Magnetic resonance imageing (MRI) allows qualitative assessment of LA
and PPVs through visualisation. However, there is a strong need for an advanced
image segmentation method to be applied to cardiac MRI for quantitative
analysis of LA and PPVs. In this study, we address this unmet clinical need by
exploring a new deep learning-based segmentation strategy for quantification of
LA and PPVs with high accuracy and heightened efficiency. Our approach is based
on a multi-view convolutional neural network (CNN) with an adaptive fusion
strategy and a new loss function that allows fast and more accurate convergence
of the backpropagation based optimisation. After training our network from
scratch by using more than 60K 2D MRI images (slices), we have evaluated our
segmentation strategy to the STACOM 2013 cardiac segmentation challenge
benchmark. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations, obtained from the
segmentation challenge, indicate that the proposed method achieved the
state-of-the-art sensitivity (90%), specificity (99%), precision (94%), and
efficiency levels (10 seconds in GPU, and 7.5 minutes in CPU).

The sigma point (SP) philtre, also known as unscented Kalman philtre, is an
attractive alternative to the extended Kalman philtre and the particle philtre.
Here, we extend the SP philtre to nonsequential Bayesian inference corresponding
to loopy factor graphs. We propose sigma point belief propagation (SPBP) as a
low-complexity approximation of the belief propagation (BP) message passing
scheme. SPBP achieves approximate marginalisations of posterior distributions
corresponding to (generally) loopy factor graphs. It is well suited for
decentralised inference because of its low communication requirements. For a
decentralised, dynamic sensor localization problem, we demonstrate that SPBP
can outperform nonparametric (particle-based) BP while requiring significantly
less computations and communications.

STECKMAP stands for  STEllar Content and  Kinematics via Maximum A Posteriori
likelihood. It   is a tool for interpreting  galaxy spectra in terms of their
stellar populations, through the derivation of their star formation  history,
age-metallicity  relation, kinematics and extinction. To do so, the observed
spectrum is projected  onto a temporal sequence of models of single stellar
populations, so as to  determine a linear combination of these models,  that fit
the observed spectrum best. The weights of the various  components  of  this
linear  combination indicate the stellar content of the population. This
procedure is  regularized using  various penalizing  functions. The  principles of
the method are detailed in Ocvirk  et al. 2006a,b. The STECKMAP software package
is  public and freely   available  at https://github.com/pocvirk/STECKMAP. A number
of authors have already adopted it and use it in their daily research. This
user guide aims at accompanying the user through the setup and first  runs of
STECKMAP.  The   last chapter will help the user to  understand and  improve his
results and experience with the   code.

Automated segmentation of anatomical structures from medical images is of great importance in various clinical applications. However, the accuracy and efficiency of existing segmentation methods can be limited due to the presence of noise and artifacts in the image data. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Post-DAE that utilizes denoising autoencoders to improve the segmentation results. The idea is to first pre-train a denoising autoencoder on a large dataset of noisy and clean image pairs, and then use the learned features to post-process the segmentation outputs from a traditional segmentation algorithm. Experimental results on a dataset of brain MRI images demonstrate that the proposed Post-DAE method achieves significantly better segmentation accuracy compared to several state-of-the-art segmentation methods. Furthermore, the computational efficiency of the method is also improved due to the reduced need for manual intervention and parameter tuning. Overall, the results suggest that the proposed method holds great potential for improving the accuracy and efficiency of anatomical segmentation in medical imaging.

The current flow of high accuracy astrophysical data, among which are the
Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) measurements by the Planck satellite, offers
an unprecedented opportunity to constrain the inflationary theory. This is
however a challenging project given the size of the inflationary landscape
which contains hundreds of different scenarios. Given that there is currently
no observational evidence for primordial non-Gaussianities, isocurvature
perturbations or any other non-minimal extension of the inflationary paradigm,
a reasonable approach is to consider the simplest models first, namely the
slow-roll single field models with minimal kinetic terms. This still leaves us
with a very populated landscape, the exploration of which requires new and
efficient strategies. It has been customary to tackle this problem by means of
approximate model independent methods while a more ambitious alternative is to
study the inflationary scenarios one by one. We have developed the new publicly
available runtime library ASPIC to implement this last approach. The ASPIC code
provides all routines needed to quickly derive reheating consistent observable
predictions within this class of scenarios. ASPIC has been designed as an
evolutive code which presently supports 118 different models, a number that may
be compared with three or four representing the present state of the art. In
this paper, for each of the ASPIC models, we present and collect new results in
a systematic manner, thereby constituting the first Encyclopaedia
Inflationaris.

This paper presents an adaptive strategy for superpixel-based region-growing image segmentation. The proposed strategy aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process by dynamically adjusting the parameters of the region-growing algorithm based on the characteristics of the input image. The strategy utilizes a set of image features, such as color and texture, to estimate the optimal parameters for each region-growing iteration. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the adaptive strategy outperforms traditional fixed-parameter approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed strategy has the potential to enhance the performance of region-growing image segmentation algorithms in various applications, such as object recognition and image analysis.
