This paper examines the   concept   of an irreversible 2-conversion  set in graphs of bounded degree. An irreversible 2-conversion set  is a  subset of vertices in  a graph such that no  vertex in  the set can be converted to  any  other vertex  outside the set using a maximum  of two conversion steps. The  paper  explores  the properties of irreversible 2-conversion sets in graphs of bounded degree and provides  conditions for their existence. Additionally, the paper discusses algorithms  and computational complexity  for finding irreversible 2-conversion  sets in such graphs. The results presented in this paper contribute to the understanding of the structural properties of graphs and have potential applications in network  optimization and algorithm design.

In recent years, deep learning (DL) methods have become powerful tools for
biomedical image segmentation. However, high annotation efforts and costs are
commonly needed to acquire sufficient biomedical training data for DL models.
To alleviate the burden of manual annotation, in this paper, we propose a new
weakly supervised DL approach for biomedical image segmentation using boxes
only annotation. First, we develop a method to combine graph search (GS) and DL
to generate fine object masks from box annotation, in which DL uses box
annotation to compute a rough segmentation for GS and then GS is applied to
locate the optimal object boundaries. During the mask generation process, we
carefully utilize information from box annotation to filter out potential
errors, and then use the generated masks to train an accurate DL segmentation
network. Extensive experiments on gland segmentation in histology images, lymph
node segmentation in ultrasound images, and fungus segmentation in electron
microscopy images show that our approach attains superior performance over the
best known state-of-the-art weakly supervised DL method and is able to achieve
(1) nearly the same accuracy compared to fully supervised DL methods with far
less annotation effort, (8) significantly better results with similar
annotation time, and (3) robust performance in various applications.

This paper presents a numerical study of  a model involving a quantum particle in  a quantum  environment. The model takes  into account the interactions between  the particle and its environment and aims to capture the dynamics of  the system. The numerical  methods  used in  the  study are  described in detail,  and the results obtained  from simulations are presented and  discussed.  The paper highlights the importance of including  the quantum nature of the environment in the model, as  it can  have a  significant impact  on the behavior of the particle.  The findings of this study contribute to a better understanding of quantum systems and  have potential applications in various  fields such as quantum computing and quantum information processing.

This paper introduces a novel algorithm for image segmentation based on dominant sets. Dominant sets, a generalization of dominant Eigenvectors, allow for the characterization of clusters in high-dimensional data spaces. The proposed algorithm extends the use of dominant sets to the realm of "constrained" image segmentation, where prior knowledge about the desired segmentation is available. By incorporating this prior knowledge into the clustering process, the algorithm is able to produce more accurate and meaningful segmentation results. The efficacy of the algorithm is demonstrated through experiments on standard benchmark datasets, where it outperforms state-of-the-art image segmentation algorithms. Additionally, the paper discusses the potential applications of the proposed algorithm in various fields, including medical image analysis and computer vision.

In this paper, we investigate the eigenvalues of non-hermitian random matrices and their relationship with the Brown measure of non-normal operators. We introduce a hermitian reduction and linearization method that allows us to analyze the spectral properties of such matrices. We show that under certain conditions, the eigenvalue distribution of non-hermitian random matrices can be approximated by the Brown measure of the corresponding non-normal operator. Our results provide insights into the spectral behavior of non-hermitian random matrices and their connection to non-normal operators in linear algebra.

The paper titled "Rethinking Atrous Convolution for Semantic Image Segmentation" presents a novel approach to semantic image segmentation using atrous convolution. The authors propose a new atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP) module that captures multi-scale contextual information by adopting multiple atrous rates. The module is integrated into a deep convolutional network and achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets. The authors also provide an extensive analysis of the proposed architecture and explain the advantages of using atrous convolution for semantic image segmentation tasks. Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding and improvement of semantic image segmentation methods by rethinking the use of atrous convolution.

This paper presents an in-situ Raman study of laser-induced graphene oxidation. Laser-induced graphene (LIG) is a promising material for various applications due to its unique properties. However, the oxidation of LIG can significantly affect its performance. In this study, we investigate the oxidation process of LIG using Raman spectroscopy. We observe the formation of various oxygen-containing functional groups on the LIG surface during the oxidation process. The intensity of the D and G bands in the Raman spectra decreases with increasing oxidation time, indicating the reduction of sp2 carbon content. Additionally, we observe the formation of a new peak at around 1700 cm-1, which is attributed to the presence of carboxyl groups. Our results provide valuable insights into the oxidation process of LIG and can guide the development of strategies to control and optimize the oxidation process for specific applications.

Semantic image segmentation  is  a challenging task in  computer  vision that involves assigning a semantic label to each   pixel in  an image. In recent years, transformer-based  models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in various  natural language processing tasks. In this  paper, we propose a fully transformer network for semantic image segmentation, where the entire network  is composed  of   transformer layers.  We introduce a novel self-attention mechanism that incorporates spatial information into  the transformer architecture, allowing the model to capture both local and global  context.   We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and compare  it with existing methods. The experimental results demonstrate  that our  fully transformer network  achieves competitive performance and outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Our findings  suggest that transformer-based  models  have great potential for semantic image segmentation tasks.

Medical image segmentation requires consensus ground truth segmentations to
be derived from multiple expert annotations. A novel approach is proposed that
obtains consensus segmentations from experts using graph cuts (GC) and semi
supervised learning (SSL). Popular approaches use iterative expectation
Maximization (EM) to estimate the Final annotation and quantify annotator's
performance. Such techniques pose the risk of getting trapped in local minima.
We propose a self consistency (SC) Score to quantify annotator consistency
Using low level image features. SSL is used to predict missing annotations by
considering global features and local image consistency. The SC score also
serves as the penalty cost in a second order markov random field (MRF) cost
function optimized using graph cuts to derive the final consensus label. graph
cut obtains a global maximum without an iterative procedure. Experimental
results on synthetic images, real data of Crohn's disease patients and retinal
images show our final segmentation To be accurate and more consistent than
competing methods.

This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting roots in soil using the U-Net architecture. The U-Net architecture is a convolutional neural network that has been widely used for image segmentation tasks. In this study, we adapt the U-Net architecture to segment roots in soil images. We propose a modified U-Net architecture that incorporates skip connections and data augmentation techniques to improve the accuracy of root segmentation. We evaluate our approach on a dataset of soil images with ground truth annotations for root segmentation. Our results show that the proposed U-Net architecture achieves high accuracy in segmenting roots in soil images, outperforming existing methods. This work has implications for plant biology research and agricultural applications, as accurate root segmentation is crucial for studying root growth and understanding plant-soil interactions.

In real-world practice, medical images acquired in different phases possess
complementary information, {\em e.g.}, radiologists often refer to both
arterial and venous scans in order to make the diagnosis. However, in medical
image analysis, fusing prediction from two phases is often difficult, because
(i) there is a domain gap between two phases, and (ii) the semantic labels are
not pixel-wise corresponded even for images scanned from the same patient. This
paper studies organ segmentation in two-phase CT scans. We propose Phase
Collaborative Network (PCN), an end-to-end framework that contains both
generative and discriminative modules. PCN can be mathematically explained to
formulate phase-to-phase and data-to-label relations jointly. Experiments are
performed on a two-phase CT dataset, on which PCN outperforms the baselines
working with one-phase data by a large margin, and we empirically verify that
the gain comes from inter-phase collaboration. Besides, PCN transfers well to
two public single-phase datasets, demonstrating its potential applications.

This paper  introduces the concept of   open-world entity segmentation, which aims to segment entities in an image without having prior  knowledge of all possible entity categories. Traditional methods  typically rely on predefined categories and are unable to handle  novel or unexpected entities. The proposed  method  trains a  deep neural network to segment entities based on a  diverse  dataset containing  known  and unknown categories. The network architecture includes a novel  open-world  output module  that estimates the presence of  unknown entities. The results  demonstrate  that the proposed method achieves accurate segmentation of known  entities and effectively identifies unknown entities. By addressing the limitations of traditional approaches,  this research  contributes to the advancement  of entity segmentation in open-world scenarios.

This paper develops a method to carry out the large-$N$ asymptotic analysis
of a class of $N$-dimensional integrals arising in the context of the so-called
quantum separation of variables method. We push further ideas developed in the
context of random matrices of size $N$, but in the present problem, two scales
$1/N^{\alpha}$ and $1/N$ naturally occur. In our case, the equilibrium measure
is $N^{\alpha}$-dependent and characterised by means of the solution to a
$2\times 2$ Riemann--Hilbert problem, whose large-$N$ behaviour is analysed in
detail. Combining these results with techniques of concentration of measures
and an asymptotic analysis of the Schwinger-Dyson equations at the
distributional level, we obtain the large-$N$ behaviour of the free energy
explicitly up to $o(1)$. The use of distributional Schwinger-Dyson is a novelty
that allows us treating sufficiently differentiable interactions and the mixing
of scales $1/N^{\alpha}$ and $1/N$, thus waiving the analyticity assumptions
often used in random matrix theory.

Superpixel Convolutional Networks (SPCNs) are image semantic segmenting techniques that use a superpixel algorithm to generate image regions that are more cohesive in terms of color and texture. These regions can then be used as input for convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to perform semantic segmentation. This paper proposes a novel approach called Bilateral Inceptions for SPCNs, which uses a combination of bilateral filtering and inception modules to improve the performance of pixel-level predictions. The proposed approach is evaluated on benchmark datasets and compared with other state-of-the-art techniques. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the Bilateral Inceptions approach in improving the accuracy of semantic segmentation compared to existing methods.

This paper aims to review and compare different models of microbial dormancy in biofilms and planktonic cultures. Microbial dormancy, or the ability of microorganisms to enter a dormant state, is a well-documented phenomenon that has significant implications in various fields including environmental microbiology and medical microbiology. In this paper, we discuss the different factors that promote microbial dormancy, such as nutrient limitation and environmental stressors, and how these factors differ in biofilms versus planktonic cultures. We also compare the different models that have been proposed to explain microbial dormancy in both biofilms and planktonic cultures, including the persister cell model and the growth advantage in stationary phase (GASP) model. Additionally, we discuss the implications of microbial dormancy in various applications, such as antibiotic resistance and biofilm formation. Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of the models of microbial dormancy in biofilms and planktonic cultures and highlights the need for further research in this area.

This paper presents  a novel approach for automatic image labelling  at the pixel level. Traditional image labelling methods rely   on either manual annotation or low-level feature extraction  techniques. In this work, we propose a deep learning-based approach that can accurately label   each pixel in an image based on its  content. Our model employs a convolutional neural   network  architecture combined with a conditional random  field  to capture  both local and global contextual information. We  evaluate the performance of our  approach on various  benchmark  datasets and  compare it with state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate that our  method achieves  superior accuracy in pixel-level image labelling tasks. This work  has potential applications in computer vision, image segmentation,  and object detection.

This paper presents effective results for Diophantine equations over finitely generated domains. The authors develop a general framework for solving Diophantine equations and provide algorithms for finding solutions. They also analyze the complexity of these algorithms and provide bounds on the size of the solutions. The effectiveness of the results is demonstrated through several examples and applications. Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding and practical implementation of solving Diophantine equations over finitely generated domains.

The incidence of thyroid nodule is very high and generally increases with the
age. Thyroid nodule may presage the emergence of thyroid cancer. The thyroid
nodule can be completely cured if detected early. Fine needle aspiration
cytology is a recognized early diagnosis method of thyroid nodule. There are
still some limitations in the fine needle aspiration cytology, and the
ultrasound diagnosis of thyroid nodule has become the first choice for
auxiliary examination of thyroid nodular disease. If we could combine medical
imaging technology and fine needle aspiration cytology, the diagnostic rate of
thyroid nodule would be improved significantly. The properties of ultrasound
will degrade the image quality, which makes it difficult to recognize the edges
for physicians. Image segmentation technique based on graph theory has become a
research hotspot at present. Normalized cut (Ncut) is a representative one,
which is suitable for segmentation of feature parts of medical image. However,
how to solve the normalized cut has become a problem, which needs large memory
capacity and heavy calculation of weight matrix. It always generates over
segmentation or less segmentation which leads to inaccurate in the
segmentation. The speckle noise in B ultrasound image of thyroid tumor makes
the quality of the image deteriorate. In the light of this characteristic, we
combine the anisotropic diffusion model with the normalized cut in this paper.
After the enhancement of anisotropic diffusion model, it removes the noise in
the B ultrasound image while preserves the important edges and local details.
This reduces the amount of computation in constructing the weight matrix of the
improved normalized cut and improves the accuracy of the final segmentation
results. The feasibility of the method is proved by the experimental results.

We introduce a new method of estimation of parameters in semiparametric and
nonparametric models. 

The method is based on estimating equations that are
$U$-statistics in the observations. The $U$-statistics are based on higher
order influence functions that extend ordinary linear influence functions of
the parameter of interest, and represent higher derivatives of this parameter. 

For parameters for which the representation cannot be perfect the method leads
to a bias-variance trade-off, and results in estimators that converge at a
slower than $\sqrt n$-rate. In a number of examples the resulting rate can be
shown to be optimal. 

We are particularly interested in estimating parameters in
models with a nuisance parameter of high dimension or low regularity, where the
parameter of interest cannot be estimated at $\sqrt n$-rate, but we also
consider efficient $\sqrt n$-estimation using novel nonlinear estimators. The
general approach is applied in detail to the example of estimating a mean
response when the response is not always observed.

This paper provides a novel approach for unsupervised segmentation of pathology
images. Staging of bladder disease is a significant factor of prognosis. Measuring the
maximum dimensions of the invasive component in a pathology images is an
important task. However, image segmentation techniques for analyzing the
extent of invasive and invasive components on pathology images can provide
pathological examination. Unfortunately, it is challenging for most of the recent
segmentation technologies that depend on supervised learning to cope with unlabeled
pathology images. In this paper, we propose a unified approach to supervised
representation learning and clustering for pathology image segmentation. Our
approach consists of three stages. In the second stage, we learn feature
representations of training patches from a target image using the spherical
k-means. The aim of this stage is to provide cluster centroids which can
be employed as filters for feature processing. In the next stage, we apply
conventional k-means to the representations generated by the centroids and then
project cluster labels to the target images. We evaluated our techniques on
pathology images of lung tumor specimen. Our studies concluded that the
proposed technique outperforms conventional k-means segmentation and the
multithreshold Otsu technique both systematically and qualitatively with an
improved normalized mutual information (NMI) score of 0.626 compared to 0.168
and 0.167, respectively. Moreover, we showed that the centroids can be
applied to the segmentation of other slices from the same sample.

This paper presents algorithms for computing minimum rainbow and strong rainbow colorings of block graphs. A block graph is a graph in which every biconnected component is a clique. A rainbow coloring of a graph is a coloring of its vertices such that every pair of vertices is connected by a rainbow path, which is a path that uses distinct colors for its edges. A strong rainbow coloring is a coloring in which every pair of vertices is connected by a rainbow path that also uses distinct colors for its internal vertices. The paper introduces a dynamic programming algorithm for computing the minimum rainbow coloring of a block graph, and extends it to compute the strong rainbow coloring. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithms are efficient and outperform existing approaches.

This paper introduces the   concept of differentiable stratified groupoids and explores their application in studying the inertia spaces associated with group actions on manifolds. The authors establish a de Rham theorem for inertia spaces,   which  provides a powerful tool for analyzing the geometric  and  topological properties of these spaces.   The paper presents the main  results, outlines the  proof techniques used, and  discusses potential applications and future  directions  for research in this area.

Deep learning has achieved great success as a powerful classification tool
and also made great progress in sematic segmentation. As a result, many
researchers also believe that deep learning is the most powerful tool for pixel
level image segmentation. Could deep learning achieve the same pixel level
accuracy as traditional image segmentation techniques by mapping the features
of the object into a non-linear function? This paper gives a short survey of
the accuracies achieved by deep learning so far in image classification and
image segmentation. Compared to the high accuracies achieved by deep learning
in classifying limited categories in international vision challenges, the image
segmentation accuracies achieved by deep learning in the same challenges are
only about eighty percent. On the contrary, the image segmentation accuracies
achieved in international biomedical challenges are close to ninty five
percent. Why the difference is so big? Since the accuracies of the competitors
methods are only evaluated based on their submitted results instead of
reproducing the results by submitting the source codes or the software, are the
achieved accuracies verifiable or overhyped? We are going to find it out by
analyzing the working principle of deep learning. Finally, we compared the
accuracies of state of the art deep learning methods with a threshold selection
method quantitatively. Experimental results showed that the threshold selection
method could achieve significantly higher accuracy than deep learning methods
in image segmentation.

Many natural decision problems can be formulated as  constraint  satisfaction
problems  for reducts $\mathbb{A}$ of finitely  bounded homogeneous structures.
This class of problems is a large generalisation  of the class of CSPs over
finite domains. Our first result is a  general polynomial-time reduction from
such infinite-domain CSPs  to finite-domain CSPs. We use this reduction to
obtain new powerful polynomial-time tractability conditions that can be
expressed in  terms of the  topological polymorphism clone  of  $\mathbb{A}$.
Moreover, we study the  subclass $\mathcal{C}$  of CSPs for structures
$\mathbb{A}$ that are reducts of a structure with  a unary language.  Also this
class $\mathcal{C}$ properly extends the class of all finite-domain CSPs.   We
apply our new  tractability conditions to prove the general tractability
conjecture of  Bodirsky and  Pinsker  for reducts  of finitely bounded  homogeneous
structures for the class $\mathcal{C}$.

In this paper, the authors present a new method called GENESIS-V2 for inferring unordered object representations without the need  for iterative refinement.  The goal  of this  work is to  improve the accuracy and efficiency of  object representation inference, which is  a  critical task  in computer vision and machine learning. The authors propose a novel approach that combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and a generative  model to  generate ordered  object representations.  GENESIS-V2 uses   a discriminative model to assign each object a unique identity and then applies a  generative model  to sample object-level permutation matrices. The  experimental results show that GENESIS-V2 achieves state-of-the-art performance  on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its  effectiveness in inferring  unordered object representations without  the need for  iterative refinement.

The Seiberg-Witten theory has provided a powerful framework for studying four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetric gauge theories. In this paper, we explore the Seiberg-Witten geometry of quiver gauge theories, which are a class of supersymmetric gauge theories with gauge groups and matter fields arranged in a linear chain. We study the moduli spaces of vacua and their topological properties, such as the intersection numbers of cycles. We also investigate the Coulomb branch geometry and discuss the role of monopole operators. Our results shed light on the dynamics and symmetries of quiver gauge theories and contribute to the broader understanding of supersymmetric gauge theories.

——Boundary information plays a very important role in the two-dimensional image segmentation, but usually ignored in the three-dimensional point cloud segmentation, which often generates ambiguous features in the feature extraction, and the boundaries of two objects are in the process of distinguishing each other, resulting in the misclassification of the transition area. In this paper, we firstly design a boundary prediction model (BPM) to predict the boundary. Based on the predicted boundary, a boundary-aware geometric encoding module (GEM) is designed to gather local features with discrimination information in the neighborhood, so as not to be mixed up with features belonging to different categories. But also to introduce additional geometric information, a lightweight geometric convolution operation (GCO) is proposed to obtain more distinctive features. On the basis of the boundary-aware GEM, the neural network is constructed, and a series of experiments are conducted on the S3DIS, ScanNet-2 and other public data sets. The results show that the performance of the system is improved a lot, and it can be regarded as a significant improvement. The source code is available at https://github.com/jchenxu/ba-gem.

This paper presents a new method for training conditional random fields (CRFs) for large-scale image segmentation tasks. Traditional methods for training CRFs rely on iterative optimization algorithms, which can be computationally expensive and time-consuming for large-scale datasets. The proposed method, called closed-form training, leverages the property that CRFs can be formulated as a Gaussian Markov random field (GMRF) to develop a closed-form solution for training. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on various image segmentation datasets, showing that it achieves comparable or better performance than state-of-the-art methods while significantly reducing training time. The closed-form training method has the potential to enhance the scalability and efficiency of CRFs for large-scale image segmentation tasks.

Single Source Ultra Resolution (SISR) methods Based on Super Resolution
Convolutional Neural Network (SRCNN) are applied to micro-computed imaging
({\mu}CT) images of limestone and limestone sediments. Digital rock imaging is
limited by the flexibility of the scanning apparatus resulting in trade-offs
between resolution and field of view, and super resolution technologies tested in
this research aim to compensate for these limitations. SRCNN models SR-Resnet, Extended
Dark SR (EDSR), and Wide-Activation Dark CR (WDSR) are used on the Digital Rock
Super Resolution 1 (DRSRD1) Dataset of 4x downsampled photos, consisting of
2000 high resolution (800x800) raw micro-CT images of Bentheimer sandstone and
Estaillades carbonate. The trained models are applied to the validation and
test data within the database and show a 3-5 dB increase in image quality compared
to bicubic interpolation, with all tested models performing within a 0.1 dB
range. Difference maps suggest that edge sharpness is largely lost in
images outside the scope of the trained model, with only low amplitude noise
related detail loss. We find that apart from generation of high-resolution
pictures, a useful side effect of super resolution technologies used to
synthetically downgraded pictures is the removal of image noise while recovering
edgewise sharpness which is important for the segmentation procedure. The model
is often tested against real low-resolution images of Bentheimer rock with image
augmentation to account for natural noise and blur. The SRCNN technique is shown
to act as a preconditioner for image segmentation under these conditions
which inevitably leads to further future growth and training of models that
segment an image directly. Picture reconstruction by SRCNN on the rock images is of
considerably lower reliability than conventional techniques and suggests SRCNN
techniques are a viable processing step in a digital rock workflow.

This paper proposes a  semi-supervised learning approach for aggregated multilayer  graphs. The approach  utilizes diffuse interface methods and  fast matrix  vector products to effectively learn from partially labeled data. The method is capable of handling large-scale  datasets  and achieves  competitive performance compared   to existing techniques. Experimental  results on real-world   datasets demonstrate  the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach. Overall, this paper presents a novel and practical solution  for semi-supervised learning on aggregated multilayer graphs.

In this paper, we review and extend a family of log-det divergences for
symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices and discuss their fundamental
properties. We show how to generate from parameterized Alpha-Beta (AB) and
Gamma Log-det divergences many well known divergences, for example, Stein's
loss, S-divergence, called also Jensen-Bregman LogDet (JBLD) divergence, the
Logdet Zero (Bhattacharryya) divergence, Affine Invariant Riemannian Metric
(AIRM) as well as some new divergences. Moreover, we establish links and
correspondences among many log-det divergences and display them on alpha-beta
plain for various set of parameters. Furthermore, this paper bridges these
divergences and shows also their links to divergences of multivariate and
multiway Gaussian distributions. Closed form formulas are derived for gamma
divergences of two multivariate Gaussian densities including as special cases
the Kullback-Leibler, Bhattacharryya, R\'enyi and Cauchy-Schwartz divergences.
Symmetrized versions of the log-det divergences are also discussed and
reviewed. A class of divergences is extended to multiway divergences for
separable covariance (precision) matrices.

Cross modal image syntheses is gaining significant interests for its ability
to estimate target images of a different modality from a given set of source
images,like estimating MR to MR, MR to CT, CT to PET etc, without the need for
an actual acquisition.Though they show potential for applications in radiation
therapy planning,image super resolution, atlas construction, image segmentation
etc.The synthesis results are not as accurate as the actual acquisition.In this
paper,we address the problem of multi modal image synthesis by proposing a
fully convolutional deep learning architecture called the SynNet.We extend the
proposed architecture for various input output configurations. And finally, we
propose a structure preserving custom loss function for cross-modal image
synthesis.We validate the proposed SynNet and its extended framework on BRATS
dataset with comparisons against three state-of-the art methods.And the results
of the proposed custom loss function is validated against the traditional loss
function used by the state-of-the-art methods for cross modal image synthesis.

It is well-known that the formation of amyloid fiber may cause invertible
damage to cells, while the underlying mechanism has not been fully uncovered.
In this paper, we construct a mathematical model, consisting of infinite ODEs
in the form of mass-action equations together with two reaction-convection
PDEs, and then simplify it to a system of 5 ODEs by using the maximum entropy
principle. This model is based on four simple assumptions, one of which is that
cell damage is raised by oligomers rather than mature fibrils. With the
simplified model, the effects of nucleation and elongation, fragmentation,
protein and seeds concentrations on amyloid formation and cell damage are
extensively explored and compared with experiments. We hope that our results
can provide a valuable insight into the processes of amyloid formation and cell
damage thus raised.

This paper investigates the phenomenon  of itinerant magnetism in spin-orbit coupled Bose gases.  The  authors explore the properties and behavior of these gases under the influence of spin-orbit coupling  and magnetic fields. They find that the interplay between spin-orbit coupling, Bose-Einstein condensation, and magnetic interactions leads to the emergence of itinerant magnetism. The paper  presents  theoretical   calculations and   experimental observations  that  elucidate the underlying mechanisms. The findings have implications for understanding magnetism in systems with spin-orbit coupling and  open   up  new  avenues for the study of Bose gases  in various contexts.

This paper aims to define the implication relation for classical logic by examining its properties and characteristics. The authors propose a formal definition of implication based on the concept of logical consequence, and discuss its relationship with other logical connectives. They also explore the implications of this definition for the interpretation and application of classical logic in various contexts. The paper concludes by highlighting the importance of a clear and precise definition of implication in order to ensure the consistency and validity of logical reasoning.

Texture segmentation is the procedure of partitioning an image into areas
with multiple colors containing a different group of pixels. Detecting the
discontinuity of the filter's output and their statistical properties help in
analyzing and classifying a given image with multiple color areas. In
this proposed paper, chili x-ray image texture segmentation is done by
applying Gabor filter. The texture segmented result obtained from Gabor filter fed
into four texture filters, namely Entropy, Standard Deviation and Range
filter. After performing texture calculation, features can be obtained by applying
statistical techniques. In this paper Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrices and Second
order statistics are used as feature extraction tools. Features derived
from statistical techniques are given to Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier.
Using this method, it is discovered that texture segmentation is followed by
the Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix feature extraction method gives a lower
accuracy rate of 84% when compared with First order feature extraction technique.
  Key Words: Texture segmentation, Color filter, Gabor filter, Features
extraction methods, SVM algorithm.

Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning. However, the privacy and security of medical data pose significant challenges in developing accurate and reliable segmentation algorithms. In this paper, we propose BUNET, a blind medical image segmentation method based on secure UNET. BUNET leverages the UNET architecture for accurate segmentation while incorporating privacy-preserving techniques to ensure the confidentiality of sensitive medical data. We evaluate the performance of BUNET on a dataset of medical images and compare it with existing segmentation methods. The results demonstrate that BUNET achieves competitive segmentation accuracy while maintaining the privacy and security of medical data. Our proposed method has the potential to enhance the development of secure and reliable medical image segmentation algorithms.

In this paper, we present a numerical study of a model that describes a quantum particle interacting with a quantum environment. The model is based on the concept of a quantum bath, which represents the environment as a collection of harmonic oscillators. We use numerical techniques to solve the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for the system and study the dynamics of the particle in the presence of the environment. We investigate the effects of different parameters, such as the coupling strength between the particle and the bath, on the behavior of the system. Our results show that the presence of the environment can significantly affect the dynamics of the particle, leading to phenomena such as decoherence and dissipation. We also discuss the implications of our findings for the understanding of quantum systems in realistic environments. Overall, our study provides valuable insights into the behavior of quantum particles in quantum environments and contributes to the ongoing research in the field of quantum mechanics.

This paper presents a new ensemble learning framework for 3D biomedical image segmentation. The framework incorporates multiple deep learning models and combines their outputs using a weighted voting approach. The weights are learned during the training process to optimize the segmentation performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The framework can be applied to various types of biomedical images and has the potential to improve medical diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents a novel approach for surface segmentation in irregularly sampled space using convex priors. The proposed method aims to find the optimal surface segmentation by minimizing an energy function that incorporates both data fidelity and prior information. The irregularly sampled space is represented by a graph structure, and the surface segmentation problem is formulated as a graph cut problem. The convex priors are used to regularize the segmentation and enforce smoothness. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method compared to existing approaches. The proposed method has potential applications in various fields such as medical imaging, computer vision, and graphics.

The paper investigates the existence of interior bubbling solutions for the critical Lin-Ni-Takagi problem in three dimensions. The Lin-Ni-Takagi problem is a system of coupled elliptic equations that arise in the study of semiclassical limit of a nonlinear Schrödinger equation. The criticality of the problem means that any solution must satisfy a certain condition related to the critical Sobolev exponent. The existence of interior bubbling solutions, which are solutions that concentrate at a single point in the interior of the domain, is an interesting and open question. The paper presents a novel approach using a new integral estimate to prove the existence of such solutions. The main result establishes the existence of interior bubbling solutions for a wide range of parameters. The paper concludes with a discussion of possible extensions and further research directions.

Ιmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn іs а рорulаr аrеа оf rеsеаrсh іn соmрutеr vіsіоn thаt hаs
mаnу аррlісаtіоns іn аutоmаtеd іmаgе рrосеssіng. А rесеnt tесhnіquе саllеd
ріесеwіsе flаt еmbеddіngs (РFΕ) hаs bееn рrороsеd fоr usе іn іmаgе
sеgmеntаtіоn; РFΕ trаnsfоrms іmаgе ріхеl dаtа іntо а lоwеr dіmеnsіоnаl
rерrеsеntаtіоn whеrе sіmіlаr ріхеls аrе рullеd сlоsе tоgеthеr аnd dіssіmіlаr
ріхеls аrе рushеd араrt. Τhіs tесhnіquе hаs shоwn рrоmіsіng rеsults, but іts
оrіgіnаl fоrmulаtіоn іs nоt соmрutаtіоnаllу fеаsіblе fоr lаrgе іmаgеs. Wе
рrороsе twо іmрrоvеmеnts tо thе аlgоrіthm fоr соmрutіng РFЕ: fіrst, wе
rеfоrmulаtе роrtіоns оf thе аlgоrіthm tо еnаblе vаrіоus lіnеаr аlgеbrа
ореrаtіоns tо bе реrfоrmеd іn раrаllеl; sесоnd, wе рrороsе utіlіzіng аn
іtеrаtіvе lіnеаr sоlvеr (рrесоndіtіоnеd соnjugаtе grаdіеnt) tо quісklу sоlvе а
lіnеаr lеаst-squаrеs рrоblеm thаt оссurs іn thе іnnеr lоор оf а nеstеd
іtеrаtіоn. Wіth thеsе twо соmрutаtіоnаl іmрrоvеmеnts, wе shоw оn а рublісlу
аvаіlаblе іmаgе dаtаbаsе thаt ΡFΕ саn bе sреd uр bу аn оrdеr оf mаgnіtudе
wіthоut sасrіfісіng sеgmеntаtіоn реrfоrmаnсе. Оur rеsults mаkе thіs tесhnіquе
mоrе рrасtісаl fоr usе оn lаrgе dаtа sеts, nоt оnlу fоr іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn, but
fоr gеnеrаl dаtа сlustеrіng рrоblеms.

This paper presents a novel method for tracking fast neutrons using a combination of scintillating fibers and silicon photomultipliers. The proposed method offers high spatial resolution and efficiency in detecting and tracking fast neutrons, which is crucial for various applications in nuclear physics and radiation detection. The experimental setup and data analysis techniques are described in detail, and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately tracking fast neutrons. The potential applications and future directions for this tracking technique are also discussed. Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of neutron detection and tracking, offering a promising solution for improving the accuracy and efficiency of neutron detection systems.

Despite the tremendous success of deep neural networks in medical image
segmentation, they typically require a large amount of costly, expert-level
annotated data. Few-shot segmentation approaches address this issue by learning
to transfer knowledge from limited quantities of labelled examples.
Incorporating appropriate prior knowledge is critical in designing
high-performance few-shot segmentation algorithms. Since strong spatial priors
exist in many medical imageing modalities, we propose a prototype-based method
-- namely, the location-sensitive local prototype network -- that leverages
spatial priors to perform few-shot medical image segmentation. Our approach
divides the difficult problem of segmenting the entyre image with global
prototypes into easily solvable subproblems of local region segmentation with
local prototypes. For organ segmentation experiments on the VISCERAL CT image
dataset, our method outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches by 10% in the
mean Dice coefficient. Extensive ablation studies demonstrate the substantial
benefits of incorporating spatial information and confirm the effectiveness of
our approach.

This paper explores the mathematical properties of square-tiled tori, which are two-dimensional surfaces consisting of square tiles arranged in a periodic pattern. The authors investigate various aspects of square-tiled tori, including their topological properties, tiling spaces, and geometric properties. They also discuss the relationship between square-tiled tori and other mathematical structures, such as flat structures and billiards. The paper provides a comprehensive overview of square-tiled tori and their relevance in various areas of mathematics.

Unsupervised image segmentation algorithms aim at identifying disjoint
homogeneous regions in an image, and have been subject to considerable
attention in the machine vision community. 

In this paper, a popular theoretical
model with it's origins in statistical physics and social dynamics, known as
the Deffuant-Weisbuch model, is applied to the image segmentation problem. The
Deffuant-Weisbuch model has been found to be useful in modelling the evolution
of a closed system of interacting agents characterised by their opinions or
beliefs, leading to the formation of clusters of agents who share a similar
opinion or belief at steady state. In the context of image segmentation, this
paper considers a pixel as an agent and it's colour property as it's opinion,
with opinion updates as per the Deffuant-Weisbuch model. 

Apart from applying
the basic model to image segmentation, this paper incorporates adjacency and
neighbourhood information in the model, which factors in the local similarity
and smoothness properties of images. Convergence is reached when the number of
unique pixel opinions, i.e., the number of colour centres, matches the
pre-specified number of clusters. Experiments are performed on a set of images
from the Berkeley Image Segmentation Dataset and the results are analysed both
qualitatively and quantitatively, which indicate that this simple and intuitive
method is promising for image segmentation. 

To the best of the knowledge of the
author, this is the first work where a theoretical model from statistical
physics and social dynamics has been successfully applied to image processing.

We model the phase oscillations of electrons in race-track microtrons by
means of an area preserving map with a fixed point at the origin, which
represents the synchronous trajectory of a refrence particle in the beam. We
study the nonlinear stability of the origin in terms of the synchronous phase
-- the phase of the synchronous particle at the injection. We estimate the size
and shape of the stability domain around the origin, whose main connected
component is enclosed by the last rotational invariant curve. We describe the
evolution of the stability domain as the synchronous phase varies. Besides, we
approximate some rotational invariant curves by level sets of certain
Hamiltonians. Finally, we clarify the role of the stable and unstable invariant
curves of some hyperbolic (fixed or periodic) points.

3D convolution neural networks (CNN) have been proved very successful in
parsing organs or tumours in 3D medical images, but it remains sophisticated
and time-consuming to choose or design proper 3D networks given different task
contexts. Recently, Neural Architecture Search (NAS) is proposed to solve this
problem by searching for the best network architecture automatically. However,
the inconsistency between search stage and deployment stage often exists in NAS
algorithms due to memory constraints and large search space, which could become
more serious when applying NAS to some memory and time consuming tasks, such as
3D medical image segmentation. In this paper, we propose coarse-to-fine neural
architecture search (C2FNAS) to automatically search a 3D segmentation network
from scratch without inconsistency on network size or input size. Specifically,
we divide search procedure into two stages: 1) the coarse stage, where we
search the macro-level topology of network, i.e. how each convolution
module is connected to other modules; 2) fine stage, where we search at
micro-level for operations in each cell based on previous searched macro-level
topology. The coarse-to-fine manner divides search procedure into two
consecutive stages and meanwhile resolves the inconsistency. We evaluate our
method on 10 public datasets from Medical Segmentation Decalthon (MSD)
challenge, and achieve state-of-the-art performance with network searched
using one dataset, which demonstrates the effectiveness and generalization of
our searched models.

The influence of fixed temperature and fixed heat flux thermal boundary
conditions on rapidly rotating convection in the plane layer geometry is
investigated for the case of stress-free mechanical boundary conditions. It is
shown that whereas the leading order system satisfies fixed temperature
boundary conditions implicitly, a double boundary layer structure is necessary
to satisfy the fixed heat flux thermal boundary conditions. The boundary layers
Consist of a classical Ekman layer adjacent to the solid boundaries that adjust
viscous stresses To zero, and a layer in thermal wind balance just outside the
ekman Layers adjusts the temperature such that the fixed heat flux thermal
boundary conditions are satisfied. The influence of these boundary layers on
the interior geostrophically balanced convection is shown to be asymptotically
weak, however. Upon defining a simple rescaling Of the thermal variables, the
leading order reduced system of governing equations are therefore Equivalent
for both boundary conditions. These results imply that any horizontal thermal
variation along the boundaries that varies on the scale of the Convection has
no leading Order influence on the interior convection.

Neural networks are becoming more and more popular for analysis of
physiological time-series. The most successful deep learning systems in this
domain combine convolutional and recurrent layers to extract useful features to
model temporal relations. Unfortunately, these recurrent models are difficult
to tune and optimize. In our experience, they often require task-specific
modifications, which makes them challenging to use for non-experts. We propose
U-Time, a fully feed-forward deep learning approach to physiological time
series segmentation developed for the analysis of sleep data. U-Time is a
temporal fully convolutional network based on U-Net architecture that was
originally proposed for image segmentation. U-Time maps sequential inputs of
arbitrary length to sequences of class labels on freely chosen temporal
scale. This is done by implicitly classifying every individual time-point of
the input signal and aggregating these classifications over fixed intervals to
form the final predictions. We evaluated U-Time for sleep stage classification
on a large collection of sleep electroencephalography (EEG) datasets. In all
cases, we found that U-Time reaches or outperforms current state-of-the-art
deep learning models while being much more robust in training process and
without requiring architecture or hyperparameter adaptation across tasks.

In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning framework for anatomy
segmentation and automatic landmark- ing. Specifically, we focus on the
challenging problem of mandible segmentation from cone-beam computed tomography
(CBCT) scans and identification of 9 anatomical landmarks of the mandible on
the geodesic space. The overall approach employs three inter-related steps. In
step 1, we propose a deep neu- ral network architecture with carefully designed
regularisation, and network hyper-parametres to perform image segmentation
without the need for data augmentation and complex post- processing refinement.
In step 2, we formulate the landmark localization problem directly on the
geodesic space for sparsely- spaced anatomical landmarks. In step 3, we propose
to use a long short-term memory (LSTM) network to identify closely- spaced
landmarks, which is rather difficult to obtain using other standard detection
networks. The proposed fully automated method showed superior efficacy compared
to the state-of-the- art mandible segmentation and landmarking approaches in
craniofacial anomalies and diseased states. We used a very challenging CBCT
dataset of 50 patients with a high-degree of craniomaxeillofacial (CMF)
variability that is realistic in clinical practise. Complementary to the
quantitative analysis, the qualitative visual inspection was conducted for
distinct CBCT scans from 250 patients with high anatomical variability. We have
also shown feasibility of the proposed work in an independent dataset from
MICCAI Head-Neck Challenge (2015) achieving the state-of-the-art performance.
Lastly, we present an in-depth analysis of the proposed deep networks with
respect to the choice of hyper-parametres such as pooling and activation
functions.

This paper presents a method for extracting gray images using fuzzy logic. The proposed method utilizes fuzzy logic to determine the grayness of an image by considering the intensity values of its pixels. The method first calculates the average intensity value of the image and then applies fuzzy logic to classify each pixel as either gray or non-gray based on its intensity value. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves high accuracy in extracting gray images compared to existing methods. The method can be applied in various image processing applications where the extraction of gray images is required.

This paper presents a novel approach for generating  realistic vehicle images  that blend  seamlessly with their surroundings. The proposed method leverages  deep learning techniques to  learn the contextual information of the environment and incorporate it  into the generated vehicle images. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of  their approach through   extensive experiments and comparisons with existing methods.  The results show that the generated   vehicle  images exhibit a high level of realism and coherence with the surrounding environment. This research has significant implications for  various  applications, such as virtual reality,  autonomous driving,  and computer graphics.

The  goal of this paper is to study harmonic  maps of finite uniton  type  into inner symmetric  spaces. More specifically, we analyze the existence and regularity of harmonic maps with finite uniton data  into  inner symmetric spaces. We establish a representation theorem for harmonic     maps    of finite uniton type into inner symmetric spaces, and then apply this result to study the case when the  target space is a symmetric space. Furthermore, we investigate the regularity  of harmonic  maps by considering the associated linearized operators. Throughout the paper, we provide various examples and applications to illustrate the  theoretical  results.

Great3 is the third edition of a competition for image analysis, which has for its aim to test and promote the development of methods for analyzing astronomical images that will be used to measure weak gravitational lensing. The latter requires the very precise estimation of very small distortions of the shape of galaxies in the presence of much larger intrinsic shapes and distortions due to the blurring due to atmospheric and optical turbulence and instrumental effects. Great3 is a challenge addressed to the astronomy, machine learning and statistics communities, and includes the test of three specific effects, two of which have never before been tested in a community challenge. The effects are the complexity of realistic galaxy models based on high-resolution space images, the spatially varying blur kernel, and the multiple exposure of images. To facilitate the entry of newcomers and to provide a diagnostic tool, the simulation software for the challenge is made available for public use, but the exact values of the parameters used in the challenge are concealed. Sample scripts for analyzing the challenge data with existing methods will also be provided. For more information see the Great3 website, and also the leaderboard page, at http://great3.org.uk/leaderboard.

Self-supervised learning is a promising way to make full use of the data in biomedical image segmentation. One of the most effective ways of achieving self-supervision is image inpainting: the task of filling in arbitrary missing areas with an image. In this paper, we focus on inpainting as the self-supervised proxy task and propose two novel structural changes to further improve the performance of deep convolutional networks. We guide the process of generating missing images by using supervoxels instead of arbitrary masks, and we focus the network on the area of interest for the main task, which we call the region of interest. We hypothesize that these two additions to the network force it to learn semantics more appropriate for the main task and test our hypothesis on two applications: brain tumor and white matter hyperintensity. We show that the proposed method outperforms supervised convolutional neural networks without self-supervision and conventional inpainting-based self-supervision methods on both small and large training sets.

This paper presents a novel approach for polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image semantic segmentation using a combination of 3D discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and Markov random field (MRF) techniques. The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional SAR image segmentation methods by incorporating both spatial and spectral information. The 3D DWT is used to decompose the polarimetric SAR image into different frequency subbands, which are then used to extract relevant features for segmentation. The MRF model is employed to capture the spatial dependencies between neighboring pixels and enforce smoothness in the segmentation results. Experimental results on real-world polarimetric SAR images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting different land cover classes. The proposed approach offers a promising solution for polarimetric SAR image segmentation, with potential applications in various fields such as agriculture, urban planning, and environmental monitoring.

Auto-DeepLab  is a  hierarchical  neural  architecture  search (NAS) method   for semantic image segmentation.  It aims to automatically discover the  optimal neural network architecture for this task. The proposed method  consists of two stages: a coarse-grained search and a fine-grained search.  In the coarse-grained search, a search space is   defined by stacking multiple cells, each containing a set of candidate operations. A  reinforcement learning algorithm is then used to search for the best cell  architecture. In the fine-grained search, the  best cell architecture is used as a building block to   construct the final network architecture. The proposed method achieves  state-of-the-art performance   on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating  its effectiveness in automatically designing neural network architectures for  semantic image segmentation.

The GRavitational lEnsing Accuracy Assessment 3 (GREAT3) challenge is the first
in a trilogy of imagery characterization challenges, with a aim of testing and
supporting the implementation of techniques for measuring astronomical images that
will be used to measure strong gravitational lensing. This measurement allows
very detailed measurement of very large galaxy size distortions, in the
absence of even greater intrinsic galaxy shapes and distortions due to the
blurring kernel induced by the atmosphere, telescope optics, and instrumental
effects. The GREAT3 challenge is posed to the science, machine learning, and
statistics communities, and involves tests of four specific effects that are
of direct importance to upcoming weak lensing surveys, three of which have
not been tested in a community challenge before. These effects involve
realistically complex galaxy models based on high-resolution imaging from
space; geographically varying, physically-motivated blurring kernel; and combination
of many different exposures. To encourage entry by persons new to the
field, and for use as a diagnostic tool, the simulation software for the
challenge is publicly accessible, although the actual values designed for the
challenge are blinded. Sample scripts to analyze the challenge data using
existing tools will not be supported. See http://great3challenge.info and
http://great3.projects.phys.ucl.ac.uk/leaderboard/ for more info.

Major winning Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), such as AlexNet, VGGNet,
ResNet, GoogleNet, include tens to hundreds of millions of parameters, which
impose considerable computation and memory overhead. This limits their
practical use for training, optimization and memory efficiency. On the
contrary, light-weight architectures, being proposed to address this issue,
mainly Suffer from low accuracy. These inefficiencies mostly stem from
following an ad hoc procedure. We propose a simple architecture, Called
SimpleNet, based on a set of designing principles, with Which we empirically
Show, a well-crafted yet simple And reasonably deep architecture can perform on
par with deeper and more complex architectures. SimpleNet provides a good
tradeoff between the computation/memory efficiency and the accuracy. Our simple
13-layer architecture outperforms most of the deeper and complex architectures
to date such as VGGNet, ResNet, and GoogleNet on Several well-known benchmarks
while having 2 to 25 times fewer number of parameters and operations. This
makes it very handy for embedded systems or systems with Computational and
memory limitations. We achieved state-of-the-art result on CIFAR10
outperforming several heavier architectures, near state of the art on MNIST and
competitive results on CIFAR100 and SVHN. We also outperformed the much larger
and Deeper architectures Such as VGGNet and popular variants of ResNets among
others on the ImageNet dataset. Models are Made available at:
https://github.com/Coderx7/SimpleNet

This  paper   introduces the concept of simultaneous core  partitions and provides several parameterizations and sums related to this  concept. Simultaneous  core partitions  are a  generalization of  the well-known concept of partitions, but with the additional constraint  that each  part must  appear a fixed number of times. The paper  explores various properties and relationships of simultaneous core partitions, including their generating functions, symmetric  polynomials, and combinatorial interpretations. Additionally, the paper presents several novel results, such as a formula  for the sum of the squares of  the parts of a  simultaneous core partition. The   findings  in this paper contribute to our understanding of simultaneous core partitions and their role  in combinatorics and algebraic  structures.

Entanglement does not  describe  all quantum correlations and  several authors
have shown the need to go beyond entanglement when  dealing with mixed states.
Various  different measures have sprung up in the literature, for a variety of
reasons, to describe bipartite and multipartite quantum correlations; some are
known under the collective name  quantum  discord. Yet, in the same sprit as the
criteria for entanglement measures, there is no general mechanism that
determines whether  a  measure of quantum  and classical correlations is a proper
measure  of correlations. This is partially due  to the fact that  the answer is  a
bit muddy. In this article we attempt tackle this muddy topic by  writing down
several criteria for a "good" measure of correlations.  We  breakup  our list into
necessary,  reasonable, and debatable conditions. We then proceed  to prove
several of these conditions for generalized measures  of  quantum correlations.
However, not all conditions are met by all measures; we  show this via  several
examples. The reasonable conditions  are related to  continuity of  correlations,
which  has  not been previously  discussed.  Continuity is an important quality if
one   wants to probe quantum correlations in the laboratory. We show that  most
types of quantum  discord are continuous but  none  are  continuous with respect to
the  measurement basis used for optimization.

Scene labeling is an important task in computer vision that involves assigning semantic labels to each pixel in an image. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for scene labeling using contextual hierarchical models. Our method leverages the hierarchical structure of scenes to capture both local and global context information. We introduce a new hierarchical graphical model that incorporates contextual information from multiple scales and levels of abstraction. We also propose a new inference algorithm that efficiently combines local and global context information to make accurate label predictions. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. Our method is also robust to variations in lighting conditions and viewpoint changes. Overall, our work contributes to the field of scene labeling by providing a new approach that effectively utilizes contextual information for accurate and efficient label predictions.

This paper presents a novel approach for video description using a multi-scale multiple instance network. The proposed network architecture consists of multiple scales of feature extraction layers followed by multiple instance learning layers. The multi-scale feature extraction layers capture both local and global information from the video frames, while the multiple instance learning layers aggregate the features to generate a video description. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed network outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. The proposed approach has potential applications in video summarization, video retrieval, and video understanding.

In this paper, we present a general framework for studying the polynomiality property of the structure coefficients of double-class algebras. We define the concept of a double-class algebra and provide a detailed analysis of its structure coefficients. We then introduce a polynomiality property for these coefficients and prove its existence under certain conditions. Our framework allows us to study the polynomiality property in a systematic and rigorous manner, providing insights into the algebraic properties of double-class algebras. We also provide several examples to illustrate the application of our framework. Overall, our work contributes to the understanding of the polynomiality property in the context of double-class algebras and provides a foundation for further research in this area.

In this paper, we investigate the confinement phase in carbon-nanotubes using the extended massive Schwinger model. We analyze the behavior of the model in the presence of an external magnetic field and study the effects of different parameters on the confinement phase. Our results show that the confinement phase is strongly influenced by the external magnetic field and the parameters of the model. We also discuss the implications of our findings for the understanding of confinement in carbon-nanotubes and propose future directions for research in this area.

Efficient Smoothing of Dilated Convolutions for Image Segmentation

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision, with applications in various fields such as medical imaging and autonomous driving. Dilated convolutions have been widely used in image segmentation models due to their ability to capture multi-scale information. However, dilated convolutions can produce jagged boundaries in the segmented images, which can negatively impact the performance of downstream tasks. In this paper, we propose an efficient smoothing method for dilated convolutions to improve the quality of segmented images. Our method leverages the inherent parallelism of dilated convolutions to efficiently smooth the boundaries of segmented objects. We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms existing smoothing techniques in terms of both segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. Our method can be easily integrated into existing image segmentation models and has the potential to improve the performance of a wide range of computer vision applications.

Researches have, in the recent years, converged on social media, and particularly on Twitter, as a new field for the empirical study of social phenomena. This is because social media allows us to obtain traces of a kind of dialogue and communication that had not previously been possible to study. Hence, we can use these data to study phenomena both specific to social media and broader social phenomena. This article offers a brief review of the literature on the study of political crowd behavior on Twitter. The works cited provide a great insight into certain social phenomena on Twitter, but they often fail to use standardized methods, which allow for a cross-study interpretation. Moreover, they often fail to ground their methods and results in social or political theory, which makes it impossible to interpret the studies from theory. Instead, the articles focus mainly on methodological innovations for the analysis of social media data, but they often fail to sufficiently prove the value of such methods. This review analyzes a small number of selected papers and discusses their theoretical approaches, methodological innovations, and the significance of their results for political scientists and sociologists.

Cloud detection and segmentation in satellite imagery is a crucial task for various applications, including weather forecasting and climate studies. In this paper, we propose an effective cloud detection and segmentation algorithm based on gradient analysis. The algorithm utilizes the gradient information of the satellite imagery to identify cloud regions accurately. We apply this algorithm to improve the performance of the PERSIANN-CCS (Precipitation Estimation from Remotely Sensed Information using Artificial Neural Networks-Cloud Classification System) for cloud detection and segmentation. Experimental results demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The improved PERSIANN-CCS with our algorithm achieves higher accuracy in cloud detection and segmentation, leading to more accurate precipitation estimation. This research contributes to the advancement of cloud detection and segmentation techniques in satellite imagery and enhances the performance of the PERSIANN-CCS system.

Deep Convolutional  Neural Networks (DCNNs)  have recently  shown outstanding
performance in semantic image segmentation. However, state-of-the-art
DCNN-based semantic segmentation methods usually suffer from high  computational
complexity due to the use  of complex network architectures. This greatly limits
their  applications in  the real-world scenarios that require real-time
processing. In this paper, we  propose  a  real-time high-performance DCNN-based
method for robust semantic  segmentation of urban street scenes, which achieves
a good trade-off between accuracy and speed. Specifically, a Lightweight
Baseline Network  with Atrous convolution and  Attention (LBN-AA)  is firstly used
as  our baseline network to  efficiently  obtain dense feature  maps.  Then, the
Distinctive Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (DASPP),  which exploits the
different sizes of pooling operations to encode  the rich and distinctive
semantic information, is   developed to detect objects  at multiple scales.
Meanwhile, a Spatial detail-Preserving Network (SPN)  with  shallow convolutional
layers is designed to generate high-resolution feature maps preserving the
detailed spatial   information. Finally, a  simple but practical  Feature Fusion
Network  (FFN) is used to effectively combine both  shallow and  deep features
from the semantic branch (DASPP) and the spatial branch (SPN), respectively.
Extensive experimental results  show that the proposed method respectively
achieves the   accuracy of 73.6% and 68.0%  mean Intersection over  Union (mIoU)
with the inference speed  of 51.0 fps and  39.3 fps on the  challenging Cityscapes
and CamVid test datasets (by only using a single  NVIDIA TITAN X card). This
demonstrates that the  proposed method offers excellent performance at the
real-time speed for semantic segmentation  of urban street  scenes.

We introduce a variant of the Wadge game for functions, and prove that each lower cone of the Weihrauch degrees can be characterized by such a game. These parametric Wadge games encompass the original Wadge game, the erasing and backtracking games, and Semmes's tree games. In particular, we suggest that the lower cones in the Weihrauch degrees are the answer to Andretta's question, namely, which classes of functions can be characterized by games. We also give an example of how to use parametric Wadge games in applications. Using tools from Weihrauch reducibility theory, we introduce games that characterize every (transfinite) level of the Baire hierarchy by an iteration of the derivative of a recurrence relation on countably branching trees.

This paper presents a  method for interactive segmentation   of medical images using  fully convolutional neural networks  (FCNs). The proposed approach allows users  to  interactively refine the segmentation results by  providing feedback during the segmentation  process.  The  FCN model is trained on a large dataset of annotated medical images and is able to accurately segment various anatomical  structures. The interactive segmentation is  achieved by incorporating user   feedback into the FCN model  through a  novel  feedback mechanism. Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in  achieving accurate and efficient segmentation.  The proposed approach has the potential to improve the accuracy  and  efficiency of medical image segmentation, which is crucial for various  medical applications.

Registration is a fundamental task in medical robotics and is often a crucial
step for many downstream tasks such as motion analysis, intra-operative
tracking and image segmentation. Popular registration methods such as ANTs and
NiftyReg optimize objective functions for each pair of images from scratch,
which are time-consuming for 3D and sequential images with complex
deformations. Recently, deep learning-based registration approaches such as
VoxelMorph have been emerging and achieve competitive performance. In this
work, we construct a test-time training for deep deformable image registration
to improve the generalization ability of conventional learning-based
registration model. We design multi-scale deep networks to consecutively model
the residual deformations, which is effective for high variational
deformations. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of multi-scale
deep registration with test-time training based on Dice coefficient for image
segmentation and mean square error (MSE), normalized local cross-correlation
(NLCC) for tissue dense tracking tasks. Two videos are in
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NvLrCaqCiAE and
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pEA1ZmtTNuQ

We present a method for segmenting neuron membranes in 2D electron microscopy
imagery. This segmentation task has been bottleneck to reconstruction efforts
of brain's synaptic circuits. One common problem is misclassification
of blurry membrane fragments as cell interior, which leads to merging of two
adjacent neuron sections into one via blurry membrane region. Human
annotators can easily avoid such errors by implicitly performing gap
completion, taking into account the continuity of membranes.
  Drawing inspiration from these human strategies, we formulate the
segmentation task as an edge labeling problem on a graph with local topological
constraints. We derive an integer linear program (ILP) that enforces membrane
continuity, i.e. the absence of gaps. The cost function of the ILP is the
pixel-wise deviation of segmentation from priori membrane probabilities
derived from data.
  Based on membrane probability maps obtained using random forest classifiers
and convolutional neural networks, our method improves the neuron boundary
segmentation accuracy compared to variety of standard segmentation
approaches. Our method successfully performs gap completion and leads to fewer
topological errors. The method could potentially also be incorporated into
other image segmentation pipelines with known topological constraints.

We present a method for reconstructing images viewed by observers based only
on their eye movements. By exploring the relationships between gaze patterns
and image stimuli, the "What Are You Looking At?" (WAYLA) system learns to
synthesise photo-realistic images that are similar to the original pictures
being viewed. The WAYLA approach is based on the Conditional Generative
Adversarial Network (Conditional GAN) image-to-image translation technique of
Isola et al. We consider two specific applications - the first, of
reconstructing newspaper images from gaze heat maps, and the second, of
detailed reconstruction of images containing only text. The newspaper image
reconstruction process is divided into two image-to-image translation
operations, the first mapping gaze heat maps into image segmentations, and the
second mapping the generated segmentation into a newspaper image. We validate
the performance of our approach using various evaluation metrics, along with
human visual inspection. All results confirm the ability of our network to
perform image generation tasks using eye tracking data.
