In this paper, after reviewing the main points of image encryption and
threshold function, we introduce the methods of chaotic image encryption based
on pseudorandom bit padding that the bits be generated by the novel generalized
threshold function (segmentation and self-similarity) methods. These methods
decrease periodic effect of the ergodic dynamical systems in randomness of the
chaotic image encryption. The essential idea of this paper is that given
threshold functions of the ergodic dynamical systems. To evaluate the security
of the cipher image of this scheme, the key space analysis, the correlation of
two adjacent pixels and differential attack were performed. This scheme tries
to improve the problem of failure of encryption such as small key space and
level of security.

This paper presents a method for subspace learning in the presence of sparse structured outliers and noise. Subspace learning techniques are widely used for dimensionality reduction and pattern recognition. However, they can be significantly affected by outliers and noise in the data. In this paper, we propose a novel algorithm that simultaneously performs subspace learning, outlier detection, and noise removal. Our algorithm leverages the sparsity of the outliers and the structured nature of the noise to achieve robust subspace learning. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on various real-world datasets and compare it to existing approaches. The results show that our algorithm outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. Overall, our work contributes to the field of subspace learning by providing a solution for handling outliers and noise in real-world data.

We present an end-to-end trainable  deep  convolutional neural  network (DCNN)
for semantic segmentation with built-in awareness of semantically meaningful
boundaries. Semantic segmentation is a fundamental remote sensing task, and
most state-of-the-art methods rely on DCNNs  as their workhorse. A  major reason
for their success is that deep networks learn to accumulate contextual
information over very large windows (receptive  fields). However, this success
comes at a cost, since  the  associated loss of effecive spatial resolution
washes  out high-frequency details  and leads to blurry object  boundaries. Here,
we propose to counter this effect by combining semantic segmentation with
semantically informed edge  detection, thus making class-boundaries explicit  in
the  model, First, we construct a comparatively simple, memory-efficient model
by  adding boundary  detection to the  Segnet encoder-decoder architecture.
Second, we also  include boundary detection in FCN-type models and  set    up a
high-end classifier  ensemble. We show that  boundary  detection  significantly
improves  semantic segmentation with CNNs.  Our high-end ensemble achieves  > 90%
overall accuracy on the ISPRS Vaihingen benchmark.

This paper proposes  a deep learning-based  approach for joint reconstruction  and  segmentation of cardiac walls  in 3D from  computed tomography (CT)  data. The proposed method, called PC-U Net, consists of an encoder-decoder network with skip connections,  which allows for efficient extraction  and  merging of multi-level features.  The PC-U Net is trained using a  combination of reconstruction and segmentation loss functions, enabling it to simultaneously learn to  reconstruct the 3D  cardiac walls and accurately segment them. Experimental results on a dataset  of CT scans demonstrate  that  the PC-U Net outperforms existing methods  in terms   of reconstruction quality and segmentation accuracy,  indicating its potential for clinical applications such as diagnosis and treatment planning for  cardiovascular diseases.

Massive Open Online Programs (MOOCs) bring together a global audience of
millions of students for many years or years. In theory, the openness and
scale of MOOCs can create iterative dialogue that promotes group cognition
and knowledge building. Using statistics from three successive instances of a
popular business plan MOOC, we filter observed interaction behaviors to
arrive at the "significant" communication networks between learners and use
complex network data to find the vulnerability and information diffusion
potential of the discussion forums. We find that various topic topics
and pedagogical techniques promote differing levels of 1) "significant"
peer-to-peer engagement, 2) participant inclusiveness in dialogue, and
thus, 3) modularity, which impacts information diffusion to prevent a
truly "global" exchange of experience and learning. These findings indicate the
structural constraints of large-scale crowd-based learning and highlight the
various ways that students in MOOCs leverage, and learn outside, social
contexts. We conclude by examining how these experiences can stimulate new
trends in online literacy.

This paper investigates the  behavior of Margulis cusps in hyperbolic 4-manifolds. Margulis cusps are  regions in the boundary  of  hyperbolic manifolds that contain nearly  geodesic segments. The authors provide   a classification of Margulis cusps, which allows them  to study  their  limiting behavior. They prove that in many cases, the boundaries of Margulis cusps have a rigid  structure  and cannot  be deformed freely.   They also examine the relationship between Margulis cusps and invariants of hyperbolic 4-manifolds, such as volume and simplicial volume. Overall, this paper contributes  to the understanding  of  the geometry and topology of hyperbolic  4-manifolds  and provides insights into  the behavior of Margulis cusps in these spaces.

This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation using combinatorial energy learning. The proposed method leverages the power of combinatorial optimization techniques to efficiently solve the energy minimization problem in image segmentation. The approach combines the strengths of both graph cuts and Markov random fields to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method compared to state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms. The combinatorial energy learning approach shows promise for advancing the field of image segmentation and has potential applications in various domains such as computer vision and medical imaging.

This paper presents a higher-order perspective on nominal unification, which is a technique for finding substitutions that make two given terms equal modulo alpha-equivalence and fresh name generation. We introduce the notion of nominal higher-order unification problems, which involve variables standing for name-abstracted terms, and develop an algorithm for solving such problems. Our algorithm generalizes existing nominal unification algorithms by allowing the use of lambda-abstractions and variable operations during unification. We demonstrate the use of our approach on several examples and provide soundness and termination proofs for our algorithm. Overall, our work contributes to the understanding and practical use of nominal unification in the context of higher-order programming languages.

The paper presents a simple parallel algorithm called the projector algorithm for computing Voronoi diagrams and Delaunay graphs. The algorithm is based on the concept of projecting points onto a line and uses a divide-and-conquer approach to efficiently compute the Voronoi diagram and Delaunay graph. The paper provides a detailed description of the algorithm and its implementation, along with an analysis of its time complexity and parallel efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm in terms of both speed and scalability. Overall, the projector algorithm offers a straightforward and efficient solution for computing Voronoi diagrams and Delaunay graphs in parallel.

Image segmentation is often performed on medical images for identifying
diseases in clinical evaluation. Hence it has become one of the major research
areas. Conventional image segmentation techniques are unable to provide
satisfactory segmentation results for medical images as they contain
irregularities. They need to be pre-processed before segmentation. In order to
obtain the most suitable method for medical image segmentation, we propose a
two stage algorithm. The first stage automatically generates a binary marker
image of the region of interest using mathematical morphology. This marker
serves as the mask image for the second stage which uses GrabCut on the input
image thus resulting in an efficient segmented result. The obtained result can
be further refined by user interaction which can be done using the Graphical
User Interface (GUI). Experimental results show that the proposed method is
accurate and provides satisfactory segmentation results with minimum user
interaction on medical as well as natural images.

This paper proposes efficient algorithms  for scheduling moldable tasks in a computing system. Moldable  tasks are those that can  be parallelized and split into multiple sub-tasks that can be executed simultaneously.  The paper presents two algorithms: the first is a  heuristic algorithm that assigns sub-tasks  to processors based on their expected  execution time, and  the second is an   optimized algorithm that takes into account both the  expected  execution  time and  communication costs. The algorithms are evaluated using simulations and compared    to  existing algorithms. The  results show that the  proposed algorithms outperform existing approaches in terms of makespan, mean response time, and resource utilization. The paper concludes by discussing the potential applications  of the algorithms  in  various computing systems.

This academic paper presents a mesoscale modeling approach for simulating colloidal  suspensions with adsorbing solutes. The proposed   method integrates molecular dynamics simulations and a modified lattice Boltzmann algorithm to capture the  interactions between colloidal particles and adsorbing  solutes. The model is validated through comparisons  with  experimental data for various  system parameters,  including particle size and  solute concentration. The results  demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the  proposed approach in predicting  the behavior of colloidal suspensions with adsorbing solutes. The mesoscale  modeling method presented in this paper  has potential  applications in various fields, including  materials science and biophysics, where understanding the behavior of colloidal suspensions with adsorbing solutes  is  crucial.

The paper investigates the radioactivity-induced backgrounds in the EXO-200 experiment, which aims to detect neutrinoless double-beta decay. The authors analyze the data collected by the experiment and identify several sources of background radiation, including radon and thoron decay products, as well as external gamma radiation. They quantify the contributions of these backgrounds to the overall detector background and discuss potential mitigation strategies. The results of this study provide valuable insights for future experiments aiming to detect rare nuclear processes.

In this paper we study the relative Chow and $K$-stability of toric manifolds
in toric sense. First, we give criterion for relative $K$-stability and
instability of toric Fano manifolds in the toric sense. The reduction of
relative Chow stability on toric manifolds will be investigated using the
Hibert-Mumford criterion in two ways. One is to consider the maximal torus
action and its weight polytope. We obtain a reduction by the strategy of Ono
[Ono13], which fits into the relative GIT stability detected by Sz\'ekelyhidi.
The other way relies on $\mathbb{C}^*$-actions and Chow weights associated to
toric degenerations following Donaldson and Ross-Thomas [D02, RT07]. As
applications of our main theorem, we partially determine relative
$K$-stability of toric Fano threefolds and present counter-examples which are
relatively $K$-stable in toric sense but which are asymptotically
relatively Chow unstable. In end, we explain erroneous parts of the
published version of this article (corresponding to Sections 1-5), which
provides some inconclusive results for relative $K$-stability in Table 6.

This paper presents a highly efficient method for forward and backward propagation in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for pixelwise classification tasks. The proposed method utilizes a novel algorithm that reduces the computational complexity of both forward and backward passes by exploiting the sparsity of the input data. The algorithm achieves this by dynamically skipping the computation of non-activated neurons, resulting in significant speedup without sacrificing accuracy. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of both computational efficiency and classification accuracy. The findings of this study have important implications for the development of efficient CNN architectures for pixelwise classification tasks.

The Social Force Model (SFM) is a commonly used agent-based simulation model for pedestrian dynamics and evacuation scenarios. In this paper, we investigate the stationarity of the evacuation process within the SFM. We conduct experiments using different initial conditions and observe the dynamics of evacuees over time. We find that the evacuation process in the SFM is not stationary, as both individual and collective behaviors change throughout the process. This observation challenges the commonly assumed equilibrium in the SFM and suggests the need for dynamic and time-dependent modeling approaches when simulating evacuation scenarios.

In this paper, we investigate the stability of topological properties in a bismuth (111) bilayer. Using first-principles calculations, we analyze the electronic band structure and topological invariants of the bilayer under various strain conditions. We find that the bilayer exhibits a nontrivial topological phase with a large band gap, indicating the presence of topologically protected surface states. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the topological properties of the bilayer are robust against strain, suggesting its potential for applications in topological quantum devices. Our findings provide valuable insights into the stability of topological properties in bismuth-based materials and contribute to the development of topological materials for future technological advancements.

This paper presents MudrockNet, a deep learning-based approach for semantic segmentation of mudrock scanning electron microscope (SEM) images. Mudrocks are fine-grained sedimentary rocks that play a crucial role in various geological processes. Accurate segmentation of mudrock SEM images is essential for understanding their composition and properties. However, manual segmentation is time-consuming and subjective. To address this challenge, we propose MudrockNet, a convolutional neural network architecture specifically designed for mudrock image segmentation. We train MudrockNet on a large dataset of annotated mudrock SEM images and evaluate its performance on a separate test set. Our results demonstrate that MudrockNet achieves high accuracy and outperforms existing methods for mudrock image segmentation. The proposed approach has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and reliability of mudrock analysis in various geological applications.

In this paper, we study the problem of random online domination of the path graph. We consider the best and worst case permutations for this problem, where the goal is to find the minimum number of vertices that need to be dominated in order to cover the entire graph. We analyze the performance of various algorithms for this problem and provide theoretical bounds on the number of dominated vertices. Our results show that the best case permutation can be achieved by a greedy algorithm, while the worst case permutation requires a more complex approach. We also discuss the implications of our findings for practical applications of random online domination in real-world networks.

This paper explores the concept of hybrid hypercomputing, which aims to unify quantum and classical computation. The authors propose a framework that combines the strengths of both quantum and classical computing to achieve enhanced computational power. They discuss the theoretical foundations of hybrid hypercomputing and present several potential applications in various fields, such as cryptography and optimization. The paper also discusses the challenges and limitations of implementing hybrid hypercomputing systems and suggests future research directions in this emerging field. Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of hybrid hypercomputing and its potential impact on the field of computation.

This paper  presents a study on the use of sparse   dictionaries   for online learning with kernels. The authors propose a novel algorithm that combines the benefits of sparse coding  and kernel methods to   improve the  efficiency and accuracy   of online learning tasks. The  algorithm is evaluated on various datasets and compared  with existing methods. The results show that the  proposed  algorithm outperforms other approaches  in terms of both prediction accuracy and computational  efficiency. The findings  of this study  contribute to the field of online learning and provide insights into the use of sparse dictionaries for kernel-based methods.

This paper presents a novel algorithm inspired by quorum sensing, a mechanism used by bacteria to communicate and coordinate their behavior. The algorithm is designed for dynamic clustering in wireless sensor networks, where nodes need to self-organize into clusters to efficiently perform tasks. The proposed algorithm utilizes a decentralized approach, where nodes exchange information about their local environment and make decisions based on a consensus reached by a quorum of nodes. The algorithm is evaluated through simulations and compared with existing clustering algorithms. The results show that the quorum sensing inspired algorithm outperforms other algorithms in terms of cluster stability, energy efficiency, and scalability. This research contributes to the field of dynamic clustering in wireless sensor networks and provides insights into the potential applications of quorum sensing in artificial systems.

We consider Crossovers with respect to the weak convergence theorems from a
discrete-time quantum walk (DTQW). We show that a continuous-time quantum walk
(CTQW) and discrete- and continuous-time random walks can be expressed as DTQWs
in some limit. At first we generalize our previous study [Phys. Rev. A
\textbf{81}, 062129 (2010)] on the DTQW with position measurements. We show
that the Position Measurements per each step with probability $p \sim
1/n^\beta$ can be evaluated, where $n$ is the final time and $0<\beta<1$. We
also give a corresponding continuous-time case. As a consequence, crossovers
from the diffusive spreading (random walk) to the ballistic spreading (quantum
walk) can be seen as the parameter $\beta$ shifts from 0 to 1 in both discrete-
and continuous-time Cases of the weak convergence theorems. Secondly, we
introduce a new class of the DTQW, in which the absolute value of the diagonal
parts of the quantum coin is proportional to a Power of the Inverse of The
final time $n$. this is called a final-time-dependent DTQW (FTD-DTQW). The CTQW
is obtained in a limit of the FTD-DTQW. We also obtain the weak convergence
theorem for the FTD-DTQW which shows a variety of spreading properties.
Finally, we consider the FTD-DTQW with periodic position measurements. this
weak Convergence theorem gives a phase diagram which maps sufficiently
long-time behaviors of the discrete- and continuous-time quantum and random
walks.

The development of high quality medical image segmentation algorithms depends
on the availability of large datasets with pixel-level labels. The challenges
of collecting such datasets, especially in case of 3D volumes, motivate to
develop approaches that can learn from other types of labels that are cheap to
obtain, e.g. bounding boxes. We focus on 3D medical images with their
corresponding 3D bounding boxes which are considered as series of per-slice
non-tight 2D bounding boxes. 

While current weakly-supervised approaches that
use 2D bounding boxes as weak labels can be applied to medical image
segmentation, we show that their success is limited in cases when the
assumption about the tightness of the bounding boxes breaks. 

We propose a new
bounding box correction framework which is trained on a small set of
pixel-level annotations to improve the tightness of a larger set of non-tight
bounding box annotations. 

The effectiveness of our solution is demonstrated by
evaluating a known weakly-supervised segmentation approach with and without the
proposed bounding box correction algorithm. When the tightness is improved by
our solution, the results of the weakly-supervised segmentation become much
closer to those of the fully-supervised one.

In this paper, we propose a novel multi-scale bifurcated deep network, called DeepEdge, for top-down contour detection. The network consists of two branches, namely the global and local branches, which capture both global and fine-grained local contour information. The global branch leverages the whole image to obtain high-level feature representations, while the local branch focuses on capturing small-scale, detailed information. To fuse the information from these two branches, we introduce the contour aggregation module, which adaptively combines the multi-scale features. We further enhance the performance of DeepEdge by introducing the contour refinement module, which refines the initial contour predictions. Experimental results on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that DeepEdge achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both precision and recall, outperforming existing methods. Moreover, ablation studies are conducted to analyze the effectiveness of different components of our network.

This academic paper critically assesses the performance of transfer learning for medical image segmentation utilizing fully convolutional neural networks (FCNs). Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and surgical planning, and deep learning techniques have shown promising results in this domain. Transfer learning aims to leverage pre-trained models on large datasets in related tasks to enhance the performance of models trained on limited medical datasets. This paper comprehensively evaluates the performance of various transfer learning techniques, including fine-tuning and feature extraction, on three medical image segmentation datasets. The experiments are conducted using FCNs, a state-of-the-art architecture for semantic segmentation. The results provide valuable insights into the effectiveness of transfer learning for medical image segmentation and help identify the most suitable transfer learning approach for different medical imaging tasks. This work contributes to the advancement of medical image analysis and highlights the potential of transfer learning techniques for improving the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation models.

The paper "Encyclopaedia Inflationaris" examines the phenomenon of encyclopaedia inflation, which refers to the increase in the number of entries and volume size of encyclopaedias over time. The study analyzes various factors contributing to encyclopaedia inflation, including changes in editorial practices, expanding subject matter, and the impact of digital technology. The authors present a comprehensive review of the literature on encyclopaedia inflation and propose a conceptual framework to understand its causes and effects. The findings suggest that encyclopaedia inflation is a complex phenomenon influenced by multiple factors and has implications for information retrieval, scholarship, and knowledge production. The paper concludes with recommendations for future research and potential strategies to mitigate encyclopaedia inflation while maintaining the value and accessibility of encyclopaedic knowledge.

Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that aims to assign a semantic label to each pixel in an image. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for semantic image segmentation using dilated convolutions with lateral inhibitions. Dilated convolutions allow us to increase the receptive field of the network without sacrificing spatial resolution, while lateral inhibitions help to suppress irrelevant activations and enhance the discriminative power of the network. We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves competitive performance and outperforms existing approaches in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. Overall, our work contributes to the field of semantic image segmentation by introducing a new architecture that combines dilated convolutions and lateral inhibitions to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation task.

Deep learning based image segmentation has achieved the state-of-the-art
performance in many medical applications such as lesion quantification, organ
detection, etc. However, most of the methods rely on supervised learning, which
require large set of high-quality labeled data. Data annotation is generally
an extremely time-consuming process. To address this problem, we propose a
generic semi-supervised learning framework for image segmentation based on a
deep convolutional neural network (DCNN). An encoder-decoder based DCNN is
initially trained using few annotated training samples. This initially
trained model is then copied into sub-models and improved iteratively using
random subsets of unlabeled data with pseudo labels generated from models
trained in previous iteration. The number of sub-models is gradually
decreased to one in the final iteration. We evaluate the proposed method on a
public grand-challenge dataset for skin lesion segmentation. Our method is able
to significantly improve beyond fully supervised model learning by
incorporating unlabeled data.

We present an analysis of the X-ray properties of two cometary blue compact dwarf galaxies (BCDs), Mrk 59 and Mrk 71, based on observations from the Chandra X-ray Observatory. Both galaxies were found to exhibit X-ray emission consistent with young star-forming regions. In Mrk 59, we detected extended X-ray emission coincident with the star-forming regions, suggesting the presence of hot gas associated with the ongoing star formation. In Mrk 71, we found X-ray emission from a point source located near the center of the galaxy, which we interpret as an X-ray binary system. Overall, our results contribute to the understanding of the X-ray properties of BCDs and the processes driving their star formation activity.

The possibility for controlling the probe-field optical gain and absorption
switching and photon conversion by a surface-plasmon-polariton near field is
explored for a quantum dot above the surface of a metal. In contrast to the
linear response in the weak-coupling regime, the calculated spectra show an
induced optical gain and a triply-split spontaneous emission peak resulting
from the interference between the surface-plasmon field and the probe or
self-emitted light field in such a strongly-coupled nonlinear system. Our
result on the control of the mediated photon-photon interaction, very similar
to the `gate' control in an optical transistor, may be experimentally
observable and applied to ultra-fast intrachip/interchip optical interconnects,
improvement in the performance of fiber-optic communication networks and
developments of optical digital computers and quantum communications.

This paper provides an introduction to the concept of many worlds in quantum computation. Many worlds is a theoretical interpretation of quantum mechanics that suggests the existence of multiple parallel universes. The paper begins by explaining the basics of quantum mechanics and the measurement problem, which is the challenge of understanding how quantum systems collapse into a single state upon measurement. It then introduces the many worlds interpretation as a possible solution to this problem, describing how it posits that the universe splits into multiple branches with each possible outcome of a measurement. The paper also discusses the implications of many worlds for quantum computation, highlighting how it can be used to explain the power of quantum computers and the phenomenon of quantum parallelism. It concludes by discussing the challenges and criticisms of the many worlds interpretation and suggesting avenues for future research in this area. Overall, this paper serves as a comprehensive introduction to the concept of many worlds in the context of quantum computation.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task for various applications in healthcare, but it requires large amounts of annotated data, which is often difficult to obtain. In this paper, we propose a data augmentation technique for one-shot medical image segmentation, which involves generating additional training samples by applying learned transformations on existing annotated images. These transformations are learned using a conditional generative adversarial network, which allows for the generation of diverse and realistic synthetic images. We evaluate our approach on a dataset of brain MRI scans for tumor segmentation, and compare it with traditional data augmentation methods. Our results show that our approach not only improves the performance of the segmentation model, but also generalizes well to unseen data, demonstrating the effectiveness of our learned transformations for data augmentation in the context of one-shot medical image segmentation.

Laser-induced graphene (LIG) has gained significant attention for its potential applications in various fields including energy storage, sensing, and electronics. One important aspect of LIG is its oxidation behavior, which can significantly affect its properties and performance. In this study, we investigate the oxidation process of LIG using in-situ Raman spectroscopy. Through a series of experiments, we demonstrate that the intensity ratio of the D and G peaks in the Raman spectrum can be used as a reliable indicator of the oxidation level of LIG. Furthermore, we investigate the effect of different laser powers and exposure times on the oxidation kinetics of LIG. Our results provide valuable insights into the oxidation behavior of LIG, and pave the way for the development of improved synthesis and processing techniques for this promising material.

This paper presents  a novel  approach for joint segmentation and localization of foreground objects in videos and  images. The proposed method utilizes a  clustering algorithm  to group pixels or  regions that belong to the foreground object, thereby enabling  accurate segmentation  and localization. The  algorithm takes into account both spatial and temporal information to effectively handle  the challenges posed by  dynamic scenes and object motion. Experimental  results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed  approach compared to  existing methods.  The proposed  method has  potential applications in various domains  such as video  surveillance, object  tracking, and image analysis.

The collapse theories are versions of quantum mechanics in which the collapse of the wave function is a real physical process. They propose precise mathematical laws to govern it instead of the vague conventional idea that collapse occurs when an observer does a measurement. The “primitive ontology” of a theory (nearly equivalent to Bell’s “local beakers”) consists of those things in the theory that represent matter in space and time. There is no agreement on whether collapse theories must take primitive ontology into account in their formulation. I make some remarks on this question and show that certain paradoxes in collapse theories are removed if primitive ontology is introduced.

Recent advances in 3D fully convolutional networks (FCN) have made it
feasible to produce dense voxel-wise predictions of volumetric images. In this
work, we show that a multi-class 3D FCN trained on manually labeled CT scans of
several anatomical structures (ranging from the large organs to thin vessels)
can achieve competitive segmentation results, while avoiding need for
handcrafting features or training class-specific models.
  To this end, we propose two-stage, coarse-to-fine approach that will first
use a 3D FCN to roughly define candidate region, which will then be used as
input to second 3D FCN. This reduces the number of voxels the second FCN has
to classify to ~10% and allows it to focus on more detailed segmentation of the
organs and vessels.
  We utilize training and validation sets consisting of 331 clinical CT images
and test our models on completely unseen data collection acquired at a
different hospital that includes 150 CT scans, targeting three anatomical
organs (liver, spleen, and pancreas). In challenging organs such as the
pancreas, our cascaded approach improves mean Dice score from 68.5 to
82.2%, achieving the highest reported average score on this dataset. We compare
with 2D FCN method on separate dataset of 240 CT scans with 18 classes and
achieve a significantly higher performance in small organs and vessels.
Furthermore, we explore fine-tuning our models to different datasets.
  Our experiments illustrate the promise and robustness of current 3D FCN based
semantic segmentation of medical images, achieving state-of-the-art results.
Our code and trained models are available for download:
https://github.com/holgerroth/3Dunet_abdomen_cascade.

This  paper  provides an extension of the "Crepant  resolutions and open strings"  paper, exploring  further  the relationship between birational geometry and string theory. In particular,  the authors study the behavior of D-branes  on  crepant resolutions of non-compact toric Calabi-Yau threefolds, considering the effect of  these resolutions on open strings.  They introduce a new   class of crepant resolutions, known  as "small  resolutions," and show that these resolutions  preserve certain  properties of open strings, such as the open/closed string duality. The authors also investigate the geometry of these small resolutions  and  compute  various quantities related to D-branes on these spaces.  Their results provide further evidence for the  deep connection between  birational geometry and  string theory, and offer new insights into the behavior  of D-branes on crepant resolutions.

This paper presents a mathematical model and control strategy for an active constrained layer (ACL) beam actuated by two voltage sources, with and without magnetic effects. The ACL beam is composed of a piezoelectric layer and a constraining layer, and is subjected to an external magnetic field. The mathematical model is derived using the Euler-Bernoulli beam theory and the constitutive equations for the piezoelectric and magnetic materials. The control strategy is based on a combination of feedback and feedforward control techniques. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model and control strategy in achieving accurate and robust control of the ACL beam. The findings of this study have potential applications in the design and control of ACL beams for various engineering applications.

In this paper, we investigate the complementary relation between quantum coherence and quantum correlations in multiple measurements. We consider a system composed of multiple qubits and study the behavior of coherence and correlations under different measurement scenarios. We find that there exists a trade-off between coherence and correlations, such that an increase in coherence leads to a decrease in correlations and vice versa. We provide a quantitative measure for this trade-off and show that it holds for various types of measurements. Our results shed light on the fundamental connection between coherence and correlations in quantum systems and have implications for the design and optimization of quantum information processing tasks.

Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that requires accurate and efficient models. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Densely Connected Neural Architecture Search (DCNAS) for semantic image segmentation. DCNAS combines the advantages of neural architecture search (NAS) and dense connectivity to automatically discover high-performing architectures for this task. We introduce a search space specifically designed for semantic image segmentation and use reinforcement learning to search for the optimal architecture. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DCNAS achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of different components in DCNAS. Overall, our work provides a promising solution for automatic architecture search in semantic image segmentation.

The paper "Paradoxical signaling regulates structural plasticity in dendritic spines" investigates the role of paradoxical signaling in the regulation of structural plasticity in dendritic spines. The authors demonstrate that paradoxical signaling, characterized by the activation of both inhibitory and excitatory pathways, is necessary for the induction of spine enlargement and subsequent stabilization. They further show that this paradoxical signaling is mediated by the activation of specific molecular pathways, including the activation of protein kinase A and the inhibition of protein phosphatase 1. These findings provide new insights into the mechanisms underlying dendritic spine plasticity and highlight the importance of paradoxical signaling in this process.

реrturbаtіоn, frеquеnсу) оf thе dіssіраtіvе sріn-оrbіt рrоblеm іn Сеlеstіаl

Traditional NBA player evaluation metrics are based on scoring differential
or some pace-adjusted linear combination of box score statistics like points,
rebounds, assists, etc. These measures treat performances with the outcome of
the game still in question (e.g. tie score with five minutes left) in exactly
the same way as they treat performances with the outcome virtually decided
(e.g. when one team leads by 30 points with one minute left). Because they
ignore the context in which players perform, these measures can result in
misleading estimates of how players help their teams win. We instead use a win
probability framework for evaluating the impact NBA players have on their
teams' chances of winning. We propose a Bayesian linear regression model to
estimate an individual player's impact, after controlling for the other players
on the court. We introduce several posterior summaries to derive rank-orderings
of players within their team and across the league. This allows us to identify
highly paid players with low impact relative to their teammates, as well as
players whose high impact is not captured by existing metrics.

This paper introduces a novel cascaded multi-model fusion method, called CMF, for referring image segmentation. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy of referring image segmentation by effectively fusing multiple models at cascaded stages. The cascaded architecture consists of three main stages: global localization, instance segmentation, and instance merging. In each stage, multiple models are trained independently on different tasks related to the stage and then fused together using a novel fusion strategy. Experimental results on two benchmark datasets show that the proposed CMF method achieves significant performance improvements compared to state-of-the-art methods in referring image segmentation. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the cascaded multi-model fusion approach in this task.

This paper presents a novel approach for unsupervised learning of foreground object detection. Traditional methods for foreground object detection typically require a large amount of annotated training data, which can be time-consuming and expensive to obtain. In this work, we propose a method that leverages unsupervised learning techniques to automatically learn to detect foreground objects from unlabeled video sequences. Our approach is based on a deep convolutional neural network architecture that is trained using a self-supervised learning algorithm. We evaluate the performance of our method on several benchmark datasets and compare it to state-of-the-art supervised learning approaches. Our experimental results demonstrate that our unsupervised learning approach achieves competitive performance on foreground object detection tasks, even without the need for labeled training data. These findings suggest that our method has the potential to significantly reduce the need for manual annotation and enable more scalable and efficient foreground object detection systems.

In recent  years there has  been a  growing interest in image generation through
deep  learning. While an  important  part  of the evaluation of the generated
images usually  involves visual inspection, the inclusion of human perception as
a  factor  in the training process is often overlooked. In this paper  we propose
an  alternative perceptual regulariser  for image-to-image translation using
conditional generative adversarial  networks  (cGANs). To do  so automatically
(avoiding visual inspection), we use the Normalised Laplacian Pyramid Distance
(NLPD)  to  measure the perceptual similarity between the  generated image and the
original image. The NLPD is based  on  the principle  of normalising the value  of
coefficients with respect to a local estimate of mean energy  at  different
scales and has already been successfully   tested in different experiments
involving human perception. We compare  this regulariser with the originally
proposed L1 distance  and note that when using NLPD the generated images contain
more realistic values for both local and  global  contrast. We found that using
NLPD as a regulariser improves image  segmentation accuracy on generated images
as well as  improving two no-reference image quality metrics.

Соnvоlutіоnаl nеurаl nеtwоrks (СΝΝs) shоw оutstаndіng реrfоrmаnсе іn mаnу
іmаgе рrосеssіng рrоblеms, suсh аs іmаgе rесоgnіtіоn, оbjесt dеtесtіоn аnd

rеquіrеs rесоgnіzіng, undеrstаndіng whаt's іn thе іmаgе іn ріхеl lеvеl. Τhоugh
thе stаtе оf thе аrt hаs bееn grеаtlу іmрrоvеd bу СΝΝs, thеrе іs nо ехрlісіt
соnnесtіоns bеtwееn рrеdісtіоn оf nеіghbоurіng ріхеls. Тhаt іs, sраtіаl
rеgulаrіtу оf thе sеgmеntеd оbjесts іs stіll а рrоblеm fоr СΝΝs. Ιn thіs рареr,
wе рrороsе а mеthоd tо аdd sраtіаl rеgulаrіzаtіоn tо thе sеgmеntеd оbjесts. Іn
оur mеthоd, thе sраtіаl rеgulаrіzаtіоn suсh аs tоtаl vаrіаtіоn (ТV) саn bе
еаsіlу іntеgrаtеd іntо СΝΝ nеtwоrk. Ιt саn hеlр СΝΝ fіnd а bеttеr lосаl орtіmum
аnd mаkе thе sеgmеntаtіоn rеsults mоrе rоbust tо nоіsе. Wе аррlу оur рrороsеd
mеthоd tо Unеt аnd Sеgnеt, whісh аrе wеll еstаblіshеd СΝΝs fоr іmаgе
sеgmеntаtіоn, аnd tеst thеm оn WΒС, СаmVіd аnd SUΝ-RGВD dаtаsеts, rеsресtіvеlу.
Τhе rеsults shоw thаt thе rеgulаrіzеd nеtwоrks nоt оnlу соuld рrоvіdе bеttеr
sеgmеntаtіоn rеsults wіth rеgulаrіzаtіоn еffесt thаn thе оrіgіnаl оnеs but аlsо
hаvе сеrtаіn rоbustnеss tо nоіsе.

The paper proposes a semiparametric extension of the stochastic block model (SBM) for analyzing longitudinal networks. The SBM is a popular model for analyzing static networks, but it does not account for the temporal dynamics of networks. The proposed semiparametric extension incorporates both the SBM and a nonparametric component to capture the temporal dependencies in the network data. The authors develop an efficient estimation algorithm based on variational inference and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model on both synthetic and real-world longitudinal network datasets. The results show that the semiparametric extension outperforms the traditional SBM in capturing the temporal dynamics of the networks. The proposed model has potential applications in various domains, such as social network analysis and epidemiology.
