This paper explores the use of lexicographic approximations for solving integer programs. The authors propose a new algorithm that combines lexicographic optimization with branch-and-bound techniques to find approximate solutions to integer programs. The algorithm is tested on a set of benchmark problems and compared to other existing methods. The results show that the proposed algorithm is able to find high-quality solutions with reasonable computational effort. The paper concludes with a discussion on the potential applications and future research directions for lexicographic approximations of integer programs.

The task of automatically segmenting radiological images requires a large amount of labeled data. The annotation of such data is very time-consuming, and the learning-based methods do not find accurate boundaries of the objects without the geometrical constraint. Contrastive learning is a part of self-supervised learning that has been recently recognized as a promising way in many application fields. In this work, we propose a new method for obtaining local and global visual features for the automatic segmentation of radiological images with limited training. Specifically, we introduce a voxel-to-volume contrastive learning for learning the global features from 3D images and we propose a local voxel-to-voxel contrastive learning for using local features of images. Moreover, we integrate a regularization term based on the elastic interaction of active contours for the boundary learning in order to obtain a reliable and robust boundary in an end-to-end learning way. The experiments on the dataset from the Atrial Segmentation Challenge clearly show the effectiveness of our method even with very limited training.

This paper introduces the concept of principal sub-manifolds, which are sub-manifolds of a given manifold that possess certain geometric properties. The authors provide a detailed definition of principal sub-manifolds and discuss their significance in various areas of mathematics, including differential geometry and topology. The paper also presents several examples of principal sub-manifolds and explores their relationship with other types of sub-manifolds. Additionally, the authors discuss the applications of principal sub-manifolds in various fields, such as physics and computer science. Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding and study of principal sub-manifolds and their role in mathematical research.

A series of active contour models have been widely used in image segmentation, and the level-set method is the most widely used solution method, which implicitly represents the active contour by a level-set function. However, the level-set method is plagued by excessive arithmetic, and it is numerically unstable, so that it must be further refined with regularization terms or initialization methods. In this paper, we use characteristic functions to represent the contours, and present a new representation of the geodesic active contour and a new and efficient implementation method, called the iterative convolution-thresholding method. This method has the advantages of being simple, efficient, and having most of the characteristics of level-set methods. Extensive experiments on two-dimensional synthetic images, two-dimensional ultrasonic images, three-dimensional CT images and three-dimensional MR images show that the proposed method not only achieves comparable or better results than the level-set method., but also achieves significant speed up.

This article gives an outline of multi-fidelity model trends. Fidelity
in modeling relates to the level of detail and precision required by a predictive
simulation or model. Typically, models with lower fidelity deliver more
precise results but demand more computational resources. Multi-fidelity
models integrate high-fidelity and low-fidelity models to provide fast yet
reliable predictions. Their increasing prominence is due to their capability to
approximate high-fidelity models with low precision and high computational expense.
This work classifies publications in multi-fidelity simulation based on many
variables, including application, surrogate selection, fidelity difference,
fidelity combination approach, field of application, and time of publication. The
research generally examines the methods employed to combine fidelities, relying on
multi-fidelity surrogate models. To properly identify the benefits of
combining multi-fidelity models, it is important to report the achieved time
savings. This paper provides recommendations for researchers to present their
multi-fidelity-related savings in a standard, straightforward, yet comprehensive manner to
guide future users. According to a select group of publications that contained
sufficient information, multi-fidelity models demonstrated savings of up to 90%
while achieving the desired level of reliability. Moreover, the savings reached
through multi-fidelity models depend strongly on the problem.
  Keywords: Multi-fidelity, Variable-complexity, Variable-fidelity, Surrogate
models, Analysis, Uncertainty analysis, Review, Survey

This paper presents a novel chaotic image encryption algorithm using a generalized threshold function. The proposed algorithm utilizes a chaotic map to generate a sequence of random numbers, which are then used to encrypt the image. The generalized threshold function is employed to enhance the security of the encryption process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves high security and robustness against various attacks, while maintaining a reasonable encryption speed. The algorithm also exhibits good resistance against statistical analysis and key space analysis. Overall, the proposed algorithm provides an effective and efficient solution for image encryption.

The task of semantic image segmentation aims to determine object labels with sharp boundaries, but suffers from the usual problems of overfitting. Recent data augmentation strategies such as local dropout and local mix have been proposed to alleviate this problem. These strategies have proved to be effective in guiding the model to less discriminative features. But because these strategies operate at the image level, affecting both the objects and the background, these strategies are ineffective in enhancing object boundaries in the fixed semantic context. We propose ObjectAug, a novel strategy to augment the object-level features for semantic image segmentation. The method first decomposes the image into its constituent objects and background, using the image’s own semantic labels. Each object is then independently augmented with standard augmentation methods such as scaling, translation and rotation, and then the area in black, where the augmentation has taken place, is filled in with an inpainting method. Objects and backgrounds are then merged to create an augmented image, in which the objects’ boundaries are enhanced in all semantic contexts. In addition, ObjectAug supports augmentation with object category information, which provides each object with a range of possibilities. It is easy to combine with other existing augmentation methods to further improve performance. A comprehensive evaluation on natural image and medical image data shows that ObjectAug clearly improves the performance of semantic segmentation.

Deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are state-of-the-art for semantic
image segmentation, but typically require many labeled training samples.
Obtaining 3D segmentations of medical images for supervised training is
difficult and labor intensive. Motivated by classical approaches for joint
segmentation and registration we therefore propose a deep learning framework
that jointly learns networks for image registration and image segmentation. In
contrast to previous work on deep unsupervised image registration, which showed
the benefit of weak supervision via image segmentations, our approach can use
existing segmentations when available and computes them via the segmentation
network otherwise, thereby providing the same registration benefit. Conversely,
segmentation network training benefits from the registration, which essentially
provides a realistic form of data augmentation. Experiments on knee and brain
3D magnetic resonance (MR) images show that our approach achieves large
simultaneous improvements of segmentation and registration accuracy (over
independently trained networks) and allows training high-quality models with
very limited training data. Specifically, in a one-shot-scenario (with only one
manually labeled image) our approach increases Dice scores (%) over an
unsupervised registration network by 2.7 and 1.8 on the knee and brain images
respectively.

In this paper we develop a family of preconditioners for the linear algebraic
systems arising from the arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian discretization of some
fluid-structure interaction models. After the time discretization, we formulate
the fluid-structure interaction equations as saddle point problems and prove
the uniform well-posedness. Then we discretize the space dimension by finite
element methods and prove their uniform well-posedness by two different
approaches under appropriate assumptions. The uniform well-posedness makes it
possible to design robust preconditioners for the discretized fluid-structure
interaction systems. Numerical examples are presented to show the robustness
and efficiency of these preconditioners.

Brain tumor segmentation plays a crucial role in the diagnosis and treatment planning for patients. However, accurate and robust segmentation remains a challenging task due to the complexity and heterogeneity of brain tumors. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Robust Multimodal Brain Tumor Segmentation via Feature Disentanglement and Gated Fusion. Our method leverages both the spatial and multimodal information of the brain images to improve segmentation accuracy. Specifically, we extract rich features from different imaging modalities using a deep convolutional neural network. Then, we disentangle the learned features into domain-specific and shared components to capture the specific characteristics of each modality and the common information across modalities. Finally, a gated fusion module is employed to leverage the disentangled features and generate the final segmentation map. Experimental results on a large publicly available dataset demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our proposed approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to noise and artifacts. Our method has the potential to contribute to more accurate and reliable brain tumor segmentation in clinical practice.

Topological alignments and snakes are used in image processing, particularly
in locating object boundaries. Both of them have their own advantages and
limitations. To improve the overall image Boundary detection system, we focused
on developing a novel algorithm for image Processing. The algorithm we propose
to develop will based on the active contour method in conjunction with
topological alignments method to enhance the image detection approach. The
algorithm presents novel technique to incorporate the advantages of both
Topological Alignments and snakes. Where the initial segmentation by
Topological Alignments Is firstly transformed Into the input of the snake model
And begins its evolvement to the interested object boundary. The results show
that the algorithm can deal with low contrast images and shape cells,
demonstrate the segmentation accuracy under weak image boundaries, Which
responsible for Lacking accuracy in image detecting techniques. We have
Achieved better segmentation and boundary detecting for the image, also the
ability of the system to improve the low contrast and deal with over and under
segmentation.

This paper addresses the domain shift Problem for segmentation. As a
solution, we propose OLVA, a Novel and lightweight unsupervised domain
adaptation method Based on a Variational Auto-Encoder (VAE) and Optimal
Transport (OT) Theory. Thanks to the VAE, our model learns a shared
cross-domain latent space that follows a normal distribution, which reduces the
domain shift. To guarantee valid segmentations, our shared latent space is
designed to model the shape rather than the intensity variations. We Further
rely on an OT loss to match and align the remaining discrepancy between the two
domains in the latent space. We demonstrate OLVA's Effectiveness for the
segmentation of multiple cardiac structures on the public Multi-Modality Whole
Heart Segmentation (MM-WHS) dataset, where the source domain consists of
annotated 3D MR images and the unlabelled target domain of 3D CTs. Our results
show remarkable improvements With an additional margin of 12.5\% dice score
over concurrent generative training approaches.

Domain Adaptation (DA) techniques are often employed in medical image segmentation
tasks to tackle the issue of differently distributed train (source) and test
(target) information. We consider the supervised DA task with a limited number of
annotated samples from the target domain. It corresponds to one of the most
important scientific setups: building a very realistic model on the maximum
necessary quantity of annotated data. Existing techniques mostly fine-tune certain
layers of the pretrained Convolutional Neural Networks (ABC). Unfortunately, there is
no consensus on which layers are harder to fine-tune, e.g. the first layers for
pictures with low-level domain change or the deeper layers for pictures with
high-level domain change. To this end, we propose SpotTUnet - a CNN architecture
that automatically chooses the layers which should be appropriately fine-tuned.
More explicitly, on the target domain, our method also learns the
policy that determines that a particular layer should be fine-tuned or reused
from the pretrained network. We show that our approach performs at the same level
as the best of the nonflexible fine-tuning tools even under the severe
scarcity of annotated databases. Moreover, we show that SpotTUnet policy allows a
layer-wise visualization of the domain shift effect on the network, which can
be further used to improve efficient domain generalization tools. In order to
extensively improve SpotTUnet performance, we use a publicly accessible database
of brain MR images (CC359), characterized by explicit domain shift. We release
a reproducible experimental pipeline.

Automatic segmentation of clinical images is an essential task for various
medical systems. In practice, a broad variety of anatomical systems are
visualised using various imaging techniques. In this paper, we investigate
if a single convolutional neural network (CNN) can be trained to perform
multiple segmentation functions.
  A single CNN is trained to segment two cells in MR brain images, the
pectoral tissue in MR breast images, and the cardiac vessels in cardiac CTA.
The CNN therefore learns to recognize the imaging modality, the visualised
anatomical structures, and the muscle classes.
  For each of the four tasks (brain MRI, breast MRI and cardiac CTA), this
combined training process resulted in a segmentation performance equivalent
to that of a CNN trained specifically for that task, demonstrating the high
capacity of CNN systems. Thus, a single system can be designed in scientific
practice to automatically perform diverse segmentation functions without
task-specific training.

The problem of segmenting given image into coherent regions is important in
Computer Vision and many industrial applications require segmenting a known
object into its components. Examples include identifying individual parts of a
component for process control work in manufacturing plant and identifying
parts of a car from a photo for automatic damage detection. Unfortunately most
of object's parts of interest in such applications share the same pixel
characteristics, having similar colour and texture. This makes segmenting the
object into its components non-trivial task for conventional image
segmentation algorithms. In this paper, we propose a "Model Assisted
Segmentation" method to tackle this problem. A 3D model of object is
registered over given image by optimising a novel gradient based loss
function. This registration obtains the full 3D pose from image of the
object. The image can have arbitrary view of the object and is not limited
to a particular set of views. The segmentation is subsequently performed using
a level-set based method, using the projected contours of the registered 3D
model as initialisation curves. The method is fully automatic and requires no
user interaction. Also, system does not require any prior training. We
present our results on photographs of real car.

Image segmentation plays a crucial role in many  computer vision and image  processing applications. This   paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using a combination of fuzzy $C$-means clustering, morphological  reconstruction,  and wavelet frames. The proposed  method uses Kullback-Leibler  divergence  as a similarity  measure for   clustering, which allows for  more accurate segmentation results. Additionally, morphological reconstruction is used to enhance the quality of the segmentation  by  removing noise and fine structures. The use  of  wavelet frames further improves the segmentation by capturing both high-frequency and low-frequency information in the image. Experimental results  on  various  benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method compared to  other state-of-the-art  approaches.

Cardiac MR image segmentation is a fundamental step in the analysis and diagnosis of heart diseases using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). This paper provides an overview of various segmentation techniques used for this purpose. The paper discusses both manual and automatic segmentation methods, including thresholding, region-based approaches, active contour models, and deep learning algorithms. The strengths and weaknesses of each technique are highlighted, along with their applications in different cardiac imaging scenarios. Moreover, the paper addresses the challenges and future directions in cardiac MR image segmentation, emphasizing the need for robust and efficient algorithms for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. Overall, this paper serves as a comprehensive resource for researchers and clinicians working in the field of cardiac MR image analysis.

3D image segmentation is one of  the  most important and ubiquitous problems in
medical image processing. It provides  detailed quantitative analysis for
accurate disease diagnosis, abnormal detection, and classification. Currently
deep learning algorithms are widely used in medical image segmentation, most
algorithms trained models with full annotated datasets. However,   obtaining
medical image datasets  is very difficult and expensive, and   full  annotation of
3D medical image  is a  monotonous and time-consuming work. Partially  labelling
informative slices in 3D images will be a great  relief of manual  annotation.
Sample selection strategies  based on active  learning have been proposed in  the
field of 2D  image,  but few  strategies focus on 3D images. In this paper, we
propose a  sparse annotation strategy based  on attention-guided active learning
for 3D   medical image segmentation. Attention  mechanism is used  to improve
segmentation accuracy and estimate the segmentation  accuracy of each slice.  The
comparative experiments with three different strategies using datasets  from the
developing human  connectome project (dHCP) show that, our strategy only needs
15%  to 20% annotated slices in brain extraction task and 30% to  35% annotated
slices   in tissue segmentation task  to achieve comparative results as full
annotation.

This paper presents a novel approach for dimension reduction in semidefinite programs using Jordan algebras. Semidefinite programs are a class of optimization problems that involve optimizing a linear objective function subject to linear matrix inequality constraints. The proposed method leverages the properties of Jordan algebras to reduce the dimensionality of the problem, thereby improving computational efficiency. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through numerical experiments on various benchmark problems. The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing dimension reduction techniques in terms of both solution quality and computational time. Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of semidefinite programming and offers a promising avenue for future research in dimension reduction techniques.

We use Minkowski Functionals to explore the presence of non-Gaussian
signatures in simulated cosmic microwave background (CMB) maps. Precisely, we
analyse the non-Gaussianities produced from the angular power spectra emerging
from a class of inflationary models with a primordial step-like potential. This
class of models are able to perform the best-fit of the low-$\ell$ `features',
revealed first in the CMB angular power spectrum by the WMAP experiment and
then confirmed by the Planck collaboration maps. Indeed, such models generate
oscillatory features in the primordial power spectrum of scalar perturbations,
that are then imprinted in the large scales of the CMB field. Interestingly, we
discover Gaussian deviations in the CMB maps simulated from the power spectra
produced by these models, as compared with Gaussian $\Lambda$CDM maps.
Moreover, we also show that the kind and level of the non-Gaussianities
produced in these simulated CMB maps are compatible with that found in the four
foreground-cleaned Planck maps. Our results indicate that inflationary models
with a step-like potential are not only able to improve the best-fit respect to
the $\Lambda$CDM model accounting well for the `features' observed in the CMB
angular power spectrum, but also suggesting a possible origin for certain
non-Gaussian signatures observed in the Planck data.

This paper proposes  a novel method called SUSAN (Segment Unannotated  image  Structure using Adversarial Network) for segmenting  unannotated images. The method utilizes an  adversarial network  framework to learn the underlying  structure of the images without the  need for  manual annotations. The proposed method consists of two main components: a generator  network and a discriminator network. The  generator network generates segmentation masks for the unannotated images,  while the discriminator network distinguishes between the generated  masks and the ground truth masks.  The two networks are trained in an  adversarial manner, where the generator   aims to fool the discriminator,   and the discriminator aims to accurately classify the masks. Experimental  results  on various   datasets demonstrate the   effectiveness  of the  proposed method in segmenting unannotated images,  achieving competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods that rely on manual annotations. The proposed method has the potential to significantly reduce the manual  effort  required for image segmentation tasks, making it a valuable tool for  various applications in computer  vision.

U-Net has  been  providing state-of-the-art performance in many medical image
segmentation problems.   Many modifications have been  proposed  for  U-Net, such as
attention  U-Net, recurrent residual  convolutional U-Net (R2-UNet), and U-Net
with residual blocks  or blocks with  dense connections. However, all these
modifications  have an encoder-decoder structure with  skip connections, and  the
number of paths for information flow is  limited. We propose LadderNet in this
paper, which can be viewed as a chain of   multiple U-Nets. Instead of  only one
pair of encoder branch and decoder branch in U-Net, a LadderNet has multiple
pairs of  encoder-decoder branches,  and has skip connections between every pair
of adjacent decoder and decoder branches in each level. Inspired by the success
of ResNet and R2-UNet,  we use  modified  residual blocks where two convolutional
layers in  one block share the same weights.  A LadderNet has  more paths   for
information flow because of skip connections and residual blocks, and  can be
viewed as  an  ensemble  of Fully Convolutional Networks (FCN). The equivalence to
an ensemble of FCNs improves  segmentation accuracy, while the shared  weights
within  each residual  block reduce parameter number. Semantic segmentation is
essential for retinal disease  detection. We tested LadderNet on  two benchmark
datasets for blood vessel segmentation  in retinal images, and achieved superior
performance over methods in  the literature. The implementation is provided
\url{https://github.com/juntang-zhuang/LadderNet}

Neural networks are becoming more and more popular for the analysis of
physiological time-series. The most successful deep learning systems in this
domain combine convolutional and recurrent layers to extract useful features to
model temporal relations. Unfortunately, these recurrent models are difficult
to tune and optimise. In our experience, they often require task-specific
modifications, which makes them challenging to use for non-experts. We propose
U-Time, a fully feed-forward deep learning approach to physiological time
series segmentation developed for the analysis of sleep data. U-Time is a
temporal fully convolutional network based on the U-Net architecture that was
originally proposed for image segmentation. U-Time maps sequential inputs of
arbitrary length to sequences of class labels on a freely chosen temporal
scale. This is done by implicitly classifying every individual time-point of
the input signal and aggregating these classifications over fixed intervals to
form the final predictions. We evaluated U-Time for sleep stage classification
on a large collection of sleep electroencephalography (EEG) datasets. In all
cases, we found that U-Time reaches or outperforms current state-of-the-art
deep learning models while being much more robust in the training process and
without requiring architecture or hyperparametre adaptation across tasks.

One of the problems on the way to successful implementation of neural
networks is the quality of annotation. For instance, different annotators can
annotate images in a different way and very often their decisions do not match
exactly and in extreme cases are even mutually exclusive which results in noisy
annotations and, consequently, inaccurate predictions.
  To avoid that problem in the task of computed tomography (CT) imaging
segmentation we propose a clearing algorithm for annotations. It consists of 3
stages:
  - annotators scoring, which assigns a higher confidence level to better
annotators;
  - nodules scoring, which assigns a higher confidence level to nodules
confirmed by good annotators;
  - nodules merging, which aggregates annotations according to nodules
confidence.
  In general, the algorithm can be applied to many different tasks (namely,
binary and multi-class semantic segmentation, and also with trivial adjustments
to classification and regression) where there are several annotators labeling
each image.

Recent progress in biomedical image segmentation based on deep convolutional
neural networks (CNNs) has drawn much attention. However, its vulnerability
towards adversarial samples cannot be overlooked. This paper is the first one
that discovers that all the CNN-based state-of-the-art biomedical image
segmentation models are sensitive to adversarial perturbations. This limits the
deployment of these methods in safety-critical biomedical fields. In this
paper, we discover that global spatial dependencies and global contextual
information in a biomedical image can be exploited to defend against
adversarial attacks. To this end, non-local context encoder (NLCE) is proposed
to model short- and long range spatial dependencies and encode global contexts
for strengthening feature activations by channel-wise attention. The NLCE
modules enhance the robustness and accuracy of the non-local context encoding
network (NLCEN), which learns robust enhanced pyramid feature representations
with NLCE modules, and then integrates the information across different levels.
Experiments on both lung and skin lesion segmentation datasets have
demonstrated that NLCEN outperforms any other state-of-the-art biomedical image
segmentation methods against adversarial attacks. In addition, NLCE modules can
be applied to improve the robustness of other CNN-based biomedical image
segmentation methods.

The Quantitative Subspace Theorem is a  fundamental result in linear algebra  that provides a quantitative bound on  the dimension of a subspace of a  vector space. In this paper, we present a  new proof of the Quantitative Subspace  Theorem using a novel approach  based  on the concept of rank. Our proof not  only provides a tighter bound on   the dimension of  the subspace, but also offers insights  into the structure of  the subspace itself. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through  several examples  and compare  our  results with existing proofs of the theorem. Our findings contribute to the understanding  of subspaces in linear algebra  and have potential applications  in various fields such as signal  processing and machine learning.

This paper proposes a novel approach called Positional Contrastive Learning (PCL) for volumetric medical image segmentation. PCL leverages the concept of contrastive learning to learn representations of medical images by maximizing the agreement between positive pairs and minimizing the agreement between negative pairs. The proposed method incorporates positional information into the contrastive learning framework by introducing a positional encoding module. This module encodes the spatial information of the medical images, enabling the model to capture the positional relationships between different regions. Experimental results on various medical image segmentation tasks demonstrate that PCL outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability. The proposed method shows promise for improving the performance of volumetric medical image segmentation and has the potential to contribute to advancements in clinical diagnosis and treatment planning.

The paper proposes a novel method for learning to segment images when the training data consists   of  misaligned and partial labels. Traditional segmentation methods rely on accurate and complete annotation, which is  often challenging and time-consuming to obtain. In this paper, we introduce a  new approach that leverages weakly supervised learning techniques to  address  the issue of misaligned and incomplete annotations.  Specifically,  we propose a dual  task network that simultaneously learns to predict both the class  labels and the alignment offsets. By jointly training these two tasks, our model is   able  to  effectively  overcome  the challenges associated  with misalignment  and  partial labeling. Experimental results on a   number of benchmark datasets demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms existing approaches in   terms  of  segmentation accuracy  and robustness to label noise. Overall, our work contributes to the field of  image segmentation by  improving the reliability and efficiency of annotation in the presence  of misaligned and partial labels.

This paper explores the limitations of pixel-wise supervision for image segmentation tasks and proposes the use of global shape descriptors as an alternative approach. The authors argue that pixel-wise supervision can be computationally expensive and may not capture the overall shape of objects accurately. They introduce several global shape descriptors, such as the convex hull and bounding box, and demonstrate their effectiveness in segmenting objects in various datasets. The results show that these global shape descriptors can achieve comparable or even better performance than pixel-wise supervision, while requiring less computational resources. The findings suggest that global shape descriptors have the potential to improve segmentation tasks and should be further explored in future research.

This paper presents a deep learning approach for object saliency detection and image segmentation. Object saliency detection aims to identify the most visually significant objects in an image, while image segmentation aims to partition an image into meaningful regions. The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, which is trained on a large dataset of annotated images. The network is able to learn high-level features that capture the salient objects and regions in an image. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The paper also provides insights into the learned features and their relevance to object saliency and image segmentation. Overall, this work contributes to the field of computer vision by providing an effective and efficient deep learning approach for object saliency detection and image segmentation.

This paper presents the limit distribution theory for maximum likelihood estimation of a log-concave density. Log-concave densities are a class of probability densities that have important applications in various fields, including economics, finance, and statistics. The maximum likelihood estimator is a widely used method for estimating parameters of a probability density function. The authors derive the limit distribution of the maximum likelihood estimator for log-concave densities and provide conditions under which the estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal. The results are illustrated through simulations and a real data example. The findings of this paper contribute to the understanding of the statistical properties of maximum likelihood estimation for log-concave densities and have implications for the application of this estimation method in practice.

Separating and labeling each instance of a nucleus (instance-aware
segmentation) is the fundamental challenge in analyzing single cell nuclei on
fluorescence microscopy images. Deep neural networks can learn the implicit
transform of a nuclear image into a probability map showing the class
membership of each pixel (nucleus or background), but the use of
post-processing steps to turn the probability map into a labeled object mask is
error-prone. This often accounts for atomic images of tumor sections and
atomic images from varying tumor preparations. In this work, we aim to
improve the efficiency of state-of-the-art deep learning systems to
segment nuclei in fluorescence images of different tissue origins and sample
preparation types without post-processing. We compare systems that
operate on pixel to pixel translation and an architecture that operates on
object detection and subsequent locally applied segmentation. In addition, we
propose a novel approach to develop synthetic images to extend the training
set. We evaluate the impact of ground truth annotation quality, image scale
and segmentation complexity on segmentation efficiency. Results show that
two out of five deep learning systems (U-Net, U-Net with ResNet34
backbone, Mask R-CNN) can segment fluorescent nuclear images on most of the
sample preparation types and tissue origins with adequate segmentation
efficiency. Mask R-CNN, an architecture used to address instance aware
segmentation tasks, outperforms other systems. Equal nuclear mean length,
consistent nuclear annotations and the use of artificially produced images
result in overall acceptable accuracy and recall from various tissues and
sample preparation types.

The abstract of this paper presents a novel approach for translating LiDAR point clouds to panoramic color images. The goal of this translation is to enable efficient perception and understanding of LiDAR data by humans. The proposed method integrates semantic segmentation and conditional generative adversarial networks to generate realistic and semantic-aware panoramic color images from LiDAR point clouds. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through extensive experiments and quantitative analysis, which demonstrate its superiority over existing approaches in terms of quality and semantic consistency. Overall, this work contributes to the field of multi-modal domain translation, specifically in the context of LiDAR data, and shows potential for practical applications in autonomous driving and robotics.

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision, which involves assigning a class label to each pixel in an image. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown state-of-the-art performance in semantic segmentation, but they often struggle to capture fine-scale details due to their fixed receptive fields. In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called Gated-SCNN, which tackles this problem by using gated convolutions. Gated convolutional layers selectively learn channel-specific spatial information, allowing the network to focus on important regions of the image while discarding irrelevant information. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Gated-SCNN on several benchmark datasets and show that it outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. Our approach achieves outstanding results on challenging tasks such as object segmentation and scene parsing, making it a promising solution for real-world applications.

This paper presents  the  development  and characterization of a double-helix neutron detector using micron-size B-10 powder. The  detector consists of two concentric helical electrodes, with   the inner electrode coated with the  B-10 powder. The detector  was tested using  a neutron source, and its performance was   evaluated in terms of efficiency and energy resolution. The results  showed that the detector had a high efficiency for  detecting neutrons and  a  good energy resolution. The double-helix design allowed  for   a compact and efficient detector, making it  suitable for various applications in neutron detection. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of using micron-size B-10 powder in double-helix neutron  detectors.

we propose a method for efficiently finding all parallel passages in a large
corpus, even if the passages are not quite identical due to rephrasing and
orthographic variation. The key ideas Are the representation of each word in
the corpus by its two Most infrequent letters, finding matched pairs of strings
of four or five words that differ by at most one word and then identifying
clusters of such matched pairs. Using this method, over 4600 parallel pairs of
passages were identified in the Babylonian Talmud, a Hebrew-Aramaic corpus Of
over 1.8 million words, in just over 30 seconds. Empirical comparisons on
sample data indicate That the coverage obtained by our method is Essentially
the same as that obtained using slow exhaustive methods.

Segmentation and analysis of individual pores and grains  of mudrocks from
scanning electron microscope images  is non-trivial because of noise, imaging
artifacts, variation in pixel grayscale values across images, and  overlaps in
grayscale values among  different physical features  such as silt  grains, clay
grains, and pores in an image, which make  their identification difficult.
Moreover,  because grains  and pores often have overlapping grayscale values,
direct application of  threshold-based segmentation techniques is not
sufficient.  Recent  advances in the field of   computer vision have  made it easier
and faster to segment  images  and identify multiple occurrences of such features
in an image, provided that ground-truth data for  training the algorithm  is
available. Here, we propose a deep learning SEM image segmentation model,
MudrockNet based  on Google's DeepLab-v3+ architecture  implemented with the
TensorFlow library. The  ground-truth data  was obtained from an image-processing
workflow applied to scanning electron microscope images of uncemented muds from
the  Kumano Basin   offshore Japan  at depths < 1.1 km.  The trained deep learning
model obtained   a pixel-accuracy about 90%, and predictions  for the test data
obtained  a mean  intersection over union (IoU) of  0.6591  for  silt grains and
0.6642  for pores. We also compared our model with the random forest classifier
using trainable Weka segmentation in  ImageJ, and it was  observed that
MudrockNet gave better predictions  for  both silt  grains  and pores. The size,
concentration, and spatial  arrangement  of the silt and clay grains can affect
the petrophysical properties of a mudrock, and an automated method to
accurately identify the different grains and pores in mudrocks  can help  improve
reservoir and seal characterization  for petroleum exploration and  anthropogenic
waste sequestration.

This paper presents a robust video-based eye tracking method that utilizes recursive estimation of pupil characteristics. Recent advancements in eye tracking technology have gained significant attention due to their potential applications in various fields such as psychology and human-computer interaction. However, existing methods are often limited by their dependency on specific hardware, sensitivity to lighting conditions, and susceptibility to occlusions. To address these challenges, the proposed method combines image processing algorithms and recursive estimation techniques to track the movement of the pupil accurately and reliably. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach in tracking eye movements under challenging and diverse conditions, including low lighting, partial occlusions, and rapid movements. The proposed method offers a promising solution for robust video-based eye tracking, paving the way for advancements in related research areas.

In this paper, we consider the well-known modal logics $\mathbf{K}$,
$\mathbf{T}$, $\mathbf{K4}$, and $\mathbf{S4}$, and we study some of their
sub-propositional fragments, namely the classical Horn fragment, the Krom
fragment, the so-called core fragment, defined as the intersection of the Horn
and the Krom fragments, plus their sub-fragments obtained by limiting the use
of boxes and diamonds in clauses. We focus, first, on the relative expressive
power of such languages: we introduce a suitable measure of expressive power,
and we obtain a complex hierarchy that encompasses all fragments of the
considered logics. Then, after observing the low expressive power, in
particular, of the Horn fragments without diamonds, we study the computational
complexity of their satisfiability problem, proving that, in general, it
becomes polynomial.

The requirements to achieve high detection efficiency (above 50\%) and
gigahertz (GHz) frame rate for the proposed 42-keV X-ray free-electron laser
(XFEL) at Los Alamos are summarized. Direct detection scenarios using C
(diamond), Si, Ge and GaAs semiconductor sensors are analyzed. Single-photon
counting (SPC) mode and weak SPC mode using Si can potentially meet the
efficiency and frame rate requirements and be useful to both photoelectric
absorption and Compton physics as the photon energy increases. 

Multilayer
three-dimensional (3D) detector architecture, as a possible means to realize
SPC modes, is compared with the widely used two-dimensional (2D) hybrid planar
electrode structure and 3D deeply entrenched electrode architecture. 

Demonstration of thin film cameras less than 100-$\mu$m thick with onboard thin
ASICs could be an initial step to realize multilayer 3D detectors and SPC modes
for XFELs.

The paper investigates the concept of clique-width in graph theory and aims to identify minimal classes of graphs with unbounded clique-width. The authors define clique-width as a measure of the complexity of a graph and explore the relationship between clique-width and the presence of certain induced subgraphs. By identifying a finite set of forbidden induced subgraphs, the authors are able to define minimal classes of graphs with unbounded clique-width. The paper provides a theoretical framework for understanding the complexity of graphs and offers insights into the structure of graphs with unbounded clique-width.

In many computer vision tasks, we expect a particular behavior of the output
with respect to rotations Of the input image. If this relationship is
explicitly encoded, instead of treated as any other variation, the complexity
of the problem is decreased, leading To a reduction in the size of the required
model. In this paper, we propose the Rotation Equivariant Vector Field Networks
(RotEqNet), a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture encoding rotation
equivariance, invariance and covariance. Each convolutional filter is applied
at multiple orientations and returns a vector field representing magnitude and
angle of the highest scoring orientation at Every spatial location. We develop
a modified convolution operator relying on this representation to obtain deep
architectures. We test RotEqNet on several problems requiring different
responses with respect to the inputs' rotation: image classification,
biomedical image segmentation, orientation estimation and patch matching. In
all Cases, we show that RotEqNet offers extremely compact models In terms of
number of parameters and provides Results In line to those of networks orders
of magnitude Larger.

The abstract of the academic paper "Multi-environment model estimation for motility analysis of Caenorhabditis Elegans" highlights the development of a statistical framework to analyze and model the motility behavior of Caenorhabditis Elegans (C. elegans) in multiple environments. The study aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the effects of environmental factors on the locomotion patterns of C. elegans, a model organism widely used in biological research. The proposed framework utilizes high-resolution video recordings of C. elegans in various environmental conditions and leverages machine learning techniques to extract relevant features and quantify motility attributes. The statistical model takes into account both within-individual and between-individual variations, allowing for accurate estimation of motility parameters and their covariates. The researchers demonstrate the application of the framework on a dataset comprising multiple C. elegans strains and different environments. The results show that the proposed method effectively captures the complexities of C. elegans motility across different conditions, enabling researchers to gain insights into the underlying mechanisms of locomotion. This study opens up new avenues for investigating the factors influencing C. elegans motility and provides a valuable tool for future research in behavioral genetics and drug screening applications.

This paper presents a novel approach called ECG-DelNet for the delineation of ambulatory electrocardiograms (ECGs) with mixed quality labeling using neural networks. The proposed method utilizes a deep learning architecture that combines convolutional and recurrent neural networks to accurately detect and delineate the QRS complex, P wave, and T wave in ECG signals. The network is trained on a dataset of ambulatory ECGs with mixed quality labeling, which includes both manually annotated and automatically labeled data. Experimental results demonstrate that ECG-DelNet achieves superior performance compared to existing methods, with high accuracy and low computational cost. The proposed approach has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of ECG delineation in clinical practice, enabling more accurate diagnosis and monitoring of cardiovascular diseases.

Edge detection is a fundamental task in computer vision and image processing, with applications in various fields such as object recognition and scene understanding. Traditional edge detection methods, such as the Canny edge detector, have been widely used due to their effectiveness and simplicity. However, these methods often rely on handcrafted features and may not perform well on complex images with noise and texture. In this paper, we propose a deep neural network architecture inspired by traditional edge detection methods. Our network combines the strengths of both traditional methods and deep learning, leveraging the power of convolutional neural networks to learn features from raw image data. We evaluate our proposed method on benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art edge detection algorithms. The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance and outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. Overall, our work bridges the gap between traditional edge detection methods and deep learning, providing a promising approach for edge detection in complex images.

This paper presents an analytic approach to the problem of matroid representability, specifically focusing on the cardinality of sets of k-independent vectors over finite fields. The authors introduce a new method for analyzing the maximum distance separable conjecture, which is a well-known open problem in the field. The paper provides theoretical results and computational experiments to support their approach. The findings suggest that the analytic approach can provide valuable insights into the problem of matroid representability and contribute to the understanding of the maximum distance separable conjecture.

The concept of Optimal Transportation (PT) and Martingale Optimal Transportation (MOT)
were influenced by problems in mathematics and finance and have evolved over the
last years, producing major developments in theory and practice. MOT examines
the issue of pricing and hedging of a monetary instrument, referred to as an
option, assuming its payoff depends on a single investment value. In this paper we
introduce Vectorial Martingale Optimal Transport (VMOT) solution, which
describes the more general and realistic scenario in which the option payoff
depends on different asset rates. We address this issue of pricing and
hedging given market information -- characterized by vectorial marginal
distributions of underlying portfolio prices -- which is an intimately useful
setup in the robust economic framework.
  We establish that the VMOT problem, as an infinite-dimensional discrete
programming, admits an algorithm for its dual program. Such existence result of
dual optimizers is important for many reasons: the double optimizers
describe how a person who is responsible for an option payoff can develop optimal
hedging portfolios, and more importantly, they can obtain valuable information
on the geometry of primal optimizers, i.e. the VMOTs. As an illustration, we
show that many martingales given marginals can exhibit an extremal
conditional correlation structure when they independently optimize the
expectation of distance-type cost functions.

A 3D visual reconstruction of an image calculates the depths of as many pixels as possible. The result is a very dense point cloud, which often contains redundant and noisy information, especially on surfaces that are largely planar, such as the ground or the walls of the scene. We are going to use semantic image segmentation to determine which parts of the scene need to be simplified and which parts need to be kept at high resolution. We propose four methods of simplification of the point cloud which reduce the size of the point cloud using the local and global statistics of the classes, while keeping more points near the class boundaries to preserve the edges and discontinuities between classes. A 3D dense model is obtained by combining the point clouds in a 3D Delaunay triangulation to cope with the variable point density. Our experimental evaluation has shown that, by utilizing the semantics of the image, one can simplify the model and reduce the noise in the point clouds.

This paper introduces a new framework for reasoning about explicit evidence systems with common knowledge. We propose a formal model that captures the dynamics of evidence accumulation and updating in a multi-agent setting. We define a set of axioms that characterize the properties of common knowledge and provide a sound and complete proof system for reasoning about explicit evidence systems. We also present several examples and applications of our framework, including reasoning about belief revision and information aggregation. Our results demonstrate the usefulness and applicability of our model in various domains, and highlight the importance of common knowledge in reasoning about explicit evidence systems.

Automated segmentation in medical image analysis is a challenging task that
requires a large amount of manually labeled data. However, manually annotating
medical data is often laborious, and most existing learning-based approaches
fail to accurately delineate object boundaries without effective geometric
constraints. Contrastive learning, a sub-area of self-supervised learning, has
recently been noted as a promising direction in multiple application fields. In
this work, we present a novel Contrastive Voxel-wise Representation Learning
(CVRL) method with geometric constraints to learn global-local visual
representations for volumetric medical image segmentation with limited
annotations. Our framework can effectively learn global and local features by
capturing 0D spatial context and rich anatomical information. Specifically, we
introduce a voxel-to-volume contrastive algorithm to learn global information
from 3D images, and propose to perform local voxel-to-voxel contrast to
explicitly make use of local cues in the embedding space. Moreover, we
integrate an elastic interaction-based active contour model as a geometric
regularization term to enable fast and reliable object delineations in an
end-to-end learning manner. Results on the Atrial Segmentation Challenge
dataset demonstrate superiority of our proposed scheme, especially in a setting
with a very limited number of annotated data.

This paper investigates the concept of an irreversible 2-conversion set in graphs of bounded degree. A 2-conversion set is a subset of vertices in a graph such that any two vertices in the set can be converted into each other by a sequence of at most two edge modifications. The authors prove that for graphs of bounded degree, there exists an irreversible 2-conversion set if and only if the graph contains a certain subgraph. They also provide an algorithm for finding such a subgraph in polynomial time. The results of this paper have implications for understanding the structure and dynamics of graphs with bounded degree.

A framework of M-estimation based fuzzy C-means clustering (MFCM) algorithm
is proposed with iterative reweighted least squares (IRLS) algorithm, and
penalty constraint and kernelization extensions of MFCM algorithms are also
developed. Introducing penalty information to the object functions of MFCM
algorithms, the spatially constrained fuzzy C-means (SFCM) is extended to
penalty constraints MFCM algorithms(abbr. pMFCM).Substituting the Euclidean
distance with kernel method, the MFCM and pMFCM algorithms are extended to
kernelized MFCM (abbr. KMFCM) and kernelized pMFCM (abbr.pKMFCM) algorithms.
The performances of MFCM, pMFCM, KMFCM and pKMFCM algorithms are evaluated in
three tasks: pattern recognition on 10 standard data sets from UCI Machine
Learning databases, noise image segmentation performances on a synthetic image,
a magnetic resonance brain image (MRI), and image segmentation of a standard
images from Berkeley Segmentation Dataset and Benchmark. The experimental
results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed algorithms in pattern
recognition and image segmentation.

Semantic segmentation is an important task in remote sensing imagery analysis, as it allows for the identification and classification of different objects and regions within an image. However, existing methods often struggle with accurately segmenting boundaries between different classes. In this paper, we propose a novel boundary loss function that addresses this issue by penalizing errors in boundary prediction. We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and compare it to state-of-the-art approaches. Our results demonstrate that the proposed boundary loss significantly improves the accuracy of semantic segmentation, particularly in challenging scenarios with complex boundaries. Overall, our work contributes to the advancement of remote sensing imagery analysis and has potential applications in various fields such as urban planning and environmental monitoring.

Semantic segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision, especially when there is limited training data available. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for one-shot image semantic segmentation by learning semantically meaningful class prototypes. We first extract class prototypes from a set of annotated training images using a clustering algorithm. These prototypes capture the visual characteristics of each class. Then, we transfer the learned prototypes to a target image by aligning them with similar regions. We use a siamese network to measure the similarity between the prototypes and the target image regions. Finally, we perform a pixel-wise classification using the transferred prototypes to generate the segmentation mask. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show that our approach achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Our proposed method provides a promising solution for one-shot semantic segmentation and has the potential to be applied in applications where acquiring a large amount of annotated data is difficult or costly.

Image segmentation is crucial step in a wide range of method image
processing systems. It is useful in visualization of the different objects
present in image. In spite of several methods available in the
literature, image segmentation still a challenging problem in most of image
processing applications. The challenge comes from fuzziness of image
objects and the overlapping of the different regions. Detection of edges in an
image is very important step towards understanding image features. There are
large numbers of edge detection operators available, each designed to be
sensitive to certain types of edges. The Quality of edge detection can be
measured from several criteria objectively. Some criteria are proposed in terms
of mathematical measurement, some of them are based on application and
implementation requirements. Since edges often occur at image locations
representing object boundaries, edge detection is extensively used in image
segmentation when images are divided into areas corresponding to different
objects. This can be used specifically for enhancing the tumor area in
mammographic images. Different methods are available for edge detection like
Roberts, Sobel, Prewitt, Canny, Log edge operators. In this paper novel
algorithms for edge detection has been proposed for mammographic images. Breast
boundary, pectoral region and tumor location can be seen clearly by using this
method. For comparison purpose Roberts, Sobel, Prewitt, Canny, Log edge
operators are used and their results are displayed. Experimental results
demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed approach.

Weighted Sobolev spaces on metric-measure spaces (X, d, m) are investigated. Let  be the weight function and let W_p_(X,d,m) and H_p_(X,d,m) be the weighted Sobolev spaces. It is proved that, under some conditions on the metric-measure structure and on the weight, W_p_(X,d,m)=H_1p_(X,d,m). In this paper some results of Muckenhaut and Zhikov are generalized to metric-measure spaces under certain conditions on the weight.

The ability to detect change-points in a dynamic network or a time series of
graphs is an increasingly important task in many applications of the emerging
discipline of graph signal processing. This paper formulates change-point
detection as a hypothesis testing problem in terms of a generative latent
position model, focusing on the special case of the Stochastic Block Model time
series. We analyze two classes of scan statistics, based on distinct underlying
locality statistics presented in the literature. Our main contribution is the
derivation of the limiting distributions and power characteristics of the
competing scan statistics. Performance is compared theoretically, on synthetic
data, and on the Enron email corpus. We demonstrate that both statistics are
admissible in one simple setting, while one of the statistics is inadmissible a
second setting.

We introduce a parametrized version of the Wadge game for functions and show
that each lower cone in the Weihrauch degrees is characterized by such a game. These parametrized Wadge games subsume the original Wadge game, the eraser and
backtrack games as well as Semmes's tree games. 

In particular, we propose that
the lower cones in the Weihrauch degrees are the answer to Andretta's question
on which classes of functions admit game characterizations. 

We then discuss some applications of such parametrized Wadge games. Using
machinery from Weihrauch reducibility theory, we introduce games characterizing
every (transfinite) level of the Baire hierarchy via an iteration of a pruning
derivative on countably branching trees.

This  paper presents a novel parallel two-pass context tree compression  algorithm utilizing  the Minimum Description Length (MDL) principle. The proposed algorithm is capable of  achieving high compression ratios  while maintaining a low  computational  complexity. The algorithm utilizes  a  parallel processing approach  to  improve the compression speed without compromising its performance. Additionally, the algorithm is shown  to be universally applicable to various  types of data, making it  highly versatile. Experimental  results demonstrate the  effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, outperforming existing context  tree-based compression algorithms in terms of both compression ratio and speed. Overall, this  paper provides a  comprehensive exploration   of a parallel two-pass MDL context tree compression algorithm, highlighting its  potential  for practical data compression applications.

The paper  "Edge Clique Cover of  Claw-free Graphs" studies  the problem of finding a minimum edge  clique cover in claw-free graphs. A claw is a subgraph  with one central vertex and  three leaves, and a vertex  clique is a subgraph where  every pair of vertices  is connected by  an  edge. The authors present a polynomial-time algorithm that finds a minimum edge clique cover in O(n^4)  time for claw-free graphs. They provide proofs of   correctness and analyze the complexity of the algorithm. The results  of this paper contribute   to  the understanding of the edge clique cover problem and provide  practical   implications for related graph theory applications.

In the field of quantum computing, error correction is a crucial aspect that ensures the reliability and accuracy of quantum information processing. This paper introduces a graphical approach for designing and verifying quantum error correction codes. The proposed graphical structures provide a visual representation of error correction codes, making it easier for researchers to understand and analyze the effectiveness of different codes. The paper also discusses the use of various graphical techniques, such as graphs and diagrams, to represent the error correction process and its associated components. The effectiveness of the proposed graphical structures is demonstrated through simulations and comparisons with existing error correction methods. Overall, this paper presents a valuable contribution to the field of quantum error correction, offering a graphical framework that enhances the design and verification process.

This paper is the second part of a series on lifting representations of finite reductive groups. In this paper, we focus on the explicit conorms of these groups. We provide a detailed analysis of the conorms and their properties, including their construction and explicit formulas. We also investigate the relationship between conorms and other important concepts in representation theory, such as the character values and the decomposition matrices. Our results provide a deeper understanding of the structure and behavior of finite reductive groups, and have potential applications in various areas of mathematics and physics.

The Aw-Rascle-Zhang (ARZ) model can be interpreted as a generalization of the
Lighthill-Whitham-Richards (LWR) model, possessing a family of fundamental
diagram curves, each of which represents a class of drivers with a different
empty road velocity. A weakness of this approach is that different drivers
possess vastly different densities at which traffic flow stagnates. This
drawback can be overcome by modifying the pressure relation in the ARZ model,
leading to the generalized Aw-Rascle-Zhang (GARZ) model. We present an approach
to determine the parameter functions of the GARZ model from fundamental diagram
measurement data. The predictive accuracy of the resulting data-fitted GARZ
model is compared to other traffic models by means of a three-detector test
setup, employing two types of data: vehical trajectory data, and sensor data.
This work also considers the extension of the ARZ and the GARZ models to models
with a relaxation term, and conducts an investigation of the optimal relaxation
time.

This paper investigates the use of multiuser  diversity for  secrecy communications in wireless networks. Specifically, the  authors propose a scheme  that utilizes opportunistic  jammer  selection to enhance the  secrecy  performance. The scheme aims to maximize the secrecy degrees of freedom (DoF) by selecting the  most  advantageous jammer for each user. The  authors derive the  secure DoF and jammer scaling law  for the proposed scheme and compare it  with existing schemes.  Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of  the proposed scheme in  improving secrecy performance  and achieving higher  secure DoF. The findings of  this study provide valuable insights for the design of secure wireless communication systems.

It has been shown recently that relativistic distortions generate a dipolar
modulation in the two-point correlation function of galaxies. To measure this
relativistic dipole it is necessary to cross-correlate different populations of
galaxies with for example different luminosities or colours. In this paper, we
construct an optimal estimator to measure the dipole with multiple populations.
We show that this estimator increases the signal-to-noise of the dipole by up
to 26 percent. Using 7 populations of galaxies, in a survey with halos and
number densities similar to those of the millennium simulation, we forecast a
cumulative signal-to-noise of 4.4. For the main galaxy sample of SDSS at low
redshift z<0.2 our optimal estimator predicts a cumulative signal-to-noise of
2.4. Finally we forecast a cumulative signal-to-noise of 5.3 in the upcoming
DESI survey. These forecasts indicate that with the appropriate choice of
estimator the relativistic dipole should be detectable in current and future
surveys.

The paper introduces a new algorithm called Multi-hop Diffusion LMS (Least Mean Squares) for energy-constrained distributed estimation. The algorithm aims to minimize the energy consumption of distributed estimation systems while maintaining accurate estimates. The proposed algorithm utilizes multi-hop communication to reduce the amount of energy required for information exchange between nodes. The authors present theoretical analysis and simulations to demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm in energy-constrained scenarios. The results show that the Multi-hop Diffusion LMS algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of energy consumption and estimation accuracy. This paper provides valuable insights and practical solutions for energy-efficient distributed estimation in resource-constrained environments.

Deep convolutional neural networks have shown outstanding performance in
medical image segmentation tasks. The usual problem when training supervised
deep learning methods is the lack of labelled data which is time-consuming and
costly to obtain. In this paper, we propose a novel uncertainty-guided
semi-supervised learning based on a student-teacher approach for training the
segmentation network using limited labelled samples and a large number of
unlabelled images. First, a teacher segmentation model is trained from the
labelled samples using Bayesian deep learning. The trained model is used to
generate soft segmentation labels and uncertainty maps for the unlabelled set.
The student model is then updated using the softly segmented samples and the
corresponding pixel-wise confidence of the segmentation quality estimated from
the uncertainty of the teacher model using a newly designed loss function.
Experimental results on a retinal layer segmentation task show that the
proposed method improves the segmentation performance in comparison to the
fully supervised approach and is on par with the expert annotator. The proposed
semi-supervised segmentation framework is a key contribution and applicable for
biomedical image segmentation across various imageing modalities where access to
annotated medical images is challenging

We introduce a new multi-dimensional nonlinear embedding -- Piecewise Flat
Embedding (PFE) -- for image segmentation. Based on the theory of sparse signal
recovery, piecewise flat embedding with diverse channels attempts to recover a
piecewise constant image representation with sparse region boundaries and
sparse clustre value scattering. The resultant piecewise flat embedding
exhibits interesting properties such as suppressing slowly varying signals, and
offers an image representation with higher region identifiability which is
desirable for image segmentation or high-level semantic analysis tasks. We
formulate our embedding as a variant of the Laplacian Eigenmap embedding with
an $L_{1,p} (0<p\leq1)$ regularisation term to promote sparse solutions. First,
we devise a two-stage numerical algorithm based on Bregman iterations to
compute $L_{1,1}$-regularised piecewise flat embeddings. We further generalise
this algorithm through iterative reweighting to solve the general
$L_{1,p}$-regularised problem. To demonstrate its efficacy, we integrate PFE
into two existing image segmentation frameworks, segmentation based on
clustreing and hierarchical segmentation based on contour detection.
Experiments on four major benchmark datasets, BSDS500, MSRC, Stanford
Background Dataset, and PASCAL Context, show that segmentation algorithms
incorporating our embedding achieve significantly improved results.

We propose a novel locally adaptive learning estimator for enhancing the
inter- and intra- discriminative capabilities of Deep Neural Networks, which
can be used as improved loss layer for semantic image segmentation tasks. Most
loss layers compute pixel-wise cost between feature maps and ground truths,
ignoring spatial layouts and interactions between neighbouring pixels with same
object category, and thus networks cannot be effectively sensitive to
intra-class connections. Stride by stride, our method firstly conducts adaptive
pooling philtre operating over predicted feature maps, aiming to merge predicted
distributions over a small group of neighbouring pixels with same category, and
then it computes cost between the merged distribution vector and their category
label. Such design can make groups of neighbouring predictions from same
category involved into estimations on predicting correctness with respect to
their category, and hence train networks to be more sensitive to regional
connections between adjacent pixels based on their categories. In the
experiments on Pascal VOC 2012 segmentation datasets, the consistently improved
results show that our proposed approach achieves better segmentation masks
against previous counterparts.

panoramic segmentation is a scene where image segmentation tasks is more
difficult. With the development of CNN networks, panoramic segmentation tasks
have been sufficiently developed.However, the current panoramic segmentation
algorithms are more concerned with context semantics, But The details of image
are not processed enough. Moreover, they cannot solve the problems which
contains the accuracy of occluded object segmentation,little object
segmentation,boundary pixel In object segmentation etc. aiming to address these
issues, this paper presents some useful tricks. (a) By changing the basic
segmentation model, the model can take into account the large objects and the
boundary pixel classification of image details. (b) Modify the loss function so
that it can take into account the boundary Pixels of multiple objects in the
image. (c) Use a semi-supervised approach to regain control of the training
process. (d) Using multi-scale training and reasoning. All these operations
Named AinnoSeg, AinnoSeg can achieve state-of-art performance on the well-known
dataset ADE20K.

In this paper, we propose a novel method for segmenting embryo eggs based on the k-means clustering algorithm in the Lab color space. The Lab color space is chosen due to its perceptually uniform characteristics, which makes it well-suited for image segmentation. We utilize the k-means algorithm to cluster the Lab color values of the pixels in the image and determine the optimal number of clusters to represent different regions. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately detecting and segmenting embryo eggs in images. This method shows promise for applications in the field of reproductive biology and assists in the automated analysis of embryo development.

Hyperspectral image segmentation is a challenging task due to the high dimensionality and complex spectral variations of hyperspectral data. This paper proposes a novel approach combining conditional random fields (CRFs) with deep feature learning to address this problem. The CRFs are used to model the spatial dependencies between pixels, while deep feature learning is employed to extract discriminative features from the hyperspectral data. The proposed approach achieves superior segmentation performance compared to existing methods on several benchmark datasets. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting hyperspectral images.
