sеgmеntаtіоn реrfоrms rоbustlу wіthоut thе nееd fоr рrіоr knоwlеdgе

This paper provides a gentle introduction to   deep learning in   the field of medical image processing.  Deep learning  has shown great promise in various applications, including image classification, segmentation, and disease detection. This paper aims to introduce the fundamental concepts  and techniques of deep learning, such as convolutional  neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), in the context of  medical  image   processing. The paper also provides an overview of  the challenges  and potential solutions in applying  deep learning to medical image analysis, as well  as the  ethical  considerations and  limitations of this technology. Overall,  this paper serves  as a comprehensive guide  for researchers  and practitioners interested in using deep learning for medical image processing.

The nematode Caenorhabditis elegans is a well-known model organism used to
investigate fundamental questions in biology. Motility assays of this small
roundworm are designed to study relationships between genes and behavior.
Commonly, motility analysis is used to classify nematode movements and
characterize them quantitatively. Over past years, C. elegans' motility has
been studied across a wide range of environments, including crawling on
substrates, swimming in fluids, and locomoting through microfluidic substrates.
However, each environment often requires customized image processing tools
relying on heuristic parameter tuning. In the present study, we propose a novel
Multi-Environment Model Estimation (MEME) framework for automated image
segmentation that is versatile across various environments. The MEME platform
is constructed around the concept of Mixture of Gaussian (MOG) models, where
statistical models for both the background environment and nematode
appearance are explicitly learned and used to accurately segment target
nematode. Our method is designed to simplify the burden often imposed on users;
here, only single image which includes a nematode in its environment must be
provided for model learning. In addition, our platform enables extraction
of nematode `skeletons' for straightforward motility quantification. We test
our algorithm on various locomotive environments and compare performances with
an intensity-based thresholding method. Overall, MEME outperforms the
threshold-based approach for the overwhelming majority of cases examined.
Ultimately, MEME provides researchers with attractive platform for C.
elegans' segmentation and `skeletonizing' across wide range of motility
assays.

We present a method for reconstructing images viewed by observers based only
on their eye movements. By exploring the relationships between gaze patterns
and image stimuli, the "What Are You Looking At?" (WAYLA) system learns to
synthesize photo-realistic images that are similar to the original pictures
being viewed. The WAYLA approach is based on the Conditional Generative
Adversarial Network (Conditional GAN) image-to-image translation technique of
Isola et al. We consider two specific applications - the first, of
reconstructing newspaper images from gaze heat maps, and the second, of
detailed reconstruction of images containing only text. The newspaper image
reconstruction process is divided into two image-to-image translation
operations, the first mapping gaze heat maps into image segmentations, and the
second mapping the generated segmentation into a newspaper image. We validate
the performance of our approach using various evaluation metrics, along with
human visual inspection. All results confirm the ability of our network to
perform image generation tasks using eye tracking data.

In this paper, we establish a correspondence between the dynamics of unicritical polynomials and the Galois theory of their iterates. We show that the dynamics of a unicritical polynomial can be understood in terms of the Galois group of its iterates, and vice versa. Specifically, we prove that the Galois group of the iterates of a unicritical polynomial determines the dynamics of the polynomial, and conversely, the dynamics of the polynomial determine the Galois group of its iterates. We provide explicit formulas and algorithms for computing the Galois group of the iterates of a given unicritical polynomial, and we demonstrate the usefulness of our correspondence in studying the dynamics of unicritical polynomials. Our results have implications for the study of complex dynamics and Galois theory, and they shed light on the interplay between these two areas of mathematics.

The paper presents DatasetGAN, a new method for generating labeled datasets with minimal human effort. Traditional methods of creating labeled datasets involve manual annotation which is time-consuming and often expensive. DatasetGAN instead proposes a generative adversarial network (GAN) approach, where a generator network creates synthetic data and a discriminator network distinguishes between the real and synthetic data. The synthetic data is then labeled by the discriminator, thereby creating a labeled dataset. Experimental results show that DatasetGAN is able to generate high-quality labeled datasets across various domains, achieving similar performance to manually labeled datasets but with significantly reduced human effort. The proposed method has the potential to greatly accelerate the process of dataset creation and make it more accessible to researchers and practitioners in machine learning and artificial intelligence.

Unsupervised video object segmentation has often been tackled by methods
based on recurrent neural networks and optical flow. Despite their complexity,
these kinds of approaches tend to favour short-term temporal dependencies and
are thus prone to accumulating inaccuracies, which cause drift over time.
Moreover, simple (static) image segmentation models, alone, can perform
competitively against these methods, which further suggests that the way
temporal dependencies are modelled should be reconsidered. Motivated by these
observations, in this paper we explore simple yet effective strategies to model
long-term temporal dependencies. Inspired by the non-local operators of [70],
we introduce a technique to establish dense correspondences between pixel
embeddings of a referance "anchor" frame and the current one. This allows the
learning of pairwise dependencies at arbitrarily long distances without
conditioning on intermediate frames. Without online supervision, our approach
can suppress the background and precisely segment the foreground object even in
challenging scenarios, while maintaining consistent performance over time. With
a mean IoU of $81.7\%$, our method ranks first on the DAVIS-2016 leaderboard of
unsupervised methods, while still being competitive against state-of-the-art
online semi-supervised approaches. We further evaluate our method on the FBMS
dataset and the ViSal video saliency dataset, showing results competitive with
the state of the art.

Building a large image dataset with high-quality object masks for semantic
segmentation is costly and time consuming. In this paper, we introduce a
principled semi-supervised framework that only uses a small set of fully
supervised images (having semantic segmentation labels and box labels) and a
set of images with only object bounding box labels (we call it the weak set).
Our framework trains the primary segmentation model with the aid of an
ancillary model that generates initial segmentation labels for the weak set and
a self-correction module that improves the generated labels during training
using the increasingly accurate primary model. We introduce two variants of the
self-correction module using either linear or convolutional functions.
Experiments on the PASCAL VOC 2012 and Cityscape datasets show that our models
trained with a small fully supervised set perform similar to, or better than,
models trained with a large fully supervised set while requiring ~7x less
annotation effort.

This paper aims to propose a novel approach for image segmentation of cross-country scenes captured in the infrared (IR) spectrum. The proposed approach integrates image processing techniques and machine learning algorithms to accurately delineate different objects and regions within the IR images. The main challenge in IR image segmentation is the low contrast and high noise levels present in the images. To address this challenge, the proposed approach utilizes a combination of intensity-based segmentation, texture analysis, and clustering algorithms. Experimental results on a dataset of IR images demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach in segmenting cross-country scenes. The proposed approach can be applied in various applications, including surveillance, military operations, and environmental monitoring.

The crystallographic phase problem is a fundamental challenge in electron diffraction, where the phase information of the diffracted waves is lost during the measurement process. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to solve the phase problem using dynamical scattering in electron diffraction. We demonstrate the feasibility of our method through simulations and experimental results. Our approach offers a promising solution to the long-standing phase problem in electron diffraction, opening up new possibilities for high-resolution structural analysis of materials.

Semantic segmentation is essentially important to biomedical image analysis.
Many recent works mainly focus on integrating the Fully Convolutional Network
(FCN) architecture with sophisticated convolution implementation and deep
supervision. In this paper, we propose to decompose the single segmentation
task into three subsequent sub-tasks, including (1) pixel-wise image
segmentation, (2) prediction of the class labels of the objects within the
image, and (3) classification of the scene the image belonging to. While these
three sub-tasks are trained to optimize their individual loss functions of
different perceptual levels, we propose to let them interact by the task-task
context ensemble. Moreover, we propose a novel sync-regularization to penalize
the deviation between the outputs of the pixel-wise segmentation and the class
prediction tasks. These effective regularizations help FCN utilize context
information comprehensively and attain accurate semantic segmentation, even
though the number of the images for training may be limited in many biomedical
applications. We have successfully applied our framework to three diverse 2D/3D
medical image datasets, including Robotic Scene Segmentation Challenge 18
(ROBOT18), Brain Tumor Segmentation Challenge 18 (BRATS18), and Retinal Fundus
Glaucoma Challenge (REFUGE18). We have achieved top-tier performance in all
three challenges.

For complex segmentation tasks, fully automatic systems are inherently
limited in their achievable accuracy for extracting relevant objects. Especially in cases where only few data sets need to be processed for a highly
accurate result, semi-automatic segmentation techniques exhibit a clear benefit
for the user. One area of application is medical image processing during an
intervention for a single patient. We propose a learning-based cooperative
segmentation approach which includes the computing entity as well as the user
into the task. 

Our system builds upon a state-of-the-art fully convolutional
artificial neural network (FCN) as well as an active user model for training. During the segmentation process, a user of the trained system can iteratively
add additional hints in form of pictorial scribbles as seed points into the FCN
system to achieve an interactive and precise segmentation result. 

The
segmentation quality of interactive FCNs is evaluated. 

Iterative FCN approaches
can yield superior results compared to networks without the user input channel
component, due to a consistent improvement in segmentation quality after each
interaction.

Tackling pattern recognition problems in areas such as computer vision,
bioinformatics, speech or text recognition is often done best by taking into
account task-specific statistical relations between output variables. In
structured prediction, this internal structure is used to predict multiple
outputs simultaneously, leading to more accurate and coherent predictions.
Structural support vector machines (SSVMs) are nonprobabilistic models that
optimize a joint input-output function through margin-based learning. Because
SSVMs generally disregard the interplay between unary and interaction factors
during the training phase, final parameters are suboptimal. Moreover, its
factors are often restricted to linear combinations of input features, limiting
its generalization power. To improve prediction accuracy, this paper proposes:
(i) Joint inference and learning by integration of back-propagation and
loss-augmented inference in SSVM subgradient descent; (ii) Extending SSVM
factors to neural networks that form highly nonlinear functions of input
features. Image segmentation benchmark results demonstrate improvements over
conventional SSVM training methods in terms of accuracy, highlighting the
feasibility of end-to-end SSVM training with neural factors.

In this paper, we propose a shape-aware semi-supervised approach for 3D semantic segmentation of medical images. Traditional methods for medical image segmentation often require large amounts of labeled data, which is time-consuming and costly to obtain. To address this issue, we leverage a small amount of labeled data along with a larger amount of unlabeled data to train our model. We introduce a novel adaptation mechanism that guides the model to better utilize the shape information present in the data. Specifically, we propose a shape-aware consistency regularization term that penalizes the model for producing inconsistent segmentations across different views of the same object. We validate our approach on a publicly available medical image dataset and demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in 3D semantic segmentation. Moreover, we show that our shape-aware regularization improves the segmentation accuracy by effectively utilizing the shape information present in the unlabeled data. Our work highlights the importance of shape-awareness in the context of medical image segmentation and provides a new direction for improving the performance of semi-supervised learning methods in this domain.

We  investigate the   behavior of flows, including turbulent flows, driven by a
horizontal body-force and   subject to a vertical magnetic field, with the
following question in mind: for very strong applied magnetic field, is the flow
mostly two-dimensional,  with remaining weak three-dimensional fluctuations, or
does it become exactly 2D, with no  dependence along the vertical?
  We first focus on the quasi-static approximation, i.e. the asymptotic limit
of vanishing magnetic Reynolds number Rm <<  1: we prove that the flow becomes
exactly 2D asymptotically   in time, regardless of the initial condition and
provided the interaction parameter  N is larger than a threshold value. We call
this property "absolute  two-dimensionalization": the attractor of the system is
necessarily a (possibly turbulent) 2D  flow.
  We  then consider  the  full-magnetohydrodynamic equations and we prove that,
for low  enough Rm and   large enough N, the flow becomes exactly  two-dimensional
in the long-time limit provided the initial vertically-dependent perturbations
are infinitesimal. We  call this  phenomenon "linear  two-dimensionalization": the
(possibly turbulent) 2D flow is  an attractor of the  dynamics, but  it  is not
necessarily  the only  attractor of the system. Some 3D  attractors  may  also  exist
and be attained for strong enough initial 3D   perturbations.
   These  results shed some light  on the existence of a dissipation anomaly for
magnetohydrodynamic flows subject  to   a strong external magnetic field.

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to image segmentation based on iterative inference from conditional score estimation. Our method leverages the power of deep neural networks to estimate the conditional score of each pixel given its context. We then iteratively update the segmentation mask by maximizing the conditional score of each pixel. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. Furthermore, we provide an in-depth analysis of the proposed method, shedding light on its strengths and limitations. Overall, our work contributes to the field of image segmentation by introducing a new approach that combines the strengths of deep learning and iterative inference.

This paper examines the challenges and proposes a novel approach to improve learning effectiveness for object detection and classification in cluttered backgrounds. Object detection and classification are important tasks in computer vision and have numerous applications such as surveillance, autonomous driving, and robotics. However, in cluttered backgrounds, the presence of irrelevant objects and occlusions can make these tasks more challenging. 

The proposed approach utilizes a deep neural network architecture that integrates object detection and classification modules. The network is trained using a combination of labeled data and weakly labeled data, which is obtained by automatically mining unlabeled images. To handle the challenges posed by cluttered backgrounds, the network incorporates spatial attention mechanisms that allow the network to focus on relevant regions of the image and suppress irrelevant information. 

The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets for object detection and classification in cluttered backgrounds. The approach achieves higher accuracy and faster execution time, making it a promising solution for practical applications. The findings contribute to the field of computer vision by providing an effective approach for improving learning effectiveness in challenging environments.

Inspired by the important historical application of exploring historical
heritage objects, in this paper we study the challenging issue of
automatically analyzing curve structures that are very weakly stamped or
etched on an object surface in the form of a very noisy depth map. Different
from most modern low-level image segmentation tools that are considered to be
very susceptible to the noise and occlusions, we propose a new supervised
learning algorithm based on Convolutional Neural Networks (ABC) to implicitly
develop and utilize more curve geometry and pattern information for addressing
this challenging issue. More specifically, we first propose a Fully
Convolutional Networks (FCN) to estimate the skeleton of curve structures and at
each skeleton pixel, a scale value is estimated to reflect the local curve
size. Then we propose a dense prediction network to refine the estimated curve
skeletons. Based on the estimated scale parameters, we then establish an adaptive
thresholding algorithm to achieve the final segmentation of curve structures.
In the laboratory, we validate the efficiency of the proposed technique on a
dataset of depth images scanned from unearthed clay sherds dating to the
Woodland period of Western South America.

Active contour models based on partial differential equations have proved
successful in image segmentation, yet the study of their geometric formulation
on arbitrary geometric graphs is still at an early stage. In this paper, we
introduce geometric approximations of gradient and curvature, which are used in
the geodesic active contour model. We prove convergence in probability of our
gradient approximation to the true gradient value and derive an asymptotic
upper bound for the error of this approximation for the class of random
geometric graphs. Two different approaches for the approximation of curvature
are presented and both are also proved to converge in probability in the case
of random geometric graphs. We propose neighborhood-based filtering on graphs
to improve the accuracy of the aforementioned approximations and define two
variants of Gaussian smoothing on graphs which include normalization in order
to adapt to graph non-uniformities. The performance of our active contour
framework on graphs is demonstrated in the segmentation of regular images and
geographical data defined on arbitrary graphs.

The 24Mg (p, ) 21Na reaction was studied at the Holifield Radioactive Ion Beam Facility at the Oak Ridge National Lab in order to obtain better data for the calculation of the 17F (, p) 20Ne astrophysical reaction. The reaction was studied using 31 MeV protons from a 12.5 mv tandem machine and enriched 24Mg. The 4He+ jets produced by the reaction were measured by a silicon array of many thin layers whose yields were measured at a range of angles. Using these data, we find a new level at 66615 keV. The angular distributions of the first four 21Na levels were used to compare the Distorted Wave Born Approximation calculations and verify the transfer of angular momentum.

Recently deep residual learning with residual units for training very deep
neural networks advanced the state-of-the-art performance on 2D image
recognition tasks, e.g., object detection and segmentation. However, how to
fully leverage contextual representations for recognition tasks from volumetric
data has not been well studied, especially in the field of medical image
computing, where a majority of image modalities are in volumetric format. In
this paper we explore the deep residual learning on the task of volumetric
brain segmentation. There are at least two main contributions in our work.
First, we propose a deep voxelwise residual network, referred as VoxResNet,
which borrows the spirit of deep residual learning in 2D image recognition
tasks, and is extended into a 3D variant for handling volumetric data. Second,
an auto-context version of VoxResNet is proposed by seamlessly integrating the
low-level image appearance features, implicit shape information and high-level
context together for further improving the volumetric segmentation performance.
Extensive experiments on the challenging benchmark of brain segmentation from
magnetic resonance (MR) images corroborated the efficacy of our proposed method
in dealing with volumetric data. We believe this work unravels the potential of
3D deep learning to advance the recognition performance on volumetric image
segmentation.

This paper presents a  comprehensive analysis of the criteria necessary for determining the efficiency and reliability of measures of quantum  correlations in physical systems. We discuss  the  importance of both  theoretical and experimental  considerations  in  the design  and evaluation of these measures, highlighting the  various  challenges faced in this field. Specifically, we  explore the properties that must be satisfied  by a  good  measure of quantum correlations, such as the ability to capture both entanglement and other nonclassical correlations,  as  well as the ability to account for the structure and    dynamics of the underlying system. Furthermore, we provide a systematic framework for determining the reliability of  different measures, including the use of logical consistency, computational efficiency, and experimental feasibility as criteria for  evaluation. Finally, we highlight some recent advancements in the  field, including the  development of new measures and  the  application of  machine  learning techniques to improve the accuracy and efficiency of quantum  correlation measurements.  Overall, this paper provides a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners in  the field  of quantum  information  science, offering insights into the criteria  that should guide the selection and evaluation  of measures of quantum correlations.

The paper presents a novel approach for liver and tumor segmentation from CT volumes using a hybrid densely connected UNet architecture, called H-DenseUNet. The proposed architecture combines the advantages of both densely connected networks and UNet, resulting in improved segmentation accuracy. The H-DenseUNet model consists of an encoder-decoder structure with skip connections and dense blocks, which enable efficient feature extraction and information propagation. The authors evaluate the performance of H-DenseUNet on a publicly available liver tumor segmentation dataset and compare it with other state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate that H-DenseUNet achieves superior segmentation accuracy and outperforms existing methods in terms of Dice similarity coefficient and mean surface distance. The proposed H-DenseUNet architecture shows great potential for accurate liver and tumor segmentation in clinical applications.

This paper considers how to separate text and/or graphics from smooth
background in screen content and mixed document images and proposes two
approaches to perform this segmentation task. The proposed methods make use of
the fact that the background in each block is usually smoothly varying and can
be modeled well by a linear combination of a few smoothly varying basis
functions, while the foreground text and graphics create sharp discontinuity. The algorithms separate the background and foreground pixels by trying to fit
background pixel values in the block into a smooth function using two different
schemes. 

One is based on robust regression, where the inlier pixels will be
considered as background, while remaining outlier pixels will be considered
foreground. The second approach uses a sparse decomposition framework where the
background and foreground layers are modeled with a smooth and sparse
components respectively. 

These algorithms have been tested on images extracted
from HEVC standard test sequences for screen content coding, and are shown to
have superior performance over previous approaches. 

The proposed methods can be
used in different applications such as text extraction, separate coding of
background and foreground for compression of screen content, and medical image
segmentation.

Image segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision and image processing. Cellular  Automata (CA) have been widely  used for various applications  due to their simplicity and parallel processing capabilities. In this paper, we propose a novel  approach  for image segmentation using CA. Our method  leverages the self-organization and emergent behavior of CA to segment images  into regions with similar characteristics. We define a set of rules governing  the  behavior of  individual cells   in the CA, which are then applied  iteratively to update the state  of each cell based on its neighbors.  We demonstrate the effectiveness  of  our method through experiments on   a variety of   datasets,  comparing our   results with state-of-the-art  segmentation algorithms. Our approach  achieves competitive performance in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency, highlighting the potential of CA in image segmentation tasks.

The academic paper titled "Extended LTLvis Motion Planning interface  (Extended Technical Report)" presents an extended version of the LTLvis motion planning interface.  The extended version integrates  additional features  and improvements to enhance the usability  and efficiency  of the interface. The paper describes the design and  implementation   of the extended interface, including the integration  of advanced visualization techniques, improved user  interaction mechanisms, and  enhanced performance. The paper  also presents experimental results and evaluations that demonstrate  the effectiveness and  benefits of   the   extended interface. Overall, this paper  provides valuable insights and contributions to the field of motion planning interfaces, highlighting the potential of the extended  LTLvis interface in various applications and domains.

This paper presents a  macroscopic acousto-mechanical analogy of a  microbubble,  which  is a small gas-filled cavity   in a liquid medium. The analogy is based on the assumption that the  microbubble can be  treated as a linear  elastic material with a compressibility  that depends on the bubble's size  and  the surrounding liquid  properties. The analogy is  derived by considering  the equations   of motion for  the microbubble  and the surrounding liquid, and  then  applying a perturbation analysis  to obtain a simplified set of equations that describe the bubble's  behavior. The resulting equations are similar to those used to describe the motion of a macroscopic elastic material subjected to  an external  force. The analogy  is validated by  comparing the predicted  behavior of the microbubble with experimental  data obtained from ultrasound imaging. The results show  good  agreement between the predicted and observed behavior, indicating that the macroscopic acousto-mechanical  analogy is a useful tool for understanding and predicting the behavior of microbubbles in a liquid medium.

Medical Image Segmentation is a  crucial task in medical imaging analysis, aiding in  the diagnosis and treatment of various   diseases. In recent years, deep learning  models have  shown great  potential in automating  this process. In this paper, we  present a  novel approach called the Medical Transformer, which incorporates a gated axial-attention  mechanism  for medical  image segmentation. Our model takes advantage of the spatial and channel-wise relationships  present in medical images, allowing for better feature extraction and understanding. We demonstrate the effectiveness  of our  approach on three different medical imaging  datasets, achieving state-of-the-art results in liver, brain, and prostate segmentation tasks. The Medical Transformer not only  outperforms  existing models but also achieves superior  generalization across datasets. This work highlights the potential of  incorporating advanced  attention  mechanisms  in medical image segmentation tasks and paves the way   for  improved automated analysis in medical  imaging.

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions. Traditional methods for image segmentation often rely on strong shape priors, which require accurate prior knowledge about the shape of the objects in the image. However, obtaining such priors can be challenging and time-consuming. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for image segmentation using weak shape priors. Our method leverages a combination of weak shape priors and deep learning techniques to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on various benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results show that our method outperforms existing approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. Overall, our work contributes to the development of image segmentation techniques that can be applied in real-world scenarios where strong shape priors are not readily available.

Although lower hybrid waves are effective at driving currents in present-day
tokamaks, they are expected to interact strongly with high-energy particles in
extrapolating to reactors. In the presence of a radial alpha particle birth
gradient, this interaction can take the form of wave amplification rather than
damping. While it is known that this amplification more easily occurs when
launching from the tokamak high-field side, the extent of this amplification
has not been made quantitative. Here, by tracing rays launched from the high-
field-side of a tokamak, the required radial gradients to achieve amplification
are calculated for a temperature and density regime consistent with a
hot-ion-mode fusion reactor. These simulations, while valid only in the linear
regime of wave amplification, nonetheless illustrate the possibilities for wave
amplification using high-field launch of the lower hybrid wave.

This paper proposes a novel Bayesian dense inverse searching algorithm for real-time stereo matching in minimally invasive surgery. Minimally invasive surgery is a complex and challenging domain where accurate depth information is crucial. Traditional stereo matching algorithms often struggle in this context due to limited texture and frequent occlusions. The proposed algorithm utilizes a Bayesian framework to estimate the disparity map, taking into account prior knowledge about the surgical scene. Experimental results on a dataset of minimally invasive surgery images demonstrate the superior performance of the algorithm compared to state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, the proposed algorithm is computationally efficient, making it well-suited for real-time applications in surgical robotics.

The possibility for controlling the Probe-field Optical gain and absorption
switching and photon conversion by a surface-plasmon-polariton near field is
explored for a quantum dot above the surface of a metal. In Contrast to the
linear response in the weak-coupling regime, the calculated spectra show an
induced Optical gain and a triply-split spontaneous emission peak resulting
from the interference between the Surface-plasmon field and the probe or
self-emitted light field in such a strongly-coupled nonlinear system. Our
result on the control of the mediated photon-photon interaction, very similar
to the `gate' control in an optical transistor, may be experimentally
observable and applied to ultra-fast intrachip/interchip optical interconnects,
improvement in the performance Of fiber-optic communication networks and
developments of optical digital computers and quantum communications.

Open Courses gathers thousands of people for a few weeks or months, with the openness and scale of MOOCs being a means of enhancing the learning and the comprehension of others. We use two instances of a popular course in strategy, using the data from the network to construct a ‘significant’ network of inter-communication, and then use complex network analysis to determine the potential of the course for communication and dissemination. We find that different topics and different pedagogical practices lead to varying degrees of 1) ‘significant’ peer-to-peer involvement, 2) ‘inclusive’ participation and 3) information dissemination, resulting in a less “global” exchange of knowledge and learning. We conclude by analyzing how these insights can lead to new developments in open courses.

The latest advances in  computer-assisted precision medicine are making it
feasible  to move from population-wide models that are  useful to discover
aggregate patterns  that hold for group-based analysis  to patient-specific
models that can drive patient-specific decisions with regard to treatment
choices, and  predictions of outcomes of treatment. Body Composition is
recognized as an important driver and risk  factor for a wide variety of
diseases, as well as a predictor of individual patient-specific clinical
outcomes to treatment choices or surgical interventions. 3D  CT images are
routinely acquired in the oncological worklows and deliver accurate rendering
of  internal  anatomy  and therefore can be used  opportunistically  to assess the
amount of skeletal muscle and adipose tissue compartments. Powerful tools of
artificial intelligence such as  deep learning   are making  it feasible now  to
segment the entire 3D image and   generate accurate measurements of all  internal
anatomy. These  will enable the overcoming of the  severe bottleneck that existed
previously, namely, the need for  manual segmentation, which was prohibitive to
scale  to the hundreds of  2D axial slices  that made  up  a  3D volumetric image.
Automated  tools such as   presented here  will now enable harvesting  whole-body
measurements from 3D CT or MRI images, leading to a new era  of  discovery of the
drivers of various diseases based on  individual tissue, organ volume, shape,
and  functional status. These measurements were hitherto  unavailable thereby
limiting the field to a very small and limited subset.   These discoveries  and
the  potential  to perform individual  image  segmentation with high speed and
accuracy are  likely to lead to the  incorporation of these 3D measures into
individual specific treatment planning models related to nutrition,  aging,
chemotoxicity, surgery and survival after  the onset of a major disease  such as
cancer.

This paper presents a novel 4D light-field dataset and convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures for material recognition. The dataset consists of a large collection of light-field images captured from different viewpoints, allowing for the capture of both spatial and angular information. The CNN architectures are designed to effectively exploit the 4D nature of the dataset, enabling accurate material recognition. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed dataset and CNN architectures, achieving state-of-the-art performance on material recognition tasks. The 4D light-field dataset and CNN architectures presented in this paper provide valuable resources for advancing the field of material recognition and can be used for various applications such as object recognition, scene understanding, and augmented reality.

This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation using a contrario selection of optimal partitions. The proposed method aims to find the most suitable partition of an image by comparing it to a set of reference partitions. The selection process is based on a statistical analysis of the differences between the image and the reference partitions. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through experiments on various image datasets, showing improved segmentation results compared to existing methods. The proposed method has the potential to be applied in various fields such as computer vision and medical imaging.

In this academic paper, we introduce a new class of generalized Einstein-Scalar-Maxwell theories that are formulated in a globally consistent manner. We investigate the physical implications and mathematical properties of these theories, including the existence of solutions and the behavior of the fields. We show that these theories provide a unified framework for describing various physical phenomena, such as black holes and electromagnetic waves, and we discuss the potential applications of these theories in different areas of physics. Overall, our findings contribute to a better understanding of the fundamental principles underlying Einstein-Scalar-Maxwell theories and pave the way for further research in this field.

This paper provides    an  introduction to second   law-like inequalities with quantum  relative entropy. The second law of thermodynamics is  a fundamental principle in physics that states that the  entropy of  an isolated system always  increases over time. In the quantum realm, the concept  of entropy is extended to  quantum relative entropy, which  measures the distinguishability  between two quantum states.  The paper explores  the  mathematical framework of quantum  relative entropy  and its connection to  the second law of thermodynamics. It discusses various inequalities derived from quantum  relative entropy that resemble the second  law, and provides examples and applications of  these inequalities in quantum information theory and statistical  mechanics. The paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of second law-like inequalities with quantum relative  entropy and their significance in the field of quantum thermodynamics.

We know that the category of co-modules of a flat Hopf algebra is abelian, but generally lacks enough projectives. In this short paper we prove that the category of connective-graded co-modules over a connective-graded, flat, finite-dimensional Hopf algebra is abelian and has enough projectives. In particular, we prove that the categories of connective-graded co-modules over the Hopf algebras of the complex bordism, Brown-Peterson and classical mod-p homology all have this property. We also prove that the category of connective-graded co-modules over the appropriate Hopf algebras is not equivalent to the category of connective-graded co-modules over a ring.

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental  task in computer vision that involves assigning a semantic label to each pixel in  an image. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for semantic segmentation using a highly  fused convolutional network (HFCN) and  multiple  soft  cost functions. Our HFCN  architecture combines  the strengths of both  encoder-decoder  and skip-connection based methods, resulting in improved performance. We incorporate multiple soft cost functions, including cross-entropy loss, boundary loss,  and region  loss, which help  to capture different aspects of  the segmentation problem. Our  experimental results on various  benchmark datasets demonstrate   that our proposed approach outperforms several state-of-the-art methods in  terms  of segmentation accuracy. Furthermore, we conduct ablation  studies to analyze the effectiveness of  our HFCN architecture and the impact  of   different soft cost functions. Overall, our method achieves competitive performance and provides valuable insights   into the task of semantic segmentation.

Semantic  segmentation  is a crucial task in computer  vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in    an image. Real-time semantic segmentation  is particularly challenging due to the need  for  fast and accurate processing. In this paper, we propose a light-weight version of the RefineNet architecture for real-time semantic segmentation.  Our approach achieves comparable performance  to the original RefineNet while  significantly  reducing the computational complexity. We evaluate our model   on  several  benchmark datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness in real-time applications.  Our results show that the  proposed light-weight RefineNet is a promising solution for real-time semantic segmentation tasks.

In this paper, we propose a protocol for the remote transfer of Gaussian quantum discord, a measure of quantum correlations, between two distant parties connected by a quantum channel. We show that it is possible to remotely generate and transfer Gaussian quantum discord by applying local operations and classical communication at both ends of the channel. We derive the conditions under which the transfer can be achieved and analyze the role of different parameters such as the channel transmissivity and the quantum noise. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of remote transfer of quantum discord and provide insights into the dynamics of quantum correlations in the presence of noise. This work has potential applications in quantum communication and information processing tasks that rely on quantum correlations.

Pixelwise segmentation of the left ventricular (LV) myocardium and the four
cardiac chambers in 2-D steady state free precession (SSFP) cine sequences is
an essential preprocessing step for a wide Range of analyses. Variability in
contrast, appearance, orientation, and placement of the heart between patients,
clinical views, scanners, and protocols makes fully automatic semantic
segmentation a notoriously difficult problem. Here, we present ${\Omega}$-Net
(Omega-Net): a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture for
simultaneous localization, transformation into a canonical orientation, and
semantic segmentation. First, an initial segmentation is performed on the Input
image, second, the features learned during this initial segmentation are used
to predict The parameters needed to transform the input image into a canonical
orientation, and third, a final segmentation is performed on the transformed
image. In this work, ${\Omega}$-Nets of varying depths were trained to detect
five foreground classes in any of three clinical views (short axis, SA,
four-chamber, 4C, two-chamber, 2C), without prior knowledge of the view being
segmented. The architecture was trained on A cohort Of patients with
hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and Healthy control subjects. network performance
as measured by Weighted foreground intersection-over-union (IoU) Was
substantially improved in the best-performing ${\Omega}$- Net compared with
U-Net segmentation without localization or orientation. In addition,
{\Omega}-Net was retrained from scratch on the 2017 MICCAI ACDC dataset, and
achieves state-of-the-art results On the LV and RV bloodpools, and performed
slightly worse In Segmentation of the LV myocardium. We conclude this
architecture represents a substantive advancement over prior approaches, with
implications for biomedical image segmentation more generally.

Currently, developments of deep learning techniques are providing
instrumental to identify, classify, and quantify patterns in medical images.
Segmentation is one of the important applications in medical image analysis. In
this regard, U-Net is the predominant approach to medical image segmentation
tasks. However, we found that those U-Net based models have limitations in
several aspects, for example, millions of parameters in the U-Net consuming
considerable computation resource and memory, lack of global information, and
missing some tough objects. Therefore, we applied two modifications to improve
the U-Net model: 1) designed and added the dilated channel-wise CNN module, 2)
simplified the U shape network. Based on these two modifications, we proposed a
novel light-weight architecture -- Channel-wise Feature Pyramid Network for
Medicine (CFPNet-M). To evaluate our method, we selected five datasets with
different modalities: thermography, electron microscopy, endoscopy, dermoscopy,
and digital retinal images. And we compared its performance with several models
having different parameter scales. This paper also involves our previous
studies of DC-UNet and some commonly used light-weight neural networks. We
applied the Tanimoto similarity instead of the Jaccard index for gray-level
image measurements. By comparsion, CFPNet-M achieves comparable segmentation
results on all five medical datasets with only 0.65 million parameters, which
is about 2% of U-Net, and 8.8 MB memory. Meanwhile, the inference speed can
reach 80 FPS on a single RTX 2070Ti GPU with the 256 by 192 pixels input size.

We tackle biomedical image segmentation in the scenario of only a few labeled
brain MR images. This is an important and challenging task in medical
applications, where manual annotations are time-consuming. Current multi-atlas
based segmentation methods use image registration to warp segments from labeled
images onto a new scan. In a different paradigm, supervised learning-based
segmentation strategies have gained popularity. These method consistently use
relatively large sets of labeled training data, and their behavior in the
regime of a few labeled biomedical images has not been thoroughly evaluated. In
this work, we provide two important results for segmentation in the scenario
where few labeled images are available. First, we propose a straightforward
implementation of efficient semi-supervised learning-based registration method,
which we showcase in a multi-atlas segmentation framework. Second, through an
extensive empirical study, we evaluate the performance of a supervised
segmentation approach, where the training images are augmented via random
deformations. Surprisingly, we find that in both paradigms, accurate
segmentation is generally possible even in the context of few labeled images.

In this paper, we investigate the phenomena of directional infrared emission resulting from cascade population inversion and four-wave mixing in Rb vapours. We demonstrate that by carefully controlling the pumping parameters, such as the power and frequency, it is possible to achieve a significant population inversion between the upper and lower energy levels of the Rb atom, leading to the emission of infrared radiation in a specific direction. We also explore the role of four-wave mixing in enhancing the directional emission and discuss the underlying physical mechanisms. This study provides valuable insights into the fundamental processes underlying the emission of infrared radiation in Rb vapours and has potential applications in areas such as laser technology and spectroscopy.

We present  a new test when there is  a nuisance parameter under the
alternative hypothesis.  The test exploits the p-value  occupation time [PVOT],
the measure  of  the nuisance  parameter  subset on which a p-value test based on a
a test statistic rejects the null hypothesis. Key contributions are: (i) An
asymptotic critical value  upper bound for our test is the significance level
{\alpha}, making inference easy.  (ii) We only require  the test statistic to
have a known or bootstrappable  limit distribution, hence we do  not  require
root(n)-Gaussian asymptotics,  allowing  for weak or non-identification, boundary
values, heavy tails, infill asymptotics, and so on. (iii)  A test  based on the
sup-p-value  may be conservative and  in some  cases have trivial power, while the
PVOT naturally  controls for this by smoothing over the nuisance parameter
space. Finally,  (iv)  the  PVOT uniquely allows for bootstrap inference  in the
presence of nuisance parameters when some  estimated parameters may not   be
identified.

The paper presents a coherent-state approach for the Majorana representation, which is a mathematical tool used  to describe quantum states of a  system. The authors propose a method  to construct  coherent  states in the Majorana   representation  and derive their properties. They also discuss the application of these coherent states in the study of  quantum systems, such as  the calculation of expectation values and  the description of quantum dynamics. The results  obtained using the coherent-state approach are  compared with those  obtained using other  methods, demonstrating the effectiveness  and usefulness of  this  approach. Overall,  the paper provides a  comprehensive and   detailed analysis of the coherent-state approach for the Majorana representation and its applications in quantum physics.

All quantum gates with one and two qubits may be described by elements of
$Spin$ groups due to isomorphisms $Spin(3) \simeq SU(2)$ and $Spin(6) \simeq
SU(4)$. However, the group of $n$-qubit gates $SU(2^n)$ for $n > 2$ has bigger
dimension than $Spin(3n)$. A quantum circuit with one- and two-qubit gates may
be used for construction of arbitrary unitary transformation $SU(2^n)$.
Analogously, the `$Spin(3n)$ circuits' are introduced in this work as products
of elements associated with one- and two-qubit gates with respect to the
above-mentioned isomorphisms.
  The matrix tensor product implementation of the $Spin(3n)$ group together
with relevant models by usual quantum circuits with $2n$ qubits are
investigated in such a framework. A certain resemblance with well-known sets of
non-universal quantum gates e.g., matchgates, noninteracting-fermion quantum
circuits) related with $Spin(2n)$ may be found in presented approach. Finally,
a possibility of the classical simulation of such circuits in polynomial time
is discussed.

Objective: Deformable image registration is A fundamental problem in medical
image analysis, with applications such as longitudinal studies, population
modeling, and atlas based Image segmentation. Registration is often phrased as
an Optimization problem, i.e., finding a deformation field that is optimal
according to a given objective function. Discrete, combinatorial, optimization
techniques have successfully been Employed to solve the resulting optimization
problem. Specifically, optimization based on $\alpha$-expansion with minimal
graph cuts has been proposed as a powerful tool for image registration. The
high computational cost of the graph-cut based optimization approach, however,
limits the utility of this approach for registration of large volume images.
Methods: Here, we propose to accelerate graph-cut based deformable registration
by dividing the image Into overlapping sub-regions and restricting the
$\alpha$-expansion moves to a single sub-region at a time. Results: We
demonstrate empirically that this approach can achieve a large reduction in
computation time -- from days to minutes -- with only a Small penalty in terms
of solution quality. Conclusion: The reduction in Computation Time provided by
the proposed Method makes graph cut based deformable registration viable for
large volume images. Significance: Graph cut based image registration has
previously been shown to produce excellent results, but the high computational
cost has hindered the adoption of the method for registration of Large medical
volume images. Our proposed method Lifts this restriction, requiring only a
small fraction of the computational cost to produce results of comparable
quality.

This paper investigates the low-frequency 1/f noise in MoS2 thin-film transistors (TFTs) by comparing single and multilayer structures. The authors fabricated MoS2 TFTs with different numbers of layers and measured their electrical characteristics and noise spectra. They found that the single-layer MoS2 TFTs exhibited lower 1/f noise compared to the multilayer structures. The authors also analyzed the noise sources and proposed a model to explain the observed behavior. This study provides valuable insights into the noise characteristics of MoS2 TFTs and offers guidance for optimizing their performance in various applications.

This paper explores  the Seiberg-Witten geometry of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ quiver  gauge theories. The Seiberg-Witten theory is  a powerful tool  for  studying the dynamics of gauge theories, and it has been extensively studied in  the  context  of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetric gauge theories. In  this paper, we focus on quiver gauge theories, which are a class  of gauge theories  with multiple  gauge groups and  matter   fields. We study  the moduli   space of vacua of  these theories and the associated Seiberg-Witten curves. We also investigate the behavior of the gauge coupling constants and  the BPS  spectrum of these theories.  Our results provide new insights into the geometric properties of quiver gauge theories and their relation to  the Seiberg-Witten theory.

This paper presents a novel approach for semantic    segmentation of 3D magnetic resonance (MR) images using a holistic decomposition convolution  (HDC)  method.   The proposed method aims to address the challenges of accurately segmenting  complex  anatomical structures in MR images by decomposing  the  input  image into multiple  scales and capturing both local and global contextual information. The HDC method  combines a  multi-scale feature  extraction module with a holistic decomposition module, which effectively captures the hierarchical structure of  the  input image. Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that the proposed  HDC method outperforms state-of-the-art  methods  in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.   The  findings  of this study suggest that  the HDC method has the potential  to improve the accuracy and efficiency of semantic segmentation in 3D MR images, which can have  significant implications for clinical applications such as tumor detection and treatment planning.

This paper examines the concept of time directionality in classical and quantum physics. It explores various theories and frameworks within these disciplines that discuss the arrow of time and its relation to the forward movement of events. The paper presents an overview of classical physics' understanding of time directionality and discusses how the laws of thermodynamics play a crucial role in determining it. Furthermore, the paper delves into the quantum realm, analyzing the implications of quantum mechanics on time directionality. It investigates how phenomena such as wavefunction collapse, entropy, and the nature of time in quantum gravity theories can affect the arrow of time in the quantum realm. Through this analysis, the paper aims to contribute to the ongoing debate about the fundamental nature of time directionality in physics and its relationship with classical and quantum theories.

In medical  image analysis,  multi-organ segmentation is a crucial task for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. However, it is often challenging due  to the imbalance between input and output data. In this paper, we propose a novel loss function called Combo Loss, which addresses this  imbalance by   considering both input  and output data. The  Combo Loss combines two components: the Dice  Loss,  which evaluates  the similarity between the predicted and ground truth  segmentations,  and the Focal Loss, which focuses on hard-to-segment regions. We conducted experiments on multiple organ  segmentation  datasets and compared the performance  of  Combo  Loss with several state-of-the-art methods. The  results demonstrate that the  Combo Loss outperforms  other approaches, especially in scenarios with  significant input and output  imbalance. Therefore, the proposed  Combo Loss could potentially  improve the accuracy and  robustness of multi-organ segmentation  algorithms in medical  image analysis.

what is aging? Mechanistic answers to this question remain Elusive despite
decades of research. Here, we propose a mathematical model of cellular aging
based on a model gene interaction network. Our network model is made of only
non-aging components - the Biological functions of gene interactions decrease
with a constant mortality rate. Death of A cell occurs in the model when an
essential Gene loses all of its interactions to other genes, equivalent to the
deletion of an essential gene. Gene interactions Are stochastic based on a
binomial distribution. We Show that the defining characteristic of biological
aging, the exponential increase of mortality rate over time, can arise from
this gene network model during The early stage of aging. Hence, we demonstrate
that cellular aging is an emergent property of this model network. Our model
predicts that the rate of aging, defined by the Gompertz coefficient, is
approximately proportional to the average Number of active interactions per
gene and that the stochastic heterogeneity of gene interactions is an important
factor in the dynamics of the aging process. This theoretic framework offers a
mechanistic foundation for the pleiotropic nature of aging and can provide
insights on cellular aging.

We study the 3-algebraic structure involved in the previously shown M2-branes
worldvolume gauge theories. We first extend an arbitrary finite dimensional
3-algebra into an infinite dimensional 3-algebra by introducing a mode number to
each generator. A special central charge in the geometry of gauge transformations
appears naturally in this extension. We present an infinite dimensional
extended 3-algebra with a general metric and also a different extension with a
Lorentzian metric. We then study ordinary finite dimensional 3-algebras with
various signatures of the metric, concentrating on the cases with a positive
tensor and the cases with a zero tensor. In the latter cases we present
a new algebra, whose corresponding theory is a decoupled invariant gauge theory
together with a free theory with global gauge symmetry, and there is no
negative kinetic term from this algebra.

аffіnіtу mаtrіх fоr vіsіоn tаsks. Wе shоw thаt bу соnstruсtіng а rоw/соlumn

Medical image segmentation  is a  critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning. However, it is challenging due to the high variability and  complexity  of  medical images. In this  paper, we propose a novel approach for robust medical image  segmentation using cooperative training and latent  space data augmentation. Our method leverages the power of multiple  models  trained on different subsets  of the data to  improve segmentation accuracy. Additionally, we  introduce  a latent space data augmentation technique that generates realistic and diverse augmented samples to enhance the  generalization capability of  the  models. We  evaluate our approach on  a large dataset  of medical images and  compare it  with  state-of-the-art segmentation methods. The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves superior segmentation performance and  outperforms existing approaches  in terms  of accuracy and robustness. Our  findings suggest that cooperative training and latent space data augmentation can significantly improve the reliability and  effectiveness of medical  image segmentation algorithms.

This paper explores the concept of dynamical boson stars, which are compact objects composed of self-gravitating scalar fields. The authors investigate the dynamical behavior of these objects by solving the Einstein-Klein-Gordon equations numerically. They find that dynamical boson stars can exhibit a rich variety of behaviors, including oscillations, collapse, and fragmentation. The authors also study the stability of these objects and find that they can be stable over long timescales. This work has implications for understanding the formation and evolution of compact objects in the universe, such as black holes and neutron stars.

DatasetGAN is a novel approach to generating labeled datasets for machine learning tasks with minimal human effort. Traditional methods of dataset creation require extensive manual annotation, which is time-consuming and expensive. In this paper, we propose a generative adversarial network (GAN) based framework that can automatically generate labeled datasets by synthesizing realistic data samples. Our approach leverages the power of GANs to learn the underlying data distribution and generate new samples that are indistinguishable from real data. We also introduce a novel labeling mechanism that allows the GAN to generate labeled samples by conditioning the generator on class labels. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach can generate high-quality labeled datasets with minimal human effort, achieving comparable performance to manually annotated datasets. DatasetGAN has the potential to significantly reduce the cost and time required for dataset creation, making it a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in the field of machine learning.

We investigate the effect of Coulomb screening on the rates of nuclear reactions during linear coasting nucleosynthesis. By taking into account the screening of the Coulomb barrier due to the presence of electrons, we find that the reaction rates are significantly enhanced compared to previous calculations. This effect becomes more pronounced at higher temperatures and densities. We discuss the implications of these findings for the production of heavy elements in astrophysical environments such as supernovae and neutron star mergers. Our results suggest that Coulomb screening can play a crucial role in nucleosynthesis processes and should be taken into consideration in future studies.

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions. Traditional methods for image segmentation often rely on complex algorithms and large computational resources. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Compassionately Conservative Balanced Cuts (CCBC) for image segmentation. The CCBC method combines the principles of compassion and conservatism to achieve a balanced and accurate segmentation. We introduce a new objective function that takes into account both the similarity between pixels and the smoothness of the segmentation boundaries. We also propose a new optimization algorithm that efficiently solves the CCBC objective function. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the CCBC method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, we show that the CCBC method is robust to noise and can handle images with complex structures. Overall, our work provides a new perspective on image segmentation and offers a promising solution for practical applications in computer vision.

Τhе реrfоrmаnсе оf dеер nеtwоrks fоr sеmаntіс іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn lаrgеlу
dереnds оn thе аvаіlаbіlіtу оf lаrgе-sсаlе trаіnіng іmаgеs whісh аrе lаbеllеd
аt thе ріхеl lеvеl. Турісаllу, suсh ріхеl-lеvеl іmаgе lаbеllіngs аrе оbtаіnеd
mаnuаllу bу а lаbоur-іntеnsіvе рrосеss. То аllеvіаtе thе burdеn оf mаnuаl іmаgе
lаbеllіng, wе рrороsе аn іntеrеstіng lеаrnіng аррrоасh tо gеnеrаtе ріхеl-lеvеl
іmаgе lаbеllіngs аutоmаtісаllу. Α Guіdеd Fіltеr Νеtwоrk (GFΝ) іs fіrst
dеvеlореd tо lеаrn thе sеgmеntаtіоn knоwlеdgе frоm а sоurсе dоmаіn, аnd suсh
GFΝ thеn trаnsfеrs suсh sеgmеntаtіоn knоwlеdgе tо gеnеrаtе соаrsе оbjесt mаsks
іn thе tаrgеt dоmаіn. Suсh соаrsе оbjесt mаsks аrе trеаtеd аs рsеudо lаbеls аnd
thеу аrе furthеr іntеgrаtеd tо орtіmіzе/rеfіnе thе GFΝ іtеrаtіvеlу іn thе

оbjесt lаbеllіngs), whоsе quаlіtу іs vеrу соmраrаblе tо thе mаnuаllу-lаbеllеd
