іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn thаn mоst ехіstіng wеаklу-suреrvіsеd аррrоасhеs.

A strong visual object tracker nowadays relies on its well-crafted modules,
which typically consist of manually-designed network architectures to deliver
high-quality tracking results. Not surprisingly, the manual design process
becomes a particularly challenging barrier, as it demands sufficient prior
experience, enormous effort, intuition and perhaps some good luck. 

Meanwhile,
neural architecture search has gaining grounds in practical applications such
as image segmentation, as a promising method in tackling the issue of automated
search of feasible network structures. 

In this work, we propose a novel
cell-level differentiable architecture search mechanism to automate the network
design of the tracking module, aiming to adapt backbone features to the
objective of a tracking network during offline training. The proposed approach
is simple, efficient, and with no need to stack a series of modules to
construct a network. Our approach is easy to be incorporated into existing
trackers, which is empirically validated using different differentiable
architecture search-based methods and tracking objectives. 

Extensive
experimental evaluations demonstrate the superior performance of our approach
over five commonly-used benchmarks. Meanwhile, our automated searching process
takes 41 (18) hours for the second (first) order DARTS method on the
TrackingNet dataset.

Strategy improvement in combinatorial   games has been studied extensively in  the literature, however, the   complexity of finding strategy improvements for  a  specific type of  game called "All-switches" has not been well understood. In this paper, we investigate the  complexity  of finding strategy improvements in the All-switches  game. We show that the  problem is  NP-complete, even for simple variants  of the game. Furthermore, we analyze  the complexity of  the problem under different restrictions on the input, such as the number of switches and the size of the game board. Our results provide insights  into the difficulty of finding strategy  improvements  in the All-switches  game and provide a foundation for further research  in this area.

Let $M$ be a compact $n$-manifold of $\operatorname{Ric}_M\ge (n-1)H$ ($H$ is
a constant). We are concerned with following space form rigidity: $M$ is
isometric to a space form of constant curvature $H$ under either of the
following conditions:
  (i) There is $\rho>0$ such that for any $x\in M$, open $\rho$-ball at
$x^*$ in the (local) Riemannian universal covering space, $(U^*_\rho,x^*)\to
(B_\rho(x),x)$, has the maximal volume i.e., volume of a $\rho$-ball in the
simply connected $n$-space form of curvature $H$.
  (ii) For $H=-1$, volume entropy of $M$ is maximal i.e. $n-1$ ([LW1]).
  The main results of this paper are quantitative space form rigidity i.e.,
statements that $M$ is diffeomorphic and close in the Gromov-Hausdorff topology
to space form of constant curvature $H$, if $M$ almost satisfies, under some
additional condition, above maximal volume condition. For $H=1$, the
quantitative spherical space form rigidity improves and generalizes the
diffeomorphic sphere theorem in [CC2].

This paper describes a computational model, called the Dirichlet process
Gaussian mixture model with latent joints (DPGMM-LJ), that can find latent tree
structure embedded in data distribution in an unsupervised manner. By combining
DPGMM-LJ and a pre-existing body map formation method, we propose a method that
enables an agent having multi-link body structure to discover Its kinematic
structure, i.e., body schema, from tactile information alone. The DPGMM-LJ is a
probabilistic model Based on Bayesian nonparametrics and an extension of
Dirichlet process Gaussian mixture model (dPGMM). In a simulation experiment,
we Used a simple fetus model that had Five body parts and performed structured
random movements In a womb-like environment. It was shown that the method could
Estimate the number of body parts and kinematic structures without any
pre-existing knowledge in many cases. Another experiment showed that the degree
of motor coordination in random movements affects the result of body schema
formation strongly. It is confirmed that the accuracy Rate for body schema
estimation had the highest value 84.6% when the ratio of motor coordination was
0.9 in our setting. These results suggest That kinematic structure Can be
estimated from tactile information obtained by a fetus moving randomly in a
womb without any visual information even though its accuracy was not so high.
They also suggest that a certain degree of motor coordination in random
movements and the sufficient Dimension of state space that represents the body
map are important to Estimate body schema correctly.

This academic paper presents a  novel  approach for the extraction of face masks in  video sequences. Face    masks are   crucial in various computer vision  tasks, such as  face  recognition and expression analysis. The  proposed  method utilizes  a combination of deep learning  techniques  and traditional image processing algorithms to accurately extract face masks from video frames. First, a deep neural network  is trained to detect and localize facial features. Then, a series  of image processing techniques, including edge detection and segmentation, are applied to refine the extracted  face  regions.  The proposed approach  is evaluated  on a large dataset  and compared  with existing  face mask extraction methods. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of accuracy and robustness. This paper provides valuable insights into the  field of  face mask extraction in video sequences and offers a promising solution  for various computer vision applications.

This paper explores the relationship between coloured gravity and electromagnetism. It begins by introducing the concept of coloured gravity and its theoretical framework. The paper then examines the similarities and differences between coloured gravity and electromagnetism, highlighting the potential for a unified theory that incorporates both phenomena. The authors propose a mathematical model that describes the interaction between coloured gravity and electromagnetism, and discuss the implications of this model for our understanding of the fundamental forces of nature. The paper concludes by suggesting avenues for future research in this area.

Medical images are often accompanied by metadata describing the image
(vendor, acquisition parameters) and the patient (disease type or severity,
demographics, genomics). This metadata is usually disregarded by image
segmentation methods. In this work, we adapt a linear conditioning method
called FiLM (Feature-wise Linear Modulation) for image segmentation tasks. This
FiLM adaptation enables integrating metadata into segmentation models for
better performance. We observed an average Dice score increase of 5.1% on
spinal cord tumor segmentation when incorporating the tumor type with FiLM. The
metadata modulates the segmentation process through low-cost affine
transformations applied on feature maps which can be included in any neural
network's architecture. Additionally, we assess the relevance of segmentation
FiLM layers for tackling common challenges in medical imaging: multi-class
training with missing segmentations, model adaptation to multiple tasks, and
training with a limited or unbalanced number of annotated data. Our results
demonstrated the following benefits of FiLM for segmentation: FiLMed U-Net was
robust to missing labels and reached higher Dice scores with few labels (up to
16.7%) compared to single-task U-Net. The code is open-source and available at
www.ivadomed.org.

This paper formulates an inverse energy flow problem which is to assume a nodal
admittance matrix (hence the network structure of a power system) from voltage
and current phasors measured at a number of buses. We show that the admittance
matrix can be uniquely determined from a sequence of measurements corresponding
to certain steady states when each node in the system is fitted with a
measurement apparatus, and a Kron-reduced admittance matrix can be measured only
if some nodes in the system are not monitored (hidden nodes). Instead, we
propose effective algorithms based on graph theory to find the actual
admittance matrix of radial networks with hidden vertices. We offer mathematical
guarantees for the recovered admittance matrix and conclude that the actual
admittance matrix can be completely recovered only from the Kron-reduced admittance
matrix under some mild assumptions. Simulations on standard test systems
verify that these algorithms are incapable of obtaining precise estimates of
the admittance matrix from noisy sensor data.

This paper presents a robust output regulation framework for continuous-time periodic systems. The proposed approach is based on the internal model principle and uses a dynamic output feedback controller to achieve robust regulation of the system's output. The controller is designed to handle uncertainties and disturbances in the system dynamics and to ensure robustness against external disturbances. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through numerical simulations on a benchmark example. The results show that the controller is able to achieve robust output regulation even in the presence of uncertainties and disturbances. Overall, the paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of robust control for continuous-time periodic systems.

The task of image segmentation is necessarily accompanied by noise due to the uncertainties as to the exact location of the boundaries between the anatomical structures. We argue that this information can be derived at no extra cost from the expert annotations, and when included in the training of neural networks it may allow a better calibration of probabilistic predictions and the real uncertainty. The concept of label smoothing (LS), where the neural network is trained on a “blurred” version of the ground truth labels, has been shown to be effective in adjusting the output predictions. But since LS is blind to the local structure of the image, it can produce over-smoothed and under-confidenced predictions even in the case of a genuinely unambiguous input. In this paper we propose spatially varying label smoothing (SVLS), a “soft labeling” technique which takes local structure into account. This technique is ideally suited to the incorporation of inter-annotator differences when multiple annotations are available. The proposed method has been tested on four different clinical image segmentation tasks of varying complexity, with different modalities, number of classes, and single and multiple expert annotations. The results demonstrate that despite its simplicity SVLS yields superior boundary predictions with improved calibration of uncertainty and model calibration.

This paper presents a method for disaggregating Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) Level 3 (L3) brightness temperatures to a finer spatial resolution of 9km using kernel machines. The proposed method utilizes a training dataset consisting of high-resolution brightness temperatures and corresponding low-resolution SMAP L3 brightness temperatures. The kernel machines are trained to learn the relationship between the high-resolution and low-resolution data, and then used to predict the high-resolution brightness temperatures for the entire SMAP L3 dataset. The results show that the proposed method achieves a high level of accuracy in disaggregating the SMAP L3 brightness temperatures, with a mean absolute error of less than 1K. This method has the potential to improve the spatial resolution of SMAP L3 data, enabling more accurate monitoring and analysis of soil moisture at a finer scale.

This paper presents a stable multiscale Petrov-Galerkin finite element method for high frequency acoustic scattering problems. The method combines a coarse-scale finite element approximation with a fine-scale Petrov-Galerkin correction to accurately capture the high frequency behavior of the solution. The stability of the method is ensured by using a multiscale stabilization technique that accounts for the interaction between the coarse and fine scales. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the method in accurately computing the scattered field for a range of high frequency scattering problems. The proposed method provides a robust and efficient approach for solving high frequency acoustic scattering problems.

In microscopic mechanical systems interactions between elastic structures are
often mediated by the hydrodynamics of a solvent fluid. At microscopic scales
the elastic structures are also subject to thermal fluctuations. Stochastic
numerical methods are developed based on multigrid which allow for the
efficient computation of both the hydrodynamic interactions in the presence of
walls and the thermal fluctuations. The presented stochastic multigrid approach
provides efficient real-space numerical methods for generating the required
stochastic driving fields with long-range correlations consistent with
statistical mechanics. The presented approach also allows for the use of
spatially adaptive meshes in resolving the hydrodynamic interactions. Numerical
results are presented which show the methods perform in practise with a
computational complexity of O(N log(N)).

This is an active contour method for image segmentation based on the use of shape templates. The shape templates are subjected to a restricted affine transformation (RAT) in order to determine the contour of the object of interest. The RAT provides five degrees of freedom: translation, rotation and scaling. The contours of the object are separated into an inner and an outer, both closed and concentric. The active contour energy is a contrast function, calculated from the intensities of the voxels lying within the inner contour and in the annulus between the inner and outer contours. We show that the contrast energy is a minimum under some conditions. The optimum RAT parameters are calculated by minimizing the contrast energy with a gradient-descent optimizer. We show that this is efficient using Green’s theorem. This method is able to deal with a wide variety of shapes because, for a given template, the optimization is done only for the RAT parameters. The method has been tested on many images to show its robustness to Gaussian and Poisson noise, to initialization, and to a partial lack of detail in the object to be segmented.

In this paper, we study the most basic domination invariants in graphs, in
which number 2 is intrinsic part of their definitions. We classify them upon
three criteria, two of which give the following previously studied invariants:
the weak $2$-domination number, $\gamma_{w2}(G)$, the $2$-domination number,
$\gamma_2(G)$, the $\{2\}$-domination number, $\gamma_{\{2\}}(G)$, the double
domination number, $\gamma_{\times 2}(G)$, the total $\{2\}$-domination number,
$\gamma_{t\{2\}}(G)$, and the total double domination number, $\gamma_{t\times
2}(G)$, where $G$ is a graph in which a corresponding invariant is well
defined. The third criterion yields rainbow versions of the mentioned six
parametres, one of which has already been well studied, and three other give
new interesting parametres. Together with a special, extensively studied Roman
domination, $\gamma_R(G)$, and two classical parametres, the domination number,
$\gamma(G)$, and the total domination number, $\gamma_t(G)$, we consider 13
domination invariants in graphs $G$. In the main result of the paper we present
sharp upper and lower bounds of each of the invariants in terms of every other
invariant, large majority of which are new results proven in this paper. As a
consequence of the main theorem we obtain some complexity results for the
studied invariants, in particular regarding the existence of approximation
algorithms and inapproximability bounds.

Salient object detection is a fundamental task in computer vision that aims to identify the most visually significant objects in an image. In recent years, deep neural networks have shown promising results in this field. However, most existing models focus on single-task saliency detection and do not fully exploit the potential of multi-task learning. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-task deep neural network model, called DeepSaliency, for salient object detection. Our model simultaneously learns to predict saliency maps and perform related tasks such as object segmentation and edge detection. We introduce a shared encoder-decoder architecture that enables the model to leverage shared representations across tasks, leading to improved performance. We also propose a novel loss function that combines task-specific and shared losses to guide the learning process. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our DeepSaliency model outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. Furthermore, ablation studies and qualitative analysis provide insights into the effectiveness of our proposed model. Overall, our work contributes to the advancement of salient object detection by leveraging the power of multi-task learning and deep neural networks.

The paper introduces a deep grouping model for unified perceptual parsing, which aims to parse complex scenes into coherent groups. The proposed model utilizes a deep neural network architecture to capture hierarchical relationships within the scene and assign object labels to different regions. It combines bottom-up grouping and top-down object hypotheses to achieve accurate scene understanding. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model on various tasks including object segmentation and scene parsing. The model outperforms state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets, showcasing its potential for real-world applications in computer vision and image understanding.

In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called Contextual Hourglass Networks (CHN) for the tasks of image segmentation and density estimation. Our method leverages the benefits of both fully convolutional networks and hourglass networks by incorporating contextual information at multiple scales. The CHN is designed to capture rich contextual information by employing multiple parallel branches, where each branch processes the input image at a different scale. Additionally, we introduce a strategic skip connection mechanism to enable information flow across different branches. We evaluate our method on various benchmark datasets and compare it to state-of-the-art methods. Our results demonstrate that the CHN achieves high accuracy and performs favorably against alternative approaches. Overall, our proposed architecture provides an effective solution for both image segmentation and density estimation tasks.

Chemically accurate and systematic analyses of the virtual space of all
possible particles are greatly restricted by the computational cost of quantum
chemistry. We introduce a composite approach that adds machine learning
corrections to computationally efficient approximate legacy quantum methods.
After training, very realistic predictions of enthalpies, free energies,
entropies, and electron correlation energies are possible, for slightly
smaller molecular sets than intended for training. For thermochemical properties of
up to 16k constitutional isomers of H$_7$O$_{10}$O$_2$ we present numerical
proof that chemical accuracy can be attained. We only predict atomic
correlation energy in post Hartree-Fock methods, at the computational expense of
Hartree-Fock, and we obtain a quantitative relation between molecular
entropy and electron correlation. The transferability of our method is
achieved, using semi-empirical quantum biology and machine learning
models trained on 1 and 10\% of 134k organic atoms, to reproduce enthalpies
of all remaining atoms at density functional theory level of accuracy.

This paper presents a novel approach to unsupervised semantic image segmentation using a  combination of StyleGAN and CLIP. StyleGAN is   a  state-of-the-art generative model that can generate high-quality images, while CLIP is a powerful image-text embedding  model that can  understand  the content of  images.  By combining these two models,  we propose a method that can  segment images  into  semantically meaningful regions without the need for any labeled training data.  Our approach leverages the style information learned by StyleGAN to guide the  segmentation process, while CLIP provides the semantic understanding necessary for accurate segmentation. We  evaluate our  method on several benchmark  datasets  and demonstrate its effectiveness in producing  high-quality segmentations. Our  results show that our approach outperforms existing unsupervised segmentation methods and achieves comparable  performance to supervised methods, highlighting  the   potential of combining generative and embedding models for  unsupervised  semantic image  segmentation.

Unpaired image-to-image  translation is the problem of mapping an image in the
source domain to one in the target domain, without requiring corresponding
image  pairs. To ensure the translated images are realistically plausible,
recent works, such as Cycle-GAN,  demands this mapping to be invertible. While,
this requirement demonstrates promising results when the domains are unimodal,
its performance is unpredictable in a multi-modal scenario  such as in an  image
segmentation task. This is because, invertibility does  not necessarily  enforce
semantic correctness. To this  end, we present a semantically-consistent GAN
framework, dubbed Sem-GAN, in which the semantics are defined by  the class
identities of image  segments in the  source  domain  as  produced by a semantic
segmentation algorithm. Our proposed framework   includes  consistency  constraints
on  the translation task  that, together with the GAN  loss and the
cycle-constraints, enforces  that the images when  translated will inherit the
appearances of the target    domain, while  (approximately) maintaining their
identities  from the source domain. We present experiments on several
image-to-image translation tasks and demonstrate that Sem-GAN improves the
quality of the  translated images significantly,  sometimes by more than 20% on
the FCN score.   Further,  we show   that semantic segmentation  models, trained with
synthetic images translated via Sem-GAN, leads to significantly  better
segmentation  results than other variants.

In biomedical image segmentation, the availability of large annotated datasets is often limited, posing challenges for training accurate deep learning models. This paper introduces SPDA, a novel data augmentation technique that leverages the properties of superpixels to generate high-quality synthetic training samples. SPDA utilizes superpixels to group pixels with similar characteristics and applies various geometric and color transformations to generate new images. Experimental results on several challenging biomedical image datasets demonstrate that the proposed SPDA approach improves the segmentation performance of deep learning models, outperforming traditional data augmentation methods. The proposed technique provides a promising solution to overcome the limited annotated data problem in biomedical image segmentation tasks.

We consider a single component reaction-diffusion equation in one dimension
with bistable nonlinearity and a nonlocal space-fractional diffusion operator
of Riesz-Feller type. Our main result shows the existence, uniqueness (up to
translations) and stability of a traveling wave solution connecting two stable
homogeneous steady states. In particular, we provide an Extension to classical
results on traveling wave solutions involving local diffusion. This extension
to evolution equations with Riesz-Feller operators requires several technical
steps. These steps are Based upon An integral representation for Riesz-Feller
operators, a comparison principle, regularity theory for space-fractional
diffusion equations, and control Of the far-field behavior.

There is large consent that succesful training of deep networks requires
many thousand annotated training samples. In this paper, we present a network
and training strategy that relies on the strong use of data augmentation to use
the available annotated samples more efficiently. The architecture consists of
a contracting path to capture context and a symmetric expanding path that
enables precise localization. We show that such a network can be trained
end-to-end from very few images and outperforms the prior best method (a
sliding-window convolutional network) on the ISBI challenge for segmentation of
neuronal structures in electron microscopic stacks. Using the same network
trained on transmitted light microscopy images (phase contrast and DIC) we won
the ISBI cell tracking challenge 2015 in these categories by a large margin.
Moreover, the network is fast. Segmentation of a 512x512 image takes less than
a second on a recent GPU. The full implementation (based on Caffe) and the
trained networks are available at
http://lmb.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/people/ronneber/u-net .

Μаnу sееmіnglу unrеlаtеd соmрutеr vіsіоn tаsks саn bе vіеwеd аs а sресіаl
саsе оf іmаgе dесоmроsіtіоn іntо sераrаtе lауеrs. Fоr ехаmрlе, іmаgе
sеgmеntаtіоn (sераrаtіоn іntо fоrеgrоund аnd bасkgrоund lауеrs); trаnsраrеnt
lауеr sераrаtіоn (іntо rеflесtіоn аnd trаnsmіssіоn lауеrs); Ιmаgе dеhаzіng
(sераrаtіоn іntо а сlеаr іmаgе аnd а hаzе mар), аnd mоrе. Ιn thіs рареr wе
рrороsе а unіfіеd frаmеwоrk fоr unsuреrvіsеd lауеr dесоmроsіtіоn оf а sіnglе
іmаgе, bаsеd оn соuрlеd "Dеер-іmаgе-Ρrіоr" (DΙΡ) nеtwоrks. Ιt wаs shоwn
[Ulуаnоv еt аl] thаt thе struсturе оf а sіnglе DІΡ gеnеrаtоr nеtwоrk іs
suffісіеnt tо сарturе thе lоw-lеvеl stаtіstісs оf а sіnglе іmаgе. Wе shоw thаt
соuрlіng multірlе suсh DІРs рrоvіdеs а роwеrful tооl fоr dесоmроsіng іmаgеs
іntо thеіr bаsіс соmроnеnts, fоr а wіdе vаrіеtу оf аррlісаtіоns. Τhіs
сараbіlіtу stеms frоm thе fасt thаt thе іntеrnаl stаtіstісs оf а mіхturе оf
lауеrs іs mоrе соmрlех thаn thе stаtіstісs оf еасh оf іts іndіvіduаl
соmроnеnts. Wе shоw thе роwеr оf thіs аррrоасh fоr Іmаgе-Dеhаzіng, Fg/Вg
Sеgmеntаtіоn, Wаtеrmаrk-Rеmоvаl, Тrаnsраrеnсу Sераrаtіоn іn іmаgеs аnd vіdео,
аnd mоrе. Τhеsе сараbіlіtіеs аrе асhіеvеd іn а tоtаllу unsuреrvіsеd wау, wіth
nо trаіnіng ехаmрlеs оthеr thаn thе іnрut іmаgе/vіdео іtsеlf.

This paper introduces a novel approach for structured prediction tasks using candidate constrained conditional random fields (CRFs). The proposed method incorporates a loss-aware framework that allows for more accurate predictions by considering the potential loss associated with each candidate label. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through experiments on various benchmark datasets, showing significant improvements in prediction accuracy compared to traditional CRF models. Additionally, the paper provides insights into the underlying mechanisms of the proposed method and discusses potential applications in natural language processing and computer vision. Overall, this work contributes to the field of structured prediction by introducing a loss-aware framework that enhances the accuracy of predictions in various domains.

Medical  image segmentation is a fundamental task  in medical image analysis.
Despite that deep convolutional neural networks have gained stellar performance
in this challenging  task,  they typically rely on large  labeled datasets, which
have limited their extension to  customized applications. By revisiting  the
superiority of atlas based segmentation  methods, we present a new framework  of
One-pass aligned Atlas Set for Images Segmentation (OASIS). To address the
problem  of time-consuming iterative  image registration used for atlas warping,
the proposed  method takes  advantage of the power of  deep  learning to  achieve
one-pass image registration. In addition, by  applying label constraint, OASIS
also makes the registration process  to be focused   on the regions to be
segmented for improving the performance of  segmentation.   Furthermore,  instead
of using image based similarity for label fusion, which  can be distracted by
the  large background areas, we propose a novel strategy to compute  the label
similarity based  weights for label fusion. Our experimental   results on  the
challenging task of  prostate MR image segmentation demonstrate that OASIS is
able to significantly increase the segmentation performance compared  to other
state-of-the-art methods.

We present near-infrared spectroscopic observations of the high-intensity HeI
10830 emission line in 45 low-metallicity HII regions. We combined these NIR
data with spectroscopic data in the optical range to derive the primordial He
abundance. The use of the HeI 10830A line, the intensity of which is very
sensitive to the density of the HII region, greatly improves the determination
of the physical conditions in the He^+ zone. This results in a considerably
tighter Y - O/H linear regression compared to all previous studies. 

We
extracted a final sample of 28 HII regions with Hbeta equivalent width
EW(Hbeta)>150A, excitation parameter O^2+/O>0.8, and with helium mass fraction
Y derived with an accuracy better than 3%. 

With this final sample we derived a
primordial He mass fraction Yp = 0.2551+/-0.0022. 

The derived value of Yp is
higher than the one predicted by the standard big bang nucleosynthesis (SBBN)
model. Using our derived Yp together with D/H = (2.53+/-0.04)x10^-5, and the
chi^2 technique, we found that the best agreement between these light element
abundances is achieved in a cosmological model with a baryon mass density
Omega_b h^2 = 0.0240+/-0.0017 (68% CL), +/-0.0028 (95.4% CL), +/-0.0034 (99%
CL) and an effective number of neutrino species Neff = 3.58+/-0.25 (68% CL),
+/-0.40 (95.4% CL), +/-0.50 (99% CL). 

A non-standard value of Neff is preferred
at the 99% CL, implying the possible existence of additional types of neutrino
species.

LIDAR point cloud and RGB images are both crucial for 3D object detection, and many modern 3D detection algorithms rely on combining these two data sources. However, the methods of combining them are ineffective, using the “Bird’s Eye View” or “Voxel” formats, which lack the accuracy of the actual triangulation. The proposed method fuses multi-source features at the 3D points directly, instead of using the Bird’s Eye View format. Besides continuous convolution, point pooling and attention aggregation are used to make the fused features more precise. In addition, based on the PACF, we propose a 3D multi-source, multi-task network: pointcloud-image RNN (PI-RCNN for short). This network uses an image segmentation layer to extract high-resolution semantic maps from images, and then combines the features of different sources with a powerful PACF. The combination of the power of PACF and the rich semantic features of the segmentation layer leads to great improvements in 3D detection. We tested PI-RCNN on the KITTI 3D test set, and obtained the best results in terms of 3D Ap.

This paper presents a study on the excitation and imaging of resonant optical modes of gold (Au) triangular nano-antennas using cathodoluminescence spectroscopy. The authors investigate the optical properties of these nano-antennas by exciting them with an electron beam and measuring the resulting cathodoluminescence emission. They demonstrate that the excitation of the nano-antennas leads to the enhancement of the local electric field, resulting in the generation of resonant optical modes. The authors also show that the cathodoluminescence spectroscopy technique allows for the imaging of these resonant modes with high spatial resolution. This study provides valuable insights into the optical properties of Au triangular nano-antennas and demonstrates the potential of cathodoluminescence spectroscopy for characterizing and imaging resonant optical modes in nanoscale systems.

Marking tumors and organs is a challenging task suffering from both inter-
and intra-observer variability. 

The literature quantifies observer variability
by generating consensus among multiple experts when they mark the same image. Automatically building consensus contours to establish quality assurance for
image segmentation is presently absent in the clinical practice. As the
\emph{big data} becomes more and more available, techniques to access a large
number of existing segments of multiple experts becomes possible. 

Fast
algorithms are, hence, required to facilitate the search for similar cases. The
present work puts forward a potential framework that tested with small datasets
(both synthetic and real images) displays the reliability of finding similar
images. 

In this paper, the idea of content-based barcodes is used to retrieve
similar cases in order to build consensus contours in medical image
segmentation. 

This approach may be regarded as an extension of the conventional
atlas-based segmentation that generally works with rather small atlases due to
required computational expenses. 

The fast segment-retrieval process via
barcodes makes it possible to create and use large atlases, something that
directly contributes to the quality of the consensus building. Because the
accuracy of experts' contours must be measured, we first used 500 synthetic
prostate images with their gold markers and delineations by 20 simulated users. The fast barcode-guided computed consensus delivered an average error of
$8\%\!\pm\!5\%$ compared against the gold standard segments. Furthermore, we
used magnetic resonance images of prostates from 15 patients delineated by 5
oncologists and selected the best delineations to serve as the gold-standard
segments. 

The proposed barcode atlas achieved a Jaccard overlap of
$87\%\!\pm\!9\%$ with the contours of the gold-standard segments.

In this paper, a novel active contour model called IEOPF (Image Energized Orthogonal Primary Functions) is proposed for image segmentation in the presence of inhomogeneities. The model utilizes orthogonal primary functions to estimate the inhomogeneities in image intensity. It also incorporates an image energizing term to drive the contour evolution. The proposed model is compared with several state-of-the-art methods on different datasets, and experimental results demonstrate its superiority in terms of accuracy and robustness. Overall, the IEOPF model provides an effective solution for image segmentation in the presence of inhomogeneities, making it suitable for various applications in image analysis and computer vision.

This paper presents a novel approach for image reconstruction using deep learning techniques. The proposed method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn the mapping between low-resolution and high-resolution images. The network is trained on a large dataset of paired low-resolution and high-resolution images, and is able to generate high-quality reconstructions of low-resolution images. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of both visual quality and quantitative metrics. The paper also discusses the limitations and potential future directions for improving the proposed approach. Overall, this work contributes to the field of image reconstruction by leveraging the power of deep learning to achieve superior results.

The paper presents a study on the existence of large conformal metrics with prescribed scalar curvature on compact Riemannian manifolds. The main result of the paper is a new existence theorem, which shows that for a certain class of Riemannian manifolds, there always exists a conformal metric with prescribed scalar curvature, under certain conditions. The paper also provides a detailed proof of this result and discusses its implications and applications in various fields of mathematics and physics, such as differential geometry and general relativity. The paper concludes with some open questions and possible future research directions.

Few-shot segmentation is a challenging task   in computer vision, where the goal is  to  segment objects in an  image given  only  a few annotated examples.  In  this paper, we propose a novel approach called  Self-Guided and Cross-Guided Learning (SGCL) for few-shot segmentation. SGCL leverages both self-guided and cross-guided learning to improve  the  segmentation performance. Self-guided  learning uses the available annotated examples  to guide  the segmentation process, while cross-guided learning utilizes information from other  images to further refine the segmentation results.  We evaluate  SGCL on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art few-shot segmentation methods. The experimental results demonstrate that SGCL achieves superior performance in terms  of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability. Our approach  shows   promise for addressing the challenges of few-shot segmentation  and has the potential  to  advance the  field of computer vision.

The abstract for the academic paper titled "Reduced Coulomb interaction in organic solar cells by the introduction of inorganic high-k nanostructured materials" states that the Coulomb interaction in organic solar cells can be reduced by introducing inorganic high-k nanostructured materials. This is important as the Coulomb interaction is a major limiting factor in the efficiency of organic solar cells. The researchers demonstrate that by incorporating high-k nanostructured materials into the organic layer of the solar cell, the Coulomb interaction between charges is significantly reduced. This reduction in Coulomb interaction results in improved charge carrier separation and enhanced overall solar cell performance. The paper provides evidence through experimental data, including device performance measurements and charge transport studies, to support the effectiveness of the introduced high-k nanostructured materials in reducing the Coulomb interaction in organic solar cells. These findings have significant implications for the development of more efficient and cost-effective organic solar cell technologies.

We use Minkowski Functionals to explore the presence of non-Gaussian
signatures in simulated cosmic microwave background (CMB) maps. Precisely, we
analyse the non-Gaussianities produced from the angular power spectra emerging
from a class of inflationary models with a primordial step-like potential. This
class of models are able to perform the best-fit of the low-$\ell$ `features',
revealed first in the CMB angular power spectrum by the WMAP experiment and
then confirmed by the Planck collabouration maps. Indeed, such models generate
oscillatory features in the primordial power spectrum of scalar perturbations,
that are then imprinted in the large scales of the CMB field. Interestingly, we
discover Gaussian deviations in the CMB maps simulated from the power spectra
produced by these models, as compared with Gaussian $\Lambda$CDM maps.
Moreover, we also show that the kind and level of the non-Gaussianities
produced in these simulated CMB maps are compatible with that found in the four
foreground-cleaned Planck maps. Our results indicate that inflationary models
with a step-like potential are not only able to improve the best-fit respect to
the $\Lambda$CDM model accounting well for the `features' observed in the CMB
angular power spectrum, but also suggesting a possible origin for certain
non-Gaussian signatures observed in the Planck data.

Anatomical and physiological modeling of right atrium (CA) and proximal
cerebral veins (PPVs) is useful for clinical management of many pulmonary
disorders. magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides quantitative analysis of LA
and PPVs through visualization. Also, there is a strong need for an advanced
image segmentation technique to be applied to cardiac MRI for statistical
characterization of LA and PPVs. In this research, we address this unmet medical need by
finding a new deep learning-based segmentation approach for analysis of
LA and PPVs with high precision and increased performance. Our strategy is based
on a multi-view convolutional neural network (CNN) with an adaptive fusion
approach and a new loss function that enables fast and more realistic convergence
of the backpropagation based optimization. After training our network from
scratch by creating more than 60K 2D MRI images (slices), we have presented our
segmentation approach to the STACOM 2013 cardiac segmentation challenge
benchmark. Qualitative and statistical analyses, derived from the
segmentation challenge, suggest that the proposed technique demonstrated the
state-of-the-art sensitivity (90%), accuracy (99%), accuracy (94%), and
performance levels (10 minutes in CPU, and 7.5 seconds in RAM).

Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based image segmentation has made great
progress in recent years. However, video object segmentation remains a
challenging task due to its high computational complexity. Most of the previous
methods employ a two-stream CNN Framework to handle spatial and motion features
separately. In this paper, We propose an end-to-end encoder-decoder style 3D
CNN to aggregate spatial and temporal information simultaneously For video
object segmentation. To efficiently process video, we propose 3D separable
convolution for the pyramid pooling module and decoder, which dramatically
reduces the number of operations while maintaining the performance. Moreover,
we also extend our framework To video action segmentation by adding an extra
classifier to predict the action label for actors in videos. extensive
experiments on several Video datasets demonstrate the superior performance of
the proposed approach for action and object segmentation compared to the
state-of-the-art.

This paper introduces a revised sunspot group number collection to improve the accuracy and reliability of sunspot data. The existing collection suffers from inconsistencies and ambiguities, leading to variations in the reported sunspot numbers. The revised collection addresses these issues by providing detailed guidelines for observing and recording sunspot group numbers, including clear definitions and classifications. The revised collection also incorporates modern data analysis techniques to ensure consistency and comparability across different observers and time periods. The authors perform a comprehensive analysis of historical sunspot data using the revised collection, confirming its effectiveness in mitigating inconsistencies and improving accuracy. The revised collection is expected to contribute to more reliable long-term sunspot studies and better understanding of solar activity.

This paper presents an analysis of vision-based abnormal red blood cell classification. The study aims to develop an automated system for the detection and classification of abnormal red blood cells using computer vision techniques. The proposed system utilizes image processing algorithms to extract relevant features from microscopic images of blood samples. These features are then used to train a machine learning model for the classification of normal and abnormal red blood cells. The performance of the system is evaluated using a dataset of blood samples with known abnormalities. The results show that the proposed system achieves high accuracy in the classification of abnormal red blood cells, demonstrating its potential for use in clinical settings for the early detection of blood disorders.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable  success in various computer vision  tasks. However, they  are limited in their ability to capture long-range dependencies due  to  their local receptive fields. In this paper, we propose a  novel architecture called Fully Hyperbolic Convolutional Neural Networks (FHCNNs) that addresses this limitation.  FHCNNs  leverage the hyperbolic space to   model long-range dependencies  by mapping   the input data onto a hyperbolic manifold. We introduce a hyperbolic convolution operation and a hyperbolic  pooling operation to perform computations  in the  hyperbolic space.  We also propose a hyperbolic activation  function   that preserves the hyperbolic geometry.  Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that FHCNNs outperform traditional CNNs in terms of capturing long-range dependencies and achieving higher  accuracy in various computer vision tasks. Our  findings suggest that leveraging the hyperbolic space  can be a  promising direction  for improving the   performance of CNNs.

This paper  presents  a theoretical proposal for the generation and analysis  of multiphoton maximally entangled states using weak nonlinearities. The  authors propose a scheme that combines a nonlinear medium with a beam splitter to  create entangled states of  multiple photons.  They  also propose  a method for analyzing  these states using   a combination of linear optics and weak nonlinearities. The authors provide a detailed  analysis of the proposed scheme and discuss  its potential applications in   quantum information processing and  quantum communication. The results  of this study suggest that the proposed  scheme could be a promising approach for generating and analyzing  multiphoton maximally entangled states.

Although spatial information of images usually enhance the robustness of the
Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) algorithm, it greatly increases the computational costs for
image segmentation. 

To achieve a sound trade-off between the segmentation
performance and the speed of clustering, we come up with a Kullback-Leibler
(KL) divergence-based FCM algorithm by incorporating a tight wavelet frame
transform and a morphological reconstruction operation. 

To enhance FCM's
robustness, an observed image is first filtered by using the morphological
reconstruction. 

A tight wavelet frame system is employed to decompose the
observed and filtered images so as to form their feature sets. Considering
these feature sets as data of clustering, an modified FCM algorithm is
proposed, which introduces a KL divergence term in the partition matrix into
its objective function. The KL divergence term aims to make membership degrees
of each image pixel closer to those of its neighbors, which brings that the
membership partition becomes more suitable and the parameter setting of FCM
becomes simplified. On the basis of the obtained partition matrix and
prototypes, the segmented feature set is reconstructed by minimizing the
inverse process of the modified objective function. To modify abnormal features
produced in the reconstruction process, each reconstructed feature is
reassigned to the closest prototype. 

As a result, the segmentation accuracy of
KL divergence-based FCM is further improved. 

What's more, the segmented image
is reconstructed by using a tight wavelet frame reconstruction operation. 

Finally, supporting experiments coping with synthetic, medical and color images
are reported. Experimental results exhibit that the proposed algorithm works
well and comes with better segmentation performance than other comparative
algorithms. Moreover, the proposed algorithm requires less time than most of
the FCM-related algorithms.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) have become increasingly important due to their
excellent empirical performance on a wide range of problems. However,
regularization is generally achieved by indirect means, largely due to the
complex set of functions defined by network and the difficulty in measuring
function complexity. There exists no method in literature for additive
regularization based on norm of the function, as is classically considered in
statistical learning theory. In this work, we propose sampling-based
approximations to weighted function norms as regularizers for deep neural
networks. We provide, to the best of our knowledge, first proof in the
literature of the NP-hardness of computing function norms of DNNs, motivating
the necessity of an approximate approach. We then derive a generalization bound
for functions trained with weighted norms and prove that a natural stochastic
optimization strategy minimizes bound. Finally, we empirically validate the
improved performance of proposed regularization strategies for both convex
function sets as well as DNNs on real-world classification and image
segmentation tasks demonstrating improved performance over weight decay,
dropout, and batch normalization. Source code will be released at time of
publication.

This paper presents a continuously updated bibliography on the topics of superiorization and perturbation resilience of algorithms. Superiorization is a methodology that aims to improve the performance of an algorithm by adding a perturbation term to the objective function. Perturbation resilience, on the other hand, refers to the ability of an algorithm to maintain its performance in the presence of perturbations. The bibliography includes references to relevant papers, books, and other resources that discuss these topics. The goal of this bibliography is to provide researchers and practitioners with a comprehensive and up-to-date collection of resources on superiorization and perturbation resilience, facilitating further research and development in these areas.

This paper explores the spectral gap properties of the unitary groups, specifically focusing on the non-commutative Sidon sets. The concept of Sidon sets, which are sets of integers with the property that the sum of any two distinct elements is always distinct, is extended to the non-commutative setting. The paper discusses the results obtained by Rider on non-commutative Sidon sets and their implications for the spectral gap properties of the unitary groups. The paper also presents new results and proofs related to Rider's work. Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding of spectral gap properties in the context of non-commutative Sidon sets and unitary groups.

In this paper, we explore deformations of symmetric simple modular Lie (super)algebras. We start by introducing the concept of deformations and how they relate to Lie algebras. Next, we focus on symmetric simple modular Lie (super)algebras and provide a brief overview of their properties and structures. We then proceed to examine various deformations of these algebras and investigate their implications. Through our analysis, we demonstrate the existence of certain deformations and discuss their significance in the context of Lie (super)algebras. Finally, we conclude with a summary of our findings and propose potential avenues for future research in this area.

We set up an algebraic framework for the study of pseudoholomorphic discs
bounding nonorientable Lagrangians, as well as equivariant extensions of such
structures arising from a torus action. 

First, we define unital cyclic twisted $A_\infty$ algebras and prove some
basic results about them, including a homological perturbation lemma which
allows one to construct minimal models of such algebras. 

We then construct an
equivariant extension of $A_\infty$ algebras which are invariant under a torus
action on the underlying complex. Finally, we construct a homotopy retraction
of the Cartan-Weil complex to equivariant cohomology, which allows us to
construct minimal models for equivariant cyclic twisted $A_\infty$ algebras. In a forthcoming paper we will use these results to define and obtain
fixed-point expressions for the open Gromov-Witten theory of $\mathbb{RP}^{2n}
\hookrightarrow \mathbb{CP}^{2n}$, as well as its equivariant extension.
