We presents in this paper a novel fish classification methodology based on a
combination between robust feature selection, image segmentation and
geometrical parameter techniques using Artificial Neural Network and Decision
Tree. Unlike existing works for fish classification, which propose descriptors
and do not analyze their individual impacts in the whole classification task
and do not make the combination between the feature selection, image
segmentation and geometrical parameter, we propose a general set of features
extraction using robust feature selection, image segmentation and geometrical
parameter and their correspondent weights that should be used as a priori
information by the classifier. 

In this sense, instead of studying techniques
for improving the classifiers structure itself, we consider it as a black box
and focus our research in the determination of which input information must
bring a robust fish discrimination.The main contribution of this paper is
enhancement recognize and classify fishes based on digital image and To develop
and implement a novel fish recognition prototype using global feature
extraction, image segmentation and geometrical parameters, it have the ability
to Categorize the given fish into its cluster and Categorize the clustered fish
into poison or non-poison fish, and categorizes the non-poison fish into its
family .

We study the applicability of a set of texture descriptors introduced in
recent work by the author to texture-based segmentation of images. The texture
descriptors under investigation result from applying graph indices from
quantitative graph theory to graphs encoding the local structure of images. The
underlying graphs arise from the computation of morphological amoebas as
structuring elements for adaptive morphology, either as weighted or unweighted
Dijkstra search trees or as edge-weighted pixel graphs within structuring
elements. In the present paper we focus on texture descriptors in which the
graph indices are entropy-based, and use them in a geodesic active contour
framework for image segmentation. Experiments on several synthetic and one
real-world image are shown to demonstrate texture segmentation by this
approach. Forthermore, we undertake an attempt to analyse selected
entropy-based texture descriptors with regard to what information about texture
they actually encode. Whereas this analysis uses some heuristic assumptions, it
indicates that the graph-based texture descriptors are related to fractal
dimension measures that have been proven useful in texture analysis.

This paper investigates the octahedral conversion of amorphous silicon dioxide (a-SiO2) in a host matrix through pulsed ion implantation. The authors demonstrate that by using a combination of high-energy ion implantation and subsequent annealing, the a-SiO2 can be transformed into a crystalline octahedral structure. The structural and optical properties of the converted material are characterized using various techniques, including X-ray diffraction and photoluminescence spectroscopy. The results show that the octahedral conversion leads to improved optical properties, making it a promising approach for the development of new materials with enhanced functionality.

This is the abstract.  The results of  measurements of X-ray photoelectron
spectra (XPS)  of  a-SiO2-host material after pulsed implantation with  [Mn+] and
[Co+, Mn+]-ions as well as DFT-calculations are   presented. The  low-energy shift
is  found in  XPS Si 2p  and O 1s core-levels of single [Mn+] and  dual [Co+, Mn+]
pulsed ion-implanted a-SiO2 (E  = 30 keV, D = 2*10^17  cm^-2) with respect to
those of untreated a-SiO2.The similar changes are found in XPS Si 2p and O 1s
of stishovite  compared to  those of quartz. This means that the pulsed
ion-implantation   induces  the local high pressure  effect which leads to an
appearance of SiO6-structural units   in alpha-SiO2 host,  forming
"stishovite-like" local  atomic structure. This process can be  described within
electronic bonding transition  from the four-fold "quartz-like" to six-fold
"stishovite-like"  high-pressure phase in  SiO2 host-matrix. It is found that
such octahedral conversion depends  on the fluence and starts with doses higher
than D = 3*10^16 cm^-2.

Recent advances in AI technology have made the forgery of digital images and
videos easier, and it has become significantly more difficult to identify such
forgeries. These forgeries, if disseminated with malicious intent, can
negatively impact social and political stability, and pose significant ethical
and legal challenges as well. Deepfake is a variant of auto-encoders that use
deep learning techniques to identify and exchange images of a person's face in
a picture or film. Deepfake can result in an erosion of public trust in digital
images and videos, which has far-reaching effects on political and social
stability. This study therefore proposes a solution for facial forgery
detection to determine if a picture or film has ever been processed by
Deepfake. The proposed solution reaches detection efficiency by using the
recently proposed separable convolutional neural network (CNN) and image
segmentation. In addition, this study also examined how different image
segmentation methods affect detection results. Finally, the ensemble model is
used to improve detection capabilities. Experiment results demonstrated the
excellent performance of the proposed solution.

This paper presents a method for correcting timing jitter  in  a femtosecond resolution on a terawatt  (TW) scale  Ti:sapphire laser system. The system is used for pump-probe experiments in free-electron laser  (FEL)  research. The authors describe the experimental  setup  and the challenges associated with timing jitter in such high-power laser systems. They propose a  technique based on a feedback   loop and   a fast photodiode to measure  and correct the timing jitter. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through experimental  results, showing a significant reduction in timing jitter   and improved stability of the laser system. The authors  conclude  that this technique  can be applied  to other  high-power laser systems for precise timing control  in FEL pump-probe experiments.

In this work, we address the task of referring image segmentation (RIS),
which aims at predicting a segmentation mask for the object described by a
natural language expression. Most existing methods focus on establishing
unidirectional or directional relationships between visual and linguistic
features to associate two modalities together, while the multi-scale context is
ignored or insufficiently modeled. 

Multi-scale context is crucial to localize
and segment those objects that have large scale variations during the
multi-modal fusion process. To solve this problem, we propose a simple yet
effective Cascaded Multi-modal Fusion (CMF) module, which stacks multiple
atrous convolutional layers in parallel and further introduces a cascaded
branch to fuse visual and linguistic features. 

The cascaded branch can
progressively integrate multi-scale contextual information and facilitate the
alignment of two modalities during the multi-modal fusion process. 

Experimental
results on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms most
state-of-the-art methods. Code is available at
https://github.com/jianhua2022/CMF-Refseg.

Urban facade segmentation from automatically acquired imagery, in contrast to
traditional image segmentation, poses several unique challenges. 360-degree
photospheres captured from vehicles are an effective way to capture a large
number of images, but this data presents difficult-to-model warping and
stitching artifacts. In addition, each pixel can belong to multiple facade
elements, and different facade elements (e.g., window, balcony, sill, etc.) are
correlated and vary wildly in their characteristics. In this paper, we propose
three network architectures of varying complexity to achieve multilabel
semantic segmentation of facade images while exploiting their unique
characteristics. Specifically, we propose a MULTIFACSEGNET architecture to
assign multiple labels to each pixel, a SEPARABLE architecture as a low-rank
formulation that encourages extraction of rectangular elements, and a
COMPATIBILITY network that simultaneously seeks segmentation across facade
element types allowing the network to 'see' intermediate output probabilities
of the various facade element classes. Our results on benchmark datasets show
significant improvements over existing facade segmentation approaches for the
typical facade elements. For example, on one commonly used dataset, the
accuracy scores for window(the most important architectural element) increases
from 4.77 to 0.97 percent compared to the best competing method, and comparable
improvements on other element types.

This paper proposes a novel approach for extracting text from high entropy images using a semi-bagging based deep neural architecture. High entropy images pose a challenge for traditional text extraction methods due to their complex and cluttered backgrounds. The proposed architecture combines the strengths of semi-supervised learning and bagging techniques to improve the accuracy and robustness of text extraction. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately extracting text from high entropy images, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. The proposed architecture has the potential to support various applications such as OCR systems, document analysis, and image understanding.

This paper presents a system level numerical analysis of a Monte Carlo simulation of the E. coli chemotaxis. Chemotaxis is the process by which bacteria move towards or away from chemical gradients in their environment. The simulation model incorporates various factors such as the concentration of attractants and repellents, the sensitivity of the bacteria to these chemicals, and the random movement of the bacteria. The numerical analysis focuses on understanding the behavior of the bacteria in response to different environmental conditions. The results show that the bacteria exhibit a biased random walk towards higher concentrations of attractants and away from repellents. The analysis also reveals the importance of the sensitivity of the bacteria to the chemicals in determining their movement patterns. Overall, this study provides insights into the mechanisms underlying bacterial chemotaxis and highlights the potential of Monte Carlo simulations for studying complex biological systems.

Various saliency detection algorithms from color images have been proposed to
mimic eye fixation or attentive object detection response of human observers
for the same scenes. However, developments on hyperspectral imaging systems
enable us to obtain redundant spectral information of the observed scenes from
the reflected light source from objects. A few studies using low-level features
on hyperspectral images demonstrated that salient object detection can be
achieved. In this work, we proposed a salient object detection model on
hyperspectral images by applying manifold ranking (MR) on self-supervised
Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) features (high-level features) from
unsupervised image segmentation task. Self-supervision of CNN continues until
clustering loss or saliency maps converges to a defined error between each
iteration. Finally, saliency estimations is done as the saliency map at last
iteration when the self-supervision procedure terminates with convergence.
Experimental evaluations demonstrated that proposed saliency detection
algorithm on hyperspectral images is outperforming state-of-the-arts
hyperspectral saliency models including the original MR based saliency model.

We propose a novel locally adaptive learning estimator for enhancing the
inter- and intra- discriminative capabilities of Deep Neural Networks, which
can be used as improved loss layer for semantic image segmentation tasks. Most
loss layers compute pixel-wise cost between feature maps and ground truths,
ignoring spatial layouts and interactions between neighboring pixels with same
object category, and thus networks cannot be effectively sensitive to
intra-class connections. Stride by stride, our method firstly conducts adaptive
pooling filter operating over predicted feature maps, aiming to merge predicted
distributions over a small group of neighboring pixels with same category, and
then it computes cost between the merged distribution vector and their category
label. 

Such design can make groups of neighboring predictions from same
category involved into estimations on predicting correctness with respect to
their category, and hence train networks to be more sensitive to regional
connections between adjacent pixels based on their categories. 

In the
experiments on Pascal VOC 2012 segmentation datasets, the consistently improved
results show that our proposed approach achieves better segmentation masks
against previous counterparts.

This paper explores two different methods for enumerating ordered trees, namely the Prüfer code and the Cayley's formula. The Prüfer code is a unique sequence of numbers that represents a labeled tree, while Cayley's formula provides a formula for calculating the number of labeled trees with a given number of vertices. The paper compares the two methods in terms of their efficiency and ease of implementation. It also discusses the applications of these enumeration techniques in various fields such as computer science and combinatorics. Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the two methods and their respective advantages and disadvantages in enumerating ordered trees.

An evacuation process is simulated within the Social Force Model. Thousand
pedestrians are leaving a room by one exit. We investigate the stationarity of
the distribution of time lags between instants when two Successive pedestrians
cross the exit. The Exponential tail of the distribution is shown To gradually
vanish. Taking fluctuations apart, the time lags decrease in time till there
are only about 50 pedestrians in The room, then they start to increase. This
suggests that at the last stage the flow is laminar. In the first stage,
clogging events slow the evacuation down. As they are more likely for larger
crowds, the flow is not stationary. The data are investigated with detrended
Fluctuation analysis.

Nowadays U-net-like FCNs predominate various biomedical image segmentation
applications and attain promising performance, largely due to their elegant
architectures, e.g., symmetric contracting and expansive paths as well as
lateral skip-connections. It remains a research direction to devise novel
architectures to further benefit the segmentation. In this paper, we develop an
ACE-net that aims to enhance the feature representation and utilization by
augmenting the contracting and expansive paths. In particular, we augment the
paths by the recently proposed advanced techniques including ASPP, dense
connection and deep supervision mechanisms, and novel connections such as
directly connecting the raw image to the expansive side. With these
augmentations, ACE-net can utilize features from multiple sources, scales and
reception fields to segment while still maintains a relative simple
architecture. Experiments on two typical biomedical segmentation tasks validate
its effectiveness, where highly competitive results are obtained in both tasks
while ACE-net still runs fast at inference.

We investigate Referring Image Segmentation (RIS), which outputs a
segmentation map corresponding to the given natural language description. To
solve RIS efficiently, we need to understand each word's relationship with
other words, each region in the image to other regions, and cross-modal
alignment between linguistic and visual domains. We argue that one of the
limiting factors in the recent methods is that they do not handle these
interactions simultaneously. 

To this end, we propose a novel architecture
called JRNet, which uses a Joint Reasoning Module(JRM) to concurrently capture
the inter-modal and intra-modal interactions. The output of JRM is passed
through a novel Cross-Modal Multi-Level Fusion (CMMLF) module which further
refines the segmentation masks by exchanging contextual information across
visual hierarchy through linguistic features acting as a bridge. 

We present
thorough ablation studies and validate our approach's performance on four
benchmark datasets, showing considerable performance gains over the existing
state-of-the-art methods.

Medical image annotation is a significant hurdle for producing accurate and reliable
machine learning models. Annotation is costly, time-consuming, and usually
requires expert expertise, especially in the scientific field. Here, we suggest
using minimal user interaction in the form of extreme point clicks to train a
segmentation model which, in effect, can be applied to speed up medical image
annotation. An initial segmentation is created based on the extreme points
using the random walker algorithms. This final segmentation is then used
as a noisy supervision signal to train a fully convolutional network that can
segment the organ of interest, based on the provided user clicks. Through
experimentation on various medical imaging datasets, we show that the
predictions of the network can be refined using multiple rounds of training with
the analysis from the same weakly annotated data. Further modifications are
shown using the clicked points within a custom-designed loss and attention
mechanism. Our methodology has the potential to speed up the process of creating
new training data for the implementation of new machine learning and deep
learning-based models for, but not solely, medical image analysis.

In supervised learning for medical image analysis, sample selection
methodologies are fundamental to attain optimum system performance promptly and
with minimal expert interactions (e.g. label querying in active learning
setup). In this paper we propose a novel sample selection methodology based on
deep features leveraging information contained in interpretability saliency
maps. In the absence of ground truth labels for informative samples, we use a
novel self supervised learning based approach for training a classifier that
learns to identify most informative sample in a given batch of images. We
demonstrate benefits of the proposed approach, termed
Interpretability-Driven Sample Selection (IDEAL), in an active learning setup
aimed at lung disease classification and histopathology image segmentation. We
analyze three different approaches to determine sample informativeness from
interpretability saliency maps: (i) observational model stemming from
findings on previous uncertainty-based sample selection approaches, (ii) a
radiomics-based model, and (iii) a novel data-driven self-supervised approach.
We compare IDEAL to other baselines using publicly available NIH chest
X-ray dataset for lung disease classification, and a public histopathology
segmentation dataset (GLaS), demonstrating potential of using
interpretability information for sample selection in active learning systems.
Results show our proposed self supervised approach outperforms other approaches
in selecting informative samples leading to state of art performance with
fewer samples.

We study the topology of the Margulis region associated with an arbitrary
screw translation $g$ acting on the 4-dimensional real hyperbolic space. This
is an invariant domain with the parabolic fixed point of $g$ on its boundary
which plays the role of an invariant horoball for a translation in dimensions
$\leq 3$. The boundary of the Margulis region is shown in terms of a
function $B_\alpha : [0,\infty) \to {\mathbb R}$ which strictly depends on the
rotation angle $\alpha \in {\mathbb Z}/{\mathbb R}$ of $g$. We obtain an
asymptotically universal upper bound for $B_\alpha(r)$ as $g \to \infty$ for
arbitrary irrational $\alpha$, as well as lower bounds when $\alpha$ is
Diophatine and the optimal bound when $\alpha$ is of bounded type. We
investigate the consequences of these results for the geometry of Margulis
cusps of hyperbolic 4-manifolds that correspond to irrational screw
translations acting on the universal cover. among other things, we prove
bi-Lipschitz rigidity of these cusps.

We consider controller design for robust output tracking and disturbance
rejection for continuous-time periodic linear systems with periodic reference
and disturbance signals. As our main results we present four different
controllers: A feedforward control law and a discrete-time dynamic error
feedback controller for output tracking and disturbance rejection, a robust
discrete-time feedback controller, and finally a discrete-time feedback
controller that achieves approximate robust output tracking and disturbance
rejection. The presented constructions are also new for time-invariant finite
and infinite-dimensional systems. 

The results are illustrated with two
examples: A periodically time-dependent system of harmonic oscillators and a
nonautonomous two-dimensional heat equation with boundary disturbance.

We discover new classes of hereditary graphs, minimal (with respect to the shortest paths) and unboundedly long-cliqued. The new classes of graphs are split permutation graphs and bi-chain graphs. Each of these classes of graphs is characterized by a finite list of forbidden minimum induced subgraphs. This contradicts a conjecture of Daligault, Rao and Thomasse, made in 2010, according to which all such minimal classes must be characterized by an infinite number of forbidden induced subgraphs. In the same paper, Daligault, Rao and Thomasse also made a conjecture that any hereditary class of unboundedly long-cliqued graphs must contain an infinite labeled anti-chain. We prove that the two classes of graphs that we are studying satisfy this conjecture. It is a canonical infinite labeled anti-chain. This leads us to make a stronger conjecture: any hereditary class of graphs, minimal and unboundedly long-cliqued, must contain a canonical infinite labeled anti-chain.

This paper proposes a deep learning object detection method for efficient clusters initialization. The method utilizes a deep neural network to detect objects in an image and then uses the detected objects as initial clusters for a clustering algorithm. The proposed method is compared with traditional methods on various datasets and shows superior performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the deep learning object detection method for clusters initialization, highlighting its potential for applications in computer vision and data analysis.

In this paper, we study the quantitative volume space form rigidity under a lower Ricci curvature bound. Specifically, we consider a compact Riemannian manifold M with a lower bound on its Ricci curvature. We introduce a new concept called the volume space form rigidity constant, which measures the quantitative deviation of the volume of M from that of a space form. We prove that under a lower Ricci curvature bound, the volume space form rigidity constant is bounded above by a constant depending only on the dimension of M and the lower Ricci curvature bound. This result demonstrates a quantitative version of the classical volume space form rigidity theorem, providing a quantitative understanding of the rigidity phenomenon for manifolds with lower Ricci curvature bounds. Our proof utilizes the Bochner-Weitzenbock formula and the Bishop-Gromov volume comparison theorem.

This paper proposes a deep structured prediction model for fine image segmentation that leverages complex relations between different image regions. The model incorporates a dense conditional random field layer to capture long-range dependencies and enforce consistency in the segmentation results. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their model on various image datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation accuracy. Furthermore, they analyze the impact of different design choices and provide insights into the strengths and limitations of their approach. Overall, this paper presents a novel deep learning framework for fine image segmentation that exploits complex relations and achieves superior performance compared to existing methods.

This paper introduces a novel approach for learning to segment images from scribbles by employing multi-scale adversarial attention gates.  The proposed method leverages  the advantages of both  attention  mechanisms  and adversarial   training  to improve the accuracy and robustness of image segmentation tasks. The attention gates are designed to selectively focus on relevant regions of the image while  the adversarial training helps to refine the  segmentation boundaries. Experiment results show that the proposed  approach outperforms existing methods in terms of  segmentation accuracy and  robustness. Additionally, the method is  shown to be effective for different types of images and datasets. Overall, this   research offers a  promising  solution  for improving the performance  of image  segmentation  algorithms.

A stable generalized complex structure is one that is generically symplectic
but degenerates along a real codimension two submanifold, where it defines a
generalized Calabi-Yau structure. We introduce a Lie algebroid which allows us
to view such structures as symplectic forms. This allows us to construct new
examples of stable structures, and also to define period maps for their
deformations in which background three-form flux is either fixed or not,
proving unobstructedness of both deformation problems. We then use the same
tools to establish local normal forms for the degeneracy locus and for
Lagrangian branes. Applying our normal forms to four-dimensional case, we
prove that any compact stable generalized complex 4-manifold has symplectic
completion, in the sense that it can be modified near its degeneracy locus to
produce compact symplectic 4-manifold.

When mathematical/computational problems reach infinity, extending analysis
and/or numerical computation beyond it becomes a notorious challenge. We
suggest that, upon suitable singular transformations (that can in principle be
computationally detected on the fly) it becomes possible to go beyond infinity
to the other side, with the solution becoming again well behaved and the
computations continuing normally. In our lumped, Ordinary Differential Equation
(ODE) examples this infinity crossing can happen instantaneously; at the
spatially distributed, Partial Differential Equation (PDE) level the crossing
of infinity may even persist for finite time, necessitating the introduction of
conceptual (and computational) buffer zones in which an appropriate singular
transformation is continuously (locally) detected and performed. These
observations (and associated tools) could set the stage for a systematic
approach to bypassing infinity (and thus going beyond it) in a broader range of
evolution equations; they also hold the promise of meaningfully and seamlessly
performing the relevant computations. Along the path of our analysis, we
present a regularization process via complexification and explore its impact on
the dynamics; we also discuss a set of compactification transformations and
their intuitive implications.

This paper  presents a method for unsupervised cross-modality domain adaptation of convolutional neural networks (ConvNets) for biomedical image  segmentations.  The proposed  method utilizes an adversarial loss to align the  feature distributions of different modalities, allowing the ConvNets to generalize across modalities without the need  for labeled   data. The authors evaluate the  performance of their method  on two  different biomedical image segmentation  tasks and demonstrate  its  effectiveness in improving segmentation accuracy compared to existing methods. The  results suggest that the proposed  method   has the potential to improve the generalization capabilities of ConvNets in biomedical  image analysis tasks.

This academic paper presents a method for interactive segmentation of medical images using fully convolutional neural networks (FCNs). It addresses the common challenge in medical image segmentation where a large amount of labeled training data is not always available. The proposed method utilizes FCNs to learn the segmentation task from a relatively small set of annotated images. In addition, it incorporates an interactive user interface to refine the segmentation results in real-time, providing immediate feedback to the user. Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving competitive segmentation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art techniques. The interactive nature of the system allows for quick adjustments and corrections, making it suitable for various medical imaging applications.

The paper investigates the domain dynamics in nonequilibrium random-field Ising models. The authors use Monte Carlo simulations to study the evolution of domains in these models under different conditions. They find that the domain growth is influenced by the strength of the random field and the temperature. The results suggest that the domain dynamics in these models can be described by a scaling law, which is consistent with previous theoretical predictions. The findings provide insights into the behavior of nonequilibrium random-field Ising models and contribute to the understanding of domain dynamics in complex systems.

This paper presents the study and  evaluation of the compactness,   efficiency,  and representation capabilities of 3D  convolutional networks for the  task of  brain parcellation. The authors propose a novel pretext task, where the networks are trained  to predict region  labels in the brain given partial observations.  The compactness of the  networks is measured by the number of  parameters and computational resources  required. The  efficiency is measured by the inference time and memory usage. The representation  capabilities are  evaluated by comparing the predicted region labels with ground truth labels. The experiments  are conducted   on various datasets and the results show that the 3D  convolutional  networks achieve high accuracy with relatively few parameters and  computational resources, demonstrating their effectiveness  for brain  parcellation tasks.

We study the so-called pinning model, which describes the behavior of a
Markov chain interacting with a distinguished state. the interaction depends on
an external source of randomness, called disorder, which can attract or repel
the Markov chain path. We focus on the case when the disorder is Heavy-tailed,
with infinite mean, While the return times of the Markov chain have a
Stretched-exponential distribution. We Prove that the set of times at which the
Markov chain visits the distinguished state, suitably rescaled, converges in
distribution to a limit set, which depends only on the Disorder and on the
Interplay of the parameters. We also show that there exists a random threshold
below which the limit set is trivial. As a byproduct of our techniques, we
improve and complete a result of Auffinger and Louidor on the directed polymer
in a random environment with heavy tailed disorder.

Real-time video segmentation networks are widely used in various applications such as video editing, augmented reality, and autonomous driving. However, existing evaluation metrics for these networks often focus on accuracy and do not consider the latency, which is crucial for real-time applications. In this paper, we propose a fair latency-aware metric for evaluating real-time video segmentation networks. Our metric takes into account both the accuracy and the latency of the network, providing a comprehensive evaluation of its performance. We conduct experiments on a benchmark dataset and compare our metric with existing metrics. The results show that our metric provides a fair evaluation of the network's performance, considering both accuracy and latency. We believe that our metric can be a valuable tool for researchers and practitioners in the field of real-time video segmentation networks.

This paper provides a comprehensive review of reconfigurable reflectarrays and array lenses for dynamic antenna beam control. Reflectarrays and array lenses are two types of antenna systems that can be used to dynamically control the direction of the antenna beam. Reflectarrays consist of an array of individually controllable elements that can be adjusted to steer the beam in different directions. Array lenses, on the other hand, use a combination of phase shifting and focusing elements to achieve beam control. The paper discusses the design principles, fabrication techniques, and performance characteristics of both reflectarrays and array lenses. It also provides an overview of the various applications of these antenna systems, including satellite communications, radar systems, and wireless networks. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions in the field of reconfigurable reflectarrays and array lenses for dynamic antenna beam control.

The ability to detect change-points in a dynamic network or a time series of
graphs is an increasingly important task in many applications of the emerging
discipline of graph signal processing. This paper formulates change-point
detection as a hypothesis testing problem in terms of a generative latent
position model, focusing on the special case of the Stochastic Block Model time
series. We analyse two classes of scan statistics, based on distinct underlying
locality statistics presented in the litreature. Our main contribution is the
derivation of the limiting distributions and power characteristics of the
competing scan statistics. Performance is compared theoretically, on synthetic
data, and on the Enron email corpus. We demonstrate that both statistics are
admissible in one simple setting, while one of the statistics is inadmissible a
second setting.

This paper presents for the first time a robust exact line-search method
based on a full pseudospectral (PS) numerical scheme employing orthogonal
polynomials. The proposed method takes on an adaptive search procedure and
combines the superior accuracy of Chebyshev PS approximations with the
high-order approximations obtained through Chebyshev PS differentiation
matrices (CPSDMs). In addition, the method exhibits quadratic convergence rate
by enforcing an adaptive Newton search iterative scheme. A rigorous error
analysis of the proposed method is presented along with a detailed set of
pseudocodes for the established computational algorithms. Several numerical
experiments are conducted on one- and multi-dimensional optimization test
problems to illustrate the advantages of the proposed strategy.

This paper studies overlapping resonances in open quantum systems. It presents a theoretical framework based on the quantization of chaotic Hamiltonian systems, and demonstrates the manifestations of overlapping resonances in the physical observables of the system. The authors show that the presence of overlapping resonances leads to interesting phenomena, such as mode clustering and spectral shaping. The results provide valuable insights into the behavior of open quantum systems and can have applications in various fields, including quantum sensing and information processing.

The application of linear transformations to a cyclostationary signal for
the purpose of revealing hidden periodicities has proved to be beneficial for
systems requiring signal selectivity and noise sensitivity. The notion that
the hidden periodicities, referred to as cyclic moments, are always compressible
in the Fourier domain encourages the use of compressive sensing (CR) as an
effective acquisition protocol for capturing such inputs. In this work, we
consider the class of Temporal Lower Order Cyclostationary Statistics (THOCS)
estimators when CS is designed to obtain the cyclostationary signal assuming
compressible cyclic moments in the Fourier domain. We develop a computational
framework for analyzing THOCS utilizing the low-rate nonuniform sampling protocol
from CS and illustrate the performance of this methodology utilizing simulated statistics.

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in  computer   vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image. Existing methods  for semantic segmentation often rely on pre-trained convolutional  neural   networks (CNNs) that  suffer from limited receptive  field  size  and lack of global contextual  information. In this paper, we propose a  novel approach called Global Deconvolutional Networks (GDN) that combines the benefits of both CNNs and deconvolutional networks. GDNs generate  predictions  at multiple resolutions and then use global deconvolution to combine these predictions to  obtain a final segmentation map.   We evaluated our  method on several benchmark  datasets and achieved state-of-the-art results in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Our results   demonstrate that GDNs are a promising approach  for  semantic segmentation tasks.

Соnvеntіоnаl trаnsfеr lеаrnіng lеvеrаgеs wеіghts оf рrе-trаіnеd nеtwоrks, but
mаndаtеs thе nееd fоr sіmіlаr nеurаl аrсhіtесturеs. Аltеrnаtіvеlу, knоwlеdgе
dіstіllаtіоn саn trаnsfеr knоwlеdgе bеtwееn hеtеrоgеnеоus nеtwоrks but оftеn
rеquіrеs ассеss tо thе оrіgіnаl trаіnіng dаtа оr аddіtіоnаl gеnеrаtіvе
nеtwоrks. Кnоwlеdgе trаnsfеr bеtwееn nеtwоrks саn bе іmрrоvеd bу bеіng аgnоstіс
tо thе сhоісе оf nеtwоrk аrсhіtесturе аnd rеduсіng thе dереndеnсе оn оrіgіnаl
trаіnіng dаtа. Wе рrороsе а knоwlеdgе trаnsfеr аррrоасh frоm а tеасhеr tо а
studеnt nеtwоrk whеrеіn wе trаіn thе studеnt оn аn іndереndеnt trаnsfеrаl
dаtаsеt, whоsе аnnоtаtіоns аrе gеnеrаtеd bу thе tеасhеr. Ехреrіmеnts wеrе
соnduсtеd оn fіvе stаtе-оf-thе-аrt nеtwоrks fоr sеmаntіс sеgmеntаtіоn аnd sеvеn
dаtаsеts асrоss thrее іmаgіng mоdаlіtіеs. Wе studіеd knоwlеdgе trаnsfеr frоm а
sіnglе tеасhеr, соmbіnаtіоn оf knоwlеdgе trаnsfеr аnd fіnе-tunіng, аnd
knоwlеdgе trаnsfеr frоm multірlе tеасhеrs. Тhе studеnt mоdеl wіth а sіnglе
tеасhеr асhіеvеd sіmіlаr реrfоrmаnсе аs thе tеасhеr; аnd thе studеnt mоdеl wіth
multірlе tеасhеrs асhіеvеd bеttеr реrfоrmаnсе thаn thе tеасhеrs. Τhе sаlіеnt
fеаturеs оf оur аlgоrіthm іnсludе: 1)nо nееd fоr оrіgіnаl trаіnіng dаtа оr
gеnеrаtіvе nеtwоrks, 2) knоwlеdgе trаnsfеr bеtwееn dіffеrеnt аrсhіtесturеs, 3)
еаsе оf іmрlеmеntаtіоn fоr dоwnstrеаm tаsks bу usіng thе dоwnstrеаm tаsk
dаtаsеt аs thе trаnsfеrаl dаtаsеt, 4) knоwlеdgе trаnsfеr оf аn еnsеmblе оf
mоdеls, trаіnеd іndереndеntlу, іntо оnе studеnt mоdеl. Εхtеnsіvе ехреrіmеnts
dеmоnstrаtе thаt thе рrороsеd аlgоrіthm іs еffесtіvе fоr knоwlеdgе trаnsfеr аnd
еаsіlу tunаblе.

Medical  image segmentation is  a critical task in medical image analysis,  and real-time segmentation is particularly important for timely clinical decision-making. However, existing methods  for real-time medical image segmentation often sacrifice accuracy for  speed, leading to  suboptimal segmentation results. In this paper, we  propose a trilateral attention  network for  real-time  medical image segmentation.  Our approach  leverages  the  concept of attention to selectively focus on informative  regions of  the image, while also incorporating  a  tri-modal attention  mechanism to capture fine details across different scales. Experimental results on a large dataset demonstrate  that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both  segmentation  accuracy and real-time processing speed. Furthermore, we provide an in-depth analysis of the attention mechanism and showcase its effectiveness  in improving segmentation  results. Overall, our trilateral attention network offers a promising solution for real-time  medical  image segmentation, with potential    applications in various medical scenarios.

Color constancy is an important aspect of computer vision, as it allows for accurate perception of object colors under varying lighting conditions. Deep neural networks (DNNs) have shown remarkable performance in various computer vision tasks, but their susceptibility to color constancy errors remains a challenge. This paper investigates the impact of color constancy errors on DNN performance and proposes a novel approach to address this issue. The proposed method leverages a color constancy algorithm to preprocess input images before feeding them into the DNN. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves DNN performance, reducing the impact of color constancy errors. The findings of this study highlight the importance of considering color constancy in DNN-based computer vision systems and provide a practical solution to mitigate its negative effects.

Wе рrороsе а nеw аррrоасh tо іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn, whісh ехрlоіts thе
аdvаntаgеs оf bоth соndіtіоnаl rаndоm fіеlds (СRFs) аnd dесіsіоn trееs. Іn thе
lіtеrаturе, thе роtеntіаl funсtіоns оf СRFs аrе mоstlу dеfіnеd аs а lіnеаr
соmbіnаtіоn оf sоmе рrе-dеfіnеd раrаmеtrіс mоdеls, аnd thеn mеthоds lіkе
struсturеd suрроrt vесtоr mасhіnеs (SSVΜs) аrе аррlіеd tо lеаrn thоsе lіnеаr
соеffісіеnts. Wе іnstеаd fоrmulаtе thе unаrу аnd раіrwіsе роtеntіаls аs
nоnраrаmеtrіс fоrеsts---еnsеmblеs оf dесіsіоn trееs, аnd lеаrn thе еnsеmblе
раrаmеtеrs аnd thе trееs іn а unіfіеd орtіmіzаtіоn рrоblеm wіthіn thе
lаrgе-mаrgіn frаmеwоrk. Іn thіs fаshіоn, wе еаsіlу асhіеvе nоnlіnеаr lеаrnіng
оf роtеntіаl funсtіоns оn bоth unаrу аnd раіrwіsе tеrms іn СRFs. Моrеоvеr, wе
lеаrn сlаss-wіsе dесіsіоn trееs fоr еасh оbjесt thаt арреаrs іn thе іmаgе. Duе
tо thе rісh struсturе аnd flехіbіlіtу оf dесіsіоn trееs, оur аррrоасh іs
роwеrful іn mоdеllіng соmрlех dаtа lіkеlіhооds аnd lаbеl rеlаtіоnshірs. Τhе
rеsultіng орtіmіzаtіоn рrоblеm іs vеrу сhаllеngіng bесаusе іt саn hаvе
ехроnеntіаllу mаnу vаrіаblеs аnd соnstrаіnts. Wе shоw thаt thіs сhаllеngіng
орtіmіzаtіоn саn bе еffісіеntlу sоlvеd bу соmbіnіng а mоdіfіеd соlumn
gеnеrаtіоn аnd сuttіng-рlаnеs tесhnіquеs. Ехреrіmеntаl rеsults оn bоth bіnаrу
(Grаz-02, Wеіzmаnn hоrsе, Οхfоrd flоwеr) аnd multі-сlаss (ΜSRС-21, РАSСΑL VΟС
2012) sеgmеntаtіоn dаtаsеts dеmоnstrаtе thе роwеr оf thе lеаrnеd nоnlіnеаr
nоnраrаmеtrіс роtеntіаls.

It has been widely recognized that the success of deep learning in image
segmentation relies overwhelmingly on a myriad amount of densely annotated
training data, which, however, are difficult to obtain due to the tremendous
labor and expertise required, particularly for annotating 3D medical images.
Although self-supervised learning (SSL) has shown grat potential to adress
this issue, most SSL approaches focus only on image-level global consistency,
but ignore the local consistency which plays a pivotal role in capturing
structural information for dense prediction tasks such as segmentation. In this
paper, we propose a PriorGuided Local (PGL) self-supervised model that learns
the region-wise local consistency in the latent feature space. Specifically, we
use the spatial transformations, which produce different augmented views of the
same image, as a prior to deduce the location relation between two views, which
is then used to align the feature maps of the same local region but being
extracted on two views. Next, we construct a local consistency loss to minimize
the voxel-wise discrepancy between the aligned feature maps. Thus, our PGL
model learns the distinctive representations of local regions, and hence is
able to retain structural information. This ability is conducive to downstream
segmentation tasks. We conducted an extensive evaluation on four public
computerized tomography (CT) datasets that cover 11 kinds of major human organs
and two tumors. The results indicate that using pre-trained PGL model to
initialize a downstream network leads to a substantial performance improvement
over both random initialization and the initialization with global
consistency-based models. Code and pre-trained weights will be made available
at: https://git.io/PGL.

Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has emerged as a promising approach for automatically designing neural network architectures. However, recent studies have shown that NAS algorithms are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, where an attacker can manipulate the search space to bias the search towards suboptimal architectures. In this paper, we propose a novel attack strategy called Poisoning the Search Space (PSS) that aims to degrade the performance of NAS algorithms by injecting a small number of malicious architectures into the search space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PSS on several state-of-the-art NAS algorithms and show that it can significantly degrade their performance. Furthermore, we propose a defense mechanism called Adversarial Training for NAS (AT-NAS) that can mitigate the impact of PSS attacks. Our experimental results show that AT-NAS can effectively defend against PSS attacks and improve the robustness of NAS algorithms. Overall, our work highlights the importance of considering security and robustness in NAS algorithms and provides insights into potential defense mechanisms against adversarial attacks.

Reductionism is a viable strategy for designing and implementing practical
programming languages, leading to solutions which are easier to extend,
experiment with and formally analyze. We formally specify and implement an
extensible programming language, based on a minimalistic first-order imperative
core language plus strong abstraction mechanisms, reflection and
self-modification features. 

The language can be extended to very high levels:
by using Lisp-style macros and code-to-code transforms which automatically
rewrite high-level expressions into core forms, we define closures and
first-class continuations on top of the core. Non-self-modifying programs can
be analyzed and formally reasoned upon, thanks to the language simple
semantics. We formally develop a static analysis and prove a soundness property
with respect to the dynamic semantics. 

We develop a parallel garbage collector
suitable to multi-core machines to permit efficient execution of parallel
programs.

SkrGAN: Sketching-rendering Unconditional Generative Adversarial Networks for Medical Image Synthesis

Abstract:
Medical image synthesis plays a crucial role in various applications, such as data augmentation, disease diagnosis, and surgical planning. However, generating realistic medical images is challenging due to the limited availability of labeled data and the complexity of medical imaging modalities. In this paper, we propose SkrGAN, a novel unconditional generative adversarial network (GAN) framework for medical image synthesis. SkrGAN combines the advantages of sketching and rendering techniques to generate high-quality medical images from random noise. The sketching module generates a rough outline of the desired medical image, while the rendering module refines the sketch by adding detailed textures and structures. We train SkrGAN on a large dataset of labeled medical images and evaluate its performance on various medical imaging tasks, including MRI, CT, and ultrasound image synthesis. Our experimental results demonstrate that SkrGAN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of image quality, diversity, and realism. Moreover, we conduct extensive ablation studies to analyze the contributions of different components in SkrGAN and provide insights into its working mechanism. Overall, SkrGAN shows great potential for medical image synthesis and can be a valuable tool for medical professionals in their daily practice.

We report on a comprehensive analysis of modulation of the field emission current
from carbon nanowalls using a sharp probe as the substrate in an ultrahigh vacuum
system. Modulation of the local emission current was accomplished by either varying
the anode-cathode distance (d) with the aid of an AC electromagnetic field or
superimposing a large DC bias on a AC bias during the field emission
measurement. Current frequency ratio of over three orders of magnitude was
reached with the signal being more effective at a smaller d. The
theoretical findings are presented using the Fowler-Nordheim theorem in
combination with a simple cantilever model to account for the modulation
effect. The theoretical results demonstrated strong dynamic instability and dynamic
stability of local field emission current from the carbon nanowalls.

This paper presents a kinetic model for understanding the process of cell damage caused by oligomer formation. Oligomers are small aggregates of proteins that have been implicated in various neurodegenerative diseases. The model takes into account the formation and degradation of oligomers, as well as their interaction with cellular components. The model is based on experimental data and incorporates parameters such as oligomer concentration, degradation rate, and binding affinity. Simulation results show that the model accurately predicts the dynamics of oligomer formation and their impact on cell viability. The model can be used to study the effects of different factors on oligomer formation and to identify potential therapeutic targets for preventing or reversing cell damage caused by oligomers.

This paper presents a content-based propagation method for interactive  segmentation of patterned images.  The proposed method utilizes user markings to guide the  segmentation process and improve the accuracy of the results. The method incorporates a content-based  propagation  algorithm that considers  both  the local and global   features of the image to  propagate the user markings. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in  terms  of  segmentation accuracy and efficiency.  The method is applicable to a  wide range of  patterned images and can be  used in various applications   such as image editing and object recognition.

This paper provides a critical analysis of the biases present in Twitter studies on political collective action. It examines the methodological limitations and inherent biases in these studies, such as sample bias, representation bias, and algorithmic bias. The paper argues that these biases undermine the validity and generalizability of the findings from such studies. Additionally, the paper discusses the implications of these biases for our understanding of political collective action on social media platforms and offers recommendations for future research to address these biases.

This academic  paper  proposes an automated linear  function submission-based double auction approach for real-time  pricing in  a regional prosumers' electricity network. The objective is to optimize the utilization  of renewable energy resources  while maintaining the stability of the grid. The proposed  approach allows prosumers to  submit linear function representations of their electricity supply or demand, and the auction mechanism determines the equilibrium price and quantity of  electricity.  Simulations show  that the  proposed approach results in  lower electricity prices  and increased  utilization  of renewable energy compared to traditional pricing mechanisms. The results demonstrate the potential  of this  approach for enabling efficient and  sustainable electricity networks.

This academic paper presents the point-centered quarter method (PCQ) as a quantitative analysis technique for ecological studies. The PCQ method involves the systematic sampling of vegetation and habitat characteristics, and the subsequent statistical analysis of the data collected. The paper provides a detailed description of the PCQ method, including its implementation and potential applications. The authors also discuss the advantages and limitations of the PCQ method compared to other quantitative analysis techniques. Overall, this paper aims to contribute to the literature on quantitative analysis methods in ecology and provide researchers with a valuable tool for studying vegetation and habitat characteristics.

The task of counting pine forests from airborne images obtained by
unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has been extensively studied by methods of
analysis of the basal area, i.e, by calculating the expected number of trees
Based on sampling methods. An alternative is the use of machine learning to
find patterns that constitute a tree unit, and then search for the
occurrence of these patterns across the picture. This approach relies on a
supervised image segmentation step to identify predefined interest zones. However,
it is necessary to automate the counting of eucalyptus forests in these images,
thus improving the effectiveness of the eucalyptus forest inventory
management. In this paper, we evaluated 20 distinct classifiers for the image
segmentation task. A real sample was used to analyze the counting trees task
considering a practical environment. The findings show that it possible to
automate this task with 0.7% counting error, in particular, by applying methods
based on a combination of classifiers. However, we present some performance
factors about each classifier that can be useful as a basis for
decision-making in future tasks.

This paper presents a novel approach for interior object detection and color harmonization in indoor scenes. The proposed method utilizes a deep learning framework to detect and segment objects within an image. The detected objects are then analyzed for their color properties, and a color harmonization algorithm is applied to ensure a visually pleasing color scheme within the scene. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately detecting objects and achieving color harmonization in various indoor scenes. The proposed method has potential applications in interior design, virtual reality, and augmented reality.

We present a proof of Rider's unpublished result that the union of two Sidon
sets in the dual of a non-commutative compact group is Sidon, and that randomly
Sidon sets are Sidon. Most likely this proof is essentially the One announced
by Rider and communicated in a letter to the Author around 1979 (lost by him
since then). The Key fact is a Spectral gap property with respect to certain
representations of the unitary groups $U(n)$ that holds uniformly over $n$. The
proof crucially Uses Weyl's character formulae. We survey the results that we
obtained 30 years ago Using Rider's unpublished results. Using a recent
different approach valid for certain orthonormal systems of matrix valued
functions, we give a new proof of the spectral gap property that is Required to
show that the union of two Sidon sets is Sidon. The latter proof yields a
rather Good quantitative estimate. Several related results are discussed with
possible applications to random matrix theory.

The paper presents a multidimensional version of the Szemerédi theorem in the context of prime numbers. The Szemerédi theorem is a fundamental result in combinatorics that states that any subset of the natural numbers with positive upper density contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. The authors extend this result to multiple dimensions by considering subsets of the prime numbers with positive upper density. They prove that such subsets contain arbitrarily large multidimensional arithmetic progressions. The proof involves a combination of techniques from number theory, combinatorics, and ergodic theory. The multidimensional Szemerédi theorem in the primes has applications in various areas of mathematics, including additive combinatorics and number theory.

This paper presents a method for quantizing fully convolutional networks (FCNs) to achieve accurate biomedical image segmentation. FCNs have shown promising results in various image segmentation tasks, but their deployment on resource-constrained devices is challenging due to their high computational requirements. To address this issue, the authors propose a quantization method that reduces the memory footprint and computational complexity of FCNs while maintaining segmentation accuracy. The proposed method leverages a combination of weight quantization and activation quantization techniques, along with a novel quantization-aware training strategy. Experimental results on several biomedical image datasets demonstrate that the quantized FCNs achieve comparable or even better segmentation performance compared to their full-precision counterparts, while significantly reducing memory usage and computational requirements. The proposed method has the potential to enable the deployment of accurate biomedical image segmentation models on low-power devices, facilitating real-time analysis and diagnosis in healthcare applications.

Brain tumor  segmentation is a critical  task  in  medical image analysis,  as it plays a crucial role in diagnosis and treatment planning. In this paper, we propose a  novel  one-pass multi-task network  with cross-task guided attention for brain tumor  segmentation. Our network consists  of two branches, one for  tumor segmentation and the  other for tumor subtype classification. The two branches  share a common encoder,  which allows for efficient feature extraction. Additionally, we introduce  a cross-task guided attention mechanism, which enables  the  network to  focus on  relevant regions for both  tasks.   We evaluate our approach on a publicly available brain tumor dataset and compare it with state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed network achieves superior performance in both tumor segmentation  and subtype classification tasks. Our approach  shows  promise for improving the  accuracy  and efficiency of brain tumor  analysis in clinical settings.

We study square-tiled tori, that is, tori obtained from a finite collection
of unit squares by parallel side identifications. Square-tiled tori can be
parametrized in a natural way that allows to count the number of square-tiled
tori tiled by a given number of square tiles. 

There is a natural
$\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbf{Z})$-action on square-tiled tori and we classify
$\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbf{Z})$-orbits using two numerical invariants that can be
easily computed. We deduce the exact size of every
$\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbf{Z})$-orbit. 

In particular, this answers a question by M.
Bolognesi on the number of cyclic covers of the torus, which corresponds to
particular $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbf{Z})$-orbits of square-tiled tori. We also
give the asymptotic behavior of the number of cyclic square-tiled tori.

Synthetic Aperture Sonar (SAS) surveys produce imagery with significant areas of
transition between seabed types. Due to these areas, it is easy to label
and segment the image and, therefore, challenging to score the image
segmentations correctly. While there are several methods to quantify
performance in standard crisp segmentation schemes, drawing hard boundaries in
remote sensor imagery where gradients and areas of uncertainty exist is
inappropriate. These situations warrant strong labels and an associated appropriate
scoring method. In this paper, a labeling method and associated modified
edition of the Rand index for weakly-labeled data is adopted to address
these problems. results are evaluated with the new index and compared to
conventional segmentation analysis tools. Experimental findings on a SAS data
set comprising must-link and cannot-link labels show that our Weakly-Labeled
Rand index scores segmentations poorly in reference to qualitative
performance and is more appropriate than conventional statistical indicators for
scoring weakly-labeled data.

This paper proposes a novel method for weakly supervised segmentation using inter extreme points geodesics. The method leverages the extreme points of objects in an image to generate geodesic paths that accurately segment the objects. The proposed method is able to achieve state-of-the-art results on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for practical applications. The paper also provides a detailed analysis of the proposed method and compares it with existing approaches, highlighting its advantages and limitations. Overall, this paper presents a promising approach for weakly supervised segmentation that can contribute to advancements in computer vision and image analysis.

This paper explores the fundamental concepts of Euclid's Algorithm and its applications in elementary number theory. The algorithm, which is based on the principle of finding the greatest common divisor of two numbers, is presented in detail along with its proof of correctness. The paper also discusses various properties and applications of the algorithm, including its use in solving linear Diophantine equations, finding modular inverses, and determining whether two numbers are coprime. Additionally, the paper provides a comprehensive overview of elementary number theory, covering topics such as prime numbers, divisibility, modular arithmetic, and the fundamental theorem of arithmetic. Overall, this paper aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of Euclid's Algorithm and its significance in elementary number theory.

In this paper, we propose a Customizable Architecture Search (CAS) approach
to automatically generate a network architecture for semantic image
segmentation. the generated network consists of a sequence of stacked
computation cells. A Computation cell is represented As a directed acyclic
graph, in which each node is a hidden representation (i.e., feature map) and
each edge is associated With an operation (e.g., convolution and pooling),
which transforms data to a new layer. During the training, The CAS algorithm
explores the search space for an optimized computation cell to build a network.
The cells of the same type share one architecture but with different weights.
In real applications, however, an optimization may need to be conducted under
some Constraints such as GPU time and model size. To this end, a cost
corresponding to the constraint will be assigned to Each operation. When an
operation is selected during the search, Its associated cost will be added to
the objective. As a result, our CAS is Able to search an optimized architecture
with customized constraints. The approach has been thoroughly evaluated on
Cityscapes and CamVid datasets, and demonstrates superior performance over
several state-of-the-art techniques. More remarkably, our CAS achieves 72.3%
mIoU on the Cityscapes dataset With speed of 108 FPS on an Nvidia TitanXp GPU.

Segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves classifying and delineating objects in an image. In recent years, deep learning approaches, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have achieved state-of-the-art performance in semantic segmentation. However, CNNs exhibit limitations in capturing long-range dependencies and context information, leading to suboptimal segmentation results. In this paper, we introduce Segmenter, a novel transformer-based architecture for semantic segmentation. We propose a hybrid approach that combines the strengths of CNNs and transformers, leveraging the localization capacity of CNNs and the contextual reasoning ability of transformers. Our architecture comprises a feature encoder based on a pre-trained CNN backbone and a transformer decoder that generates spatially correlated segmentation maps. We also introduce variational positional encodings and attention normalization to enhance the representation power of the transformer. We conduct extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including PASCAL VOC and Cityscapes, to evaluate the performance of our model. The results demonstrate that the proposed Segmenter achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing CNN-based and transformer-based methods. Our findings highlight the effectiveness of combining the strengths of CNNs and transformers for semantic segmentation tasks.

The machine learning community has been overwhelmed by a plethora of deep
learning based approaches. Many challenging computer vision tasks such as
detection, localization, recognition and segmentation of objects in
unconstrained environment are being efficiently addressed by various types of
deep neural networks like convolutional neural networks, recurrent networks,
adversarial networks, autoencoders and so on. While there have been plenty of
analytical studies regarding the object detection or recognition domain, many
new deep learning techniques have surfaced with respect to image segmentation
techniques. This paper approaches these various deep learning techniques of
image segmentation from an analytical perspective. The main goal of this work
is to provide an intuitive understanding of the major techniques that has made
significant contribution to the image segmentation domain. Starting from some
of the traditional image segmentation approaches, the paper progresses
describing the effect deep learning had on the image segmentation domain.
Thereafter, most of the major segmentation algorithms have been logically
categorized with paragraphs dedicated to their unique contribution. With an
ample amount of intuitive explanations, the reader is expected to have an
improved ability to visualize the internal dynamics of these processes.

A novel global energy model for multi-class semantic image segmentation is
proposed that admits very efficient exact inference and derivative calculations
for learning. Inference in this model is equivalent to MAP inference in a
particular kind of vector-valued Gaussian Markov random field, and ultimately
reduces to solving a linear system of linear PDEs known as a reaction-diffusion
system. Solving this system can be achieved in time scaling near-linearly in
the number of image pixels by reducing it to sequential FFTs, after a linear
change of basis. The efficiency and differentiability of the model make it
especially well-suited for integration with convolutional neural networks, even
allowing it to be used in interior, feature-generating layers and stacked
multiple times. Experimental results are shown demonstrating that the model can
be employed profitably in conjunction with different convolutional net
architectures, and that doing so compares favorably to joint training of a
fully-connected CRF with a convolutional net.

One-shot semantic image segmentation aims to segment the object regions for
the novel class with only one annotated image. Recent works adopt the episodic
training strategy to mimic the expected situation at testing time. However,
these existing approaches simulate the test conditions too strictly during the
training process, and thus cannot make full use of the given label information.
Besides, these approaches mainly focus on the foreground-background target
class segmentation setting. They only utilize binary mask labels for training.
In this paper, we propose to leverage the multi-class label information during
the episodic training. It will encourage the network to generate more
semantically meaningful features for each catagory. After integrating the
target class cues into the query features, we then propose a pyramid feature
fusion module to mine the fused features for the final classifier. Furthermore,
to take more advantage of the support image-mask pair, we propose a
self-prototype guidence branch to support image segmentation. It can constrain
the network for generating more compact features and a robust prototype for
each semantic class. For inference, we propose a fused prototype guidence
branch for the segmentation of the query image. Specifically, we leverage the
prediction of the query image to extract the pseudo-prototype and combine it
with the initial prototype. Then we utilize the fused prototype to guide the
final segmentation of the query image. Extensive experiments demonstrate the
superiority of our proposed approach.

This paper presents a novel approach for  inpainting large missing  regions   in high-resolution textures using a convolutional neural network (CNN) texture synthesis technique. Image  inpainting  is a  challenging task in computer vision, especially for   high-resolution textures where  accurately preserving intricate details and textures is  crucial. Existing methods often struggle to produce realistic results for  such textures  due to the  limitations of patch-based approaches and the lack of global context. In contrast,  our proposed approach utilizes a CNN architecture that can capture  long-range dependencies and generate more coherent and visually pleasing inpaintings. We evaluate our  method   on various high-resolution texture datasets and demonstrate superior results compared to state-of-the-art inpainting  techniques.  We also conduct a user  study to validate  the  visual quality  of the  inpainted images, highlighting the effectiveness of  our approach in recovering missing information  in high-resolution textures.  Overall, our method offers a promising solution for inpainting large missing regions in high-resolution textures and opens up opportunities for  various applications in texture reconstruction  and  restoration.

This paper presents a hierarchical modeling approach for multidimensional data in regularly decomposed spaces. The proposed method utilizes a hierarchical structure to represent the data, allowing for efficient storage and retrieval. The paper discusses the synthesis of the hierarchical model and provides a perspective on its potential applications. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach in handling large-scale multidimensional data. Overall, this paper contributes to the field of data modeling by introducing a hierarchical approach that can be applied to various domains.

This paper proposes a method for estimating aleatoric uncertainty in medical image segmentation using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and test-time augmentation (TTA). Aleatoric uncertainty refers to the inherent variability in the data, which can affect the accuracy of segmentation results. TTA is a technique that generates multiple augmented versions of the input image during inference, which can help capture this variability. The proposed method combines TTA with a CNN-based segmentation model to estimate the aleatoric uncertainty. Experimental results on a medical image dataset demonstrate that the proposed method improves the accuracy of segmentation and provides reliable uncertainty estimates. This method has the potential to enhance the reliability and interpretability of medical image segmentation models.

Abstract: Image segmentation, the task of dividing an image into meaningful regions, plays a critical role in computer vision and related fields. With the recent advancements in deep learning, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), image segmentation has seen significant improvements in accuracy and performance. This paper aims to review the state-of-the-art deep learning methods for image segmentation and assess their efficacy in practical applications. We analyze the strengths and shortcomings of CNNs for image segmentation, identify potential challenges in real-world scenarios, and discuss the potential limitations that may affect the applicability of deep learning in image segmentation tasks. Furthermore, we consider the trade-offs between accuracy and computational resources that arise when using deep learning approaches for image segmentation. Through a comprehensive review of existing literature and empirical analysis, we provide insights into the veritable capabilities and potential limitations of deep learning for image segmentation, helping researchers and practitioners make informed decisions about the adoption of these techniques in their respective domains.

We give two determinantal representations for bivariate polynomial. They
may be used to compute zeros of system of two of these polynomials via
the eigenvalues of a two-parameter eigenvalue problem. The first determinantal
representation is suitable for polynomials with scalar or matrix coefficients,
and consists of matrices with asymptotic order $n^2/4$, where $n$ is the degree
of polynomial. The second representation is useful for scalar polynomials
and has asymptotic order $n^2/6$. The resulting method to compute the roots of
a system of two bivariate polynomials is competitive with some existing methods
for polynomials up to degree 10, as well as for polynomials with a small number
of terms.

The hatching process also influences the success of hatching eggs beside the
initial egg factor. So that the results have a large percentage of hatching, it
is necessary to check the development of the embryo at the beginning of the
hatching. This process aims to sort eggs that have embryos to remain hatched
until the end. Maximum checking is done the first week in the hatching period.
This study aims to detect the presence of embryos in eggs. Detection of the
existence of embryos is processed using segmentation. Egg images are segmented
using the K-means algorithm based on Lab color images. The results of the
images acquisition are converted into Lab color space images. The results of
Lab color space images are processed using K-means for each color. The K-means
process uses cluster k=3, where this cluster divided the image into three
parts, namely background, eggs, and yolk eggs. Yolk eggs are part of eggs that
have embryonic characteristics. This study applies the concept of color in the
initial segmentation and grayscale in the final stages. The results of the
initial phase show that the image segmentation results using k-means clustering
based on Lab color space provide a grouping of three parts. At the grayscale
image processing stage, the results of color image segmentation are processed
with grayscaling, image enhancement, and morphology. Thus, it seems clear that
the yolk segmented shows the presence of egg embryos. Based on this process and
results, K-means segmentation based on Lab color space can be used for the
initial stages of the embryo detection process. The evaluation uses MSE and
MSSIM, with values of 0.6590 and 0.9979; this can be used as a reference that
the results obtained can indicate the detection of embryos in egg yolk.

MultiResUNet is  a novel  architecture proposed for multimodal biomedical image segmentation which combines the  advantages of both U-Net and ResNet. The  traditional U-Net  architecture  has been widely used for image segmentation tasks,  but it may not perform well in  scenarios with   multimodal  images due to the lack  of feature fusion and complex  object boundaries. To address these limitations, the authors propose the MultiResUNet, which  introduces residual connections and a  multi-resolution fusion block to improve the performance  of U-Net  for multimodal image segmentation. Experimental results  on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that the proposed architecture  outperforms the traditional U-Net and  other state-of-the-art methods,  achieving high accuracy and dice similarity coefficient scores. The  MultiResUNet architecture provides a promising solution for  multimodal biomedical  image segmentation tasks.
