This paper proposes an efficient 3D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture for action/object segmentation in video. Traditional convolutional neural networks are designed for 2D images and lack the ability to effectively capture temporal dependencies in videos. The proposed model extends the traditional 2D CNN to a 3D CNN by incorporating an additional temporal dimension. The network is trained on a large dataset of video clips with pixel-level annotation for action/object segmentation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed 3D CNN outperforms traditional 2D CNNs and achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets. The model also demonstrates computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-time video analysis applications. Overall, the proposed 3D CNN provides an effective and efficient solution for action/object segmentation in video.

Since the generative neural networks have made a breakthrough in the image
generation problem, lots of researches on their applications have been studied
such as image restoration, style transfer and image completion. However, there
has been few research generating objects in uncontrolled real-world
environments. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for vehicle image
generation in real-world scenes. Using a subnetwork based on a precedent work
of image completion, our model makes the shape of an object. Details of objects
are trained by an additional colorization and refinement subnetwork, resulting
in a better quality of generated objects. Unlike many other works, our method
does not require any segmentation layout but still makes a plausible vehicle in
the image. We evaluate our method by using images from Berkeley Deep Drive
(BDD) and Cityscape datasets, which are widely used for object detection and
image segmentation problems. The adequacy of the generated images by the
proposed method has also been evaluated using a widely utilized object
detection algorithm and the FID score.

This paper examines the dynamics of conflicts in Wikipedia, a popular online collaborative encyclopedia. The study analyzes the patterns and characteristics of conflicts that arise within the Wikipedia community, as well as the factors that contribute to their escalation or resolution. The research utilizes a combination of quantitative and qualitative methods, including data mining and content analysis, to identify and analyze conflict-related events and their outcomes. The findings reveal that conflicts in Wikipedia are multifaceted and can be triggered by various factors, such as content disputes, personal conflicts, and power struggles. The study also highlights the role of community norms, governance mechanisms, and dispute resolution processes in managing and resolving conflicts. The implications of these findings for the sustainability and effectiveness of online collaborative platforms are discussed, along with recommendations for improving conflict management strategies in Wikipedia and similar online communities.

This paper investigates the formation and behavior of holes and cracks in rigid foam films. Rigid foam films are widely used in various applications such as insulation and packaging. The authors characterize the dynamics of hole and crack formation using high-speed imaging techniques. They also study the influence of film thickness, temperature, and mechanical properties on the formation and expansion of holes and cracks. The results of this study provide insights into the fracture behavior of rigid foam films and can be used to optimize their performance in practical applications.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach for selective image super-resolution, which aims to enhance the resolution of specific regions of interest in an image while leaving the rest of the image unchanged. Our method combines convolutional neural networks with a new attention mechanism that allows the network to selectively focus on different regions of the image. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a diverse range of images and show that it outperforms existing methods in terms of both subjective and objective evaluations. We also provide insights into the inner workings of our network through visualizations and analysis of the attention maps. Overall, our proposed method provides a promising solution for selective image super-resolution, with applications in various fields such as medical imaging and surveillance.

Being able to effectively identify clouds and monitor their evolution is one
important step toward more accurate quantitative precipitation estimation and
forecast. In this study, a new gradient-based cloud-image segmentation
technique is developed using tools from image processing techniques. This
method integrates morphological image gradient magnitudes to separable cloud
systems and patches boundaries. A varying scale-kernel is implemented to reduce
the sensitivity of image segmentation to noise and capture objects with various
finenesses of the edges in remote-sensing images. The proposed method is
flexible and extendable from single- to multi-spectral imagery. Case studies
were carried out to validate the algorithm by applying the proposed
segmentation algorithm to synthetic radiances for channels of the Geostationary
Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES-R) simulated by a high-resolution
weather prediction model. The proposed method compares favorably with the
existing cloud-patch-based segmentation technique implemented in the
PERSIANN-CCS (Precipitation Estimation from Remotely Sensed Information using
Artificial Neural Network - Cloud Classification System) rainfall retrieval
algorithm. Evaluation of event-based images indicates that the proposed
algorithm has potential to improve rain detection and estimation skills with an
average of more than 45% gain comparing to the segmentation technique used in
PERSIANN-CCS and identifying cloud regions as objects with accuracy rates up to
98%.

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into different regions or objects. In recent years,  deep learning techniques   have shown promising results  in various computer vision tasks, including image segmentation. This  paper presents SegNet,  a deep convolutional  encoder-decoder architecture specifically designed for image segmentation. The proposed  architecture consists of an encoder network that  extracts   high-level features from the  input image and a decoder network that reconstructs the segmented image. The  encoder network utilizes a series of  convolutional and  pooling layers   to progressively downsample the input image, while the decoder network uses  upsampling and deconvolutional layers to recover the spatial resolution  of the  segmented  image. Additionally, skip connections are introduced to preserve fine-grained  details during the upsampling process. Experimental results  on benchmark datasets demonstrate   that SegNet achieves state-of-the-art performance in image segmentation tasks, outperforming existing  methods in terms of  accuracy and efficiency. The proposed architecture shows great   potential for various applications,   such as  medical imaging, autonomous driving, and object  recognition.

Membrane curvature sensing plays a crucial role in many cellular processes, including membrane trafficking, cell division, and organelle formation. Here, we investigate the ability of amphipathic peptides to sense and respond to anisotropic membrane curvature. Through molecular dynamics simulations and experimental studies, we demonstrate that these peptides have a strong preference for sensing highly curved membranes with asymmetric curvature profiles. Our findings suggest that amphipathic peptides can act as key regulators of membrane curvature and provide insight into the mechanisms underlying their curvature-sensing capabilities. Understanding the role of these peptides in membrane remodeling may have implications for the development of new therapeutic strategies targeting membrane curvature-related diseases.

The "bag-of-frames" approach (BOF), which encodes audio signals as the
long-term statistical distribution of short-term spectral features, is commonly
regarded as an effective and sufficient way to represent environmental sound
recordings (soundscapes) since its introduction in an influential 2007 article.
The present paper describes a concep-tual replication of this seminal article
using several new soundscape datasets, with results strongly questioning the
adequacy of the BOF approach for the task. We show that the good accuracy
originally re-ported with BOF likely result from a particularly thankful
dataset with low within-class variability, and that for more realistic
datasets, BOF in fact does not perform significantly better than a mere
one-point av-erage of the signal's features. Soundscape modeling, therefore,
may not be the closed case it was once thought to be. Progress, we ar-gue,
could lie in reconsidering the problem of considering individual acoustical
events within each soundscape.

This paper proposes a new approach for image segmentation based on a contrario reasoning. The goal is to partition an image into regions corresponding to different objects or regions of interest. The proposed algorithm starts by generating a large number of candidate partitions and then selects the optimal one using a novel a contrario reasoning framework. The algorithm takes into account both local and global features of the image to determine the optimal partition. Experimental results on a variety of images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in producing accurate and visually appealing image segmentation results.

In a  k-linear triangulated  category (where k is a field) we show that the
existence of Auslander-Reiten triangles implies that objects  are  determined,  up
to shift,  by knowing dimensions of homomorphisms between them. In most cases
the objects  themselves  are distinguished  by this  information, a conclusion
which was also  reached  under slightly different hypotheses in a theorem of
Jensen, Su and Zimmermann. The approach is to consider bilinear forms on
Grothendieck groups  which are analogous to the  Green ring of a finite group.
   We specialize to  the category of perfect complexes for a self-injective
algebra, for which the Auslander-Reiten quiver has a known shape. We
characterize the position in  the quiver of many kinds  of perfect  complexes,
including those of lengths 1, 2 and 3,  rigid complexes and truncated  projective
resolutions. We describe completely the quiver  components which contain
projective modules. We  obtain relationships between  the homology of complexes
at different places in  the  quiver,  deducing that  every self-injective algebra
of  radical length at  least 3 has indecomposable perfect complexes with
arbitrarily large  homology in any given degree. We find also that homology
stabilizes away from the  rim of the quiver. We show that when  the algebra is
symmetric, one of the forms considered earlier is Hermitian, and  this allows  us
to  compute its  values   knowing  them  only on objects  on the rim of the quiver.

The paper proposed a novel mutual consistency neural network (MC-Net+) to improve the performance of semi-supervised image segmentation by combining labeled and unlabeled data. The MC-Net+ model is motivated by the observation that deep neural networks, when limited data is used to train, tend to make inaccurate and easily misclassified prediction at ambiguous regions (such as narrow branches and glued edges) for image segmentation. With these difficult data samples at the region level, semi-supervised image segmentation models can be trained more effectively. So the proposed MC-Net+ model is composed of two new designs: the first is that the model contains one common encoder and multiple slightly different decoders. Using different up-sampling methods, the difference between the probabilities predicted by the different decoders is calculated as the uncertainty of the model. It can be used to identify the unlabeled difficult regions; the second is that the new constraint of mutual consistency is introduced between one decoder's probabilities and other decoders' soft labels. Then the difference between the soft labels of different decoders can be minimized, and the invariant and low-entropy features of the difficult regions are learned. In the experiments, a comparison of the results of MC-Net+ with five semi-supervised models on three public medical images was made. The experiments on two common semi-supervised settings also show that our method has higher performance than other methods, and the new semi-supervised method for medical image segmentation has been established.

This academic paper investigates Diophantine approximations for translation surfaces and planar resonant sets.  The  authors  develop a method  for constructing explicit metrics  on  compact surfaces where the Diophantine exponents can be computed  explicitly. They also introduce a new notion of  resonant sets in planar  domains, which they  refer  to  as "planar resonant sets". The authors provide several applications of their results, including estimating the number of resonances in a region and studying the  equidistribution  properties of orbits under the  geodesic flow. Overall, this paper  contributes to the  understanding of Diophantine approximations for translation surfaces  and provides new insights into planar  resonant sets.

This paper presents a novel approach for soft-thresholding in both discrete and continuous-time domains with dynamic inputs. The proposed method utilizes a dynamic thresholding function that adapts to the changing input signal. The discrete-time soft-thresholding algorithm is derived using a recursive formulation, while the continuous-time soft-thresholding algorithm is obtained by solving a differential equation. The performance of the proposed algorithms is evaluated through simulations and compared with existing methods. The results demonstrate that the dynamic soft-thresholding approach outperforms traditional methods in terms of signal recovery and noise reduction. This research contributes to the field of signal processing by providing a new framework for soft-thresholding that can effectively handle dynamic inputs.

This paper proposes a semi-supervised domain adaptation method called Adaptive and Progressive Feature Alignment (APFA). The method aims to improve the performance of classifiers on a target domain by leveraging unlabeled data from both the source and target domains. APFA iteratively aligns the feature distributions of the unlabeled data by minimizing the domain discrepancy using a progressive alignment strategy. In each iteration, a classifier is trained using the aligned features and then used to estimate the pseudo-labels of the unlabeled target samples. These pseudo-labels are then used to further refine the alignment of the features. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that APFA outperforms existing domain adaptation methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance on both unsupervised and semi-supervised domain adaptation tasks.

We construct Hamiltonian Floer complexes associated  to  continuous,  and even
lower semi-continuous, time dependent exhaustion functions on  geometrically
bounded  symplectic manifolds. We  further  construct functorial continuation maps
associated to monotone homotopies between them, and operations which  give rise
to a product and unit.  The work rests on novel techniques for energy
confinement of Floer solutions as well as  on methods of Non-Archimedean
analysis. The   definition  for general Hamiltonians  utilizes the notion of
reduced  cohomology familiar from Riemannian geometry, and  the continuity
properties  of Floer cohomology. This gives rise in  particular  to localized
Floer theory. We  discuss various functorial properties as well as some
applications to existence of periodic orbits and to displaceability.

In this paper, we study the nesting statistics in the $O(n)$ loop model on random maps of arbitrary topologies. We consider a lattice model where loops of $n$ different colors are randomly placed on a two-dimensional lattice. We investigate the distribution of nested loops, which are loops that are completely contained within another loop. We derive exact expressions for the average number of nested loops and the average size of nested loops in the thermodynamic limit. We also analyze the scaling behavior of the nesting statistics as a function of the loop length and the lattice size. Our results provide insights into the behavior of the $O(n)$ loop model on random maps and can be applied to various physical systems, such as polymers and spin systems.

Let $R$ be an artin algebra and $\mathcal{C}$ an additive  subcategory of
$\operatorname{mod}(R)$. We construct  a $t$-structure   on the homotopy category
$\operatorname{K}^{-}(\mathcal{C})$ whose  heart $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{C}}$ is
a natural  domain for higher Auslander-Reiten (AR) theory. The abelian
categories $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{mod}(R)}$ (which is the  natural domain
for classical AR theory) and $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{C}}$ interact via  various
functors. If  $\mathcal{C}$ is functorially finite then
$\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{C}}$  is a quotient category of
$\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{mod}(R)}$. We illustrate the theory  with two
examples:
   Iyama developed a higher AR theory when  $\mathcal{C}$ is a maximal
$n$-orthogonal subcategory, see \cite{I}. In this case we show that  the simple
objects of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{C}}$ correspond to Iyama's  higher AR
sequences and derive his higher AR duality  from the existence of a Serre
functor   on the   derived  category
$\operatorname{D}^b(\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{C}})$.
   The category $\mathcal{O}$ of a complex semi-simple Lie algebra
$\mathfrak{g}$ fits into higher AR theory by  considering $R$ to be the
coinvariant   algebra of the   Weyl group of  $\mathfrak{g}$.

A key problem in salient object detection is how to effectively model the
semantic properties of salient objects in a data-driven manner. In this paper,
we propose a multi-task deep saliency model based on a fully convolutional
neural network (FCNN) with global input (whole raw images) and global output
(whole saliency maps). In principle, the proposed saliency model takes a
data-driven strategy for encoding the underlying saliency prior information,
and then sets up a multi-task learning scheme for exploring the intrinsic
correlations between saliency detection and semantic image segmentation. Through collaborative feature learning from such two correlated tasks, the
shared fully convolutional layers produce effective features for object
perception. 

Moreover, it is capable of capturing the semantic information on
salient objects across different levels using the fully convolutional layers,
which investigate the feature-sharing properties of salient object detection
with great feature redundancy reduction. 

Finally, we present a graph Laplacian
regularized nonlinear regression model for saliency refinement. 

Experimental
results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in comparison with the
state-of-the-art approaches.

In this paper we prove some conjectures of Laborde-Zubieta on the enumeration of angles in tree-like tableaux and symmetric tree-like tableaux. Besides, we enumerate the angles in permutation tableaux of type B and symmetric alternative tableaux. The proof is based on the bijection of Corteel and Nadeau between permutation tableaux and permutations. Besides, we give a bijection between angles and permutation-sets of length one, which gives an alternative proof of the enumeration of angles. Then we give a bijection between angles and sequences of length one in permutations, which gives an alternative proof of the enumeration of angles. Finally we introduce conjectured polynomial analogues of these enumerations and explain the implication of these enumerations in the theory of PASEP.

This paper presents an information-theoretic derivation of min-cut based clustering, a popular method for partitioning data into clusters. The authors propose a novel approach that leverages the concept of mutual information to measure the similarity between data points and determine the optimal cut that minimizes the information loss. The derived clustering algorithm is shown to outperform existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The theoretical analysis and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in various clustering tasks. Overall, this paper provides a new perspective on min-cut based clustering and contributes to the advancement of information-theoretic clustering algorithms.

This paper presents AinnoSeg, a novel approach for panoramic segmentation with high performance. The proposed method utilizes a deep learning framework to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation of panoramic images. AinnoSeg incorporates a panoramic feature extraction module to capture the unique characteristics of panoramic images, followed by a segmentation module that utilizes a modified U-Net architecture. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on various benchmark datasets, outperforming existing methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of AinnoSeg in various segmentation tasks, including object segmentation and semantic segmentation. The proposed method has the potential to be applied in various real-world applications, such as autonomous driving and virtual reality.

  Τhе lіmіts оf thе соrrеsроndіng К\"аhlеr роlаrіzаtіоns bесоmе dеgеnеrаtе

Strategy improvement is a widely-used and well-studied class of algorithms
for solving graph-based infinite games. These algorithms are parameterized by a
switching rule, and one of the most natural rules is "all switches" which
switches as many edges as possible in each iteration. 

Continuing a recent line
of work, we study all-switches strategy improvement from the perspective of
computational complexity. 

We consider two natural decision problems, both of
which have as input a game $G$, a starting strategy $s$, and an edge $e$. The
problems are: 1.) 

The edge switch problem, namely, is the edge $e$ ever
switched by all-switches strategy improvement when it is started from $s$ on
game $G$? 2.) The optimal strategy problem, namely, is the edge $e$ used in the
final strategy that is found by strategy improvement when it is started from
$s$ on game $G$? We show $\mathtt{PSPACE}$-completeness of the edge switch
problem and optimal strategy problem for the following settings: Parity games
with the discrete strategy improvement algorithm of V\"oge and Jurdzi\'nski;
mean-payoff games with the gain-bias algorithm [14,37]; and discounted-payoff
games and simple stochastic games with their standard strategy improvement
algorithms. 

We also show $\mathtt{PSPACE}$-completeness of an analogous problem
to edge switch for the bottom-antipodal algorithm for finding the sink of an
Acyclic Unique Sink Orientation on a cube.

This paper presents a multi-task deep learning approach for image segmentation by utilizing recursive approximation tasks. The proposed method leverages the ability of deep neural networks to learn multiple tasks simultaneously, and enhances it with recursive approximation tasks to improve segmentation accuracy. The Recursive Approximation Network (RAN) is developed, which consists of multiple subnetworks, each responsible for a specific approximation task. The subnetworks are trained jointly with the main segmentation task, facilitating the transfer of knowledge across tasks and enhancing the overall performance. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The effectiveness of the recursive approximation tasks is demonstrated through ablation studies and analysis of learned representations. Overall, this work highlights the potential of multi-task deep learning and recursive approximation tasks for image segmentation tasks.

This  paper explores the concept of  crepant resolutions  and  their relationship to open strings in the context of  string  theory. Crepant resolutions are a mathematical tool used to resolve singularities in algebraic varieties, and  they have been shown to have important implications in string theory. The paper presents a detailed  analysis  of the  mathematical properties of crepant resolutions and their connection  to open strings. The authors also  discuss the physical implications of crepant resolutions in the context  of  string theory,  including  their  role in understanding the  behavior of D-branes and the emergence of gauge theories. The paper concludes with a discussion of  future  directions  for research in this area.

We present ObSuRF, a method which turns a single image of a scene into a 0D
model represented as a set of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs), with each NeRF
corresponding to a different object. A single forward pass of an encoder
network outputs a set of latent vectors describing the objects in the scene.
These vectors are used independently to condition a NeRF decoder, defining the
geometry and appearance of each object. We make learning more computationally
efficient by deriving a novel loss, which allows training NeRFs on RGB-D inputs
without explicit ray marching. After confirming that the model performs equal
or better than state of the art on three 4D image segmentation benchmarks, we
apply it to two multi-object 3D datasets: A multiview version of CLEVR, and a
novel dataset in which scenes are populated by ShapeNet models. We find that
after training ObSuRF on RGB-D views of training scenes, it is capable of not
only recovering the 3D geometry of a scene depicted in a single input image,
but also to segment it into objects, despite receiving no supervision in that
regard.

We present a model of articular cartilage lesion formation to simulate the
effects of cyclic loading. This model extends and modifies the
reaction-diffusion-delay model by Graham et al. 2012 for the spread of lesion
formed though single traumatic event. Our model represents "implicitly" the
effects of loading, meaning through a cyclic sink term in equations for
live cells.
  Our model forms the basis for in silico studies of cartilage damage relevant
to questions in osteoarthritis, for example, that may not be easily answered
through in vivo or in vitro studies.
  Computational results are presented that indicate impact of differing
levels of EPO on articular cartilage lesion abatement.

Directional infrared emission at 1367 and 5230 nm is generated in Rb vapours
that are step-wise excited by low-power resonant light. The mid-infrared
radiation originating from amplified spontaneous emission on the 5D-6P
transition consists of forward- and backward-directed components with
distinctive spectral and spatial properties. Diffraction limited near-infrared
light at 1367 nm generated in the co-propagating direction only is a product of
parametric wave mixing around the 5P-5D-6P-6S-5P transition loop. This highly
non-degenerate mixing process involves one externally applied and two
internally generated optical fields. Similarities between wave mixing generated
blue and near-IR light are demonstrated.

In this paper, we consider unsupervised partitioning issues, such as
clustering, image segmentation, video segmentation and other change-point
detection issues. We focus on partitioning solutions based specifically or
explicitly on the minimization of Euclidean distortions, which involve
mean-based change-point detection, K-means, spectral clustering and normalized
cuts. Our primary objective is to develop a Mahalanobis metric for these unsupervised
problems, leading to feature weighting and/or selection. This is done in a
supervised manner by considering the availability of multiple potentially partially
labelled data that share the same metric. We cast the metric learning
problem as a large-margin structured analysis problem, with proper definition
of regularizers and losses, leading to a convex optimization problem which can
be resolved easily with iterative methods. We provide experiments where
we show how learning the metric can greatly reduce the partitioning
efficiency in synthetic examples, bioinformatics, video segmentation and image
segmentation problems.

This paper provides a pedestrian outlook on the potential modifications and advancements in jet technology that may occur in the next decade. It explores various areas of jet modification, including engine efficiency, noise reduction, and environmental impact. The paper discusses the current state of jet technology and highlights the challenges and opportunities for improvement. It also examines the potential impact of emerging technologies, such as electric propulsion and alternative fuels, on jet modification. The paper concludes with a discussion on the potential benefits and implications of these modifications for the aviation industry and society as a whole.

This paper explores  the  benefits  of linear  conditioning  with  metadata for image segmentation. Image segmentation is a  crucial  task  in computer vision,  and recent advancements  have  shown  the effectiveness  of deep learning models for this task. However, these models often require a large amount of labeled  data for training, which  can  be  expensive and time-consuming to obtain. In this  paper,  we propose a novel approach that leverages metadata information to improve the performance of image segmentation models.  Specifically, we introduce a linear conditioning mechanism that incorporates metadata features into the model's  architecture. We conduct experiments on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of  segmentation accuracy.  Furthermore,   we show that our method is able to achieve comparable performance  with significantly   fewer labeled samples, making it a  more cost-effective solution for image segmentation  tasks. Overall, our findings  highlight the potential benefits of linear conditioning with metadata for improving the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation models.

The paper introduces a new method for calculating stochastic distances between relaxed complex Wishart distributions. These distances are of interest in many applications, including statistical inference and machine learning. The authors derive analytic expressions for these distances, allowing for efficient computation and comparison. The accuracy of the derived expressions is demonstrated through numerical experiments. The proposed method offers a valuable tool for analyzing and comparing relaxed complex Wishart distributions in various research domains.

Multi-atlas segmentation approach is one of the most widely-used image
segmentation techniques in biomedical applications. There are two major
challenges in this category of methods, i.e., atlas selection and label fusion.
In this paper, we propose a novel multi-atlas segmentation method that
formulates multi-atlas segmentation in a deep learning framework for better
solving these challenges. The proposed method, dubbed deep fusion net (DFN), is
a deep architecture that integrates a feature extraction subnet and a non-local
patch-based label fusion (NL-PLF) subnet in a single network. The network
parameters are learned by end-to-end training for automatically learning deep
features that enable optimal performance in a NL-PLF framework. The learned
deep features are further utilized in defining a similarity measure for atlas
selection. By evaluating on two public cardiac MR datasets of SATA-13 and LV-09
for left ventricle segmentation, our approach achieved 0.833 in averaged Dice
metric (ADM) on SATA-13 dataset and 0.95 in ADM for epicardium segmentation on
LV-09 dataset, comparing favorably with the other automatic left ventricle
segmentation methods. We also tested our approach on Cardiac Atlas Project
(CAP) testing set of MICCAI 2013 SATA Segmentation Challenge, and our method
achieved 0.815 in ADM, ranking highest at the time of writing.

Thalamus segmentation plays a critical role in studying various brain disorders and understanding functional connectivity. This paper presents a novel multi-contrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) approach for thalamus segmentation. Our method utilizes multiple MRI contrasts, including T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and diffusion-weighted images, to leverage the complementary information they provide. We propose a deep learning framework that combines convolutional neural networks and recurrent neural networks to achieve accurate and robust thalamus segmentation. Experimental results on a large dataset demonstrate the superiority of our approach compared to state-of-the-art methods and highlight the potential of multi-contrast MRI for improved thalamus segmentation. Overall, this paper contributes to advancing the field of neuroimaging by presenting a promising technique for thalamus segmentation using multi-contrast MRI.

This paper proposes a novel approach for instrument segmentation in robotic surgery using unsupervised learning with cycle-consistent adversarial networks (CycleGANs). The goal is to automatically segment surgical instruments from the background in surgical videos without the need for manual annotations. The proposed method leverages the cycle-consistency property of CycleGANs to learn a mapping between the instrument and background domains, enabling the generation of synthetic instrument images from background images and vice versa. The generated synthetic images are then used to train a segmentation model, which is evaluated on a dataset of real surgical videos. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting instruments in robotic surgery, highlighting its potential for improving surgical workflow and assisting surgeons in real-time.

This research paper proposes a novel method for segmenting eye fundus images using a deep neural convolution network with a convex shape prior. The authors argue that incorporating shape priors can improve accuracy and facilitate the segmentation process. They evaluate their proposed method on a dataset of eye fundus images, comparing it with other state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed convex shape prior approach outperforms existing methods, achieving higher accuracy and better segmentation results. The authors conclude that incorporating a convex shape prior can enhance the performance of deep neural convolution networks for eye fundus image segmentation.

The collisions of bremsstrahlung and pair production in a medium can be coherent for a long distance in the high-energy limit, and this causes a suppression known as the Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal (LPM) effect. In this paper we continue the study of the situation when the coherence of two consecutive breakings is shared (a case which is of interest for correcting the usual calculation of the LPM effect in QCD), avoiding the soft-gluon approximation. In particular, this paper considers the subtle problem of separating double breaking (for example, double bremstreakhs) from the case of independent bremstreakhs (the case which is treated by the conventional Monte Carlo simulation based only on the rate of the single breaking). We illustrate the method by calculating the rate of real double bremstreakhs from an initial gluon under certain assumptions (thick media, small *, large Nc and the neglect of a moment for a process at a four-gluon vertex) and explicitly obtaining the correction to the rate due to the overlapping coherence of the two breakings.

In this review, intended for non-specialists and beginners, we recount the
current status of the concept of jet modification in dense matter. We commence
with an overview of the "classical" observables which can be calculated
without recourse to event generators. These involve double and dual neutron
suppression, nuclear modification factor versus reaction plane etc. All of
these measurements are designed to justify both the required underlying physical
picture of plane modification as well as the final obtained values of jet
transport parameters. This is accompanied by a review of the more sophisticated
observables which have emerged with the ability to reconstruct full jets, and
the problems posed therein. This is accompanied by a preview of upcoming
scientific advances in the field and an outlook on how the interface
between these technologies, theoretical changes, and upcoming data
will allow you to accurately identify properties of the medium which effect
the modification of hard jets.

Residual amplitude modulation (RAM) is a common phenomenon in interferometric gravitational wave (GW) detectors that can significantly degrade the sensitivity of these instruments. RAM arises from various sources, including imperfect optics, non-linearities in the photo-detectors, and environmental disturbances. In this paper, we present a comprehensive review and analysis of RAM in GW detectors, focusing on its origin, measurement techniques, and mitigation strategies. We discuss the impact of RAM on the sensitivity of GW detectors and propose several approaches to mitigate this effect, including active feedback control systems and improved optical designs. Through numerical simulations and experimental data, we demonstrate the effectiveness of these mitigation strategies and provide recommendations for future developments in the field. This paper serves as a valuable resource for researchers and engineers involved in the design and operation of interferometric GW detectors, helping to improve their sensitivity and detection capabilities.

This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation using geodesic paths and implicit region-based homogeneity enhancement. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation by incorporating both local and global information. The geodesic paths are computed based on the gradient of the image, and the homogeneity enhancement is achieved by iteratively updating the region boundaries. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving accurate and efficient image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach for referring segmentation, a task that involves segmenting an object in an image based on a natural language description. The proposed method, called Cross-Modal Progressive Comprehension (CMPC), leverages both visual and textual information to improve the accuracy of segmentation. CMPC consists of two stages: a pre-training stage where a visual-semantic embedding model is trained, and a fine-tuning stage where the model is further optimized using a cross-modal progressive comprehension framework. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that CMPC outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability. The proposed approach has the potential to advance the field of referring segmentation and contribute to the development of more effective computer vision systems.

This paper proposes a novel approach for cross-modality domain adaptation in medical image segmentation. The proposed method, called Synergistic Image and Feature Adaptation (SIFA), aims to address the challenge of adapting segmentation models trained on one modality to another modality with limited labeled data. SIFA leverages both image-level and feature-level adaptation techniques to effectively transfer knowledge from the source modality to the target modality. Experimental results on two publicly available medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving superior segmentation performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The findings of this study highlight the potential of SIFA for improving the generalization and applicability of medical image segmentation models across different modalities.

Segmentation of the left atrium (LA) from cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is crucial for the diagnosis and treatment of various cardiac diseases. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for LA segmentation by combining global shape priors and local intensity priors through mixture modeling. We first apply a global shape prior to guide the general shape of the LA. Then, we use an autoencoder to learn the local intensity distribution of the LA. We incorporate these priors into a mixture model and employ an expectation-maximization algorithm to iteratively estimate the segmentation. Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy. Our proposed framework has the potential to improve the clinical workflow and assist in the diagnosis and treatment of cardiac diseases.

Although having achieved great success in medical image segmentation, deep
convolutional neural networks usually require large dataset with manual
annotations for training and are difficult to generalize to unseen classes.
Few-shot learning has the potential to address these challenges by learning new
classes from only few labeled examples. In this work, we propose a new
framework for few-shot medical image segmentation based on prototypical
networks. Our innovation lies in design of two key modules: 1) a context
relation encoder (CRE) that uses correlation to capture local relation features
between foreground and background regions; and 2) a recurrent mask refinement
module that repeatedly uses the CRE and prototypical network to recapture the
change of context relationship and refine the segmentation mask iteratively.
Experiments on two abdomen CT datasets and abdomen MRI dataset show the
proposed method obtains substantial improvement over state-of-the-art
methods by an average of 16.32%, 8.45% and 6.24% in terms of DSC, respectively.
Code is publicly available.

Producing manual, pixel-accurate, image segmentation labels is tedious and
time-consuming. This is often a rate-limiting factor when large amounts of
labelled images are required, such as for training deep convolutional networks
for instrument-background segmentation in surgical scenes. No large datasets
comparable to industry standards in the computer vision community are available
for this task. To circumvent this problem, we propose to automate the creation
of a realistic training dataset by exploiting techniques stemming from special
effects and harnessing them to target training performance rather than visual
appeal. Foreground data is captured by placing sample surgical instruments over
a chroma key (a.k.a. green screen) in a controlled environment, thereby making
extraction of the relevant image segment straightforward. Multiple lighting
conditions and viewpoints can be captured and introduced in the simulation by
moving the instruments and camera and modulating the light source. Background
data is captured by collecting videos that do not contain instruments. In the
absence of pre-existing instrument-free background videos, minimal labelling
effort is required, just to select frames that do not contain surgical
instruments from videos of surgical interventions freely available online. We
compare different methods to blend instruments over tissue and propose a novel
data augmentation approach that takes advantage of the plurality of options. We
show that by training a vanilla U-Net on semi-synthetic data only and applying
a simple post-processing, we are able to match the results of the same network
trained on a publicly available manually labelled real dataset.

Advances in the diagnosis of complex manufacturing and biological processes have made it necessary to unconsciously develop a decision process on the fly. However, most of the existing unsupervised methods are either too expensive or require a manual setting of the flow capacities (e.g., in a maximum-flow or a minimum-cut method). In this paper we propose a fully unsupervised segmentation method that enables continuous maximal-flow computation on the image domain, while obtaining the flow parameters from the characteristics of the image. We show that the maximum-a posteriori estimation of image attributes can be formulated as a continuous flow problem, where the flow capacities are known. The flow capacities are obtained iteratively using a novel Markov random field prior on the image domain. We provide theoretical results that demonstrate the consistency of the flow capacities. We test our method on two real-world applications, brain tumor image segmentation and the classification of defects in a medical device using a scanning electron microscope. The experimental results show that our method has similar performance as a few existing supervised and unsupervised methods and yields a more than 90% improvement in the Dice score when compared with the unsupervised methods.

Medical image segmentation is a critical task in healthcare, but it often requires a large amount of labeled data for training accurate models. In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised contrastive learning approach for label-efficient medical image segmentation. Our method leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to learn representations that capture the underlying structure and semantics of medical images. We integrate a contrastive loss function into the segmentation framework to encourage the model to pull together instances of the same class and push apart instances of different classes, using both labeled and unlabeled data. Experimental results on two medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate that our semi-supervised approach achieves superior performance compared to supervised methods that use only labeled data. Our approach significantly reduces the reliance on labeled data, making it a promising solution for label-efficient medical image segmentation.

Quasi-power law ensembles are discussed from the viewpoint of nonextensive
Tsallis distributions defined by a nonextensive parameter $q$. A number
of probable sources of such distributions are given in more detail. It is
further demonstrated that data suggest that nonextensive values deduced
from Tsallis distributions functions $f\left(p_T\right)$, $q_1$, and from
multiplicity distributions (connected with Tsallis entropy), $q_2$, are not
similar and that they are linked via $q_1 + q_2 = 2$. It is often shown
that Tsallis distributions can be derived indirectly from Shannon information
entropy, provided some special restrictions are imposed. They are connected with
the type of computational systems under consideration (additive or
inverse). However, it is demonstrated how a Tsallis distribution can
accommodate the log-oscillating behaviour also shown in some multiparticle
data.

Τhіs wоrk рrороsеs thе usе оf Вауеsіаn аррrохіmаtіоns оf unсеrtаіntу frоm
dеер lеаrnіng іn а rоbоt рlаnnеr, shоwіng thаt thіs рrоduсеs mоrе саutіоus
асtіоns іn sаfеtу-сrіtісаl sсеnаrіоs. Τhе саsе studу іnvеstіgаtеd іs mоtіvаtеd
bу а sеtuр whеrе аn аеrіаl rоbоt асts аs а "sсоut" fоr а grоund rоbоt. Τhіs іs
usеful whеn thе bеlоw аrеа іs unknоwn оr dаngеrоus, wіth аррlісаtіоns іn sрасе
ехрlоrаtіоn, mіlіtаrу, оr sеаrсh-аnd-rеsсuе. Ιmаgеs tаkеn frоm thе аеrіаl vіеw
аrе usеd tо рrоvіdе а lеss оbstruсtеd mар tо guіdе thе nаvіgаtіоn оf thе rоbоt
оn thе grоund. Ехреrіmеnts аrе соnduсtеd usіng а dеер lеаrnіng sеmаntіс іmаgе
sеgmеntаtіоn, fоllоwеd bу а раth рlаnnеr bаsеd оn thе rеsultіng соst mар, tо
рrоvіdе аn еmріrісаl аnаlуsіs оf thе рrороsеd mеthоd. Α соmраrіsоn wіth sіmіlаr
аррrоасhеs іs рrеsеntеd tо роrtrау thе usеfulnеss оf сеrtаіn tесhnіquеs, оr
vаrіаtіоns wіthіn а tесhnіquе, іn sіmіlаr ехреrіmеntаl sеttіngs. Тhе mеthоd іs
аnаlуzеd tо аssеss thе іmрасt оf vаrіаtіоns іn thе unсеrtаіntу ехtrасtіоn, аs
wеll аs thе аbsеnсе оf аn unсеrtаіntу mеtrіс, оn thе оvеrаll sуstеm wіth thе
usе оf а dеfіnеd mеtrіс whісh mеаsurеs surрrіsе tо thе рlаnnеr. Тhе аnаlуsіs іs
реrfоrmеd оn multірlе dаtаsеts, shоwіng а sіmіlаr trеnd оf lоwеr surрrіsе whеn
unсеrtаіntу іnfоrmаtіоn іs іnсоrроrаtеd іn thе рlаnnіng, gіvеn thrеshоld vаluеs
оf thе hуреrраrаmеtеrs іn thе unсеrtаіntу ехtrасtіоn hаvе bееn mеt. Wе fіnd
thаt tаkіng unсеrtаіntу іntо ассоunt lеаds tо раths thаt соuld bе 18% lеss
rіskу оn аn аvеrаgе.

This paper reports a CPU-level real-time sound matching technique for surgical
images (10 MHz on 640 * 480 image with a single core of i5-9400). The proposed
technique is built on the fast ''dense inverse searching'' algorithm, which
estimates the disparity of the stereo images. The overlapping photo patches
(arbitrary squared image segment) from the images at various scales are
aligned based on the photometric consistency presumption. We propose a statistical
methodology to consider the probability of the optimal patch disparity at
various scales. Specifically, we introduce a spatial Gaussian mixed probability
distribution to address the pixel-wise probability within the patch. In-vivo
and synthetic studies show that our technique can handle errors caused
from the textureless surfaces and the photometric inconsistency caused by the
Lambertian reflectance. Our statistical approach accurately balances the probability
of the patch for stereo images at various scales. Experiments demonstrate that
the estimated depth has greater precision and less outliers than the baseline
methods in the surgical scenario.

This paper presents new results on classical and quantum counter automata. Counter automata are a type of finite automaton that use a counter to keep track of the number of occurrences of a certain event. The paper first introduces the concept of classical counter automata and provides a formal definition. It then presents new results on the expressive power of classical counter automata, showing that they can recognize languages that cannot be recognized by other types of automata. The paper also introduces the concept of quantum counter automata, which are counter automata that operate on quantum states. It presents a formal definition of quantum counter automata and discusses their expressive power. The paper concludes with a comparison of classical and quantum counter automata and discusses potential applications of these models in various fields.

pictures, lower resolution detailed image segmentation gets far more
attention. In this paper, we propose and study a task called Meticulous Object
Segmentation (MOS), which is focused on analyzing well-defined foreground
objects with elaborate patterns in low resolution images (e.g. 2k - 4k). To this
end, we propose the MeticulousNet which uses a dedicated decoder to
capture the object boundary details. Accordingly, we design a Hierarchical
Point-wise Refining (HierPR) block to better identify object borders, and
reformulate the decoding procedure as a recursive coarse to fine refinement of
the object mask. To improve segmentation quality near object borders, we
propose the Meticulosity Value (MQ) score comparing both the mask coverage
and boundary precision. In addition, we collect a MOS benchmark database
featuring 600 low quality photos with complex objects. We offer
extensive statistical proof proving that MeticulousNet can reveal
pixel-accurate segmentation boundaries and is comparable to state-of-the-art
techniques for low resolution object segmentation tasks.

Contemporary deep-learning based medical image segmentation requires annotating labor of the experts. The data-hungry deep models show inferior performance when there is limited annotated data. In this paper, we propose a data-efficient learning framework based on the recent concept of Generative Adversarial Nets (GANs). The proposed method is an extension of our previous work by introducing a new unsupervised adversarial loss and structured prediction architecture. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to demonstrate a structured prediction based on GANs framework for medical image segmentation. We specifically apply our method for retinal blood vessel segmentation. Our experimental study was performed with a very small amount of annotated data (0.8–1.6% of the annotated amount of a contemporary model). On the DRIVE and STARE datasets, the proposed method significantly outperforms our previous work and other supervised models. The experimentally derived annotated data ablation procedure revealed several important factors to effectively train GAN based semi-supervised models with an encoder-decoder style network architecture.

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision and is particularly challenging when dealing with complex networks. In this paper, we propose a general framework for complex network-based image segmentation. The framework utilizes the structural properties of complex networks to achieve accurate and efficient image segmentation. We present a novel algorithm that incorporates network-based clustering and graph-cut methods to segment images. Performance evaluation on several benchmark datasets demonstrates that our proposed framework outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. Overall, our framework provides a valuable tool for image segmentation in the context of complex networks.

Segmentation is one of the key problems in hyperspectral image processing. Recently, deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have become a powerful model in the context of object segmentation and object recognition, demonstrating excellent results. However, a graphical model such as a conditional random field can capture more information from the data and improve the accuracy of the segmentation. In this paper, we propose a method to simultaneously consider the spatial and spectral information of hyperspectral images by combining CNNs and conditional random fields. Using multiple spectral cubes to learn deep features, we construct a deep conditional random field by formulating potential functions based on CNN-learned unary and pairwise potential functions to effectively extract the semantic relationship between the patches that consist of multiple cubes. In addition, a practical conditional random field is used to avoid the expensive iterative iterative training of conditional random fields. In addition, a deep deconvolution network is introduced to enhance the performance of the region extraction. Finally, we introduce a new data set and test the performance of our proposed method using this new data set and other widely used data sets to evaluate the effectiveness of the method. The evaluation results are compared with the results of several state-of-the-art models and show that the proposed method has promising potential.

The paper introduces a new convolutional neural network architecture called Fast Fully Octave Convolutional Neural Network (FFO-Net) for document image segmentation. The proposed network utilizes octave convolutions, which operate at multiple scales and hierarchical representations, to effectively capture features across different levels of abstraction. These octave convolutions are implemented using a combination of traditional convolutions and low-pass filtering operations, resulting in a more efficient and faster network compared to existing methods. The FFO-Net is trained on a large-scale dataset of document images and achieves superior performance in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency compared to state-of-the-art segmentation networks. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, making it a promising solution for document image segmentation tasks.

In last few years, Deep Learning (DL) has been showing superior
performance in different modalities of biomedical image analysis. Several DL
architectures have been proposed for classification, segmentation, and
detection tasks in medical imaging and computational pathology. In this paper,
we propose a new DL architecture, the NABLA-N network, with better feature
fusion techniques in decoding units for dermoscopic image segmentation tasks.
The NABLA-N network has several advances for segmentation tasks. First, this
model ensures better feature representation for semantic segmentation with a
combination of low to high-level feature maps. Second, this network shows
better quantitative and qualitative results with the same or fewer network
parameters compared to other methods. In addition, Inception Recurrent
Residual Convolutional Neural Network (IRRCNN) model is used for skin cancer
classification. The proposed NABLA-N network and IRRCNN models are evaluated
for skin cancer segmentation and classification on benchmark datasets from
the International Skin Imaging Collaboration 2018 (ISIC-2018). The experimental
results show superior performance on segmentation tasks compared to the
Recurrent Residual U-Net (R2U-Net). The classification model shows around 87%
testing accuracy for dermoscopic skin cancer classification on ISIC2018
dataset.

MeanShift is a  popular mode-seeking clustering algorithm used in a wide range
of applications in machine learning. However, it is  known to  be prohibitively
slow, with  quadratic runtime per  iteration. We propose MeanShift++, an
extremely fast mode-seeking algorithm  based on MeanShift that uses a grid-based
approach to speed up the mean shift step, replacing the  computationally
expensive neighbors search   with a density-weighted mean of adjacent grid cells.
In  addition, we show  that this grid-based technique  for   density estimation
comes with theoretical guarantees.  The runtime is linear   in  the number of
points and exponential in dimension,  which makes MeanShift++ ideal on
low-dimensional applications such as image  segmentation and object tracking. We
provide extensive experimental analysis showing  that MeanShift++ can  be more
than 10,000x faster than  MeanShift with competitive clustering results on
benchmark datasets and nearly identical  image segmentations  as MeanShift.
Finally, we show promising results for object tracking.

It has been the object of intense study, both in the way of analysis and of evolution of the methods of min-cut clustering, which have been based on a heuristic cost function introduced by Shi and Malik. It is still not known if this heuristic can be derived from a more general principle that could lead to a generalization of the problem to other circumstances. In this paper, we establish relationships between the regularized cut in a K-partitioned graph and the importance information as defined by the Information Bottleneck method. On a graph of fast mixing, we show that the cost functions introduced by Shi and Malik are well approximated by the rate of loss of predictability of the location of random walkers on the graph. On a graph generated by a random walk, the best partition obtained by information theoretic methods coincides with the best partition obtained by min-cut.

This paper proposes a novel image segmentation method based on Kullback-Leibler divergence-based fuzzy C-means clustering, incorporating morphological reconstruction and wavelet frames. The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional image segmentation techniques by integrating the advantages of fuzzy clustering, morphological reconstruction, and wavelet frames. The Kullback-Leibler divergence is used as a similarity measure to improve the accuracy of the clustering process. Morphological reconstruction is employed to enhance the segmentation results by removing noise and preserving object boundaries. Wavelet frames are utilized to capture both local and global image features, enabling more accurate segmentation. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method compared to state-of-the-art image segmentation techniques.

Object detection has received much attention recently, and many heuristic models have been proposed. In this paper, we formulate the problem of generating a saliency map as a regression problem. The method is based on multi-level image segmentation and uses the supervised learning method to map the feature of the area to the score of the saliency. In the end, the scores of all the areas at all the levels are combined to produce a saliency map. This paper makes two contributions. The first is to propose a discriminant regional feature integration method for detecting objects. Compared with existing heuristic models, our method can automatically integrate the features of the area with high dimension and select the features with high accuracy; the second is that by considering the common area properties and two well-known concepts for detecting objects, namely, the contrast of the area and the contrast of the background, the proposed method outperforms the existing methods on six commonly used data sets. However, it is just as fast as most existing methods.

This paper examines the structural limitations of learning in Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) by focusing on communication vulnerability and information diffusion. The authors argue that the design and structure of MOOCs can hinder effective communication and information sharing among participants, leading to limited learning outcomes. Through a case study of a popular MOOC platform, the authors analyze the network structure and communication patterns among participants. They find that certain individuals, referred to as "communication hubs," play a crucial role in information diffusion, while others, referred to as "communication isolates," have limited access to information. The authors discuss the implications of these findings for the design and facilitation of MOOCs, highlighting the need for strategies to mitigate communication vulnerability and promote equitable information diffusion. Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding of the structural limitations of learning in MOOCs and provides insights for improving the effectiveness of online learning environments.

This paper investigates the relationship between high order three-term recursions, Riemann-Hilbert minors, and Nikishin systems on star-like sets. The main objective is to establish a connection between these different mathematical concepts and provide a deeper understanding of their interplay. The authors present theoretical results, including the derivation of new formulas and integral representations. Additionally, numerical examples and simulations are provided to illustrate the practical implications of the theoretical findings. The paper concludes with insights into potential applications of these concepts in various fields, such as signal processing and data analysis. Overall, this study contributes to the existing body of knowledge on high order three-term recursions, Riemann-Hilbert minors, and Nikishin systems, and opens up new avenues for further research in these areas.

This paper investigates the universality of the luminosity-metallicity and mass-metallicity relations for compact star-forming galaxies at redshifts 0 < z < 3. The authors analyze a sample of galaxies from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey and the DEEP2 survey, and measure their luminosities, metallicities, and masses. They find that the luminosity-metallicity and mass-metallicity relations hold for compact star-forming galaxies across a wide range of redshifts, suggesting that these relations are universal and not strongly dependent on redshift. This result has important implications for our understanding of galaxy evolution and the processes that regulate the chemical enrichment of galaxies over cosmic time.

This paper presents a novel approach  for few-shot 3D multi-modal  medical image segmentation using generative adversarial learning. The  proposed method leverages a generative  adversarial network (GAN) to  generate synthetic images  that can be used to  augment the limited training data available  for  few-shot   learning.  The GAN is   trained to generate realistic images that  are similar to  the target modality, while also preserving the anatomical structures of interest. The generated images are then used to train a  segmentation network, which  is able  to generalize to new unseen images with only a few  annotated examples. Experimental  results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate the effectiveness  of the proposed approach, achieving   competitive segmentation performance  with significantly fewer training samples compared to traditional methods. The  proposed method has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy  of medical image segmentation tasks, especially in scenarios where annotated  data  is scarce.

In recent years, deep  learning  has rapidly become a method of choice for the
segmentation of medical  images. Deep Neural Network (DNN) architectures such as
UNet have achieved  state-of-the-art results on many medical  datasets. To
further improve the performance in the segmentation task, we develop an
ensemble system which combines various deep learning architectures. We propose
a   two-layer ensemble of deep  learning models for the segmentation of  medical
images. The prediction for each training image  pixel made by each model  in the
first layer  is used as the  augmented data  of  the training image  for the second
layer  of  the ensemble. The prediction of the second layer is  then combined by
using  a weights-based scheme in which each model contributes differently to the
combined result. The  weights  are found by solving linear regression problems.
Experiments conducted on two  popular medical  datasets namely CAMUS and
Kvasir-SEG  show that  the proposed  method achieves better results concerning  two
performance metrics (Dice Coefficient and Hausdorff distance) compared  to some
well-known benchmark algorithms.

Deep learning has been widely accepted as a promising solution for medical
image segmentation, given a sufficiently large representative dataset of images
with corresponding annotations. 

With ever increasing amounts of annotated
medical datasets, it is infeasible to train a learning method always with all
data from scratch. This is also doomed to hit computational limits, e.g.,
memory or runtime feasible for training. 

Incremental learning can be a
potential solution, where new information (images or anatomy) is introduced
iteratively. Nevertheless, for the preservation of the collective information,
it is essential to keep some "important" (i.e. representative) images and
annotations from the past, while adding new information. 

In this paper, we
introduce a framework for applying incremental learning for segmentation and
propose novel methods for selecting representative data therein. We
comparatively evaluate our methods in different scenarios using MR images and
validate the increased learning capacity with using our methods.

The Gaussian core model is a widely used model in statistical physics to study the behavior of particles in high dimensions. In this paper, we investigate the properties of the Gaussian core model in high dimensions and provide a comprehensive analysis of its thermodynamic and structural properties. We derive analytical expressions for the equation of state and the radial distribution function, and compare our results with numerical simulations. Our findings show that the Gaussian core model exhibits interesting phase behavior in high dimensions, including the presence of a liquid-gas phase transition. We also discuss the implications of our results for other models in statistical physics and suggest possible directions for future research. Overall, our study provides valuable insights into the behavior of particles in high dimensions and contributes to the understanding of complex systems in statistical physics.

This paper presents a novel approach for enhancing the resolution of underdrawings in artworks using generative adversarial deep neural networks (GANs) and style transfer techniques. Underdrawings, which are preliminary sketches or outlines hidden beneath the final layers of paint or ink, often suffer from low resolution and visibility. The proposed method leverages the power of GANs to generate high-resolution versions of underdrawings by learning from a dataset of paired low-resolution and high-resolution images. The style transfer technique is then applied to refine the generated images and align them with the original artwork's style. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enhancing the resolution and visibility of underdrawings, providing valuable insights for art restoration and preservation.

Cardiac image  segmentation is  a critical task in medical image analysis, but it often requires a   large amount of annotated data for training deep learning models.  Annotation of medical  images by experts is time-consuming and expensive.  In this  paper, we propose a  novel framework called Dual-Teacher  that integrates both intra-domain and inter-domain teachers to improve  annotation  efficiency in cardiac segmentation. The intra-domain  teacher is trained on a large amount of synthetic  cardiac MRI data to  generate pseudo-labels, while the inter-domain teacher is trained on a  small amount  of manually annotated real cardiac MRI data.  The intra-domain teacher guides the training of  the inter-domain teacher by providing pseudo-labels, which are refined using a self-training strategy. Our  experiments demonstrate  that  the Dual-Teacher framework achieves comparable segmentation performance with the  state-of-the-art methods while reducing  the annotation effort by up to 80%. This work shows promise  for improving  the efficiency  of cardiac segmentation  and has the potential to  be  applied in other medical image  analysis  tasks.

In this paper, we mainly study the stability of iterated polynomials and the linear transformations that preserve the strong q-log-convexity of polynomials. Let n,k denote an array of non-negative numbers. Then we give criteria for the transformation yn (q) = sum_k=0 nT_nk xk (q) that preserve the strong q-log-convexity of xk (q) and show that xk (q) is strong q-log-convex. We prove some linear transformations, such as the two kinds of Stirling transformations, two kinds of Jacobi-Stirling transformations, two kinds of Legendre-Stirling transformations, and central factorial transformations, preserve the strong q-log-convexity in a unified way. By applying the method of interpolating zeros, we establish two criteria for the stability of iterated polynomials and strong q-log-convexity of polynomials. We prove the stability of iterated polynomials implies the strong q-log-convexity. In addition, we prove the alternating sequences, the longest alternating subsequence, and the up-down sequences of permutations are q-log-convex sequences.

Microbial dormancy is a common phenomenon observed in biofilms and planktonic cultures, where a subset of cells enter a dormant state characterized by reduced metabolic activity and increased resistance to environmental stresses. Understanding the mechanisms and dynamics of microbial dormancy is crucial for various applications, including the development of strategies to control biofilm formation and improve the efficacy of antimicrobial treatments. In this paper, we review and compare different models of microbial dormancy in biofilms and planktonic cultures, including the quorum sensing model, the persister cell model, and the bet-hedging model. We discuss the strengths and limitations of each model and highlight the key factors that influence the transition to and from dormancy. Additionally, we explore the implications of microbial dormancy for biofilm formation, antibiotic resistance, and microbial community dynamics. Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of the current understanding of microbial dormancy in biofilms and planktonic cultures and identifies areas for future research.
