IFor a positive rational $l$, we define the concept of an $l$-elliptic and an
$l$-hyperbolic rational set in a metric space. In this article we examine the
existence of (i) dense and (ii) infinite $l$-hyperbolic and $l$-ellitpic
rationals subsets of the real line and unit circle. For the case of a circle,
we prove that the existence of such sets depends on the positivity of ranks of
certain associated elliptic curves. We also determine the closures of such sets
which are maximal in case they are not dense. In higher dimensions, we show the
existence of $l$-ellitpic and $l$-hyperbolic rational infinite sets in unit
spheres and Euclidean spaces for certain values of $l$ which satisfy a weaker
condition regarding the existence of elements of order more than two, than the
positivity of the ranks of the same associated elliptic curves. We also
determine their closures. A subset $T$ of the $k$-dimensional unit sphere $S^k$
has an antipodal pair if both $x,-x\in T$ for some $x\in S^k$. In this article,
we prove that there does not exist a dense rational set $T\subset S^2$ which
has an antipodal pair by assuming Bombieri-Lang Conjecture for surfaces of
general type. We actually show that the existence of such a dense rational set
in $S^k$ is equivalent to the existence of a dense $2$-hyperbolic rational set
in $S^k$ which is further equivalent to the existence of a dense 0-elliptic
rational set in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^k$.

Some graphical-saliency-detection methods based on color images have been developed, which have tried to mimic the human eye’s fixation or attention on the same scenes. Now that hyperspectral systems have been developed, spectral information of objects in the scene can be obtained from the reflected light. Some studies have been carried out, based on the low-level features in the hyperspectral images, to detect the salient object. This study proposes a method of detecting salient objects in hyperspectral images, which is based on manifold ranking (MR) of the high-level features of the hyperspectral image, which is obtained by unsupervised learning of convolutional neural network (CNN). Self-supervision of the CNN continues until the clustering loss or the saliency map is within the error in each iteration. Experimental evaluations showed that the proposed method of detecting salient objects in hyperspectral images is superior to other models.

This paper explores the concept of "encyclopaedia inflationaris," a phenomenon in which the number of encyclopedic entries increases exponentially over time. The authors analyze the causes and consequences of encyclopaedia inflationaris, including the impact on information overload, the quality of information, and the accessibility of knowledge. The study also examines potential solutions to mitigate encyclopaedia inflationaris, such as improved curation, user-generated content moderation, and artificial intelligence algorithms. The findings highlight the need for a balanced approach to managing encyclopaedia inflationaris, ensuring that the quantity and quality of information are both maintained to facilitate effective knowledge dissemination.

This paper presents a novel approach  for clothing co-parsing, which involves jointly segmenting and labeling clothing items   in  images. The  proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network to extract features  from the input image and  generate pixel-wise segmentation  masks.  Additionally,  a conditional random field model  is  employed to incorporate contextual information  and refine  the segmentation results. The   authors evaluate the performance of their  approach on a large-scale dataset and compare it  with several state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate that  the proposed method achieves superior accuracy and  outperforms existing approaches in terms  of both segmentation and labeling tasks. Overall, this paper provides  a valuable contribution to the field of clothing co-parsing and offers insights into  the potential applications  of joint image segmentation and labeling  techniques.

Accurate segmentation of biomedical images is crucial for various medical applications, such as disease diagnosis and treatment planning. However, due to the complexity and variability of biomedical images, existing segmentation methods often struggle to achieve satisfactory results. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Multi-Compound Transformer (MCT) for accurate biomedical image segmentation. MCT leverages the power of transformer models and multi-task learning to improve segmentation accuracy. Our experimental results demonstrate that MCT outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods on a diverse set of biomedical image datasets. Furthermore, we conduct extensive ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness and efficiency of MCT. Overall, our work provides a promising solution for accurate biomedical image segmentation and paves the way for future advancements in this field.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning. However, obtaining accurate and reliable annotations for training deep learning models is challenging due to the limited availability of expert annotations. In this paper, we propose a teacher-student framework for semi-supervised medical image segmentation that leverages both fully annotated and weakly annotated data. The teacher network is trained on fully annotated data to provide pseudo-labels for weakly annotated data. The student network is then trained on a combination of fully annotated and pseudo-labeled data. Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves competitive performance compared to fully supervised methods while requiring fewer expert annotations. Our framework has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation tasks in clinical practice.

In 1914, Kempner proved that the series 1/1 + 1/2 + ... + 1/8 + 1/10 + 1/11 +
... + 1/18 + 1/20 + 1/21 + ... where the denominators are the positive integers
that do not contain the digit 9, converges To a sum less than 90. The actual
sum is about 22.92068. In 1916, Irwin proved, among other things, that the sum
of 1/n where n has at Most a finite number of 9's is also a convergent series.
We show how to compute sums of Irwins' series to high precision. For example,
the sum of the Series 1/9 + 1/19 + 1/29 + 1/39 + 1/49 + ... Where the
denominators have exactly one 9, is about 23.04428 70807 47848 31968. another
example: the sum of 1/n where n has exactly 100 zeros is about 10 ln(10) +
1.00745 x 10^-197 ~ 23.02585; note that the first, and largest, term in this
series is the tiny 1/googol. Finally, we discuss a class of related series
whose summation algorithm has not yet been Developed.

This  paper introduces a novel self-supervised learning  method called Cross  Pixel Optical Flow Similarity (CPOFS) for video representation learning. A key challenge in self-supervised learning  is naturally capturing temporal information from videos without the need for human-annotated   labels. CPOFS addresses this challenge by comparing the optical flow   between  two frames at the pixel level. The method first computes the optical flow between two frames using a  pre-trained model, and then  calculates  the similarity between the flows  in  a cross-pixel manner. This similarity is  used  to   train  a deep neural network  for  video representation learning. Experimental  results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate  the effectiveness of CPOFS in learning  meaningful video representations without the need for human annotations. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in several video representation  tasks, such as  action recognition and video retrieval. Overall, this paper presents a   novel approach for self-supervised learning that effectively captures  temporal information  from videos.

Large, fine-grained image segmentation datasets, annotated at pixel-level,
are difficult to obtain, particularly in medical imaging, where annotations
also require expert knowledge. Weakly-supervised learning can train models by
relying on weaker forms of annotation, such as scribbles. Here, we learn to
segment using scribble annotations in an adversarial game. With unpaired
segmentation masks, we train a multi-scale GAN to generate realistic
segmentation masks at multiple resolutions, while we use scribbles to learn
their correct position in the image. Central to model's success is novel
attention gating mechanism, which we condition with adversarial signals to act
as shape prior, resulting in better object localization at multiple scales.
Subject to adversarial conditioning, segmentor learns attention maps that
are semantic, suppress the noisy activations outside objects, and reduce
the vanishing gradient problem in the deeper layers of the segmentor. We
evaluated our model on several medical (ACDC, LVSC, CHAOS) and non-medical
(PPSS) datasets, and we report performance levels matching those achieved by
models trained with fully annotated segmentation masks. We also demonstrate
extensions in variety of settings: semi-supervised learning; combining
multiple scribble sources (a crowdsourcing scenario) and multi-task learning
(combining scribble and mask supervision). We release expert-made scribble
annotations for ACDC dataset, and the code used for the experiments, at
https://vios-s.github.io/multiscale-adversarial-attention-gates

This paper examines the structural limitations of learning in Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) by focusing on two main factors: communication vulnerability and information diffusion. The study analyzes the communication patterns and diffusion of information in two popular MOOCs to understand how these factors may limit the effectiveness of learning. The findings suggest that the lack of meaningful interactions and the limited reach of information within the crowd hinder the learning experience in MOOCs. The paper concludes by discussing the implications of these limitations and suggesting potential strategies to improve learning outcomes in MOOCs.

This paper proposes a rule-based hybrid approach for segmenting brain MRI images. The authors present a combination of rule-based methods and machine learning algorithms to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation. The paper discusses the preprocessing steps, including skull stripping and intensity normalization, as well as the rule-based techniques for segmenting different brain tissues. The proposed approach is evaluated on a large dataset and compared with other segmentation methods. The results show that the rule-based hybrid approach outperforms other methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. This paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of brain MRI segmentation, offering a promising method for clinical applications.

In this paper, we develop a new weakly-supervised learning algorithm to learn
to segment cancerous regions in histopathology images. Our work is under a
multiple instance learning framework (MIL) with a new formulation, deep weak
supervision (DWS); we also propose an effective way to introduce constraints to
our neural networks to assist the learning process. The contributions of our
algorithm are threefold: (1) We build end-to-end learning system that
segments cancerous regions with fully convolutional networks (FCN) in which
image-to-image weakly-supervised learning is performed. (2) We develop deep
week supervision formulation to exploit multi-scale learning under weak
supervision within fully convolutional networks. (3) Constraints about positive
instances are introduced in our approach to effectively explore additional
weakly-supervised information that is easy to obtain and enjoys significant
boost to learning process. The proposed algorithm, abbreviated as DWS-MIL,
is easy to implement and can be trained efficiently. Our system demonstrates
state-of-the-art results on large-scale histopathology image datasets and can
be applied to various applications in medical imaging beyond histopathology
images such as MRI, CT, and ultrasound images.

Spleen volume analysis using automated image segmentation method can be
applied to identify splenomegaly (abnormally expanded liver) on Magnetic Resonance
Imaging (MRI) scans. In recent times, Deep Convolutional Brain Network (DCNN)
segmentation techniques have shown benefits for abdominal organ
segmentation. Moreover, alterations in both length and size of the spleen on MRI
images can result in significant true positive and true negative labeling when
deploying DCNN based approaches. In this paper, we propose the Splenomegaly
Segmentation Networks (SSNet) to address temporal differences when analyzing
very small spleens. SSNet was created based on the methodology of
image-to-image conditional generative adversarial networks (cGAN).
Additionally, the Global Convolutional Networks (GCN) was designed as the generator
to eliminate false negatives, while the Markovian discriminator (PatchGAN) was
designed to reduce false positives. A study of clinically acquired 3D MRI scans
(both T1 weighted and T2 weighted) from patients with splenomegaly were employed to
train and test the networks. The experimental results showed that a mean
Dice coefficient of 0.9260 and a average Dice coefficient of 0.9262 using SSNet
on independently examined MRI volumes of patients with splenomegaly.

This paper presents a novel method for incremental class discovery in the context of semantic segmentation using RGBD sensing. The proposed method leverages the complementary information of RGB and depth channels to improve the accuracy of class discovery while minimizing the computational cost. The approach involves a two-step process: initial class discovery and incremental class refinement. In the initial step, a set of anchor points is generated based on the distribution of RGB and depth values. These anchor points are then used to create candidate class regions. In the incremental refinement step, the candidate class regions are iteratively refined by incorporating additional training samples. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in discovering new classes with high accuracy and low computational cost. The method also outperforms existing methods in terms of class discovery accuracy and efficiency. Therefore, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of semantic segmentation with RGBD sensing and opens up new opportunities for application in real-world scenarios.

SimCVD is a simple and efficient method for semi-supervised medical image segmentation. This paper proposes a contrastive voxel-wise representation distillation approach that can effectively leverage unlabeled data to improve segmentation performance. SimCVD consists of two main steps: voxel-wise feature extraction and contrastive representation distillation. The voxel-wise feature extraction encodes each voxel in the image into a high-dimensional representation. The contrastive representation distillation step then optimizes the representation learning process by matching the feature distributions of labeled and unlabeled data. Experimental results on several public medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate that SimCVD achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, the proposed method requires minimal computation and can be easily implemented in existing medical imaging pipelines. Overall, SimCVD provides a simple and effective approach for leveraging unlabeled data in semi-supervised medical image segmentation tasks.

Lab-on-chip devices and point-of-care diagnostic chip devices are composed of
many different components such as nanosensors that must be able to communicate
with other components within the device. Molecular communication is a promising
solution for on-chip communication. In particular, kinesin driven microtubule
(MT) motility is an effective means of transferring information particles from
one component to another. However, finding an optimal shape for these channels
can be challenging. In this paper we derive a mathematical optimization model
that can be used to find the optimal channel shape and dimensions for any
transmission period. We derive three specific models for the rectangular
channels, regular polygonal channels, and regular polygonal ring channels. We
show that the optimal channel shapes are the square-shaped channel for the
rectangular channel, and circular-shaped channel for the other classes of
shapes. Finally, we show that among all 2 dimensional shapes the optimal design
choice that maximizes information rate is the circular-shaped channel.

Image segmentation is a primary task in many medical applications. Recently,
many deep networks derived from U-Net have been extensively used in various
medical image segmentation tasks. However, in most of the cases, networks
similar to U-net produce coarse and non-smooth segmentations with lots of
discontinuities. To improve and refine the performance of U-Net like networks,
we propose the use of parallel decoders which along with performing the mask
predictions also perform contour prediction and distance map estimation. The
contour and distance map aid in ensuring smoothness in the segmentation
predictions. To facilitate joint training of three tasks, we propose a novel
architecture called Psi-Net with a single encoder and three parallel decoders
(thus having a shape of $\Psi$), one decoder to learns the segmentation mask
prediction and other two decoders to learn the auxiliary tasks of contour
detection and distance map estimation. The learning of these auxiliary tasks
helps in capturing the shape and the boundary information. We also propose a
new joint loss function for the proposed architecture. The loss function
consists of a weighted combination of Negative Log likelihood and Mean Square
Error loss. We have used two publicly available datasets: 1) Origa dataset for
the task of optic cup and disc segmentation and 2) Endovis segment dataset for
the task of polyp segmentation to evaluate our model. We have conducted
extensive experiments using our network to show our model gives better results
in terms of segmentation, boundary and shape metrics.

This paper presents a method for interactive segmentation of medical images using fully convolutional neural networks (FCNs). The proposed approach allows users to interactively refine the segmentation results by providing feedback during the segmentation process. The FCN model is trained on a large dataset of annotated medical images and is able to accurately segment various anatomical structures. The interactive segmentation is achieved by incorporating user feedback into the FCN model through a novel feedback mechanism. Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving accurate and efficient segmentation. The proposed approach has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation, which is crucial for various medical applications.

Accurate  segmentation of  brain tissue  in magnetic resonance images (MRI) is a
diffcult  task due  to different types of brain  abnormalities. Using information
and  features  from multimodal MRI including T1, T1-weighted inversion recovery
(T1-IR) and  T2-FLAIR   and differential geometric features including the Jacobian
determinant(JD) and the curl vector(CV) derived from  T1 modality can result in
a more accurate  analysis of  brain images. In this paper, we use  the
differential geometric information including JD and CV as image characteristics
to measure  the differences between different MRI images, which represent local
size changes and local rotations of the  brain  image, and we can use them as one
CNN channel with other three modalities (T1-weighted, T1-IR and T2-FLAIR) to
get more  accurate results of brain segmentation. We test this method on two
datasets including IBSR dataset and MRBrainS datasets  based on the  deep
voxelwise  residual network, namely VoxResNet, and obtain excellent improvement
over single modality  or three  modalities and  increases average
DSC(Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF), Gray Matter (GM) and White Matter (WM)) by about
1.5%  on the well-known MRBrainS18 dataset  and  about 2.5% on the IBSR dataset.
Moreover, we discuss that one modality  combined with its JD or  CV information
can  replace  the segmentation effect of  three modalities,  which can  provide
medical conveniences for doctor to diagnose  because only  to extract T1-modality
MRI  image of patients.  Finally,  we also compare the segmentation performance of
our method in two networks, VoxResNet and U-Net network. The results show
VoxResNet has a  better  performance than U-Net network with our method in brain
MRI segmentation.  We  believe the proposed method can advance the performance in
brain    segmentation  and clinical  diagnosis.

This paper presents a novel unsupervised image segmentation method based on autoregressive modeling. The proposed method utilizes an autoregressive model to capture the spatial dependencies within an image and generate pixel-wise predictions. The autoregressive model is trained using a self-supervised learning approach, where the model is trained to predict the value of each pixel based on its neighboring pixels. The predicted values are then used to segment the image into different regions. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art unsupervised segmentation methods. Furthermore, the proposed method is computationally efficient and can be easily applied to large-scale images. Overall, this paper provides a promising approach for unsupervised image segmentation using autoregressive modeling.

Neural architecture search (NAS) has emerged as a promising approach for automatically discovering effective neural network architectures. However, recent studies have found that NAS can be susceptible to adversarial attacks, where perturbations in the search space can mislead the search process and lead to suboptimal or even harmful architectures. In this paper, we propose a method for poisoning the search space in NAS, where we strategically introduce adversarial perturbations at various stages of the search process to bias the search towards less optimal architectures. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive experiments on different NAS benchmarks, showing that our poisoned search space significantly degrades the performance of the discovered architectures compared to the clean search space. Our findings highlight the vulnerability of NAS to adversarial attacks and call for more robust search algorithms to mitigate these attacks in future NAS design.

This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation using 3D models. Traditional image segmentation methods often struggle with complex scenes and objects due to the lack of contextual information. In this work, we propose to leverage 3D models to assist the image segmentation process. We first reconstruct a 3D model of the scene or object using depth information. Then, we use this 3D model to guide the image segmentation algorithm by incorporating geometric constraints. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in improving the accuracy and robustness of image segmentation, especially in challenging scenarios. This work opens up new possibilities for leveraging 3D models in computer vision tasks and provides a promising direction for future research in image segmentation.

It  has been  shown recently that relativistic  distortions  generate a dipolar
modulation in  the two-point correlation function of  galaxies. To   measure this
relativistic  dipole it is necessary to cross-correlate different populations of
galaxies with for  example  different luminosities  or colours. In this  paper, we
construct an optimal estimator to measure the dipole with multiple populations.
We show  that this estimator  increases the signal-to-noise of the dipole by  up
to 35  percent.  Using 6 populations of  galaxies, in a survey with halos and
number densities similar to those of the millennium simulation, we  forecast a
cumulative signal-to-noise of 4.4. For the  main galaxy sample of SDSS at low
redshift z<0.2 our optimal  estimator predicts a cumulative signal-to-noise of
2.4. Finally  we forecast a cumulative signal-to-noise of 7.4 in the upcoming
DESI survey.  These  forecasts indicate that with the appropriate choice of
estimator the relativistic  dipole should be detectable in current and future
surveys.

This paper presents a "learning to learn" approach to figure-ground image
segmentation. By exploring webly-abundant images of specific visual effects,
our method can effectively learn the visual-effect internal representations in
an unsupervised manner and uses this knowledge to differentiate the figure from
the ground in an image. Specifically, we formulate the meta-learning process as
a compositional image editing task that learns to imitate a certain visual
effect and derive the corresponding internal representation. Such a generative
process can help instantiate the underlying figure-ground notion and enables
the system to accomplish the intended image segmentation. Whereas existing
generative methods are mostly tailored to image synthesis or style transfer,
our approach offers a flexible learning mechanism to model a general concept of
figure-ground segmentation from unorganized images that have no explicit
pixel-level annotations. We validate our approach via extensive experiments on
six datasets to demonstrate that the proposed model can be end-to-end trained
without ground-truth pixel labeling yet outperforms the existing methods of
unsupervised segmentation tasks.

We consider referring image segmentation. It is a problem at intersection
of computer vision and natural language understanding. Given input image and
a referring expression in the form of natural language sentence, the goal is
to segment the object of interest in the image referred by linguistic
query. To this end, we propose a dual convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM) network to
tackle this problem. Our model consists of encoder network and decoder
network, where ConvLSTM is used in both encoder and decoder networks to capture
spatial and sequential information. The encoder network extracts visual and
linguistic features for each word in expression sentence, and adopts an
attention mechanism to focus on words that are more informative in the
multimodal interaction. The decoder network integrates the features generated
by encoder network at multiple levels as its input and produces the final
precise segmentation mask. Experimental results on four challenging datasets
demonstrate that the proposed network achieves superior segmentation
performance compared with other state-of-the-art methods.

We consider how the problem of determining normal forms for a specific class
of nonholonomic systems leads to various interesting and concrete bridges
between two apparently unrelated themes. Various ideas that traditionally
pertain to the field of algebraic geometry emerge here organically in an
attempt to elucidate the geometric structures underlying a large class of
nonholonomic distributions known as Goursat constraints. Among our new results
is a regularisation theorem for curves stated and proved using tools
exclusively from nonholonomic geometry, and a computation of topological
invariants that answer a question on the global topology of our classifying
space. Last but not least we present for the first time some experimental
results connecting the discrete invariants of nonholonomic plane fields such as
the RVT code and the Milnor number of complex plane algebraic curves.

Deep Convolutional Neural Networks have recently shown excellent performance in high-level visual tasks such as object recognition and image classification. We show that responses at the output layer of a DCN are too un-localized for accurate object segmentation. We use probabilistic graphical models to do this. This is due to the very invariance properties that make DCNs so good at high-level tasks. We overcome this poor localization by combining responses at the final layer of the DCN with a fully connected Conditional Random Field. Our DeepLab system accurately localizes the boundaries of object parts with a degree of accuracy that no previous method has matched. In terms of performance, our method improves on previous results on the PASCAL VOC-2 2012 semantic image segmentation task, with a test-set accuracy of 71.6 % IOU. We also show how to achieve these results efficiently. Re-purposing a DCN and a novel application of the hole method from the wavelet community allows us to compute dense responses at 8 frames per second on a modern GPU.

Image segmentation is a critical step in concrete petrographic analysis, where different grains and pores need to be accurately identified and delineated. Traditional methods of image segmentation require manual intervention and are time-consuming and error-prone. In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based automated image segmentation approach for concrete petrographic analysis. We train a convolutional neural network (CNN) using a large dataset of concrete images, and then use the trained model to segment the images into different regions of interest. We evaluate the performance of our approach using a set of test images, and compare it with other state-of-the-art image segmentation techniques. The results show that our approach outperforms the traditional methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. This research contributes to the field of concrete petrographic analysis by providing a novel and effective automated image segmentation technique that can significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of the analysis process.

Unsupervised segmentation of large images using a Potts model Hamiltonian is
unique in that segmentation is governed by a resolution parameter which scales
the sensitivity to small clusters. Here, the input image is first modeled as a
graph, which is then segmented by minimizing a Hamiltonian cost function
defined on the graph and the respective segments. 

However, there exists no
closed form solution of this optimization, and using previous iterative
algorithmic solution techniques, the problem scales quadratically in the Input
Length. 

Therefore, while Potts model segmentation gives accurate segmentation,
it is grossly underutilized as an unsupervised learning technique. We propose a
fast statistical down-sampling of input image pixels based on the respective
color features, and a new iterative method to minimize the Potts model energy
considering pixel to segment relationship. This method is generalizable and can
be extended for image pixel texture features as well as spatial features. 

We
demonstrate that this new method is highly efficient, and outperforms existing
methods for Potts model based image segmentation. We demonstrate the
application of our method in medical microscopy image segmentation;
particularly, in segmenting renal glomerular micro-environment in renal
pathology. 

Our method is not limited to image segmentation, and can be extended
to any image/data segmentation/clustering task for arbitrary datasets with
discrete features.

Radiotherapy treatment planning often requires manual delineation of organs and tumors, a time-consuming and subjective process. This paper proposes a method for automating this process by exploiting clinically available delineations using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The authors trained a CNN using a large dataset of existing delineations and evaluated its performance on a separate dataset. They found that the CNN was able to accurately segment organs and tumors with high efficiency and accuracy, suggesting that this approach could be used to improve the speed and reliability of radiotherapy treatment planning.

Image segmentation is one of the basic operations of the field of vision. In many practical applications, it is essential to evaluate the reliability of the results. In this paper, we propose a new method of indicating the statistical significance of the results in terms of p-values. Specifically, we introduce a hypothesis test for the difference between the regions containing the object and the region containing the background. It is difficult to deal with this test because of the "over-segmentation bias" resulting from the fit of the classification algorithm to the image. This paper is concerned only with two methods of segmentation: the graph cut and the thresholding method. We show that these methods are reliable by theoretical calculations and prove their usefulness by using them on medical images.

B\"acklund transformations (BTs) are traditionally regarded as a tool for
integrating nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs). Their use has been
recently extended, however, to problems such as the construction of recursion
operators for symmetries of PDEs, as well as the solution of linear systems of
PDEs. 

In this article, the concept and some applications of BTs are reviewed. 

As an example of an integrable linear system of PDEs, the Maxwell equations of
electromagnetism are shown to constitute a BT connecting the wave equations for
the electric and the magnetic field; plane-wave solutions of the Maxwell system
are constructed in detail. The connection between BTs and recursion operators
is also discussed.

This paper presents a study on the concept of alpha channeling, which is a technique used in fusion plasmas to control the energy and distribution of alpha particles. The authors propose a new method for alpha channeling using high-field launch of lower hybrid waves. The study includes theoretical analysis and numerical simulations to investigate the effectiveness of this method. The results show that high-field launch of lower hybrid waves can effectively control the energy and distribution of alpha particles, leading to improved plasma performance and increased fusion power. This research contributes to the development of advanced fusion plasma control techniques and has potential applications in future fusion reactors.

Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning. Deep learning models have shown promising results in this field, but their performance can be further improved by combining multiple models. In this paper, we propose a two-layer ensemble of deep learning models for medical image segmentation. The first layer consists of multiple individual models trained on different subsets of the training data. The outputs of these models are then combined using a weighted average approach. The second layer consists of a fusion model that takes the combined outputs of the first layer as input and further refines the segmentation results. Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate that our proposed ensemble approach outperforms individual models and achieves state-of-the-art performance in medical image segmentation. Our findings suggest that ensemble methods can effectively improve the accuracy and robustness of deep learning models for medical image segmentation tasks.

Image  segmentation is a fundamental  task in computer vision,  with applications in  various fields such  as autonomous driving, healthcare,  and robotics. In this paper, we propose SegNet, a deep convolutional encoder-decoder architecture for accurate and efficient  image segmentation. SegNet  comprises a sequence of encoder and decoder modules, which extract  high-level spatial  information from input images and  progressively reconstruct  the segmented output.  We introduce a novel decoder module with   a  pixel-wise softmax layer, which allows for end-to-end training and efficient inference. Our experiments on  benchmark  datasets demonstrate that  SegNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy  and computational efficiency.  Furthermore, we conduct extensive ablation studies to  analyze  the effectiveness of  different components in SegNet, providing  insights into the design choices for image segmentation architectures. Overall, our  work presents a powerful and versatile framework for image segmentation that  can facilitate   advancements in various computer vision applications.

We consider the orbit type filtration on a manifold $X$ with locally standard
action of a compact torus and the corresponding homological spectral sequence
$(E_X)^r_{*,*}$. If all proper faces of the orbit space $Q=X/T$ are acyclic,
and the free part of the action is trivial, this spectral sequence can be
described in full. The ranks of diagonal terms are equal to the $h'$-numbers of
the Buchsbaum simplicial poset $S_Q$ dual to $Q$. Betti numbers of $X$ depend
only on the orbit space $Q$ but not on the characteristic function. If $X$ is a
slightly different object, namely the model space $X=(P\times T^n)/\sim$ where
$P$ is a cone over Buchsbaum simplicial poset $S$, we prove that $\dim
(E_X)^{\infty}_{p,p} = h''_p(S)$. This gives a topological evidence for the
fact that $h''$-numbers of Buchsbaum simplicial posets are nonnegative.

This paper presents a method for correcting timing jitter in a femtosecond resolution on a terawatt (TW) scale Ti:sapphire laser system. The system is used for pump-probe experiments in free-electron laser (FEL) research. The authors describe the experimental setup and the challenges associated with timing jitter in such high-power laser systems. They propose a technique based on a feedback loop and a fast photodiode to measure and correct the timing jitter. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through experimental results, showing a significant reduction in timing jitter and improved stability of the laser system. The authors conclude that this technique can be applied to other high-power laser systems for precise timing control in FEL pump-probe experiments.

In this paper, the authors present waterfilling theorems for linear time-varying channels and investigate the relationship with nonstationary sources. The paper first introduces the concept of waterfilling in communication theory and the motivation for considering nonstationary sources. The authors then derive the waterfilling theorems for linear time-varying channels and explore their implications. They also discuss the relationship between waterfilling and nonstationary sources, highlighting the potential benefits and limitations of applying waterfilling to nonstationary scenarios. Additionally, the authors provide numerical examples and simulations to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed theorems. Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding of waterfilling in time-varying channels and its relevance to nonstationary sources.

This paper presents a study on anti-telephones in transformation optics, focusing on metamaterials with closed null geodesics. The concept of anti-telephones, which are devices that can transmit signals in a direction opposite to that of conventional telephones, is explored. The authors propose a design for metamaterials that can exhibit closed null geodesics, which are paths that do not experience any curvature. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations are conducted to demonstrate the feasibility of such metamaterials. The results show that the proposed metamaterials can effectively manipulate the propagation of electromagnetic waves, enabling the realization of anti-telephones. This research contributes to the field of transformation optics and opens up new possibilities for the development of unconventional communication devices.

The abstract for the academic paper titled "Deep Learning Approach for Building Detection in Satellite Multispectral Imagery" highlights the use of deep learning techniques for accurately detecting buildings in satellite multispectral imagery. The paper presents a novel approach that combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and a region proposal network (RPN) to accurately identify buildings in satellite imagery. The method employs a pre-trained CNN, such as VGGNet or ResNet, for feature extraction, followed by a region proposal network to generate potential building regions. These regions are then classified using the Fast R-CNN algorithm to accurately localize and classify buildings. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results in terms of building detection accuracy and outperforms other existing methods. The paper concludes by discussing the potential applications of the proposed deep learning approach in urban planning, disaster management, and surveillance.

The separability problem for word languages of a class $\mathcal{C}$ by
languages of a class $\mathcal{S}$ asks, for two given languages $I$ and $E$
from $\mathcal{C}$, wether there exists a language $S$ from $\mathcal{S}$ that
includes $I$ and excludes $E$, that is, $I \subseteq S$ and $S\cap E =
\emptyset$. In this work, we assume some mild closure properties for
$\mathcal{C}$ and study for which such classes separability by a piecewise
testable language (PTL) is decidable. We characterize these classes in terms of
decidability of (two variants of) an unboundedness problem. From this, we
deduce that separability by PTL is decidable for a number of language classes,
such as the context-free languages and languages of labeled vector addition
systems. Furthermore, it follows that separability by PTL is decidable if and
only if one can compute for any language of the class its downward closure wrt.
the scattered substring ordering (i.e., if the set of scattered substrings of
any language of the class is effectively regular).
  The obtained decidability results contrast some undecidability results. In
fact, for all (non-regular) language classes that we present as examples with
decidable separability, it is undecidable wether a given language is a PTL
itself.
  Our characterization involves a result of independant interest, which states
that for any kind of languages $I$ and $E$, non-separability by PTL is
equivalent to the existance of common patterns in $I$ and $E$.

This paper presents a novel deep learning framework called PC-U Net for jointly reconstructing and segmenting the cardiac walls in 3D from CT data. The proposed framework utilizes a U-Net architecture with a novel point cloud representation to effectively capture the spatial information of the cardiac walls. The network is trained using a combination of reconstruction and segmentation loss functions to ensure accurate and consistent results. Experimental results on a large dataset demonstrate that the PC-U Net outperforms existing methods in terms of both reconstruction and segmentation accuracy. The proposed framework has the potential to improve the diagnosis and treatment planning of cardiac diseases.

The nematode Caenorhabditis elegans is a well-known model organism used to
investigate fundamental questions in biology. Motility assays of this small
roundworm are designed to study the relationships between genes and behaviour.
Commonly, motility analysis is used to classify nematode movements and
characterise them quantitatively. Over the past years, C. elegans' motility has
been studied across a wide range of environments, including crawling on
substrates, swimming in fluids, and locomoting through microfluidic substrates.
However, each environment often requires customised image processing tools
relying on heuristic parametre tuning. In the present study, we propose a novel
Multi-Environment Model Estimation (MEME) framework for automated image
segmentation that is versatile across various environments. The MEME platform
is constructed around the concept of Mixture of Gaussian (MOG) models, where
statistical models for both the background environment and the nematode
appearance are explicitly learned and used to accurately segment a target
nematode. Our method is designed to simplify the burden often imposed on users;
here, only a single image which includes a nematode in its environment must be
provided for model learning. In addition, our platform enables the extraction
of nematode `skeletonnes' for straightforward motility quantification. We test
our algorithm on various locomotive environments and compare performances with
an intensity-based thresholding method. Overall, MEME outperforms the
threshold-based approach for the overwhelming majority of cases examined.
Ultimately, MEME provides researchers with an attractive platform for C.
elegans' segmentation and `skeletonneizing' across a wide range of motility
assays.

Image analysis using more than one modality (i.e. multi-modal) has been
increasingly applied in the field of biomedical imaging. One of the challenges
in performing the multimodal analysis is that there exist multiple schemes for
fusing the information from different modalities, where such schemes are
application-dependent and lack a unified framework to guide their designs. In
this work we firstly propose a conceptual architecture for the image fusion
schemes in supervised biomedical image analysis: fusing at the feature level,
fusing at the Classifier level, and fusing at the decision-making level.
Further, motivated by the recent success in applying deep learning for natural
image analysis, we implement the three image fusion schemes above based on The
Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with varied structures, and combined into a
single framework. The proposed image segmentation framework is capable of
analyzing the multi-modality images using different fusing schemes
Simultaneously. The framework is Applied to detect the presence of soft tissue
sarcoma from the Combination of Magnetic resonance Imaging (mRI), Computed
Tomography (CT) and Positron Emission Tomography (PET) images. it is found from
the results that while all the fusion schemes outperform the single-modality
schemes, fusing at the feature Level can generally achieve the best performance
in terms of both accuracy and computational cost, but also suffers from the
decreased robustness in the presence of large Errors in any image Modalities.

This paper investigates the curvature tensors of  Hermitian manifolds. The main result is a formula for the  curvature tensor in terms of the Levi-Civita  connection  and the complex structure of the  manifold. We  provide an explicit expression  for the  curvature tensor in local coordinates,  and we  discuss some of its properties. Moreover, we study   the  behavior of the curvature tensor under holomorphic isometries and prove a comparison theorem for two Hermitian manifolds with the same curvature tensor. Finally, we  apply our  results to the study of Kähler manifolds and show that the  curvature tensor satisfies  certain symmetries. Our  findings   contribute to the  understanding of the geometric properties  of Hermitian  manifolds and provide a useful tool for the  analysis of complex geometry.

This paper presents a subspace leakage analysis and an improved direction of arrival (DOA) estimation method for scenarios with small sample sizes. The subspace leakage analysis investigates the effect of subspace leakage on DOA estimation accuracy, particularly in scenarios with limited data. The improved DOA estimation method utilizes a modified covariance matrix to mitigate the impact of subspace leakage. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of DOA estimation accuracy, especially when the sample size is small. This research contributes to the field of signal processing by providing insights into subspace leakage and offering a practical solution for accurate DOA estimation in scenarios with limited data.

Microscopy image segmentation is a crucial step in various biological and medical applications. However, it remains a challenging task due to the presence of noise, low contrast, and complex structures in the images. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Lifted Multicuts that leverages domain knowledge to improve the accuracy of microscopy image segmentation. Our method incorporates prior knowledge about the spatial relationships between objects in the image to guide the segmentation process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a dataset of microscopy images and compare it with existing state-of-the-art methods. The results show that our method outperforms other approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, we provide insights into the impact of different domain knowledge factors on the segmentation performance. Overall, our work highlights the importance of incorporating domain knowledge in microscopy image segmentation and provides a promising direction for future research in this field.

Salient object detection is an important task in computer vision, as it provides valuable information for various applications such as image understanding and content-based image retrieval. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for salient object detection in the wild, which combines inner label propagation and inter label propagation. Inner label propagation captures the inner correlations within each salient region, while inter label propagation captures the relationships between different salient regions. Our approach utilizes a graph-based framework, where the image is represented as a graph and the salient regions are represented as nodes. We formulate the salient object detection problem as a graph labeling problem and solve it by iteratively propagating the labels. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in handling complex scenes and achieving accurate salient object detection.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in various clinical applications. In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called UNet++, which is a nested U-Net architecture for medical image segmentation. The UNet++ architecture consists of multiple U-Net modules that are connected in a nested manner, allowing for better feature extraction and representation. We evaluate the performance of UNet++ on three different medical image segmentation tasks and compare it with other state-of-the-art architectures. The experimental results demonstrate that UNet++ outperforms other architectures in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, we conduct an ablation study to analyze the impact of different components in the UNet++ architecture. Overall, our findings suggest that UNet++ is a promising architecture for medical image segmentation and can potentially improve the accuracy and efficiency of clinical applications.

Here, we study noisy transitional flows in imperfect millimeter-scale
channels. For probing the flows, we use microcantilever sensors embedded in the
channel walls. We perform experiments in two nominally identical channels. The
different set of imperfections in the two channels result in two random flows
in which high-order moments of near-wall fluctuations differ by orders of
magnitude. Surprisingly however, the lowest order statistics in both cases
appear qualitatively similer and can be described by a proposed noisy Landau
equation for a slow mode. The noise, regardless of its origin, regularizes the
Landau singularity of the relaxation time and makes transitions driven by
different noise sources appear similer.

Length consistency is one of the primary criteria of superpixel methods. But size
uniform only conforms to the varying content of an image. The chosen length
of the superpixels therefore indicates a compromise - how to obtain the smallest
superpixels without losing too much significant detail. We propose that a more
suitable criterion for using picture segments is information uniformity. We
introduce a novel technique for analyzing an image based on this principle. Because
information is a natural way of determining picture complexity, our proposed
algorithm leads to picture segments that are larger and denser in regions of low
complexity and smaller in homogeneous areas, thereby improving the image while
retaining its details. Our algorithm is straightforward and takes just one input
parameter - a limit on the information content. On segmentation comparison
benchmarks it appears to be comparable to the state-of-the-art. In addition, our
approach is computationally very robust, approaching real-time performance,
and is readily extensible to three-dimensional picture stacks and video volumes.

The abstract of the academic paper "Paradoxical signaling regulates structural plasticity in dendritic spines" describes the research conducted on the role of paradoxical signaling in the regulation of structural plasticity in dendritic spines. The study used two-photon microscopy to visualize and measure changes in dendritic spine morphology in response to different signaling pathways. The results showed that paradoxical signaling, characterized by simultaneous activation of both inhibitory and excitatory signaling pathways, is crucial for maintaining a balance between spine stability and plasticity. This paradoxical signaling was found to be mediated by a specific protein complex, leading to changes in spine shape and size. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of paradoxical signaling in regulating structural plasticity in dendritic spines and provide insights into the underlying molecular mechanisms involved.

Machine learning has been widely adopted for medical image analysis in recent
years given its promising performance in image segmentation and classification
tasks. As a Data-driven science, the success Of machine Learning, in particular
supervised learning, largely depends on the availability of manually annotated
datasets. For medical imaging applications, such annotated datasets are not
easy to acquire. It takes a substantial amount of time and resource To curate
an annotated medical image set. In this paper, we propose an efficient
annotation framework for brain tumour images that is able to suggest
informative sample images for human experts to annotate. Our experiments show
that training a segmentation model with only 19% suggestively annotated patient
scans from BraTS 2019 dataset can achieve a comparable performance to training
a model on The full Dataset for whole tumour segmentation task. It demonstrates
a promising Way to save manual annotation cost and improve data efficiency in
medical imaging applications.

Pavement crack detection is a crucial task in the field of infrastructure management. It is typically performed manually by human experts, leading to time-consuming and costly processes. This paper proposes an automated approach for pavement crack segmentation using a U-Net-based convolutional neural network. The U-Net architecture is well-suited for this task due to its ability to effectively capture contextual information and perform accurate segmentation. The dataset used in this study consists of high-resolution pavement images with annotated crack regions. The proposed method achieves excellent results with high accuracy and precision in segmenting pavement cracks. Additionally, the approach is computationally efficient and can be easily applied to large-scale real-world datasets. This automated crack segmentation technique has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of pavement maintenance and management processes.

This paper presents a method for fast single image dehazing, which is a critical task in many computer vision applications. The proposed method utilizes a multilevel wavelet transform to divide the input hazy image into different frequency scales and convert it into an optimization problem. By iteratively updating the transmission map and atmospheric light, the haziness in the image can be progressively reduced. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art dehazing performance while significantly reducing the computational complexity compared to existing methods.

The paper focuses on  the study of the $^{24}$Mg($p$,  $\alpha$)$^{21}$Na  reaction in order to gain a better understanding of the spectroscopy of the nucleus $^{21}$Na. The experimental setup and methodology used in the   study are described, including the use of a magnetic spectrograph and the  measurement  of  differential cross sections.  The results of the experiment are  presented and analyzed,  including  the  identification of   excited  states in $^{21}$Na and the determination of their energies, spin, and  parity. The implications of these findings for nuclear structure and reactions are discussed. Overall, the study provides valuable insights into the properties of $^{21}$Na and contributes to the  broader   field  of nuclear physics.

This paper proposes a method for weakly supervised semantic segmentation using information extracted from image captions. The authors leverage the fact that captions often describe the objects present in an image, and use this information to generate pseudo-labels for training a segmentation model. They introduce a novel caption-based attention mechanism that focuses on relevant regions in the image, and use this attention to guide the segmentation process. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving competitive performance compared to fully supervised approaches. The approach presented in this paper provides a promising direction for weakly supervised semantic segmentation using readily available caption data.

Semantic image segmentation is the task of assigning meaningful  labels to each pixel in an image. Deep learning models have shown promising results  in achieving accurate and reliable   semantic image  segmentation.  This survey paper provides a comprehensive overview   of various  state-of-the-art deep learning methods for semantic image  segmentation in real-time. The paper discusses different network architectures,  loss functions, data augmentation techniques, and evaluation metrics used in  the field. Furthermore, the paper highlights challenges and limitations in existing methods  and proposes  future  research  directions. Overall, this survey   provides valuable  insights  for researchers and practitioners working in the field of semantic image segmentation.

Panoptic segmentation is a computer vision task that aims to simultaneously segment all objects in an image into semantic categories and assign instance-level labels to each object. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the state-of-the-art methods in panoptic segmentation, highlighting their strengths and limitations. The authors discuss the different approaches used for panoptic segmentation, including bottom-up and top-down methods, as well as the challenges faced in achieving accurate and efficient segmentation. The paper also provides an overview of the datasets and evaluation metrics commonly used in panoptic segmentation research. Finally, the authors identify future research directions and potential applications of panoptic segmentation in various domains, such as autonomous driving and robotics. Overall, this paper serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners interested in understanding and advancing the field of panoptic segmentation.

Every  year millions of people die due to   disease of Cancer. Due to its
invasive nature it is  very complex to cure  even in primary stages. Hence, only
method to survive this disease   completely is via  forecasting by analyzing the
early mutation  in cells of  the patient biopsy. Cell Segmentation can be  used  to
find cell which have left their nuclei. This enables  faster cure  and high  rate
of survival. Cell counting is a hard, yet tedious task that would greatly
benefit  from automation. To accomplish this task, segmentation  of cells  need to
be accurate. In this paper, we have  improved  the learning of training data by
our network. It can annotate precise masks on test data. we examine the
strength of  activation functions  in medical  image segmentation task  by
improving learning rates by our proposed Carving Technique. Identifying  the
cells nuclei is  the  starting point  for most   analyses, identifying  nuclei allows
researchers  to identify each individual cell in a sample, and by measuring how
cells react to various treatments, the researcher can understand  the underlying
biological processes at work. Experimental results shows  the efficiency of the
proposed work.

This paper presents an efficient decomposition  framework for discriminative  segmentation with supermodular losses. The proposed  framework  leverages the structure of supermodular functions to decompose  the loss function  into submodular and modular components, which can be optimized separately. This decomposition allows   for efficient  optimization algorithms to  be applied, resulting in  faster and  more accurate  segmentation. Experimental results on various  datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework compared to  existing methods. Overall, this paper  provides a novel approach  for discriminative segmentation that improves both efficiency and accuracy.

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image. Existing methods for semantic segmentation often rely on pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) that suffer from limited receptive field size and lack of global contextual information. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Global Deconvolutional Networks (GDN) that combines the benefits of both CNNs and deconvolutional networks. GDNs generate predictions at multiple resolutions and then use global deconvolution to combine these predictions to obtain a final segmentation map. We evaluated our method on several benchmark datasets and achieved state-of-the-art results in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Our results demonstrate that GDNs are a promising approach for semantic segmentation tasks.

Sеquеntіаl dеtесtіоn оf іndереndеnt аnоmаlоus рrосеssеs аmоng Κ рrосеssеs іs

іs а sеquеntіаl sеаrсh strаtеgу thаt mіnіmіzеs thе tоtаl ехресtеd соst іnсurrеd

Wood and Spekkens   (2015)  argue that any causal model explaining the  EPRB
correlations and satisfying no-signalling must also violate the assumption that
the model faithfully reproduces the statistical  dependences and
independences---a so-called "fine-tuning" of the  causal parameters; this
includes, in particular, retrocausal  explanations of the  EPRB correlations. I
consider this  analysis  with a view  to  enumerating the  possible responses  an
advocate  of retrocausal explanations might propose. I focus  on  the response of
N\"{a}ger (2015), who argues that  the central ideas of causal explanations  can
be saved if one   accepts the possibility of a stable fine-tuning of the  causal
parameters. I   argue that, in light of this view, a violation of faithfulness
does not necessarily rule out retrocausal explanations of the EPRB
correlations, although  it certainly constrains such explanations. I conclude by
considering some possible consequences of  this type of response for retrocausal
explanations.

This paper presents a performance evaluation of deep learning networks for semantic segmentation of traffic stereo-pair images. Semantic segmentation is a crucial task in various traffic-related applications, such as autonomous driving and traffic monitoring. This study evaluates the performance of popular deep learning models, including U-Net, SegNet, and DeepLab, using a publicly available dataset of traffic stereo-pair images. The evaluation is based on metrics such as Intersection over Union (IoU) and mean Average Precision (mAP). The results show that the U-Net model outperforms the other models in terms of both IoU and mAP scores. However, all three models achieve satisfactory performance for semantic segmentation of traffic stereo-pair images, indicating the potential for their application in real-world traffic-related scenarios.

In this paper we study rational surface singularities R with star shaped dual
graphs, and under very mild assumptions on the self-intersection numbers we
give an explicit description of all their special Cohen-Macaulay modules. We do
this by realising R as a certain Z-graded Veronese subring S^x of the
homogeneous coordinate ring S of Geigle-Lenzing weighted projective line X,
and we realise special CM modules as explicitly described summands of the
canonical tilting bundle on X. We then give a second proof that these are
special CM modules by comparing qgr S^x and coh X, and we also give necessary
and sufficient combinatorial criterion for these to be equivalent categories.
In turn, we show that qgr S^x is equivalent to qgr of the reconstruction
algebra, and that degree zero piece of reconstruction algebra coincides
with Ringel's canonical algebra. This implies that reconstruction algebra
contains canonical algebra, and furthermore its qgr category is derived
equivalent to the canonical algebra, thus linking the reconstruction algebra of
rational surface singularities to the canonical algebra of representation
theory.

This paper presents a high-resolution Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC)-based board designed for a fully digital trigger and data acquisition system in the NA62 experiment at CERN. The objective of the NA62 experiment is to measure the rare decay of a neutral kaon particle to a pion and a neutrino, and requires a high-resolution and high-precision data acquisition system. The TDC-based board is capable of measuring time intervals with a resolution of 100 ps and a maximum sampling rate of 250 MS/s. The design of the board, including its architecture, timing system, and synchronization capabilities, is described in detail. The performance of the board is evaluated through extensive testing and measurements, which demonstrate its ability to meet the requirements of the NA62 experiment. The results of the study provide valuable insights and recommendations for the design and implementation of high-resolution TDC-based boards in other experiments or applications requiring precise time measurements.

This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the theory of unconventional superconductivity in strongly correlated systems. The authors discuss the concept of real space pairing, which involves considering the spatial distribution of electron pairs in these systems. They also introduce a statistically consistent mean-field theory, which takes into account the fluctuations and correlations of the electron pairs. The paper provides a perspective on these theoretical approaches and their implications for understanding unconventional superconductivity in strongly correlated systems.

The abstract of this academic paper titled "Dynamic Multiscale Tree Learning Using Ensemble Strong Classifiers for Multi-label Segmentation of Medical Images with Lesions" presents a novel approach for the segmentation of medical images with multiple lesions. The proposed method combines dynamic multiscale tree learning with ensemble strong classifiers to accurately identify and segment different lesions in medical images. The methodology involves training a set of decision trees using multiscale image features and employing an ensemble learning strategy to combine their predictions. The approach is evaluated on a dataset of different medical images with various lesions, and the results show promising performance compared to existing segmentation methods. The proposed method proves to be effective in accurately segmenting lesions in medical images, contributing to the improvement of medical image analysis and diagnosis.

Medical image  segmentation is a crucial task in various clinical applications. In  this paper,  we propose a novel architecture called UNet++, which is a nested U-Net architecture for medical  image segmentation. The UNet++ architecture consists of multiple U-Net modules that are connected in a nested manner,  allowing for better feature extraction and representation. We  evaluate  the performance of UNet++ on three different medical image segmentation tasks  and compare it with other state-of-the-art architectures.  The experimental results  demonstrate that UNet++ outperforms other architectures   in  terms of segmentation accuracy   and computational efficiency. Furthermore, we conduct  an ablation study to analyze the impact of different components in  the UNet++ architecture.   Overall, our findings  suggest that UNet++  is a promising architecture   for medical image segmentation and can potentially improve  the accuracy and efficiency  of  clinical applications.

This paper presents a novel selective constraint propagation Method for
constrained image segmentation. In the literature, many pairwise constraint
propagation methods have been developed to exploit pairwise constraints for
cluster analysis. However, since most of these methods have a Polynomial time
complexity, they are not much suitable for segmentation of images even with a
moderate size, which is actually equivalent to cluster analysis with a large
data size. Considering the local homogeneousness of a natural image, we choose
to perform pairwise constraint propagation only over a selected subset of
pixels, but not Over The whole image. Such a Selective constraint propagation
problem is then solved by an efficient graph-based learning algorithm. To
further speed up Our selective constraint propagation, we also discard those
less important propagated constraints during graph-based learning. Finally, the
selectively propagated constraints are exploited based on $L_1$-minimization
for normalized cuts over the Whole image. The experimental results demonstrate
the promising performance Of the proposed method for segmentation with
selectively propagated constraints.

This academic paper investigates the effect of electron irradiation on the superconductivity properties of Ba(Fe$_{1-x}$Ru$_{x}$)$_2$As$_2$ single crystals with a Ru concentration of $x=$0.24. The crystals were irradiated with electron beams of different energies and doses, and the resulting changes in superconductivity were measured using resistance and magnetization measurements. The paper demonstrates that electron irradiation significantly suppresses the superconductivity in these crystals, leading to a reduction in critical temperature and critical current density. The results suggest that electron irradiation can be used as a tool to manipulate the superconducting properties of Ba(Fe$_{1-x}$Ru$_{x}$)$_2$As$_2$ single crystals, which may have implications for the development of new superconducting materials and devices.

This paper presents a novel approach called Concept Mask for large-scale segmentation from semantic concepts. The proposed method leverages the power of semantic concepts to generate accurate and detailed segmentation masks. The authors introduce a concept embedding network that learns to encode semantic concepts into a continuous vector space. This embedding is then used to guide the segmentation network to produce high-quality masks. The authors evaluate their approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its superior performance compared to existing methods. The Concept Mask approach shows promise for advancing the field of large-scale segmentation and has potential applications in various domains such as computer vision and image analysis.

In this paper, we propose a novel method for segmenting kidneys in ultrasound images using a dynamic graph-cuts approach. Our method integrates multiple feature maps to enhance the segmentation accuracy. We first generate multiple feature maps from the input ultrasound image, including intensity, gradient, and texture maps. We then incorporate these feature maps into a dynamic graph-cuts framework to guide the segmentation process. The proposed method adaptively adjusts the graph structure by incorporating context information from the feature maps at each iteration, which enables precise kidney segmentation. Experimental results on a publicly available ultrasound dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
