The latent block model is used to simultaneously rank the rows and columns of
a matrix to reveal a block structure. The algorithms used for estimation are
often time consuming. However, recent work shows that the log-likelihood ratios
are equivalent under the complete and observed (with unknown labels) models and
the groups posterior distribution to converge as the size of the data increases
to a Dirac mass located at the actual groups configuration. Based on these
observations, the algorithm $Largest$ $Gaps$ is proposed in this paper to
perform clustering using only the marginals of the matrix, when the number of
blocks is very small with respect to the size of the whole matrix in the case
of binary data. In addition, a model selection method is incorporated with a
proof of its consistency. Thus, this paper shows that studying simplistic
configurations (few blocks compared to the size of the matrix or very
contrasting blocks) with complex algorithms is useless since the marginals
already give very good parameter and classification estimates.

This paper presents a novel approach for learning sparse high-dimensional filters for image filtering tasks. The proposed method combines the strengths of dense conditional random fields (CRFs) and bilateral neural networks to achieve efficient and effective filtering. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on various image filtering tasks, including denoising, deblurring, and inpainting. The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both visual quality and computational efficiency. Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of image filtering and highlights the potential of sparse high-dimensional filters for various image processing tasks.

Semantic segmentation has a wide array of applications ranging from
medical-image analysis, scene understanding, autonomous driving and robotic
navigation. This work deals with medical image segmentation and in particular
with accurate polyp detection and segmentation during colonoscopy examinations.
Several convolutional neural network architectures have been proposed to
effectively deal with this task and with the problem of segmenting objects at
different scale input. The basic architecture in image segmentation consists of
an encoder and a decoder: the first uses convolutional filters to extract
features from the image, the second is responsible for generating the final
output. In this work, we compare some variant of the DeepLab architecture
obtained by varying the decoder backbone. We compare several decoder
architectures, including ResNet, Xception, EfficentNet, MobileNet and we
perturb their layers by substituting ReLU activation layers with other
functions. The resulting methods are used to create deep ensembles which are
shown to be very effective. Our experimental evaluations show that our best
ensemble produces good segmentation results by achieving high evaluation scores
with a dice coefficient of 0.884, and a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of
0.818 for the Kvasir-SEG dataset. To improve reproducibility and research
efficiency the MATLAB source code used for this research is available at
GitHub: https://github.com/LorisNanni.

Although deep models have greatly improved the accuracy and robustness of
image segmentation, obtaining segmentation results with highly accurate
boundaries and fine structures is still a challenging problem. In this paper,
we propose a simple yet powerful Boundary-Aware Segmentation Network (BASNet),
which comprises a predict-refine architecture and a hybrid loss, for highly
accurate image segmentation. The predict-refine architecture consists of a
densely supervised encoder-decoder network and a residual refinement module,
which are respectively used to predict and refine a segmentation probability
map. The hybrid loss is a combination of the binary cross entropy, structural
similarity and intersection-over-union losses, which guide the network to learn
three-level (ie, pixel-, patch- and map- level) hierarchy representations. We
evaluate our BASNet on two reverse tasks including salient object segmentation,
camouflaged object segmentation, showing that it achieves very competitive
performance with sharp segmentation boundaries. Importantly, BASNet runs at
over 70 fps on a single GPU which benefits many potential real applications.
Based on BASNet, we further developed two (close to) commercial applications:
AR COPY & PASTE, in which BASNet is integrated with augmented reality for
"COPYING" and "PASTING" real-world objects, and OBJECT CUT, which is a
web-based tool for automatic object background removal. Both applications have
already drawn huge amount of attention and have important real-world impacts.
The code and two applications will be publicly available at:
https://github.com/NathanUA/BASNet.

When a droplet spreads on a solid substrate, it is unclear what are the
correct boundary conditions to impose at the moving contact line. The classical
no-slip condition is generally acknowledged to lead to a non-integrable
singularity at the moving contact line, for which a slip condition, associated
with a small slip parameter, $\lambda$, serves to alleviate. In this paper, we
discuss what occurs as the slip parameter, $\lambda$, tends to zero. In
particular, we explain how the zero-slip limit should be discussed in
consideration of two distinguished:: one where time is held constant $t =
O(1)$, and one where time tends to infinity at the rate $t = O(|\log
\lambda|)$. The crucial result is that in the case where time is held constant,
the $\lambda \to 0$ limit converges to the slip-free equation, and contact line
slippage occurs as a regular perturbative effect. However, if $\lambda \to 0$
and $t \to \infty$, then contact line slippage is a leading-order singular
effect.

Image segmentation and image restoration are Two important topics in image
processing with great achievements. In this paper, we propose a new multiphase
segmentation model by combining image restoration and image Segmentation
models. Utilizing image Restoration aspects, the proposed segmentation model
can effectively and robustly tackle high noisy images, blurry images, Images
with missing pixels, and vector-valued Images. In particular, One of the most
important segmentation models, the piecewise constant Mumford-Shah model, can
be extended easily in this way to segment gray and vector-valued images
corrupted for example by noise, blur or Missing pixels after coupling a new
data fidelity term which comes from image restoration topics. It can be solved
efficiently using the alternating minimization algorithm, and we prove the
convergence of this algorithm with Three variables under mild condition.
Experiments on many synthetic and real-world images demonstrate that our method
gives better segmentation results in comparison to others state-of-the-art
segmentation models especially for blurry images and images with missing pixels
values.

In this paper,  we study  the dynamics of polynomial skew products of the form f(z,w) = (p(z),  q(z,w)), where p(z) is  a polynomial  of degree at least 2 and q(z,w) is a polynomial in w  with coefficients depending on  z. We introduce  the concept of axiom A for  such  skew products and prove  that if   f satisfies  axiom A, then the postcritical set of f  is a compact subset of C^2. We also provide examples of polynomial skew products that satisfy axiom A and discuss their  dynamical properties.  Our results contribute to the understanding of the dynamics of polynomial skew products   and provide a framework for further research  in  this area.

An important issue with oversampled FIR analysis filter banks (FBs) is to
determine inverse synthesis FBs, when they exist. Given Any complex oversampled
FIR analysis FB, we first provide an algorithm to determine whether there
Exists an inverse FIR synthesis system. We also provide a method to ensure the
Hermitian symmetry property on the synthesis side, which is serviceable to
processing real-valued signals. As an invertible analysis scheme corresponds to
a redundant decomposition, there is No unique inverse FB. Given a particular
solution, we Parameterize the whole family of inverses through a null space
Projection. The resulting reduced parameter set simplifies design procedures,
since the Perfect reconstruction constrained optimization problem is recast as
an unconstrained optimization problem. The design of Optimized synthesis FBs
based on time or frequency localization criteria is then investigated, using a
simple yet efficient gradient algorithm.

We define and investigate, via numerical analysis, a one dimensional
toy-model of a cloud chamber. An energetic quantum particle, whose Initial
state is a superposition of two identical wave packets with opposite average
momentum, interacts during its evolution and exchanges (small amounts of)
energy with an array of localized spins. Triggered by the interaction with the
environment, the initial superposition state turns into an incoherent sum of
two States describing the following situation: or the particle is going to the
left and a large number of spins on the left side changed their states, or The
same is happening on the Right side. this evolution is reminiscent of what
happens in a cloud chamber where a quantum Particle, emitted as a spherical
wave by a radioactive source, marks its passage inside a supersaturated
vapour-chamber in the form of a sequence of small liquid bubbles Arranging
themselves around a possible classical trajectory of the particle.

This academic paper introduces a novel approach to enhance semantic image segmentation using near-infrared information. Traditional methods for semantic image segmentation rely solely on visible light, which limits their ability to accurately identify objects in low light or challenging conditions. In this paper, we propose a method that combines visible light images with near-infrared images to improve segmentation accuracy. We utilize a deep neural network architecture that takes advantage of the complementary information provided by near-infrared images. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms traditional methods in challenging lighting conditions. This research has important implications for various applications, including autonomous driving, surveillance, and medical imaging.

In this paper, the authors propose a 3D segmentation method  using exponential logarithmic loss  (ELL) for objects with highly unbalanced sizes. The existing   segmentation  methods struggle to accurately  segment objects with varying sizes,  as they are designed to handle objects of similar proportions.  The  proposed method  incorporates the  use of ELL,  which can effectively address the imbalance issue by penalizing larger objects and giving more importance to smaller objects.   Additionally, the authors introduce a  multi-scale  approach  to handle objects at  different scales. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms  existing methods in terms of   segmentation accuracy and robustness, particularly for highly unbalanced object sizes.

YouTube-VOS is a sequence-to-sequence video object segmentation method that leverages the large-scale YouTube-VOS dataset. The method utilizes a convolutional LSTM network to model the temporal dependencies in video sequences and generate accurate object masks. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on the YouTube-VOS dataset, outperforming previous methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. The paper presents detailed experimental results and analysis, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method for video object segmentation tasks.

Semantic segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that involves assigning a class label to each pixel in an image. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for learning high-level prior information using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for semantic segmentation. We introduce a new architecture called the High-level Prior Network (HPN), which is designed to capture and leverage high-level semantic information from the input image. The HPN is trained in a supervised manner using a large dataset of annotated images. We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods. Our experimental results demonstrate that the HPN outperforms existing approaches in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. Furthermore, we show that the learned high-level prior can be transferred to other related tasks, such as object detection and image classification, leading to improved performance. Overall, our work highlights the importance of incorporating high-level prior information in semantic segmentation and provides a promising solution for achieving better results in this field.

Deep learning based  image segmentation has  achieved the   state-of-the-art
performance in many medical  applications  such as lesion quantification, organ
detection, etc. However, most of the  methods rely  on supervised learning, which
require  a  large set of  high-quality labeled data. Data annotation is generally
an extremely time-consuming process. To address this  problem, we propose a
generic semi-supervised learning framework  for  image segmentation based on a
deep convolutional neural network (DCNN). An encoder-decoder based DCNN is
initially trained using a  few annotated  training samples. This  initially
trained model is then copied  into  sub-models and  improved iteratively using
random  subsets of unlabeled data  with pseudo labels generated from models
trained in the previous  iteration.  The number of sub-models is gradually
decreased to one in the final  iteration. We evaluate the proposed method on a
public grand-challenge dataset for skin  lesion segmentation. Our method is able
to  significantly improve beyond fully  supervised model learning by
incorporating unlabeled data.

Efficient and easy segmentation of images and volumes is of great practical
importance. Segmentation problems that motivate our Approach originate from
microscopy imaging commonly used in materials science, medicine, and biology.
We formulate image segmentation as a probabilistic pixel classification
problem, and we apply segmentation as a step towards Characterising image
content. Our method allows the user to define structures of interest by
interactively marking a subset of pixels. Thanks to the real-time feedback, the
user can place new markings strategically, depending on the current outcome.
The final pixel classification may be obtained from a very modest user Input.
An important ingredient of our method is A graph that encodes image content.
This graph is built In an unsupervised manner during initialisation and is
based on Clustering of image features. Since we combine a limited amount of
user-labelled data with the clustering information obtained from the unlabelled
Parts of the image, our method fits in the general framework of semi-supervised
learning. we demonstrate how this can be a very efficient approach to
segmentation through pixel classification.

In this paper, we investigate the chiral phase transition in a planar four-Fermi model in the presence of a tilted magnetic field. We use a mean-field approximation to study the behavior of the chiral condensate and the quark number density as a function of temperature and magnetic field strength. We find that the chiral phase transition is significantly affected by the presence of the tilted magnetic field, leading to a modification of the critical temperature and the order of the phase transition. Our results provide insights into the role of magnetic fields in the chiral symmetry breaking and may have implications for the study of QCD phase diagram in the presence of strong magnetic fields.

This paper investigates the concept of almost hypohamiltonian graphs, which are graphs that are almost Hamiltonian but have one missing edge. The authors provide a characterization of almost hypohamiltonian graphs and present several results related to their properties. They also discuss the relationship between almost hypohamiltonian graphs and other types of graphs, such as hypohamiltonian graphs and almost Hamiltonian graphs. The paper concludes with open questions and directions for future research in this area.

A severe application of stress on  articular  cartilage can initiate a cascade
of biochemical reactions that can lead to the development of osteoarthritis. We
constructed a multiscale mathematical  model of the process with three
components:  cellular, chemical, and mechanical. The cellular component
describes the different  chondrocyte states  according to the chemicals these
cells release. The  chemical component models the change in concentrations of
those  chemicals. The mechanical component   contains a simulation of  pressure
application onto a cartilage explant  and  the resulting  strains that initiate
the  biochemical processes. The model  creates a framework for  incorporating
explicit mechanics, simulated by  finite element analysis, into a theoretical
biology framework.

This paper proposes a minimalist design  of  a robust real-time quantum random number generator (RQRNG).  The design is based on  the  principles of quantum mechanics and utilizes the inherent randomness of quantum    phenomena. The proposed RQRNG consists of a  single photon source, a beam  splitter, and two single photon  detectors. We demonstrate that  the  design provides true randomness  and has excellent statistical properties. The implemented RQRNG  achieves  a high   bit rate and low bias, making it suitable for a wide range of applications.  The simplicity and robustness of the design make it a practical solution for generating random numbers in real-time.

We study the phase diagramme of the spin-3/2 Blume-Emery-Griffiths model on a
honeycomb lattice by Monte Carlo simulations in order to verify the presence of
some peculiar features predicted by the effective field theory (EFT) with
correlations. The locations of the order-disorder phase boundaries are
estimated from thermal variations of the magnetic susceptibility curves. It is
found that for positive values of the biquadratic interactions the critical
boundary shows a discontinuous character as a function of the single-ion
anisotropy strength, in line with the EFT expectations. However, for negative
values of the biquadratic interactions the step-like variation of the critical
frontier predicted by EFT was not reproduced.

Traditional deep neural systems struggle to transfer knowledge and generalize
from domains when deploying to real-world systems. Domain generalization
(DG) seeks to develop a universal representation from many source domains to
reduce the network generalization ability on unseen target domains. Recent
DG methods generally focus on the data-level consistency scheme to advance the
generalization capability of deep systems, without considering the synergistic
regularization of other consistent schemes. In this paper, we present a
novel Hierarchical Consistency framework for Domain Generalization (HCDG) by
ensembling Extrinsic Consistency and Intrinsic Consistency. Particularly, for
Extrinsic Consistency, we leverage the knowledge from different source domains
to enforce data-level consistency. Also, we design a novel Amplitude
Gaussian-mixing approach for Fourier-based data augmentation to maintain such
consistency. For Intrinsic Consistency, we perform task-level consistency for
the same instance under the dual-task form. We evaluate the proposed HCDG
structure on three medical image segmentation tasks, i.e., optic cup/disc
segmentation on fundus images and prostate MRI segmentation. Extensive
experimental findings manifest the efficiency and versatility of our HCDG
framework. Code will be available once accept.

The  paper investigates the generalised colouring numbers of  graphs that  exclude a fixed minor. The generalised colouring  number of a graph is  the minimum  number of colours needed to colour the vertices such that no  two adjacent vertices have  the same colour. The paper focuses on  graphs that do not contain a fixed minor, which  is a  smaller graph that   can  be  obtained by  contracting edges or deleting vertices from the   original graph. The authors provide upper and lower bounds on the generalised colouring numbers  of these graphs and discuss  the implications of these results. They also explore the relationship between  the generalised  colouring  numbers  and other graph parameters, such as the chromatic number and the clique number. The paper concludes with open questions and directions for  future research in this  area.

This paper presents a novel approach for dense 3D visual mapping by leveraging semantic simplification. The proposed method aims  to address the  challenges of high computational complexity  and memory  requirements associated with traditional dense   3D mapping  techniques. The approach involves segmenting the input image sequence into  regions  of interest based  on semantic  labels, and  then simplifying these  regions using geometric  and semantic cues. By  simplifying the input data, the computational burden is reduced while preserving the relevant visual information.  The simplified data is used to  construct a dense 3D semantic map, which can be used for applications such as robotic  navigation  and scene understanding. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness  of the proposed  method  in terms  of efficiency and accuracy compared to  traditional dense 3D  mapping techniques.

This paper presents a novel approach for multi-object segmentation using shape priors based on gradient vector flow (GVF). The proposed method aims to optimize the segmentation process by incorporating shape priors into the energy functional. The shape priors are represented by GVF, which captures the global shape information of the objects. The energy functional is formulated as a combination of data term and shape prior term, and is minimized using an iterative optimization algorithm. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving accurate and robust multi-object segmentation. The proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning. However, the lack of annotated data in medical imaging limits the performance of deep learning models. In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised meta-learning approach with disentanglement for domain-generalised medical image segmentation. Our method leverages a small amount of annotated data from the target domain and a large amount of unannotated data from multiple source domains to learn a domain-generalised segmentation model. We introduce a disentanglement module that separates the shared and domain-specific features, enabling the model to adapt to new domains more effectively. Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalisation capability. Our work provides a promising solution for improving medical image segmentation in scenarios with limited annotated data.

This paper investigates the existence  and properties of solitons  in a hard-core bosonic system. The authors use a  Gross-Pitaevskii type equation  to describe the system  and explore the conditions under  which solitons can form. They also go beyond the Gross-Pitaevskii equation and consider additional effects   such as interactions and external potentials. The authors find that solitons can exist  in the  system under certain conditions  and that  their properties can be modified by the presence of interactions and  external potentials. This   study  provides valuable insights into the behavior  of  solitons  in  hard-core bosonic systems and expands our understanding of their dynamics.

This paper presents a case study on the application of Neural Architecture Search (NAS) in the operational context of remote sensing. NAS is a technique that automates the design of neural network architectures, allowing for the discovery of optimal architectures for specific tasks. In this study, NAS is applied to the task of land cover classification using remote sensing data. The authors propose a NAS framework that incorporates domain-specific knowledge and constraints to guide the search process. The results show that the NAS approach outperforms traditional handcrafted architectures in terms of classification accuracy. The study also highlights the challenges and limitations of applying NAS in the operational context, such as computational requirements and the need for domain expertise. Overall, this paper demonstrates the potential of NAS in improving the efficiency and effectiveness of remote sensing applications.

Despite recent progress on semantic segmentation, there still exist huge
challenges in medical ultra-resolution image segmentation. The methods based on
multi-branch structure can make a good balance between computational burdens
and segmentation accuracy. However, the fusion structure in these methods
require to be designed elaborately to achieve desirable result, which leads to
model redundancy. In this paper, we propose Meta Segmentation Network (MSN) to
solve this challenging problem. With the help of meta-learning, the fusion
module of MSN is quite simple but effective. MSN can fast generate the weights
of fusion layers through a simple meta-learner, requiring only a few training
samples and epochs to converge. In addition, to avoid learning all branches
from scratch, we further introduce a particular weight sharing mechanism to
realize a fast knowledge adaptation and share the weights among multiple
branches, resulting in the performance improvement and significant parameters
reduction. The experimental results on two challenging ultra-resolution medical
datasets BACH and ISIC show that MSN achieves the best performance compared
with the state-of-the-art methods.

We study the Brown measure of certain  non-hermitian operators arising from
Voiculescu's  free probability theory. Usually those   operators appear  as the
limit in *-moments of certain ensembles of non-hermitian  random matrices, and
the Brown measure gives then a canonical candidate  for the limit eigenvalue
distribution of the random matrices. A prominent class  for our  operators is
given by  polynomials in *-free variables. Other explicit  examples include
R-diagonal elements and elliptic elements, for which the Brown   measure  was
already known,  and a new class   of triangular-elliptic elements.  Our method  for
the calculation of the Brown measure  is based on a rigorous mathematical
treatment of the hermitian reduction method, as considered  in the physical
literature, combined with subordination ideas and  the linearization trick.

The paper "Loss Max-Pooling for Semantic Image Segmentation"  proposes a novel approach for  semantic image  segmentation using a loss max-pooling mechanism. The authors first introduce the concept of  loss max-pooling,  which aims  to enhance the selection of region proposals  for subsequent classification.  They then describe how the proposed method can be integrated into existing semantic image  segmentation frameworks,  and demonstrate its effectiveness  through  extensive experiments  on benchmark datasets. The results show that  the loss max-pooling approach outperforms alternative  methods in terms  of segmentation accuracy,  highlighting its potential for improving semantic image  segmentation tasks.

This paper adresses statistical performance of subspace DoA estimation
using sensor array, in the asymptotic regime where the number of samples and
sensors both converge to infinity at same rate. Improved subspace DoA
estimators were derived (termed as G-MUSIC) in previous works, and were shown
to be consistent and asymptotically Gaussian distributed in case where the
number of sources and their DoA remain fixed. In this case, which models widely
spaced DoA scenarios, it is proved in the present paper that the traditional
MUSIC method also provides DoA consistent estimates having the same asymptotic
variances as G-MUSIC estimates. The case of DoA that are spaced of the
order of beamwidth, which models closely spaced sources, is also considered.
It is shown that G-MUSIC estimates are still able to consistently separate the
sources, while it is no longer the case for the MUSIC ones. The asymptotic
variances of G-MUSIC estimates are also evaluated.

The Riemann hypothesis is one of  the most famous unsolved  problems in mathematics. In  this paper,  we explore various equivalences of the Riemann hypothesis and their connections to  other important conjectures and inequalities. We  begin by discussing the Robin inequality, which is a result related to the Riemann hypothesis. We then introduce Lagarias  criterion, which provides a necessary and sufficient condition  for the Riemann hypothesis  to  hold. Finally,  we examine  the connections between the Riemann  hypothesis and other conjectures, such  as the Goldbach conjecture and  the twin  prime conjecture. Through our  analysis, we  aim to shed light on  the deep connections between these conjectures  and provide further insights into  the Riemann  hypothesis.

This paper  presents a recurrent segmentation approach for variable computational budgets. The  proposed method utilizes a recurrent neural  network to iteratively refine the segmentation  results based  on the available computational resources. The model is trained using a  combination of supervised and reinforcement learning techniques to optimize the segmentation performance under  different computational constraints.  Experimental results  on various datasets demonstrate  the  effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving high-quality  segmentation results with limited computational  resources. The recurrent segmentation method  shows     promise for applications in real-time or resource-constrained scenarios where computational budgets may vary.

This paper investigates the curvature  tensors of  Hermitian manifolds.  The authors provide  a comprehensive analysis of the various  types of curvature tensors that can be defined on  such manifolds, including the Ricci curvature  tensor, the scalar curvature tensor, and the Weyl curvature tensor. The   paper  also explores the relationships between these curvature  tensors and their properties. The authors  present several examples and applications of these curvature tensors in the context of Hermitian  manifolds.  Overall,   this paper contributes to the understanding of the geometric properties of Hermitian manifolds and  provides   a foundation for further research in this area.

The combings of oriented compact three-manifolds are the homotopy classes of nowhere-zero vector fields in these manifolds. The first invariant of a combing is its Euler characteristic, i.e. the Euler characteristic of the bundle to which the Euler characteristic of a combing representative normalizes the tangent bundle of the three-manifold M. It only depends on the Spit-brain structure of the combing. If this Euler characteristic is a torsion element of the cubic tensor product H2(M,Z), then the combing is called a torsion. Gompf introduced a Q-valued invariant of the torsion of closed three-manifolds, which distinguishes all torsions representing a given Spit-brain structure. This invariant defines a homotopy group for the Heegaard-Floer homology H2(M,Z). We give an alternative definition of this invariant and write it as a link number. We also introduce a similar invariant p1 for the combings of manifolds closed in S2. We show that the  invariant, the simplest integral invariant of rational homology spheres, is the natural invariant of the combings of rational homology balls, which reads as (p1+frac14p1+ frac12p1), where  is the Casson-Walker invariant. We also give a self-contained presentation of combings.

This paper presents a modeling and simulation study on the effects of cyclic loading on the formation of articular cartilage lesions. The study aims to understand the underlying mechanisms of lesion formation and provide insights into potential preventive measures. A finite element model of the knee joint is developed, incorporating the mechanical properties of articular cartilage and the loading conditions experienced during cyclic activities. The model is validated using experimental data and then used to simulate the effects of different loading parameters on lesion formation. The results show that cyclic loading can lead to the development of cartilage lesions, with higher loading magnitudes and frequencies resulting in more severe lesions. The study also investigates the role of cartilage thickness and composition in lesion formation. Overall, the findings contribute to a better understanding of the biomechanics of articular cartilage and provide a basis for future research on preventive strategies for cartilage lesions.

In this work, case of semantic segmentation on a small image dataset
(simulated by 1000 randomly selected images from PASCAL VOC 2012), where only
weak supervision signals (scribbles from user interaction) are available is
studied. Especially, to tackle the problem of limited data annotations in image
segmentation, transferring different pre-trained models and CRF based methods
are applied to enhance segmentation performance. To this end, RotNet,
DeeperCluster, and Semi&Weakly Supervised Learning (SWSL) pre-trained models
are transferred and finetuned in DeepLab-v2 baseline, and dense CRF is
applied both as a post-processing and loss regularization technique. The
results of my study show that, on this small dataset, using a pre-trained
ResNet50 SWSL model gives results that are 7.4% better than applying an
ImageNet pre-trained model; moreover, for the case of training on the full
PASCAL VOC 2012 training data, this pre-training approach increases mIoU
results by almost 4%. On other hand, dense CRF is shown to be very
effective as well, enhancing results both as a loss regularization
technique in weakly supervised training and as post-processing tool.

We study the problem of scheduling $n$ independent moldable tasks on $m$
processors that arises in large-scale parallel computations. When tasks are
monotonic, the best known result is a $(\frac{3}{2}+\epsilon)$-approximation
algorithm for makespan minimization with a complexity linear in $n$ and
polynomial in $\log{m}$ and $\frac{1}{\epsilon}$ where $\epsilon$ is
arbitrarily small. We propose a new perspective of the existing speedup models:
the speedup of a task $T_{j}$ is linear when the number $p$ of assigned
processors is small (up to a threshold $\delta_{j}$) while it presents
monotonicity when $p$ ranges in $[\delta_{j}, k_{j}]$; the bound $k_{j}$
indicates an unacceptable overhead when parallelizing on too many processors.
The generality of this model is proved to be between the classic monotonic and
linear-speedup models. For any given integer $\delta\geq 5$, let $u=\left\lceil
\sqrt[2]{\delta} \right\rceil-1\geq 2$. In this paper, we propose a
$\frac{1}{\theta(\delta)} (1+\epsilon)$-approximation algorithm for makespan
minimization where $\theta(\delta) = \frac{u+1}{u+2}\left( 1- \frac{k}{m}
\right)$ ($m\gg k$). As a by-product, we also propose a
$\theta(\delta)$-approximation algorithm for throughput maximization with a
common deadline.

Background: The trend towards large-scale studies including population
imageing poses new challenges in terms of quality control (QC). This is a
particular issue when automatic processing tools, e.g. image segmentation
methods, are employed to derive quantitative measures or biomarkers for later
analyses. Manual inspection and visual QC of each segmentation isn't feasible
at large scale. However, it's important to be able to automatically detect when
a segmentation method fails so as to avoid inclusion of wrong measurements into
subsequent analyses which could lead to incorrect conclusions. Methods: To
overcome this challenge, we explore an approach for predicting segmentation
quality based on Reverse Classification Accuracy, which enables us to
discriminate between successful and failed segmentations on a per-cases basis.
We validate this approach on a new, large-scale manually-annotated set of 4,800
cardiac magnetic resonance scans. We then apply our method to a large cohort of
7,250 cardiac MRI on which we have performed manual QC. Results: We report
results used for predicting segmentation quality metrics including Dice
Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and surface-distance measures. As initial
validation, we present data for 400 scans demonstrating 99% accuracy for
classifying low and high quality segmentations using predicted DSC scores. As
further validation we show high correlation between real and predicted scores
and 95% classification accuracy on 4,800 scans for which manual segmentations
were available. We mimic real-world application of the method on 7,250 cardiac
MRI where we show good agreement between predicted quality metrics and manual
visual QC scores. Conclusions: We show that RCA has the potential for accurate
and fully automatic segmentation QC on a per-case basis in the context of
large-scale population imageing as in the UK Biobank Imageing Study.

The paper "A common approach to three open problems in number theory" presents a unified framework for solving three long-standing problems in number theory. The three problems considered are the Goldbach conjecture, the twin prime conjecture, and the Collatz conjecture. By introducing a novel methodology combining techniques from algebraic number theory, analytic number theory, and combinatorics, the authors propose a common approach to tackle these three problems. The paper provides a detailed analysis of the proposed approach, including proofs and computational results. The findings of this research have the potential to significantly advance the field of number theory and may lead to solutions for these open problems.

The segmentation of nanoscale electron microscopy (EM) images is crucial but
challenging in connectomics. Recent advances in deep learning have demonstrated
the significant potential of automatic segmentation for tera-scale EM images.
However, none of the existing segmentation methods are error-free, and they
require proofreading, which is typically implemented as an interactive,
semi-automatic process via manual intervention. Herein, we propose a fully
automatic proofreading method based on reinforcement learning. The main idea is
to model the human decision process in proofreading using a reinforcement agent
to acheive fully automatic proofreading. We systematically design the proposed
system by combining multiple reinforcement learning agents in a hierarchical
manner, where each agent focuses only on a specific task while preserving
dependency between agents. Furthermore, we also demonstrate that the episodic
task setting of reinforcement learning can efficiently manage a combination of
merge and split errors concurrently presented in the input. We demonstrate the
efficacy of the proposed system by comparing it with state-of-the-art
proofreading methods using various testing examples.

In this paper we introduce and study a new family of combinatorial simplicial
complexes, which we call immediate snapshot complexes. Our construction and
terminology is strongly motivated by theoretical distributed computing, as
these complexes are combinatorial models of the standard protocol complexes
associated to immediate snapshot read/write shared memory communication model.
In order to define the immediate snapshot complexes we need a new combinatorial
object, which we call a witness structure. These objects are indexing the
simplices in the immediate snapshot complexes, while a special operation on
them, called ghosting, describes the combinatorics of taking simplicial
boundary. In general, we develop the theory of witness structures and use it to
prove several combinatorial as well as topological properties of the immediate
snapshot complexes.

Slack and margin Rescaling are variants of the structured output SVM, which
is frequently applied To problems in computer vision such as image
segmentation, object localization, and learning parts based object models. They
define convex Surrogates to task specific loss functions, which, when
specialized to non-additive loss functions for multi-label problems, yield
extensions to increasing set functions. We demonstrate in this Paper that we
may use These concepts To define polynomial time convex extensions of arbitrary
supermodular functions, providing an analysis framework for the tightness of
these surrogates. This analysis framework Shows that, while neither margin nor
slack rescaling dominate the other, known bounds on supermodular functions can
be used to derive extensions that dominate both of these, indicating possible
directions for defining novel structured output prediction surrogates. In
addition To the analysis of structured prediction loss functions, these results
imply an approach To supermodular minimization in which margin rescaling is
combined with non-polynomial time convex extensions to compute a sequence of LP
relaxations reminiscent of a cutting plane method. This approach is applied to
the problem of selecting representative exemplars from a set of images,
validating our theoretical contributions.

In this paper, we investigate the effects of Coulomb screening on the process of linear coasting nucleosynthesis. We use a combination of analytical and numerical methods to study the impact of Coulomb screening on the production of light elements during the early stages of the universe. Our results show that Coulomb screening can significantly affect the abundance of light elements, particularly helium and lithium. We also find that the degree of Coulomb screening depends on the temperature and density of the plasma, as well as the nuclear reaction rates. These findings have important implications for our understanding of primordial nucleosynthesis and the evolution of the early universe.

Cutting and pasting image segments feels intuitive: the choice of source
templates gives artists flexibility in recombining existing source material. Formally, this process takes an image set as input and outputs a collage of the
set elements. 

Such selection from sets of source templates does not fit easily
in classical convolutional neural models requiring inputs of fixed size. 

Inspired by advances in attention and set-input machine learning, we present a
novel architecture that can generate in one forward pass image collages of
source templates using set-structured representations. This paper has the
following contributions: (i) a novel framework for image generation called
Memory Attentive Generation of Image Collages (MAGIC) which gives artists new
ways to create digital collages; (ii) from the machine-learning perspective, we
show a novel Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) architecture that uses
Set-Transformer layers and set-pooling to blend sets of random image samples -
a hybrid non-parametric approach.

shown that in these situations there exist regular spherically symmetric problems.

condensates. The defect is a cavity filled with two BEC on the backdrop of
the BEC. The droplet is an object on the backdrop of the empty space. For
(a) and (b) cases the obtained objects are supported by a constant internal
trapping potential and for (c) case the droplet is a self-maintaining object
without any internal potential. The idea of design of an
elementary logic qubit device on the basis of this droplet is debated.

In a MIMO radar network the multiple transmit elements may emit waveforms
that differ on power and bandwidth. In this paper, we are asking, given that
these two resources are limited, what is the optimal power, optimal bandwidth
and optimal joint power and bandwidth allocation for best localization of
multiple targets. The well known Cr\'amer-Rao lower bound for target
localization accuracy is used as a figure of merit and approximate solutions
are found by minimizing a sequence of convex problems. Their quality is
assessed through extensive numerical simulations and with the help of a
lower-bound on the true solution. Simulations results reveal that bandwidth
allocation policies have a definitely stronger impact on performance than
power.

In this paper, we explicitly calculate the aether-like corrections for the
gravitational field in the case when the space-time involves an additional compact
spatial dimension besides of usual two dimensions. Our method is based on
an explicit summation over the Kaluza-Klein tower of fields which turns out to
be no more important than the finite-temperature calculations. We found some
new terms which can be treated as different five-dimensional generalizations of
the aether-like terms $\kappa^{mnpq}F_{mn}F_{pq}$ and
$\bar{\psi}c^{mn}\gamma_m\partial_n\psi$ which in three dimensions are treated
as key ingredients of the Lorentz-breaking extension of the standard
model. We have seen that these new terms become to dominate in the limit where
the extra dimension is very large, enabling me to assume that there will be
essential modifications of quantum corrections if our space indeed has a large
additional spatial dimension. However, we have seen that in the CPT-even case we
have extra new particles as a result of the additional dimension.

This paper  presents  a new method for   controlling the evolution of active contours  in  image segmentation  tasks. The proposed  method, called Deep Active Contours  using Locally  Controlled  Distance Vector Flow (DAC-DFV),  integrates  deep learning and  vector flow-based contour evolution. The model is  designed to adaptively determine  the local direction of  contour propagation based on  image features, thus improving the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that DAC-DFV outperforms  existing methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. The proposed method shows promising potential for a wide range of applications  in medical imaging and computer vision.

We report on synthesis and anisotropic physical properties of URhIn$_{5}$.
High quality single crystals were grown in In-flux. The compound undergoes a
second order phase transition into an antiferromagnetic state at
T$_{\textrm{N}}$ = 98 K. The transition is field independant up to 9 T. An
increase of the resistivity $\rho$ with j along the [100], [110] and [001]
tetragonal axis indicates a spin-density-wave induced order with the gap
opening first along the [001] direction. The magnetic susceptibility $\chi$ =
M/H exhibits a strong anisotropy. Above T $=$ 200 K, $\chi$(T) follows
Curie-Weiss law with the effective moment of $\mu_{\textrm{eff}}$ = 3.71
$\mu_{\textrm{B}}/$U and the Weiss temperatures of $\theta_{\textrm{P}}^{[100]}
= -900$ K and $\theta_{\textrm{P}}^{[001]} = -500$ K for H $\parallel$ [100]
and H $\parallel$ [001] respectively. The characteristic Kondo-like temperature
for URhIn$_{5}$ yields T$_{\textrm{K}} =$ 125 K.

This paper presents a radiative transfer model for calculating the reflectance and transmittance of light in contaminated rough slabs. The model takes into account multiple scattering and absorption effects, as well as the presence of surface roughness and contaminants on the slab. The model is based on the Monte Carlo method, which simulates the path of photons through the slab and accounts for interactions with the rough surface and contaminants. The model is validated against experimental data and shows good agreement. This radiative transfer model can be used to study the influence of surface roughness and contaminants on the optical properties of slabs, and has potential applications in fields such as remote sensing, environmental monitoring, and non-destructive testing.

This paper presents a  comprehensive  review of the use of tungsten disulfide (WS2) as  a saturable  absorber  for ultrafast photonic applications in mode-locked and  Q-switched lasers. WS2 has emerged as a promising  material  due to its  unique optical and   electronic  properties, including a large  bandgap and strong nonlinear absorption. The paper discusses the fabrication methods  of WS2-based saturable absorbers and their integration  into laser systems. It also highlights the recent advancements in WS2-based mode-locked and Q-switched lasers,  including their performance characteristics and potential applications. The review  concludes with a discussion on the  challenges and future prospects  of WS2 as  a saturable absorber for ultrafast photonic applications.

This paper investigates the stability and monotonicity properties of certain discretizations of the Biot's model, which is a mathematical model used to describe the behavior of fluid-saturated porous media. The authors analyze two different discretization schemes and prove that they both exhibit stability and monotonicity under certain conditions. The stability property ensures that the numerical solution of the discretized model remains bounded and does not blow up, while the monotonicity property guarantees that the solution preserves the ordering of the initial data. These properties are important for the accuracy and reliability of numerical simulations of the Biot's model. The authors provide numerical experiments to validate their theoretical results and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed discretization schemes. Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding and development of numerical methods for the Biot's model, which has applications in various fields such as geomechanics and petroleum engineering.

Measurement-device-independent quantum  key distribution (MDI-QKD) is   a   promising approach for secure communication. However, it is  susceptible to various attacks, such as the photon-number-splitting (PNS) attack. In this paper, we propose a modified coherent state for  MDI-QKD that is resistant to the PNS  attack. We experimentally demonstrate  the  feasibility of our approach and show that it achieves a  higher secure key rate compared  to conventional MDI-QKD schemes. Our  results suggest that the modified coherent state    can enhance the  security and performance of MDI-QKD systems, making  them more suitable for practical applications.

Real-time semantic video segmentation is a challenging task due to the strict
requirements of inference speed. Recent approaches mainly devote great efforts
to reducing the model size for high efficiency. In this paper, we rethink this
problem from a different viewpoint: using knowledge contained in compressed
videos. We propose a simple and effective framework, dubbed TapLab, to tap into
resources from the compressed domain. Specifically, we design a fast feature
warping module using motion vectors for acceleration. To reduce the noise
introduced by motion vectors, we design a residual-guided correction module and
a residual-guided frame selection module using residuals. TapLab significantly
reduces redundant computations of the state-of-the-art fast semantic image
segmentation models, running 3 to 10 times faster with controllable accuracy
degradation. The experimental results show that TapLab achieves 62.6% mIoU on
the Cityscapes dataset at 99.8 FPS with a single GPU card for the 4889x6785
videos. A high-speed version even reaches the speed of 160+ FPS. Codes will be
available soon at https://github.com/Sixkplus/TapLab.

In part I, using the theory of $\infty$-categories, we constructed a natural
``continuous action'' of $\operatorname {Ham} (M, \omega) $ on the Fukaya
catagory of a closed monotone symplectic manifold. Here we show that this
action is generally homotopically non-trivial, i.e implicitly the main part of
a conjecture of Teleman. We use this to give various applications. For example
we find new curvature constraint phenomena for smooth and singular
$\mathcal{G}$-connections on principal $\mathcal{G}$-bundles over $S ^{4}$,
where $\mathcal{G}$ is $\operatorname {PU} (2)$ or $\operatorname {Ham} (S ^{2}
)$. Even for the classical group $\operatorname {PU} (2)$, these phenomena are
invisible to Chern-Weil theory, and are inaccessible to known Yang-Mills theory
and quantum characteristic classes techniques. So this can be understood as one
application of Floer theory and the theory of $\infty$-categories in basic
differential geometry. We also develop, based on this $\infty$-categorical
Fukaya theory, some basic new integer valued invariants of smooth manifolds,
called quantum obstruction. On the way we also construct what we call quantum
Maslov classes, which are higher degree variants of the relative Seidel
morphism. This also leads to new applications in Hofer geometry of the space of
Lagrangian equators in $S^2$.

This paper presents a macroscopic acousto-mechanical analogy of a microbubble, which is a small gas-filled cavity in a liquid medium. The analogy is based on the assumption that the microbubble can be treated as a linear elastic material with a compressibility that depends on the bubble's size and the surrounding liquid properties. The analogy is derived by considering the equations of motion for the microbubble and the surrounding liquid, and then applying a perturbation analysis to obtain a simplified set of equations that describe the bubble's behavior. The resulting equations are similar to those used to describe the motion of a macroscopic elastic material subjected to an external force. The analogy is validated by comparing the predicted behavior of the microbubble with experimental data obtained from ultrasound imaging. The results show good agreement between the predicted and observed behavior, indicating that the macroscopic acousto-mechanical analogy is a useful tool for understanding and predicting the behavior of microbubbles in a liquid medium.

Accurate delineation of pathological lungs from computed tomography (CT)
images remains mostly unsolved becasue available methods fail to provide a
reliable generic solution due to high variability of abnormality appearance.
Local descriptor-based classification methods have shown to work well in
annotating pathologies; however, these methods are usually computationally
intensive which restricts their widespread use in real-time or near-real-time
clinical applications. In this paper, we present a novel approach for fast,
accurate, reliable segmentation of pathological lungs from CT scans by
combining region-based segmentation method with local descriptor classification
that is performed on an optimized sampling grid. Our method works in two
stages; during stage one, we adapted the fuzzy connectedness (FC) image
segmentation algorithm to perform initial lung parenchyma extraction. In the
second stage, texture-based local descriptors are utilized to segment abnormal
imaging patterns using a near optimal keypoint analysis by employing centroid
of supervoxel as grid points. The quantitative results show that our
pathological lung segmentation method is fast, robust, and improves on current
standards and has potential to enhance the performance of routine clinical
tasks.

In this paper, we propose a novel method for augmenting the accuracy of mitotic cell count in histopathology images. Our proposed method utilizes a Field Of Interest (FOI) proposal technique that effectively identifies the regions of interest in the image that contain mitotic cells. These regions are then analyzed and classified using a deep learning-based algorithm to accurately count the number of mitotic cells. Experimental results on a large dataset of histopathology images demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of mitotic cell count accuracy. Additionally, the proposed method reduces the computational complexity and time required for mitotic cell counting, making it more suitable for real-world applications in clinical settings. Overall, our study presents a significant advancement in mitotic cell count accuracy and efficiency.

This paper presents the design and implementation of an FPGA-based data read-out system for the Belle 2 pixel detector. The Belle 2 experiment is a high-energy physics experiment that aims to study the properties of B mesons. The pixel detector is a crucial component of the Belle 2 experiment, responsible for detecting and measuring the trajectories of charged particles. The data read-out system is responsible for collecting and processing the data from the pixel detector. The proposed system utilizes FPGA technology to achieve high-speed data transfer and processing. The design and implementation of the system are described in detail, including the architecture, data flow, and control logic. The performance of the system is evaluated through simulations and experiments, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling the high data rates of the pixel detector. The results show that the FPGA-based data read-out system is capable of meeting the requirements of the Belle 2 experiment, providing a reliable and efficient solution for data collection and processing.

Since acquiring pixel-wise annotations for training convolutional neural
networks for semantic image segmentation is time-consuming, weakly supervised
approaches that only require class tags have been proposed. In this work, we
propose another form of supervision, namely image captions as they can be found
on the Internet. These captions have two advantages. They do not require
additional curation as it is the case for the clean class tags used by current
weakly supervised approaches and they provide textual context for the classes
present in an image. To leverage such textual context, we deploy a multi-modal
network that learns a joint embedding of the visual representation of the image
and the textual representation of the caption. The network estimates text
activation maps (TAMs) for class names as well as compound concepts, i.e.
combinations of nouns and their attributes. The TAMs of compound concepts
describing classes of interest substantially improve the quality of the
estimated class activation maps which are then used to train a network for
semantic segmentation. We evaluate our method on the COCO dataset where it
achieves state of the art results for weakly supervised image segmentation.

While   making a tremendous impact in various fields,  deep neural networks
usually require large amounts of labeled data for training which are expensive
to collect in many applications, especially in  the medical domain. Unlabeled
data, on the other hand, is much more abundant. Semi-supervised learning
techniques, such as  co-training,  could provide a powerful tool  to  leverage
unlabeled data. In  this paper, we propose a novel framework, uncertainty-aware
multi-view  co-training  (UMCT), to address  semi-supervised learning on 3D data,
such as volumetric data from medical imaging.  In our  work, co-training is
achieved by exploiting  multi-viewpoint  consistency of 3D data. We  generate
different views  by rotating   or permuting the 3D data and utilize asymmetrical
3D kernels  to encourage diversified features  in different sub-networks. In
addition, we  propose  an uncertainty-weighted label fusion mechanism to  estimate
the  reliability of each view's prediction  with Bayesian deep  learning. As one
view requires the supervision from other views in co-training, our
self-adaptive approach computes a confidence score for the  prediction  of each
unlabeled sample in order to assign a reliable pseudo label. Thus, our approach
can take  advantage of unlabeled data during  training. We show the effectiveness
of our proposed semi-supervised method on  several public  datasets from  medical
image segmentation tasks (NIH pancreas & LiTS  liver tumor dataset). Meanwhile,
a  fully-supervised method based on our approach  achieved state-of-the-art
performances  on  both the LiTS  liver tumor segmentation  and the Medical
Segmentation Decathlon  (MSD) challenge, demonstrating the  robustness and value
of our framework, even when fully  supervised training is feasible.

We present a numerical strategy for the design of dual-wavelength sources based on optical fibers. This dual-wavelength source is based on the soliton splitting and the frequency shift of the soliton itself, which occur in the supercontinuum generation process. The wavelength, temporal width and peak power are found by a genetic algorithm which is best suited for each input pulse. This strategy is implemented on a grid platform to take advantage of distributed computing. The results are useful for optical coherence tomography applications where it is necessary to have two bell-shaped pulses at the two corners of the second near-infrared window.

This paper explores the phenomenon known as the quantum Zeno effect and its connection to the concept of Hamlet and similar effects in the context of polarization measurements. The quantum Zeno effect refers to the inhibition or prevention of a physical process through frequent measurement or detection of its state. This study investigates the relationship between the quantum Zeno effect and the quantum Hamlet effect, wherein frequent measurements can stave off the collapse of a quantum system into a definite state. The focus is specifically on polarization measurements, and experimental evidence is presented to support the existence of these effects. The findings of this research contribute to a deeper understanding of quantum mechanics and its implications for control and manipulation of quantum systems.

This paper introduces the concept of edge-intersecting and non-splitting  one  bend paths  in  a grid. It  presents a method to construct the corresponding graphs for  these paths, which have applications in  network design and routing. The paper also analyzes  the properties and structures of these graphs, providing insights into their  connectivity, diameter,  and  ultra-metrics. Additionally, the paper  proposes an algorithm to  efficiently determine the  shortest   edge-intersecting and non-splitting one bend  paths in a  grid. Experimental results   demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed algorithm. Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding and utilization of graphs of edge-intersecting and non-splitting one bend paths in grid-based  systems.

An irreversible $k$-threshold process (also a $k$-neighbor bootstrap
percolation) is a dynamic process on a graph where vertices change color from
white to black if they have at least $k$ black neighbors. An irreversible
$k$-conversion set of a graph $G$ is a subset $S$ of vertices of $G$ such that
the irreversible $k$-threshold process starting with $S$ black eventually
changes all vertices of $G$ to black. We show that deciding the existence of an
irreversible 2-conversion set of a given size is NP-complete, even for graphs
of maximum degree 4, which answers a question of Dreyer and Roberts.
Conversely, we show that for graphs of maximum degree 3, the minimum size of an
irreversible 2-conversion set can be computed in polynomial time. Moreover, we
find an optimal irreversible 3-conversion set for the toroidal grid,
simplifying constructions of Pike and Zou.

This paper introduces NeurReg, a neural registration framework that utilizes deep learning for accurately aligning medical images with different modalities and/or patient-specific anatomical variations. NeurReg leverages the concept of cycle-consistent adversarial networks (CycleGANs) to simultaneously learn registration and segmentation tasks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of NeurReg on various medical imaging datasets, achieving superior registration accuracy compared to state-of-the-art classical registration methods. Furthermore, we showcase its application in image segmentation by training a neural network to perform segmentation on the registered images. Our results suggest that NeurReg can significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image registration and segmentation processes, thereby enabling advanced image analysis and clinical decision-making.

TFLMS: Large Model Support in TensorFlow by Graph Rewriting

This paper introduces TFLMS, an approach to support large models in TensorFlow through graph rewriting techniques. Large models, especially those with deep neural network architectures, often encounter memory limitations during training and inference. TFLMS addresses this challenge by introducing novel strategies to optimize memory usage and accelerate the execution of TensorFlow graphs.

The authors present a comprehensive analysis of the memory bottlenecks in TensorFlow and propose a set of graph rewriting rules to overcome these limitations. These rules leverage the unique characteristics of deep neural networks and adapt the graph representation to enable efficient operations on subgraphs.

TFLMS also introduces a memory-efficient parallel execution strategy for TensorFlow graphs, enabling models to scale across multiple GPUs. By applying graph rewriting techniques, TFLMS reduces the memory footprint of large models, allowing them to fit into the available GPU memory and leading to significant speedups in both training and inference.

The authors provide an extensive evaluation of TFLMS on a variety of benchmarks, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing memory usage and improving performance for large models. They also compare TFLMS with other existing approaches and discuss its advantages and limitations.

Overall, this paper presents a novel approach, TFLMS, which addresses the memory limitations of large models in TensorFlow. The proposed graph rewriting techniques offer a promising solution to optimize memory usage and accelerate the execution of deep neural networks, enabling researchers and practitioners to train and deploy larger and more complex models.

This paper presents a robust regression approach for image binarization under
significant background variations and observation noises. The work is motivated
by the need of identifying foreground regions in noisy microscopic image or
degraded document images, where significant background variation and severe
noise make an image binarization challenging. The proposed method first
estimates the background of an input image, subtracts the estimated background
from the input image, and apply a global thresholding to the subtracted outcome
for achieving a binary image of foregrounds. A robust regression approach was
proposed to estimate the background intensity surface with minimal effects of
foreground intensities and noises, and a global threshold selector was proposed
on the basis of a model selection criterion in a sparse regression. The
proposed approach was validated using 26 test images and the corresponding
ground truths, and the outcomes of the proposed work were compared with those
from nine existing image binarization methods. The approach was also combined
with three state-of-the-art morphological segmentation methods to show how the
proposed approach can improve their image segmentation outcomes.

Background: Cardiac MRI derived biventricular mass and function values,
such as end-systolic volume (ESV), end-diastolic volume (EDV), ejection
fraction (EF), stroke volume (SV), and ventricular mass (VM) are clinically
poorly recognized. Image segmentation can be difficult and time-consuming, due
to the intricate physiology of the human heart.
  Objectives: This study uses $\nu$-net (/nju:u$\varepsilon$t/) -- a deep
learning technique providing for fully-automated low quality segmentation of
right (RV) and left ventricular (SV) endocardium and epicardium for extraction
of cardiac function parameters.
  Methods: A set consisting of 253 manually segmented cases has been designed to
train a deep neural network. Moreover, the network has been implemented on 4
different multicenter data sets with a total of over 1000 cases.
  Results: For LV EF the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) is 98, 95,
and 80 % (95 %), and for RV EF 96, and 87 % (80 %) on the respective data sets
(human expert ICCs indicated in parenthesis). The SV VM ICC is 95, and 94 % (84
%), and the RV VM ICC is 83, and 83 % (54 %). This analysis describes a simple
adjustment process, providing for the adaptation to distinct segmentation
philosophies. $\nu$-net displays state of-the-art performance in terms of dice
coefficient.
  Conclusions: Biventricular mass and function values can be analyzed
accurately in high quality by using a deep neural network for cardiac MRI
segmentation, particularly in the anatomically complex right ventricle. Adaption
to individual segmentation styles by using a simple adjustment method is
feasible, providing for the extraction of novel data without time-consuming
additional training.

Unsuреrvіsеd іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn аlgоrіthms аіm аt іdеntіfуіng dіsjоіnt
hоmоgеnеоus rеgіоns іn аn іmаgе, аnd hаvе bееn subjесt tо соnsіdеrаblе
аttеntіоn іn thе mасhіnе vіsіоn соmmunіtу. Ιn thіs рареr, а рорulаr thеоrеtісаl
mоdеl wіth іt's оrіgіns іn stаtіstісаl рhуsісs аnd sосіаl dуnаmісs, knоwn аs
thе Dеffuаnt-Wеіsbuсh mоdеl, іs аррlіеd tо thе іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn рrоblеm. Τhе
Dеffuаnt-Wеіsbuсh mоdеl hаs bееn fоund tо bе usеful іn mоdеllіng thе еvоlutіоn
оf а сlоsеd sуstеm оf іntеrасtіng аgеnts сhаrасtеrіsеd bу thеіr оріnіоns оr
bеlіеfs, lеаdіng tо thе fоrmаtіоn оf сlustеrs оf аgеnts whо shаrе а sіmіlаr
оріnіоn оr bеlіеf аt stеаdу stаtе. Ιn thе соntехt оf іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn, thіs
рареr соnsіdеrs а ріхеl аs аn аgеnt аnd іt's соlоur рrореrtу аs іt's оріnіоn,
wіth оріnіоn uрdаtеs аs реr thе Dеffuаnt-Wеіsbuсh mоdеl. Араrt frоm аррlуіng
thе bаsіс mоdеl tо іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn, thіs рареr іnсоrроrаtеs аdjасеnсу аnd
nеіghbоurhооd іnfоrmаtіоn іn thе mоdеl, whісh fасtоrs іn thе lосаl sіmіlаrіtу
аnd smооthnеss рrореrtіеs оf іmаgеs. Соnvеrgеnсе іs rеасhеd whеn thе numbеr оf
unіquе ріхеl оріnіоns, і.е., thе numbеr оf соlоur сеntrеs, mаtсhеs thе
рrе-sресіfіеd numbеr оf сlustеrs. Εхреrіmеnts аrе реrfоrmеd оn а sеt оf іmаgеs
frоm thе Βеrkеlеу Ιmаgе Sеgmеntаtіоn Dаtаsеt аnd thе rеsults аrе аnаlуsеd bоth
quаlіtаtіvеlу аnd quаntіtаtіvеlу, whісh іndісаtе thаt thіs sіmрlе аnd іntuіtіvе
mеthоd іs рrоmіsіng fоr іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn. То thе bеst оf thе knоwlеdgе оf thе
аuthоr, thіs іs thе fіrst wоrk whеrе а thеоrеtісаl mоdеl frоm stаtіstісаl
рhуsісs аnd sосіаl dуnаmісs hаs bееn suссеssfullу аррlіеd tо іmаgе рrосеssіng.

Quantitative image analysis often depends on an accurate classification of the digitized areas by means of a process of segmentation. But artifacts of the microscope, like the partial volume effect and noise of the photographic plates, cause a variation in the intensity of the digitized intensities of the constituent classes, and in consequence the intensities of one class overlap those of another. The result is that the digitized intensity distributions are ambiguous and that the thresholding methods do not give a satisfactory result because of the ambiguous overlap regions. The ambiguity is more complex when there are more than two constituents, as in unsaturated granular media. Consequently, in these cases it is necessary to use a sequence of steps: first, the ambiguous transition regions between the classes are located and eliminated, which enables the global thresholding of the one-class areas; then the transition regions are classified by means of a distance function, and finally both segregations are combined to produce a classified image. This sequence includes three methods of locating transitional areas, and we have shown that these methods can separate ambiguous transitional areas from the one-class regions with satisfactory accuracy on a large number of digitized images. For typical levels of noise in the images, the misclassification errors and area differences between each class of the synthetic images and the resulting classified images were 0.69-1.48 and 0.01–0.74 % respectively, showing that the accuracy of the segregation is quite satisfactory. It has been shown that the method can accurately segregate x-ray microtomographic images of granular media.

This paper proposes a novel approach for training multi-organ segmentation networks using sample selection by relaxed upper confident bound. The authors argue that current methods for training such networks often suffer from the problem of imbalanced training data, leading to poor performance on underrepresented organs. To address this issue, they introduce a sample selection strategy based on the relaxed upper confident bound, which aims to select informative samples that can improve the network's performance on underrepresented organs. The proposed method is evaluated on a large dataset of abdominal CT scans and compared with several state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves the segmentation accuracy for underrepresented organs, outperforming existing methods. The authors conclude that the sample selection strategy based on relaxed upper confident bound is an effective approach for training multi-organ segmentation networks.

Еnеrgу-еffісіеnt соmmunісаtіоn usіng а сlаss оf sраtіаl mоdulаtіоn (SΜ) thаt
еnсоdеs thе sоurсе іnfоrmаtіоn еntіrеlу іn thе аntеnnа іndісеs іs соnsіdеrеd іn
thіs рареr. Τhе еnеrgу-еffісіеnt mоdulаtіоn dеsіgn іs fоrmulаtеd аs а соnvех
орtіmіzаtіоn рrоblеm, whеrе mіnіmum асhіеvаblе аvеrаgе sуmbоl роwеr соnsumрtіоn
іs dеrіvеd wіth rаtе, реrfоrmаnсе, аnd hаrdwаrе соnstrаіnts. Τhе thеоrеtісаl
rеsult bоunds аnу mоdulаtіоn sсhеmе оf thіs сlаss, аnd еnсоmраssеs thе ехіstіng
sрасе shіft kеуіng (SSΚ), gеnеrаlіzеd SSΚ (GSSΚ), аnd Ηаmmіng соdе-аіdеd SSΚ
(НSSΚ) sсhеmеs аs sресіаl саsеs. Τhе thеоrеtісаl орtіmum іs асhіеvеd bу thе
рrороsеd рrасtісаl еnеrgу-еffісіеnt НSSΚ (ЕΕ-ΗSSΚ) sсhеmе thаt іnсоrроrаtеs а
nоvеl usе оf thе Наmmіng соdе аnd Ηuffmаn соdе tесhnіquеs іn thе аlрhаbеt аnd
bіt-mарріng dеsіgns. Ехреrіmеntаl studіеs dеmоnstrаtе thаt ЕЕ-ΗSSК
sіgnіfісаntlу оutреrfоrms ехіstіng sсhеmеs іn асhіеvіng nеаr-орtіmаl еnеrgу
еffісіеnсу. Аn аnаlуtісаl ехроsіtіоn оf kеу рrореrtіеs оf thе ехіstіng GSSΚ
(іnсludіng SSК) mоdulаtіоn thаt mоtіvаtеs а fundаmеntаl соnsіdеrаtіоn fоr thе
