This paper presents a study on the  optimal boundary control of a  simplified Ericksen-Leslie system for   nematic liquid crystal flows in two dimensions.  The goal is to find an optimal control  strategy that minimizes a cost functional representing the  total energy of the system. The authors derive the necessary  optimality conditions  for the control problem and propose a numerical scheme based on the  finite  element method to solve it. The   effectiveness  of the proposed approach is demonstrated through numerical  simulations. The findings of  this study contribute to the  understanding and optimization  of nematic liquid crystal flows, which have important applications in  various   fields including materials science and display technology.

Privacy amplification is a crucial step in secure communication protocols, where two parties aim to establish a shared secret key over an insecure channel. Non-signaling privacy amplification protocols are designed to ensure that an eavesdropper cannot gain any information about the shared key. In this paper, we prove the impossibility of achieving non-signaling privacy amplification. We demonstrate that any protocol that claims to achieve non-signaling privacy amplification must either leak information to the eavesdropper or result in a shared key that is not uniformly distributed. Our proof is based on information-theoretic arguments and provides a fundamental limitation on the achievable level of privacy in secure communication protocols. This result has implications for the design and analysis of privacy amplification protocols and highlights the need for alternative approaches to achieve secure communication.

This fusion of the tensor of Maxwell and the Riemann-Christoffel curvature tensor can be shown to lead to a geometrical theory of electricity and magnetism. While this theory gives directly the classical Maxwell equations, it extends the interpretation of them by giving geometrical definitions to the density of charge and the density of mass and the four-velocity that determines their motion. These geometrical definitions are reminiscent of the interpretation of mass in general revolu-tionary theory in terms of the scalar curvature r2 and the emergence of gravity. The theory of gravity emerging from this theory is shown to be equivalent to Einstein's general theory of relativity with the addition of a momenta-energy tensor which mimics the properties of dark matter or dark energy. In a word, the proposed geometrical interpretation of the Maxwell tensor puts both electric and gravitational phenomena on an equal footing by linking them to the curvature of space-time. We compare the solution of the geometrical theory with the solution of the classical Maxwell and Einstein equations.

In the present paper, we derive a closed-form solution of the multi-period
portfolio choice problem for a quadratic utility function with and without a
riskless asset. All results are derived under weak conditions on the asset
returns. No assumption on the correlation structure between different time
points is needed and no assumption on the distribution is imposed. All
expressions are presented in terms of the conditional mean vectors and the
conditional covariance matrices. If the multivariate process of the asset
returns is independent it is shown that in the case without a riskless asset
the solution is presented as a sequence of optimal portfolio weights obtained
by solving the single-period Markowitz optimisation problem. The process
dynamics are included only in the shape parametre of the utility function. If a
riskless asset is present then the multi-period optimal portfolio weights are
proportional to the single-period solutions multiplied by time-varying
constants which are depending on the process dynamics. Remarkably, in the case
of a portfolio selection with the tangency portfolio the multi-period solution
coincides with the sequence of the simple-period solutions. Finally, we compare
the suggested strategies with existing multi-period portfolio allocation
methods for real data.

We study a natural variant of the implicational fragment of propositional
logic. Its formulas are pairs of conjunctions of positive literals, related
together by an implicational-like connective; the semantics of this sort of
implication is defined in terms of a threshold on a conditional probability of
the consequent, given the antecedent: we are dealing with what the data
analysis community calls confidence of partial implications or association
rules. Existing studies of redundancy among these partial implications have
characterized so far only entailment from one premise and entailment from two
premises, both in the stand-alone case and in the case of presence of
additional classical implications (this is what we call "relative entailment"). 

By exploiting a previously noted alternative view of the entailment in terms of
linear programming duality, we characterize exactly the cases of entailment
from arbitrary numbers of premises, again both in the stand-alone case and in
the case of presence of additional classical implications. 

As a result, we
obtain decision algorithms of better complexity; additionally, for each
potential case of entailment, we identify a critical confidence threshold and
show that it is, actually, intrinsic to each set of premises and antecedent of
the conclusion.

Unsupervised image segmentation algorithms aim at identifying disjoint
homogeneous regions in an image, and Have been subject to considerable
attention in the machine vision community. In this paper, a popular theoretical
model with it's origins in statistical physics and social dynamics, Known as
The Deffuant-Weisbuch model, is applied to the image segmentation problem. The
Deffuant-Weisbuch model has been found to be useful in modelling the evolution
of a closed system of interacting agents characterised By their opinions or
beliefs, leading to the formation of clusters of agents who share a similar
opinion or belief at steady state. In the context of image segmentation, this
paper considers a pixel as an agent and it's colour property as it's opinion,
with opinion updates as per the Deffuant-Weisbuch model. Apart from applying
the basic model to image segmentation, this paper incorporates adjacency and
neighbourhood information in The model, which factors in the local similarity
and smoothness properties of images. Convergence is reached when the number of
unique pixel opinions, I.e., The number of colour centres, matches the
pre-specified Number of clusters. Experiments Are performed on A set of images
from the Berkeley Image Segmentation Dataset and The results are analysed both
qualitatively and quantitatively, which indicate that this simple and intuitive
method is promising for image segmentation. To the best of the knowledge of the
Author, this is the first work where a theoretical model from statistical
physics and social dynamics has been successfully applied to image processing.

Cardiac segmentation   is  a crucial step in medical image analysis for diagnosing and   treating cardiovascular diseases. However, accurate and  robust  segmentation remains  challenging due to the complex anatomical structures and variations in cardiac images.  In this paper, we propose a novel approach for cardiac segmentation that incorporates strong anatomical guarantees. Our method leverages a deep learning framework  combined with a  graph-based optimization algorithm to  achieve accurate  and consistent segmentation results. We evaluate our  approach on a large dataset of cardiac images and compare  it with state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate  that our method outperforms existing approaches in terms  of segmentation  accuracy and robustness. Furthermore, our approach provides strong anatomical guarantees, ensuring that the segmented regions adhere to the expected  cardiac anatomy. Overall, our proposed  method  has  the potential   to improve the accuracy  and reliability of cardiac segmentation in clinical    practice.

Тhе реrсерtuаl-bаsеd grоuріng рrосеss рrоduсеs а hіеrаrсhісаl аnd

This academic paper presents a novel approach for the extraction of face masks in video sequences. Face masks are crucial in various computer vision tasks, such as face recognition and expression analysis. The proposed method utilizes a combination of deep learning techniques and traditional image processing algorithms to accurately extract face masks from video frames. First, a deep neural network is trained to detect and localize facial features. Then, a series of image processing techniques, including edge detection and segmentation, are applied to refine the extracted face regions. The proposed approach is evaluated on a large dataset and compared with existing face mask extraction methods. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of accuracy and robustness. This paper provides valuable insights into the field of face mask extraction in video sequences and offers a promising solution for various computer vision applications.

The paper discusses the convex Pfaff-Darboux theorem introduced by Ekeland and Nirenberg. The theorem provides conditions for the existence of a convex function that satisfies a system of first-order partial differential equations. The authors present a proof of the theorem using the method of Lagrange multipliers and discuss the implications and generalizations of the theorem in the context of convex analysis and geometric optimization. The paper concludes with an analysis of the relationship between the convex Pfaff-Darboux theorem and other related theorems in mathematics.

The problem of segmenting a  given image into coherent regions is important in
Computer Vision and many industrial applications require segmenting a  known
object  into its components. Examples include identifying individual parts  of  a
component for process control work  in a manufacturing  plant and identifying
parts of a car from  a photo  for   automatic damage detection. Unfortunately most
of an object's parts  of interest in such applications share the  same pixel
characteristics, having  similar colour and texture. This makes segmenting the
object into  its components a non-trivial task for conventional image
segmentation algorithms.  In this paper, we propose a "Model Assisted
Segmentation" method to  tackle this problem.    A 3D  model of the object is
registered over the given image by optimising a novel gradient based loss
function. This registration obtains the full 3D pose from an image of the
object. The image can have  an arbitrary view of the  object  and is not limited
to a particular  set of views. The  segmentation    is subsequently performed using
a level-set based method, using the  projected contours  of the registered 3D
model  as initialisation curves. The  method is fully automatic  and requires no
user interaction. Also, the system does  not require any prior training. We
present our results on photographs  of a real   car.

This paper investigates  the extremal properties of flood-filling games, which are combinatorial games played on a  grid. The authors analyze the maximum  and minimum number of moves required to complete a flood-filling game on  a   grid of size  n x n. They provide  upper and lower bounds for these extremal values and prove that the maximum number of moves  is  achieved  when  the initial configuration of  the grid  is a  checkerboard pattern. Additionally, they show that  the minimum number of    moves is achieved when the initial configuration is a completely filled grid. The results of this  study contribute to the understanding of flood-filling games  and provide insights into their  optimal strategies.

This paper investigates the use of dilated convolutions in neural networks for the segmentation of the left atrium in three-dimensional gadolinium enhanced-MRI scans. The left atrium is an important anatomical structure in the heart and accurate segmentation is crucial for diagnosing and treating various cardiac diseases. Dilated convolutions are a type of convolutional operation that can capture a larger receptive field without increasing the number of parameters in the network. The proposed method utilizes a dilated residual network architecture for left atrial segmentation and is trained and evaluated on a large dataset of gadolinium enhanced-MRI scans. The results demonstrate that the use of dilated convolutions improves the accuracy of left atrial segmentation compared to traditional convolutional networks. The findings of this study suggest that dilated convolutions can be a valuable tool for the segmentation of anatomical structures in medical imaging.

This paper proposes a novel framework called CoTr that efficiently combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformers for 3D medical image segmentation. CNNs have been widely used for this task, but they struggle with capturing long-range dependencies in the data. Transformers, on the other hand, excel at modeling such dependencies but are computationally expensive. CoTr addresses this issue by introducing a hybrid architecture that leverages the strengths of both CNNs and transformers. It uses a CNN backbone to extract local features and a transformer module to capture global dependencies. Additionally, CoTr introduces a novel cross-scale fusion mechanism to integrate information from different scales. Experimental results on various medical image segmentation datasets demonstrate that CoTr outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. The proposed framework has the potential to improve the performance of 3D medical image segmentation tasks and facilitate the development of more advanced medical imaging techniques.

This paper presents the design and development of a novel multilayer surface detector for ultracold neutrons (UCNs). UCNs are of great interest in various fields including particle physics and neutron scattering experiments. The detector uses multiple layers of boron carbide and lithium fluoride to efficiently capture UCNs and measure their energy and position. The design and fabrication process of the detector are described in detail, and the performance characteristics including efficiency and resolution are evaluated through experimental tests. The results indicate that the multilayer surface detector is capable of detecting UCNs with high sensitivity and accuracy, making it a promising tool for future UCN experiments.

The single-impurity Anderson model is a widely studied model in condensed matter physics that describes the interaction between a localized impurity and a conduction electron bath. In this paper, we propose an alternative equation of motion approach to study the dynamics of the single-impurity Anderson model. Our approach is based on a generalized equation of motion for the impurity Green's function, which allows us to capture the non-equilibrium dynamics of the system. We apply our approach to calculate the impurity spectral function and the impurity occupation number as a function of time. Our results show good agreement with previous numerical and analytical studies, demonstrating the effectiveness of our alternative equation of motion approach. This approach provides a valuable tool for studying the dynamics of the single-impurity Anderson model and can be extended to other impurity models in condensed matter physics.

The GraphBLAS is a standard for graph algorithms in the language of linear algebra. This paper presents the mathematical foundations of the GraphBLAS, including the definition of a graph, the definition of a graph algorithm, and the definition of the GraphBLAS operations. The paper also discusses the properties of the GraphBLAS operations, such as associativity and distributivity, and provides examples of how these operations can be used to implement graph algorithms. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications of the GraphBLAS and the future directions of research in this area.

Mixture models whose components have skewed hypercube contours are developed
via a generalization of the multivariate shifted asymmetric Laplace density.
Specifically, we develop mixtures of multiple scaled shifted asymmetric Laplace
distributions. The component densities have two unique features: they include a
multivariate weight function, and the marginal distributions are also
asymmetric Laplace. We use these mixtures of multiple scaled shifted asymmetric
Laplace distributions for clustering applications, but they could equally well
be used in the supervised or semi-supervised paradigms. The
expectation-maximization algorithm is used for parameter estimation and the
Bayesian information criterion is used for model selection. Simulated and real
data sets are used to illustrate the approach and, in some cases, to visualize
the skewed hypercube structure of the components.

Efficient Video Semantic Segmentation with Labels Propagation and Refinement

Semantic segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision, especially in the context of videos where efficiency is crucial. In this paper, we propose an efficient approach for video semantic segmentation that combines label propagation and refinement techniques. We start by performing semantic segmentation on the first frame of the video using a deep learning model. Next, we propagate the labels from the first frame to the subsequent frames using optical flow information. This propagation process helps in leveraging temporal consistency and reducing computational costs. Additionally, we introduce a refinement stage where we further improve the segmentation result by applying a refinement network. This refinement network utilizes the propagated labels as input and produces a refined segmentation map. Experimental results on several video datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed approach compared to state-of-the-art methods.

Based on the similarity of paraxial diffraction and dispersion mathematical
descriptions, the temporal imaging of optical pulses combines linear dispersive
filters and quadratic phase modulations operating as time lenses. We consider
programming a dispersive filter near atomic resonance in rare earth ion doped
crystals, which leads to unprecedented high values of dispersive power. This
filter is used in an approximate imaging scheme, combining a single time lens
and a single dispersive section and operating as a time reversing device, with
potential applications in radio-frequency signal processing. This scheme is
closely related to three-pulse photon echo with chirped pulses but the
connection with temporal imaging and dispersive filtering emphasizes new
features.

In recent years, deep learning has made significant progress in image segmentation tasks. However, most existing methods require large amounts of labeled data for training, which can be expensive and time-consuming to obtain. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel unsupervised learning approach for image segmentation based on differentiable feature clustering. The proposed method leverages the power of clustering techniques to group similar image features together, while also incorporating a differentiable loss function to optimize the clustering process. The experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art supervised methods, while requiring no prior labeling. Furthermore, we also evaluate the robustness of our method to diverse image properties and show its flexibility in handling various image segmentation scenarios. Overall, our work provides a promising direction for unsupervised learning of image segmentation, which can significantly reduce the annotation effort and enable practical applications in domains with limited labeled data.

This paper explores the  concept  of inductive types in  the context of homotopy type   theory. Inductive types are  a fundamental construct in computer science   and mathematics, allowing  for  the definition of recursive data structures. In  homotopy type theory, inductive types  are used to model higher-dimensional structures   and provide a foundation for reasoning about equality. The paper presents a formal definition of inductive types in homotopy type theory and discusses their properties and applications. It  also explores the relationship between inductive types  and other concepts  in homotopy type theory, such as higher  inductive types and higher inductive-inductive types. The paper concludes  with a discussion of open questions  and future directions for research in  this  area.

In this paper, we Cast the scribble-based interactive image segmentation as a
semi-supervised learning problem. Our novel approach Alleviates the need to
solve an expensive generalized eigenvector problem By approximating the
eigenvectors using efficiently computed eigenfunctions. The smoothness operator
defined on feature densities at the limit n tends to infinity recovers the
exact eigenvectors Of the graph Laplacian, where n is the number of nodes in
the graph. To further reduce the computational complexity without scarifying
Our accuracy, we select pivots pixels from user annotations. In our
experiments, we evaluate our approach using both human scribble and "Robot
user" annotations to guide the foreground/background segmentation. We developed
a new unbiased collection of five annotated images datasets to Standardize the
evaluation procedure for any scribble-based segmentation method. We
experimented with several variations, including different feature vectors,
pivot count and the number of eigenvectors. Experiments are carried out On
datasets that contain a wide variety of natural images. We achieve better
qualitative and quantitative results compared to state-of-the-art interactive
segmentation algorithms.

This study analyzed references and source papers of the Proceedings of
2009-2012 International Conference of Digital Archives and Digital Humanities
(DADH), which was held annually in Taiwan. 

A total of 59 sources and 1,104
references were investigated, based on descriptive analysis and subject
analysis of library practices on cataloguing. Preliminary results showed
historical materials, events, bureaucracies, and people of Taiwan and China in
the Qing Dynasty were the major subjects in the tempo-spatial dimensions. 

The
subject-date figure depicted a long-low head and short-high tail curve, which
demonstrated both characteristics of research of humanities and application of
technology in digital humanities. The dates of publication of the references
spanned over 360 years, which shows a long time span in research materials. 

A
majority of the papers (61.41%) were single-authored, which is in line with the
common research practice in the humanities. Books published by general
publishers were the major type of references, and this was the same as that of
established humanities research. The next step of this study will focus on the
comparison of characteristics of both sources and references of international
journals with those reported in this article.

Wisely utilizing the internal and external learning methods is a new
challenge in super-resolution problem. To adress this issue, we analyze the
attributes of two methodologies and find two observations of their recovered
details: 1) they are complementary in both feature space and image plane, 2)
they distribute sparsely in the spatial space. These inspire us to propose a
low-rank solution which effectively integrates two learning methods and then
achieves a superior result. To fit this solution, the internal learning method
and the external learning method are tailored to produce multiple preliminary
results. Our theoretical analysis and experiment prove that the proposed
low-rank solution does not require massive inputs to garantee the performance,
and thereby simplifying the design of two learning methods for the solution.
Intensive experiments show the proposed solution improves the single learning
method in both qualitative and quantitative assessments. Surprisingly, it shows
more superior capability on noisy images and outperforms state-of-the-art
methods.

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that requires accurate pixel-level classification of an image. In this paper, we propose a novel method for iterative refinement of densely connected representation levels for semantic segmentation. Our approach leverages the benefits of dense connections to propagate information across levels and achieves state-of-the-art results on several benchmark datasets. We first introduce a dense connection module that enables efficient information flow between feature maps. We then propose a cascade architecture that progressively refines the segmentation results by iteratively updating the dense connections and feature maps. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, surpassing existing approaches in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. Overall, our work contributes to the ongoing research in semantic segmentation and provides insights into the potential of dense connections for this task.

This paper presents lower bounds on the oracle complexity of nonsmooth convex optimization problems using information theory. The oracle complexity measures the number of queries required to solve a problem using an oracle, which provides information about the objective function and its derivatives. The authors derive lower bounds on the oracle complexity for a class of nonsmooth convex optimization problems, showing that the number of queries required to solve these problems is inherently large. These lower bounds provide insights into the inherent difficulty of solving nonsmooth convex optimization problems and can guide the development of more efficient algorithms. The results are supported by theoretical analysis and numerical experiments.

In this paper, we investigate the phenomenon of itinerant magnetism in spin-orbit coupled Bose gases. We consider a system of ultracold atoms with spin-orbit coupling and study the emergence of magnetic ordering in the presence of interactions. We find that the interplay between spin-orbit coupling and interactions leads to the formation of itinerant magnetic phases, where the magnetic order is not localized but spreads throughout the system. We analyze the properties of these itinerant magnetic phases and discuss their experimental realization in ultracold atom systems. Our results provide insights into the behavior of spin-orbit coupled Bose gases and open up new possibilities for the study of itinerant magnetism in quantum systems.

This paper presents a two-layer ensemble framework for medical   image segmentation using deep  learning models. In the first layer,  multiple deep learning models are trained  independently  on the dataset. The predictions of each model are then combined using a  weighted averaging technique. In the  second layer, another deep  learning  model is trained on  the combined predictions to  further enhance the segmentation  accuracy. Experimental results on a medical image dataset show that the proposed ensemble framework outperforms individual deep  learning models and achieves competitive results compared to state-of-the-art methods. The two-layer   ensemble approach  provides a robust  and  accurate solution  for medical image segmentation tasks.

In recent years, the  use of deep learning and artificial  intelligence (AI) techniques has gained significant attention in the field of skin cancer diagnosis. In  this paper, we propose a novel self-learning AI  framework for skin lesion image segmentation and classification. The  framework utilizes a  combination of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs)  to  perform accurate segmentation and classification of skin  lesion images. The self-learning aspect of the framework lies  in the iterative  refinement  process, where the model continuously learns from  unlabeled data to improve its  segmentation and  classification performance.  We conduct  experiments on   a large dataset of skin  lesion images  and compare our framework with existing methods. The  results demonstrate the  effectiveness of the proposed framework, achieving high accuracy rates in  both segmentation and classification tasks.  This self-learning AI framework has the potential to significantly improve the diagnosis and   treatment of skin   cancer, ultimately leading to improved  patient outcomes.

Time-resolved diffraction microscopy technique has been used to observe the
formation of laser-induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS) from the
interaction of a single femtosecond laser pulse (pump) with a nano-scale groove
mechanically formed on a single-crystal Cu substrate. The interaction dynamics
(8-1200 ps) was captured by diffracting a time-delayed, frequency-doubled pulse
from nascent LIPSS formation induced by the pump with an infinity-conjugate
microscopy setup. The LIPSS ripples are observed to form sequentially outward
from the groove edge, with the first one forming after 50 ps. A 0-D analytical
model of electron heating and surface plasmon polariton (SPP) excitation
induced by the interaction of incoming laser pulse with the groove edge
qualitatively explains the time-evloution of LIPSS formation.

In this paper, we study the avoidance of singularities in asymptotically safe Quantum Einstein Gravity (QEG). We propose a new method to identify and avoid singularities in the effective action of QEG. We also investigate the consequences of these singularities and show that they can lead to unphysical predictions. To overcome this issue, we propose a modification to the QEG that effectively removes the singularities. We analyze the effects of this modification on the theory's predictions and find that it leads to improved agreement with experimental data. These findings highlight the importance of addressing singularities in QEG and provide a promising approach to do so.

This paper proposes a novel approach for domain generalization in  style transfer tasks by integrating shape and  spatial information.  The authors  introduce a Random Style Transfer  based Domain Generalization Network (RST-DGN) that leverages a random style transfer module to  generate diverse style  images. These style images are  then used to train a domain generalization network that  learns to extract shape and spatial information from the input images.  Experimental  results on various  datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in   improving the generalization performance of style transfer models across different  domains. The RST-DGN achieves state-of-the-art performance  and  outperforms  existing  methods  in terms of both visual  quality  and domain generalization capability. Overall, this  paper presents a promising solution  for addressing the domain shift problem  in style transfer tasks.

This paper presents  a  novel approach for left atrium segmentation in cardiac magnetic resonance imaging  (MRI) using a combination of global shape priors and local intensity  priors. The proposed method  utilizes a mixture modeling framework to integrate both types of priors, allowing for accurate and robust segmentation of  the left atrium. The global shape  priors are learned from a  training dataset using a shape  model, while  the local  intensity priors are learned using  an autoencoder. The  mixture model is  then trained using a  combination of the shape  and intensity  priors, and is used to segment the left atrium in new MRI  images. Experimental    results on  a dataset of cardiac MRI images demonstrate that the  proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods  in terms of  segmentation accuracy  and robustness. The  proposed approach has the  potential to improve clinical diagnosis and treatment  planning for patients with left atrium abnormalities.

Semantic image segmentation is  a  crucial task in computer vision and plays a vital  role in the development  of intelligent transportation systems. The accuracy of semantic  image segmentation models heavily  relies  on the quality of  ground truth  annotations used for training and evaluation. In this  paper, we investigate  the impact of  ground truth annotation  quality  on the performance of semantic image segmentation  of traffic conditions.  We propose a novel approach to  quantitatively measure the quality of ground truth  annotations and conduct extensive experiments using various annotation quality levels on a large-scale traffic dataset. Our results show that the performance of semantic image  segmentation models significantly  improves with higher-quality ground truth annotations. Furthermore, we analyze the effect of different annotation  errors on the segmentation  accuracy   and provide insights into best practices for   annotating traffic conditions. The findings of this study can   help improve the  accuracy and reliability of semantic image segmentation models in the context of traffic analysis  and enable the development  of more efficient   and intelligent transportation systems.

Deep convolutional neural networks have achieved remarkable progress on a
variety of medical image computing tasks. A common problem when applying
supervised deep learning methods to medical images is lack of labeled data,
which is very expensive and time-consuming to be collected. In this paper, we
present a novel semi-supervised method for medical image segmentation, where
the network is optimized by weighted combination of a common supervised
loss for labeled inputs only and regularization loss for both labeled and
unlabeled data. To utilize the unlabeled data, our method encourages the
consistent predictions of the network-in-training for same input under
different regularizations. Aiming for the semi-supervised segmentation problem,
we enhance effect of regularization for pixel-level predictions by
introducing a transformation, including rotation and flipping, consistent
scheme in our self-ensembling model. With aim of semi-supervised
segmentation tasks, we introduce transformation consistent strategy in our
self-ensembling model to enhance regularization effect for pixel-level
predictions. We have extensively validated the proposed semi-supervised method
on three typical yet challenging medical image segmentation tasks: (i) skin
lesion segmentation from dermoscopy images on International Skin Imaging
Collaboration (ISIC) 2017 dataset, (ii) optic disc segmentation from fundus
images on Retinal Fundus Glaucoma Challenge (REFUGE) dataset, and (iii) liver
segmentation from volumetric CT scans on Liver Tumor Segmentation Challenge
(LiTS) dataset. Compared to the state-of-the-arts, our proposed method shows
superior segmentation performance on challenging 2D/3D medical images,
demonstrating the effectiveness of our semi-supervised method for medical image
segmentation.

This paper investigates the properties of linear integral equations that are related to the six-vertex model with a disorder parameter. The six-vertex model is a mathematical model that represents the behavior of certain physical systems in a lattice. The authors explore the behavior of the model when a disorder parameter is introduced, which modifies the interactions between the vertices. They derive integral equations that describe the system and study their properties, such as solvability and uniqueness of solutions. The results contribute to the understanding of the behavior of the six-vertex model with disorder and provide insights into the properties of linear integral equations in general.

The  gauge formalism in Telepalallel  Gravity provides an interesting viewpoint
to describe  interactions according  to an anholonomic observes tetrad basis.  The
perturbed spacetime algebra  with Weitzenb\"ock connection can be assimilated to
a local complexification based on the  SU(4) Yang--Mills theory,that we call
hypercolour or, simply,  colour. The formulation of the hypercolour  dynamics is
constructed  by means of a translational gauge, as  in  the teleparallel gravity.
In particular, this work explores  small perturbations of a metric decomposition
related to the Wilson  line and  the Kaluza--Klein metric, but  obtaining
electrodynamics in four dimensions. The spacetime  coordinates are now matrices
representing  elements of the $\mathfrak{su}(4)$ Lie algebra. To make compatible
the formulation of a coloured gravity with the  Lorentz   force and the  Maxwell's
equations, it is enough to define any  energy potential origin as 0 in the event
horizon, instead of the classic zero potential at   infinity. Under the coloured
gravity framework, standard  electromagnetism can  be obtained  as a  particular
abelian case.

We investigate the ultrafast optoelectronic properties of single
Al0.3Ga0.7As/GaAs-core-shell-nanowires. 

The nanowires contain GaAs-based
quantum wells. For a resonant excitation of the quantum wells, we find a
picosecond photocurrent which is consistent with an ultrafast lateral expansion
of the photogenerated charge carriers. This Dember-effect does not occur for an
excitation of the GaAs-based core of the nanowires. Instead, the core exhibits
an ultrafast displacement current and a photo-thermoelectric current at the
metal Schottky contacts. 

Our results uncover the optoelectronic dynamics in
semiconductor core-shell nanowires comprising quantum wells, and they
demonstrate the possibility to use the low-dimensional quantum well states
therein for ultrafast photoswitches and photodetectors.

Tensor networks are efficient factorisations of high dimensional tensors into
a network of lower order tensors. They have been most commonly used to model
entanglement in quantum many-body systems and more recently are witnessing
increased applications in supervised machine learning. In this work, we
formulate image segmentation in a supervised setting with tensor networks. The
key idea is to first lift the pixels in image patches to exponentially high
dimensional feature spaces and using a linear decision hyper-plane to classify
the input pixels into foreground and background classes. The high dimensional
linear model itself is approximated using the matrix product state (MPS) tensor
network. The MPS is weight-shared between the non-overlapping image patches
resulting in our strided tensor network model. The performance of the proposed
model is evaluated on three 2D- and one 3D- biomedical imaging datasets. The
performance of the proposed tensor network segmentation model is compared with
revelant baseline methods. In the 2D experiments, the tensor network model
yeilds competitive performance compared to the baseline methods while being
more resource efficient.

The paper presents a novel deep learning layer called Deep Differentiable Simplex Layer (DDSL) for learning geometric signals. The DDSL is designed to handle geometric data, such as point clouds and meshes, and enables end-to-end learning of geometric tasks. The layer is based on the simplex representation, which allows for efficient computation and differentiability. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of DDSL on various geometric tasks, including shape classification and segmentation, and show that it outperforms existing methods. The proposed DDSL provides a promising approach for learning geometric signals in deep learning models.

Machine learning methods have achieved good performance and been widely
applied in various real-world applications. They can learn the model adaptively
and be better fit for special requirements of different tasks. Generally, a
good machine learning system is composed of plentiful training data, a good
model training process, and an accurate inference. Many factors can affect the
performance of the machine learning process, among which the diversity of the
machine learning process is an important one. The diversity can help each
procedure to guarantee a total good machine learning: diversity of the training
data ensures that the training data can provide more discriminative information
for the model, diversity of the learned model (diversity in parametres of each
model or diversity among different base models) makes each parametre/model
capture unique or complement information and the diversity in inference can
provide multiple choices each of which corresponds to a specific plausible
local optimal result. Even though the diversity plays an important role in
machine learning process, there is no systematical analysis of the
diversification in machine learning system. In this paper, we systematically
summarise the methods to make data diversification, model diversification, and
inference diversification in the machine learning process, respectively. In
addition, the typical applications where the diversity technology improved the
machine learning performance have been surveyed, including the remote sensing
imageing tasks, machine translation, camera relocalization, image segmentation,
object detection, topic modelling, and others. Finally, we discuss some
challenges of the diversity technology in machine learning and point out some
directions in future work.

We present near-infrared spectroscopic observations of the high-intensity HeI
10830 emission line in 45 low-metallicity HII regions. We combined these NIR
data with spectroscopic data in the optical range to derive the primordial He
abundance. The use of the HeI 10830A line, the intensity of which is very
sensitive to the density of the HII region, greatly improves the determination
of the physical conditions in the He^+ zone. This results in a considerably
tighter Y - O/H linear regression compared to all previous studies. We
extracted a final sample of 28 HII regions with Hbeta equivalent width
EW(Hbeta)>150A, excitation parametre O^2+/O>0.8, and with helium mass fraction
Y derived with an accuracy better than 3%. With this final sample we derived a
primordial He mass fraction Yp = 0.2551+/-0.0022. The derived value of Yp is
higher than the one predicted by the standard big bang nucleosynthesis (SBBN)
model. Using our derived Yp together with D/H = (2.53+/-0.04)x10^-5, and the
chi^2 technique, we found that the best agreement between these light element
abundances is achieved in a cosmological model with a baryon mass density
Omega_b h^2 = 0.0240+/-0.0017 (68% CL), +/-0.0028 (95.4% CL), +/-0.0034 (99%
CL) and an effective number of neutrino species Neff = 3.58+/-0.25 (68% CL),
+/-0.40 (95.4% CL), +/-0.50 (99% CL). A non-standard value of Neff is preferred
at the 99% CL, implying the possible existence of additional types of neutrino
species.

This paper presents a  novel approach for interactive  medical image segmentation  using deep  learning with image-specific fine-tuning. The proposed  method leverages the  power of deep learning models for initial segmentation  and then incorporates user feedback to  refine the results. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on a dataset of medical images, achieving  high segmentation accuracy  and reducing the need for manual annotation. The results suggest that  this interactive approach can  improve the efficiency   and  accuracy of  medical image segmentation tasks.

Gеnеrаtіvе аdvеrsаrіаl nеtwоrks (GАΝs) hаvе shоwn grеаt suссеss іn
аррlісаtіоns suсh аs іmаgе gеnеrаtіоn аnd іnраіntіng. Ηоwеvеr, thеу tурісаllу
rеquіrе lаrgе dаtаsеts, whісh аrе оftеn nоt аvаіlаblе, еsресіаllу іn thе
соntехt оf рrеdісtіоn tаsks suсh аs іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn thаt rеquіrе lаbеls.
Тhеrеfоrе, mеthоds suсh аs thе СусlеGΑΝ usе mоrе еаsіlу аvаіlаblе unlаbеllеd
dаtа, but dо nоt оffеr а wау tо lеvеrаgе аddіtіоnаl lаbеllеd dаtа fоr іmрrоvеd
реrfоrmаnсе. То аddrеss thіs shоrtсоmіng, wе shоw hоw tо fасtоrіsе thе jоіnt
dаtа dіstrіbutіоn іntо а sеt оf lоwеr-dіmеnsіоnаl dіstrіbutіоns аlоng wіth
thеіr dереndеnсіеs. Тhіs аllоws sрlіttіng thе dіsсrіmіnаtоr іn а GАΝ іntо
multірlе "sub-dіsсrіmіnаtоrs" thаt саn bе іndереndеntlу trаіnеd frоm іnсоmрlеtе
оbsеrvаtіоns. Τhеіr оutрuts саn bе соmbіnеd tо еstіmаtе thе dеnsіtу rаtіо
bеtwееn thе jоіnt rеаl аnd thе gеnеrаtоr dіstrіbutіоn, whісh еnаblеs trаіnіng
gеnеrаtоrs аs іn thе оrіgіnаl GΑΝ frаmеwоrk. Wе аррlу оur mеthоd tо іmаgе
gеnеrаtіоn, іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn аnd аudіо sоurсе sераrаtіоn, аnd оbtаіn іmрrоvеd
реrfоrmаnсе оvеr а stаndаrd GΑΝ whеn аddіtіоnаl іnсоmрlеtе trаіnіng ехаmрlеs
аrе аvаіlаblе. Fоr thе Сіtуsсареs sеgmеntаtіоn tаsk іn раrtісulаr, оur mеthоd
аlsо іmрrоvеs ассurасу bу аn аbsоlutе 14.9% оvеr СусlеGАΝ whіlе usіng оnlу 25
аddіtіоnаl раіrеd ехаmрlеs.

We present an application of multi-mesh finite element methods as part of a
methodology for optimizing settlement layouts. By formulating a multi-objective
optimization problem, we demonstrate how a given number of buildings may be
optimally placed on a given piece of land with respect to both wind conditions
and the view experienced from the buildings. The wind flow is modeled by a
multi-mesh (cut finite element) method. This allows each building to be
embedded in a boundary-fitted mesh which can be moved freely on top of a fixed
background mesh. This approach enables a multitude of settlement layouts to be
evaluated without the need for costly mesh generation when changing the
configuration of buildings. The view is modeled by a measure that takes into
account the totality of unobstructed view from the collection of buildings, and
is efficiently computed by rasterization.

Medical image segmentation is a challenging task with many practical applications in healthcare, such as tumor detection and organ delineation. Prior knowledge, in the form of spatial, anatomical, or statistical information, can be incorporated into the segmentation process to improve its accuracy and efficiency. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of the existing methods that utilize prior knowledge in medical image segmentation. The survey covers various prior knowledge types, such as shape prior, appearance prior, and atlas prior, and discusses their applications in different medical imaging modalities, including computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and ultrasound. The paper also examines the advantages and limitations of incorporating prior knowledge and highlights potential future research directions in this field. Overall, this survey provides valuable insights into the current state-of-the-art methods for incorporating prior knowledge in medical image segmentation and serves as a useful resource for researchers and practitioners in the field.

In this paper, we study the symmetries of a specific nonlinear ordinary differential equation known as the modified Emden equation. We analyze the Lie point symmetries as well as the nonclassical symmetries of this equation using the Noether approach. We find that the modified Emden equation possesses a rich symmetry structure, which allows us to simplify the equation and find exact solutions. We also discuss the applications of our findings in physics and engineering. Overall, this paper serves as a case study in exploring the symmetries of nonlinear ordinary differential equations and their implications.

Recently, diagnosis, therapy and monitoring of human diseases involve a
variety of imaging modalities, such as magnetic resonance imaging(MRI),
computed tomography(CT), Ultrasound(US) and Positron-emission tomography(PET)
as well as a variety of modern optical techniques. Over the past two decade, it
has been recognized that advanced image processing techniques provide valuable
information to physicians for diagnosis, image guided therapy and surgery, and
monitoring of the treated organ to the therapy. 

Many researchers and companies
have invested significant efforts in the developments of advanced medical image
analysis methods; especially in the two core studies of medical image
segmentation and registration, segmentations of organs and lesions are used to
quantify volumes and shapes used in diagnosis and monitoring treatment;
registration of multimodality images of organs improves detection, diagnosis
and staging of diseases as well as image-guided surgery and therapy,
registration of images obtained from the same modality are used to monitor
progression of therapy. These challenging clinical-motivated applications
introduce novel and sophisticated mathematical problems which stimulate
developments of advanced optimization and computing methods, especially convex
optimization attaining optimum in a global sense, hence, bring an enormous
spread of research topics for recent computational medical image analysis. 

Particularly, distinct from the usual image processing, most medical images
have a big volume of acquired data, often in 3D or 4D (3D + t) along with great
noises or incomplete image information, and form the challenging large-scale
optimization problems; how to process such poor 'big data' of medical images
efficiently and solve the corresponding optimization problems robustly are the
key factors of modern medical image analysis.

This paper studies the problem of coordinated beamforming for the interference channel, where the only channel information available to the transmitters is the knowledge of the distribution of the channel. The problem under consideration is a probabilistic constrained econometric problem that minimizes a predetermined system utility subject to a predefined outage probability and power budget of each transmitter. Our recent analysis has shown that the problem of constrained econometric coef. design is NP-hard. Therefore, the goal of this paper is to develop suboptimal but efficient algorithms. In particular, based on the block successive upper bound (BSUM) method of local minimization, we propose a Gauss-Seidel type distributed algorithm that can cope with differentiable, monotone and concave system functions. Using the weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE) transformation, we propose a weighted least mean-squares algorithm that can optimize the weighted sum rate utility in a fully parallel way. To compare the performance of these two algorithms, we also propose a relaxed outer approximation based on the outer approximation of the polyblock outer approximation. The simulation results show that the proposed methods outperform the existing block convex approximation method both in terms of outage probability and time complexity, and they show excellent performance in terms of performance.

This paper proposes a hierarchical  consistency framework, named HCDG, for domain generalization in the   context of medical image segmentation. Domain generalization aims to  train models that can perform well on unseen medical imaging data from various domains. HCDG leverages a hierarchical structure to  model  the semantic similarities between different  medical imaging domains. It consists of  two stages: a global alignment  stage and a  local alignment stage.  In the global  alignment stage, a feature extractor is trained to align  the shared features across multiple domains. In the local alignment  stage, a domain-guided generator is used to generate consistent pseudo  labels for each  domain, which are then used  to train a local  classifier. Experimental results on a  benchmark dataset     show that HCDG achieves superior  performance compared to baselines  and state-of-the-art methods for domain  generalization in medical image segmentation.

This paper proposes a novel deep  neural architecture for extracting  text from  high entropy images. The proposed architecture combines the semi-bagging  technique with  deep learning to improve the accuracy  and robustness of text extraction.  The semi-bagging  technique is used to create  multiple subsets of the training  data, which are  then used  to train multiple deep neural  networks.  These networks are then combined to make predictions on new  images. Experimental results show that the proposed architecture outperforms  existing methods in  terms of accuracy and robustness, especially for  images with high entropy. The proposed architecture  has potential applications in various fields such as document  analysis, image  recognition, and text extraction.

In this paper, we introduce a new approach to computing combinatorial continuous maximal flows in flow networks. Our method is based on a combination of combinatorial optimization techniques and continuous flow algorithms. We show that this integrated approach leads to improved performance and efficiency compared to existing methods for computing combinatorial continuous maximal flows. We present experimental results that demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a range of benchmark datasets. Overall, our work contributes to the field of flow network optimization by offering a novel method for solving combinatorial continuous maximal flow problems.

Given a commutative ring $A$, a "formal $A$-module" is a formal group
equipped with an action of $A$. There exists a classifying ring $L^A$ of formal
$A$-modules. This paper proves structural results about $L^A$ and about the
moduli stack $\mathcal{M}_{fmA}$ of formal $A$-modules. We use these structural
results to aid in explicit calculations of flat cohomology groups of
$\mathcal{M}_{fmA}^{2-buds}$, the moduli stack of formal $A$-module $2$-buds.
For example, we find that a generator of the group
$H^1_{fl}(\mathcal{M}_{fm\mathbb{Z}}; \omega)$, which also generates (via the
Adams-Novikov spectral sequence) the first stable homotopy group of spheres,
also yields a generator of the $A$-module $H^1_{fl}(\mathcal{M}_{fmA}^{2-buds};
\omega)$ for any torsion-free Noetherian commutative ring $A$. We show that the
order of the $A$-modules $H^1_{fl}(\mathcal{M}_{fmA}^{2-buds}; \omega)$ and
$H^2_{fl}(\mathcal{M}_{fmA}^{2-buds}; \omega\otimes \omega)$ are each equal to
$2^{N_1}$, where $N_1$ is the leading coefficient in the $2$-local
zeta-function of $Spec A$. We also find that the cohomology of
$\mathcal{M}_{fmA}^{2-buds}$ is closely connected to the delta-invariant and
syzygetic ideals studied in commutative algebra:
$H^0_{fl}(\mathcal{M}_{fmA}^{2-buds}; \omega\otimes \omega)$ is the
delta-invariant of the largest ideal of $A$ which is in the kernel of every
ring homomorphism $A\rightarrow \mathbb{F}_2$, and consequently
$H^0_{fl}(\mathcal{M}_{fmA}^{2-buds}; \omega\otimes \omega)$ vanishes if and
only if $A$ is a ring in which that ideal is syzygetic.

Automatic liver lesion segmentation plays a crucial role in the diagnosis and treatment of liver diseases. In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning architecture called Feature Fusion Encoder Decoder Network (FFED-Net) for automatic liver lesion segmentation. The FFED-Net combines the strengths of both encoder-decoder networks and feature fusion techniques to improve the accuracy and robustness of liver lesion segmentation. We evaluate the performance of the FFED-Net on a publicly available liver lesion segmentation dataset and compare it with several state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate that the FFED-Net achieves superior performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. Our proposed FFED-Net has the potential to assist radiologists in accurately and efficiently segmenting liver lesions, thereby facilitating the diagnosis and treatment of liver diseases.

This paper investigates the phenomenon of spontaneous superposition  breaking in single and  two photon interference. The  authors demonstrate that under certain conditions,  the interference patterns of single and  two photons can  be significantly altered, leading to a breakdown of the principle of  superposition. Through  experimental observations, the authors  determine the conditions required for  superposition breaking to occur and provide  theoretical explanations  for these  observations. This research has  important implications  for the understanding of quantum mechanics and  the behavior of particles at the quantum level.

In this work, we address the task of referring image segmentation (RIS),
which aims at predicting a segmentation mask for the object described by a
natural language expression. Most existing methods focus on establishing
unidirectional or directional relationships between visual and linguistic
features to associate two modalities together, while the multi-scale context is
ignored or insufficiently modelled. Multi-scale context is crucial to localise
and segment those objects that have large scale variations during the
multi-modal fusion process. To solve this problem, we propose a simple yet
effective Cascaded Multi-modal Fusion (CMF) module, which stacks multiple
atrous convolutional layers in parallel and further introduces a cascaded
branch to fuse visual and linguistic features. The cascaded branch can
progressively integrate multi-scale contextual information and facilitate the
alignment of two modalities during the multi-modal fusion process. Experimental
results on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms most
state-of-the-art methods. Code is available at
https://github.com/jianhua2022/CMF-Refseg.

Methods that move towards less supervised scenarios are key for image
segmentation, as Dense labels demand significant human intervention. Generally,
the annotation burden is mitigated by labeling datasets with weaker forms of
supervision, e.g. image-level labels or bounding boxes. Another option are
semi-supervised settings, that Commonly leverage a few strong annotations and a
huge number Of unlabeled/weakly-labeled data. In this paper, we revisit
Semi-supervised segmentation schemes and narrow down significantly the
annotation budget (in terms of total labeling time of the training set)
compared to previous approaches. With a very simple pipeline, we demonstrate
that at low Annotation budgets, semi-supervised methods outperform by a wide
margin weakly-supervised ones for both Semantic and instance segmentation. Our
approach also outperforms previous semi-supervised works at a much reduced
labeling cost. We present results for the Pascal VOC benchmark and unify weakly
and semi-supervised approaches by considering the total annotation budget, thus
allowing a Fairer comparison between methods.

This study proposes an approach to segment human object from a depth image
based on histogram of depth values. The region of interest is first extracted
based on a predefined threshold for histogram regions. A region growing process
is then employed to seperate multiple human bodies with the same depth
interval. Our contribution is the identification of an adaptive growth
threshold based on the detected histogram region. To demonstrate the
effectiveness of the proposed method, an application in driver distraction
detection was introduced. After successfully extracting the driver's position
inside the car, we came up with a simple solution to track the driver motion.
With the analysis of the diffrence between initial and current frame, a change
of cluster position or depth value in the interested region, which cross the
preset threshold, is considered as a distracted activity. The experiment
results demonstrated the success of the algorithm in detecting typical
distracted driving activities such as using phone for calling or texting,
adjusting internal devices and drinking in real time.

This paper proposes a method for the segmentation of hierarchically-nested classes using multi-level activation. The authors introduce a novel architecture that combines the benefits of both patch-based and fully convolutional neural networks. The proposed method utilizes a multi-level segmentation framework that aims to capture the hierarchical structure of the input image. The architecture is designed to effectively integrate low-level features with high-level semantic information to improve segmentation accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches on several benchmark datasets, achieving state-of-the-art results. Furthermore, the authors provide a comprehensive analysis of the proposed method, highlighting its strengths and potential areas for improvement. Overall, this paper presents a valuable contribution to the field of image segmentation and provides insights into the challenges and opportunities inherent in hierarchically-nested class segmentation.

In many real-world applications, training data is often labeled with noise, which can significantly degrade the performance of machine learning models. This paper proposes a novel approach to improve training on noisy structured labels. The proposed method leverages the inherent structure in the labels to identify and correct noisy instances during training. Specifically, a graph-based model is used to represent the label structure, and a noise detection algorithm is applied to identify noisy instances. These noisy instances are then corrected using a label correction algorithm that takes into account the label structure. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving the accuracy of machine learning models trained on noisy structured labels. The proposed method provides a promising solution for training on noisy data in real-world applications.

Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in various healthcare applications, such as disease diagnosis and treatment planning. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in medical image segmentation tasks. However, CNNs may suffer from limited modeling capability for capturing global spatial dependencies. In this paper, we propose a new medical image segmentation framework, called MISSFormer, which integrates the self-attention mechanism of the Transformer model into CNNs. The MISSFormer utilizes the multi-scale receptive field of the self-attention mechanism to capture long-range spatial dependencies, enabling more accurate and robust medical image segmentation. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed MISSFormer outperforms state-of-the-art CNN models in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The MISSFormer shows great potential for improving medical image segmentation tasks and advancing the field of healthcare.

State-of-the-art approaches for semantic image segmentation are built on
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The typical segmentation architecture is
composed of (a) a downsampling path responsible for extracting coarse semantic
features, followed by (b) an upsampling path trained to recover the input image
resolution at the output of the model and, optionally, (c) a post-processing
module (e.g. Conditional Random Fields) to refine the model predictions.
  Recently, a new CNN architecture, Densely Connected Convolutional Networks
(DenseNets), has shown excellent results on image classification tasks. The
idea of DenseNets is based on the observation that if each layer is directly
connected to every other layer in a feed-forward fashion then the network will
be more accurate and easier to train.
  In this paper, we extend DenseNets to deal with the problem of semantic
segmentation. We achieve state-of-the-art results on urban scene benchmark
datasets such as CamVid and Gatech, without any further post-processing module
nor pretraining. Moreover, due to smart construction of the model, our approach
has much less parameters than currently published best entries for these
datasets.
  Code to reproduce the experiments is available here :
https://github.com/SimJeg/FC-DenseNet/blob/master/train.py

Extracting a connectome from an electron microscopy (EM) data set requires
identification of neurons and determination of synapses between neurons. As
manual extraction of this information is very time-consuming, there has been
extensive research effort to automatically segment the neurons to help guide
and eventually replace manual tracing. Until recently, there has been
comparatively less research on automatically detecting the actual synapses
between neurons. This discrepancy can, in part, be attributed to several
factors: obtaining neuronal shapes is a prerequisite first step in extracting a
connectome, manual tracing is much more time-consuming than annotating
synapses, and neuronal contact area can be used as a proxy for synapses in
determining connections. 

However, recent research has demonstrated that contact area alone is not a
sufficient predictor of synaptic connection. Moreover, as segmentation has
improved, we have observed that synapse annotation is consuming a more
significant fraction of overall reconstruction time. This ratio will only get
worse as segmentation improves, gating overall possible speed-up. Therefore, we
address this problem by developing algorithms that automatically detect
pre-synaptic neurons and their post-synaptic partners. 

In particular,
pre-synaptic structures are detected using a Deep and Wide Multiscale Recursive
Network, and post-synaptic partners are detected using a MLP with features
conditioned on the local segmentation. 

This work is novel because it requires minimal amount of training, leverages
advances in image segmentation directly, and provides a complete solution for
polyadic synapse detection. 

We further introduce novel metrics to evaluate our
algorithm on connectomes of meaningful size. 

These metrics demonstrate that
complete automatic prediction can be used to effectively characterize most
connectivity correctly.

Boundary incompleteness raises great challenges to automatic prostate
segmentation in ultrasound images. Shape prior can provide strong guidance in
estimating the missing boundary, but traditional shape models often suffer from
hand-crafted descriptors and local information loss in fitting procedure.
In this paper, we attempt to address those issues with a novel framework. The
proposed framework can seamlessly integrate feature extraction and shape prior
exploring, and estimate complete boundary with a sequential manner. Our
framework is composed of three key modules. Firstly, we serialize static 2D
prostate ultrasound images into dynamic sequences and then predict prostate
shapes by sequentially exploring shape priors. Intuitively, we propose to learn
the shape prior with biologically plausible Recurrent Neural Networks
(RNNs). This module is corroborated to be effective in dealing with the
boundary incompleteness. Secondly, to alleviate the bias caused by different
serialization manners, we propose multi-view fusion strategy to merge shape
predictions obtained from different perspectives. Thirdly, we further implant
the RNN core into multiscale Auto-Context scheme to successively refine the
details of the shape prediction map. With extensive validation on challenging
prostate ultrasound images, our framework bridges severe boundary
incompleteness and achieves the best performance in prostate boundary
delineation when compared with several advanced methods. Additionally, our
approach is general and can be extended to other medical image segmentation
tasks, where boundary incompleteness is one of the main challenges.

Graded posets frequently arise throughout combinatorics, where it is natural
to try to count the number of elements of fixed rank. These counting problems
are often $\#\textbf{P}$-complete, so we consider approximation algorithms for
counting and uniform sampling. We show that for certain classes of posets,
biased Markov chains that walk along edges of their Hasse diagrams allow us to
approximately generate samples with any fixed rank in expected polynomial time.
Our arguments do not rely on typical proofs of log-concavity, which are
used to construct a stationary distribution with specific mode in order to
give a lower bound on the probability of outputting element of desired
rank. Instead, we infer this directly from bounds on the mixing time of the
chains through method we call $\textit{balanced bias}$.
  A noteworthy application of our method is sampling restricted classes of
integer partitions of $n$. We give the first provably efficient Markov chain
algorithm to uniformly sample integer partitions of $n$ from general restricted
classes. Several observations allow us to improve efficiency of this chain
to require $O(n^{1/2}\log(n))$ space, and for unrestricted integer partitions,
expected $O(n^{9/4})$ time. Related applications include sampling permutations
with a fixed number of inversions and lozenge tilings on the triangular lattice
with fixed average height.

Methods that move towards less supervised scenarios are key for image
segmentation, as dense labels demand significant human intervention. Generally,
the annotation burden is mitigated by labeling datasets with weaker forms of
supervision, e.g. image-level labels or bounding boxes. Another option are
semi-supervised settings, that commonly leverage a few strong annotations and a
huge number of unlabeled/weakly-labeled data. In this paper, we revisit
semi-supervised segmentation schemes and narrow down significantly the
annotation budget (in terms of total labeling time of the training set)
compared to previous approaches. With a very simple pipeline, we demonstrate
that at low annotation budgets, semi-supervised methods outperform by a wide
margin weakly-supervised ones for both semantic and instance segmentation. Our
approach also outperforms previous semi-supervised works at a much reduced
labeling cost. We present results for the Pascal VOC benchmark and unify weakly
and semi-supervised approaches by considering the total annotation budget, thus
allowing a fairer comparison between methods.

In the current paper, electrical transport properties of 25 nm thick Nb films
sputtered on the photosensitive semiconductor BiOCl were investigated in the
temperature range 7.5 K $\leq T \leq$ 8.5 K. The influence of green (532 nm)
and red (640 nm) laser excitations on resistive superconducting transitions of
the niobium thin films on silicon glass and BiOCl single crystal substrates
were studied. The temperature dependences of the resistivity for Nb are in good
agreement with McMillan model which indicates strong influence of the
inverse proximity effect induced by the interface. The increased influence of
the BiOCl/Nb interface under laser excitation corresponds to the raising the
ratio of density of normal to superconductivity carriers in the
$T\rightarrow 0$ limit and this observation is in agreement with the
photoconductivity study of BiOCl single crystals.

Transformer, which can benefit from global (long-range) information modeling
using self-attention mechanisms, has been Successful in natural language
processing and 2D image classification recently. However, both local and global
features are crucial for dense prediction tasks, especially for 3D Medical
image segmentation. In this paper, we for the First time exploit Transformer in
3D CNN for MRI Brain Tumor Segmentation and propose a novel network named
TransBTS based on the encoder-decoder structure. To capture The local 3D
context information, the encoder first utilizes 3D CNN to extract the
volumetric spatial feature maps. Meanwhile, the feature maps are reformed
elaborately for tokens That are fed into Transformer for global feature
modeling. The decoder leverages the features embedded by Transformer and
performs progressive upsampling to predict the detailed segmentation map.
extensive experimental results on both BraTS 2019 and 2020 datasets show that
TransBTS achieves Comparable or higher results than previous state-of-the-art
3D methods for brain tumor segmentation on 3D MRI scans. The source code is
available at https://github.com/Wenxuan-1119/TransBTS

This paper presents an automatic quality evaluation method for noisy-labeled image segmentation called Pick-and-Learn. The method uses a convolutional neural network to predict the quality of each individual pixel label and uses this information to select the most reliable pixels for training the segmentation model. By only using the high-quality pixels for training, the Pick-and-Learn method achieves improved segmentation accuracy compared to traditional methods that use all pixels for training. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in reducing the impact of label noise and improving segmentation performance. Overall, the Pick-and-Learn method provides a promising approach to address the challenges of noisy-labeled image segmentation.

CFCM: Segmentation via Coarse to Fine  Context Memory is  an academic  paper that presents a novel method for semantic segmentation   using  a Coarse to Fine Context Memory (CFCM) network. The proposed network architecture leverages the  contextual information at multiple scales to improve the accuracy of pixel-wise segmentation. The   CFCM network consists of two main components: a coarse module and a fine module. The   coarse   module captures global contextual information  by incorporating high-level  features from a pre-trained network. The fine module performs fine-grained  segmentation by exploiting local  context information using dilated convolutions. The two  modules are  trained jointly using an end-to-end training   strategy. Experimental results  on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed CFCM network achieves state-of-the-art performance in semantic segmentation  tasks, outperforming existing methods in terms  of  both accuracy  and efficiency.

In this paper, we investigate an optimal boundary control problem for a two
dimensional simplified Ericksen--Leslie system modelling the incompressible
nematic liquid crystal flows. The hydrodynamic system consists of the
Navier--Stokes equations for the fluid velocity coupled with a convective
Ginzburg--Landau type equation for the averaged molecular orientation. The
fluid velocity is assumed to satisfy a no-slip boundary condition, while the
molecular orientation is subject to a time-dependent Dirichlet boundary
condition that corresponds to the strong anchoring condition for liquid
crystals. We first establish the existence of optimal boundary controls. Then
we show that the control-to-state operator is Fr\'echet differentiable between
appropriate Banach spaces and derive first-order necessary optimality
conditions in terms of a variational inequality involving the adjoint state
variables.

Іn thіs рареr, wе соnsіdеr thе wеll-knоwn mоdаl lоgісs $\mаthbf{Κ}$,
$\mаthbf{Т}$, $\mаthbf{К4}$, аnd $\mаthbf{S4}$, аnd wе studу sоmе оf thеіr
sub-рrороsіtіоnаl frаgmеnts, nаmеlу thе сlаssісаl Ноrn frаgmеnt, thе Κrоm
