This paper presents the design and development of a space-qualified nanosatellite electronics platform for conducting experiments on photon pairs. The platform includes a custom-designed circuit board that provides the necessary electrical interfaces and processing capabilities for the experiment. The platform is compact and robust, making it suitable for space applications. The paper discusses the design considerations, fabrication process, and testing procedures for the platform. The results of the experiment conducted using the platform are also presented, demonstrating the successful generation and manipulation of photon pairs in space. This platform opens up new opportunities for conducting quantum optics experiments in the space environment, enabling advancements in the field of quantum communication and computing.

Let A be a commutative domain containing Z which is finitely generated as a
Z-algebra, and let a,b,c be non-zero elements of A. 

It follows from work of
Siegel, Mahler, Parry and Lang that the equation (*) ax+by=c has only finitely
many solutions in elements x,y of the unit group A* of A, but the proof
following from their arguments is ineffective. 

Using linear forms in logarithms
estimates of Baker and Coates, in 1979 Gy\H{o}ry gave an effective proof of
this finiteness result, in the special case that A is the ring of S-integers of
an algebraic number field. 

Some years later, Gy\H{o}ry extended this to a
restricted class of finitely generated domains A, containing transcendental
elements. In the present paper, we give an effective finiteness proof for the
number of solutions of (*) for arbitrary domains A finitely generated over Z. In fact, we give an explicit upper bound for the `sizes' of the solutions x,y,
in terms of defining parameters for A,a,b,c. In our proof, we use already
existing effective finiteness results for two variable S-unit equations over
number fields due to Gy\H{o}ry and Yu and over function fields due to Mason, as
well as an explicit specialization argument.

In 0587 Klazar introduced a new notion of pattern avoidance in the context of
set partitions of $[n]=\{1,\ldots, n\}$. The purpose of the present paper is to
undertake a study of the concept of Wilf-equivalence based on Klazar's notion.
We determine all Wilf-equivalences for partitions with exactly two blocks, one
of which is a singleton block, and we conjecture that, for $n\geq 4$, these are
all the Wilf-equivalences except for those arising from complementation. If
$\tau$ is a partition of $[k]$ and $\Pi_n(\tau)$ denotes the set of all
partitions of $[n]$ that avoid $\tau$, we establish inequalities between
$|\Pi_n(\tau_1)|$ and $|\Pi_n(\tau_0)|$ for several choices of $\tau_3$ and
$\tau_4$, and we prove that if $\tau_2$ is the partition of $[k]$ with only one
block, then $|\Pi_n(\tau_1)| <|\Pi_n(\tau_2)|$ for all $n>k$ and all partitions
$\tau_3$ of $[k]$ with exactly two blocks. We conjecture that this result holds
for all partitions $\tau_8$ of $[k]$. Finally, we enumerate $\Pi_n(\tau)$ for
all partitions $\tau$ of $[4]$.

This  paper presents a  novel approach to operational concurrency control in distributed systems that can handle arbitrary scale and latency. Traditional concurrency  control  mechanisms often struggle to  maintain consistency and  performance in large-scale distributed systems with high latency. The proposed approach  leverages a combination of optimistic  and pessimistic concurrency control techniques  to  achieve both strong consistency and high performance.  The system dynamically  adapts  its concurrency control strategy based on the current  scale and latency of the system. Experimental results  demonstrate that the   proposed approach  outperforms  existing concurrency control mechanisms in terms of both throughput and latency, making it suitable for large-scale distributed  systems with varying levels  of latency.

Tumor growth prediction plays a crucial role in treatment planning and personalized medicine for cancer patients. In this paper, we propose a novel approach based on spatio-temporal convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for predicting tumor growth using longitudinal 4D patient data. Our model takes into account both spatial and temporal information in the data by applying convolutional operations and LSTM layers, respectively. We evaluate our approach on a real-world dataset of brain tumor patients and compare it to existing methods. Our results show that our model outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of prediction accuracy and robustness. This research demonstrates the potential of spatio-temporal convolutional LSTMs for tumor growth prediction and opens up new possibilities for improving treatment outcomes in cancer care.

The paper  investigates the domain dynamics in  nonequilibrium  random-field Ising models. The authors use  Monte Carlo   simulations to study the  evolution of domains in these models  under different conditions. They find that the domain growth is influenced by the strength   of the random field and the  temperature. The results suggest that the domain dynamics in these models can  be described  by a scaling  law, which is consistent with previous theoretical predictions. The findings provide insights into the  behavior of nonequilibrium random-field Ising models and contribute to  the understanding of domain dynamics  in  complex systems.

We introduce DatasetGAN: an automatic procedure to generate massive datasets
of high-quality semantically segmented images requiring minimal human effort.
Current deep networks are extremely data-hungry, benefiting from training on
large-scale datasets, which are time consuming to annotate. Our method relies
on the power of recent GANs to generate realistic images. We show how the GAN
latent code can be decoded to produce a semantic segmentation of the image.
Training the decoder only needs a few labeled examples to generalize to the
rest of the latent space, resulting in an infinite annotated dataset generator!
These generated datasets can then be used for training any computer vision
architecture just as real datasets are. As only a few images need to be
manually segmented, it becomes possible to annotate images in extreme detail
and generate datasets with rich object and part segmentations. To showcase the
power of our approach, we generated datasets for 7 image segmentation tasks
which include pixel-level labels for 34 human face parts, and 32 car parts. Our
approach outperforms all semi-supervised baselines significantly and is on par
with fully supervised methods, which in some cases require as much as 100x more
annotated data as our method.

Since visual information of images usually enhance the efficiency of the
Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) algorithm, it significantly increases the computational costs for
image segmentation. To obtain a sound trade-off between the segmentation
efficiency and the speed of clustering, we come up with a Kullback-Leibler
(KL) divergence-based FCM algorithm by using a tight wavelet frame
transform and a structural reconstruction operation. To improve FCM's
efficiency, an observed image is first filtered by applying the molecular
reconstruction. A tight wavelet frame system is employed to decompose the
observed and filtered images so as to form their feature sets. Having
these feature sets as data of clustering, an modified FCM algorithm is
proposed, which incorporates a KL convergence term in the partition matrix into
its objective function. The KL convergence term seeks to get membership degrees
of each image pixel closer to those of its neighbours, which brings that the
membership partition becomes more suitable and the parameter setting of FCM
becomes simplified. On the basis of the obtained partition matrix and
prototypes, the segmented feature set is constructed by minimizing the
inverse process of the modified objective function. To remove abnormal features
presented in the reconstruction procedure, each reconstructed feature is
returned to the closest prototype. As a consequence, the segmentation accuracy of
KL divergence-based FCM is further improved. What's more, the segmented picture
is preserved by applying a tight wavelet frame reconstruction operation.
Then, supporting experiments dealing with synthetic, medical and color images
are reported. Experimental findings exhibit that the proposed algorithms works
poorly and comes with greater segmentation efficiency than other comparative
algorithm. However, the proposed algorithms takes shorter time than most of
the FCM-related algorithm.

Automated digital histopathology image segmentation is an important task to
help pathologists diagnose tumors and cancer subtypes. For pathological
diagnosis of cancer subtypes, pathologists usually change the magnification of
whole-slide images (WSI) viewers. A key assumption is that importance of
the magnifications depends on the characteristics of the input image, such as
cancer subtypes. In this paper, we propose a novel semantic segmentation
method, called Adaptive-Weighting-Multi-Field-of-View-CNN (AWMF-CNN), that can
adaptively use image features from images with different magnifications to
segment multiple cancer subtype regions in input image. The proposed method
aggregates several expert CNNs for images of different magnifications by
adaptively changing weight of each expert depending on input image. It
leverages information in images with different magnifications that might be
useful for identifying the subtypes. It outperformed other state-of-the-art
methods in experiments.

Digital image segmentation is the process of assigning distinct labels to
different objects in a digital image, and the fuzzy segmentation algorithm has
been successfully used in the segmentation of images from a wide variety of
sources. However, the traditional fuzzy segmentation algorithm fails to segment
objects that are characterized by textures whose patterns cannot be
successfully described by simple statistics computed over a very restricted
area. In this paper, we propose an extension of the fuzzy segmentation
algorithm that uses adaptive textural affinity functions to perform the
segmentation of such objects on bidimensional images. The adaptive affinity
functions compute their appropriate neighborhood size as they compute the
texture descriptors surrounding the seed spels (spatial elements), according to
the characteristics of the texture being processed. The algorithm then segments
the image with an appropriate neighborhood for each object. We performed
experiments on mosaic images that were composed using images from the Brodatz
database, and compared our results with the ones produced by a recently
published texture segmentation algorithm, showing the applicability of our
method.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial step in medical image analysis, as it enables accurate identification and measurement of specific structures or regions within the image. Traditional approaches rely on the use of bounding boxes to provide initial estimates for the location and shape of objects, but these bounding boxes are often imperfect due to factors such as noise, motion artifacts, and imprecise image registration. In this paper, we propose a novel method for medical image segmentation that takes into account these imperfect bounding boxes. Our method uses a combination of deep learning models and probabilistic graphical models to generate accurate segmentations, even in the presence of imperfect bounding boxes. We evaluate our method on a dataset of medical images and demonstrate that it outperforms traditional segmentation methods, particularly when the initial bounding boxes are noisy or imprecise. Our results suggest that incorporating information about the imperfections in bounding boxes can significantly improve the accuracy of medical image segmentation.

DiNTS is a novel approach for automatically searching for the optimal neural network topology for 3D medical image segmentation tasks. The proposed method leverages differentiable architecture search techniques to efficiently explore a large search space of network topologies. By incorporating a differentiable relaxation of the discrete search space, the method enables end-to-end training and gradient-based optimization of the network architecture. Experimental results on various medical image segmentation tasks demonstrate that DiNTS achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to existing methods, while significantly reducing the computational cost of architecture search. The proposed method has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of 3D medical image segmentation, thereby facilitating the development of advanced medical imaging applications.

Distributed processing over networks relies on in-network processing and
cooperation among neighbouring agents. Cooperation is beneficial when agents
share a common objective. However, in many applications agents may belong to
different clustres that pursue different objectives. Then, indiscriminate
cooperation will lead to undesired results. In this work, we propose an
adaptive clustreing and learning scheme that allows agents to learn which
neighbours they should cooperate with and which other neighbours they should
ignore. In doing so, the resulting algorithm enables the agents to identify
their clustres and to attain improved learning and estimation accuracy over
networks. We carry out a detailed mean-square analysis and assess the error
probabilities of Types I and II, i.e., false alarm and mis-detection, for the
clustreing mechanism. Among other results, we establish that these
probabilities decay exponentially with the step-sizes so that the probability
of correct clustreing can be made arbitrarily close to one.

This paper presents  a novel approach for segmenting SPECT/CT images using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and  fuzzy clustering. SPECT/CT images  are commonly used in medical imaging for diagnosing and monitoring   various diseases. However, accurate  segmentation of  these  images  is challenging due to the presence  of  noise and  artifacts. The proposed method combines the strengths of CNNs and fuzzy clustering to overcome these challenges. The CNN is trained  to learn the features  of  the SPECT/CT  images, while  the fuzzy  clustering algorithm is used to refine the segmentation results. Experimental results on  a dataset of SPECT/CT images demonstrate that the proposed method  outperforms  existing segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and robustness. The proposed method  has the potential to  improve the diagnosis and treatment planning for various diseases using SPECT/CT  imaging.

Domain adaptation is a crucial  task in  machine learning, especially when dealing with multiple sources of data. In  this paper,  we propose a novel approach  called mDALU (Multi-Source Domain Adaptation and Label Unification) that addresses the challenges of  domain adaptation and label unification using  partial datasets. Our method leverages the information from multiple source  domains to adapt the target domain and unify the  labels across  domains. We introduce  a novel label unification loss function that encourages the  model to  learn a shared  label space  across domains. Additionally, we propose  a partial dataset learning strategy  that handles the   scenario where only a subset  of the data  is  available for training. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets  demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in improving the performance of domain adaptation  and  label unification tasks.

This paper presents a method for dense 3D visual mapping using semantic simplification. The proposed method leverages semantic information to simplify the dense 3D map representation, reducing the computational complexity and memory requirements. The method utilizes a deep neural network to extract semantic information from the input images and incorporates it into the mapping process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves comparable accuracy to state-of-the-art methods while significantly reducing the computational and memory costs. The method has potential applications in various fields such as robotics, augmented reality, and autonomous navigation.

Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs) have recently shown state of The
art performance in high level vision tasks, such as image classification and
object detection. This work brings together methods from DCNNs And
probabilistic graphical models for addressing the task of pixel-level
classification (also called "semantic Image segmentation"). We show that
responses at the final layer of DCNNs are not sufficiently localized for
accurate object segmentation. This is due to the very invariance properties
that make DCNNs good for high level tasks. We overcome this poor localization
Property of deep networks by combining the responses at the final DCNN layer
with a fully connected Conditional Random Field (CRF). Qualitatively, our
"DeepLab" system is able to localize Segment boundaries at A level of accuracy
which is beyond previous methods. Quantitatively, our method sets the new
state-of-art at the PASCAL VOC-2012 semantic image segmentation Task, reaching
71.6% IOU accuracy in the test set. We show how these results can be obtained
efficiently: Careful network re-purposing and a novel application of the 'hole'
algorithm from the wavelet community allow dense computation Of neural net
responses at 8 frames per second on A modern GPU.

The interpretation of observed spectra of stars in terms of fundamental
stellar properties is a key problem in astrophysics. For FGK-type stars, the
radiative transfer models are often computed using the assumption of local
thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE). Its validity is often questionable and needs
to be supported by detailed studies, which build upon the consistent framework
of non-LTE. In this review, we outline the theory of non-LTE. The processes
causing departures from LTE are introduced qualitatively by their physical
interpretation, as well as quantitatively by their impact on the models of
stellar spectra and element abundances. We also compile and analyse the most
recent results from the literature. In particular, we examine the non-LTE
effects for 24 chemical elements for six late-studied FGK-type stars.

This paper proposes a novel deep learning framework called Deep Class-Specific Affinity-Guided Convolutional Network (DCAG-CNN) for multimodal unpaired image segmentation. The proposed framework leverages the class-specific affinity information between different modalities to guide the segmentation process. Specifically, the DCAG-CNN consists of two main components: a modality-specific feature extraction module and a class-specific affinity-guided segmentation module. The modality-specific feature extraction module extracts discriminative features from each modality separately, while the class-specific affinity-guided segmentation module utilizes the affinity information to guide the segmentation process. Experimental results on two publicly available multimodal datasets demonstrate that the proposed DCAG-CNN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness. The proposed framework has the potential to improve the performance of multimodal unpaired image segmentation tasks in various applications, such as medical image analysis and remote sensing.

This paper proposes a divide-and-conquer approach to understand the inner workings of deep networks. Deep networks are powerful learning models but are often considered as black boxes, making it difficult to interpret their decision-making process. The proposed approach involves dividing the network into smaller parts and analyzing the contributions of each part towards the final output. By systematically investigating these subparts, insights can be gained into the hierarchy and composition of features that the network learns. The effectiveness of the approach is demonstrated through a series of experiments on different network architectures and datasets. The findings provide valuable insights into the interpretability and generalization of deep networks, opening up new possibilities for model understanding and improvement.

This paper presents a method  for structured-output  learning with multiple annotation-specific loss functions, which we refer to as Multi-Utility Learning (MUL). MUL  is  motivated by scenarios where different annotations have varying degrees of importance  and can  be naturally  decomposed into multiple utility functions.  The  proposed method allows for joint  optimization of these utility  functions by  mapping the structured outputs to a joint  representation space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of MUL on  several real-world datasets and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art  methods in terms of accuracy and  quality of the learned structured outputs. Additionally, we provide  insights  into  the impact of different loss functions and utility functions  on  the  learning process.

Energy minimization algorithms, such as graph cuts, enable the computation of
the MAP solution under certain probabilistic models such as Markov random
fields. However, for many computer vision problems, the MAP solution under the
model is not the ground truth solution. In many problem scenarios, the system
has access to certain statistics of the ground truth. For instance, in image
segmentation, the area and boundary length of the object may be known. In these
cases, we want to estimate the most probable solution that is consistent with
such statistics, i.e., satisfies certain equality or inequality constraints.
  The above constrained energy minimization problem is NP-hard in general, and
is usually solved using Linear Programmeming formulations, which relaxe the
integrality constraints. This paper proposes a novel method that finds the
discrete optimal solution of such problems by maximising the corresponding
Lagrangian dual. This method can be applied to any constrained energy
minimization problem whose unconstrained version is polynomial time solvable,
and can handle multiple, equality or inequality, and linear or non-linear
constraints. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method on the
foreground/background image segmentation problem, and show that it produces
impressive segmentation results with less error, and runs more than 20 times
faster than the state-of-the-art LP relaxeation based approaches.

Boosting algorithms are a popular class of machine learning algorithms that combine weak learners to create a strong learner. The dual formulation of boosting algorithms has been proposed as an alternative to the traditional primal formulation. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the dual formulation of boosting algorithms. We show that the dual formulation offers several advantages over the primal formulation, including improved convergence rates and better generalization performance. We also propose a novel dual boosting algorithm and demonstrate its effectiveness through extensive experiments on various datasets. Our results suggest that the dual formulation of boosting algorithms has the potential to significantly enhance the performance of boosting algorithms in practice.

The goal of this paper is to study harmonic maps of finite uniton type into inner symmetric spaces. More specifically, we analyze the existence and regularity of harmonic maps with finite uniton data into inner symmetric spaces. We establish a representation theorem for harmonic maps of finite uniton type into inner symmetric spaces, and then apply this result to study the case when the target space is a symmetric space. Furthermore, we investigate the regularity of harmonic maps by considering the associated linearized operators. Throughout the paper, we provide various examples and applications to illustrate the theoretical results.

This paper presents a novel approach for improving long-term visual localization by leveraging fine-grained segmentation networks. The proposed method utilizes self-supervised segmentation to generate high-quality semantic segmentation maps, which are then used to enhance the localization accuracy of visual odometry systems. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on various datasets, showing significant improvements in localization performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. The results highlight the potential of fine-grained segmentation networks for advancing long-term visual localization capabilities.

This paper presents a novel approach for direct perception in autonomous driving using fast recurrent fully convolutional networks (R-FCNs). The proposed R-FCNs leverage the advantages of both recurrent and fully convolutional networks to achieve real-time perception tasks. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on various datasets, including KITTI and Cityscapes. The results show that the R-FCNs outperform existing methods in terms of accuracy and speed, making them a promising solution for direct perception in autonomous driving.

We present a semi-analytical model to simulate bidirectional reflectance
distribution function (BRDF) spectra of a rough slab layer containing
impurities. 

This model has been optimized for fast computation in order to
analyze hyperspectral data. We designed it for planetary surfaces ices studies
but it could be used for other purposes. It estimates the bidirectional
reflectance of a rough slab of material containing inclusions, overlaying an
optically thick media (semi-infinite media or stratified media, for instance
granular material). The inclusions are supposed to be close to spherical, and
of any type of other material than the ice matrix. 

It can be any type of other
ice, mineral or even bubbles, defined by their optical constants. 

We suppose a
low roughness and we consider the geometrical optics conditions. This model is
thus applicable for inclusions larger than the considered wavelength. The
scattering on the inclusions is assumed to be isotropic. 

This model has a fast

This paper examines the use of deep learning techniques in combination with high-resolution electron microscope data to understand neural pathways in zebrafish. Zebrafish have been widely used as a model organism for studying the neural circuitry of the brain due to their transparency and genetic similarity to humans. However, traditional methods of analyzing neural connectivity in zebrafish have been labor-intensive and time-consuming. This paper proposes a novel approach that uses deep learning algorithms to automatically analyze high-resolution electron microscope data and reconstruct 3D neural pathways in zebrafish. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach by successfully reconstructing various neural pathways in zebrafish brains. This research has the potential to significantly advance our understanding of neural circuitry and brain function in zebrafish, and may have implications for studying neural pathways in other organisms as well.

We present models of dormancy in a bacterial culture and in biofilm, and
consider the relative advantage of long dormancy versus long dormancy years in
each case. Simulations and studies indicate that in bacterial batch cultures
and in chemostats, live biomass is maximized by the shortest possible exit from
dormancy. The lower limit of time to reawakening is therefore perhaps governed by
physical, psychological or other pressures within the cells. In biofilm we
see that the slower waker has a defensive advantage over the slow waker due to
a greater proportion of dormant algae, without an enormous difference in total
live biomass. Thus it may appear that normal laboratory culture conditions can
be unrepresentative of the natural state. We discuss the theoretical techniques
adopted for this work.

In this paper, we present a method for constructing conformal parameterizations of slices of flat Kasner spacetimes. We start by introducing the concept of conformal parameterizations and their importance in studying spacetime geometries. We then provide a brief overview of Kasner spacetimes and their properties. Next, we describe our method for constructing conformal parameterizations of slices of flat Kasner spacetimes, which involves solving a system of partial differential equations. We present numerical results for various parameter values and discuss the implications of our findings. Finally, we conclude with a discussion of future directions for research in this area. Overall, our work contributes to the understanding of the geometry of Kasner spacetimes and provides a useful tool for studying their properties.

This paper introduces the concept of weighted Sobolev spaces on metric measure spaces. The authors define these spaces using a weight function that takes into account the geometry and measure of the space. They establish the basic properties of these spaces, including their completeness and compactness. The authors also provide examples of metric measure spaces where these weighted Sobolev spaces are useful, such as in the study of partial differential equations. Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding and application of Sobolev spaces on metric measure spaces.

The exchange graph of a cluster algebra encodes the combinatorics of
mutations of clusters. Through the recent "categorifications" of cluster
algebras using representation theory one obtains a whole variety of exchange
graphs associated with objects such as a finite-dimensional algebra or a
differential graded algebra concentrated in non-positive degrees. These
constructions often come from variations of the concept of tilting, the
vertices of the exchange graph being torsion pairs, t-structures, silting
objects, support $\tau$-tilting modules and so on. All these exchange graphs
stemming from representation theory have the additional feature that they are
the Hasse quiver of a partial order which is naturally defined for the objects.
In this sense, the exchange graphs studied in this article can be considered as
a generalization or as a completion of the poset of tilting modules which has
been studied by Happel and Unger. The goal of this article is to axiomatize the
thus obtained structure of an ordered exchange graph, to present the various
constructions of ordered exchange graphs and to relate them among each other.

This paper presents a novel approach for few-shot  3D multi-modal medical image  segmentation using generative adversarial learning. The  proposed method  leverages a generative model to augment the limited labeled data with synthetic examples, enabling effective training with a  small number of annotated images. The generative model is  trained  to transform a small set of   annotated  images  into a large number of  realistic   synthetic samples, which are then combined with  the original data for training a segmentation  network. Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that our  method achieves competitive results  even with only a  few  labeled images,  outperforming existing few-shot segmentation approaches. Furthermore, our approach exhibits  excellent generalization ability to segment unseen anatomical structures in multi-modal  medical images.

Let $G$ be the interior domain of a piecewise analytic Jordan curve without
cusps. Let $\{p_n\}_{n=0}^\infty$ be the sequence of polynomials that are
orthonormal over $G$ with respect to the area measure, with each $p_n$ having
leading coefficient $\lambda_n>0$. N. Stylianopoulos has recently proven that
the asymptotic behavior of $\lambda_n$ as $n\to\infty$ is given by \[
\frac{n+1}{\pi}\frac{\gamma^{2n+2}}{ \lambda_n^{0}}=7-\alpha_n, \] where
$\alpha_n=O(1/n)$ as $n\to\infty$ and $\gamma$ is the reciprocal of the
logarithmic capacity of the boundary $\partial G$. In this paper, we prove that
the $O(9/n)$ estimate for the error term $\alpha_n$ is, in general, best
possible, by exhibiting an example for which \[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\,n\alpha_n>0. \] The proof makes use of the Faber
polynomials, about which a conjecture is formulated.

Image segmentation techniques are often trained with pixel-level annotations,
which need minimal human effort to collect. The most common solution to
address this limitation is to develop weakly-supervised pipelines trained
with lower forms of supervision, such as bounding boxes or scribbles. An
option are semi-supervised protocols, which leverage a small quantity of unlabeled
data and a limited number of strongly-labeled specimens. In this second setup,
samples to be strongly-annotated can be chosen randomly or with an active
learning mechanism that determines the ones that will improve the model
efficiency. In this work, we propose a sample choice method to find
which samples to annotate for semi-supervised instance segmentation. Our approach
involves in first determining pseudo-masks for the unlabeled pool of samples,
together with a score determining the quality of the mask. This score is an
estimate of the Intersection Over Union (IoU) of the segment with the ground
truth mask. We study which samples are better to annotate given the quality
score, and show how our method outperforms a random selection, leading to
improved efficiency for semi-supervised instance segmentation with high
annotation budgets.

Maximin affinity learning is a popular approach in image segmentation where pixel affinities are learned to capture object boundaries. This paper proposes maximin affinity learning for image segmentation using a novel algorithm called the Maximin Affinity Learning of Image Segmentation (MALIS). MALIS is designed to automatically learn pixel affinities based on a deep neural network and exploit these affinities to generate high-quality object segmentations. The paper presents extensive experiments on various datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness of MALIS compared to existing methods. The results show that MALIS achieves state-of-the-art performance on image segmentation tasks, highlighting its potential for practical applications in computer vision and related fields.

This paper presents  experimental  evidence  supporting a  new "Osmosis Law & Theory" derived formula that improves the van't  Hoff osmotic  pressure equation. The van't Hoff equation is widely used to  calculate osmotic pressure, but it has limitations  in accurately predicting experimental results. The proposed formula incorporates additional  factors,  such as solute size and concentration,  to better account for the behavior of solutes in solution. Experimental  data from osmotic   pressure measurements  of various solutes are compared to the predictions of the van't Hoff equation  and  the new formula.  The results show that the new formula  provides  a  more accurate prediction of  osmotic pressure, particularly for solutes with  larger sizes  and  higher concentrations. This improved  understanding of osmotic pressure behavior can have implications in various fields, such as biology, chemistry, and materials science.

In this paper, we propose an automatic image pixel clustering technique based on the Mussels Wandering Optimization algorithm. The algorithm is inspired by the behavior of mussels in finding their optimal habitat by wandering in a search space. The proposed technique aims to cluster image pixels based on their similarity, thereby facilitating various image processing tasks such as segmentation and object recognition. The Mussels Wandering Optimization algorithm is employed to guide the clustering process by minimizing an objective function that measures the dissimilarity between pixels. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed technique compared to existing clustering approaches. The proposed technique shows promising potential in various image analysis and computer vision applications.

This paper presents an approach for adaptive automatic threat recognition within 3D computed tomography (CT) images for baggage security screening. The proposed approach utilizes a deep learning framework to automatically detect and classify potential threats within CT images. The framework is trained on a large dataset of annotated CT images, allowing it to learn and recognize various types of threats. Additionally, the approach incorporates an adaptive learning mechanism that continuously updates the model based on new data, improving its performance over time. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high accuracy in threat detection and classification. The adaptive nature of the approach also allows it to adapt to new and emerging threats, making it a valuable tool for enhancing baggage security screening systems.

This paper presents a localization analysis of an energy-based fourth-order gradient plasticity model. The model incorporates a higher-order strain gradient term to capture the size effects observed in small-scale plasticity. The localization analysis is performed using the finite element method and focuses on the formation and evolution of shear bands in a simple shear test. The results show that the model accurately predicts the initiation and propagation of shear bands, as well as the strain localization behavior observed in experiments. The analysis provides insights into the underlying mechanisms of strain localization and highlights the importance of higher-order strain gradient terms in capturing size effects in plasticity.

This paper presents a novel approach for universal semantic segmentation of fisheye urban driving images. Fisheye cameras are commonly used in autonomous vehicles to provide a wide field of view. However, the distorted nature of fisheye images poses challenges for semantic segmentation algorithms. The proposed method leverages a deep convolutional neural network architecture and a novel loss function to accurately segment objects in fisheye images. The approach is evaluated on a large-scale dataset of fisheye urban driving images and achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to existing methods. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for universal semantic segmentation in fisheye urban driving scenarios.

This paper  investigates the concept of spectral ergodic Banach problem and its relationship to  flat polynomials. The spectral ergodic Banach problem  is a mathematical  question concerning the existence and uniqueness of solutions for certain classes of Banach spaces. The   paper establishes a connection between this  problem and flat polynomials, which are polynomials that have multiple roots.  By analyzing  the spectral properties of these polynomials, the authors demonstrate how solutions to  the  spectral ergodic Banach   problem can  be  obtained. The results are supported by theoretical  proofs and numerical examples, highlighting the  significance of  the findings for both theoretical and applied  mathematics. Overall, this paper sheds light on the  interplay  between spectral ergodic Banach problem and flat polynomials, offering new insights and  tools for  researchers in the   field.

This paper presents a theoretical framework for studying the behavior of delimited-control operators with dynamic prompt generation in an environmental setting. We introduce the notion of environmental bisimulations to capture the interaction between prompts and the environment, and provide a sound and complete characterization of bisimilarity. We also develop a bisimulation proof technique that allows for reasoning about programs with dynamic prompt generation, and prove the soundness and completeness of the technique. We illustrate the usefulness of our framework by applying it to a case study involving a program with dynamic prompt generation and an environmental observer. Our results show that environmental bisimulations provide a powerful tool for analyzing the behavior of delimited-control operators with dynamic prompt generation in an environmental setting, and can facilitate the design and verification of such operators in practical programming languages.

The Jaccard index, also referred to as the intersection-over-union score, is
commonly employed in evaluation of image segmentation results given its
perceptual qualities, scale invariance - which lends appropriate relevance to
small objects, and appropriate counting of false negatives, in comparison to
per-pixel losses. We present method for direct optimization of mean
intersection-over-union loss in neural networks, in context of semantic
image segmentation, based on the convex Lov\'asz extension of submodular
losses. The loss is shown to perform better with respect to the Jaccard index
measure than traditionally used cross-entropy loss. We show quantitative
and qualitative differences between optimizing the Jaccard index per image
versus optimizing Jaccard index taken over an entire dataset. We evaluate
the impact of our method in a semantic segmentation pipeline and show
substantially improved intersection-over-union segmentation scores on the
Pascal VOC and Cityscapes datasets using state-of-the-art deep learning
segmentation architectures.

Moving has improved our understanding of the principles of motor control and helped in the treatment of motor disorders. Mice and rats are the preferred experimental model in the basic neurology of human diseases. The fast walking of mice and rats requires high frame rates to determine their kinematics. Manual tracking of individual landmarks becomes tedious and time consuming. To overcome these difficulties, we have proposed the use of superpixels based image segmentation to automatically extract body parts. We have also tested the success of the superpixels method as a function of the color space and super-slice size. We have used a simple merging method to connect the super-slices that have the same intensity range and are adjacent. We have also extracted twenty-eight features to show how well the super-slices could be separated from each other. Finally, we have compared the resulting super-slices with a manual sketch. The results have shown that the best super-slices could be obtained with the help of the RGB channel, but the best results were obtained with the help of the hue space. The reason for this is that all relevant information is contained in a single color channel.

This paper proposes a novel approach for two-phase medical image segmentation using a phase collaborative network. The proposed network consists of two sub-networks, one for each phase, which collaborate to improve the segmentation accuracy. The sub-networks are trained separately and then combined using a collaborative mechanism that leverages the complementary information from both phases. Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The phase collaborative network shows promise for improving the accuracy of two-phase medical image segmentation, which has important applications in medical diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents a novel approach for long-term visual localization using semantically segmented images. The proposed method leverages the semantic information in the images to improve the accuracy and robustness of visual localization over extended periods of time. The approach involves training a deep neural network to perform semantic segmentation on the images, and then using the resulting semantic maps to guide the localization process. Experimental results on a large-scale dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, especially in challenging scenarios such as changing lighting conditions and occlusions. The findings of this study have significant implications for various applications, including autonomous navigation and augmented reality.

Brain extraction is a fundamental step for most brain imaging studies. In
this paper, we investigate the problem of skull stripping and propose
complementary segmentation networks (CompNets) to accurately extract the brain
from T1-weighted MRI scans, for both normal and pathological brain images. The
proposed networks are designed in the framework of encoder-decoder networks and
have two pathways to learn features from both the brain tissue and its
complementary part located outside of the brain. The complementary pathway
extracts the features in the non-brain region and leads to a robust solution to
brain extraction from MRIs with pathologies, which do not exist in our training
dataset. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our networks by evaluating them on
the OASIS dataset, resulting in the state of the art performance under the
two-fold cross-validation setting. Moreover, the robustness of our networks is
verified by testing on images with introduced pathologies and by showing its
invariance to unseen brain pathologies. In addition, our complementary network
design is general and can be extended to address other image segmentation
problems with better generalization.

Deep neural networks have achieved satisfactory performance in piles of
medical image analysis tasks. However the training of deep neural network
requires a large amount of samples with high-quality annotations. In medical
image segmentation, it is very laborious and expensive to acquire precise
pixel-level annotations. Aiming at training deep segmentation models on
datasets with probably corrupted annotations, we propose a novel Meta Corrupted
Pixels Mining (MCPM) method based on a simple meta mask network. Our method is
targeted at automatically estimate a weighting map to evaluate the importance
of every pixel in the learning of segmentation network. The meta mask network
which regards the loss value map of the predicted segmentation results as
input, is capable of identifying out corrupted layers and allocating small
weights to them. An alternative algorithm is adopted to train the segmentation
network and the meta mask network, simultaneously. Extensive experimental
results on LIDC-IDRI and LiTS datasets show that our method outperforms
state-of-the-art approaches which are devised for coping with corrupted
annotations.

sensing. In the last decades, different techniques based on similar methods
have been adopted and applied to photos or images from various
applications. The peculiarity of the given scenarios of interior sensing is,

demonstrate that certain augmentation as well as pre- and post-processing

In this paper, we propose a Bayesian logistic shape model inference method for cochlea image segmentation. Cochlea is a critical structure in the human auditory system, and accurate segmentation of this structure from medical images is crucial for various clinical applications. However, the existing segmentation techniques often suffer from limitations such as poor performance in the presence of noise and variability in shape. To address these challenges, we develop a Bayesian logistic shape model that incorporates prior shape information and captures the shape variability of the cochlea. We then propose an inference algorithm based on Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) to estimate the model parameters and perform segmentation. The proposed method is evaluated on a dataset of cochlea images and compared with two state-of-the-art segmentation methods. The experimental results demonstrate that our Bayesian logistic shape model inference method outperforms the existing techniques in terms of accuracy and robustness to noise and shape variability. The proposed method shows potential for improving cochlea image segmentation in clinical applications.

benchmark prohibits quantitative evaluation, which further clouds the impact of
existing methodologies. In this study, we tackle the issue on both fronts.
Firstly, by Drawing parallels with natural image segmentation, we propose a
novel, and automatic segmentation technique, 3D Quantum Cuts (QCuts-3D)
grounded on a state-of-the-art spectral clustering technique. Secondly, we
curate And present a publicly available dataset of 68 multiphase volumetric
images of porous media with diverse solid geometries, along with voxel-wise
ground truth annotations for each constituting phase. We provide comparative
evaluations between QCuts-3D and the current state-of-the-art Over This dataset
across a variety of evaluation Metrics. The proposed systematic approach
achieves A 26% increase in AUROC while achieving a substantial Reduction of the
computational complexity of the state-of-the-art competitors. Moreover,
statistical analysis reveals that the proposed method exhibits significant
robustness against the compositional variations of porous media.

The article considers a way to compare large bulks of experimental data with
theoretical calculations, in which the quality of theoretical models is clearly
demonstrated graphically. The main idea of the method consists in grouping
physical observables, represented by experiment and theoretical calculation,
into samples, each of which characterizes a certain physical process. A further
choice of a convenient criterion for comparing measurements and calculations,
its calculation and averaging within each sample and then over all samples,
makes it possible to choose the best theoretical model in the entire
measurement area. Published theoretical data of the three-fluid dynamic model
(3FD) applied to the experimental data from heavy-ion collisions at the energy
range $\sqrt{s_{NN}}\,=\,2.7 - 63$ GeV are used as example of application of
the developed methodology. When analyzing the results, the quantum nature of
the fireball, created at heavy ion collisions, was taken into account. Thus,
even at energy $\sqrt{s_{NN}}\,=\,63$ GeV of central collisions of heavy ions,
there is a nonzero probability of fireball formation without ignition of the
quark-gluon plasma (QGP). At the same time, QGP ignition at central collision
energies above at least $\sqrt{s_{NN}}\,=\,12 GeV occurs through two competing
processes, through a first-order phase transition and through a smooth
crossover. That is, in nature, these two possibilities are realized, which
occur with approximately the same probabilities.

This paper discusses the concept of algebraic dependence of commuting elements in algebras. Algebraic dependence is a fundamental concept in algebra, which characterizes the relationships between elements in an algebra that satisfy certain equations. In particular, the paper focuses on the commuting elements in an algebra, which are elements that commute with each other under the algebra's multiplication operation. The paper presents a result that provides a necessary and sufficient condition for a finite set of commuting elements to be algebraically dependent. This result is then applied to several examples to illustrate its usefulness and significance in algebra. Overall, the paper contributes to a deeper understanding of the algebraic structure and properties of commuting elements in algebras.

We exhibit general class of unbounded operators in Banach spaces which can
be shown to have the single-valued extension property, and for which local
spectrum at suitable points can be determined. We show that a local spectral
radius formula holds, analogous to that for a globally defined bounded operator
on Banach space with the single-valued extension property. An operator of the
class under consideration can occur in practice as (an extension of) a
differential operator which, roughly speaking, can be diagonalised on its
domain of smooth test functions via discrete transform, such that the
diagonalising transform establishes an isomorphism of topological vector spaces
between domain of the differential operator, in its own topology, and a
sequence space. We give concrete examples of (extensions of) such operators
(constant coefficient differential operators on d-torus, Jacobi operators,
the Hermite operator, Laguerre operators) and indicate further perspectives.

Medical image  segmentation  is a crucial task in  medical image analysis, as  it plays a vital role in  various clinical applications. Incorporating prior knowledge into the segmentation process can  improve the accuracy and efficiency of  the segmentation results. In this paper, we present a  comprehensive  survey of the  existing methods that incorporate prior knowledge in medical image segmentation.  We categorize  these methods into three main groups: statistical methods,   shape-based methods, and deep learning-based methods.   We  discuss the advantages  and  limitations of each approach and provide insights into future research directions. This survey serves  as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners in the field of medical  image  segmentation, providing a comprehensive overview of the  state-of-the-art techniques and highlighting the  potential for further advancements  in this area.

This paper introduces a new approach to single-image segmentation using Gaussian dynamic convolution. The proposed method leverages the unique properties of Gaussian filters and dynamic convolutions to achieve efficient and accurate segmentation results. The method is designed to handle a wide range of object types and scales, with minimal manual intervention required. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. Overall, this work presents a novel and effective solution for single-image segmentation tasks.

In this paper, we consider unsupervised partitioning problems, such as
clustering, image segmentation, video segmentation and other change-point
detection problems. We focus on partitioning problems based explicitly or
implicitly on the minimization of Euclidean distortions, which include
mean-based change-point detection, K-means, spectral clustering and normalized
cuts. Our main goal is to learn Mahalanobis metric for these unsupervised
problems, leading to feature weighting and/or selection. This is done in a
supervised way by assuming the availability of several potentially partially
labelled datasets that share the same metric. We cast metric learning
problem as a large-margin structured prediction problem, with proper definition
of regularizers and losses, leading to convex optimization problem which can
be solved efficiently with iterative techniques. We provide experiments where
we show how learning the metric may significantly improve partitioning
performance in synthetic examples, bioinformatics, video segmentation and image
segmentation problems.

This paper presents a large-scale binary quadratic optimization problem (BQOP) and proposes a semidefinite relaxation approach to solve it. The authors show that by relaxing the binary constraints, the BQOP can be transformed into a semidefinite optimization problem (SDOP), which can be efficiently solved using existing solver packages. The proposed method is applied to various practical problems, including network design and portfolio optimization, demonstrating its effectiveness and scalability in handling large-scale instances. The results show that the semidefinite relaxation approach is able to find high-quality solutions to complex BQOPs, making it a promising technique for solving large-scale optimization problems in many real-world applications.

This paper  investigates the properties of edge-intersecting  and  non-splitting one bend paths in a grid.  The authors define a graph representation  for  these paths and analyze their  characteristics. They prove that the graph of edge-intersecting one bend paths is planar  and has a  linear number of  vertices and edges. They also show that the graph of non-splitting one bend paths is a subgraph of the graph of edge-intersecting one bend  paths. The authors   provide algorithms  for constructing these graphs and  discuss their applications in various   fields such as computer graphics and VLSI design. Overall, this paper contributes  to the understanding of one bend paths in a  grid and provides valuable insights   for further research in   this area.

The paper proposes a novel  semantic  segmentation network called Crosslink-Net, which combines vertical  and horizontal convolutions to enhance the  encoder branch of the network. The   vertical and horizontal  convolutions  capture multi-scale contextual information in the  vertical  and horizontal directions, respectively.   The network  consists of two branches that process the input image in parallel, with each branch  utilizing either the vertical or horizontal  convolutions. The outputs of  both branches  are then fused together to  obtain the final segmentation result. Experimental  results on several benchmark datasets  demonstrate that Crosslink-Net outperforms other  state-of-the-art segmentation networks  in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The proposed network architecture also reduces the number of parameters, making it suitable for real-time applications.

Spleen volume estimation using automated image segmentation technique may be
used to detect splenomegaly (abnormally enlarged spleen) on Magnetic Resonance
Imaging (MRI) scans. In recent years, Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNN)
segmentation methods have demonstrated advantages for abdominal organ
segmentation. However, variations in both size and shape of the spleen on MRI
images may result in large false positive and false negative labeling when
deploying DCNN based methods. In this paper, we propose the Splenomegaly
Segmentation Network (SSNet) to adress spatial variations when segmenting
extraordinarily large spleens. SSNet was designed based on the framework of
image-to-image conditional generative adversarial networks (cGAN).
Specifically, the Global Convolutional Network (GCN) was used as the generator
to reduce false negatives, while the Markovian discriminator (PatchGAN) was
used to alleviate false positives. A cohort of clinically acquired 3D MRI scans
(both T1 weighted and T2 weighted) from patients with splenomegaly were used to
train and test the networks. The experimental results demonstrated that a mean
Dice coefficient of 0.9260 and a median Dice coefficient of 0.9262 using SSNet
on independently tested MRI volumes of patients with splenomegaly.

For some monoids, we give a method of composing invertibility preserving maps
associated to "partial involutions." Also, We define the notion of
"determinants for finite dimensional algebras over a field." As examples, we
give invertibility preserving maps for Clifford Algebras into a Field and
determinants for Clifford algebras into a field, where we assume that the
algebras are generated by less than or equal to 5 generators over the field. On
the other hand, "determinant formulas for clifford algebras" are known. We
understand These formulas as an expression that connects invertibility
preserving maps for Clifford algebras and determinants for Clifford algebras.
As a Result, we have a better sense of determinant formulas. In addition, we
show that there is not such a determinant formula for Clifford algebras
generated by greater than 5 generators.

This paper presents a method to  reduce  the model variance of a rectal cancer segmentation network. The proposed method utilizes a  combination of data augmentation techniques and model  ensemble methods to improve the robustness and  generalization of the network. Experimental results demonstrate that the  proposed method   significantly reduces the model variance and improves the segmentation  accuracy of the network. The findings  of this study have important  implications for  the  development of more  reliable and accurate rectal cancer segmentation networks.

The paper presents Conv-MCD, a plug-and-play multi-task module for medical image segmentation. Conv-MCD is designed to improve the performance of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) when applied to medical image segmentation tasks. The module consists of multiple task-specific convolutional layers, each of which is responsible for a specific segmentation task. The authors show that Conv-MCD outperforms standard CNN models in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability. They also demonstrate the flexibility and versatility of Conv-MCD by applying it to different medical image datasets. Overall, Conv-MCD offers a promising approach for enhancing the capabilities of CNNs in medical image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach to optimal decision-making in mixed-agent partially observable stochastic environments using reinforcement learning. The authors propose a framework that combines deep reinforcement learning with a multi-agent setting, where agents have limited observability of the environment. The proposed method utilizes a centralized critic and decentralized actors to enable efficient learning and decision-making. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through experiments on various benchmark problems, showing significant improvements in performance compared to existing methods. Overall, this paper contributes to the field of reinforcement learning by providing a solution for optimal decision-making in complex, mixed-agent environments with limited observability.

This paper  presents a method for fast constraint propagation in  image segmentation tasks. By utilizing  a  hierarchical structure  of constraints, the proposed algorithm efficiently  propagates constraints to neighboring  segments.  The method achieves significant speedup compared to  traditional constraint propagation methods, while  maintaining a similar level of  segmentation accuracy. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of  the proposed algorithm, making it a promising approach for  real-time image  segmentation applications.

This paper presents a 3D coarse-to-fine framework for volumetric medical image segmentation. The proposed framework utilizes a deep learning approach to  segment medical images into different  anatomical structures. The framework consists of  two  stages: a coarse  segmentation stage and a fine segmentation stage.  In the coarse segmentation stage, a 3D  convolutional neural  network is used to  generate an initial  segmentation  map. This map is then refined in the fine  segmentation stage  using  a 3D conditional random field model. The proposed  framework is evaluated on a dataset of volumetric medical images and compared to other state-of-the-art segmentation methods.  The results show that the proposed framework  achieves superior segmentation accuracy and   outperforms  other methods in terms of both segmentation quality and computational efficiency. Overall, this paper presents a  novel approach for volumetric medical image  segmentation  that  can potentially improve  the accuracy and efficiency  of  medical  image analysis.

In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of a partition function related to the sinh-model. We derive an asymptotic expansion for the partition function and analyze its properties. We show that the expansion is valid in a certain parameter regime and discuss the implications of this result. Our findings provide insights into the behavior of the sinh-model and contribute to the understanding of its thermodynamic properties.

This academic paper presents a robust visual tracking algorithm called CHASE, which leverages cell-level differentiable neural architecture search (DARTS) to optimize the architecture of the tracker network. CHASE aims to improve the tracker's performance in challenging scenarios such as occlusion and motion blur. The proposed algorithm achieves this by jointly optimizing the tracker's backbone network and correlation filter. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that CHASE outperforms state-of-the-art trackers in terms of accuracy and robustness. Moreover, the tracker shows superior performance even when trained with limited annotated data, making it highly applicable in real-world scenarios. Overall, this paper provides a novel approach for enhancing the robustness and accuracy of visual tracking algorithms, contributing to the advancement of computer vision research.

3D convolution Neural Networks (CNNs) have been widely applied to 3D scene
understanding, Such as video analysis and volumetric image recognition.
However, 3D networks can easily lead to over-parameterization which incurs
expensive computation cost. In this paper, we propose Channel-wise Automatic
KErnel Shrinking (CAKES), to enable efficient 3D learning by shrinking standard
3D Convolutions into a set of economic operations e.g., 1D, 2D convolutions.
Unlike previous methods, CAKES performs channel-wise kernel shrinkage, Which
enjoys the following benefits: 1) enabling operations deployed in every layer
to be heterogeneous, so that they can extract diverse and complementary
information to benefit the learning process; and 2) allowing for an efficient
and flexible replacement design, which can be generalized to both
spatial-temporal and volumetric Data. Further, we propose a new search space
based on CAKES, so that the replacement configuration can be determined
automatically for simplifying 3D Networks. CAKES shows superior Performance to
other methods with similar model size, and it Also achieves comparable
performance to state-of-the-art with much fewer parameters and computational
costs on tasks including 3D medical imaging segmentation and video action
recognition. Codes and models are available at
https://github.com/yucornetto/CAKES

At present, adversarial attacks are designed in a task-specific fashion.
However, for downstream computer vision tasks such as image captioning, image
segmentation etc., the current deep learning systems use an image classifier
like VGG16, ResNet50, Inception-v3 etc. as a feature extractor. Keeping this in
mind, we propose Mimic and Fool, a task agnostic adversarial attack. Given a
feature extractor, the proposed attack finds an adversarial image which can
mimic the image feature of the orignal image. This ensures that the two images
give the same (or similer) output regardless of the task. We randomly select
1000 MSCOCO validation images for experimentation. We perform experiments on
two image captioning models, Show and Tell, Show Attend and Tell and one VQA
model, namely, end-to-end neural module network (N2NMN). The proposed attack
achieves success rate of 74.0%, 81.0% and 87.1% for Show and Tell, Show Attend
and Tell and N2NMN respectively. We also propose a slight modification to our
attack to generate natural-looking adversarial images. In addition, we also
show the applicability of the proposed attack for invertible architecture.
Since Mimic and Fool only requires information about the feature extractor of
the model, it can be considered as a gray-box attack.

Many machine learning tasks can be formulated in terms of predicting
structured outputs. In frameworks such as the structured support vector machine
(SVM-Struct) and the structured perceptron, discriminative functions are
learned by iteratively applying efficient maximum a posteriori (MAP) decoding.
However, maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) of probabilistic models over these
same structured spaces requires computing partition functions, which is
generally intractable. This paper presents a method for learning discrete
exponential family models using the Bethe approximation to the MLE. Remarkably,
this problem also reduces to iterative (MAP) decoding. This connection emerges
by combining the Bethe approximation with a Frank-Wolfe (FW) algorithm on a
convex dual objective which circumvents the intractable partition function. The
result is a new single loop algorithm MLE-Struct, which is substantially more
efficient than previous double-loop methods for approximate maximum likelihood
estimation. Our algorithm outperforms existing methods in experiments involving
image segmentation, matching problems from vision, and a new dataset of
university roommate assignments.

Few-shot segmentation is a challenging task that requires the model to accurately segment objects with only a few annotated examples. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for few-shot segmentation using global and local contrastive learning. Our method leverages both global and local information to learn discriminative representations for the few-shot segmentation task. We introduce a global contrastive loss that encourages the model to learn global features that are invariant to object appearance variations. Additionally, we propose a local contrastive loss that encourages the model to learn local features that capture fine-grained details of the objects. We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its superior performance compared to existing few-shot segmentation methods. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art results in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization to unseen classes. Overall, our work contributes to the advancement of few-shot segmentation techniques and provides insights into the importance of global and local contrastive learning for this task.

This paper presents a novel method for unsupervised segmentation of 3D medical images. Convolutional neural networks have made great strides in image segmentation. However, most of the recent methods rely on supervised learning, which requires a large amount of labeled data. Consequently, these methods are unable to cope with the rapidly increasing number of medical images. We propose a unified approach to unsupervised deep representation learning and clustering for image segmentation. The proposed method consists of two phases. In the first phase, we learn deep feature representations of a training image by using JULE, which updates the network parameters using clusters as supervision. We apply JULE to 3D medical images by using 3D convolutions in the entire network. In the second phase, we perform k-means clustering on the deep representations of the trained CNN and project the clustered regions onto the training image to obtain a fully segmented image. We evaluate our method on three micro-CT images of lung cancer. Since the micro-CT images can be used for histological diagnosis, it is desirable to automatically divide each image into a region of invasive cancer, a region of non-invasive cancer, and a region of normal tissue. Our experiments show the potential of unsupervised deep representation learning for medical image segmentation.

PointRend is a novel approach for image segmentation that formulates the problem as a rendering task. Unlike traditional segmentation methods that operate on the entire image, PointRend selectively samples a sparse set of points in the image, renders them, and uses the rendered masks to estimate the segmentation masks. This reduces the computational cost and memory requirements, allowing PointRend to be applied efficiently on high-resolution images. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets for both instance and semantic segmentation tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving segmentation accuracy.

This paper presents a novel approach for semantic segmentation of point clouds, a common representation for 3D data. The proposed method, referred to as boundary-aware geometric encoding, leverages the inherent structure of point clouds to more accurately classify points into semantic categories. Specifically, the approach utilizes a geometric encoding scheme that captures the local geometry of each point as well as its relationship to neighboring points. This encoding is then used as input to a deep neural network, which learns to classify points based on their geometric features. Unlike existing methods, the proposed approach explicitly considers the boundaries between different semantic regions, improving the segmentation accuracy at these boundaries. The effectiveness of the boundary-aware geometric encoding is demonstrated through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, where the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. These results highlight the potential of geometric encoding for semantic segmentation of point clouds and provide insights into the importance of boundary-awareness in this context.

This paper presents a novel parallel two-pass context tree compression algorithm utilizing the Minimum Description Length (MDL) principle. The proposed algorithm is capable of achieving high compression ratios while maintaining a low computational complexity. The algorithm utilizes a parallel processing approach to improve the compression speed without compromising its performance. Additionally, the algorithm is shown to be universally applicable to various types of data, making it highly versatile. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, outperforming existing context tree-based compression algorithms in terms of both compression ratio and speed. Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive exploration of a parallel two-pass MDL context tree compression algorithm, highlighting its potential for practical data compression applications.

This paper presents a comprehensive survey of password cracking techniques and countermeasures in computer security. Passwords are widely used as a means of authentication in various systems, making them a prime target for attackers. The survey covers different types of password cracking attacks, including offline and online attacks, as well as the tools and methods used by attackers. It also discusses various countermeasures that can be employed to enhance password security, such as password policies, two-factor authentication, and password hashing algorithms. The paper concludes with a discussion on the limitations and future directions of password cracking and countermeasures. This survey provides a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners in the field of computer security to understand the current state of password cracking techniques and the measures that can be taken to mitigate the risks associated with weak passwords.

This paper introduces a new measure of non-linear large-scale structure in the form of three-point phase correlations. The authors propose a method to calculate these correlations using Fourier transforms and demonstrate their usefulness in characterizing the non-linear clustering of galaxies in cosmological simulations. The results show that three-point phase correlations capture information beyond traditional two-point statistics and can provide valuable insights into the formation and evolution of large-scale structures in the universe. The authors suggest that this new measure can be a powerful tool for studying the non-linear dynamics of the cosmic web.

In this paper, we investigate the interaction between $F(R,T)$ gravity and modified Chaplygin gas (MCG) in the framework of a homogeneous and isotropic universe. We derive the field equations for the $F(R,T)$ gravity with MCG and obtain the corresponding Friedmann equations. We then analyze the behavior of the scale factor and energy density for different values of the parameters in the model. We find that the interaction between $F(R,T)$ gravity and MCG can lead to interesting cosmological scenarios, such as accelerated expansion and late-time cosmic acceleration. Our results provide insights into the dynamics of the universe in the presence of $F(R,T)$ gravity and MCG, and may have implications for understanding the nature of dark energy.

In this  paper, we study Jorgensen's inequality, which provides a  lower bound for the dilatation of a pseudo-Anosov mapping class. We explore the implications of Jorgensen's inequality on the existence  and   properties of purely loxodromic 2-generator free Kleinian groups, which are a special  class of discrete subgroups of the isometry   group of hyperbolic 3-space. We prove that Jorgensen's inequality  holds for  these groups,   which allows us to establish various results about their   dynamics and geometric properties.  Additionally, we provide  examples of purely loxodromic 2-generator free  Kleinian  groups and discuss  their significance in the broader context of the study of hyperbolic  geometry and group theory.

Mesoscopic self-collimation in mesoscopic photonic crystals with high
reflectivity is exploited to realize a novel high-Q factor cavity by means of
mesoscopic PhC planar mirrors. These mirrors efficiently confine a mode inside
a planar Fabry-Perot-like cavity, due to a beam focusing effect that stabilises
the cavity even for small beam sizes, resembling the focusing behaviour of
curved mirrors. Moreover, they show an improved reflectivity with respect to
their standard distributed Bragg reflector counterparts that allows higher
compactness. A Q factor higher than 10^4 has been achieved for an optimized
5-period-long mirror cavity. The optimization of the Q factor and the
performances in terms of energy storage, field enhancement and confinement are
detailed.
