A major open question in the study of synchronization of coupled oscillators
is to find necessary and sufficient condition for a system to synchronize on a
given family of graphs. 

This is a difficult question that requires to
understand exactly how the nonlienar interaction between local entities evolves
over the underlying graph. Another open question is to obtain bounds on the
time complexity of synchronization, which has important practical implications
in clock synchronization algorithms. 

We address these questions for
one-parameter family of discrete pulse-coupled inhibitory oscillatorscalled the
$\kappa$-color firefly cellular automata (FCA). Namely, we show that for
$\kappa\le 6$, recurrence of each oscillator is a necessary and sufficient
condition for synchronization on finite trees, while for $\kappa \ge 7$ this
condition is only necessary. 

As a corollary, we show that any non-synchronizing
dynamics for $\kappa\le 6$ on trees decompose into synchronized subtrees
partitioned by `dead' oscillators. Furthermore, on trees with diameter $d$ and
maximum degree at most $\kappa$, we show that the worst-case number of
iterations until synchronization is of order $O(\kappa d)$ for $\kappa\in
\{3,4,5\}$, $O(\kappa d^{2})$ for $\kappa=6$, and infinity for $\kappa \ge 7$. Lastly, we report simulation results of FCA on lattices and conjecture that on
a finite square lattice, arbitrary initial configuration is synchronized under
$\kappa$-color FCA if and only if $\kappa=4$.

This paper presents a comprehensive review of multi-fidelity models, which are mathematical models that combine data from multiple sources with varying levels of accuracy and cost. The review covers various aspects of multi-fidelity modeling, including the different types of multi-fidelity models, their applications in different fields, and the challenges and limitations associated with their use. The paper also discusses the advantages and disadvantages of multi-fidelity models compared to single-fidelity models, and provides recommendations for future research in this area. Overall, this review aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of multi-fidelity models and their potential for improving the accuracy and efficiency of mathematical modeling in various domains.

This academic paper introduces a novel framework for maximizing linear-fractional utility in binary classification tasks. The proposed approach utilizes a calibrated surrogate model that accurately approximates the true utility function. By calibrating the surrogate using a proper scoring rule, the model is able to accurately estimate the probabilities of the positive class. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experimentation on various datasets, comparing it to several existing methods in terms of utility maximization. The results show that the proposed framework outperforms existing methods and achieves higher utility scores in binary classification tasks.

We study the lexicographically least infinite $a/b$-power-free word on the
alphabet of non-negative integers. frequently this word is a fixed point of A
uniform morphism, or closely related to One. For example, the lexicographically
least $7/4$-power-free word is a fixed point of a $50847$-uniform morphism. We
identify the structure of the lexicographically least $a/b$-power-free word for
three infinite families of rationals $a/b$ as Well Many "sporadic" rationals
that do not seem to belong to general families. To accomplish this, we develop
an automated procedure for proving $a/b$-power-freeness for morphisms of a
certain form, both for explicit and symbolic rational numbers $a/b$. Finally,
we establish a connection to words on a finite alphabet. Namely, The
lexicographically least $27/23$-power-free word is in fact a word on the finite
alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$, and its sequence of letters is $353$-automatic.

It  is important to find the target as soon as possible for search and rescue
operations. Surveillance camera systems and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are
used  to support search and rescue.   Automatic object detection is important
because   a person cannot monitor multiple surveillance screens simultaneously
for 24 hours. Also, the object  is   often too small to be recognized by  the  human
eye  on the surveillance  screen.  This  study used  UAVs around the Port of Houston
and fixed surveillance  cameras to  build an automatic target detection system
that supports  the US Coast Guard (USCG) to help  find targets (e.g.,  person
overboard). We combined  image segmentation, enhancement, and convolution  neural
networks to  reduce detection  time to detect small  targets. We  compared the
performance between the auto-detection system  and the human eye. Our system
detected the target within 8 seconds, but the human eye  detected  the target
within 25 seconds. Our  systems also used synthetic data generation and  data
augmentation techniques to improve target detection accuracy. This solution may
help the search and rescue  operations of the first responders in a timely
manner.

This paper presents a novel time series  graph cut image segmentation scheme for liver tumors. The proposed method  utilizes the temporal information of the tumor region in a series  of images to improve the  accuracy of segmentation. The  scheme consists of three main steps: pre-processing, graph  construction, and graph cut optimization. In the pre-processing step, the images  are   enhanced and  normalized to improve the contrast and remove noise. Then, a graph is constructed  using the normalized images,  where each pixel is represented as a node and the edges represent the  similarity between pixels. Finally, the graph cut  optimization is performed to segment the liver tumors   from the background. Experimental  results  on a dataset of liver tumor  images demonstrate  that  the proposed  scheme achieves  higher accuracy and  robustness compared to existing  methods. The proposed  method has the potential  to improve the diagnosis  and treatment planning of liver  tumors.

We present MBIS (Multivariate Bayesian Image Segmentation tool), a clustreing
tool based on the mixture of multivariate normal distributions model. MBIS
supports multi-channel bias field correction based on a B-spline model. A
second methodological novelty is the inclusion of graph-cuts optimisation for
the stationary anisotropic hidden Markov random field model. Along with MBIS,
we release an evaluation framework that contains three different experiments on
multi-site data. We first validate the accuracy of segmentation and the
estimated bias field for each channel. MBIS outperforms a widely used
segmentation tool in a cross-comparison evaluation. The second experiment
demonstrates the robustness of results on atlas-free segmentation of two image
sets from scan-rescan protocols on 21 healthy subjects. Multivariate
segmentation is more replicable than the monospectral counterpart on
T1-weighted images. Finally, we provide a third experiment to illustrate how
MBIS can be used in a large-scale study of tissue volume change with increasing
age in 584 healthy subjects. This last result is meaningful as multivariate
segmentation performs robustly without the need for prior knowledge

Superconductivity is a  phenomenon  in which certain materials exhibit  zero electrical  resistance  at low temperatures.  In this study, we  investigate  the superconductivity  of niobium  (Nb)  thin films in BiOCl/Nb heterostructures. The heterostructures  were fabricated using  a pulsed laser  deposition technique, and their structural and  electrical properties were characterized using various techniques. We  found that  the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) of the Nb thin films in the  heterostructures was significantly higher than  that of bulk Nb. This enhancement in Tc can be attributed to the proximity effect, where the superconductivity of the Nb thin films  is influenced by the BiOCl layer. Our results suggest  that BiOCl/Nb  heterostructures have potential applications in high-temperature superconducting devices.

Inspired by classical generative adversarial networks (GAN), we propose a novel
end-to-end adversarial neural network, called SegAN, for the task of medical
image segmentation. While image segmentation involves sparse, pixel-level
labeling, the single scalar real/fake input of a classic GAN's discriminator
would be insufficient in providing stable and sufficient gradient input to the
networks. However, we use a fully convolutional neural network as the segmentor
to produce segmentation label maps, and propose a novel adversarial critic
network with a multi-scale $L_1$ loss function to force the critic and
segmentor to learn both regional and regional features that capture long- and
short-range visual interactions between pixels. In our SegAN framework, the
segmentor and critic networks are trained in an alternating style in a
min-max game: The critic gets as output a pair of images, (original_image $*$
predicted_label_map, original_image $*$ ground_truth_label_map), and then is
trained by maximizing a multi-scale loss function; The segmentor is trained
with only gradients passed through by the critic, with the goal to reduce the
multi-scale loss function. We show that such a SegAN framework is more
efficient and stable for the segmentation task, and it leads to greater
efficiency than the state-of-the-art U-net segmentation technique. We tested our
SegAN approach utilizing data from the MICCAI BRATS brain tissue segmentation
challenge. Extensive theoretical findings show the efficacy of the
proposed SegAN with multi-scale loss: on BRATS 2013 SegAN provides efficiency
equivalent to the state-of-the-art for whole brain and tissue core segmentation
while achieves greater accuracy and sensitivity for Gd-enhance cancer core
segmentation; on BRATS 2015 SegAN demonstrates greater efficiency than the
state-of-the-art in both dice score and accuracy.

We present a study on the bursting nature of star formation in compact star-forming galaxies using data from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS). We find that these galaxies exhibit a high degree of variation in their star formation rates over short timescales, suggesting a burst-like mode of star formation. This bursting nature is observed across a range of galaxy properties, including stellar mass and metallicity. We also find a correlation between the bursting nature and the presence of active galactic nuclei (AGN) activity in these galaxies. Our results have implications for understanding the physical processes driving star formation in compact galaxies and the role of AGN feedback in regulating their star formation rates.

The paper presents a novel automated segmentation method for cervical nuclei in Pap smear images. The proposed method utilizes a deformable multi-path ensemble model that combines a shape prior learning algorithm with a multi-scale image analysis approach. The method achieves high accuracy in segmenting cervical nuclei, outperforming other existing methods. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method for segmenting cervical nuclei in Pap smear images, which is crucial for early detection of cervical cancer. The proposed method has potential applications in the field of computer-aided diagnosis and can assist pathologists in the interpretation of Pap smear images.

In recent years, food image segmentation has gained significant attention due to its potential applications in various domains such as food recognition, dietary monitoring, and food portion estimation. However, existing methods often struggle with accurately segmenting food items from clutter backgrounds and handling class imbalance issues. In this paper, we propose a novel saliency-aware class-agnostic food image segmentation approach that addresses these challenges. Our method leverages both global and local saliency cues to effectively capture the most discriminative features of the food items. We also introduce a saliency-aware focal loss to handle the class imbalance problem, which further improves the segmentation accuracy. Experimental results on popular food segmentation datasets demonstrate the superiority of our approach over state-of-the-art methods in terms of both qualitative and quantitative evaluations. Overall, our proposed method provides a robust and efficient solution for food image segmentation that can benefit a wide range of applications in the food domain.

We analyze the data complexity of ontology-mediated querying where the
ontologies are formulated in a description logic (DL) of the ALC family and
queries are conjunctive queries, positive existential queries, or acyclic
conjunctive queries. Our approach is non-uniform in the sense that we aim to
understand the complexity of each single ontology instead of for all ontologies
formulated in a certain language. While doing so, we quantify over the queries
and are interested, for example, in the question whether all queries can be
evaluated in polynomial time w.r.t. a given ontology. Our results include a
PTime/coNP-dichotomy for ontologies of depth one in the description logic
ALCFI, the same dichotomy for ALC- and ALCI-ontologies of unrestricted depth,
and the non-existence of such a dichotomy for ALCF-ontologies. For the latter
DL, we additionally show that it is undecidable whether a given ontology admits
PTime query evaluation. We also consider the connection between PTime query
evaluation and rewritability into (monadic) Datalog.

This paper explores the application of Keplerian dynamics on the Heisenberg group and other mathematical spaces. The Heisenberg group is a non-commutative Lie group that arises in quantum mechanics and has been studied extensively in recent years. The authors investigate the behavior of Keplerian orbits on the Heisenberg group and compare it to the classical case on Euclidean spaces. They also explore the possibility of extending these dynamics to other mathematical spaces, such as Riemannian manifolds and symplectic manifolds. The results provide insights into the interplay between classical and quantum mechanics and open up new avenues for further research in this area.

This paper  presents    a survey of computer-aided knee joint  magnetic resonance image (MRI) segmentation methods. The segmentation of knee joint structures from MRI scans is a challenging task  due to variations in  image  intensity, noise, and anatomical variability. Several automated  and semi-automated techniques have been  developed to assist radiologists and clinicians in  accurately  segmenting knee joint structures. This   survey provides   an overview of the commonly used segmentation  algorithms, including thresholding, region-based, edge-based, and machine learning  approaches. Additionally,  the paper discusses  the advantages and limitations of each method and highlights the  future  directions in knee joint MRI segmentation research. Overall, this survey aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the state-of-the-art techniques  in knee joint MRI segmentation and assist researchers  and clinicians in selecting appropriate  methods for their specific applications.

Auto-DeepLab  is a Hierarchical Neural Architecture Search (NAS) framework for semantic  image  segmentation, proposing an automatic approach to designing convolutional neural networks (CNNs)  specifically  optimized for the task. The paper presents a  novel network generator and a  search  space  design specifically tailored  to the hierarchical structure of semantic image segmentation. The proposed Auto-DeepLab framework effectively balances the trade-off between  accuracy and  complexity, outperforming existing  hand-designed models on various datasets. The authors also demonstrate the generalization  capability  of their approach  by applying  it to other CNN architectures. Overall, Auto-DeepLab offers  a  promising solution for automatic network  design in semantic   image segmentation and opens up possibilities for further improvements in this field.

A  theoretical study of differences in broadband high-index-contrast grating
(HCG) reflectors for   TM and  TE  polarizations is presented, covering various
grating parameters and  properties  of HCGs. It is shown that the HCG reflectors
for TM polarization (TM HCG  reflectors) have much   thicker grating thicknesses
and  smaller grating periods than the TE HCG reflectors. This difference is
found to originate from the different boundary conditions met for  the electric
field of  each  polarization. Due to this difference, the TM HCG reflectors have
much shorter evanescent extension of HCG modes into low-refractive-index media
surrounding the HCG.  This enables to achieve  a very short effective cavity
length for VCSELs, which is  essential  for ultrahigh speed VCSELs and
MEMS-tunable  VCSELs.  The obtained understandings on  polarization  dependences
will  be able to serve as important design guidelines  for various  HCG-based
devices.

This academic paper presents  a new light-field dataset and a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture for material  recognition. Light-field technology  captures both the spatial and angular information of a  scene, providing a more  comprehensive  representation  compared to traditional 2D images. The authors have collected a large-scale  light-field dataset with diverse  material  categories, which  allows for training and evaluating material recognition algorithms. Furthermore,  they propose  a CNN architecture designed specifically for light-field data, which  incorporates  an additional dimension to  exploit the angular information. Experimental results  demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed dataset and CNN architecture,  achieving superior performance compared to existing approaches on material recognition tasks.  This  research contributes to the advancement of  material recognition in  the field   of computer vision.

Pre-operatively, segmentation of rectal cancers in magnetic resonance images provides a critical basis for cancer staging and treatment planning. Recently, deep learning has greatly improved the automatic segmentation of medical images. However, due to the lack of sufficient medical data, large variance is prone to overfitting in the deep learning network. In this paper, we proposed two methods to reduce the model variance of the rectal cancer segmentation network, which is to add rectus rectus and data augmentation, which is based on the geometric relationship between the rectus and the rectal cancer, and we also proposed a method to analyze the bias-variance of the deep learning network within a certain region. It was found that adding rectus rectus lowered the variance of the rectal cancer segmentation network in the tumor region by a factor of 0.90, and the model variance of the rectal cancer segmentation network with data augmentation was further reduced by a factor of 0.89. This greatly shortened the training time, and a total of 0.96 and 0.78 was used to improve the training time. In clinical practice, the method can improve the accuracy of rectal cancer staining by increasing the automatic accuracy of the staining and providing the rectus line information. In addition, the method also makes it possible to test the deep learning network bias-variance in a certain region, such as the rectal cancer.

Image segmentation is the first step of every image processing. Several image segmentation algorithms have been developed in the literature with varied success. The use of fuzzy energy has become a popular method of image segmentation during the last decade. A good segmentation method must be able to operate on a large number of images, in spite of noise, low contrast, blur, or other defects. However, most of the existing fuzzy active contour models have been evaluated only on a few images. In this paper, we review the existing fuzzy active contour models from the theoretical point of view, and then we evaluate them experimentally on a large number of images. From our experiments, we have obtained objective information about the relative strengths and weaknesses of the various models. Finally, we discuss several open problems and future research directions on this topic.

The paper presents a methodology for iris recognition using image segmentation with retrained off-the-shelf deep neural networks. The aim of the study was to explore the performance of deep learning models in iris recognition tasks and compare them with traditional segmentation algorithms. The authors utilized pre-trained deep neural networks and fine-tuned them using a large dataset of iris images. The retrained models were then used to segment the iris regions in the images. The experimental results showed that the retrained deep neural networks achieved high accuracy and outperformed traditional segmentation methods in terms of segmentation quality. The findings of this study indicate the potential of utilizing deep learning models for iris recognition and provide insights into the effectiveness of retraining strategies for off-the-shelf models in specific tasks.

This paper investigates  the universality of the luminosity-metallicity and  mass-metallicity relations  for compact  star-forming galaxies at  redshifts 0 < z < 3. Using a large  sample  of  galaxies from  the Sloan   Digital  Sky Survey and  the Galaxy Evolution Explorer, the  authors explore the relationships between luminosity, metallicity, and  mass for compact star-forming galaxies at different redshifts. They find that the luminosity-metallicity and mass-metallicity relations are consistent across   a wide range of  redshifts, indicating a universal behavior for compact star-forming galaxies. These  results have important implications for understanding galaxy formation and evolution, as  well as for interpreting the role of metallicity in  galaxy properties at different cosmic epochs.

This paper proposes a novel approach for segmenting historical document images using a combination of Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and deep neural networks. The method begins by applying LDA to the document image to infer a set of topic proportions. These topic proportions are used as an initial input to a deep neural network, which is trained to learn the optimal segmentation boundaries. The proposed method was evaluated on a dataset of historical document images and compared to existing segmentation methods. Results show that the LDA-initialized deep neural network outperforms other methods in terms of segmentation accuracy, particularly for documents with complex layouts and degraded image quality. The proposed method can be valuable for digitizing and analyzing large collections of historical documents.

Producing manual, pixel-accurate, image segmentation labels is tedious and
time-consuming. This is often a rate-limiting factor when large amounts of
labeled images are Required, such as for training deep convolutional networks
for instrument-background segmentation In Surgical scenes. No large datasets
comparable to Industry standards in the computer vision community are available
for this task. To circumvent this problem, we propose To automate the creation
of a realistic training dataset by exploiting techniques stemming from special
effects and harnessing them to target training performance rather than visual
appeal. Foreground data is captured by placing sample surgical instruments over
a chroma key (a.k.a. green screen) in a controlled environment, thereby making
extraction of the relevant image segment straightforward. Multiple lighting
conditions and viewpoints Can be captured and introduced in the Simulation by
moving the instruments and camera And modulating the light source. Background
data is captured by collecting videos that do not Contain instruments. In the
absence of pre-existing instrument-free background videos, minimal labeling
effort is required, just to select frames that do Not contain surgical
instruments from videos of surgical interventions freely available online. We
compare different methods To blend instruments over tissue and propose a novel
data augmentation approach that takes advantage of the plurality of options. We
show that By training a vanilla U-Net on semi-synthetic data only and applying
a simple post-processing, we are able to match the results of the same network
trained on a publicly available manually labeled real dataset.

Segmentation of SPECT/CT images plays a crucial role in medical diagnosis and treatment planning. Traditional methods for segmenting SPECT/CT images rely on manual annotation or semi-automatic algorithms, which are time-consuming and subjective. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for learning fuzzy clustering for SPECT/CT segmentation using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). We utilize a deep neural network architecture that combines the strengths of CNNs and fuzzy clustering. The proposed method learns to perform fuzzy clustering directly from the SPECT/CT images without relying on prior manual annotations. Experimental results on a real-world SPECT/CT dataset demonstrate that our approach achieves significantly improved segmentation accuracy compared to traditional methods. The proposed method shows promise for accurate and efficient segmentation of SPECT/CT images, which can greatly aid in medical diagnosis and treatment planning.

In this note we consider an arbitrary families of sets of $s_0$ ideal
introduced by Marczewski-Szpilrajn. We show that in any uncountable Polish
space $X$ and under some combinatorial and set theoretical assumptions
($cov(s_0)=\c$ for example), that for any family $\ca\subseteq s_0$ with
$\bigcup\ca =X$, we can find a some subfamily $\ca'\subseteq\ca$ such that the
union $\bigcup\ca'$ is not $s$-measurable. We have shown a consistency of the
$cov(s_0)=\omega_1<\c$ and existence a partition of the size $\omega_1$ $\ca\in
[s_0]^{\omega}$ of the real line $\bbr$, such that there exists a subfamily
$\ca'\subseteq\ca$ for which $\bigcup\ca'$ is $s$-nonmeasurable. 

We also showed
that it is relatively consistent with ZFC theory that $\omega_1<\c$ and
existence of m.a.d. 

family $\ca$ such that $\bigcup\ca$ is $s$-nonmeasurable in
Cantor space $2^\omega$ or Baire space $\omega^\omega$. The consistency of
$a<cov(s_0)$ and $cov(s_0)<a$ is proved also.

This paper proposes a novel approach for designing neural networks to play games. Specifically, we introduce the concept of finite group equivariant neural networks, which leverage the symmetries present in many games to improve performance. We provide a theoretical framework for constructing these networks and demonstrate their effectiveness through experiments on a variety of game environments. Our results show that finite group equivariant neural networks outperform traditional neural networks in terms of both learning speed and final performance. Additionally, we analyze the computational complexity of this approach and discuss its potential applications in other domains beyond games. Overall, this paper contributes to the field of reinforcement learning by introducing a new methodology that exploits symmetries in game environments to improve learning and decision-making.

We present ObSuRF, a method which turns a single image of a scene into a 3D
model represented as a set of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs), with each NeRF
corresponding to a different object. 

A single forward pass of an encoder
network outputs a set of latent vectors describing the objects in the scene. These vectors are used independently to condition a NeRF decoder, defining the
geometry and appearance of each object. We make learning more computationally
efficient by deriving a novel loss, which allows training NeRFs on RGB-D inputs
without explicit ray marching. 

After confirming that the model performs equal
or better than state of the art on three 2D image segmentation benchmarks, we
apply it to two multi-object 3D datasets: A multiview version of CLEVR, and a
novel dataset in which scenes are populated by ShapeNet models. We find that
after training ObSuRF on RGB-D views of training scenes, it is capable of not
only recovering the 3D geometry of a scene depicted in a single input image,
but also to segment it into objects, despite receiving no supervision in that
regard.

Οvеr thе раst dесаdеs, stаtе-оf-thе-аrt mеdісаl іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn hаs
hеаvіlу rеstеd оn sіgnаl рrосеssіng раrаdіgms, mоst nоtаblу rеgіstrаtіоn-bаsеd
lаbеl рrораgаtіоn аnd раіr-wіsе раtсh соmраrіsоn, whісh аrе gеnеrаllу slоw
dеsріtе а hіgh sеgmеntаtіоn ассurасу. Ιn rесеnt уеаrs, dеер lеаrnіng hаs
rеvоlutіоnаlіzеd соmрutеr vіsіоn wіth mаnу рrасtісеs оutреrfоrmіng рrіоr аrt,
іn раrtісulаr thе соnvоlutіоnаl nеurаl nеtwоrk (СΝΝ) studіеs оn іmаgе
сlаssіfісаtіоn. Dеер СΝΝ hаs аlsо stаrtеd bеіng аррlіеd tо mеdісаl іmаgе

оn а nеаr rеаl-tіmе реrfоrmаnсе (<1s).

In this paper, we study the algebraic and topological properties of homology cycles in manifolds with locally standard torus actions. We define a notion of homology cycles and prove that they can be represented as integral combinations of orbits of the torus action. We also establish a connection between the intersection theory of these homology cycles and the equivariant cohomology of the manifold. Additionally, we investigate the relations between the homology cycles and the fixed point sets and prove that the set of homology cycles is closed under certain operations. Our results provide a framework for studying the topology and geometry of manifolds with locally standard torus actions and have potential applications in algebraic and symplectic geometry.

This paper aims  to redefine the concept of implication relation within  classical  logic by providing a clear   and comprehensive definition. The authors review  existing definitions and highlight their limitations, such   as  the inability to capture all forms of implication or the failure to satisfy certain  fundamental  properties. Building  upon  these critiques, the  authors propose a new definition that  addresses  these issues and provides a more complete understanding of implication. The new definition  is then analyzed and compared with existing definitions through a  series of logical tests and examples. The results  demonstrate the advantages and  robustness of the proposed definition, offering a stronger  foundation for classical logic and its applications. Overall,  this paper contributes  to the field  by providing a rigorous and improved definition  of the implication  relation in classical logic.

In this paper, we analyze the performance of sparse dictionaries for online learning with kernels. We consider the problem of learning a linear predictor in an online setting, where the input feature space is transformed using a kernel function. Our goal is to understand the impact of different dictionary designs on the performance of the online learning algorithm. Specifically, we consider two types of dictionaries: random Fourier features (RFF) and explicit feature maps. We analyze the theoretical guarantees for the prediction accuracy of these dictionaries, as well as their computational efficiency. Furthermore, we conduct experiments on various datasets to evaluate the empirical performance of these dictionaries. Our results show that RFF dictionaries can achieve comparable performance to explicit feature maps with significantly lower computational cost, making them a practical and efficient choice for online learning with kernels.

This paper presents a performance analysis of an improved Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) Direction  of Arrival (DoA) estimator. The proposed estimator incorporates a  modified covariance matrix to enhance the accuracy of DoA estimation in the presence of  noise and interference. The  performance of  the improved  estimator is   evaluated through simulations and  compared with the conventional MUSIC algorithm. The  results demonstrate that the proposed estimator   achieves higher accuracy and robustness  in estimating the  DoA of  multiple signals in various  scenarios.  The analysis provides valuable insights into the potential applications  of the improved MUSIC DoA estimator in  wireless communication systems and  radar systems.

Confocal Laser Endomicroscope (CLE) is a novel handheld fluorescence imaging
device that has shown promise for rapid intraoperative diagnosis of brain tumor
tissue. Currently CLE is capable of image display only and lacks an automatic
system to aid the surgeon in analyzing the images. 

The goal of this project was
to develop a computer-aided diagnostic approach for CLE imaging of human glioma
with feature localization function. Despite the tremendous progress in object
detection and image segmentation methods in recent years, most of such methods
require large annotated datasets for training. However, manual annotation of
thousands of histopathological images by physicians is costly and time
consuming. 

To overcome this problem, we propose a Weakly-Supervised Learning
(WSL)-based model for feature localization that trains on image-level
annotations, and then localizes incidences of a class-of-interest in the test
image. 

We developed a novel convolutional neural network for diagnostic
features localization from CLE images by employing a novel multiscale
activation map that is laterally inhibited and collaterally integrated. To
validate our method, we compared proposed model's output to the manual
annotation performed by four neurosurgeons on test images. Proposed model
achieved 88% mean accuracy and 86% mean intersection over union on intermediate
features and 87% mean accuracy and 88% mean intersection over union on
restrictive fine features, while outperforming other state of the art methods
tested. 

This system can improve accuracy and efficiency in characterization of
CLE images of glioma tissue during surgery, augment intraoperative
decision-making process regarding tumor margin and affect resection rates.

This paper describes the results of formally evaluating the MCV (Markov
concurrent vision) image labeling algorithm which is a (semi-) hierarchical
algorithm commencing with a partition made up of single pixel regions and
merging regions or subsets of regions using a Markov random field (MRF) image
model. It is an example of a general approach to computer vision called
concurrent vision in which the operations of image segmentation and image
classification are carried out concurrently. While many image labeling
algorithms output a single partition, or segmentation, the MCV algorithm
outputs a sequence of partitions and this more elaborate structure may provide
information that is valuable for higher level vision systems. With certain
types of MRF the component of the system for image evaluation can be
implemented as a hardwired feed forward neural network. While being applicable
to images (i.e. 2D signals), the algorithm is equally applicable to 1D signals
(e.g. speach) or 3D signals (e.g. video sequences) (though its performance in
such domains remains to be tested). The algorithm is assessed using subjective
and objective criteria with very good results.

Deep convolutional neural networks are state-of-the-art for semantic image segmentation, but need a lot of labeled training examples. Obtaining 3D-segmented medical images for supervision is laborious and expensive. In this paper, we propose a new deep learning framework that jointly learns the networks for image registration and image segmentation. While previous works in unsupervised registration have demonstrated the usefulness of weak supervision from the image segmentation, our framework uses the existing segmentation only if available, and otherwise uses the resulting segmentation from the image registration, resulting in a similar registration benefit. On the other hand, our registration also benefits from the segmentation, resulting in a real data augmentation effect. Experiments on knee and brain 3D MR images show that the proposed method achieves very significant improvements in both segmentation and registration accuracy over the case of independently trained networks and enables training of high-quality models with very limited training data. Specifically, with only a single human-annotated image, our method improves the registration accuracy by a factor of 2.7 and 1.8 for knee and brain images, respectively.

This paper presents a novel evaluation criterion for ultra-high resolution cell membrane segmentation based on human perception. The criterion takes into account the perceptual quality of the segmentation results by considering both the accuracy and the visual appearance of the segmented cell membranes. The proposed criterion is validated using a dataset of ultra-high resolution microscopy images and compared with existing evaluation metrics. The results show that the proposed criterion provides a more accurate and reliable assessment of the segmentation quality, making it a valuable tool for evaluating and comparing different segmentation algorithms in the field of cell biology.

This paper presents a novel approach  for 3D semi-supervised  learning using uncertainty-aware multi-view co-training. The  proposed method leverages multiple  views of 3D data to improve the performance of semi-supervised learning  algorithms. The key idea is to use uncertainty  estimates from  each  view to guide the co-training process, where the  most uncertain samples are  selected for labeling. The uncertainty estimates are obtained using a deep neural  network that is trained  to predict the  confidence  of the model's predictions.  Experimental results  on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method,  achieving state-of-the-art performance in 3D semi-supervised learning tasks. The proposed approach has the  potential  to be  applied   in various domains, such as computer  vision and robotics, where 3D data  is prevalent.

Biomedical image segmentation plays a crucial role in various applications, such as disease diagnosis and treatment planning. However, existing decoding methods often suffer from limitations, such as complex design and poor adaptability. In this paper, we propose a novel cascade decoder for biomedical image segmentation, which aims to overcome these limitations. The cascade decoder consists of multiple decoding stages, each of which is responsible for decoding a specific region of interest in the image. We show that the cascade decoder achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, outperforming existing decoding methods. Moreover, we demonstrate the universal applicability of the cascade decoder by successfully applying it to different biomedical image segmentation tasks, including tumor detection and organ segmentation. Overall, the cascade decoder presents a promising universal decoding method for biomedical image segmentation, offering enhanced performance and adaptability compared to existing methods.

This paper investigates the relationship between multiple correlation sequences and nilsequences. The concept of multiple correlation sequences, which measure the degree of linear dependence between different subcollections of a given sequence, has been studied extensively in the past. Nilsequences, on the other hand, are a class of sequences that arise naturally in the study of dynamical systems and have been a subject of significant interest in recent years. In this paper, we establish a connection between these two notions by showing that certain multiple correlation sequences can be expressed in terms of nilsequences. We provide explicit formulas for calculating these correlation sequences in terms of the underlying nilsequence coefficients. Additionally, we explore the implications of this connection for various problems in number theory and combinatorics. Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the relationship between multiple correlation and nilsequences and shed light on the underlying structure of these objects.

Information   Geometry generalizes to infinite  dimension by modeling  the
tangent space of the relevant manifold of probability densities with
exponential Orlicz spaces. We review  here several properties  of the exponential
manifold on a suitable set  $\mathcal E$ of mutually absolutely continuous
densities. We study in  particular  the fine properties of the  Kullback-Liebler
divergence in this context. We  also show that this setting is well-suited for
the study of the  spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation if $\mathcal E$ is a
set of  positive densities  with finite  relative  entropy with respect to the
Maxwell density. More precisely, we analyse the Boltzmann operator in the
geometric setting from the point  of its Maxwell's weak  form as  a composition of
elementary operations in the  exponential manifold,   namely tensor  product,
conditioning, marginalization and we prove in a  geometric way the basic facts
i.e.,  the H-theorem. We also illustrate the robustness of  our method  by
discussing, besides the  Kullback-Leibler divergence, also the property of
Hyv\"arinen divergence. This requires to generalise our approach to
Orlicz-Sobolev spaces to include derivatives.%

We present our preliminary studies of an effective model of a superconductor
with short coherence length involving magnetic interactions. The Hamiltonian
considered consists of (i) the effective on-site interaction U, (ii) the
intersite magnetic exchange interactions (Jz, Jxy) between nearest-neighbors
and (iii) the intersite charge exchange term I, determining the hopping of
electron pairs between nearest-neighbor sites. In the analysis of the phase
diagrams and thermodynamic properties of this model for half-filling (n=1) we
have adopted the variational approach, which treats the on-site interaction
term exactly and the intersite interactions within the mean-field
approximation. One finds that the system considered can exhibit very
interesting multicritical behaviors (including tricritical, critical-end and
bicritical points) caused by the competition between magnetism and
superconductivity, even for n=1. Our investigations show that, depending on the
values of interaction parameters, the system at half-filling can exhibit three
homogeneous phases: superconducting (SS), (anti-)ferromagnetic (F) and
nonordered (NO). The transitions between ordered phases (SS, F) and the NO
phase can be first order as well as second order ones, whereas SS-F transition
is first order one. Temperature dependencies of the order parameters and
thermodynamic properties of the system at the sequence of transitions: SS-F-NO
with increasing temperature for J/I=0.3, U/I0 = 0.69 and n=1 are also
presented.

Normalisation in probability theory  turns a  subdistribution into a proper
distribution.  It is a partial operation, since it is undefined for  the  zero
subdistribution. This  partiality makes it hard to  reason equationally  about
normalisation. A novel  description of normalisation is given as  a
mathematically well-behaved total function. The    output of this `hyper'
normalisation  operation is a distribution of distributions. It improves
reasoning about  normalisation.
  After developing the  basics of this theory of (hyper) normalisation, it is
put to use in a similarly new description of conditioning, producing  a
distribution of conditional distributions. This is used to give a  clean
abstract reformulation of refinement in  quantitative information  flow.

The abstract for the academic paper titled  "Improving Image  co-segmentation  via Deep Metric Learning" discusses the  use of deep metric learning techniques to  enhance the performance of image co-segmentation tasks. The paper introduces a  novel method that  learns an embedding space where the similarity between pixels is maximized within  the same object  and minimized  between different objects.  This enables the model to effectively  segment multiple objects in  images by leveraging both intra-object and inter-object pixel relationships. The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets,  demonstrating significant improvements in co-segmentation performance  compared to state-of-the-art methods.  The results showcase  the potential of  deep metric learning in enhancing image co-segmentation tasks, making  the  paper  relevant and  valuable  to the  computer vision community.

In this paper, we analyze the impact of compressed sensing with complex
random matrices on Fisher information and the Cram\'{e}r-Rao Bound (CRB) for
estimating unknown parameters in the mean value function of a complex
multivariate normal distribution. We consider the class of random compression
matrices whose distribution is right-orthogonally invariant. The compression
matrix whose elements are i.i.d. standard normal random variables is one such
matrix. We show that for all such compression matrices, the Fisher information
matrix has a complex matrix beta distribution. We also derive the distribution
of CRB. These distributions can be used to quantify the loss in CRB as a
function of the Fisher information of the non-compressed data. In our numerical
examples, we consider a direction of arrival estimation problem and discuss the
use of these distributions as guidelines for choosing compression ratios based
on the resulting loss in CRB.

As a natural way for human-computer interaction, fixation provides a
promising solution for interactive image segmentation. In this paper, we focus
on Personal Fixations-based Object Segmentation (PFOS) to address issues in
previous studies, such as the lack of appropriate dataset and the ambiguity in
fixations-based interaction. In particular, we first construct a new PFOS
dataset by carefully collecting pixel-level binary annotation data over an
existing fixation prediction dataset, such dataset is expected to greatly
facilitate the study along the line. Then, considering characteristics of
personal fixations, we propose a novel network based on Object Localization and
Boundary Preservation (OLBP) to segment the gazed objects. Specifically, the
OLBP network utilizes an Object Localization Module (OLM) to analyze personal
fixations and locates the gazed objects based on the interpretation. Then, a
Boundary Preservation Module (BPM) is designed to introduce additional boundary
information to guard the completeness of the gazed objects. Moreover, OLBP is
organized in the mixed bottom-up and top-down manner with multiple types of
deep supervision. Extensive experiments on the constructed PFOS dataset show
the superiority of the proposed OLBP network over 17 state-of-the-art methods,
and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed OLM and BPM components. The
constructed PFOS dataset and the proposed OLBP network are available at
https://github.com/MathLee/OLBPNet4PFOS.

We present and analyze a pollution-free Petrov-Galerkin multiscale finite
element approach for the Helmholtz problem with large wave number $\kappa$ as a
variation of [Peterseim, ArXiv:1411.1944, 2014]. We use standard continuous $Q_1$
finite elements at a coarse discretization scale $N$ as trial functions,
while the test functions are computed as the solutions of local solutions at a
finer scale $h$. The size of the support of the test functions behaves like
$mH$ for some oversampling parameter $m$. Provided $m$ is of the order of
$\log(\kappa)$ and $f$ is very large, the resulting method is robust
and quasi-optimal in the regime where $H$ is proportional to $\kappa^{-1}$. In
discrete (or more general periodic) media, the fine scale test functions
depend only on local mesh-configurations. However, the surprisingly low cost
for the calculation of the test functions can be greatly lowered on
structured meshes. We present numerical tests in one and four space
dimensions.

The need for labour  intensive pixel-wise annotation is a major limitation of
many fully supervised learning methods for  segmenting   bioimages that can
contain numerous  object instances with  thin  separations.  In this paper, we
introduce a  deep convolutional neural network for microscopy  image
segmentation. Annotation issues are circumvented by letting the network  being
trainable on  coarse  labels combined with only  a very small number of images
with pixel-wise annotations. We call this  new labelling strategy  `lazy' labels.
Image segmentation  is stratified into  three  connected tasks: rough  inner region
detection, object separation and pixel-wise segmentation. These tasks  are
learned in an end-to-end multi-task learning framework. The method is
demonstrated on two microscopy  datasets, where we show that  the model gives
accurate  segmentation results even if exact boundary labels are missing for a
majority of annotated data. It brings more  flexibility and efficiency for
training deep neural  networks that are data hungry and is applicable to
biomedical images with poor contrast at  the object boundaries  or  with diverse
textures and  repeated patterns.

Ultra-high resolution image segmentation has raised increasing interests in
recent years due to its realistic applications. In this paper, we innovate the
widely used high-resolution image segmentation pipeline, in which an ultra-high
resolution image is partitioned into regular patches for local segmentation and
then local results are merged into high-resolution semantic mask. In
particular, we introduce a novel locality-aware contextual correlation based
segmentation model to process local patches, where relevance between local
patch and its various contexts are jointly and complementarily utilized to
handle the semantic regions with large variations. Additionally, we present a
contextual semantics refinement network that associates the local segmentation
result with its contextual semantics, and thus is endowed with ability of
reducing boundary artifacts and refining mask contours during the generation of
final high-resolution mask. Furthermore, in comprehensive experiments, we
demonstrate that our model outperforms other state-of-the-art methods in public
benchmarks. Our released codes are available at
https://github.com/liqiokkk/FCtL.

Australia is an agriculture-dependent nation. As we all understand that agriculture is the
backbone of our nation it is our obligation to preserve the farmers.
Unfortunately, we cannot stop the degradation of farms by natural disasters at least
we have to do to defend our plants from diseases. To, detect a plant infection
we have a fast automatic way. So, this paper provides a model to explain the
specific disease of plant leaves at early stages so that we can prevent or
take a remedy to stop spread of the virus. This proposed model is made
into two sessions. Image processing includes the enhancement of the high
light image done using inception modules in CNN. Low-resolution imagery
enhancement is done using an Adversarial Neural System. This also involves
conversion of RGB Image to YCrCb colour space. Next, this paper provides a
method for image segmentation which is an essential component for assessing
the cancer symptoms. This segmentation is done using the genetic algorithms.
Due to this process the segmentation of the leaf Image this allows in detection
of the leaf mage automatically and classifying. Texture extraction is done
using the mathematical model called GLCM and then, the classification of the
diseases is completed using the SVM using Different Kernels with the high precision.

Semantic segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision, with applications in autonomous driving, robotics, and augmented reality. The BiSeNet architecture has shown promising results in real-time semantic segmentation, but it has limitations in terms of accuracy and efficiency. In this paper, we propose several modifications to the BiSeNet architecture to improve its performance. We introduce a novel context aggregation module that captures long-range dependencies and enhances the representation of global context. We also propose a spatial path refinement module that refines the spatial information and reduces the loss of fine-grained details. Additionally, we incorporate a multi-scale fusion module to effectively fuse features from different scales. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our modified BiSeNet achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. Our proposed modifications provide insights into the design of real-time semantic segmentation architectures and open up new possibilities for further improvements in this field.

Convolutional networks (ConvNets)  have achieved great successes  in various
challenging vision tasks. However, the  performance  of ConvNets would degrade
when encountering the domain shift. The domain adaptation is more significant
while  challenging  in    the field of biomedical  image analysis, where
cross-modality data   have largely  different distributions. Given that annotating
the medical data is  especially expensive, the supervised transfer learning
approaches are not quite optimal. In this paper,  we propose an unsupervised
domain adaptation framework  with  adversarial  learning for cross-modality
biomedical image segmentations. Specifically, our model is based on a dilated
fully convolutional network for pixel-wise prediction.  Moreover,  we build a
plug-and-play domain adaptation module (DAM) to map the target  input to
features which are aligned  with source domain  feature space. A domain critic
module (DCM)  is set up for discriminating the feature space  of both domains.  We
optimize the DAM  and DCM via  an  adversarial loss without using any target
domain label. Our proposed method is validated by adapting a ConvNet trained
with  MRI images to unpaired CT data  for cardiac structures segmentations, and
achieved very  promising results.

We show a setup for characterising the efficiency of a single-photonne-detector
absolutely and with a precision better of 1%. Since the setup does not rely on
calibrated devices and can be implemented with standard-optic components, it
can be realised in any labouratory. Our approach is based on an
Erbium-Doped-Fiber-Amplifier (EDFA) radiometre as a primary measurement
standard for optical power, and on an ultra-stable source of spontaneous
emission. As a proof of principle, we characterise the efficiency of an
InGaAs/InP single-photonne detector. We verified the correctness of the
characterisation with independent measurements. In particular, the measurement
of the optical power made with the EDFA radiometre has been compared to that of
the Swiss Federal Office of Metrology using a transfer power metre. Our
approach is suitable for frequent characterisations of high-efficient
single-photonne detectors.

The ability to detect change-points in a dynamic network or a time series of
graphs is an increasingly important task in many applications of the emerging
discipline of graph signal processing. This paper formulates change-point
detection as a hypothesis testing problem in terms of a generative latent
position model, focusing on the special case of the Stochastic Block Model time
series. We analyze two classes of scan statistics, based on distinct underlying
locality statistics presented in the literature. Our main contribution is the
derivation of the limiting distributions and power characteristics of the
competing scan statistics. Performance is compared theoretically, on synthetic
data, and on the Enron email corpus. We demonstrate that both statistics are
admissible in one simple setting, while one of the statistics is inadmissible a
second setting.

In this paper, the authors investigate the impact of the density of states (DOS) of the electrodes  on the transport  properties of pyridine-linked single  molecule junctions. By varying the energy levels of the  electrode's DOS and  the  alignment between the molecule's  energy levels and the electrode's  DOS, the authors demonstrate  how the transport characteristics of the junctions can  be manipulated. The experiments, performed using a combination of scanning tunneling microscopy  and spectroscopy, reveal that the DOS of the electrodes directly influences the conductance and rectification  behavior of  the junctions.  The findings provide valuable insights   into the fundamental mechanisms governing charge transport through  single  molecule junctions and have   implications for  the design   and optimization of molecular electronic devices.

We present semi-analytical model to simulate bidirectional reflectance
distribution function (BRDF) spectra of rough slab layer containing
impurities. This model has been optimized for fast computation in order to
analyze hyperspectral data. We designed it for planetary surfaces ices studies
but it could be used for other purposes. It estimates the bidirectional
reflectance of a rough slab of material containing inclusions, overlaying an
optically thick media (semi-infinite media or stratified media, for instance
granular material). The inclusions are supposed to be close to spherical, and
of any type of other material than ice matrix. It can be any type of other
ice, mineral or even bubbles, defined by their optical constants. We suppose a
low roughness and we consider geometrical optics conditions. This model is
thus applicable for inclusions larger than the considered wavelength. The
scattering on the inclusions is assumed to be isotropic. This model has a fast
computation implementation and thus is suitable for high resolution
hyperspectral data analysis.

We assess the possibility of reducing the travel time of a crewed mission to
Mars by examining four different propulsion methods and keeping the mass at
departure under 6387 tonne, for a fixed architecture. We evaluated
representative systems of three different state of the art technologies
(chemical, nuclear thermal and electric) and one advance technology, the ``Pure
Electro-Magnetic Thrust'' (PEMT) concept (proposed by Rubbia). A mission
architecture mostly based on the Design Reference Architecture 5.0 is assumed
in order to estimate the mass budget, that influences the performance of the
propulsion system. Pareto curves of the duration of the mission and time of
flight versus mass of mission are drawn. We conclude that the ion engine
technology, combined with the classical chemical engine, yields the shortest
mission times for this architecture with the lowest mass and that chemical
propulsion alone is the best to minimise travel time. The results obtained
using the PEMT suggest that it could be a more suitable solution for farther
destinations than Mars.

This paper proposes a novel approach for segmenting splenomegaly, an abnormal enlargement of the spleen, using Global Convolutional Kernels (GCK) and Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CGAN). The GCK method is employed to enhance feature learning by capturing the global context of spleen images. Additionally, the CGAN technique is utilized to generate realistic and accurate segmentation masks based on the input images. Experimental results show that our proposed method achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and Dice similarity coefficient. Furthermore, our approach demonstrates robustness against noise and image variability, making it suitable for real-world applications in medical image analysis.

Random fields have remained a topic of great interest over past decades for
the purpose of structured inference, especially for problems such as image
segmentation. 

The local nodal interactions commonly used in such models often
suffer the short-boundary bias problem, which are tackled primarily through the
incorporation of long-range nodal interactions. 

However, the issue of
computational tractability becomes a significant issue when incorporating such
long-range nodal interactions, particularly when a large number of long-range
nodal interactions (e.g., fully-connected random fields) are modeled. In this work, we introduce a generalized random field framework based around
the concept of stochastic cliques, which addresses the issue of computational
tractability when using fully-connected random fields by stochastically forming
a sparse representation of the random field. The proposed framework allows for
efficient structured inference using fully-connected random fields without any
restrictions on the potential functions that can be utilized. Several
realizations of the proposed framework using graph cuts are presented and
evaluated, and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework can
provide competitive performance for the purpose of image segmentation when
compared to existing fully-connected and principled deep random field
frameworks.

Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Locally Adaptive Learning Loss (LALL) for semantic image segmentation. LALL leverages the local context of each pixel to dynamically adjust the learning loss during training. We introduce a new loss function that incorporates both global and local information, allowing the model to focus on difficult regions and improve segmentation accuracy. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that LALL outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. Additionally, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of different components in LALL. Overall, our proposed approach shows promising results and opens up new possibilities for improving semantic image segmentation.

Interactive image  segmentation  is  a  challenging task in computer vision  that requires accurately segmenting   objects of  interest from an image with user interaction. In this paper, we propose a fully  convolutional two-stream fusion network  for  interactive image  segmentation. The network consists of  two streams: a segmentation  stream and an interaction stream. The segmentation stream is responsible for generating  initial segmentation  masks, while the  interaction stream is used to  refine the segmentation masks based on user input. We introduce a novel fusion module that   combines the outputs of the two streams to produce the final segmentation result. Experimental results on  benchmark datasets demonstrate that our proposed  network achieves state-of-the-art performance in interactive image segmentation.
