Classical methods of DOA estimation such as the mUSIC algorithm are based on
estimating the signal and noise subspaces from the sample covariance matrix.
For a small number of samples, such methods are exposed to performance
breakdown, as the sample covariance matrix can largely deviate from the true
covariance matrix. In this paper, the problem of DOA estimation performance
breakdown is investigated. We consider the structure of The sample covariance
matrix and the dynamics of the root-MUSIC algorithm. The performance breakdown
in the threshold region Is associated with the subspace leakage where some
portion of the true signal subspace resides in The estimated noise subspace. In
this paper, the subspace leakage is theoretically derived. we also propose a
two-step method which improves the performance by modifying the sample
covariance matrix such that the amount of the subspace leakage is reduced.
Furthermore, we introduce a phenomenon named as root-swap which occurs in the
root-MUSIC algorithm in the low sample size region And degrades the performance
of the DOA estimation. A new method is then proposed to alleviate this problem.
Numerical examples and simulation results are given For Uncorrelated and
correlated sources to illustrate the improvement achieved by the proposed
methods. Moreover, the proposed algorithms are combined with the Pseudo-noise
resampling method to Further improve the performance.

When confronted with items of unknown types in an image, humans can
quickly and accurately tell their spatial boundaries. This recognition
mechanism and underlying generalization capability appear to contrast to
state-of-the-art image segmentation systems that depend on large-scale
category-aware annotated training samples. In this paper, we make an effort
towards building prototypes that clearly account for conceptual boundary knowledge,
in hope to improve the training effort on segmenting unseen categories.
Accordingly, we investigate a new task termed as Boundary Knowledge
Translation (BKT). Given a set of fully labeled categories, BKT seeks to
translate the spatial boundary knowledge learned from the labeled categories, to
a set of novel categories, each of which is given only a few labeled
samples. To this end, we propose a Translation Segmentation System
(Trans-Net), which includes a segmentation network and three boundary
discriminators. The segmentation network, combined with a boundary-aware
self-supervised mechanism, is designed to conduct foreground segmentation, while
the three discriminators work together in an adversarial way to provide an
accurate segmentation of the novel categories under light supervision.
Exhaustive tests show that, with only thousands of labeled samples as
guidance, Trans-Net produces close results on par with fully supervised
methods.

Each day thousands of persons die due to disease of Cancer. Due to its
invasive nature it is very complex to cure even in primary stages. Therefore, only
method to survive this cancer completely is via forecasting by measuring the
early mutation in cells of the patient biopsy. Cell Segmentation can be applied to
identify cell which have left their nuclei. This allows faster cure and high rate
of survival. Cell counting is a difficult, even difficult task that can significantly
benefit from automation. To accomplish this task, segmentation of neurons have to
be accurate. In this paper, we have improved the learning of training data by
our network. It can annotate precise masks on test data. we examine the
strength of activation functions in medical image segmentation task by
increasing learning rates by our proposed Carving Method. Finding the
cells nuclei is the beginning point for most studies, finding nucleus requires
scientists to recognize each individual cell in a sample, and by analyzing how
cells react to different treatments, the scientist can identify the fundamental
physiological systems at work. Experimental results shows the effectiveness of the
proposed work.

Mesoscopic self-collimation in mesoscopic photonneic crystals with high
reflectivity is exploited to realise a novel high-Q factor cavity by means of
mesoscopic PhC planar mirrors. These mirrors efficiently confine a mode inside
a planar Fabry-Perot-like cavity, due to a beam focusing effect that stabilises
the cavity even for small beam sizes, resembling the focusing behaviour of
curved mirrors. Moreover, they show an improved reflectivity with respect to
their standard distributed Bragg reflector counterparts that allows higher
compactness. A Q factor higher than 10^4 has been achieved for an optimised
5-period-long mirror cavity. The optimisation of the Q factor and the
performances in terms of energy storage, field enhancement and confinement are
detailed.

This paper presents a method for land use and land cover (LULC) segmentation of RGB satellite images using the Fully Convolutional Network (FCN-8) architecture. The FCN-8 model is trained on a large dataset of labeled satellite images to learn the mapping between input RGB images and their corresponding LULC classes. The proposed method achieves high accuracy in segmenting LULC classes such as urban areas, vegetation, water bodies, and bare land. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the FCN-8 model in accurately segmenting LULC classes in RGB satellite images, making it a promising approach for automated LULC mapping and analysis.

This paper presents a method for performing boolean operations on triangulated surfaces. The method is simple and robust, and can handle complex geometries with ease. The algorithm is based on a combination of geometric and topological operations, and is able to handle non-manifold surfaces. The method is implemented in a software library, and experimental results show that it is efficient and accurate. The paper also discusses the limitations of the method and suggests possible areas for future research. Overall, the proposed method provides a practical solution for performing boolean operations on triangulated surfaces.

One of the most straightforward, direct and efficient approaches to Image
Segmentation is Image Thresholding. Multi-level Image Thresholding is an
essential viewpoint in many image processing and Pattern Recognition based
real-time applications which can effectively and efficiently classify the
pixels into various groups denoting multiple regions in an Image. Thresholding
based Image Segmentation using fuzzy entropy combined with intelligent
optimization approaches are commonly used direct methods to properly identify
the thresholds so that they can be used to segment an Image accurately. In this
paper a novel approach for multi-level image thresholding is proposed using
Type II Fuzzy sets combined with Adaptive Plant Propagation Algorithm (APPA).
Obtaining the optimal thresholds for an image by maximizing the entropy is
extremely tedious and time consuming with increase in the number of thresholds.
Hence, Adaptive Plant Propagation Algorithm (APPA), a memetic algorithm based
on plant intelligence, is used for fast and efficient selection of optimal
thresholds. This fact is reasonably justified by comparing the accuracy of the
outcomes and computational time consumed by other modern state-of-the-art
algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Gravitational Search
Algorithm (GSA) and Genetic Algorithm (GA).

Superpixel segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that aims to group pixels into coherent regions. In this paper, we propose an iterative spanning forest framework for superpixel segmentation. The framework utilizes a graph-based representation of the image and iteratively constructs a spanning forest by merging adjacent regions. We introduce a novel merging criterion based on the similarity between regions, which allows for the creation of compact and homogeneous superpixels. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed framework compared to state-of-the-art methods.

This  paper explores the relationship between Hirzebruch-type inequalities and plane curve  configurations. The authors investigate the   inequalities for configurations of curves in the plane and provide a detailed analysis of their properties.  They also establish connections between these inequalities and other geometric and  topological  properties of the curve configurations. The  results presented in this paper contribute  to   the understanding of  the interplay between Hirzebruch-type inequalities  and  plane curve configurations, and have potential applications in various areas of   mathematics and physics.

We consider the wave equation on a manifold $(\Omega,g)$ of dimension $d\geq
2$ with smooth strictly convex boundary $\partial\Omega\neq\emptyset$, with
Dirichlet boundary conditions. We construct a sharp local in time parametrix
and then proceed to obtain dispersion estimates: our fixed time decay rate for
the Green function exhibits a $t^{1/4}$ loss with respect to the boundary less
case. We precisely describe where and when these losses occur and relate them
to swallowtail type singularities in the wave front set, proving that our decay
is optimal. Moreover, we derive better than expected Strichartz estimates,
balancing lossy long time estimates at a given incidence with short time ones
with no loss: for $d=3$, it heuristically means that, on average the decay loss
is only $t^{1/6}$.

We investigate general aspects of the mass defects of strange stars in the
context of the Field Correlator Method, without magnetic field. 

The main
parameters of the model that enter the corresponding nonperturbative equation
of state of the quark gluon plasma are the gluon condensate $G_2$ and the large
distance static $Q{\bar Q}$ potential $V_1$. We calculate mass defects of
stellar configurations in the central density range $11<\log\rho_c<18$. In
general, the mass defects are strongly dependent on the model parameters. 

For a
large range of values of $G_2$ and $V_1$, we obtain anomalous mass defects with
magnitudes around $10^{53}\,$erg\,, of the same order of the observed energies
of gamma-ray bursts and neutrino emissions in SN1987A, and of the theoretically
predicted energies of the quark-novae explosions.

This paper proposes a novel approach for compressing 3D medical images and accurately segmenting them in cloud-based environments using machine vision techniques. The proposed method combines advanced compression algorithms with deep learning-based image segmentation models to achieve efficient transmission and accurate segmentation of medical images. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in reducing the size of medical images while preserving important diagnostic information, as well as achieving high segmentation accuracy in a cloud-based environment. The proposed method has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image analysis and transmission in cloud-based healthcare systems.

Crowd segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision due to the complex and crowded nature of the scenes. In this paper, we propose a fully convolutional neural network (FCN) architecture for crowd segmentation. The proposed network leverages the power of deep learning and utilizes a fully convolutional architecture to learn pixel-wise crowd segmentation. We evaluate our approach on multiple publicly available crowd datasets and compare our results with existing state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our FCN model, outperforming other approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Additionally, we provide insights into the learned representations and analyze the effects of various network architectures and parameters. Overall, our work contributes to the field of crowd segmentation and demonstrates the potential of fully convolutional neural networks for this challenging task.

Let $k$ a field of characteristic zero. Let $X$ be a smooth, projective,
geometrically rational $k$-surface. Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a universal torsor
over $X$ with a $k$-point et $\mathcal{T}^c$ a smooth compactification of
$\mathcal{T}$. There is an open question: is $\mathcal{T}^c$ $k$-birationally
equivalent to a projective space? We know that the unramified cohomology groups
of degree 1 and 2 of $\mathcal{T}$ and $\mathcal{T}^c$ are reduced to their
constant part. For the analogue of the third cohomology groups, we give a
sufficient condition using the Galois structure of the geometrical Picard group
of $X$. This enables us to show that
$H^{3}_{nr}(\mathcal{T}^{c},\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}(2))/H^3(k,\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}(8))$
vanishes if $X$ is a generalised Ch\^atelet surface and that this group is
reduced to its $6$-primary part if $X$ is a del Pezzo surface of degree at
least 7.

We propose  a general framework  to  build  certified proofs of distributed
self-stabilizing  algorithms with the proof assistant Coq. We first define in
Coq the locally shared memory model with composite  atomicity,   the most commonly
used model in the self-stabilizing area.  We  then validate our framework by
certifying a non  trivial part of an existing silent self-stabilizing algorithm
which  builds a $k$-clustering of  the network. We also certify a quantitative
property related  to the output of this algorithm. Precisely, we show that the
computed $k$-clustering contains at  most  $\lfloor \frac{n-1}{k+1} \rfloor + 1$
clusterheads, where $n$ is the number of nodes in the network. To obtain  these
results, we also  developed a library which contains   general tools  related  to
potential functions and  cardinality of sets.

This paper describes a novel algorithm for the problem of structural image
segmentation through an interactive model-based method. Interaction is
reflected in the model creation, which is done according to user traces drawn
over a given output image. Both model and output are then represented by means of
attributed relational graphs based on the fly. Appearance features are taken
into account as object characteristics and structural properties are expressed as
relational characteristics. To cope with possible topological similarities between
both graphs, a new structure called the deformation graph is adopted. The
segmentation process corresponds to obtaining a labelling of the output graph that
minimizes the deformations introduced in the model when it is updated with
input data. This method has shown to be better than other segmentation
approaches, with competitive input quality. Moreover, the approach solves the
issue of multiple label segmentation in an effective manner. Encouraging results
on both natural and target-specific color images, as well as examples demonstrating
the reusability of the model, are described and discussed.

Deep structured output learning shows tremendous promise in tasks like semantic
image segmentation. We proffer a new, efficient deeply structured model learning
scheme, in which we show how deep Convolutional Neural Systems (CNNs) can be
designed to estimate the messages in message passing inference for structured
prediction with Conditional Random Field (CRFs). With such CNN message
estimators, we obviate the need to find or evaluate potential functions for
message analysis. This confers considerable efficiency for learning, because
otherwise when conducting structured learning for a CRF with CNN potentials it
is possible to undertake expensive inference for each stochastic gradient
iteration. The network output dimension for message estimation is the same as
the number of classes, in comparison to the network output for general CNN
potential functions in CRFs, which is exponential in the order of the
potentials. Thus CNN message learning has more network constraints and is more
efficient for situations that a small number of classes are involved. We apply our
approach to semantic image segmentation on the PASCAL VOC 2012 database. We
achieve an intersection-over-union score of 73.4 on its test set, which is the
highest reported outcome for methods utilizing the VOC training images alone. This
excellent performance shows the reliability and validity of our CNN
message learning approach.

Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in computer  vision that requires accurate pixel-level  classification  of an image. In this paper, we propose a  novel method for iterative refinement of densely connected representation levels for semantic segmentation. Our approach  leverages  the benefits of  dense   connections to propagate information across levels and achieves  state-of-the-art results on several benchmark datasets.  We first introduce a dense connection  module that enables efficient information  flow between feature  maps. We then propose a cascade architecture that progressively refines the segmentation results   by   iteratively updating  the dense connections and feature maps.  Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, surpassing existing approaches in terms  of both accuracy and  computational  efficiency. Overall, our work contributes  to the ongoing research  in semantic segmentation and provides  insights into the potential of dense connections for this  task.

This paper proposes a novel approach for super-realtime facial landmark detection and shape fitting using deep regression of shape model parameters. The method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to directly regress the shape model parameters from a given image. By leveraging the characteristics of the shape model, such as shape priors and shape variations, the proposed approach achieves accurate and robust facial landmark detection even in challenging conditions (e.g., occlusions, significant pose variations, and low-resolution images). Experimental evaluation on several benchmark datasets demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in terms of both accuracy and speed. The super-realtime nature of the proposed approach makes it suitable for real-time applications, such as face tracking, facial expression analysis, and augmented reality.

This paper proposes a few-shot brain segmentation method using deep heteroscedastic multi-task networks trained on weakly labeled data. The authors address the challenge of limited annotated data for brain segmentation by leveraging weak labels and few-shot learning techniques. They introduce a novel heteroscedastic multi-task network architecture that can handle uncertainty in the weak labels and learn from limited annotated data. The proposed method is evaluated on a publicly available brain segmentation dataset and achieves competitive results compared to state-of-the-art methods. The findings suggest that the proposed approach can effectively leverage weakly labeled data for few-shot brain segmentation tasks.

In this paper, we present an overview of modern convex optimization techniques applied to medical image analysis. Convex optimization has emerged as a powerful tool in various fields, including medical image analysis, due to its ability to find global optima and its efficiency in solving large-scale optimization problems. We discuss the application of convex optimization to various tasks in medical image analysis such as image denoising, image registration, image segmentation, and image reconstruction. We also highlight several key algorithms and methods that have been developed for these tasks, including convex relaxation, non-convex relaxations, and distributed optimization. Finally, we provide a discussion on the challenges and future directions in the application of convex optimization to medical image analysis, including the incorporation of deep learning and the development of new optimization frameworks.

This paper introduces the concept of ordered exchange graphs, which are a variation of the traditional exchange graphs used in combinatorial optimization problems. Ordered exchange graphs are designed to capture the inherent ordering of elements in a problem setting, allowing for a more accurate representation and analysis of the problem. The paper presents the formal definition of ordered exchange graphs and discusses their properties and applications in various optimization problems. Additionally, the paper proposes a novel algorithm for constructing ordered exchange graphs and evaluates its performance on a set of benchmark problems. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of ordered exchange graphs in improving the efficiency and accuracy of optimization algorithms. Overall, this paper contributes to the field of combinatorial optimization by introducing a new graph representation and algorithmic technique that can be applied to a wide range of optimization problems.

Most of the advances in semantic segmentation have been achieved with daytime images with good lighting conditions. Here we address the problem of semantic segmentation of nighttime images and improve the state-of-the-art by adapting daytime models to nighttime images without using nighttime annotations. Moreover, we design a new evaluation framework to address the great uncertainty in the semantics of nighttime images. The main contributions are a curriculum framework that progressively adapts daytime semantic models to nighttime images through annotated synthetic images and unannotated real images taken at darker and darker times of day, which learns to use the correspondences between different times of day to determine the labels of the real images, and an uncertainty-aware annotation and evaluation framework, designed for nighttime images, which includes regions of images beyond human perception. Our experiments on real images show that our guided curriculum adaptation outperforms existing methods on both standard and uncertainty-aware metrics. We also show that selectively invalidating predictions can lead to better performance in the presence of uncertainty, which can benefit safety-related applications that involve the presence of invalid inputs.

This paper presents a method for segmenting images of humans using parametric shape priors. The method utilizes a parametric shape model to represent the structural characteristics of human body parts. The image segmentation is performed by fitting the shape model to the image data. The method can handle images with varying backgrounds and lighting conditions. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting human images. The proposed approach shows promise for applications such as human tracking, activity recognition, and virtual reality.

A quantum edge detector for image segmentation in optical environments is
presented in this work. A Boolean version of the same detector is presented
too. The quantum version of the new edge detector works with computational
basis states, exclusively. This way, we can easily avoid the problem of quantum
measurement retrieving the result of applying the new detector on the image.
Besides, a new criterion and logic based on projections onto vertical axeis of
Bloch's Sphere exclusively are presented too. This approach will allow us: 1) a
simpler development of logic quantum operations, where they will closer to
those used in the classical logic operations, 2) building simple and robust
classical-to-quantum and quantum-to-classical interfaces. Said so far is
extended to quantum algorithms outside image processing too. In a special
section on metric and simulations, a new metric based on the comparison between
the classical and quantum versions algorithms for edge detection of images is
presented. Notable differences between the results of classical and quantum
versions of such algorithms (outside and inside of quantum computer,
respectively) show the existence of implementation problems involved in the
experiment, and that they have not been properly modelled for optical
environments. However, although they are different, the quantum results are
equally valid. The latter is clearly seen in the computer simulations

In this paper, we study the structure and cohomology of moduli spaces of formal modules. We begin by introducing the notion of a formal module and its associated moduli space. We then investigate the structure of these moduli spaces, including their dimension and smoothness properties. Next, we compute the cohomology groups of these moduli spaces using various techniques, such as the Leray spectral sequence and the Grothendieck spectral sequence. We also establish connections between the cohomology of moduli spaces of formal modules and other areas of algebraic geometry, such as the cohomology of moduli spaces of vector bundles. Finally, we apply our results to the study of deformation theory and the classification of formal groups. Overall, our work provides a comprehensive understanding of the structure and cohomology of moduli spaces of formal modules, and sheds light on their connections to other areas of algebraic geometry.

Ultra-high resolution photo segmentation has raised increasing interests in
recent decades due to its realistic applications. In this paper, we innovate the
commonly used high-resolution photo segmentation pipeline, in which an ultra-high
resolution photo is partitioned into regular patches for local segmentation and
then the local results are merged into a high-resolution semantic mask. In
particular, we introduce a novel locality-aware contextual correlation based
segmentation model to process regional patches, where the relevance between local
patch and its other contexts are jointly and complementarily applied to
handle the semantic regions with wide differences. Specifically, we present a
semantic syntax refinement network that associates the local segmentation
result with its semantic semantics, and therefore is endowed with the capability of
removing boundary artifacts and improving mask contours during the generation of
final high-resolution mask. Thus, in comprehensive tests, we
demonstrate that our model outperforms other state-of-the-art approaches in public
benchmarks. Our released codes are accessible at
http://github.com/liqiokkk/FCtL.

This paper presents a novel approach  for visualising radiology  data  using holographic technology and automating medical image  segmentation through machine learning algorithms. The  authors propose a system that allows users to view  and interact with radiology data in a three-dimensional holographic space, enabling a  more intuitive interpretation of complex  medical images. Furthermore, they introduce   an automated machine learning-based approach for segmenting medical images, leveraging a large dataset of annotated  images to train the  model.  The  authors  evaluate the performance of their system and compare it with conventional methods, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing  the visualisation and segmentation of radiology data.  Overall,  this paper provides  valuable insights into the potential  of holographic technology  and  machine learning for improving the  analysis and interpretation of medical images in the field of radiology.

We describe a Fourier transform spectroscopy technique for directly measuring
band structures, and apply it to a spin-1 spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein
condensate. In our technique, we suddenly change the Hamiltonian of the system
by adding a spin-orbit coupling interaction and measure populations in
different spin states during the subsequent unitary evolution. We then
reconstruct the spin and momentum resolved spectrum from the peak frequencies
of the Fourier transformed populations. In addition, by periodically modulating
the Hamiltonian, we tune the spin-orbit coupling strength and use our
spectroscopy technique to probe the resulting dispersion relation. The
frequency resolution of our method is limited only by the coherent evolution
timescale of the Hamiltonian and can otherwise be applied to any system, for
example, to measure the band structure of atoms in optical lattice potentials.

Graphs are widely used to represent complex systems such as social networks, financial transactions, and biological interactions. Detecting anomalies in time series of graphs is an important problem in various domains. Traditional methods for anomaly detection often consider global statistics of the graph, which may overlook local abnormalities. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that leverages locality statistics for anomaly detection in time series of graphs. Specifically, we introduce a framework that uses graph embeddings to capture local structural information and then applies statistical techniques to identify anomalous patterns. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through experiments on real-world datasets, showing that it outperforms existing methods in detecting anomalies accurately and efficiently. Our findings suggest that considering locality statistics is crucial for achieving accurate anomaly detection in time series of graphs.

Automated medical image segmentation, specifically using deep learning, has
shown outstanding performance in semantic segmentation tasks. However, these
methods rarely quantify their uncertainty, which may lead to errors in
downstream analysis. In this work we propose to use Bayesian neural networks to
quantify uncertainty within the domain of semantic segmentation. We also
propose a method to convert voxel-wise segmentation uncertainty into volumetric
uncertainty, and calibrate the accuracy and reliability of confidence intervals
of derived measurements. When applied to a tumour volume estimation
application, we demonstrate that by using such modelling of uncertainty, deep
learning systems can be made to report volume estimates with well-calibrated
error-bars, making them safer for clinical use. We also show that the
uncertainty estimates extrapolate to unseen data, and that the confidence
intervals are robust in the presence of artificial noise. This could be used to
provide a form of quality control and quality assurance, and may permit further
adoption of deep learning tools in the clinic.

RatLesNetv2 is a fully convolutional network designed for the segmentation of brain lesions in rodent models. The network architecture is based on the U-Net model and incorporates dilated convolutions and residual connections to improve the segmentation accuracy. The network was trained and evaluated on a large dataset of rodent brain MRI scans with manually annotated lesion masks. The results demonstrate that RatLesNetv2 outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed network has the potential to facilitate the study of brain lesions in rodent models and improve the understanding of neurological disorders.

Label  smoothing is a commonly used technique in neural network  training that promotes robustness and generalization by introducing a small amount of uncertainty in  the    ground truth labels.  However, traditional  label smoothing methods treat all data points equally, without considering  the  inherent uncertainty that may vary across different regions of the input space. In this paper, we propose  a novel  approach called Spatially Varying Label Smoothing (SVLS) that  captures the uncertainty in expert  annotations on  a spatially varying basis.  Our method utilizes the spatial information from the input data to guide the  smoothing process, allowing for  more accurate  modeling of uncertainty and better performance in downstream tasks.   We demonstrate  the effectiveness of SVLS  on several benchmark datasets and show that it outperforms  traditional label  smoothing methods  in terms of both overall accuracy and uncertainty estimation.  Our findings highlight  the importance   of spatially varying uncertainty modeling and suggest that  SVLS can be a valuable tool in various domains where expert  annotations are used.

Semantic segmentation of  high-resolution satellite imagery is a challenging  task due to the presence of fine-grained  details and large spatial extent.  In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called  PP-LinkNet for improving the accuracy of semantic segmentation in high-resolution  satellite imagery. PP-LinkNet  combines the  advantages  of  both LinkNet and Pyramid Pooling modules to effectively capture  both local and global contextual information. Additionally, we introduce a multi-stage training strategy that progressively refines    the segmentation results by leveraging the knowledge learned  from  previous stages. Experimental results on benchmark datasets   demonstrate that PP-LinkNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. The proposed architecture and training  strategy have the potential to significantly improve the  performance  of semantic segmentation in  high-resolution  satellite  imagery applications.

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into multiple regions based on their visual characteristics. Traditional methods for image segmentation often rely on hand-engineered features and heuristic algorithms, which may struggle to capture complex patterns and variations in real-world images. In this paper, we propose a novel image segmentation technique using overlapping group sparsity. We formulate the problem of image segmentation as a sparse coding problem, where each image patch is represented as a linear combination of a few prototype patches. To encourage spatial consistency and preserve image structures, we introduce an overlapping group sparsity regularization term that encourages neighboring patches to have similar representations. We solve the resulting optimization problem using an iterative algorithm that alternates between updating the representation and updating the prototype patches. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art image segmentation techniques while requiring fewer assumptions and prior knowledge about image structures. Our approach also exhibits robustness to noise and occlusions, making it suitable for various real-world applications.

Automata with monitor counters, where the transitions do not depend on
counter values, and nested weighted automata are two expressive
automata-theoretic frameworks for quantitative properties. For a well-studied
and wide class of quantitative functions, we establish that automata with
monitor counters and nested weighted automata are equivalent. We study for the
first time such quantitative automata under probabilistic semantics. We show
that several problems that are undecidable for the classical questions of
emptiness and universality become decidable under the probabilistic semantics.
We present a complete picture of decidability for such automata, and even an
almost-complete picture of computational complexity, for the probabilistic
questions we consider.

This paper proposes a  novel algorithm,  called the Multi-Plane Block-Coordinate Frank-Wolfe (MP-BCFW) algorithm,  for training Structural Support Vector Machines (SVMs)  with a costly max-Oracle.  The  max-Oracle is a key component in  the training process of Structural SVMs, but it  can be computationally expensive  to compute.  The MP-BCFW algorithm  addresses this issue by  introducing a multi-plane block-coordinate strategy that reduces the number  of max-Oracle calls required during training. The  algorithm  iteratively updates the  model parameters by solving a series  of subproblems  on different planes, each   of which corresponds to a different subset of the training data. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets   demonstrate that the MP-BCFW algorithm achieves comparable performance to  existing methods while significantly reducing the computational cost of  the max-Oracle.

From the autonomous vehicle driving to clinical diagnosis, the requirement of the
task of image segmentation is everywhere. Segmentation of an image is one of
the important functions in computer vision. This task is comparatively
complicated than other vision functions as it needs low-level visual data.
So, image segmentation can be of two kinds: semantic segmentation and
instance segmentation. The combined version of these three basic functions is known
as panoptic segmentation. In the recent era, the success of deep convolutional
neural networks (CNN) has affected the field of segmentation greatly and brought
you many successful models to date. In this study, we are trying to get a
look at the evolution of both semantic and instance segmentation work based
on CNN. We have also specified comparative architectural descriptions of some
state-of-the-art prototypes and discuss their training details to present a lucid
interpretation of hyper-parameter tuning of those models. We have therefore drawn a
similarity among the performance of those models on other datasets. Also,
we have taken a glimpse of some state-of-the-art panoptic segmentation models.

Picture segmentation is a fundamental and challenging issue in computer
vision with applications spanning many sectors, such as scientific imaging,
remote sensing, and autonomous vehicles. Recently, convolutional neural
systems (CNN) have acquired traction in the construction of automated segmentation
pipelines. While CNN-based models are adept at learning abstract features
from raw image data, their efficiency is dependent on the availability and
size of appropriate training datasets. However, these models are generally able
to capture the details of object boundaries and generalize poorly to unseen
classes. In this thesis, we devise novel approaches that address these
problems and develop sophisticated representation learning structures for
fully-automatic semantic segmentation in scientific imaging and mainstream
computer vision. In particular, our contributions include (1) state-of-the-art
2D and 3D image segmentation systems for computer vision and medical imagery
research, (2) an end-to-end trainable image segmentation framework that incorporates
CNNs and active contour models with learnable parameters for fast and stable
object delineation, (3) a novel method for disentangling edge and texture
processing in segmentation systems, and (4) a novel few-shot learning model in
both supervised settings and semi-supervised settings where synergies between
latent and image spaces are leveraged to try to segment images given limited
training data.

In  this paper, we  present a demonstration of spectral level reconstruction of intrinsic $B$-mode   power. We propose a novel method that  allows for  the reconstruction of the intrinsic $B$-mode power  spectrum  from temperature and polarization data. Our method involves decomposing the   power spectrum  into a sum of spectral components and calibrating  these components  using known theoretical models. We show that our method can accurately  reconstruct the intrinsic $B$-mode power spectrum, thereby   providing valuable insights into the underlying physics of the cosmic microwave background  radiation. Overall, our demonstration highlights the potential  of spectral level reconstruction  as a powerful tool for analyzing and  interpreting large-scale cosmological  data sets.

In this paper, we mainly study stability of iterated polynomials and
linear transformations preserving the strong $q$-log-convexity of polynomials
  Let $[T_{n,k}]_{n,k\geq0}$ be an array of nonnegative numbers. We give some
criteria for linear transformation $$y_n(q)=\sum_{k=0}^nT_{n,k}x_k(q)$$
preserving strong $q$-log-convexity (resp. log-convexity). As applications,
we derive that some linear transformations (for instance, Stirling
transformations of two kinds, the Jacobi-Stirling transformations of two kinds,
the Legendre-Stirling transformations of two kinds, the central factorial
transformations, and so on) preserve strong $q$-log-convexity (resp.
log-convexity) in a unified manner. In particular, we confirm a conjecture of
Lin and Zeng, and extend some results of Chen {\it et al.}, and Zhu for strong
$q$-log-convexity of polynomials, and some results of Liu and Wang for
transformations preserving the log-convexity.
  The stability property of iterated polynomials implies $q$-log-convexity.
By applying method of interlacing of zeros, we also present two criteria
for stability of iterated Sturm sequences and $q$-log-convexity of
polynomials. As consequences, we get the stabilities of iterated Eulerian
polynomials of type $A$ and $B$, and their $q$-analogs. In addition, we also
prove that the generating functions of alternating runs of type $A$ and $B$,
the longest alternating subsequence and up-down runs of permutations form a
$q$-log-convex sequence, respectively.

In this paper, we present a method for accurately tracking the three-dimensional (3D) motion of colloidal particles undergoing Brownian motion. We use digital holographic microscopy (DHM) combined with a joint reconstruction algorithm to track the particles in 3D. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method by tracking the motion of different-sized colloidal particles and analyzing their diffusion behavior. Our results show that our tracking method is robust and provides accurate measurement of particle positions in 3D. This method has potential applications in the study of colloidal systems and can contribute to a deeper understanding of their behavior.

This paper examines the concept of edge-set graphs, which are graphical representations of a graph's edges. The authors focus on a specific type of graph known as certain graphs, and investigate the properties and characteristics of their edge-set graphs. By analyzing various properties, such as connectivity and edge-density, the authors provide insights into the relationships between certain graphs and their edge-set graphs. The findings of this study contribute to a deeper understanding of the structure and connectivity of certain graphs, and offer potential applications in fields such as network analysis and optimization.

The paper presents a proof that the $\pi$-calculus, a process calculus used for modeling concurrent and distributed systems, is both behaviourally complete and orbit-finitely executable. Behavioural completeness means that the $\pi$-calculus can express any computable behaviour, while orbit-finite executability means that any $\pi$-calculus process can be executed in a finite number of steps. The proof is based on a novel encoding of the $\pi$-calculus into a variant of the $\lambda$-calculus, which allows for the translation of $\pi$-calculus processes into executable $\lambda$-calculus terms. The paper also discusses the implications of these results for the practical use of the $\pi$-calculus in the design and analysis of concurrent and distributed systems.

Deep convolutional neural networks have shown outstanding performance in
medical image segmentation tasks. The usual problem when training supervised
deep learning methods is the lack of labeled data which is time-consuming and
costly to obtain. In this paper, we propose a novel uncertainty-guided
semi-supervised learning based on a student-teacher approach for training the
segmentation network using limited labeled samples and a large number of
unlabeled images. First, a teacher segmentation model is trained from the
labeled samples using Bayesian deep learning. The trained model is used to
generate soft segmentation labels and uncertainty maps for the unlabeled set.
The student model is then updated using the softly segmented samples and the
corresponding pixel-wise confidence of the segmentation quality estimated from
the uncertainty of the teacher model using a newly designed loss function.
Experimental results on a retinal layer segmentation task show that the
proposed method improves the segmentation performance in comparison to the
fully supervised approach and is on par with the expert annotator. The proposed
semi-supervised segmentation framework is a key contribution and applicable for
biomedical image segmentation across various imaging modalities where access to
annotated medical images is challenging

In this paper, we investigate the dynamics of two driven, dissipative, nonlinear cavities coupled with single and two-photon exchange. We analyze  the spin squeezing, entanglement, and coherence properties of the system  under different driving and dissipation conditions. We find that the system  exhibits rich  dynamics,  including the  generation of spin squeezing and entanglement, as well as the preservation of coherence. We also  explore the   effects of different  parameters on  these properties and  discuss potential  applications  of our findings  in quantum information processing and  quantum  metrology.

This paper presents a novel approach for visualizing radiology data using holographic technology and automating the process of medical image segmentation using machine learning algorithms. The authors propose a system that combines holographic displays with advanced machine learning techniques to enhance the interpretation and analysis of radiology images. The system utilizes a deep learning model to automatically segment medical images, reducing the time and effort required for manual segmentation. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through experiments and evaluations, showing improved accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional methods. The proposed system has the potential to revolutionize the field of radiology by providing a more intuitive and efficient way to visualize and analyze medical images.

Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning. However, existing segmentation frameworks often suffer from limited robustness and generalization, leading to unreliable results and reduced clinical utility. In this paper, we propose a novel approach towards a robust and generalized medical image segmentation framework. Our method leverages a combination of deep learning techniques, including convolutional neural networks and generative adversarial networks, to improve segmentation accuracy and generalization across different medical imaging modalities and datasets. We evaluate our framework on a diverse set of medical image datasets and demonstrate its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Our results suggest that our proposed framework has the potential to significantly enhance the reliability and clinical utility of medical image segmentation in various healthcare applications.

Accurately segmenting buildings in aerial imagery is a challenging task due to variations in building shapes, sizes, and textures. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end trainable deep active contour model for automated image segmentation. We leverage recent advancements in deep learning to enhance the traditional active contour model by incorporating convolutional and recurrent neural networks. Our model is trained on a large dataset of aerial imagery and is capable of accurately delineating buildings in unseen images. We evaluate the performance of our model against existing methods on a benchmark dataset, and demonstrate superior accuracy and efficiency. Our proposed approach has the potential to aid in various applications such as urban planning and disaster response.

This paper presents an active set algorithm for estimating parameters in generalized linear models with ordered predictors. The algorithm is designed to handle cases in which predictors are ordered and represent ordinal variables, such as Likert scale responses. The algorithm uses an iterative procedure to update both the parameter estimates and the active set of predictors, which are determined based on their contribution to the model fit. The performance of the algorithm is evaluated through simulations and compared to other existing methods. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm provides accurate and efficient parameter estimates, particularly in cases with a large number of predictors. The algorithm can be used in various fields where generalized linear models with ordered predictors are commonly employed, such as psychology, social sciences, and health research.

This paper presents a novel approach to information segmentation called Uniform Information Segmentation (UIS). UIS is a technique that aims to divide a given document into segments based on the uniformity of information within each segment. The proposed method utilizes a combination of statistical and linguistic features to identify boundaries between segments. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of UIS in accurately segmenting documents and outperforming existing segmentation methods. The paper also discusses the potential applications of UIS in information retrieval, document summarization, and other related tasks. Overall, this research contributes to the field of information segmentation by introducing a new approach that improves the accuracy and efficiency of segmenting documents.

Estimates of the Higgs and top quark masses, $m_{H} \simeq 125.10 \pm 0.14$
[GeV] and $m_{t} \simeq 172.76 \pm 0.30$ [GeV] based on the experimental
results place the Standard Model in the region of the metastable vacuum. 

A
consequence of the metastability of the Higgs vacuum is that it should induce
the decay of the electroweak vacuum in the early Universe with catastrophic
consequences. It may happen that certain universes were lucky enough to survive
the time of canonical decay, that is the exponential decay, and live longer. 

This means that it is reasonable to analyze conditions allowing for that. 

We
analyze properties of an ensemble of Universes with unstable vacua considered
as an ensemble of unstable systems from the point of view of the quantum theory
of unstable states. We found some symmetry relations for quantities
characterizing the metastable state. We also found a relation linking the decay
rate, ${\it\Gamma}$ of the metastable vacuum state with the Hubble parameter
$H(t)$,
  which may help to explain why a universe with an unstable vacuum that lives
longer then the canonical decay times need not decay.

We study the dynamics of the magnetization and the process of domain growth for the random-field Ising models with random fields with a uniform and a Gaussian distribution of different intensities. The size of the domain is determined directly by the Hoshen-Kopelman method. Both the magnetization and the largest domain size grow as a power law with the average value of the field and with an exponent whose value decays exponentially with increasing field intensity. In addition, for weak fields the relaxation obeys different regimes at initial and later times. There are no significant differences between the results obtained for the uniform and the Gaussian distributions, which confirms the universality assumption.

Semantic image  segmentation   is  an  important task in computer  vision, with applications ranging  from autonomous driving to  medical imaging. In this paper,  we propose a novel approach to improve semantic  image segmentation by incorporating  boundary  detection. We introduce a new edge-aware loss function  that penalizes  the misclassification of boundaries,  and we  develop a  new  network architecture that combines both semantic segmentation and edge detection. Our experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy, particularly in  the presence of complex and ambiguous boundaries. These findings  highlight the  benefits of integrating boundary detection into semantic image segmentation, and open up new possibilities for more  accurate  and robust scene understanding.

This paper presents a method for tracking the Brownian motion of colloidal particles in three dimensions using digital holographic microscopy and joint reconstruction. The authors propose a joint reconstruction algorithm that combines multiple holograms of the same particle to improve the accuracy of the tracking. The algorithm takes into account the diffraction effects and noise in the holograms to estimate the position and orientation of the particles. The authors validate the method using both simulated and experimental data, and demonstrate its ability to accurately track the motion of colloidal particles in three dimensions. The proposed method has potential applications in various fields, including biophysics and materials science.

Accurate medical image segmentation commonly requires effective learning of
the complementary information from multimodal data. 

However, in clinical
practice, we often encounter the problem of missing imaging modalities. We
tackle this challenge and propose a novel multimodal segmentation framework
which is robust to the absence of imaging modalities. Our network uses feature
disentanglement to decompose the input modalities into the modality-specific
appearance code, which uniquely sticks to each modality, and the
modality-invariant content code, which absorbs multimodal information for the
segmentation task. With enhanced modality-invariance, the disentangled content
code from each modality is fused into a shared representation which gains
robustness to missing data. 

The fusion is achieved via a learning-based
strategy to gate the contribution of different modalities at different
locations. We validate our method on the important yet challenging multimodal
brain tumor segmentation task with the BRATS challenge dataset. 

With
competitive performance to the state-of-the-art approaches for full modality,
our method achieves outstanding robustness under various missing modality(ies)
situations, significantly exceeding the state-of-the-art method by over 16% in
average for Dice on whole tumor segmentation.

This report provides an overview of the current state of the art deep
learning architectures and optimisation techniques, and uses the ADNI
hippocampus MRI dataset as an example to compare the effectiveness and
efficiency of different convolutional architectures on the task of patch-based
3-dimensional hippocampal segmentation, which is important in the diagnosis of
Alzheimer's Disease. We found that a slightly unconventional "stacked 2D"
approach provides much better classification performance than simple 2D patches
without requiring significantly more computational power. We also examined the
popular "tri-planar" approach used in some recently published studies, and
found that it provides much better results than the 2D approaches, but also
with a moderate increase in computational power requirement. Finally, we
evaluated a full 3D convolutional architecture, and found that it provides
marginally better results than the tri-planar approach, but at the cost of a
very significant increase in computational power requirement.

Urban facade segmentation from automatically acquired imagery, in contrast to
traditional image segmentation, poses several unique challenges. 360-degree
photospheres captured from vehicles are an effective way to capture a large
number of images, but this data presents difficult-to-model warping and
stitching artifacts. In addition, each pixel can belong to multiple facade
elements, and different facade elements (e.g., window, balcony, sill, etc.) are
correlated and vary wildly in their characteristics. In this paper, we propose
three network architectures of varying complexity to acheive multilabel
semantic segmentation of facade images while exploiting their unique
characteristics. Specifically, we propose a MULTIFACSEGNET architecture to
assign multiple labels to each pixel, a SEPARABLE architecture as a low-rank
formulation that encourages extraction of rectangular elements, and a
COMPATIBILITY network that simultaneously seeks segmentation across facade
element types allowing the network to 'see' intermediate output probabilities
of the various facade element classes. Our results on benchmark datasets show
significant improvements over existing facade segmentation approaches for the
typical facade elements. For example, on one commonly used dataset, the
accuracy scores for window(the most important architectural element) increases
from 0.91 to 0.97 percent compared to the best competing method, and comparable
improvements on other element types.

This paper presents a deep learning approach for estimating the recurrence of atrial fibrillation (AF) using an end-to-end framework. AF is a common cardiac arrhythmia that can lead to serious health complications. Accurate estimation of AF recurrence is crucial for guiding treatment decisions and monitoring patient outcomes. The proposed approach utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract features from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals and a recurrent neural network (RNN) to model temporal dependencies. The model is trained on a large dataset of ECG recordings from patients with known AF recurrence outcomes. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed deep learning approach achieves high accuracy in estimating AF recurrence, outperforming traditional machine learning methods. The findings suggest that deep learning techniques can provide valuable insights for predicting AF recurrence and improving patient care in clinical settings.

In this paper we analyze the Cardy-Lewellen equation in general diagonal
model. We show that in these models it takes simple form due to some general
properties of conformal field theories, like pentagon equations and OPE
associativity. This implies, that the Cardy-Lewellen equation has simple form
also in non-rational diagonal models. We specialize our finding to the
Liouville and Toda field theories. In particular we prove, that conjectured
recently defects in Toda field theory indeed satisfy the cluster equation. We
also derive the Cardy-Lewellen equation in all $sl(n)$ Toda field theories and
prove that the forms of boundary states found recently in $sl(3)$ Toda field
theory hold in all $sl(n)$ theories as well.

AinnoSeg is a deep learning-based approach for panoramic segmentation that achieves high performance on both speed and accuracy. Panoramic images require specialized segmentation methods due to their unique 360-degree field of view. AinnoSeg uses a fully convolutional network with a U-Net architecture to capture spatial and contextual information in panoramic images. It incorporates an attention mechanism to prioritize important regions for better segmentation results. Additionally, AinnoSeg introduces a new loss function that combines focal loss and IoU loss to improve accuracy. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that AinnoSeg outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy, while also achieving faster processing times. This makes it a valuable tool for applications such as panoramic image editing and virtual reality content creation.

This academic paper presents a novel method for joint segmentation and localization in videos and images by introducing the concept of foreground clustering. The proposed method first generates a set of candidate segment proposals using a pre-trained convolutional neural network. Then, a foreground clustering algorithm is applied to group these proposals into coherent foreground objects. This clustering algorithm utilizes both appearance and motion cues to capture the spatio-temporal coherence of the foreground objects. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method in accurately segmenting and localizing foreground objects in videos and images. This method has potential applications in computer vision tasks such as video object segmentation, object tracking, and scene understanding.

Automatic parsing of anatomical objects in X-ray images is important to several
scientific systems in particular towards image-guided invention and workflow
automation. Existing deep network models provide a substantial quantity of labeled
information. Moreover, maintaining precise pixel-wise labeling in X-ray images relies
largely on skilled researchers due to the wide overlaps of anatomy and the
complex color patterns. On the other hand, organs in 3D CT scans preserve
stronger structures as well as sharper boundaries and therefore can be readily
interpreted. In this paper, we propose a novel modeling framework for learning
automatic X-ray image parsing from labeled CT scans. Moreover, a Dense
Image-to-Image network (DI2I) for multi-organ segmentation is first trained on
X-ray like Digitally Reconstructed Radiographs (DRRs) rendered from 3D CT
volumes. Then we introduce a Task Driven Generative Adversarial Networks
(TD-GAN) design to achieve simultaneous style transfer and encoding for
unseen real X-ray pictures. TD-GAN consists of a modified cycle-GAN substructure
for pixel-to-pixel translation between DRRs and X-ray images and an additional
component using the pre-trained DI2I to enforce segmentation consistency. The
TD-GAN structure is general and can be readily adapted to other learning tasks.
In the numerical experiments, we validate the proposed model on 815 DRRs and
153 topograms. While the vanilla DI2I without any adaptation fails entirely
on segmenting the topograms, the proposed model does not provide any topogram
labels and is able to obtain a promising average dice of 85% which produces
the same level accuracy of supervised training (88%).

in this paper We start a global study of the parameter space (dissipation,
perturbation, frequency) of the dissipative spin-orbit problem in Celestial
Mechanics with the Aim of delimiting regions where the dynamics, or at least
some of its important features, is determined. This is done via a study of the
corresponding family of time $2\pi$-maps. In the same spirit as Chenciner in
his 1895 article on bifurcations Of elliptic fixed points, we are at first
interested in delimiting regions where the normal hyperbolicity is sufficiently
important to guarantee the persistence of an invariant attractive (resp.
repulsive) circle under Perturbation. As a tool, we use an analogue for
diffeomorphisms in this family of R\"ussmann's translated curve theorem in
analytic category.

To model recurrent interaction events in continuous time, an extension of the
stochastic block model is proposed where every individual belongs to a latent
group and interactions between two individuals follow a conditional
inhomogeneous Poisson process with intensity driven by the individuals' latent
groups. The model is shown to be identifiable and its estimation is based on a
semiparametric variational expectation-maximization algorithm. Two versions of
the method are developed, using either a nonparametric histogram approach (with
an adaptive choice of the partition size) or kernel intensity estimators. The
number of latent groups can be selected by an integrated classification
likelihood criterion. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of our procedure
on synthetic experiments, analyse two datasets to illustrate the utility of our
approach and comment on competing methods.

This paper explores the relationship between tail risk constraints and maximum entropy in financial portfolios. The authors propose a novel approach to portfolio optimization that incorporates tail risk constraints using a maximum entropy framework. They demonstrate that incorporating tail risk constraints can lead to improved portfolio performance, particularly during periods of market stress. The authors also provide empirical evidence supporting the effectiveness of their approach using historical data from various asset classes. Overall, this paper contributes to the literature on portfolio optimization by highlighting the importance of considering tail risk constraints and providing a practical framework for incorporating them into portfolio construction.

We present the design  and performance of a non-imaging concentrator for use
in broad-band polarimetry   at millimeter through  submillimeter wavelengths. A
rectangular geometry preserves the input polarization state as the concentrator
couples f/2 incident  optics  to a 2 pi sr detector. Measurements of the co-polar
and cross-polar  beams in both  the few-mode and highly over-moded  limits  agree
with a  simple model based on mode  truncation. The measured co-polar beam
pattern is nearly independent  of  frequency in both linear polarizations. The
cross-polar  beam  pattern is dominated by  a uniform term corresponding to
polarization efficiency 94%. After  correcting  for efficiency, the remaining
cross-polar response is -18 dB.

Image segmentation is a primary task in many medical applications. Recently,
many deep networks derived from U-Net have been extensively used in various
medical image segmentation tasks. However, in most of the cases, networks
similar to U-net produce coarse and non-smooth segmentations with lots of
discontinuities. To improve and refine the performance of U-Net like networks,
we propose the use of parallel decoders which along with performing the mask
predictions also perform contour prediction and distance map estimation. The
contour and distance map aid in ensuring smoothness in the segmentation
predictions. To facilitate joint training of three tasks, we propose a novel
architecture called Psi-Net with a single encoder and three parallel decoders
(thus having a shape of $\Psi$), one decoder to learns the segmentation mask
prediction and other two decoders to learn the auxiliary tasks of contour
detection and distance map estimation. The learning of these auxiliary tasks
helps in capturing the shape and the boundary information. We also propose a
new joint loss function for the proposed architecture. The loss function
consists of a weighted combination of Negative Log likelihood and Mean Square
Error loss. We have used two publicly available datasets: 1) Origa dataset for
the task of optic cup and disc segmentation and 2) Endovis segment dataset for
the task of polyp segmentation to evaluate our model. We have conducted
extensive experiments using our network to show our model gives better results
in terms of segmentation, boundary and shape metrics.

This paper presents a novel approach for the segmentation of medical imaging data using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The segmentation of medical images plays a crucial role in various clinical applications, such as tumor detection, organ localization, and treatment planning. However, the manual segmentation process is time-consuming and prone to inter-observer variability. To address these challenges, we propose a CNN-based segmentation method that can automatically learn the features and classify the pixels of medical images. The proposed approach consists of three main steps: data preprocessing, CNN training, and post-processing. In the data preprocessing step, we apply various preprocessing techniques to enhance the quality of the medical images. Then, we train a CNN model using a large dataset of annotated medical images. The trained CNN model can accurately classify the pixels of medical images into different anatomical structures or lesions. Finally, we employ post-processing techniques, such as morphological operations and conditional random fields, to refine the segmentation results and improve the overall accuracy. We evaluate the proposed approach on a publicly available dataset of brain MRI images, and the experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. The proposed CNN-based segmentation method has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation and facilitate various clinical applications.

Quantum random number  generators (QRNGs) have  gained significant attention due to their  inherent randomness and potential applications  in cryptography and simulation. However, existing  QRNG designs often suffer from  limitations such as  low speed,  high cost, and vulnerability to external disturbances. In this paper, we  propose a minimalist design for  a robust real-time QRNG that addresses  these limitations. Our design utilizes a single-photon source,  a beam splitter, and a single-photon detector, resulting  in a simple and cost-effective setup. We demonstrate the robustness of our design by  conducting extensive experiments under  various environmental  conditions and external  disturbances. The results   show that our QRNG achieves high-speed generation of random numbers with excellent statistical  properties,   while remaining resilient to external disturbances.  Our  minimalist design offers a promising solution for practical implementation of  QRNGs  in various applications.

It is known that the two-dimensional loop-erase random walk (LERW) is a random curve, whose continuum limit is a Schramm–Loewner evolution (SLE) with parameter kappa = 2. In this article we study the ‘off-critical’ random walks: random walks with a penalty function depending on the number of steps. On the one hand, we find counterparts of a number of LERW quantities in terms of symplectic fermions with c=-2, which enables us to advance towards a field-theoretic description of LERWs. On the other hand, we find a counterpart of the Loewner evolutions in the continuum limit of off-critical LERWs, thereby presenting an example of using SLE-like tools on models close to their critical point. Such a description is, of course, quite complex, because the finite correlation length outside the critical point precludes the use of conformal invariance. Our work shows that this question need not be intractable. We shall present the results with a special emphasis on the general features, which should be seen as relevant to other ‘off-critical’ models.

This paper presents a study on ranking users, papers, and authors in online scientific communities. The authors propose a novel ranking algorithm that takes into account various factors such as user activity, paper citations, and author reputation. The algorithm is evaluated on a large dataset from a popular online scientific community and compared with existing ranking methods. The results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms other methods in terms of accuracy and effectiveness. The findings of this study have implications for improving the visibility and credibility of users, papers, and authors in online scientific communities.

Over the past decade, Deep Convolutional Neural Networks have been widely
adopted for medical image segmentation and shown to achieve adequate
performance. However, due to the inherent inductive biases present in the
convolutional architectures, they lack understanding of long-range dependencies
in the image. Recently proposed Transformer-based architectures that leverage
self-attention mechanism encode long-range dependencies and learn
representations that are highly expressive. This motivates us to explore
Transformer-based solutions and study the feasibility of using
Transformer-based network architectures for medical image segmentation tasks.
Majority of existing Transformer-based network architectures proposed for
vision applications require large-scale datasets to train properly. However,
compared to the datasets for vision applications, for medical imaging the
number of data samples is relatively low, making it difficult to efficiently
train transformers for medical applications. To this end, we propose a Gated
Axial-Attention model which extends the existing architectures by introducing
an additional control mechanism in the self-attention module. Furthermore, to
train the model effectively on medical images, we propose a Local-Global
training strategy (LoGo) which further improves the performance. Specifically,
we operate on the whole image and patches to learn global and local features,
respectively. The proposed Medical Transformer (MedT) is evaluated on three
different medical image segmentation datasets and it is shown that it achieves
better performance than the convolutional and other related transformer-based
architectures. Code: https://github.com/jeya-maria-jose/Medical-Transformer

This paper presents a new approach to lung image segmentation using the fuzzy possibilistic C-means (FPCM) algorithm. Lung image segmentation is an important task in medical image analysis, as it plays a crucial role in the diagnosis and treatment of lung diseases. The proposed approach combines the advantages of both fuzzy clustering and possibilistic clustering, allowing for more accurate and robust segmentation results. The FPCM algorithm is modified to incorporate spatial information, which helps to preserve the shape and boundaries of lung structures. Experimental results on a dataset of lung CT images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, with improved segmentation accuracy compared to existing methods. The proposed approach has the potential to contribute to the development of computer-aided diagnosis systems for lung diseases.

3D image segmentation is one of the most important and ubiquitous problems in
medical image processing. It provides detailed quantitative analysis for
accurate disease diagnosis, abnormal detection, and classification. Currently
deep learning algorithms are widely used in medical image segmentation, most
algorithms trained models with full annotated datasets. 

However, obtaining
medical image datasets is very difficult and expensive, and full annotation of
3D medical image is a monotonous and time-consuming work. 

Partially labelling
informative slices in 3D images will be a great relief of manual annotation. Sample selection strategies based on active learning have been proposed in the
field of 2D image, but few strategies focus on 3D images. 

In this paper, we
propose a sparse annotation strategy based on attention-guided active learning
for 3D medical image segmentation. 

Attention mechanism is used to improve
segmentation accuracy and estimate the segmentation accuracy of each slice. The
comparative experiments with three different strategies using datasets from the
developing human connectome project (dHCP) show that, our strategy only needs
15% to 20% annotated slices in brain extraction task and 30% to 35% annotated
slices in tissue segmentation task to achieve comparative results as full
annotation.

The recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) combined with the
vast amount of data generated by today's medical applications, has contributed to the
implementation of imaging AI technologies throughout the entire value chain of clinical
imaging, including image reconstruction, clinical imagery segmentation,
image-based treatment and treatment planning. Notwithstanding the successes and
future potential of AI in clinical imaging, several stakeholders are concerned of
the potential risks and societal consequences of imaging AI technologies, which are
considered as complex, opaque, and impossible to comprehend, use, and trust
in critical medical systems. Besides these difficulties and challenges, there are
still no concrete policies and best practices for directing future AI
technologies in clinical imaging towards enhanced trust, safety and adoption.
To bridge this gap, this journal includes a careful choice of guiding
guidelines drawn from the accumulated insights, consensus, and best
practices from three big European projects on AI in Medical Systems. These
guiding concepts are named FUTURE-AI and its building blocks consist of (i)
Fairness, (ii) Universality, (iii) Traceability, (iv) Usability, (v) Robustness
and (vi) Explainability. In a step-by-step method, these recommendations are
further translated into a framework of concrete guidelines for identifying,
designing, implementing, and integrating technically, clinically and socially
trustworthy AI solutions into scientific practice.

This paper presents Ω-Net, a deep neural network framework for fully automatic detection, orientation, and segmentation of cardiac MR images in a multi-view setting. Ω-Net combines convolutional neural networks with recurrent neural networks to achieve accurate and robust performance in various cardiac imaging scenarios. The network is trained on a large dataset of annotated cardiac MR images and achieves state-of-the-art results in terms of detection, orientation, and segmentation accuracy. The proposed method has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of cardiac imaging analysis, leading to improved diagnostic outcomes in the field of cardiology.

This paper proposes a generative synthetic augmentation approach for nuclei image segmentation called Label-to-Image Translation (LIT). LIT utilizes a Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) to generate synthetic images that are similar to the original nuclei images. The approach incorporates both the input labels and the image content as input to the generator network, enabling it to generate more diverse and realistic synthetic images. The authors evaluate the performance of LIT on benchmark datasets for nuclei image segmentation and compare it with other augmentation techniques. The results show that LIT improves the performance of nuclei image segmentation models, achieving state-of-the-art results on the benchmark datasets. The authors also conduct ablation studies to analyze the effect of different components in LIT and provide insights into the underlying mechanisms. Overall, this paper presents an effective and novel approach for generative synthetic augmentation in the context of nuclei image segmentation.

Aggregating multi-level feature representation plays a critical role in
achieving robust volumetric medical image segmentation, which is important for
the auxiliary diagnosis and treatment. Unlike the recent neural architecture
search (NAS) methods that typically searched the optimal operators in each
network layer, but missed a good strategy to search for feature aggregations,
this paper proposes a novel NAS method for 3D medical image segmentation, named
UXNet, which searches both the scale-wise feature aggregation strategies as
well as the block-wise operators in the encoder-decoder network. UXNet has
several appealing benefits. (6) It significantly improves flexibility of the
classical UNet architecture, which only aggregates feature representations of
encoder and decoder in equivalent resolution. (2) A continuous relaxation of
UXNet is carefully designed, enabling its searching scheme performed in an
efficient differentiable manner. (3) Extensive experiments demonstrate the
effectiveness of UXNet compared with recent NAS methods for medical image
segmentation. The architecture discovered by UXNet outperforms existing
state-of-the-art models in terms of Dice on several public 8D medical image
segmentation benchmarks, especially for the boundary locations and tiny
tissues. The searching computational complexity of UXNet is cheap, enabling to
search a network with the best performance less than 1.5 days on two TitanXP
GPUs.

With a p-p bandgap of 2.15eV, a large carrier mobility and a strong valence effect, black phosphorus (P) has been suggested as a new two-dimensional two-dimensional semiconducting crystal with a large direct bandgap. The crystallinity of black phosphorus is sensitive to a variety of external influences that may cause a device to fail, even before the optical image of the device changes.
