Here we systematically study the effects of the environment on the black phosphorus crystals by recording the electrical characteristics of the devices for a month under various controlled conditions, including ambient light, air and humidity. We also analyzed the effects of different temperatures and currents on the structure, performance and failure mode of black P devices. These results show that the procedures developed for other two-dimensional materials cannot be applied directly to black P devices, and that an improved procedure must be developed to ensure the stability of the device.

Statistical photo characterization also depends on accurate classification of
pixels through a segmentation procedure. Also, imaging artifacts such as the
partial volume effect and detector noise complicate the classification procedure.
These effects increase the pixel frequency variation of each component class,
forcing intensities from one class to overlap with another. This reduced
variation makes threshold based segmentation methods ineffective due to
ambiguous overlap regions in the pixel frequency distributions. The class
ambiguity gets far more complex for structures with more than one
constituents, such as unsaturated moist granular media. In this paper, we
propose an image extraction workflow that ensures segmentation accuracy for
multiphase applications. Next, the ambiguous transition areas between classes are
identified and removed, which provides for global thresholding of single-class
regions. Then the transition states are identified using a distance function,
and then both segmentations are combined into one classified image. This
workflow provides two approaches for analyzing transition pixels and we
demonstrate on a range of synthetic images that these methods are unable to
effectively separate the ambiguous transition pixels from the single-class
areas. For situations with typical amounts of image noise, misclassification
errors and area variations calculated between each class of the synthetic
images and the resultant segmented images range from 0.69-1.48% and 0.01-0.74%,
respectively, indicating the segmentation accuracy of this technique. We
demonstrate that we are unable to efficiently segment x-ray microtomography images
of moist granular media employing these computationally efficient techniques.

This paper explores the dimensions of multi-fan algebras, which are a generalization of the classical fan algebras. The authors provide a comprehensive analysis of the dimensions of these algebras, including their relationship with the dimensions of the underlying fans. They also investigate the behavior of the dimensions under various operations on multi-fan algebras, such as taking direct sums and tensor products. The results obtained in this study contribute to a deeper understanding of multi-fan algebras and their properties.

We desgin a novel fully convolutional network architecture for shapes,
denoted by Shape Fully Convolutional Networks (SFCN). 3D shapes are represented
as graph structures in the SFCN architecture, based on novel graph convolution
and pooling operations, which are similar to convolution and pooling operations
used on images. Meanwhile, to build our SFCN architecture in the original image
segmentation fully convolutional network (FCN) architecture, we also design and
implement a generating operation} with bridging function. This ensures that the
convolution and pooling operation we have designed can be successfully applied
in the original FCN architecture. In this paper, we also present a new shape
segmentation approach based on SFCN. Furthermore, we allow more general and
challenging input, such as mixed datasets of different categories of shapes}
which can prove the ability of our generalisation. In our approach, SFCNs are
trained triangles-to-triangles by using three low-level geometric features as
input. Finally, the feature voting-based multi-label graph cuts is adopted to
optimise the segmentation results obtained by SFCN prediction. The experiment
results show that our method can effectively learn and predict mixed shape
datasets of either similar or different characteristics, and achieve excellent
segmentation results.

In this paper we propose a new class of Dynamic Mixture Models (DAMMs) being
able to sequentially adapt the mixture components as well as the mixture
composition using information comming from the data. The information driven
nature of the proposed class of models allows to exactly compute the full
likelihood and to avoid computer intensive simulation schemes. An extensive
Monte Carlo experiment reveals that the new proposed model can accurately
approximate the more complicated Stochastic Dynamic Mixture Model previously
introduced in the literature as well as other kind of models. The properties of
the new proposed class of models are discussed through the paper and an
application in financial econometrics is reported.

This paper investigates the tradeoff between stretch and length in geometric networks. The stretch of a path in a network is defined as the ratio of the length of the path in the network to the shortest path between the same two nodes. The length of a network is the sum of the lengths of all its edges. The authors analyze the average case and worst case scenarios for this tradeoff in geometric networks. They provide theoretical results and experimental evaluations to demonstrate the relationship between stretch and length in different network configurations. The findings of this study can be useful for designing efficient and reliable geometric networks.

The scaling properties of the time series are usually studied by the scaling laws of the empirical moments, which are time-averaged estimates of the moments of the dynamic variable. The presence of nonlinearities in the scaling laws of the empirical moments is usually regarded as a sign of multifractality of the data. We show that, with the exception of Brownian motion, this method does not reveal the true monofractal nature of the Lévy processes. We prove that, for this class of processes, the method introduces an apparent multifractality which can be described by a piecewise linear scaling function with two regimes, corresponding to the stability and the inertia of the process under investigation. This result is motivated by previous numerical results and is obtained by the introduction of a suitable normalization which can correct the empirical moments without hiding their dependence on time, in cases when the moments they estimate are not existent.

Information flow is the branch of security that studies the leakage of
information due to correlation Between secrets and observables. Since in
general such correlation cannot be avoided completely, it is important to
quantify the leakage. The most followed approaches to defining appropriate
measures are those based on information theory. In particular, one of the most
successful approaches is the recently proposed $g$-leakage framework, which
Encompasses most of the information-theoretic ones. A problem With $g$-leakage,
however, is that it is defined in terms of a minimization problem, which, in
the case of large Systems, Can be computationally rather heavy. In this paper
we study the case In which the channel Associated to the system can be
decomposed into Simpler channels, which typically happens when the observables
consist of multiple components. Our main contribution is the derivation of
bounds on the (multiplicative version of) $g$-leakage of the whole system in
terms of the $g$-leakages of its components. We also consider the particular
cases of min-entropy leakage and of parallel channels, generalizing And
systematizing results from the literature. We demonstrate the effectiveness of
our method and evaluate the precision of our bounds using examples.

Detection faults in seismic data is a crucial step for seismic structural
interpretation, reservoir characterization and well placement. Some recent
works regard it as an image segmentation task. The task of image segmentation
requires huge labels, especially 2D seismic data, which has a complex structure
and lots of noise. Therefore, its annotation requires expert experience and a
huge workload. In this study, we present lambda-BCE and lambda-smooth L1loss to
effectively train 3D-CNN by some slices from 8D seismic data, so that the model
can learn the segmentation of 1D seismic data from a few 2D slices. In order to
fully extract information from limited data and suppress seismic noise, we
propose an attention module that can be used for active supervision training
and embedded in the network. The attention heatmap label is generated by the
original label, and letting it supervise the attention module using the
lambda-smooth L1loss. The experiment demonstrates the effectiveness of our loss
function, the method can extract 3D seismic features from a few 9D slice
labels. And it also shows the advanced performance of the attention module,
which can significantly suppress the noise in the seismic data while increasing
the model's sensitivity to the foreground. Finally, on the public test set, we
only use the 2D slice labels training that accounts for 6.0% of the 3D volume
label, and achieve similar performance to the 3D volume label training.

This paper proposes a guided curriculum model adaptation approach coupled with an uncertainty-aware evaluation for the task of semantic nighttime image segmentation. The proposed approach leverages the concept of curriculum learning to gradually adapt the model to the challenging nighttime conditions by iteratively selecting and training on samples with increased difficulty. Additionally, an uncertainty estimation module is incorporated to evaluate the model's performance and guide the curriculum adaptation process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods for nighttime image segmentation, achieving state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets. The findings suggest the effectiveness of guided curriculum learning and uncertainty-aware evaluation in improving semantic nighttime image segmentation.

Visual saliency is a fundamental problem in both cognitive and computational
sciences, including computer vision. In this CVPR 2015 paper, we discover that
a high-quality visual saliency model can be trained with multiscale features
extracted using a popular deep learning architecture, convolutional neural
networks (CNNs), which have had many successes in visual recognition tasks. For
learning such saliency models, we introduce a neural network architecture,
which has fully connected layers on top of CNNs responsible for extracting
features at three different scales. We then propose a refinement method to
enhance spatial coherence of our saliency results. Finally, aggregating
multiple saliency maps computed for different levels of image segmentation can
further boost performance, yielding saliency maps better than those
generated from single segmentation. To promote further research and
evaluation of visual saliency models, we also construct a new large database of
4447 challenging images and their pixelwise saliency annotation. Experimental
results demonstrate that our proposed method is capable of achieving
state-of-the-art performance on all public benchmarks, improving F-Measure
by 5.0% and 13.2% respectively on MSRA-B dataset and our new dataset
(HKU-IS), and lowering the mean absolute error by 5.7% and 35.1% respectively
on these two datasets.

In this paper we describe a new mobile architecture, MobileNetV2, that
improves the state of  the art performance of mobile models on multiple tasks
and benchmarks as well as across a spectrum of different model sizes. We also
describe efficient ways  of applying  these  mobile models to object detection  in
a novel framework  we call SSDLite. Additionally, we demonstrate how to build
mobile semantic segmentation  models through a reduced form  of DeepLabv3 which
we  call Mobile  DeepLabv3.
   The MobileNetV2  architecture is based on an inverted residual structure where
the   input and output of the residual block are thin bottleneck layers  opposite
to traditional residual models which use  expanded representations in the input
an MobileNetV2 uses lightweight depthwise convolutions to filter features in
the intermediate expansion layer. Additionally, we  find that  it is important to
remove  non-linearities in the narrow layers  in order to maintain
representational power. We demonstrate  that this improves performance and
provide  an intuition  that led to this  design. Finally, our approach allows
decoupling of the input/output domains from  the expressiveness  of  the
transformation, which provides  a convenient framework for further  analysis. We
measure our performance  on Imagenet classification,  COCO object detection, VOC
image  segmentation. We evaluate the trade-offs between  accuracy,  and number of
operations measured by multiply-adds  (MAdd), as well   as    the number of
parameters

Semi-supervised learning (SSL) uses unlabeled data during training to learn
better models. Previous studies on SSL for medical image segmentation focused
mostly on improving model generalization to unseen data. In some applications,
however, our primary interest is not generalization but to obtain optimal
predictions on specific unlabeled database that is fully available during
model development. Examples include population studies for extracting imaging
phenotypes. This work investigates an often overlooked aspect of SSL,
transduction. It focuses on quality of predictions made on the unlabeled
data of interest when they are included for optimization during training,
rather than improving generalization. We focus on the self-training framework
and explore its potential for transduction. We analyze it through lens of
Information Gain and reveal that learning benefits from the use of calibrated
or under-confident models. Our extensive experiments on large MRI database
for multi-class segmentation of traumatic brain lesions shows promising results
when comparing transductive with inductive predictions. We believe this study
will inspire further research on transductive learning, a well-suited paradigm
for medical image analysis.

This paper presents  a novel approach for image segmentation using 3D models.  Traditional  image segmentation methods often struggle with complex scenes   and  objects due to the lack of contextual information. In this work, we propose to leverage 3D  models to assist the image segmentation process. We  first reconstruct a  3D model of  the scene or object using depth   information. Then, we use this 3D model to guide the image  segmentation algorithm by incorporating geometric constraints.  Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of  our approach  in  improving the accuracy and robustness of image segmentation,  especially  in challenging scenarios.  This work opens up new possibilities for leveraging 3D models  in computer  vision tasks and provides a  promising  direction for future research in image segmentation.

This paper investigates the algebraic dependence of commuting elements in algebras. Specifically, we study the conditions under which a set of commuting elements in an algebra is algebraically dependent. We provide necessary and sufficient conditions for algebraic dependence in various types of algebras, including commutative algebras, Lie algebras, and associative algebras. We also explore the relationship between algebraic dependence and other algebraic properties, such as the dimension of the algebra and the existence of a basis. Our results have implications for the study of algebraic structures and can be applied to various areas of mathematics and physics.

This paper proposes a novel unsupervised adaptation method, named Adapt Everywhere, for point-cloud-based multi-modal cardiac image segmentation. The method leverages the information contained in source and target point-clouds to adapt the source network to the target domain. The authors introduce an entropy minimization loss to encourage consistent predictions across different modalities and a global minimal entropy loss to regularize the adaptation process. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on two cardiac image datasets, outperforming existing approaches. The Adapt Everywhere method shows great potential for improving multi-modal cardiac image segmentation accuracy and generalizability.

In this paper, we study the spectral gap properties of the unitary groups and examine the results on non-commutative Sidon sets by Rider. We analyze the behavior of the spectral gap in the context of the unitary groups and investigate the implications of Rider's results. Specifically, we discuss the relationship between the spectral gap and the existence of non-commutative Sidon sets. Our findings contribute to the understanding of the spectral gap properties of the unitary groups and shed light on the connection between these properties and the existence of non-commutative Sidon sets.

The jeu de taquin process produced a standard Young tableau from a skew
standard Young tableau by shifting its entries to the northwest. We generalize
this process to posets: certain partial numberings of any poset are shifted
upward. A poset is said to have the jeu de taquin property if the numberings
resulting from this process do not depend upon certain choices made during the
process. Young diagrams are the posets which underlie standard Young tableaux.
These posets have the jeu de taquin property. d-Complete posets are posets
which satisfy certain local structual conditions. They are mutual
generalizations of Young diagrams, shifted Young diagrams, and rooted trees. We
prove that all d-complete posets have the jeu de taquin property. The proof
shows that each d-complete poset actually has the stronger "simultaneous"
property; this may lead to an algebraic understanding of the main result. A
partial converse is stated: "Non-overlapping" simultaneous posets are
d-complete.

The paper proposes a novel Kernelized image segmentation scheme for noisy
images that utilizes the concept of Smallest Univalue Segment Assimilating
Nucleus (SUSAN) and incorporates spatial constraints by computing circular
colour map induced weights. Fuzzy damping coefficients are obtained for each
nucleus or center pixel on the basis of the corresponding weighted SUSAN area
values, the weights being equal to the inverse of the number of horizontal and
vertical moves required to reach a neighborhood pixel from the center pixel.
These weights are used to vary the contributions of the different nuclei in the
Kernel based framework. The paper also presents an edge quality metric obtained
by fuzzy decision based edge candidate selection and final computation of the
blurriness of the edges after their selection. The inability of existing
algorithms to preserve edge information and structural details in their
segmented maps necessitates the computation of the edge quality factor (EQF)
for all the competing algorithms. Qualitative and quantitative analysis have
been rendered with respect to state-of-the-art algorithms and for images ridden
with varying types of noises. Speckle noise ridden SAR images and Rician noise
ridden Magnetic Resonance Images have also been considered for evaluating the
effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in extracting important segmentation
information.

This paper presents a novel deep learning approach called DeepEdge   for top-down contour detection.  The proposed method utilizes a multi-scale  bifurcated deep network architecture that combines both  global and local information to accurately detect object boundaries. The network consists of two branches, one for global context extraction  and the other for local feature learning. These   branches are then fused  at  multiple  scales to generate high-resolution contour  maps. Experimental results  on benchmark datasets demonstrate that DeepEdge outperforms  state-of-the-art methods in terms of contour detection accuracy. Additionally, the   proposed method  is computationally efficient,  making  it suitable for real-time applications.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial step in medical image analysis for diagnosis and treatment planning. In this paper, we propose a multi-modal convolutional neural network (CNN) based approach for medical image segmentation. The proposed approach utilizes multiple modalities of medical images to capture complementary information and improve the segmentation accuracy. We also investigate different image fusion schemes to integrate the information from multiple modalities. Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach and highlight the impact of different image fusion schemes on the segmentation performance. The proposed approach has the potential to enhance the accuracy and reliability of medical image segmentation, thereby benefiting clinical decision-making and patient care in the field of medical imaging.

In this work we   theoretically suggest and consider a realistic experiment of
single photon interference at beam splitter where micro-detector of the photon
trajectories is presented   by single atom. It admits  studying of the quantum
entanglement between photon and detector (Schr\"odinger cat effect) which
clearly demonstrates that detection procedure (collapse) has  no any absolute
character. Also  it admits   modeling  of the collapse by spontaneous
(non-dynamical) unitary symmetry  (superposition) breaking (effective  hiding) by
quantum-classical continuous phase transition. (Practically, collapse can be
considered as an especial case of   the general formalism   of spontaneous symmetry
breaking.) Finally  it  admits a simple solution of the quantum mechanics
foundation problem.

This paper proposes  a novel  approach for  end-to-end  training of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Conditional  Random Fields  (CRFs) using differentiable dual-decomposition. The   authors introduce a new  energy function that combines the CNN and  CRF potentials, and develop a  differentiable dual-decomposition algorithm  to optimize this energy function. They demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on various computer vision tasks, including image segmentation and object recognition, achieving  state-of-the-art performance. The proposed method allows for joint training  of CNNs and  CRFs, eliminating the need for separate   training and  inference steps, and enabling end-to-end optimization. The experimental results validate the superiority of the proposed approach over  existing methods, highlighting  its  potential  for advancing  the field of computer vision.

In this article, we examine the behavior of Riemannian and Hermitian
curvature tensors of Hermitian metric, when one of curvature tensors
obeys all the symmetry conditions of curvature tensor of a K\"ahler metric.
We will call such metrics G-K\"ahler-like or K\"ahler-like, for lack of better
terminologies. Such metrics are always balanced when the manifold is compact,
so in a way they are more special than balanced metrics, which drew a lot of
attention in the study of non-K\"ahler Calabi-Yau manifolds. In particular we
derive various formulas on difference between Riemannian and Hermitian
curvature tensors in terms of torsion of Hermitian connection. We
believe that these formulas could lead to further applications in the study of
Hermitian geometry with curvature assumptions.

This paper  presents a novel  approach for multi-modal image segmentation  using a hyper-densely connected  convolutional neural  network (CNN) called HyperDense-Net. The proposed network architecture  incorporates dense connections at  multiple levels  to enhance information  flow and improve segmentation accuracy. The HyperDense-Net is trained and  evaluated on a dataset consisting of multi-modal medical images,  achieving state-of-the-art  performance compared to existing  methods. The results demonstrate  the effectiveness of  the proposed approach in  accurately segmenting multi-modal images, highlighting its potential for various medical imaging applications.

This paper explores the phenomenon of a $\pi$ phase shift induced by interface anisotropy in the precession of magnetization initiated by laser heating. The authors investigate how the interaction between light and a magnetic material can lead to a change in the magnetization dynamics, specifically a $\pi$ phase shift. They conduct experiments using a custom-built setup and demonstrate the impact of varying laser parameters on the phase shift. The results suggest that interface anisotropy plays a significant role in this phenomenon and provide insights into the underlying physics. This research contributes to the understanding of magnetization dynamics and has potential implications for applications such as data storage and spintronics.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach for solving the constrained maximum a  posteriori (MAP) inference problem. We introduce the concept of  multi-dimensional parametric mincuts, which allows us to efficiently  explore the solution space while  satisfying  the   given constraints. Our method leverages the power of  mincuts to find the optimal solution  by iteratively updating the parameters and  performing mincut  computations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach  on various  benchmark  datasets and compare it with existing methods. The experimental results show  that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches in terms of   both accuracy and efficiency.  Overall, our work provides  a promising solution for solving the constrained  MAP inference  problem in multi-dimensional settings.

Increasing the Mini-batch size for stochastic gradient descent offers
significant opportunities to reduce wall-clock training time, but there are a
variety of theoretical and systems challenges that impede the widespread
success of This technique. We investigate these issues, with an emphasis on
time to convergence and total computational cost, through an extensive
Empirical analysis Of network training across several architectures and problem
domains, including image classification, image segmentation, and language
modeling. Although it is common practice to increase the batch size in order to
fully exploit available computational resources, we find a substantially more
nuanced picture. Our main finding is that across a wide range of network
architectures and problem domains, increasing the batch size beyond a certain
point yields no decrease in wall-clock time to convergence for \emph{either}
Train or test loss. This batch size is usually substantially below the capacity
of current systems. We show that popular training strategies for large Batch
size optimization Begin to fail before we can populate all available compute
resources, and we show that the point at which these methods break down Depends
more on attributes like model architecture and Data complexity than it does
directly on the size of the dataset.

This paper presents a novel approach for adapting semantic image segmentation models from daytime to nighttime conditions. The proposed method, called Dark Model Adaptation, leverages a combination of domain adaptation techniques and image enhancement algorithms to effectively transfer knowledge from daytime images to nighttime images. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach through extensive experiments on various datasets and show that the adapted models achieve comparable performance to models trained directly on nighttime data. The results suggest that Dark Model Adaptation can be a valuable tool for improving the performance of semantic image segmentation models in low-light conditions.

This paper proposes  a method for  cross-modal progressive comprehension in the  context of referring segmentation. Referring segmentation aims to locate and segment a specific  object in an image given a   natural  language   description. The proposed method takes  advantage  of  both visual and textual information  to progressively refine the object  segmentation. The approach consists of two key components: a cross-modal  attention module and a progressive segmentation module. The cross-modal attention module  learns to align  the visual and textual features by attending to relevant regions in the image  and text. The   progressive segmentation module uses the aligned  features to iteratively refine the  object segmentation. The experimental results on benchmark datasets  demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms several state-of-the-art techniques  in terms of object segmentation accuracy while being more  interpretable and explainable.

Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) of nanoscale objects in their native
conditions and at different temperatures are of critical importance in
revealing details of their interactions with ambient environments. Currently
available environmental capsules are equipped with thin electron transparent
membranes and allow imaging the samples at atmospheric pressure. However these
capsules do not provide the temperature control over the sample. Here we
developed and tested a thermoelectric cooling / heating setup for available
environmental capsules to allow ambient pressure in situ SEM studies over the
-53 {\deg}C to 100 {\deg}C temperature range in gaseous, liquid, and frozen
environments. The design of the setup also allows correlation of the SEM with
optical microscopy and spectroscopy. As a demonstration of the possibilities of
the developed approach, we performed real-time in situ microscopy studies of
water condensation on a surface of wing scales of Morpho sulkowskyi butterfly.
We have found that the initial water nucleation takes place on the top of the
scale ridges. These results confirmed earlier discovery of a polarity gradient
of the ridges of Morpho butterflies. Our developed thermoelectric cooling /
heating setup for available SEM environmental capsules promises to impact
diverse needs for in-situ nano-characterization including materials science and
catalysis, micro-instrumentation and device reliability, chemistry and biology.

A single-elimination (SE) tournament is a popular way to select a winner in
both sports competitions and in elections. A natural and well-studied question
is the tournament fixing problem (TFP): given the set of all pairwise match
outcomes, can a tournament organiser rig an SE tournament by adjusting the
initial seeding so that their favourite player wins? We prove new sufficient
conditions on the pairwise match outcome information and the favourite player,
under which there is guaranteed to be a seeding where the player wins the
tournament. Our results greatly generalise previous results. We also
investigate the relationship between the set of players that can win an SE
tournament under some seeding (so called SE winners) and other traditional
tournament solutions. In addition, we generalise and strengthen prior work on
probabilistic models for generating tournaments. For instance, we show that
\emph{every} player in an $n$ player tournament generated by the Condorcet
Random Model will be an SE winner even when the noise is as small as possible,
$p=\Theta(\ln n/n)$; prior work only had such results for $p\geq
\Omega(\sqrt{\ln n/n})$. We also establish new results for significantly more
general generative models.

This paper presents a series of experiments conducted to increase the used energy with the PEGASUS railgun. The railgun is a type of electromagnetic launcher that uses magnetic fields to accelerate projectiles to high velocities. The goal of this research is to optimize the energy transfer efficiency of the railgun system. The experiments involve varying parameters such as projectile mass, rail length, and magnetic field strength to determine their effects on energy transfer. The results show that increasing the projectile mass and rail length leads to higher energy transfer, while increasing the magnetic field strength has a more complex effect. These findings provide valuable insights for improving the performance of railgun systems and can contribute to the development of more efficient and powerful electromagnetic launchers.

This paper presents a novel approach to semantic segmentation using generative models. The proposed method leverages the power of generative models to improve the performance of semantic segmentation tasks, particularly in scenarios with limited labeled data. The authors introduce a semi-supervised learning framework that combines labeled and unlabeled data to train the generative model, which is then used for segmentation. Additionally, the paper demonstrates the strong out-of-domain generalization capabilities of the proposed method, showing its effectiveness in segmenting images from unseen domains. Experimental results on benchmark datasets validate the superiority of the proposed approach compared to existing methods, highlighting its potential for practical applications in computer vision.

This paper investigates the $L^2$  well-posedness of boundary  value problems for parabolic systems with measurable coefficients. The authors establish the  existence  and uniqueness of weak solutions in the $L^2$ space for a class  of parabolic  systems with  measurable coefficients.  They also prove the regularity of the solutions and provide estimates  for the solutions in terms of the  data.  The results  obtained  in this paper  contribute to the understanding of the well-posedness of boundary value problems for  parabolic systems with measurable  coefficients.

Incorporating shape information is essential for the delineation of many
organs and anatomical structures in medical images. While previous work has
mainly focused on parametric spatial transformations applied on refrence
template shapes, in this paper, we adress the Bayesian inference of parametric
shape models for segmenting medical images with the objective to provide
interpretable results. The proposed framework defines a likelihood appearance
probability and a prior label probability based on a generic shape function
through a logistic function. A referance length parameter defined in the
sigmoid controls the trade-off between shape and appearance information. The
inference of shape parameters is performed within an Expectation-Maximisation
approach where a Gauss-Newton optimization stage allows to provide an
approximation of the posterior probability of shape parameters. This framework
is applied to the segmentation of cochlea structures from clinical CT images
constrained by a 10 parameter shape model. It is evaluated on three different
datasets, one of which includes more than 200 patient images. The results show
performances comparable to supervised methods and better than previously
proposed unsupervised ones. It also enables an analysis of parameter
distributions and the quantification of segmentation uncertainty including the
effect of the shape model.

There are several methods to determine how many flooding operations are needed to flood a coloured graph in the one-player game flood-it to make it monochromatic, but there are still many open questions concerning the maximum number of operations that might be required in the worst case. We begin a systematic investigation of this problem, with the aim of determining for a given graph the maximum number of operations that can be required for all possible colourings of the graph. We give several upper and lower bounds on this quantity, and show that they are tight for trees; we also discuss how much these bounds can be improved by concentrating on graphs with many edges.

This paper investigates the compositions of invertibility preserving maps for certain monoids and their application to Clifford algebras. The authors explore the properties of these maps and provide examples of their application in the context of Clifford algebras. The results of this study contribute to a deeper understanding of the structure and properties of these monoids and their relationship to Clifford algebras.

This paper continues the study  of  lifting representations of finite reductive groups. In particular, we focus on the  explicit conorms of these lifting representations. We provide a  general formula for computing the conorms, which allows us to explicitly determine the  conorms  for various finite reductive groups.  We also establish several  interesting properties of the conorms, such  as their relation to the central characters of  the lifting representations. Overall, our results  contribute to a deeper understanding of the lifting  representations  of finite  reductive groups and  provide a useful  tool for studying  their  properties.

This paper proposes a deep learning architecture that attains statistically
significant improvements over traditional algorithms in Poisson image denoising
espically when the noise is strong. 

Poisson noise commonly occurs in low-light
and photon- limited settings, where the noise can be most accurately modeled by
the Poission distribution. Poisson noise traditionally prevails only in
specific fields such as astronomical imaging. 

However, with the booming market
of surveillance cameras, which commonly operate in low-light environments, or
mobile phones, which produce noisy night scene pictures due to lower-grade
sensors, the necessity for an advanced Poisson image denoising algorithm has
increased. Deep learning has achieved amazing breakthroughs in other imaging
problems, such image segmentation and recognition, and this paper proposes a
deep learning denoising network that outperforms traditional algorithms in
Poisson denoising especially when the noise is strong. The architecture
incorporates a hybrid of convolutional and deconvolutional layers along with
symmetric connections. The denoising network achieved statistically significant
0.38dB, 0.68dB, and 1.04dB average PSNR gains over benchmark traditional
algorithms in experiments with image peak values 4, 2, and 1. 

The denoising
network can also operate with shorter computational time while still
outperforming the benchmark algorithm by tuning the reconstruction stride
sizes.

Recently, there has been focus on penalized log-likelihood variance
estimation for sparse linear variance (precision) matrices. The penalty is
responsible for inducing sparsity, and a very common choice is the convex $l_1$
norm. Unfortunately, the highest estimator efficiency is not usually achieved with this
penalty. The most natural sparsity promoting "norm" is the non-convex $l_0$
penalty but its absence of convexity has prevented its usage in sparse cumulative
likelihood analysis. In this paper we consider non-convex $l_0$ penalized
log-likelihood inverse covariance estimation and present a novel cyclic descent
algorithm for its algorithm. Convergence to a local minimizer is proved,
which is highly non-trivial, and we demonstrate through simulations the reduced
bias and superior reliability of the $l_0$ penalty as compared to the $l_1$
penalty.

This paper proposes a  semi-supervised learning approach for eye image segmentation, utilizing a combination of labeled and unlabeled  data.   Eye  image segmentation is an  important  step in  various medical applications  such as diagnosing eye  diseases and monitoring treatment progress.  However, acquiring a large amount of annotated data for training is time-consuming and  costly. The proposed method leverages both labeled and  unlabeled data  to improve segmentation accuracy. A convolutional  neural network is trained  using the labeled data, while a self-training approach is employed to iteratively label  the unlabeled data.  The effectiveness of  the  proposed method is evaluated on   a dataset  of eye images, and the  results show significant improvement in segmentation  accuracy compared to using only labeled data. This research  contributes to the field of medical imaging by providing an efficient and cost-effective  solution for eye image segmentation.

This  paper proposes a novel approach for multimodal and semi-supervised  image  segmentation. The proposed method disentangles the   different modalities of the input data, aligns  them to a common feature space, and fuses  them  to  generate accurate segmentation results.  The disentanglement  step involves learning separate  representations for each modality, while the alignment step utilizes a shared feature space to ensure consistency across modalities. The fusion step combines the aligned representations  to produce  the final   segmentation output.  Experimental results on  various  datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in  terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness. The proposed method has potential applications in medical imaging, remote sensing, and other domains  where multimodal and semi-supervised image segmentation is  required.

Generative adversarial networks (GANs) have shown great success in
applications such as image generation and inpainting. However, they typically
require large datasets, which are often not available, especially in the
context of prediction tasks such as image segmentation that require labels.
Therefore, methods such as the CycleGAN use more easily available unlabelled
data, but do not offer a way to leverage additional labelled data for improved
performance. To address this shortcoming, we show how to factorise the joint
data distribution into a set of lower-dimensional distributions along with
their dependencies. This allows splitting the discriminator in a GAN into
multiple "sub-discriminators" that can be independently trained from incomplete
observations. Their outputs can be combined to estimate the density ratio
between the joint real and the generator distribution, which enables training
generators as in the original GAN framework. We apply our method to image
generation, image segmentation and audio source separation, and obtain improved
performance over a standard GAN when additional incomplete training examples
are available. For the Cityscapes segmentation task in particular, our method
also improves accuracy by an absolute 14.9% over CycleGAN while using only 26
additional paired examples.

Little is known about the global topology of the Fatou set $U(f)$ for
holomorphic endomorphisms $f: \mathbb{CP}^k \to \mathbb{CP}^k$, when $k >1$.
Classical theory describes $U(f)$ as the complement in $ \mathbb{CP}^k$ of the
support of a dynamically-defined closed positive $(1,1)$ current. Given any
closed positive $(1,1)$ current $S$ on $ \mathbb{CP}^k$, we give a definition
of linking number between closed loops in $\mathbb{CP}^k \setminus \supp S$ and
the current $S$. It has the property that if $lk(\gamma,S) \neq 0$, then
$\gamma$ represents a non-trivial homology element in $H_1(\mathbb{CP}^k
\setminus \supp S)$.
  As an application, we use these linking numbers to establish that many
classes of endomorphisms of $\mathbb{CP}^2$ have Fatou components with
infinitely generated first homology. For example, we prove that the Fatou set
has infinitely generated first homology for any polynomial endomorphism of
$\mathbb{CP}^2$ for which the restriction to the line at infinity is hyperbolic
and has disconnected Julia set. In addition we show that a polynomial skew
product of $\mathbb{CP}^2$ has Fatou set with infinitely generated first
homology if some vertical Julia set is disconnected. We then conclude with a
section of concrete examples and questions for further study.

Markov Random Fields (MRFs) are widely used in computer vision and machine learning for applications such as image denoising and segmentation. Inference in MRFs can be computationally expensive, which limits their practical use in real-time applications. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for accelerated inference in MRFs based on smooth Riemannian optimization techniques. Our method exploits the underlying geometric structure of MRFs to perform more efficient computations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets, showing significant speed-ups compared to state-of-the-art methods while maintaining similar performance. This work opens up new possibilities for real-time applications of MRF-based models in computer vision and machine learning.

Abstract:

Sleep staging, the classification of sleep into different stages, is a crucial task in sleep medicine. Traditional methods for sleep staging rely on manually annotating sleep stages from polysomnography (PSG) recordings, which is time-consuming and requires expertise. In recent years, deep learning techniques have shown promising  results in automating sleep staging.  However,  most existing methods focus on classifying short segments of time series data without considering the temporal dependencies within  the data.

In this  paper,  we propose U-Time,  a fully  convolutional network for  time series segmentation  applied to   sleep staging. U-Time takes advantage of the  fully convolutional  architecture and  dilated  convolutions  to capture both local  and global  temporal dependencies  within the time series data. Additionally,  we incorporate recurrent connections to model longer-term dependencies and improve the segmentation  performance.

We evaluate U-Time on a publicly available benchmark dataset for sleep staging, achieving state-of-the-art performance. Our results show that U-Time outperforms existing methods in  terms of both accuracy    and F1 score. Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies  to investigate the effects of different components of  U-Time, showing the importance  of the dilated convolutions and  recurrent  connections.

Overall,  our  findings demonstrate the effectiveness  of the proposed U-Time model for  time  series  segmentation applied to sleep  staging. The fully  convolutional architecture, dilated  convolutions, and recurrent  connections all contribute  to improving the segmentation performance.  The proposed  U-Time model has the potential to  significantly reduce the annotation burden in sleep  medicine and improve the accuracy of sleep staging.

Automatic histopathology image segmentation is crucial to disease analysis.
Limited available labeled data hinders the generalizability of trained models
under the fully supervised setting. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) based on
generative methods has been proven to be effective in utilizing diverse image
characteristics. However, it has not been well explored what kinds of generated
images would be more useful for model training and how to use such images. In
this paper, we propose a new data guided generative method for histopathology
image segmentation by leveraging the unlabeled data distributions. First, we
design an image generation module. Image content and style are disentangled and
embedded in a clustering-friendly space to utilize their distributions. New
images are synthesized by sampling and cross-combining contents and styles.
Second, we devise an effective data selection policy for judiciously sampling
the generated images: (1) to make the generated training set better cover the
dataset, the clusters that are underrepresented in the original training set
are covered more; (2) to make the training process more effective, we identify
and oversample the images of "hard cases" in the data for which annotated
training data may be scarce. Our method is evaluated on glands and nuclei
datasets. We show that under both the inductive and transductive settings, our
SSL method consistently boosts the performance of common segmentation models
and attains state-of-the-art results.

Color image segmentation is an important task in computer vision and image processing. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for color image segmentation using adaptive particle swarm optimization (APSO) and fuzzy C-means (FCM) clustering. APSO is used to optimize the parameters of FCM, which helps in achieving better segmentation results. The proposed method adaptively adjusts the inertia weight and acceleration coefficients of APSO based on the fitness values of the particles. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed method outperforms several state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms and shows promising results for color image segmentation.

Соnvоlutіоnаl Νеtwоrks (СоnvΝеts) ехсеl аt sеmаntіс sеgmеntаtіоn аnd hаvе
bесоmе а vіtаl соmроnеnt fоr реrсерtіоn іn аutоnоmоus drіvіng. Εnаblіng аn
аll-еnсоmраssіng vіеw оf strееt-sсеnеs, оmnіdіrесtіоnаl саmеrаs рrеsеnt
thеmsеlvеs аs а реrfесt fіt іn suсh sуstеms. Моst sеgmеntаtіоn mоdеls fоr
раrsіng urbаn еnvіrоnmеnts ореrаtе оn соmmоn, nаrrоw Fіеld оf Vіеw (FоV)
іmаgеs. Тrаnsfеrrіng thеsе mоdеls frоm thе dоmаіn thеу wеrе dеsіgnеd fоr tо
360-dеgrее реrсерtіоn, thеіr реrfоrmаnсе drорs drаmаtісаllу, е.g., bу аn
аbsоlutе 30.0% (mΙоU) оn еstаblіshеd tеst-bеds. Τо brіdgе thе gар іn tеrms оf
FоV аnd struсturаl dіstrіbutіоn bеtwееn thе іmаgіng dоmаіns, wе іntrоduсе
Еffісіеnt Соnсurrеnt Аttеntіоn Νеtwоrks (ΕСАΝеts), dіrесtlу сарturіng thе
іnhеrеnt lоng-rаngе dереndеnсіеs іn оmnіdіrесtіоnаl іmаgеrу. Іn аddіtіоn tо thе
lеаrnеd аttеntіоn-bаsеd соntехtuаl рrіоrs thаt саn strеtсh асrоss 360-dеgrее
іmаgеs, wе uрgrаdе mоdеl trаіnіng bу lеvеrаgіng multі-sоurсе аnd
оmnі-suреrvіsеd lеаrnіng, tаkіng аdvаntаgе оf bоth: Dеnsеlу lаbеlеd аnd
unlаbеlеd dаtа оrіgіnаtіng frоm multірlе dаtаsеts. То fоstеr рrоgrеss іn
раnоrаmіс іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn, wе рut fоrwаrd аnd ехtеnsіvеlу еvаluаtе mоdеls оn
Wіld РΑnоrаmіс Sеmаntіс Sеgmеntаtіоn (WіldΡАSS), а dаtаsеt dеsіgnеd tо сарturе
dіvеrsе sсеnеs frоm аll аrоund thе glоbе. Οur nоvеl mоdеl, trаіnіng rеgіmеn аnd
multі-sоurсе рrеdісtіоn fusіоn еlеvаtе thе реrfоrmаnсе (mІоU) tо nеw
stаtе-оf-thе-аrt rеsults оn thе рublіс РАSS (60.2%) аnd thе frеsh WіldΡАSS
(69.0%) bеnсhmаrks.

Polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) image segmentation is
currently of great importance in image processing for remote sensing
applications. However, it is a challenging task due to two main reasons.
Firstly, label information is difficult to acquire due to high annotation
costs. Secondly, speckle effect embedded in the PolSAR imaging process
remarkably degrades segmentation performance. To address these two issues,
we present a contextual PolSAR image semantic segmentation method in this
paper.With a newly defined channelwise consistent feature set as input, the
three-dimensional discrete wavelet transform (3D-DWT) technique is employed to
extract discriminative multi-scale features that are robust to speckle noise.
Then Markov random field (MRF) is further applied to enforce label smoothness
spatially during segmentation. By simultaneously utilizing 3D-DWT features and
MRF priors for first time, contextual information is fully integrated
during the segmentation to ensure accurate and smooth segmentation. To
demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we conduct extensive
experiments on three real benchmark PolSAR image data sets. Experimental
results indicate that proposed method achieves promising segmentation
accuracy and preferable spatial consistency using minimal number of labeled
pixels.

We present approaches for the study of fluid-structure interactions subject
to thermal fluctuations. A mixed mechanical description is utilized combining
Eulerian and Lagrangian reference frames. We establish general conditions for
operators coupling these descriptions. Stochastic driving fields for the
formalism are derived using principles from statistical mechanics. The
stochastic differential equations of the formalism are found to exhibit
significant stiffness in some physical regimes. To cope with this issue, we
derive reduced stochastic differential equations for several physical regimes.
We also present stochastic numerical methods for each regime to approximate the
fluid-structure dynamics and to generate efficiently the required stochastic
driving fields. To validate the methodology in each regime, we perform analysis
of the invariant probability distribution of the stochastic dynamics of the
fluid-structure formalism. We compare this analysis with results from
statistical mechanics. To further demonstrate the applicability of the
methodology, we perform computational studies for spherical particles having
translational and rotational degrees of freedom. We compare these studies with
results from fluid mechanics. The presented approach provides for
fluid-structure systems a set of rather general computational methods for
treating consistently structure mechanics, hydrodynamic coupling, and thermal
fluctuations.

This paper presents a novel approach for jointly segmenting and deconvoluting ultrasound images using a hierarchical Bayesian model based on generalized Gaussian priors. Ultrasound images often suffer from poor resolution and noise, which can make accurate segmentation challenging. To address this, the proposed model integrates the segmentation and deconvolution processes, allowing for the estimation of both the true underlying image and the regions of interest simultaneously. The generalized Gaussian priors are used to model the statistical characteristics of the image and the segmentation, enabling robust estimation and accurate delineation of boundaries. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach compared to existing methods, with improved segmentation accuracy and reduced noise levels. The proposed model has the potential to enhance the interpretation and analysis of ultrasound images in various medical applications.

This   paper provides  a comprehensive review of reconfigurable reflectarrays and array lenses for dynamic antenna beam  control. These technologies play  a crucial role in  modern wireless  communication systems,  allowing  for  rapid adaptation of the antenna beam to  changing environmental conditions and communication requirements. The paper discusses the principles, design  considerations, and performance metrics  of reconfigurable reflectarrays and array lenses.  It also presents an   overview of  the recent advancements in materials, fabrication techniques, and integration methods for these devices. Finally, the paper highlights the  challenges and potential future directions  in  the field, aiming to inspire further research and development in dynamic antenna beam control.

Locate then Segment: A Strong Pipeline for Referring Image Segmentation is an academic paper that introduces a robust pipeline for referring image segmentation. The pipeline consists of two main stages: localization and segmentation. The localization stage uses a convolutional neural network (CNN) to identify the object of interest in the image. This CNN is trained using a large-scale object localization dataset. The segmentation stage utilizes a fully convolutional network (FCN) to segment the object in the localized region. This FCN is trained using a combination of synthetic and real data. Experimental results show that the proposed pipeline achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple referring image segmentation benchmarks. The pipeline is also shown to be highly effective in challenging scenarios, such as low-resolution and noisy images. This work demonstrates the importance and effectiveness of a strong pipeline approach for referring image segmentation.

This paper presents a model for understanding social dynamics in a collaborative environment. The model takes into account the opinions and conflicts among individuals and aims to identify consensus among them. The authors propose a mathematical framework that incorporates various factors such as individual preferences, influence of others, and the evolution of opinions over time. The model is validated through simulations and case studies, demonstrating its effectiveness in capturing the complex dynamics of social interactions. The findings of this study contribute to the understanding of collaborative environments and can be applied to various domains such as online communities, team decision-making, and social networks.

This study examines the growth  and success rates of   petitions on the UK   No. 10 Downing Street website. Using  a unique dataset of  over  3 million petitions,  we investigate factors that  contribute to the popularity and ultimate success of a petition. We find that petition  growth is influenced by various factors, including the topic of the petition,  the  number of  initial  signatures, and the use of social media. Additionally, we analyze the success  rates  of petitions and find that  factors such as the number of signatures, the time elapsed  since  the petition was created, and the  response time from the government  all play a role in determining success. Our findings provide insights into  the dynamics of online petition platforms and can inform policymakers  and platform  administrators in enhancing the effectiveness of such platforms.

Large linear systems with sparse, non-symmetric matrices arise in the
modeling of Markov chains or in the discretization of convection-diffusion
problems. Due to their potential to solve sparse linear systems with an effort
that is linear in the number of unknowns, algebraic multigrid (AMG) methods are
of fundamental interest for such systems. For symmetric positive definite
matrices, fundamental theoretical convergence results are established, and
efficient AMG solvers have been developed. In contrast, for non-symmetric
matrices, theoretical convergence results have been provided only recently. A
property that is sufficient for convergence is that the matrix be an M-matrix.
In this paper, we present how the simulation of incompressible fluid flows with
particle methods leads to large linear systems with sparse, non-symmetric
matrices. In each time step, the Poisson equation is approximated by meshfree
finite differences. While traditional least squares approaches do not guarantee
an M-matrix structure, an approach based on linear optimization yields
optimally sparse M-matrices. For both types of discretization approaches, we
investigate the performance of a classical AMG method, as well as an AMLI type
method. While in the considered test problems, the M-matrix structure turns out
not to be necessary for the convergence of AMG, problems can occur when it is
violated. In addition, the matrices obtained by the linear optimization
approach result in fast solution times due to their optimal sparsity.

Interactive medical image segmentation is   a challenging task   that requires expertise and specialized tools.  In this  paper, we  propose a  novel approach that combines point-based interaction and sequential patch learning for interactive medical  image segmentation. Our method allows users to select a set of points  on the image to  indicate the  regions of interest, and these  points are used to generate a set of image patches for training a  deep learning model. The model learns to predict the segmentation mask  for each patch,   and these predictions are combined to  produce the  final segmentation  result. We evaluate our method on multiple  medical image datasets and compare it with existing interactive segmentation methods. The  experimental  results demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency. Our  approach  has the potential to improve  the clinical  workflow by providing  a  user-friendly and efficient  tool for interactive medical image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel deep learning architecture called MDU-Net for biomedical image segmentation. The proposed MDU-Net combines the U-Net architecture with dense connections and multi-scale feature fusion. The dense connections enable information flow between different layers, enhancing the gradient flow and alleviating the vanishing gradient problem. The multi-scale feature fusion module integrates features from different scales, allowing the network to capture both local and global contextual information. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that MDU-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance in biomedical image segmentation tasks, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The proposed MDU-Net has the potential to contribute to the field of biomedical image analysis and facilitate various medical applications.

The upgrades of the Belle experiment and the KEKB accelerator aim to increase
the data set of the experiment by the factor 50. This will be achieved by
increasing the luminosity of the accelerator which requires a significant
upgrade of the detector. A new pixel detector based on DEPFET technology will
be installed to handle the increased reaction rate and provide better vertex
resolution. One of the features of the DEPFET detector is a long integration
time of 20 {\mu}s, which increases detector occupancy up to 3 %. 

The detector
will generate about 2 GB/s of data. 

An FPGA-based two-level read-out system,
the Data Handling Hybrid, was developed for the Belle 2 pixel detector. 

The
system consists of 40 read-out and 8 controller modules. 

All modules are built
in {\mu}TCA form factor using Xilinx Virtex-6 FPGA and can utilize up to 4 GB
DDR3 RAM. The system was successfully tested in the beam test at DESY in
January 2014. The functionality and the architecture of the Belle 2 Data
Handling Hybrid system as well as the performance of the system during the beam
test are presented in the paper.

The abstract for the academic paper "Uncertainties in the Sunspot Numbers: Estimation and Implications" discusses the challenges associated with measuring and estimating sunspot numbers, as well as the potential implications of these uncertainties. The paper highlights the various sources of uncertainty in sunspot data, including instrument calibration, observer bias, and data gaps. It also presents different statistical methods for estimating uncertainties and quantifying their impact on various scientific analyses. The authors emphasize the importance of understanding and accounting for these uncertainties in order to improve the accuracy and reliability of sunspot data, as well as to enhance our understanding of solar activity and its effects on Earth's climate. The paper concludes with recommendations for future research and data collection efforts in order to reduce uncertainties and improve the quality of sunspot data.

This paper investigates the relationship between generalized theta functions, strange duality, and odd orthogonal bundles on curves. The authors explore the connection between these three concepts and provide a detailed analysis of their properties and interactions. The paper presents various mathematical proofs and explanations to support the findings and conclusions. The research contributes to the understanding of generalized theta functions, strange duality, and odd orthogonal bundles on curves, and presents new insights and perspectives in this area of study. Overall, this paper serves as a valuable resource for mathematicians interested in these topics.

Accurate image segmentation plays a crucial role in medical image analysis,
yet it faces great challenges of various shapes, diverse sizes, and blurry
boundaries. To address these difficulties, square kernel-based encoder-decoder
architecture has been proposed and widely used, but its performance remains
still unsatisfactory. To further cope with these challenges, we present a novel
double-branch encoder architecture. Our architecture is inspired by two
observations: 1) Since the discrimination of features learned via square
convolutional kernels needs to be further improved, we propose to utilize
non-square vertical and horizontal convolutional kernels in the double-branch
encoder, so features learned by the two branches can be expected to complement
each other. 2) Considering that spatial attention can help models to better
focus on the target region in a large-sized image, we develop an attention loss
to further emphasize the segmentation on small-sized targets. Together, the
above two schemes give rise to a novel double-branch encoder segmentation
framework for medical image segmentation, namely Crosslink-Net. The experiments
validate the effectiveness of our model on four datasets. The code is released
at https://github.com/Qianyu1226/Crosslink-Net.

We study a randomized algorithm for graph domination, by which, according to
a uniformly chosen permutation, vertices are revealed and added to the
dominating set if not already dominated. We determine the expected size of the
dominating set produced by the algorithm for the path graph $P_n$ and use this
to derive the expected size for some related families of graphs. We then
provide a much-refined analysis of the worst and best cases of this algorithm
on $P_n$ and enumerate the permutations for which the algorithm has the
worst-possible performance and best-possible performance. The case of
dominating the path graph has connections to previous work of Bouwer and Star,
and of Gessel on greedily coloring the path.

This paper presents a novel approach for one-stage shape instantiation from a single 2D image to a 3D point cloud. The proposed method leverages deep learning techniques to directly predict the 3D shape of an object from a 2D image, without the need for intermediate steps such as 2D-to-3D reconstruction. The key idea is to train a convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn the mapping between 2D image features and 3D point cloud representations. The network is trained on a large dataset of paired 2D images and corresponding 3D point clouds, and is able to generalize to unseen objects. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately reconstructing 3D shapes from 2D images, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. The proposed approach has potential applications in various fields such as computer vision, robotics, and augmented reality.

We introduce various quantities that can be defined for an arbitrary matroid,
and show that certain conditions on these quantities imply that a matroid is
not representable over $\mathbb{F}_q$ where $q$ is a prime power. Mostly, for a
matroid of rank $r$, we examine the proportion of size-$(r-k)$ subsets that are
dependent, and give bounds, in terms of the cardinality of the matroid and $q$,
for this proportion, below which the matroid is not representable over
$\mathbb{F}_q$. We also explore connections between the defined quantities and
demonstrate that they can be used to prove that random matrices have high
proportions of subsets of columns independant. Our study relates to the results
of our papers [4,5,11] dealing with the cardinality of sets of $k$-independent
vectors over $\mathbb{F}_q$ and the Maximal Distance Separation Conjecture over
$\mathbb{F}_q$.

The winning condition of a parity game with costs involves an arbitrary, but
fixed bound on the cost incurred between instances of odd colors and the first
occurrence of a larger even one. Such games quantitatively extend parity games
while preserving most of their attractive properties, i.e, determining the
winner is in NP and co-NP and one team has positional winning strategies.
  We show that the types of parity games with costs are slightly
varied when asking for strategies realizing the minimum such bound: The
solution problem becomes PSPACE-complete and exponential memory is both
possible in general and not necessary. However, solving and playing parity
games with costs optimally is easier than just winning them. However, we show
that the tradeoff between the memory size and the realized bound is gradual in
general. All these findings hold true for both a binary and binary encoding of
costs.
  Instead, we investigate Streett games with costs. Here, playing optimally is
as difficult as winning, both in terms of complexity and memory.

This paper presents a novel approach for screen content image segmentation using least absolute deviation fitting. The proposed method aims to accurately segment screen content images by effectively separating the foreground and background regions. The method utilizes the least absolute deviation fitting technique to estimate the parameters of a linear model that represents the screen content. Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting screen content images, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. The proposed method shows promising potential for various applications, such as image editing and object recognition, where accurate screen content segmentation is crucial.

In computer vision, many problems such as image segmentation, pixel
labelling, and scene parsing can be formulated as binary quadratic programs
(BQPs). 

For submodular problems, cuts based methods can be employed to
efficiently solve large-scale problems. However, general nonsubmodular problems
are significantly more challenging to solve. Finding a solution when the
problem is of large size to be of practical interest, however, typically
requires relaxation. 

Two standard relaxation methods are widely used for
solving general BQPs--spectral methods and semidefinite programming (SDP), each
with their own advantages and disadvantages. 

Spectral relaxation is simple and
easy to implement, but its bound is loose. 

Semidefinite relaxation has a
tighter bound, but its computational complexity is high, especially for large
scale problems. In this work, we present a new SDP formulation for BQPs, with
two desirable properties. 

First, it has a similar relaxation bound to
conventional SDP formulations. Second, compared with conventional SDP methods,
the new SDP formulation leads to a significantly more efficient and scalable
dual optimization approach, which has the same degree of complexity as spectral
methods. We then propose two solvers, namely, quasi-Newton and smoothing Newton
methods, for the dual problem. Both of them are significantly more efficiently
than standard interior-point methods. In practice, the smoothing Newton solver
is faster than the quasi-Newton solver for dense or medium-sized problems,
while the quasi-Newton solver is preferable for large sparse/structured
problems. 

Our experiments on a few computer vision applications including
clustering, image segmentation, co-segmentation and registration show the
potential of our SDP formulation for solving large-scale BQPs.

In his work, Klazar introduced a new notion of avoidance of patterns in the context of set partitions, with n=1... n. The purpose of this paper is to study the concept of Wilf-equivalence, in connection with the concept of avoidance. We determine all the equivalents of the pairwise blocks with exactly two blocks, of which one is a single block, and it is conjectured that, for n> 4, these are all the equivalents of the pairwise blocks, except those arising from the complementation. If we have a partition of the order k and let us denote the set of all the partitions of the order n, which avoid the partition k, then for various choices of $tau_1$ and $tau_2$, we prove that if $tau_2$ is a partition of the order k with exactly one block, then for all the partitions of the order k with exactly two blocks, $Pi_n(tau_1) Pi_n(tau_2)$, and it is conjectured that for all partitions $tau_1$ of the order k, this result is true.

This paper  presents a   method for   realistic image normalization  in the context of multi-domain  segmentation. Image normalization is  an important preprocessing step in many computer vision tasks,  including segmentation. However, existing  methods often fail to   account for variations in lighting,  color, and texture across different domains. The proposed method addresses this issue by learning a domain-specific normalization function using a generative  adversarial  network. The effectiveness of the proposed method  is demonstrated through extensive  experiments on two real-world datasets, showing significant improvements in segmentation performance compared to existing normalization methods.  The paper concludes by discussing  the  implications of the proposed method and potential directions for future  research in this area.

Person re-identification is becoming a hot research for developing both
machine learning algorithms and video surveillance applications. The task of
person re-identification is to determine which person in a gallery has the same
identity to a probe image. This task basically assumes that the subject of the
probe image belongs to the gallery, that is, the gallery contains this person.
However, in practical applications such as searching a suspect in a video, this
assumption is usually not true. In this paper, we consider the open-set person
re-identification problem, which includes two sub-tasks, detection and
identification. The detection sub-task is to determine the presence of the
probe subject in the gallery, and the identification sub-task is to determine
which person in the gallery has the same identity as the accepted probe. We
present a database collected from a video surveillance setting of 6 cameras,
with 200 persons and 7,413 images segmented. Based on this database, we develop
a benchmark protocol for evaluating the performance under the open-set person
re-identification scenario. Several popular metric learning algorithms for
person re-identification have been evaluated as baselines. From the baseline
performance, we observe that the open-set person re-identification problem is
still largely unresolved, thus further attention and effort is needed.

let $Ham (M,\omega ) $ denote the Frechet Lie group of Hamiltonian
symplectomorphisms of a monotone symplectic manifold $(M, \omega) $. Let $NFuk
(M, \omega)$ be the $A _{\infty} $-nerve of the Fukaya category $Fuk (M,
\omega)$, and let $(|\mathbb{S}|, NFuk (M, \omega))$ denote the $NFuk (M,
\omega)$ part of the ``space of $\infty$-categories'' $|\mathbb{S}| $.
Using Floer-Fukaya theorem for a monotone $(M, \omega)$ we construct a natural
up to homotopy classifying map \begin{equation*}
  BHam (M, \omega) \to (|\mathbb{S}|, NFuk (M, \omega)). \end{equation*} This
verifies one sense of a theorem of Teleman on existence of action of $Ham (M
, \omega)$ on the Fukaya category of $(M, \omega ) $. This construction is very
closely linked to the notion of the Seidel tensor and the quantum
characteristic classes of the author, and this map is supposed to be the
deepest expression of their fundamental geometric theory. In part II the above
map is seen to be invariant by an explicit calculation. In particular, we
arrive at a new non-trivial ``quantum'' invariant of any smooth manifold, which
motives the statement of a type of ``quantum'' Novikov conjecture.

thе аsуmрtоtіс bеhаvіоr оf $\lаmbdа_n$ аs $n\tо\іnftу$ іs gіvеn bу \[

For nonzero alpha$ in A we consider the equations [ D(F) = alpha ]=0,  where alpha  A and n > 2  D(F) n, alpha  A, where A is an A-order of Omega, that is, a subring of the integral closure of A in Omega which contains A and has a K-basis.
