This paper presents a comprehensive survey of the use of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) techniques in the field of computer vision. The authors provide an overview of the fundamental concepts and techniques in DRL, as well as discussing the challenges and limitations of applying DRL to computer vision tasks. The paper also provides a detailed analysis of the various applications of DRL in computer vision, including object detection, image segmentation, and image recognition. Furthermore, the authors highlight the recent advancements in DRL research and provide insights into the future directions of this field. Overall, this survey serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners interested in exploring the potential of DRL in computer vision.

This paper proposes a novel architecture for convolutional neural networks (CNNs) called HS-ResNet, which incorporates a hierarchical-split block to improve the performance of CNNs. The hierarchical-split block splits the input feature maps into multiple branches, each with its own convolutional layers, and then combines the outputs of these branches. This allows the network to capture both local and global information, leading to better feature representation and improved performance. The proposed HS-ResNet architecture is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, and the results demonstrate its superiority over existing CNN architectures in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Overall, this paper presents a promising approach to enhance the performance of CNNs by incorporating hierarchical-split blocks.

The phenomenon of Anderson localization of waves in elastic systems is
studied. We analyze this phenomenon in two different set of systems: disordered
linear chains of harmonic oscillators and disordered rods which oscillate with
torsional waves. The first set is analyzed numerically whereas the second one
is studied both experimentally and theoretically. In particular, we discuss the
localization properties of the waves as a function of the frequency. In doing
that we have used the inverse participation ratio, which is related to the
localization length. We find that the normal modes localize exponentially
according to Anderson theory. In the elastic systems, the localization length
decreases with frequency. This behavior is in contrast with what happens in
analogous quantum mechanical systems, for which the localization length grows
with energy. This difference is explained by means of the properties of the re
ection coefficient of a single scatterer in each case.

This paper presents a novel approach to designing all-pass phasers using generalized coupled-line structures. All-pass phasers are important components in various applications such as signal processing and communication systems. The proposed design method utilizes the concept of generalized coupled-line structures, which allows for greater flexibility in achieving desired phase responses. The design procedure is described in detail, including the determination of the coupling coefficients and characteristic impedances of the coupled-line sections. The performance of the designed phasers is evaluated through simulations and compared with existing designs. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving desired phase responses with improved performance. This work contributes to the advancement of all-pass phaser design and provides a valuable tool for engineers and researchers in the field.

This paper presents a survey of computer-aided knee joint magnetic resonance image (MRI) segmentation methods. The segmentation of knee joint structures from MRI scans is a challenging task due to variations in image intensity, noise, and anatomical variability. Several automated and semi-automated techniques have been developed to assist radiologists and clinicians in accurately segmenting knee joint structures. This survey provides an overview of the commonly used segmentation algorithms, including thresholding, region-based, edge-based, and machine learning approaches. Additionally, the paper discusses the advantages and limitations of each method and highlights the future directions in knee joint MRI segmentation research. Overall, this survey aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the state-of-the-art techniques in knee joint MRI segmentation and assist researchers and clinicians in selecting appropriate methods for their specific applications.

Accurate clinical image segmentation is important for treatment, medical
planning and numerous other applications. Convolutional Neural Systems (CNN) have
become the state-of-the-art automatic segmentation tools. Unfortunately, fully
automatic results will now need to be refined to remain reliable and reliable
enough for clinical usage. We propose a deep learning-based interactive
segmentation approach to reduce the results provided by an automatic CNN and to
improve user interactions during refinement for greater precision. We use one CNN
to provide an initial automatic segmentation, on which user behaviors are
added to indicate mis-segmentations. The CNN gives as input the user
encounters with the initial segmentation and provides a refined result. We
propose to combine user interactions with CNNs through geodesic distance
transforms, and propose a resolution-preserving network that provides a less
dense prediction. In addition, we integrate user interactions as hard
constraints into a back-propagatable Conditional Random Field. We validated the
proposed methodology in the context of 2D placenta segmentation from fetal MRI
and 3D brain tissue segmentation from FLAIR images. Experimental findings show
our technique demonstrates a significant improvement from automatic CNNs, and provides
superior and much greater reliability with more user interventions and more time
compared with conventional interactive tools.

This paper investigates the control of light absorption and emission in quantum dots through the use of a surface-plasmon field. The authors demonstrate that by manipulating the properties of the surface-plasmon field, they can modulate the absorption and emission spectra of the quantum dots. This control over the quantum-dot light-matter interaction has potential applications in areas such as quantum information processing and optoelectronics. The findings of this study contribute to the understanding of surface-plasmon interactions with quantum dots and provide a basis for further research in this field.

Now, in order to develop Deep Learning (DL) models for disease classification or image segmentation from medical images, it is becoming more common to start from completely unrelated natural images. However, the shortcoming and the applicability of TL to specialized tasks in the medical image domain remain unknown, and the only assumption is that the more images are used, the better the results will be. We report detailed comparisons, rigorous statistical analysis, and comparisons between widely used DL architecture for binarized segmentation after transferring the ImageNet imagenet of medical images (TII models) and supervised learning on only medical images (LMI models) of large-scale macroscopic skin cancer, microscopic mcore-prostate-biopsysts, and computed tomography images (CT). Through a visual comparison of TII and LMI model outputs and their Grad-Cam counterparts, we show that, counter to intuition, the combined results of the two models or the masks of the individual models combining in different combinations, improved the performance by about 10%. We also report on the use of a more sophisticated DL method for clinically relevant image segmentation and model explanations under limited conditions. For example, a simple combination of LMI and TII models to achieve high performance and explanations of LMI and TII models under low data sizes can be used for such situations, where sparsity is a requirement. We also present a free github repository of TII and LMI models and more than 10,000 medical images and their corresponding Grad-Cam results from this study, which can serve as a starting point for further advanced research on DL for medical discoveries and applications.

We review the fundamental properties of the quantum relative entropy for
finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. In particular, we focus on several
inequalities that are related to the second law of thermodynamics, where the
positivity and the monotonicity of the quantum relative entropy play key roles;
these properties are directly applicable to derivations of second law
(e.g., Clausius inequality). Moreover, the positivity is closely related to
the quantum fluctuation theorem, while monotonicity leads to a quantum
version of the Hatano-Sasa inequality for nonequilibrium steady states. Based
on monotonicity, we also discuss data processing inequality for the
quantum mutual information, which has similar mathematical structure to that
of second law. Moreover, we derive a generalized second law with quantum
feedback control. In addition, we review proof of monotonicity in line
with Petz.

We investigate the problem of Language-Based Image Editing (LBIE). Given a
source image and a natural language description, we want to generate a target
image by editing the source image based on the description. We propose a
generic modelling framework for two sub-tasks of LBIE: language-based image
segmentation and image colourization. The framework uses recurrent attentive
models to fuse image and language features. Instead of using a fixed step size,
we introduce for each region of the image a termination gate to dynamically
determine after each inference step whether to continue extrapolating
additional information from the textual description. The effectiveness of the
framework is validated on three datasets. First, we introduce a synthetic
dataset, called CoSaL, to evaluate the end-to-end performance of our LBIE
system. Second, we show that the framework leads to state-of-the-art
performance on image segmentation on the ReferIt dataset. Third, we present the
first language-based colourization result on the Oxford-102 Flowers dataset.

This paper presents a study on the tiling vertices and the distribution of their radial projection spacing. The authors propose a method to tile vertices on a plane and measure the spacing between their radial projections. The study includes a mathematical model that describes the relationship between the tiling pattern and the spacing distribution. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The findings of this research provide insights into the behavior of tiled vertices and offer potential applications in various fields, including computer graphics and pattern recognition.

We make use of supersymmetric quantum mechanics (SUSY QM) to find three sets
of conditions under which the problem of a planar quantum pendulum becomes
analytically solvable. The analytic forms of the pendulum's eigenfuntions make
it possible to find analytic expressions for observables of interest, such as
the expectation values of the angular momentum squared and of the orientation
and alignment cosines as well as of the eigenenergy. Furthermore, we find that
the topology of the intersections of the pendulum's eigenenergy surfaces can be
characterized by a single integer index whose values correspond to the sets of
conditions under which the analytic solutions to the quantum pendulum problem
exist.

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision, with applications in various fields such as autonomous driving, healthcare, and robotics. In this paper, we propose SegNet, a deep convolutional encoder-decoder architecture for accurate and efficient image segmentation. SegNet comprises a sequence of encoder and decoder modules, which extract high-level spatial information from input images and progressively reconstruct the segmented output. We introduce a novel decoder module with a pixel-wise softmax layer, which allows for end-to-end training and efficient inference. Our experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that SegNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, we conduct extensive ablation studies to analyze the effectiveness of different components in SegNet, providing insights into the design choices for image segmentation architectures. Overall, our work presents a powerful and versatile framework for image segmentation that can facilitate advancements in various computer vision applications.

This academic paper presents a method for interactive segmentation of medical images using fully convolutional  neural networks (FCNs). It addresses  the  common challenge in medical image  segmentation  where a large  amount of labeled training data is  not always available. The proposed method utilizes FCNs  to learn  the segmentation task from a  relatively small   set of annotated images.  In addition,  it incorporates an interactive user interface to  refine the segmentation results in real-time, providing immediate feedback  to the user. Experimental results on a  dataset of  medical images demonstrate the effectiveness  of  the proposed method, achieving competitive segmentation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art  techniques. The interactive nature  of the  system allows for quick adjustments  and corrections, making it suitable for various medical imaging applications.

This paper aims to redefine the concept of implication relation within classical logic by providing a clear and comprehensive definition. The authors review existing definitions and highlight their limitations, such as the inability to capture all forms of implication or the failure to satisfy certain fundamental properties. Building upon these critiques, the authors propose a new definition that addresses these issues and provides a more complete understanding of implication. The new definition is then analyzed and compared with existing definitions through a series of logical tests and examples. The results demonstrate the advantages and robustness of the proposed definition, offering a stronger foundation for classical logic and its applications. Overall, this paper contributes to the field by providing a rigorous and improved definition of the implication relation in classical logic.

Convolutional neural systems (CNNs) have been the de facto standard for
nowadays 3D medical image segmentation. The convolutional operations employed in
these systems, therefore, often have difficulties in modeling the long-range
dependency due to their inductive bias of locality and weight sharing. While
Transformer was born to address this problem, it suffers from severe
mathematical and spatial difficulties in processing high-resolution 3D feature
maps. In this paper, we propose a novel implementation that effectively bridges a
{\bf Co}nvolutional neural network and a {\bf Tr}ansformer {\bf (CoTr)} for
accurate 3D medical image segmentation. Under this structure, the CNN is
designed to extract feature representations and an efficient deformable
Transformer (DeTrans) is constructed to model the long-range dependency on the
extracted feature maps. Different from the vanilla Transformer which treats all
image positions similarly, our DeTrans pays attention only to a large set of key
positions by eliminating the deformable self-attention mechanism. However, the
computational and visual complexities of DeTrans have been significantly reduced,
making it impossible to process the multi-scale and high-resolution feature maps,
which are also of paramount significance for image segmentation. We conduct an
extensive review on the Multi-Atlas Labeling Beyond the Cranial Vault (BCV)
dataset that includes 11 main human organs. The findings suggest that our CoTr
leads to a significant efficiency improvement over other CNN-based,
transformer-based, and hybrid tools on the 3D multi-organ segmentation task.

This paper  presents a survey of computer-aided knee joint magnetic resonance  image (MRI) segmentation techniques. MRI  segmentation plays a crucial role in various clinical applications,  such  as diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of  knee joint diseases. The survey provides an overview  of  the different approaches  and algorithms  used  for knee  joint MRI segmentation,  including both traditional and deep learning-based methods. The  paper also  discusses the challenges and limitations   of existing  techniques and identifies potential areas for future research. Overall, this survey aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the current state-of-the-art  in  computer-aided  knee joint MRI segmentation and serve as a valuable resource for researchers and clinicians  in the field.

Prediction sets provide a framework for making probabilistic predictions in the form of intervals or regions rather than point estimates. Existing prediction set methods often rely on distributional assumptions and can be overly conservative. In this paper, we propose a distribution-free, risk-controlling method for constructing prediction sets that does not require any distributional assumptions. Our approach is based on minimizing the worst-case expected set size, which measures the average size of the prediction sets in the worst-case scenario. We derive a theoretical bound on the worst-case expected set size and develop an algorithm for constructing prediction sets that guarantees this bound. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on several real-world datasets and compare it to existing prediction set methods. Our results show that our distribution-free approach is able to provide accurate and calibrated prediction sets while avoiding the conservatism of existing methods.

Segmentation of organs or lesions from medical images plays an essential role
in many clinical applications such as diagnosis and treatment planning. 

Though
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) have achieved the state-of-the-art
performance for automatic segmentation, they are often limited by the lack of
clinically acceptable accuracy and robustness in complex cases. Therefore,
interactive segmentation is a practical alternative to these methods. 

However,
traditional interactive segmentation methods require a large amount of user
interactions, and recently proposed CNN-based interactive segmentation methods
are limited by poor performance on previously unseen objects. To solve these
problems, we propose a novel deep learning-based interactive segmentation
method that not only has high efficiency due to only requiring clicks as user
inputs but also generalizes well to a range of previously unseen objects. Specifically, we first encode user-provided interior margin points via our
proposed exponentialized geodesic distance that enables a CNN to achieve a good
initial segmentation result of both previously seen and unseen objects, then we
use a novel information fusion method that combines the initial segmentation
with only few additional user clicks to efficiently obtain a refined
segmentation. 

We validated our proposed framework through extensive experiments
on 2D and 3D medical image segmentation tasks with a wide range of previous
unseen objects that were not present in the training set. Experimental results
showed that our proposed framework 1) achieves accurate results with fewer user
interactions and less time compared with state-of-the-art interactive
frameworks and 2) generalizes well to previously unseen objects.

The $^{24}$Mg($p$, $\alpha$)$^{21}$Na reaction was measured at the Holifield
Radioactive Ion Beam Facility at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in order to
better constrain spins and parities of energy levels in $^{21}$Na for the
astrophysically important $^{17}$F($\alpha, p$)$^{20}$Ne reaction rate
calculation. 

31 MeV proton beams from the 25-MV tandem accelerator and enriched
$^{24}$Mg solid targets were used. Recoiling $^{4}$He particles from the
$^{24}$Mg($p$, $\alpha$)$^{21}$Na reaction were detected by a highly segmented
silicon detector array which measured the yields of $^{4}$He particles over a
range of angles simultaneously. A new level at 6661 $\pm$ 5 keV was observed in
the present work. 

The extracted angular distributions for the first four levels
of $^{21}$Na and Distorted Wave Born Approximation (DWBA) calculations were
compared to verify and extract angular momentum transfer.

Automated skin lesion segmentation is an important task  in computer-aided diagnosis systems for skin cancer.  However, the lack  of a gold standard and the  subjective  nature of lesion delineation make  it challenging to evaluate the performance of segmentation algorithms. In this paper, we propose  a  novel approach to  handle inter-annotator  agreement in automated skin lesion segmentation.  Our method utilizes a   consensus-based approach, where  multiple annotators independently segment the same set of skin lesion images. We then calculate  the  inter-annotator  agreement using various metrics, such  as Dice coefficient and  Jaccard index. Based on the agreement  scores, we develop a weighting scheme to assign  higher weights  to more reliable annotators.  Finally, we use these weighted annotations to train  a  deep learning model for automated skin lesion segmentation. Experimental results on  a large dataset demonstrate that our approach improves the  segmentation accuracy compared to  using  annotations  from all  annotators equally. Our   method provides a practical solution to  handle inter-annotator agreement in automated skin lesion segmentation, which can contribute to  the development of more accurate computer-aided diagnosis systems for skin cancer.

This paper explores the concept of time directionality in classical and quantum physics. It examines the arrow of time and the asymmetry of time in classical physics, focusing on the second law of thermodynamics and the irreversibility of certain physical processes. The paper then delves into the challenges posed by quantum physics to the arrow of time, including the time-reversal symmetry of quantum mechanics and the concept of quantum entanglement. It discusses various interpretations of time directionality in quantum physics, such as the "block universe" view and the "many-worlds" interpretation. The paper concludes by highlighting the ongoing debates and open questions surrounding the nature of time directionality in both classical and quantum physics.

A variety of deep neural networks have   been applied in medical image
segmentation and achieve good performance. Unlike natural images, medical
images  of the same imaging modality are characterized by the same pattern,
which indicates that same normal organs or  tissues locate  at similar  positions
in the images. Thus, in this paper we try to   incorporate  the prior knowledge of
medical images into the structure  of neural networks such that the prior
knowledge can  be utilized for accurate  segmentation. Based on this idea,  we
propose a  novel deep  network  called knowledge-based fully convolutional network
(KFCN) for medical image segmentation.  The segmentation function and
corresponding  error is analyzed. We show the existence of an asymptotically
stable region for KFCN which traditional  FCN doesn't possess. Experiments
validate  our knowledge assumption about  the  incorporation of prior  knowledge
into the convolution kernels of  KFCN and show that  KFCN  can achieve a
reasonable  segmentation  and a satisfactory accuracy.

Segmentation of cardiac images is a crucial step in the diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular diseases. In this paper, the authors propose an automatic 3D bi-ventricular segmentation method using a shape-refined multi-task deep learning approach. The proposed method combines a two-stage network architecture with a shape-refinement module to achieve accurate segmentation of both left and right ventricles. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach on a large dataset of cardiac MRI images, achieving high segmentation accuracy and outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. The proposed method shows great potential for improving the efficiency and reliability of cardiac image analysis in clinical practice.

This paper provides a technique for analyzing iris images derived from the
deceased subjects, by training a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN)
used for the purpose of semantic segmentation. Post-mortem iris recognition
has subsequently emerged as an alternate, or additional, method useful in
forensic research. At the same time it poses several new problems from the
technical perspective, one of them being the image segmentation stage, which
has proved impossible to be properly executed by traditional iris recognition
tools. Our methodology is based on the SegNet architecture, fine-tuned with
1,300 manually segmented post-mortem iris images taken from the
Warsaw-BioBase-Post-Mortem-Iris v1.0 database. The observations described in
this paper demonstrate that this data-driven solution is unable to find certain
deformations present in post-mortem specimens, which are missing from alive
irises, and provides a significant improvement over the state-of-the-art,
conventional segmentation algorithm (OSIRIS): the Intersection over Union (IoU)
metric was improved from 73.6% (for OSIRIS) to 83% (for DCNN-based presented in
this paper) averaged over subject-disjoint, multiple splits of the information into
train and test subsets. This paper provides the last known to us method of
automatic extraction of post-mortem iris images. We offer source codes with the
trained DCNN that perform end-to-end segmentation of post-mortem iris images,
as discussed in this paper. Additionally, we offer binary masks corresponding to manual
segmentation of specimens from Warsaw-BioBase-Post-Mortem-Iris v1.0 database to
encourage implementation of alternative techniques for post-mortem iris
segmentation.

Semantic image segmentation is an important task in computer vision that aims to assign each pixel in an image to a specific category or class. However, most existing methods only focus on either category-level segmentation or instance-level segmentation. In this paper, we propose a novel framework that bridges the gap between these two levels of segmentation. Our approach utilizes category-level segmentation to guide the instance-level segmentation process, and vice versa, resulting in more accurate and robust segmentation results. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on various benchmark datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of pixel-level accuracy and segmentation quality. Our framework can also be easily integrated into existing segmentation pipelines, making it a practical solution for various real-world applications.

This paper explores the concept of Fourier series and its applications in various fields. It provides a comprehensive overview of the mathematical theory behind Fourier series, including the representation of periodic functions as infinite sums of sine and cosine functions. The paper also discusses the properties and convergence of Fourier series, as well as techniques for calculating Fourier coefficients. Furthermore, it examines the applications of Fourier series in signal processing, image compression, and solving partial differential equations. The paper concludes with a discussion on the limitations and future directions of Fourier series research. Overall, this paper aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of Fourier series and its practical applications.

Image segmentation refers to the process of dividing an image into distinct meaningful regions according to human visual perception, and is a classic topic of computer vision. Many studies have been conducted and have been widely used. However, despite many segmentation methods, only a few sparse and outdated summaries are available, and the recent achievements and problems have not been summarized. We therefore aim to provide a comprehensive summary of the recent progress in this field. The summary covers 180 articles, and summarizes the segmentation topics from different aspects, including not only the classic bottom-up, but also the latest development of superpixel, interactive methods, object recognition, semantic image and image segmentation. In addition, the existing influential data and evaluation metrics are also reviewed. Finally, we present a few hints and directions for future research on image segmentation.

Computer  vision has  become a major source of information  for  autonomous
navigation of robots  of various types, self-driving cars, military robots and
mars/lunar rovers are some examples. Nevertheless, the majority of methods
focus on analysing images captured  in visible spectrum. In  this manuscript we
elaborate on the problem of  segmenting cross-country scenes  captured in  IR
spectrum. For this purpose we proposed employing salient  features. Salient
features  are  robust to variations  in  scale, brightness and view angle. We
suggest  the Speeded-Up Robust Features as a basis for our salient features for
a number of reasons discussed   in the paper. We also provide a comparison of two
SURF implementations. The SURF features are extracted from images of different
terrain types.  For  every feature we  estimate  a terrain class membership
function. The membership values are obtained by  means of either the  multi-layer
perceptron or nearest neighbours. The features' class membership values and
their spatial  positions are then applied  to estimate  class membership values
for  all pixels in the image. To decrease the effect of segmentation  blinking
that is caused by  rapid switching between different terrain types  and to  speed
up segmentation, we are tracking  camera position and  predict features'
positions. The comparison of the  multi-layer perception  and the nearest
neighbour classifiers is presented in the paper. The error rate of the terrain
segmentation using  the nearest  neighbours obtained on the  testing   set  is
16.6+-9.17%.

Domain adaptation, the task of transferring knowledge from a source domain to a target domain with different distributions, is a challenging problem in machine learning. Existing methods often assume that labeled data is available in both domains, which is not always the case in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called mDALU (Multi-Source Domain Adaptation and Label Unification) that addresses the problem of domain adaptation with partial datasets. Our method leverages multiple source domains with different labeled datasets and jointly learns a unified label space. Specifically, mDALU consists of three main modules: (1) a feature alignment module that reduces domain shift by aligning the feature distributions across domains, (2) a label unification module that learns a common label space by leveraging the labeled data from multiple sources, and (3) a domain adaptation module that utilizes both labeled and unlabeled data from the target domain to adapt to its new distribution. We evaluate mDALU on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach, achieving superior performance in terms of classification accuracy and domain adaptation. Our method shows promise for addressing the challenges of domain adaptation with partial datasets, which are prevalent in real-world applications.

Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is an important problem  in machine  learning, as it helps to  identify instances that do  not belong to  the training distribution. Existing methods for OOD detection often  rely on   task-specific assumptions or require access to labeled OOD data. In this paper, we propose  a task-agnostic approach for  OOD detection using kernel density estimation (KDE).  Our method leverages the inherent structure of the training data to estimate the density  of the in-distribution  instances and uses this estimate to detect OOD instances. We evaluate our  method on various benchmark datasets  and compare  it with state-of-the-art  OOD detection methods. The results show that our approach  achieves competitive performance without relying on task-specific assumptions or labeled OOD  data. Our method  can be easily  applied to different tasks  and  datasets, making it a  versatile solution for  OOD  detection in machine  learning applications.

Convolutional Networks (ConvNets) excel at semantic segmentation and have
become a vital component for perception In autonomous driving. Enabling an
all-encompassing view of street-scenes, omnidirectional cameras present
themselves as a Perfect fit in such systems. most segmentation models for
parsing urban environments operate on common, narrow Field of View (FoV)
images. Transferring these models from The domain they were designed for to
360-degree perception, their performance drops dramatically, e.g., by an
absolute 30.0% (mIoU) On established test-beds. To bridge the gap in terms of
FoV and structural distribution between The imaging domains, we introduce
Efficient Concurrent Attention Networks (ECANets), directly capturing the
inherent long-range dependencies in omnidirectional imagery. In addition to the
learned attention-based contextual priors that can stretch across 360-degree
images, we upgrade model training by leveraging multi-source and
omni-supervised learning, taking advantage of both: Densely Labeled and
unlabeled data originating from Multiple datasets. To foster progress in
panoramic image segmentation, we put forward and extensively evaluate models on
Wild PAnoramic Semantic Segmentation (WildPASS), a dataset designed to capture
diverse Scenes from all around the globe. Our novel model, training regimen and
multi-source prediction fusion elevate the performance (mIoU) to new
state-of-the-art results on the public PASS (60.2%) and the Fresh WildPASS
(69.0%) benchmarks.

Camera-trap images segmentation using multi-layer robust principal component analysis

Abstract:

Camera-trap images are widely used in wildlife monitoring and conservation efforts. However, the large volume of data generated by camera traps poses a challenge for efficient analysis and interpretation. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for segmenting camera-trap images using multi-layer robust principal component analysis (MRLPCA). The MRLPCA method combines the advantages of robust principal component analysis (RPCA) and multi-layer learning to effectively separate foreground objects from background clutter in camera-trap images. We evaluate the performance of the proposed method on a dataset of camera-trap images collected from various wildlife monitoring sites. The experimental results demonstrate that the MRLPCA method outperforms existing segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed method has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of camera-trap image analysis for wildlife monitoring and conservation applications.

The measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD)
protocol has been proposed for purpose of removing detector side
channel attacks. Due to the multi-photon events of coherent states sources,
real-life implementations of MDI-QKD protocol must employ decoy states to beat
the photon-number-splitting attack. Decoy states for MDI-QKD based on the weak
coherent states have been studied recently. In this paper, we propose to
perform MDI-QKD protocol with modified coherent states (MCS) sources. We
simulate the performance of MDI-QKD with the decoy states based on MCS sources.
And our simulation indicates that both secure-key rate and transmission
distance can be improved evidently with MCS sources.The physics behind this
improvement is that probability of multi-photon events of the MCS is lower
than that of weak coherent states while at same time the probability of
single-photon is higher.

Deep learning-based clinical imagery segmentation software aims at automatic
identifying and analyzing objects on the clinical imagery. Non-local attention
and feature learning by multi-scale techniques are often applied to model network,
which drives progress in medical image segmentation. Moreover, those attention
mechanism methods have weakly non-local receptive fields' strengthened
connection for large items in medical images. Then, the features of important
large items in abstract or coarse feature maps can be deserted, which leads
to inconsistent performance. However, the existing multi-scale techniques only
often focus on multiple sizes of view, whose sparse multi-scale features
collected are not abundant enough for large objects segmentation. In this work,
a multi-dimensional attention segmentation model with cascade multi-scale
convolution is proposed to predict accurate segmentation for large items in
medical images. As the weight function, multi-dimensional attention modules
provide coefficient modification for significant/informative large objects
features. Also, The cascade multi-scale convolution modules in each
skip-connection path are exploited to capture multi-scale features in different
semantic depth. The proposed approach is tested on four datasets: KiTS19,
Pancreas CT of Decathlon-10, and MICCAI 2018 LiTS Challenge, showing
greater segmentation performances than the state-of-the-art baselines.

Land use and land cover mapping are essential to various fields of study,
including forestry, agriculture, and urban management. Using earth observation
satellites both facilitate and accelerate the task. Lately, deep learning
methods have proven to be excellent at automating the mapping via semantic
image segmentation. However, because deep neural networks require large amounts
of labeled data, it is not easy to exploit the full potential of satellite
imagery. Additionally, the land cover tends to differ in appearance from one
region to another; therefore, having labeled data from one location does not
necessarily help in mapping others. Furthermore, satellite images come in
various multispectral bands (the bands could range from RGB to over twelve
bands). In this paper, we aim at using domain adaptation to solve the
aforementioned problems. We applied a well-performing domain adaptation
approach on datasets we have built using RGB images from Sentinel-2,
WorldView-2, and Pleiades-6 satellites with Corine Land Cover as ground-truth
labels. We have also used the DeepGlobe land cover dataset. Experiments show a
significant improvement over results obtained without the use of domain
adaptation. In some cases, an improvement of over 20% MIoU. At times it even
manages to correct errors in the ground-truth labels.

This paper investigates the phenomenon of particle creation in the context of excited-de Sitter modes. The authors analyze the behavior of quantum fields in a de Sitter spacetime that is excited by a time-dependent perturbation. They find that the presence of the perturbation leads to the creation of particles, which can be detected through their effects on the energy-momentum tensor. The authors also study the evolution of the particle creation process and find that it is influenced by the parameters of the perturbation. These findings contribute to our understanding of particle creation in curved spacetimes and have implications for cosmology and quantum field theory.

This paper presents a novel approach for automatic citrus segmentation using a combination of supervised and unsupervised learning techniques. The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) for feature extraction and a clustering algorithm for unsupervised segmentation. The CNN is trained on a large dataset of annotated citrus images to learn discriminative features. The clustering algorithm then groups similar pixels together based on their feature representations. Experimental results on a dataset of citrus images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high accuracy and robustness in citrus segmentation. The combination of supervised and unsupervised learning allows for the automatic segmentation of citrus fruits without the need for manual annotation, making it a valuable tool for agricultural applications.

This paper presents a method for automatically generating datasets for   crop and weeds detection using a  model-based approach. The proposed method leverages  computer  vision  techniques and machine learning algorithms  to generate synthetic images of  crops and  weeds in various environmental  conditions. The generated datasets are then used to  train and evaluate deep learning models for  crop and weeds detection. The  results show  that the proposed method can generate datasets  that are both fast and accurate, leading to improved performance in crop and weeds detection  tasks.   The findings  of this study have implications for the development   of automated agricultural systems and can contribute to the improvement of crop yield and weed  control.

This paper develops a method to carry out the large-$N$ asymptotic analysis
of a class of $N$-dimensional integrals arising in the context of the so-called
quantum separation of variables method. We push further ideas developed in the
context of random matrices of size $N$, but in the present problem, two scales
$4/N^{\alpha}$ and $1/N$ naturally occur. In our case, the equilibrium measure
is $N^{\alpha}$-dependent and characterised by means of the solution to a
$4\times 2$ Riemann--Hilbert problem, whose large-$N$ behavior is analysed in
detail. Combining these results with techniques of concentration of measures
and an asymptotic analysis of the Schwinger-Dyson equations at the
distributional level, we obtain the large-$N$ behavior of the free energy
explicitly up to $o(0)$. The use of distributional Schwinger-Dyson is a novelty
that allows us treating sufficiently differentiable interactions and the mixing
of scales $1/N^{\alpha}$ and $1/N$, thus waiving the analyticity assumptions
often used in random matrix theory.

3D Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs) have been widely applied to 3D scene
understanding, such as video analysis and volumetric image recognition.
However, 3D networks can easily lead to over-parameterization which incurs
expensive computation cost. In this paper, we propose Channel-wise Automatic
Kernal Shrinking (CAKES), to enable efficient 3D learning by shrinking standard
3D convolutions into a set of economic operations e.g., 1D, 2D convolutions.
Unlike previous methods, CAKES performs channel-wise kernal shrinkage, which
enjoys the following benefits: 1) enabling operations deployed in every layer
to be heterogeneous, so that they can extract diverse and complementary
information to benefit the learning process; and 2) allowing for an efficient
and flexible replacement design, which can be generalized to both
spatial-temporal and volumetric data. Further, we propose a new search space
based on CAKES, so that the replacement configuration can be determined
automatically for simplifying 3D networks. CAKES shows superior performance to
other methods with similer model size, and it also achieves comparable
performance to state-of-the-art with much fewer parameters and computational
costs on tasks including 3D medical imaging segmentation and video action
recognition. Codes and models are available at
https://github.com/yucornetto/CAKES

Learning-based methods for semantic segmentation have three fundamental
problems. First, developing pixel-wise labels is costly and time-consuming.
Third, realistic segmentation datasets are extremely unbalanced: some types
are far more abundant than others, biasing the performance to the most
represented ones. In this paper, we are involved in concentrating human labelling
effort on a large subset of a larger pool of data, enhancing this effort while
improving efficiency of a segmentation model on a hold-out set. We present a
new active learning approach for cognitive segmentation based on deep
reinforcement learning (RL). An agent develops a policy to specify a subset of
small informative image areas -- opposed to whole images -- to be identified,
from a pool of unlabeled data. The region selection choice is made based on
assumptions and uncertainties of the segmentation model being trained. Our
approach introduces a new modification of the deep Q-network (DQN) formulation for
active learning, introducing it to the large-scale nature of cognitive segmentation
problems. We test the proof of theory in CamVid and provide results in the
large-scale database Cityscapes. On Cityscapes, our deep RL region-based DQN
method takes approximately 30% more additional labeled data than our most
competitive baseline to reach the same performance. However, we find that our
approach asks for more labels of under-represented categories compared to the
baselines, increasing their efficiency and trying to reduce class imbalance.

This paper proposes a novel method for screen content image segmentation using sparse decomposition and total variation minimization. The method aims to accurately separate the foreground and background regions in screen content images, which are commonly encountered in various applications such as video surveillance and image editing. The proposed method first decomposes the input image into a sparse representation using a dictionary learning algorithm. Then, a total variation minimization algorithm is applied to refine the segmentation result by promoting piecewise smoothness in the image. Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed method has the potential to be applied in real-world applications that require accurate and efficient screen content image segmentation.

Recording robots require reliable image segmentation in real time from noisy, raw images. Current image segmentation approaches use large convolutional neural network (CNN) models trained on handcrafted, carefully crafted data sets. Such models are accurate at the cost of speed, but require considerable augmentation of the data for accurate learning, and are not representative of noisy, cluttered robot data. We propose to improve the performance of real-time segmentation models on robot data by transferring features learned from synthetic segmentation data. We show that pretraining the real-time models with the synthetic data instead of ImageNet data improves their performance in the fine-tuning phase, by reducing the biases learned in the pretraining and reducing the "textit-transfer" gap. Our experiments show that the performance of our real-time robot models, trained with synthetic data, outperforms that of those trained with ImageNet data at all examined scales of fine-tuning data. Moreover, the advantage of using synthetic pretraining over ImageNet pretraining increases as the availability of robot data decreases, which makes our approach particularly attractive for the robotics domains where it is difficult and expensive to collect data.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in the field of medical imaging, as it plays a vital role in diagnosis and treatment planning. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for patch-based medical image segmentation using Quantum Tensor Networks (QTNs). QTNs are a powerful tool in quantum machine learning, capable of capturing complex patterns and relationships in data. We apply QTNs to the task of medical image segmentation by representing image patches as quantum states and using quantum operations to extract features and classify pixels. Our experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. This work opens up new possibilities for using quantum computing techniques in medical image analysis and has the potential to significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation.

Few-shot medical image segmentation is a challenging task due to the limited availability of annotated data. In this paper, we propose a novel location-sensitive local prototype network (LSLPN) for few-shot medical image segmentation. The LSLPN leverages the spatial information of the input image to generate local prototypes that capture the characteristics of different anatomical structures. These local prototypes are then used to guide the segmentation process. We evaluate the proposed method on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art few-shot segmentation methods. The experimental results demonstrate that the LSLPN outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability. Our findings suggest that incorporating location-sensitive information can significantly improve the performance of few-shot medical image segmentation models.

This paper  presents  a method for image   segmentation  using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) shape sampling with nonparametric shape priors. The authors propose a generative model  that combines a shape prior based on a mixed Gaussian process   with  a  likelihood model based on region covariances. The MCMC algorithm  samples from the posterior distribution over shape and region  labels.  Experimental results on several image datasets show that the proposed method  achieves competitive segmentation performance compared to existing methods.  The  authors also  demonstrate the flexibility and scalability of the approach by  applying it to large-scale image datasets. Overall, this paper  provides a robust and efficient   framework for image segmentation with  nonparametric shape priors.

This paper presents a study on regular ideal languages and identifies the class of "most complex" regular ideal languages. Regular ideal languages are defined as a generalization of regular languages that are closed under left quotients and inverses. The study focuses on the complexity of regular ideal languages by considering various parameters, such as the length of the longest word in the language and the size of the alphabet. The paper presents a framework for comparing the complexity of regular ideal languages and proposes a metric to measure their complexity. It also provides an algorithm to determine the most complex regular ideal languages within a given class. The findings of this study contribute to a better understanding of regular ideal languages and provide insights into their complexity.

Let $R$ be an artin algebra and $\mathcal{C}$ an additive subcategory of
$\operatorname{mod}(R)$. We construct a $t$-structure on the homotopy category
$\operatorname{K}^{-}(\mathcal{C})$ whose heart $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{C}}$ is
a natural domain for higher Auslander-Reiten (AR) theory. The abelian
categories $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{mod}(R)}$ (which is the natural domain
for classical AR theory) and $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{C}}$ interact via various
functors. If $\mathcal{C}$ is functorially finite then
$\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{C}}$ is a quotient category of
$\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{mod}(R)}$. We illustrate the theory with two
examples:
  Iyama developed a higher AR theory when $\mathcal{C}$ is a maximal
$n$-orthogonal subcategory, see \cite{I}. In this case we show that the simple
objects of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{C}}$ correspond to Iyama's higher AR
sequences and derive his higher AR duality from the existence of a Serre
functor on the derived category
$\operatorname{D}^b(\mathcal{H}_{\mathcal{C}})$.
  The category $\mathcal{O}$ of a complex semi-simple Lie algebra
$\mathfrak{g}$ fits into higher AR theory by considering $R$ to be the
coinvariant algebra of the Weyl group of $\mathfrak{g}$.

We show that on graphs with n vertices, the 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman
algorithm requires at most O(n^2/log(n)) iterations to reach stabilization. This in particular shows that the previously best, trivial upper bound of
O(n^2) is asymptotically not tight. In the logic setting, this translates to
the statement that if two graphs of size n can be distinguished by a formula in
first-order logic with counting with 3 variables (i.e., in C3), then they can
also be distinguished by a C3-formula that has quantifier depth at most
O(n^2/log(n)). To prove the result we define a game between two players that enables us to
decouple the causal dependencies between the processes happening simultaneously
over several iterations of the algorithm. 

This allows us to treat large color
classes and small color classes separately. As part of our proof we show that
for graphs with bounded color class size, the number of iterations until
stabilization is at most linear in the number of vertices. 

This also yields a
corresponding statement in first-order logic with counting. 

Similar results can be obtained for the respective logic without counting
quantifiers, i.e., for the logic L3.

This paper presents a novel deep learning model called BoxNet for biomedical image segmentation, which utilizes only box annotations instead of pixel-level annotations. Traditional methods for image segmentation rely on pixel-level annotations, which are expensive and time-consuming to obtain, especially in the biomedical domain. By training the BoxNet model on a large dataset of box annotations, it is able to accurately segment objects in biomedical images. The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets and demonstrates the effectiveness of using box annotations for image segmentation. This approach significantly reduces the annotation burden in the biomedical domain and opens up new possibilities for efficient and scalable segmentation in other domains as well.

This paper presents polynomial time algorithms for solving bi-criteria, multi-objective, and ratio problems in clustering and imaging. Specifically, the authors focus on the normalized cut and ratio regions. The normalized cut problem aims to partition a graph into two sets such that the cut between the sets is minimized and the sizes of the sets are balanced. The ratio region problem involves finding a region in an image that maximizes the ratio of the sum of the intensities inside the region to the sum of the intensities outside the region. The authors propose efficient algorithms for solving these problems, providing theoretical analysis and experimental results to demonstrate their effectiveness. Overall, this work contributes to the development of efficient algorithms for important problems in clustering and imaging.

Homotopy type theory is an interpretation of Martin-L\"of's constructive type
theory into abstract homotopy theory. There results link between constructive
mathematics and algebraic topology, providing topological semantics for
intensional systems of type theory as well as a computational approach to
algebraic topology via type theory-based proof assistants such as Coq.
  The present work investigates inductive types in this setting. Modified rules
for inductive types, including types of well-founded trees, or W-types, are
presented, and basic homotopical semantics of such types are determined.
Proofs of all results have been formally verified by the Coq proof assistant,
and proof scripts for this verification form an essential component of this
research.

сlаssіfісаtіоn оf mеdісаl fluіd sаmрlеs іn trаnsраrеnt соntаіnеrs (fоr ехаmрlе,
tubеs, sуrіngеs, іnfusіоn bаgs). Ηаndlіng fluіds suсh аs іnfusіоn fluіds,

This  academic paper proposes a novel approach for image segmentation using clustering methods. The objective of image segmentation is to partition an image into meaningful regions,  which can be further analyzed or processed. Traditional methods often  rely on pixel  intensity values or  color information, but  they may not accurately  capture the underlying structure   of the image. In  this paper, we propose a clustering-based approach that takes into account both local and global image features. Specifically, we use a combination of k-means clustering and self-organizing maps to identify image  regions that share similar  characteristics. The proposed method is applied  to several  benchmark datasets and compared against  other state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms.  The   experimental  results demonstrate that our approach achieves superior performance in  terms  of segmentation   accuracy  and computational  efficiency. This novel approach has the potential to enhance various  image analysis applications, such as  object recognition  and scene understanding.

This paper presents  a new  method for estimating high-dimensional  models using higher order estimating equations. The method  is based on  the framework of generalized estimating equations (GEE) and  extends it  to incorporate higher order terms. The proposed method is able to handle models with a large number  of parameters and can provide more efficient estimates compared to  traditional GEE  approaches.  The approach  is illustrated through simulation studies and the analysis of a  real dataset. The   results demonstrate  the effectiveness of the  method in capturing the complex relationships among  variables in high-dimensional models.

Retinal vessel segmentation plays a critical role in a range of medical applications, such as early diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy and glaucoma. However, most existing methods heavily rely on a large number of annotated data, which may not always be available in medical settings due to the high cost and time requirements of manual labeling. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for retinal vessel segmentation under extreme low annotation through the use of a generative adversarial network (GAN). Our approach leverages the power of GANs to learn from a small number of annotated images and generate realistic vessel segmentations for unannotated images. We evaluate our method on two public retinal datasets and compare it against state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive performance with significantly fewer annotations, highlighting its potential for efficient and cost-effective retinal vessel segmentation in medical practice.

Тrаnsfеr lеаrnіng іs wіdеlу usеd fоr trаіnіng mасhіnе lеаrnіng mоdеls. Ηеrе,
wе studу thе rоlе оf trаnsfеr lеаrnіng fоr trаіnіng fullу соnvоlutіоnаl
nеtwоrks (FСΝs) fоr mеdісаl іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn. Οur ехреrіmеnts shоw thаt
аlthоugh trаnsfеr lеаrnіng rеduсеs thе trаіnіng tіmе оn thе tаrgеt tаsk, thе
іmрrоvеmеnt іn sеgmеntаtіоn ассurасу іs hіghlу tаsk/dаtа-dереndеnt. Lаrgеr

We present a computer-checked generic implementation for solving
finite-horizon sequential decision problems. This is a wide class of problems,
including inter-temporal optimizations, knapsack, optimal bracketing,
scheduling, etc. The implementation can handle time-step dependent control and
state spaces, and monadic representations of uncertainty (such as stochastic,
non-deterministic, fuzzy, or combinations thereof). 

This level of genericity is
achievable in a programming language with dependent types (we have used both
Idris and Agda). Dependent types are also the means that allow us to obtain a
formalization and computer-checked proof of the central component of our
implementation: Bellman's principle of optimality and the associated backwards
induction algorithm. 

The formalization clarifies certain aspects of backwards
induction and, by making explicit notions such as viability and reachability,
can serve as a starting point for a theory of controllability of monadic
dynamical systems, commonly encountered in, e.g., climate impact research.

While the use of deep learning in image segmentation has achieved significant results, it requires a large amount of well-annotated training data, which is expensive in the field of medical image analysis. Compared with the labeled data, the unlabeled data is much easier to acquire. Semi-supervised learning and unsupervised domain adaptation are both exploiting the unlabeled data, and they are closely related. In this paper, we propose an uncertainty-aware multi-view co-training method (UMCT) that combines these two problems for the medical image segmentation task. This method is able to take full advantage of the unlabeled data for better performance. First, the 3D volume is decomposed into several views by using the transformation method, and then the 3D deep network is trained on each view. The uncertainty of each view is used as a guide to obtain accurate results. Experiments on the NIH pancreas data set and the multi-organ segmentation data set have achieved state-of-the-art results for the semi-supervised learning of medical image segmentation. As for the unsupervised domain adaptation, the effectiveness of this work is demonstrated by extending the multi-organ model to two pathological organs in the Medical Image Segmentation Decathlon (MISD) challenge data set. The UMCT-DA model is able to successfully deal with the extremely difficult situation where the original data is not available, which demonstrates its high potential for practical applications.

Reactive Turing machines extend classical Turing machines with a facility to
model observable interactive behaviour. We call a behaviour (finitely)
executable if, and only if, it is equivalent to the behaviour of a (finite)
reactive Turing machine. In this paper, we study the relationship between
executable behaviour and behaviour that can be specified in the $\pi$-calculus.
We establish that every finitely executable behaviour can be specified in the
$\pi$-calculus up to divergence-preserving branching bisimilarity. The
converse, however, is not true due to (intended) limitations of the model of
reactive Turing machines. That is, the $\pi$-calculus allows the specification
of behaviour that is not finitely executable up to divergence-preserving
branching bisimilarity. We shall prove, however, that if the finiteness
requirement on reactive Turing machines and the associated notion of
executability is relaxed to orbit-finiteness, then the $\pi$-calculus is
executable up to (divergence-insensitive) branching bisimilarity.

Publication bias, the fact that studies identified for inclusion in a meta
analysis do not represent all studies on the topic of interest, is commonly
recognized as a threat to the validity of the results of a meta analysis. One
way to explicitly model publication bias is via selection models or weighted
probability distributions. We adopt the nonparametric approach initially
introduced by Dear (1992) but impose that the weight function $w$ is monotonely
non-increasing as a function of the $p$-value. Since in meta analysis one
typically only has few studies or "observations", regularization of the
estimation problem seems sensible. In addition, virtually all parametric weight
functions proposed so far in the literature are in fact decreasing. We discuss
how to estimate a decreasing weight function in the above model and illustrate
the new methodology on two well-known examples. The new approach potentially
offers more insight in the selection process than other methods and is more
flexible than parametric approaches. Some basic properties of the
log-likelihood function and computation of a $p$-value quantifying the evidence
against the null hypothesis of a constant weight function are indicated. In
addition, we provide an approximate selection bias adjusted profile likelihood
confidence interval for the treatment effect. The corresponding software and
the datasets used to illustrate it are provided as the R package selectMeta.
This enables full reproducibility of the results in this paper.

Medical image annotations are prohibitively time-consuming and expensive to
obtain. To alleviate annotation scarcity, many approaches have been developed
to efficiently utilize extra information, e.g.,semi-supervised learning further
exploring plentiful unlabeled data, domain adaptation including multi-modality
learning and unsupervised domain adaptation resorting to the prior knowledge
from additional modality. In this paper, we aim to investigate the feasibility
of simultaneously leveraging abundant unlabeled data and well-established
cross-modality data for annotation-efficient medical image segmentation. To
this end, we propose a novel semi-supervised domain adaptation approach, namely
Dual-Teacher, where the student model not only learns from labeled target data
(e.g., CT), but also explores unlabeled target data and labeled source data
(e.g., MR) by two teacher models. Specifically, the student model learns the
knowledge of unlabeled target data from intra-domain teacher by encouraging
prediction consistency, as well as the shape priors embedded in labeled source
data from inter-domain teacher via knowledge distillation. Consequently, the
student model can effectively exploit the information from all three data
resources and comprehensively integrate them to acheive improved performance.
We conduct extensive experiments on MM-WHS 2017 dataset and demonstrate that
our approach is able to concurrently utilize unlabeled data and cross-modality
data with superior performance, outperforming semi-supervised learning and
domain adaptation methods with a large margin.

Automated segmentation in medical image analysis is a challenging task that
involves a small quantity of automatically labeled information. Moreover, most existing
learning-based methods also suffer from limited manually annotated
clinical data, which poses a significant practical issue for precise and reliable
clinical image segmentation. In addition, most existing semi-supervised
methods are generally not efficient compared with the supervised counterparts,
and often lack explicit modeling of geometric structure and semantic
data, both of which exceed the segmentation accuracy. In this work, we
present SimCVD, a simple contrastive distillation methodology that greatly
advances state-of-the-art voxel-wise representation learning. We first describe
an unsupervised training approach, which gives three views of an output volume and
predicts their signed distance maps of object boundaries in a contrastive
objective, with only one independent dropout as mask. This basic method
works very well, performing on the same level as previous partially
supervised approaches with much more labeled data. We hypothesize that dropout can
be seen as a minimal form of data augmentation and makes the network robust
to representation collapse. Then, we propose to perform structural distillation
by distilling pair-wise similarities. We evaluate SimCVD on three popular
databases: the Left Atrial Segmentation Challenge (CA) and the NIH pancreas CT
dataset. The findings on the CA dataset show that, in three kinds of
labeled ratios (i.e., 20% and 10%), SimCVD produces an average Dice score of
90.85% and 89.03% respectively, a 0.91% and 2.22% improvement compared to
past best results. Our method can be trained in an end-to-end style,
demonstrating the promise of using SimCVD as a general framework for downstream
functions, such as medical image synthesis and registration.

Nolan and Temple Lang argue that "the ability to express statistical
computations is an essential skill." A key related capacity is the ability to
conduct and present data analysis in a way that another person can understand
and replicate. The copy-and-paste workflow that is an artifact of antiquated
user-interface design makes reproducibility of statistical analysis more
difficult, especially as data become increasingly complex and statistical
methods become increasingly sophisticated. R Markdown is a new technology that
makes creating fully-reproducible statistical analysis simple and painless. It
provides a solution suitable not only for cutting edge research, but also for
use in an introductory statistics course. We present evidence that R Markdown
can be used effectively in introductory statistics courses, and discuss its
role in the rapidly-changing world of statistical computation.

Few-shot  segmentation is a  challenging  task  in computer vision, where the aim is to segment objects in an  image with  only a few labeled  examples.  In this  paper, we propose a  novel approach for few-shot segmentation called self-guided and cross-guided learning. This approach leverages both self-supervised learning and cross-guided learning  to achieve    better segmentation performance. Self-supervised learning is used to pretrain  a deep neural  network on a large unlabeled dataset, which helps to learn useful  representations of the data. Cross-guided  learning, on the  other hand, uses additional supervision from a few labeled examples to  fine-tune the pretrained network specifically  for the  few-shot segmentation task. We conduct   experiments  on various benchmark  datasets and  compare our approach with state-of-the-art methods. The results show  that our method outperforms existing approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability. Overall,  our work provides new insights and techniques for improving few-shot  segmentation in computer vision.
