The paper investigates the $L^2$ well-posedness of boundary value problems for parabolic systems with measurable coefficients. The authors analyze the existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in the $L^2$ framework and provide criteria for the regularity of these solutions. They introduce a suitable variational formulation and prove the existence of solutions using the Galerkin approximation method. The authors also establish estimates for the solutions and prove uniqueness by combining the characteristics of parabolic systems and the regularity properties of the coefficients. Their results provide a foundation for the analysis of boundary value problems for parabolic systems with measurable coefficients and contribute to the theoretical understanding of these systems.

This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting manifold valued images using active contour models. Manifold valued images are a type of data representation that can capture complex structures and relationships in high-dimensional data. The proposed method extends traditional active contour models to handle manifold valued images by incorporating a Riemannian metric and a geodesic distance function. The active contour model is formulated as an energy minimization problem, which is solved using an iterative optimization algorithm. Experimental results on various manifold valued image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method compared to existing segmentation techniques. The proposed approach has potential applications in medical imaging, computer vision, and other fields where manifold valued images are commonly encountered.

Wood and Spekkens (2015) argue that any causal model explaining the EPRB
correlations and satisfying no-signalling must also violate the assumption that
the model faithfully reproduces the statistical dependences and
independences---a so-called "fine-tuning" of the causal parameters; this
includes, in particular, retrocausal explanations of the EPRB correlations. I
consider this analysis with a view to enumerating the possible responses an
advocate of retrocausal explanations might propose. 

I focus on the response of
N\"{a}ger (2015), who argues that the central ideas of causal explanations can
be saved if one accepts the possibility of a stable fine-tuning of the causal
parameters. I argue that, in light of this view, a violation of faithfulness
does not necessarily rule out retrocausal explanations of the EPRB
correlations, although it certainly constrains such explanations. 

I conclude by
considering some possible consequences of this type of response for retrocausal
explanations.

This paper presents a novel approach for accurately delineating ambulatory electrocardiograms (ECG) by using neural networks. The proposed method, called ECG-DelNet, is designed to handle the challenges posed by mixed quality labeling in ambulatory ECG data. ECG-DelNet consists of a multi-scale convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture that leverages both global and local contextual information for accurate delineation of ECG signals. The model is trained on a dataset comprising ambulatory ECG data with mixed quality labeling, which simulates real-world scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of ECG-DelNet in accurately delineating ECG signals, even in the presence of mixed quality labeling. The proposed method can potentially improve the accuracy and efficiency of ambulatory ECG analysis in clinical settings.

This paper  explores sub-propositional  fragments of  modal logic, which are  subsets of the language of  modal  logic that do not include all  possible propositional variables. The authors investigate the expressive power and computational complexity  of these fragments,  focusing on  the relationship between the  size  of the fragment and the  complexity of reasoning tasks. They provide a  comprehensive analysis of  various sub-propositional fragments and their properties, including decidability, expressiveness, and  complexity of reasoning tasks such as satisfiability and validity. The  results of this study contribute to  a  better understanding  of  the limitations and capabilities of sub-propositional fragments of modal  logic, and have implications for the design and analysis of modal logic systems.

This paper presents a pilot study on the integration of eye-tracking technology into medical image segmentation. The aim of the study is to investigate the feasibility and potential benefits of using eye-tracking data to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation tasks. The authors developed a software tool called Gaze2Segment, which combines eye-tracking data with traditional segmentation algorithms. The tool was tested on a small group of participants who performed segmentation tasks on medical images while their eye movements were recorded. The results showed that the integration of eye-tracking data improved the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process. The findings suggest that eye-tracking technology has the potential to enhance medical image segmentation and could be a valuable tool for medical professionals in the future. However, further research is needed to validate these findings and explore the full potential of eye-tracking technology in medical image analysis.

This paper presents a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art fuzzy active contour models for image segmentation. Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision and has numerous applications in various fields. Fuzzy active contour models are a popular approach for image segmentation due to their ability to handle complex and ambiguous image data. The paper provides an overview of the basic concepts and principles of fuzzy active contour models, including the use of fuzzy sets and fuzzy logic in the segmentation process. It then reviews several recent advancements in fuzzy active contour models, including the incorporation of spatial information, texture information, and shape priors. The paper also discusses the evaluation metrics used to assess the performance of fuzzy active contour models and provides a comparative analysis of different models based on these metrics. Finally, the paper concludes with a discussion on the challenges and future directions in the field of fuzzy active contour models for image segmentation. Overall, this paper serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners interested in the latest developments in fuzzy active contour models for image segmentation.

This paper presents an approach for adaptive automatic threat recognition within 3D computed tomography (CT) images for baggage security screening. Baggage security screening plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety of air travel. While manual screening methods are currently used, they are time-consuming and prone to errors. To improve the efficiency and accuracy of baggage screening, automated methods based on CT imaging have been developed. However, these methods often struggle with detecting rare or novel threats and suffer from high false alarm rates. In this paper, we propose an adaptive approach that combines deep learning techniques with transfer learning and anomaly detection to address these challenges. The proposed method is capable of recognizing known threats with high accuracy and can also identify previously unseen threats. We evaluate our approach on a large dataset of 3D CT images and compare its performance to existing methods. The results demonstrate that our adaptive approach outperforms conventional methods, achieving higher detection rates with lower false alarm rates. This work provides a promising solution for improving the effectiveness of baggage security screening and enhancing aviation safety.

To the problem of the subdivision of a surface, which is defined by an elevation on a two-dimensional grid and by features observed at each pixel, it is added the problem of classifying these features and their topological relationships in the form of boundary conditions, which are to be used to classify the pixels. This problem has important applications in hydrology, planetary science, and biochemistry, but is especially difficult because of several reasons. First, the spatial extent of the classes follows the contours of the surface in topological space, despite their size and shape. Second, the topological structure exists on different spatial scales, depending on the different resolutions of the surface. Deep neural networks that have proved so successful for image segmentation are often not applicable to this task because they rely on convolution and pooling operations to learn the regular patterns of structures on the grid. We propose instead to represent the topological structure of the surface by a contour tree skeleton, which is a polytree capturing the evolution of the surface contours with the different heights. And we propose a graph neural network based on this tree skeleton to represent the topological structure of the surface at different spatial scales. Our model has been evaluated on real hydrological data and shows improved performance over several previous methods in terms of classification accuracy.

The abstract for the academic paper titled "Time Dependent  Variational Principle and Coherent State Orbits for a  Trapped Ion" discusses the application of the time dependent variational principle  (TDVP) and coherent  state orbits to study the dynamics of  a trapped  ion.  The  authors  present a variational method that allows for the determination of  the time  evolution  of  the ion's wave function in terms of coherent state trajectories. The TDVP is utilized to derive the equations of motion for the coherent states, and  the resulting equations are solved numerically to investigate  the ion's behavior in a harmonic trap. The  authors demonstrate that the coherent  state orbits accurately describe the quantum  dynamics of the ion, and they discuss how  this  approach can be  extended   to more complex systems.   The results of this research contribute to a better understanding  of the  dynamics  of trapped ions and have potential applications in  quantum computing  and precision measurement.

This  paper presents a method for analyzing  timed systems using tree automata. Timed systems are systems that involve the use of time, such  as real-time systems or systems  with time constraints. Tree automata are a formalism used  to  describe and  analyze tree structures. The proposed method involves modeling the  behavior of timed  systems as tree structures and then using tree automata to analyze  and   verify properties  of these  systems. The paper provides a detailed explanation  of the method and   presents  experimental results demonstrating  its effectiveness in analyzing timed  systems. The results show  that the proposed method can accurately analyze and verify properties of timed systems, making  it a valuable tool  for the design and analysis of such systems.

Accurate segmentation of different sub-regions of gliomas including
peritumoral edema, necrotic core, enhancing and non-enhancing tumor core from
multimodal MRI scans has important clinical relevance in diagnosis, prognosis
and treatment of brain tumors. However, due to the highly heterogeneous
appearance and shape, segmentation of the sub-regions is very challenging. 

Recent development using deep learning models has proved its effectiveness in
the past several brain segmentation challenges as well as other semantic and
medical image segmentation problems. Most models in brain tumor segmentation
use a 2D/3D patch to predict the class label for the center voxel and variant
patch sizes and scales are used to improve the model performance. However, it
has low computation efficiency and also has limited receptive field. U-Net is a
widely used network structure for end-to-end segmentation and can be used on
the entire image or extracted patches to provide classification labels over the
entire input voxels so that it is more efficient and expect to yield better
performance with larger input size. 

Furthermore, instead of picking the best
network structure, an ensemble of multiple models, trained on different dataset
or different hyper-parameters, can generally improve the segmentation
performance. 

In this study we propose to use an ensemble of 3D U-Nets with
different hyper-parameters for brain tumor segmentation. 

Preliminary results
showed effectiveness of this model. In addition, we developed a linear model
for survival prediction using extracted imaging and non-imaging features,
which, despite the simplicity, can effectively reduce overfitting and
regression errors.

We construct a mesoscale model of colloidal suspensions that contain solutes
reversibly adsorbing onto the colloidal particle surfaces. The present model
describes the coupled dynamics of the colloidal particles, the host fluid, and
the solutes through the Newtonne-Euler equations of motion, the hydrodynamic
equations, and the advection-diffusion equation, respectively. The solute
adsorption is modelled through a square-well potential, which represents a
short-range attractive interaction between a particle and a solute molecule.
The present model is formulated to be solved through direct numerical
simulations. Some numerical results are presented to validate the simulations.
The present model enables investigations of solute adsorption effects in the
presence of a fluid flow and an inhomogeneous solute concentration
distribution.

In this paper, we present a comprehensive review of the shape dynamics description of gravity. Shape dynamics is a novel approach to understanding the nature of gravity that aims to provide a background-independent formulation of the theory. We discuss the key ideas and concepts behind shape dynamics, including the role of conformal transformations and the emergence of spacetime geometry. We also explore the implications of shape dynamics for the cosmological constant problem and the black hole information paradox. Finally, we discuss the current status of shape dynamics research and potential future directions. Overall, this paper provides a thorough overview of the shape dynamics description of gravity and its implications for our understanding of the fundamental nature of the universe.

Image segmentation and classification are the two main fundamental   steps in
pattern recognition. To  perform medical image  segmentation or classification
with deep learning models, it requires training on  large image dataset with
annotation. The dermoscopy images (ISIC archive) considered  for this  work  does
not have  ground truth information for lesion segmentation. Performing manual
labelling on this dataset is time-consuming. To  overcome  this issue,
self-learning annotation scheme was proposed  in the two-stage  deep learning
algorithm. The two-stage deep learning algorithm consists  of  U-Net segmentation
model with the annotation scheme  and CNN classifier model. The  annotation
scheme uses a K-means clustering  algorithm along with merging conditions to
achieve initial labelling information for training the U-Net model.   The
classifier models namely  ResNet-50  and  LeNet-5 were trained and  tested on the
image dataset without segmentation for comparison and with the U-Net
segmentation for implementing the proposed self-learning  Artificial
Intelligence (AI) framework. The classification results  of  the  proposed AI
framework  achieved training accuracy of 93.8% and testing accuracy of 82.42%
when compared with the two classifier models directly  trained  on the  input
images.

This paper investigates the dynamic structural and topological phase transitions that occur on the Warsaw Stock Exchange. The study employs a phenomenological approach to analyze the fluctuations and patterns observed in the stock market using network theory. The authors identify several structural and topological changes that represent critical points in the market dynamics. They utilize a variety of statistical measures to characterize these transitions and demonstrate their significance in understanding the underlying mechanisms of the stock market. The findings contribute to the field of econophysics and provide valuable insights for investors and policymakers.

The paper presents a stability and equilibrium analysis of laneless traffic with local control laws. Laneless traffic refers to a situation where vehicles are free to move across multiple lanes and change lanes as needed. The local control laws are individual vehicle-based control mechanisms that govern the behavior of each vehicle in response to its immediate environment. The authors use mathematical modeling and analysis techniques to study the stability properties and equilibrium conditions of laneless traffic under various control laws. The results of the analysis provide insights into the dynamics and behavior of laneless traffic and can inform the design of efficient and safe traffic control systems.

Cache coherence protocols based on self-invalidation and self-downgrade have
recently seen increased popularity due to their simplicity, potential
performance efficiency, and low energy consumption. However, such protocols
result in memory instruction reordering, thus causing extra programme behaviours
that are often not intended by the programmemers. We propose a novel formal model
that captures the semantics of programmes running under such protocols, and
features a set of fences that interact with the coherence layer. Using the
model, we design an algorithm to analyse the reachability and check whether a
programme satisfies a given safety property with the current set of fences. We
describe a method for insertion of optimal sets of fences that ensure
correctness of the programme under such protocols. The method relies on a
counter-example guided fence insertion procedure. One feature of our method is
that it can handle a variety of fences (with different costs). This diversity
makes optimisation more difficult since one has to optimise the total cost of
the inserted fences, rather than just their number. To demonstrate the strength
of our approach, we have implemented a prototype and run it on a wide range of
examples and benchmarks. We have also, using simulation, evaluated the
performance of the resulting fenced programmes.

This paper presents a robust video-based eye tracking method using recursive estimation of pupil characteristics. The proposed method utilizes a combination of image processing techniques and recursive estimation algorithms to accurately track the movement of the pupil in real-time. The method is able to handle various challenges such as occlusions, changes in lighting conditions, and head movements. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method compared to existing eye tracking techniques. The proposed method has potential applications in fields such as human-computer interaction, virtual reality, and medical diagnostics.

Quasi-trees generalize trees in that the unique "path" between two nodes may
be infinite and have any countable order type. They are used to define the
rank-width of a countable graph in such a way that it is equal to the least
upper-bound of the rank-widths of its finite induced subgraphs. Join-trees are
the corresponding directed trees. They are useful to define the modular
decomposition of a countable graph. We also consider ordered join-trees, that
generalize rooted trees equipped with a linear order on the set of sons of each
node. We define algebras with finitely many operations that generate (via
infinite terms) these generalized trees. We prove that the associated regular
objects (those defined by regular terms) are exactly the ones that are the
unique models of monadic second-order sentences. These results use and
generalize a similar result by W. Thomas for countable linear orders.

The ephemeral digitisation of the left heart myocardium and the four cardiac chambers in the two-dimensional images produced by steady-state free-precession is an essential pre-processing operation for a variety of operations on the images. Despite the vast differences in the arrangement of the heart between different patients, clinical views, scanning machines, and procedures, a totally automatic method for locating and classifying these images is notoriously difficult. In this paper, we present the method of O-Net, or o-Net, which represents a novel type of convolutional neural network for the simultaneous localization, rotation into a canonical orientation, and occlusion of cardiac cavities in a two-dimensional tomographic sequence. First, a preliminary localization is performed on the input image, then a secondary localization is performed using the learned features of the previous localization, and finally a third localization is performed on the transformed image. In this study, o-Nets of various depths were trained to detect five heart classes in all three clinical views (short-axis, 4C, and 2C) without any knowledge of the clinical view being segmented. This architecture was trained on a cohort of patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and healthy volunteers. The o-Nets' performances, as measured by the IOU measure of foreground occlusion, were significantly improved by the o-Nets compared to the U-Nets, which did not localize or orient the images. In addition, O-Net was trained on the MICCAI ACDC dataset for the segmentation of the LV and the RV blood pools, while it performed slightly worse in the segmentation of the LV myocardium. We conclude that this architecture represents a major advancement in biomedical image segmentation.

Since the generative neural networks have made a breakthrough in the image
generation problem, lots of researches on their applications have been studied
such as image restoration, style transfer and image completion. However, there
has been few research generating objects in uncontrolled real-world
environments. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for vehical image
generation in real-world scenes. Using a subnetwork based on a precedent work
of image completion, our model makes the shape of an object. Details of objects
are trained by an additional colorization and refinement subnetwork, resulting
in a better quality of generated objects. Unlike many other works, our method
does not require any segmentation layout but still makes a plausible vehical in
the image. We evaluate our method by using images from Berkeley Deep Drive
(BDD) and Cityscape datasets, which are widely used for object detection and
image segmentation problems. The adequacy of the generated images by the
proposed method has also been evaluated using a widely utilized object
detection algorithm and the FID score.

This paper proposes a novel method for transferring knowledge between multi-modal and mono-modal segmentation networks. As multi-modal segmentation networks are often more accurate but also more computationally expensive, this knowledge distillation approach aims to distill the knowledge from the multi-modal network into a lighter mono-modal network. The proposed method leverages a shared encoder architecture and a task-specific decoder to enable effective knowledge transfer. Experiment results demonstrate that the distilled mono-modal network achieves comparable or even better performance than the multi-modal network while requiring significantly fewer computational resources. This method has the potential to facilitate the deployment of multi-modal segmentation networks in real-world applications with limited computational resources.

Quasi-trees generalize trees by allowing the one and only path between any two nodes to be infinite and of any order type. They are used in the definition of the rank-width of a countable graph by making it equal to the least upper bound of the rank-widths of all finite induced subgraphs of the graph. Join-trees are the directed version of quasi-trees. They are useful in the definition of the block-decomposition of a countable graph. We also consider ordered join-trees, which generalize rooted trees by imposing a linear order on the set of the descendants of each node. We define finitely many operations that can generate (through the generation of infinite sequences) these generalized trees. We prove that the regular objects (described by regular terms) are precisely the models of the second-order sentences. This is a result generalizing a result of W. Thomas concerning countable linear orders.

An often-employed method for the automatic extraction of a foreground object from an image is to define a limiting box that surrounds the object. Then, by means of a boolean encoding of the image, a refined characterization is obtained. The major difficulty in the methods for this type of automatic extraction is the preference for an input ring that encloses the object in question. This increases the effort needed to provide the required annotations, and inhibits the use of automatically obtained boxes. We propose a new method for handling a case in which the limiting box only loosely surrounds the foreground object, the Markov Random Field (MRF) model, including a constraint on global similarity for better discrimination between the foreground and the background, and an energy term to favour consistent labelling of similar-appearing pixels. Then, by means of an iterative maximum flow method, the MRF is solved. In the experiments, we test LooseCut on three public image data sets and compare it with several state-of-the-art interactive methods for image segmentation. We also show that LooseCut can improve the performance of unsupervised methods for image segmentation and saliency detection.

In this paper, we present a path integral representation of the Lorentzian spinfoam model, which can be used to describe the dynamics of 4-dimensional spacetime from a quantum gravity perspective. We derive the asymptotic behavior of the path integral and discuss its implications for the geometry of simplicial complexes. We also investigate how the simplicial geometry of the model relates to the continuum limit and discuss possible applications in the study of black holes and cosmology. Our results provide valuable insights into the nature of spacetime at the quantum level and contribute to ongoing research in quantum gravity.

This   paper presents  a comprehensive survey of high-level prior-based loss functions for medical image   segmentation. Medical  image segmentation plays a critical role in various clinical applications,  such as diagnosis, treatment planning, and   image-guided interventions. However, accurate segmentation in medical images is a challenging  task  due to   the  variability in image  appearance, noise, and artifacts. High-level prior-based  loss functions leverage prior knowledge, such as anatomical shape or spatial context, to improve the accuracy  of  segmentation models. In this survey, we  categorize and analyze various  high-level prior-based loss functions  proposed in  the literature. We discuss their strengths, limitations, and potential applications. Furthermore, we provide an overview of the evaluation metrics used to assess  the performance   of  these loss functions. Finally, we highlight open research challenges and future directions in the field of high-level prior-based   loss functions for medical  image segmentation. This survey serves as  a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners in the medical image analysis  community interested in leveraging prior  knowledge for improving segmentation accuracy.

This paper proposes a novel approach for cardiac pathology classification using cine MRI with motion characterization. The approach utilizes semi-supervised learning of apparent flow in order to achieve explainability in the classification results. The proposed method involves training a deep learning model with both labeled and unlabeled data to leverage the benefits of both supervised and unsupervised learning. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately classifying cardiac pathologies while providing interpretable explanations for the classification decisions. This paper contributes to the field of cardiac pathology classification by enhancing both the accuracy and interpretability of the classification results.

Οvеr thе lаst twо dесаdеs, dеер lеаrnіng hаs trаnsfоrmеd thе fіеld оf
соmрutеr vіsіоn. Dеер соnvоlutіоnаl nеtwоrks wеrе suссеssfullу аррlіеd tо lеаrn
dіffеrеnt vіsіоn tаsks suсh аs іmаgе сlаssіfісаtіоn, іmаgе sеgmеntаtіоn, оbjесt
dеtесtіоn аnd mаnу mоrе. Ву trаnsfеrrіng thе knоwlеdgе lеаrnеd bу dеер mоdеls
оn lаrgе gеnеrіс dаtаsеts, rеsеаrсhеrs wеrе furthеr аblе tо сrеаtе fіnе-tunеd
mоdеls fоr оthеr mоrе sресіfіс tаsks. Rесеntlу thіs іdеа wаs аррlіеd fоr

ассurасу wаs sub-орtіmаl, соmраrеd tо сlаssіс fеаturе-bаsеd sоlutіоns, thіs
еffоrt lеd tо а surgе оf lеаrnіng-bаsеd роsе еstіmаtіоn mеthоds. Ηеrе, wе
rеvіеw dеер lеаrnіng аррrоасhеs fоr саmеrа роsе еstіmаtіоn. Wе dеsсrіbе kеу
mеthоds іn thе fіеld аnd іdеntіfу trеnds аіmіng аt іmрrоvіng thе оrіgіnаl dеер

According to the World Health Organization, breast cancer is the most common
form of cancer in women. It is the second leading cause of death among women
round the world, becoming the most fatal form of cancer. Mammographic image
segmentation is a fundamental task to support image analysis and diagnosis,
taking into account shape analysis of mammary lesions and their borders.
However, mammogramme segmentation is a very hard process, once it is highly
dependent on the types of mammary tissues. In this work we present a new
semi-supervised segmentation algorithm based on the modification of the GrowCut
algorithm to perform automatic mammographic image segmentation once a region of
interest is selected by a specialist. In our proposal, we used fuzzy Gaussian
membership functions to modify the evolution rule of the original GrowCut
algorithm, in order to estimate the uncertainty of a pixel being object or
background. The main impact of the proposed method is the significant reduction
of expert effort in the initialisation of seed points of GrowCut to perform
accurate segmentation, once it removes the need of selection of background
seeds. We also constructed an automatic point selection process based on the
simulated annealing optimisation method, avoiding the need of human
intervention. The proposed approach was qualitatively compared with other
state-of-the-art segmentation techniques, considering the shape of segmented
regions. In order to validate our proposal, we built an image classifier using
a classical multilayer perceptron. We used Zernike moments to extract segmented
image features. This analysis employed 685 mammogrammes from IRMA breast cancer
database, using fat and fibroid tissues. Results show that the proposed
technique could achieve a classification rate of 91.28\% for fat tissues,
evidencing the feasibility of our approach.

Domain adaptation (DA) has drawn high interests for its capacity to adapt a
model trained on labeled source data to perform well on unlabeled or weakly
labeled target data from a different domain. Most common DA techniques require
the concurrent access to the input images of both the source and target
domains. However, in practice, it is common that the source images are not
available in the adaptation phase. This is a very frequent DA scenario in
medical imaging, for instance, when the source and target images come from
different clinical sites. We propose a novel formulation for adapting
segmentation networks, which relaxes such a constraint. Our formulation is
based on minimizing a label-free entropy loss defined over target-domain data,
which we further guide with a domain invariant prior on the segmentation
regions. Many priors can be used, derived from anatomical information. Here, a
class-ratio prior is learned via an auxiliary network and integrated in the
form of a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence in our overall loss function. We
show the effectiveness of our prior-aware entropy minimization in adapting
spine segmentation across different MRI modalities. Our method yields
comparable results to several state-of-the-art adaptation techniques, even
though is has access to less information, the source images being absent in the
adaptation phase. Our straight-forward adaptation strategy only uses one
network, contrary to popular adversarial techniques, which cannot perform
without the presance of the source images. Our framework can be readily used
with various priors and segmentation problems.

Semantic image  segmentation is   a fundamental task in  computer vision that involves assigning a label  to each pixel in an image. Atrous convolution,  also known as dilated convolution, has been widely used in recent years to improve the   performance of semantic image segmentation models.  However, the current  approach  of using atrous  convolution in a deep  neural network has limitations in terms of capturing both local and global contextual information. In  this paper, we propose a new approach called "Rethinking Atrous Convolution"  that addresses these   limitations. Our approach involves using multiple atrous rates in parallel to capture both local and global contextual  information. We also   introduce a  new  module called the  "ASPP" (Atrous  Spatial Pyramid Pooling) module, which further enhances the performance  of our approach. Experimental results on  benchmark  datasets demonstrate that our approach   outperforms existing methods in terms of both  accuracy and efficiency. Overall, our work provides a new  perspective  on the use of atrous convolution for semantic image segmentation and offers a promising direction for future research in this   field.

This paper presents a novel approach for background-foreground segmentation in the context of interior sensing in the automotive industry. Interior sensing systems are becoming increasingly important for various applications such as driver monitoring, occupant detection, and gesture recognition. Accurate segmentation of the background and foreground is a crucial step in these systems, as it allows for the extraction of relevant information from the scene. However, existing methods often struggle with challenging scenarios such as low lighting conditions, occlusions, and complex backgrounds. In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based approach that leverages the power of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to achieve robust and accurate background-foreground segmentation. Our method utilizes a combination of spatial and temporal information to improve the segmentation performance. We evaluate our approach on a large dataset of interior sensing images and compare it with state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy and robustness. Overall, our work contributes to the advancement of interior sensing systems in the automotive industry by providing a reliable and efficient solution for background-foreground segmentation.

The BEC-BCS crossover for a NJL model with diquark interactions is studied in
the presance of an external magnetic field. Particular attention is paid to
different regularization schemes used in the literature. A thorough comparsion
of results is performed for the case of a cold and magnetized two-color NJL
model. According to our results, the critical chemical potential for the BEC
transition exhibits a clear inverse magnetic catalysis effect for magnetic
fields in the range $ 1 \lesssim eB/m_\pi^2 \lesssim 20 $. As for the BEC-BCS
crossover, the corresponding critical chemical potential is very weakly
sensitive to magnetic fields up to $eB \sim 9\ m_\pi^2$, showing a much smaller
inverse magnetic catalysis as compared to the BEC transition, and displays a
strong magnetic catalysis from this point on.

The random walker (RW) algorithm is used for both image segmentation and
Registration, and possesses several useful properties that make it popular in
medical imaging, such as being globally optimizable, allowing user interaction,
and providing uncertainty information. The RW algorithm defines a weighted
graph over an image and Uses the graph's Laplacian matrix to regularize its
solutions. This regularization reduces to solving a large system of equations,
which may be excessively time consuming in some applications, such as when
interacting with a human user. Techniques have been developed that precompute
eigenvectors of a Laplacian offline, after image acquisition But before any
analysis, in order speed up the RW algorithm online, when segmentation or
Registration is being performed. However, precomputation requires certain
algorithm parameters be fixed offline, Limiting their flexibility. In this
paper, we develop techniques to update the Precomputed data online when RW
Parameters are altered. specifically, we dynamically determine the number of
eigenvectors needed for a desired accuracy based on User input, and derive
update equations for the eigenvectors when the edge weights or topology of the
image graph are changed. We present results demonstrating that our techniques
make RW with precomputation much more robust to offline settings While only
sacrificing minimal accuracy.

We present a computer-checked generic framework for solving
finite-horizon sequential decision problems. This is a broad class of solutions,
including inter-temporal optimizations, knapsack, optimal bracketing,
scheduling, etc. The framework can handle time-step dependent control and
state spaces, and monadic representations of uncertainty (such as stochastic,
non-deterministic, fuzzy, or variations thereof). This level of genericity is
possible in a programming language with dependent categories (we have used both
Idris and Agda). dependent categories are only the means that require we to provide a
formalization and computer-checked proof of the central component of our
implementation: Bellman's theory of optimality and the related backwards
induction algorithm. The implementation describes many concepts of backwards
induction and, by making explicit assumptions such as viability and reachability,
can serve as a starting point for a notion of stability of monadic
dynamical networks, often seen in, e.g., environmental impact analysis.

This academic paper investigates the application of Neural Architecture Search (NAS) in the field of remote sensing. NAS has emerged as a promising approach to automatically design deep neural networks that excel in various tasks. However, its application in operational contexts, such as remote sensing, has not been extensively explored. The paper examines the feasibility, performance, and efficiency of NAS in remote sensing by conducting a case study. The study utilizes a large-scale remote sensing dataset and compares the performance of NAS-designed models with manually designed models. Experimental results demonstrate that NAS can effectively discover high-performing deep neural network architectures for remote sensing tasks. Furthermore, the NAS-designed models outperform the manually designed models in terms of accuracy, robustness, and generalization capabilities. The paper concludes that NAS holds great potential in improving the efficiency and effectiveness of remote sensing applications by automating the design process of deep neural networks.

A key problem in salient object detection is how to effectively model the
semantic properties of salient objects in a data-driven manner. In this paper,
we propose a multi-task deep saliency model based on a fully convolutional
neural network (FCNN) with global input (whole raw images) and global output
(whole saliency maps). In principle, the proposed saliency model takes a
data-driven strategy for encoding the underlying saliency prior information,
and then sets up a multi-task learning scheme for exploring the intrinsic
correlations between saliency detection and semantic image segmentation.
Through collabourative feature learning from such two correlated tasks, the
shared fully convolutional layers produce effective features for object
perception. Moreover, it is capable of capturing the semantic information on
salient objects across different levels using the fully convolutional layers,
which investigate the feature-sharing properties of salient object detection
with great feature redundancy reduction. Finally, we present a graph Laplacian
regularised nonlinear regression model for saliency refinement. Experimental
results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in comparison with the
state-of-the-art approaches.

Environmental Microorganism Data Set Fifth Version (EMDS-5) is a microscopic
image dataset including original Environmental Microorganism (EM) images and
two sets of Ground Truth (GT) images. The GT image sets include a single-object
GT image set and a multi-object GT image set. The EMDS-4 dataset has 89 types
of EMs, each of which contains 20 original EM images, 20 single-object GT
images and 20 multi-object GT images. EMDS-3 can realize to evaluate image
preprocessing, image segmentation, feature extraction, image classification and
image retrieval functions. In order to prove the effectiveness of EMDS-5, for
each function, we select the most representative algorithms and price
indicators for testing and evaluation. The image preprocessing functions
contain two parts: image denoising and image edge detection. Image denoising
uses nine kinds of filters to denoise 25 kinds of noises, respectively. In the
aspect of edge detection, six edge detection operators are used to detect the
edges of the images, and two evaluation indicators, peak-signal to noise ratio
and mean structural similarity, are used for evaluation. Image segmentation
includes single-object image segmentation and multi-object image segmentation.
Six methods are used for single-object image segmentation, while k-means and
U-net are used for multi-object segmentation.We extract nine features from the
images in EMDS-5 and use the Support Vector Machine classifier for testing. In
terms of image classification, we select the VGG28 feature to test different
classifiers. We test two types of retrieval approaches: texture feature
retrieval and deep learning feature retrieval. We select the last layer of
features of these two deep learning networks as feature vectors. We use mean
average precision as the evaluation index for retrieval.

Mixture models whose components have skewed hypercube contours are developed
via a generalization of the multivariate shifted asymmetric Laplace density.
Specifically, we develop mixtures of multiple scaled shifted asymmetric Laplace
distributions. The component densities have two unique features: they include a
multivariate weight function, and the marginal distributions are also
asymmetric Laplace. We use these mixtures of multiple scaled shifted asymmetric
Laplace distributions for clustering applications, but they could equally well
be used in the supervised or semi-supervised paradigms. The
expectation-maximization algorithm is used for parameter estimation and the
Bayesian information criterion is used for model selection. Simulated and real
data sets are used to illustrate the approach and, in some cases, to visualize
the skewed hypercube structure of the components.

It is well-known in image processing that computational cost increases
rapidly with the number and dimensions of the images to be processed. Several
fields, such as medical imaging, routinely use numerous very large images,
which might also be 3D and/or captured at several frequency bands, all adding
to the computational expense. Multiresolution analysis is a method of
increasing the efficiency of the segmentation process. One multiresolution
approach is the coarse-to-fine segmentation strategy, whereby the segmentation
starts at a coarse resolution and is then fine-tuned during subsequent steps.
The starting resolution for segmentation is generally selected arbitrarily with
no clear selection criteria. The research reported in this paper showed that
starting from different resolutions for image segmentation results in different
accuracies and computational times, even for images of the same category
(depicting similar scenes or objects). An automated method for resolution
selection for an input image would thus be beneficial. This paper introduces a
framework for the automated selection of the best resolution for image
segmentation. We propose a measure for defining the best resolution based on
user/system criteria, offering a trade-off between accuracy and computation
time. A learning approach is then introduced for the selection of the
resolution, whereby extracted image features are mapped to the previously
determined best resolution. In the learning process, class (i.e., resolution)
distribution is generally imbalanced, making effective learning from the data
difficult. Experiments conducted with three datasets using two different
segmentation algorithms show that the resolutions selected through learning
enable much faster segmentation than the original ones, while retaining at
least the original accuracy.

This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting greenhouses on high-resolution optical satellite imagery using deep learning techniques. The proposed method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to automatically learn and extract relevant features from the input images. The CNN is trained on a large dataset of labeled greenhouse images, enabling it to accurately classify pixels as either greenhouse or non-greenhouse. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated on a test dataset, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately segmenting greenhouses. The proposed approach offers a promising solution for automating the process of greenhouse segmentation, which can have various applications in agriculture, urban planning, and environmental monitoring.

Semantic segmentation models trained on public datasets have achieved great
success in recent years. However, these models didn't consider the
personalization issue of segmentation though it is important in practice. In
this paper, we address the problem of personalized image segmentation. The
objective is to generate more accurate segmentation results on unlabeled
personalized images by investigating data's personalized traits. To open up
future research in this area, we collect a large dataset containing various
users' personalized images called PIS (Personalized Image Semantic
Segmentation). We also survey some recent researches related to this problem
and report their performance on our dataset. Furthermore, by observing the
correlation among a user's personalized images, we propose baseline method
that incorporates the inter-image context when segmenting certain images.
Extensive experiments show that our method outperforms existing methods on
the proposed dataset. The code and PIS dataset will be made publicly
available.

The problem of a strongly correlated system in which periodicly separated André-Hubbard centers are introduced into a narrow-band metal is discussed. Besides the interaction between the magnetic moments of these centers and the strong local Coulomb potential, the model also takes into account the interplay of the local and the band states. In order to study the effect of deformation on the electrical properties of the system, phonons and elastic energy are accounted for. Green's functions are calculated for both the local and the band states, and the energy spectrum is studied as a function of the temperature and the external pressure. The criterion for the transition from metal to insulator for the case of an odd number of the centers is derived, and the phase diagram of the metal-insulator transition is constructed.

In this paper, the authors investigate the impact of the density of states (DOS) of the electrodes on the transport properties of pyridine-linked single molecule junctions. By varying the energy levels of the electrode's DOS and the alignment between the molecule's energy levels and the electrode's DOS, the authors demonstrate how the transport characteristics of the junctions can be manipulated. The experiments, performed using a combination of scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy, reveal that the DOS of the electrodes directly influences the conductance and rectification behavior of the junctions. The findings provide valuable insights into the fundamental mechanisms governing charge transport through single molecule junctions and have implications for the design and optimization of molecular electronic devices.

This paper discusses solutions to the T-systems with principal coefficients. The T-systems, which are a class of difference equations, have been widely studied in various areas of mathematics, physics, and computer science. The focus of this paper is on the T-systems with principal coefficients, which are a special subclass of T-systems that have an added constraint on their coefficients. 

The paper first introduces the T-systems and provides a brief overview of their properties and applications. It then introduces the concept of principal coefficients and discusses their significance in the context of T-systems. 

The main contribution of this paper is the development of new techniques for solving the T-systems with principal coefficients. The paper presents a general algorithm that can be used to find closed-form solutions to these systems. The algorithm is based on a combination of algebraic manipulations and recursive formulas. 

To demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm, the paper presents several examples of T-systems with principal coefficients and their corresponding solutions. In each case, the algorithm is able to find the solutions in a straightforward and efficient manner. 

Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive study of the T-systems with principal coefficients and offers a new algorithm for solving these systems. The results of this paper are expected to have implications in various fields of mathematics, physics, and computer science where T-systems are used.

The possibility for controlling probe-field optical gain and absorption
switching and photon conversion by a surface-plasmon-polariton near field is
explored for a quantum dot above the surface of a metal. In contrast to the
linear response in weak-coupling regime, the calculated spectra show an
induced optical gain and triply-split spontaneous emission peak resulting
from interference between surface-plasmon field and the probe or
self-emitted light field in such strongly-coupled nonlinear system. Our
result on control of the mediated photon-photon interaction, very similar
to `gate' control in an optical transistor, may be experimentally
observable and applied to ultra-fast intrachip/interchip optical interconnects,
improvement in the performance of fiber-optic communication networks and
developments of optical digital computers and quantum communications.

In this paper, we present a demonstration of spectral level reconstruction of intrinsic $B$-mode power. We propose a novel method that allows for the reconstruction of the intrinsic $B$-mode power spectrum from temperature and polarization data. Our method involves decomposing the power spectrum into a sum of spectral components and calibrating these components using known theoretical models. We show that our method can accurately reconstruct the intrinsic $B$-mode power spectrum, thereby providing valuable insights into the underlying physics of the cosmic microwave background radiation. Overall, our demonstration highlights the potential of spectral level reconstruction as a powerful tool for analyzing and interpreting large-scale cosmological data sets.

This paper presents a novel method for screen content image segmentation using robust regression and sparse decomposition. Screen content images often contain various types of objects, such as texts, icons, and graphics, which pose challenges for traditional segmentation methods. The proposed method first utilizes robust regression to separate the foreground and background pixels based on their intensity values. Then, sparse decomposition is employed to further refine the segmentation by considering the structural coherence within each object. Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The proposed method can be a valuable tool for applications such as image editing and video processing.

The interpretation of observed  spectra of stars in terms of fundamental
stellar  properties  is a  key problem in astrophysics. For FGK-type stars, the
radiative transfer models are often computed using  the assumption of local
thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE). Its  validity is often questionable  and needs
to  be supported by detailed studies, which build upon the  consistent framework
of non-LTE.  In this review, we outline the theory of non-LTE.  The  processes
causing departures from LTE are introduced qualitatively by their physical
interpretation, as  well as quantitatively by their impact  on the  models of
stellar spectra and  element abundances. We also compile and analyse  the   most
recent results from the  literature. In  particular, we  examine the non-LTE
effects  for 24 chemical elements for six late-studied FGK-type stars.

The paper contains a short review of techniques examining regional wealth
inequalities based on Recently published research work but is also presenting
unpublished features.
  The data pertains to Italy (IT), Over The period 2007-2011: the number of
cities In regions, the number of inhabitants in cities And in regions, as well
as the Aggregated tax income of the cities and of regions. Frequency-size plots
and cumulative distribution function plots, scatter plots and rank-size plots
are displayed. The rank-size rule of a few cases is discussed. Yearly data of
the aggregated tax income is transformed into a few indicators: the Gini,
Theil, and Herfindahl-Hirschman indices. Numerical results confirm that IT is
divided into very different regional realities. One region is selected for a
short discussion: Molise.
  A note on the "first digit Benford law" for testing data validity is
presented.

Osteoarthritis (OA) is one of the major health issues among the elderly
population. MRI is the most popular technology to observe and evaluate the
progress of OA course. 

However, the extreme labor cost of MRI analysis makes
the process inefficient and expensive. Also, due to human error and subjective
nature, the inter- and intra-observer variability is rather high. 

Computer-aided knee MRI segmentation is currently an active research field
because it can alleviate doctors and radiologists from the time consuming and
tedious job, and improve the diagnosis performance which has immense potential
for both clinic and scientific research. In the past decades, researchers have
investigated automatic/semi-automatic knee MRI segmentation methods
extensively. 

However, to the best of our knowledge, there is no comprehensive
survey paper in this field yet. In this survey paper, we classify the existing
methods by their principles and discuss the current research status and point
out the future research trend in-depth.

This paper presents a computer vision pipeline for automated determination of cardiac structure and function and detection of disease using two-dimensional echocardiography. The pipeline consists of several stages, including image preprocessing, feature extraction, and disease detection. The image preprocessing stage involves noise reduction and image enhancement techniques to improve the quality of the echocardiography images. The feature extraction stage extracts relevant features from the images, such as left ventricular dimensions and ejection fraction. Finally, the disease detection stage uses machine learning algorithms to classify the images into different disease categories, such as myocardial infarction or heart failure. The pipeline was evaluated on a dataset of echocardiography images and achieved promising results, demonstrating its potential for automated cardiac diagnosis.

This paper presents a  novel approach to image segmentation using linear conditioning with metadata. The traditional methods  for image segmentation  often require labor-intensive manual annotation or rely on complex   algorithms that can   be computationally expensive.  In this study, we propose a  new framework that leverages the metadata associated with images to provide additional information  for  segmentation.  The proposed method  combines linear conditioning techniques with deep learning models  to improve the  accuracy and efficiency of segmentation tasks. We  demonstrate the effectiveness of  our approach through extensive experiments on  benchmark datasets and compare the results with existing state-of-the-art methods.  The results show that our method outperforms the traditional methods  in terms of segmentation accuracy while  reducing the computational   complexity. We believe that our approach has the  potential to significantly advance the  field of  image segmentation and open  up new  possibilities for  applications in various domains, such as medical imaging and autonomous driving.

This paper presents the development of a  novel deep  learning-based segmentation network specifically designed for mobile and web applications. The  proposed network, called the Boundary-Aware  Segmentation Network (BASNet),  aims to  accurately segment objects from  images while  also  preserving their boundaries. The design of BASNet  incorporates a two-step process consisting  of boundary and region refinement modules, which contribute to the  accurate  detection  and localization  of object  boundaries. The authors extensively  evaluate the performance of  BASNet on various  benchmark datasets and compare it  to state-of-the-art segmentation networks. Results show that BASNet achieves significantly improved segmentation accuracy  and boundary preservation, making it a promising solution for mobile and web applications  that require precise object segmentation.

Accurate segmentation of 3D medical images is crucial for various clinical applications. However, manual annotation of these images is  time-consuming  and requires extensive expertise. In this paper, we propose a  sparse annotation strategy  based on  attention-guided active learning for 3D medical image segmentation. Our  method uses an attention module to  guide the  active learning process, selecting the most informative samples  for  annotation. We evaluate the performance of our method  on a  dataset of liver  tumor segmentations and compare it  with  other active learning methods.  The results demonstrate that our approach achieves comparable or superior performance with  significantly  fewer   annotations. This  suggests that our method can effectively reduce the annotation workload and improve the  efficiency  of 3D medical image segmentation.

Liver segmentation is an important task in medical image analysis, as it plays a crucial role in various clinical applications. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for liver segmentation in abdominal CT images using an auto-context neural network and self-supervised contour attention. The auto-context neural network is designed to capture the contextual information of the liver region, while the self-supervised contour attention mechanism helps to refine the segmentation results by focusing on the liver boundary. Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy and robustness. The proposed approach has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of liver segmentation in clinical practice, thereby facilitating the diagnosis and treatment of liver diseases.

This paper presents a deep learning approach for object saliency detection and image segmentation.  Object saliency  detection   aims to identify the  most  visually significant objects in an image,   while image segmentation aims to partition  an image into meaningful regions. The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, which  is trained on a large dataset of annotated images. The network  is  able to  learn high-level features that capture the salient objects and regions in an  image. Experimental  results on benchmark  datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms  existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and  efficiency. The paper also provides insights into the learned features and  their  relevance  to object saliency and image segmentation. Overall, this work contributes  to the  field of computer vision by providing an  effective and  efficient deep learning  approach  for object saliency detection  and image segmentation.

Analyzing the exchange energy of two conduction electrons in crystal we
find that the exchange energy may be negative and, thus, singlet state may be
favorable. A full overlap in real space of wave functions of two conduction
electrons leads to a deeper exchange energy. Thus, the exchange interaction
causes bond between two conduction electrons in real space. The singlet bond
is possible because the singlet electrons can simultaneously and permanently
occupy one spatial ground state, so average energy of paired electrons is
lower than energy of unpaired electrons. Thus, pairing is a result of
the Pauli Exclusion Principle. If conduction electrons, before pairing, are put
on Fermi surface in the momentum space, then every pair may exist
permanently in time. The motion of conduction electrons in the crystal may
prevent formation of Cooper pairs, because the kinetic energy of motion
is usually larger than the binding energy in the pair. Conduction electrons as
standing waves are local and have zero momenta, hence their momenta are
synchronous; therefore, weak singlet bonds are stable despite large kinetic
energy on Fermi surface. The local pairing of standing waves explains the
inverse isotope effect, Tc-dome, insulator-superconductor transitions and many
other facts about superconductors. The electron pairs, as bosons, can form a
macroscopically coherent Bose-Einstein-Condensate and, thus, become
non-dissipative and non-local.

We study the finite element formulation of general boundary conditions for
incompressible flow problems. Distinguishing between the contributions from the
inviscid and Viscid parts of the equations, we use Nitsche's method to develop
a discrete weighted weak formulation valid for all values of the viscosity
parameter, including the limit case of The Euler equations. In order to control
the discrete kinetic energy, additional consistent terms are introduced. We
treat the limit case as a (degenerate) system of hyperbolic equations, using a
balanced spectral decomposition of the flux Jacobian matrix, in analogy with
compressible flows. then, following the theory of Friedrich's systems, the
natural characteristic boundary condition is generalized to The considered
physical boundary conditions. Several numerical experiments, including standard
benchmarks For viscous flows as well as inviscid flows are Presented.

Fully convolutional neural networks (FCNNs) trained on a large number of
images with strong pixel-level annotations have become the new state of the art
for the semantic segmentation task. While there have been recent attempts to
learn FCNNs from image-level weak annotations, they need additional
constraints, such as the size of an object, to obtain reasonable performance. 

To address this issue, we present motion-CNN (M-CNN), a novel FCNN framework
which incorporates motion cues and is learned from video-level weak
annotations. Our learning scheme to train the network uses motion segments as
soft constraints, thereby handling noisy motion information. When trained on
weakly-annotated videos, our method outperforms the state-of-the-art EM-Adapt
approach on the PASCAL VOC 2012 image segmentation benchmark. 

We also
demonstrate that the performance of M-CNN learned with 150 weak video
annotations is on par with state-of-the-art weakly-supervised methods trained
with thousands of images. 

Finally, M-CNN substantially outperforms recent
approaches in a related task of video co-localization on the YouTube-Objects
dataset.

In applications of supervised learning applied to medical image segmentation,
the need for large amounts of labeled data typically goes unquestioned. In
particular, in the case of brain anatomy segmentation, hundreds or thousands of
weakly-labeled volumes are often used as training data. In this paper, we first
observe that for many brain structures, a small number of training examples,
(n=9), weakly labeled using Freesurfer 6.0, plus simple data augmentation,
suffice as training data to achieve high performance, achieving overall mean
Dice coefficient of $0.84 \pm 0.12$ compared to Freesurfer over 28 brain
structures in T1-weighted images of $\approx 4000$ 9-10 year-olds from the
Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study. We then examine two varieties of
heteroscedastic network as a method for improving classification results. An
existing proposal by Kendall and Gal, which uses Monte-Carlo inference to learn
to predict the variance of each prediction, yields overall mean Dice of
$0.85 \pm 0.14$ and showed statistically significant improvements over 25 brain
structures. Meanwhile novel heteroscedastic network which directly learns the
probability that example has been mislabeled yielded an overall mean Dice of
$0.87 \pm 0.11$ and showed statistically significant improvements over all but
one of the brain structures considered. The loss function associated to this
network can be interpreted as performing form of learned label smoothing,
where labels are only smoothed where they are judged to be uncertain.

This academic paper presents a novel domain adaptation framework specifically designed for medical image segmentation tasks. The proposed framework aims to address the challenge of limited labeled medical images in a target domain by leveraging abundant labeled images from a source domain. The framework consists of two main components: feature adaptation and label adaptation. Feature adaptation includes unsupervised domain adaptation techniques such as domain adversarial training and domain-specific normalization. Label adaptation utilizes a self-training approach combined with uncertainty estimation to iteratively refine the segmentation labels in the target domain. Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in improving segmentation performance in the target domain. The proposed framework contributes to the field of medical image segmentation by providing a practical and efficient approach to overcome the lack of labeled data in a target domain.

Identify the cells' nuclei is the important point for most medical analyses.
To assist doctors finding the accurate cell' nuclei location automatically is
highly demanded in the clinical practise. Recently, fully convolutional neural
network (FCNs) serve as the back-bone in many image segmentation, like liver
and tumer segmentation in medical field, human body block in technical filed.
The cells' nuclei identification task is also kind of image segmentation. To
achieve this, we prefer to use deep learning algorithms. we construct three
general frameworks, one is Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Mask
RCNN), which has the high performance in many image segmentations, one is
U-net, which has the high generalisation performance on small dataset and the
other is DenseUNet, which is mixture network architecture with Dense Net and
U-net. we compare the performance of these three frameworks. And we evaluated
our method on the dataset of data science bowl 2018 challenge. For single model
without any ensemble, they all have good performance.

Nanoparticles of high refractive index materials can possess strong magnetic
polarizabilities and give rise to artificial magnetism in the optical spectral
range. While The response of individual Dielectric or metal spherical particles
can be described analytically via multipole decomposition In the Mie series,
the influence of substrates, in many cases present in experimental
observations, requires different approaches. Here, the comprehensive numerical
studies of the influence of a substrate on the spectral response of high- index
dielectric nanoparticles were performed. In particular, Glass, perfect electric
conductor, gold, and hyperbolic metamaterial substrates were investigated.
optical properties of nanoparticles were Characterized via Scattering
cross-section spectra, electric field profiles, and induced electric and
magnetic moments. The presence of substrates was shown to introduce significant
impact on particle's magnetic resonances and resonant scattering
cross-sections. Variation of substrate material provides an additional degree
of freedom in tailoring properties of emission of magnetic multipoles,
important in many applications.

The study investigates the strong monogamy conjecture in a four-qubit system. The strong monogamy conjecture is a fundamental principle in quantum information theory that provides constraints on the distribution of entanglement between multiple parties. The authors analyze various scenarios and provide a detailed mathematical framework to study the strong monogamy conjecture in a four-qubit system. The results highlight the limitations and constraints of entanglement distribution in this system, shedding light on the nature of multipartite entanglement. This research contributes to the understanding of quantum entanglement and its applications in quantum information processing.

Medical image segmentation plays a crucial  role in various  medical applications. However,  due to inconsistent image quality and variability  in anatomical  structures, medical segmentation algorithms often encounter challenges in accurately delineating boundaries. In this   paper, we propose a  new perspective on medical segmentation called  "medical matting",  which leverages the concept of uncertain alpha matting. We introduce a   novel medical matting framework that estimates the uncertainty of  segmentation boundaries to provide more  reliable  segmentations. Our approach combines deep learning-based  segmentation  with uncertainty estimation using Bayesian neural networks.  We evaluate the proposed framework on various medical images datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art segmentation methods. The results demonstrate that medical matting yields more  accurate and  robust segmentations, especially in  challenging cases with  blurred or  ambiguous  boundaries. Our work opens up new opportunities for improving medical image   segmentation  and  can be applied in a wide range of medical  applications.

The paper introduces a deep grouping model for  unified perceptual  parsing, which  aims to parse complex scenes  into coherent  groups. The proposed model utilizes a deep neural network architecture to  capture hierarchical  relationships within the scene and assign object  labels to different regions. It combines bottom-up grouping and top-down object hypotheses to achieve accurate scene understanding. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of  the proposed model on various  tasks  including object segmentation and  scene  parsing. The model  outperforms  state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets,  showcasing  its potential for real-world applications in  computer vision and image understanding.
